verses.m: ‘O Lord of gods, the slayer who commits the sin of killing those who have given up fighting, does not go to heaven, which is reserved for those who have done meritorious deeds. (4)

verses.text:
युद्धश्रद्धाथवा तेऽस्ति शङ्खचक्रगदाधर।
अहं स्थितोऽस्मि पश्यामि बलं दर्शय यत् तव॥ ५॥
verses.m: ‘O bearer of the conch, the discus and the club, if you are keen on fighting, here I stand; show your prowess, so that I may witness it.’ (5)

verses.text:
माल्यवन्तं स्थितं दृष्ट्वा माल्यवन्तमिवाचलम्।
उवाच राक्षसेन्द्रं तं देवराजानुजो बली॥ ६॥
verses.m: Seeing Mālyavān, the chief of the Rākṣasas, standing firm like Mount Mālyavān, the mighty younger brother of Indra spoke to him as follows: (6)

verses.text:
युष्मत्तो भयभीतानां देवानां वै मयाभयम्।
राक्षसोत्सादनं दत्तं तदेतदनुपाल्यते॥ ७॥
verses.m: ‘I am implementing the assurance of safety and the pledge of exterminating the Rākṣasas given by me to the gods, who are afraid of you. (7)

verses.text:
प्राणैरपि प्रियं कार्यं देवानां हि सदा मया।
सोऽहं वो निहनिष्यामि रसातलगतानपि॥ ८॥
verses.m: ‘Service must always be done to the gods by me even at the cost of my life hence I will kill you all even though you enter the nether world.’ (8)

verses.text:
देवदेवं ब्रुवाणं तं रक्ताम्बुरुहलोचनम्।
शक्त्या बिभेद संक्रुद्धो राक्षसेन्द्रो भुजान्तरे॥ ९॥
verses.m: The enraged Rākṣasa chieftain struck with his Śakti (javelin) the breast of the Lord of gods, whose eyes were like a red lotus, even while He was speaking as above. (9)

verses.text:
माल्यवद्भुजनिर्मुक्ता शक्तिर्घण्टाकृतस्वना।
हरेरुरसि बभ्राज मेघस्थेव शतह्रदा॥ १०॥
verses.m: Hurled by the arm of Mālyavān, the Śakti, with jingling bells, shone on Hari’s breast like a streak of lightning athwart a cloud. (10)

verses.text:
ततस्तामेव चोत्कृष्य शक्तिं शक्तिधरप्रियः।
माल्यवन्तं समुद्दिश्य चिक्षेपाम्बुरुहेक्षणः॥ ११॥
verses.m: Pulling out that very Śakti, Hari, the lotus-eyed, the Beloved of Lord Skanda (the bearer of a lance), hurled it back at Mālyavān. (11)

verses.text:
स्कन्दोत्सृष्टेव सा शक्तिर्गोविन्दकरनिःसृता।
कांक्षन्ती राक्षसं प्रायान्महोल्केवाञ्जनाचलम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: As though shot by Skanda, that Śakti shot by the hands of Govinda, went in search of Mālyavān like a large meteor would proceed towards a hill of antimony. (12)

verses.text:
सा तस्योरसि विस्तीर्णे हारभारावभासिते।
आपतद् राक्षसेन्द्रस्य गिरिकूट इवाशनिः॥ १३॥
verses.m: On the broad chest of that Rākṣasa chieftain, which was illumined with necklaces, the Śakti descended even as the thunderbolt on a mountain-peak. (13)

verses.text:
तया भिन्नतनुत्राणः प्राविशद् विपुलं तमः।
माल्यवान् पुनराश्वस्तस्तस्थौ गिरिरिवाचलः॥ १४॥
verses.m: With his armour broken to pieces by the Śakti, Mālyavān fell into a deep swoon; pulling himself up, however, he stood unshaken like a mountain. (14)

verses.text:
ततः कालायसं शूलं कण्टकैर्बहुभिश्चितम्।
प्रगृह्याभ्यहनद् देवं स्तनयोरन्तरे दृढम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Then he violently struck Śrī Hari in the centre of the chest with a pike made of iron and covered with many spikes. (15)

verses.text:
तथैव रणरक्तस्तु मुष्टिना वासवानुजम्।
ताडयित्वा धनुर्मात्रमपक्रान्तो निशाचरः॥ १६॥
verses.m: Likewise, striking the younger brother of Indra, Śrī Hari, with his fist, the Rākṣasa, keen on fighting, then withdrew to a bow’s length. (16)

verses.text:
ततोऽम्बरे महान् शब्दः साधुसाध्विति चोत्थितः।
आहत्य राक्षसो विष्णुं गरुडं चाप्यताडयत्॥ १७॥
verses.m: A loud cry of ‘Bravo, Bravo!’ then arose in the skies. Having struck Viṣṇu, the Rākṣasa struck Garuḍa also. (17)

verses.text:
वैनतेयस्ततः क्रुद्धः पक्षवातेन राक्षसम्।
व्यपोहद् बलवान् वायुः शुष्कपर्णचयं यथा॥ १८॥
verses.m: Provoked to anger, Garuḍa thereupon drove off the Rākṣasa with the blast (arising from the flapping) of his wings even as a strong wind would scatter a heap of dried leaves. (18)

verses.text:
द्विजेन्द्रपक्षवातेन द्रावितं दृश्य पूर्वजम्।
सुमाली स्वबलैः सार्धं लङ्कामभिमुखो ययौ॥ १९॥
verses.m: Seeing his elder brother driven off by the blast arising from the wings of Garuḍa, Sumālī made for Laṅkā, accompanied by his forces. (19)

verses.text:
पक्षवातबलोद्धूतो माल्यवानपि राक्षसः।
स्वबलेन समागम्य ययौ लङ्कां ह्रिया वृतः॥ २०॥
verses.m: Blown away by the wind arising from the wings of Garuḍa, and covered with shame, the Rākṣasa, Mālyavān too, fled to Laṅkā, joined by his forces. (20)

verses.text:
एवं ते राक्षसा राम हरिणा कमलेक्षण।
बहुशः संयुगे भग्ना हतप्रवरनायकाः॥ २१॥
verses.m: “O lotus-eyed Rāma, in this manner those Rākṣasas were repeatedly worsted in battle by Śrī Hari and their foremost leaders were killed. (21)

verses.text:
अशक्नुवन्तस्ते विष्णुं प्रतियोद्धुं बलार्दिताः।
त्यक्त्वा लङ्कां गता वस्तुं पातालं सहपत्नयः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Tormented by His might, the Rākṣasas, being unable to fight Viṣṇu in return, left Laṅkā and went to the nether world with their wives to reside there. (22)

verses.text:
सुमालिनं समासाद्य राक्षसं रघुसत्तम।
स्थिताः प्रख्यातवीर्यास्ते वंशे सालकटङ्कटे॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Those warriors well-known for their bravery, lived there under the protection of Sumālī who was born in the line of Sālakaṭaṅkaṭā. (23)

verses.text:
ये त्वया निहतास्ते तु पौलस्त्या नाम राक्षसाः।
सुमाली माल्यवान् माली ये च तेषां पुरःसराः।
सर्व एते महाभागा रावणाद् बलवत्तराः॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Sumālī, Mālyavān and Mālī and those who marched at their head, were all highly blessed and stronger than Rāvaṇa; while the other Rākṣasas who were killed by You, came in the line of Pulastya, O jewel among the Raghus! (24)

verses.text:
न चान्यो राक्षसान् हन्ता सुरारीन् देवकण्टकान्।
ऋते नारायणं देवं शङ्खचक्रगदाधरम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: “None other than Lord Nārāyaṇa, the bearer of the conch, the discus and the club, could have killed the Rākṣasas, the enemies and tormentors of gods. (25)

verses.text:
भवान् नारायणो देवश्चतुर्बाहुः सनातनः।
राक्षसान् हन्तुमुत्पन्नो ह्यजय्यः प्रभुरव्ययः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “You are indeed Lord Nārāyaṇa, the four-armed, the ancient one; You are the invincible and imperishable Lord! You were born to destroy the Rākṣasas. (26)

verses.text:
नष्टधर्मव्यवस्थानां काले काले प्रजाकरः।
उत्पद्यते दस्युवधे शरणागतवत्सलः॥ २७॥
verses.m: “You, the creator, who are fond of those who have taken refuge in You, appear from time to time to destroy the barbarians (Dasyus) who violate all the bounds of Dharma. (27)

verses.text:
एषा मया तव नराधिप राक्षसाना-
मुत्पत्तिरद्य कथिता सकला यथावत्।
भूयो निबोध रघुसत्तम रावणस्य
जन्मप्रभावमतुलं ससुतस्य सर्वम्॥ २८॥
verses.m: “O king, I have thus related in detail to you today all about the origin of the Rākṣasas. Learn from me further, O jewel among the Raghus, the origin of Rāvaṇa and his son, as also all about their immeasurable powers. (28)

verses.text:
चिरात् सुमाली व्यचरद् रसातलं
स राक्षसो विष्णुभयार्दितस्तदा।
पुत्रैश्च पौत्रैश्च समन्वितो बली
ततस्तु लङ्कामवसद् धनेश्वरः॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Tormented by the fear of Viṣṇu, that mighty ogre, Sumālī wandered for long in the nether world with his sons and grandsons. Meanwhile, Vaiśravaṇa took up his abode in Laṅkā.” (29)

verses.text:
कस्यचित् त्वथ कालस्य सुमाली नाम राक्षसः।
रसातलान्मर्त्यलोकं सर्वं वै विचचार ह॥ १॥
verses.m: “After sometime the Rākṣasa known as Sumālī, emerged from the nether world and actually wandered, they say, all over the world of mortals. (1)

verses.text:
नीलजीमूतसंकाशस्तप्तकाञ्चनकुण्डलः।
कन्यां दुहितरं गृह्य विना पद्ममिव श्रियम्॥ २॥
verses.m: “Resembling a dark cloud and wearing earrings made of pure gold, he was holding by the hand his daughter, who resembled Lakṣmī without the lotus. (2)

verses.text:
राक्षसेन्द्रः स तु तदा विचरन् वै महीतले।
तदापश्यत् स गच्छन्तं पुष्पकेण धनेश्वरम्॥ ३॥
गच्छन्तं पितरं द्रष्टुं पुलस्त्यतनयं विभुम्।
तं दृष्ट्वामरसंकाशं गच्छन्तं पावकोपमम्॥ ४॥
रसातलं प्रविष्टः सन्मर्त्यलोकात् सविस्मयः।
इत्येवं चिन्तयामास राक्षसानां महामतिः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “While that Rākṣasa chieftain was thus actually wandering on the earth, he happened to see Kubera proceeding in the aerial car, Puṣpaka, to see his powerful father, Viśarwā, the son of Pulastya. Filled with wonder to see him, who was godlike and resplendent like fire, flying, the highly intelligent Sumālī, left the world of human beings, went to the nether world and thought as follows: (3—5)

verses.text:
किं कृत्वा श्रेय इत्येवं वर्धेमहि कथं वयम्।
अथाब्रवीत् सुतां रक्षः कैकसीं नाम नामतः॥ ६॥
verses.m: ‘What has to be done to ensure the permanent good of the ogres! How shall we prosper?’ “Then the Rākṣasa told his daughter by name Kaikasī: (6)

verses.text:
पुत्रि प्रदानकालोऽयं यौवनं व्यतिवर्तते।
प्रत्याख्यानाच्च भीतैस्त्वं न वरैः प्रतिगृह्यसे॥ ७॥
verses.m: ‘My child, you are passing beyond the period of youth, this is the time to give you away in marriage; suitors hold back for fear of rejection. (7)

verses.text:
त्वत्कृते च वयं सर्वे यन्त्रिता धर्मबुद्धयः।
त्वं हि सर्वगुणोपेता श्रीः साक्षादिव पुत्रिके॥ ८॥
verses.m: ‘Pious-minded as we are, we have all exerted ourselves to see you married. Daughter, you are endowed with all good qualities and almost the same as Lakṣmī. (8)

verses.text:
कन्यापितृत्वं दुःखं हि सर्वेषां मानकांक्षिणाम्।
न ज्ञायते च कः कन्यां वरयेदिति कन्यके॥ ९॥
verses.m: ‘To be the father of an unmarried girl is a source of anxiety to all who care for their honour; for they do not know who will accept their daughter, O child! (9)

verses.text:
मातुः कुलं पितृकुलं यत्र चैव च दीयते।
कुलत्रयं सदा कन्या संशये स्थाप्य तिष्ठति॥ १०॥
verses.m: ‘An unmarried girl ever exposes to risk the reputation of three families, the family of her mother, of her father and that to which she is gifted. (10)

verses.text:
सा त्वं मुनिवरं श्रेष्ठं प्रजापतिकुलोद्भवम्।
भज विश्रवसं पुत्रि पौलस्त्यं वरय स्वयम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: ‘Hence, O daughter, you had better choose yourself and accept as your husband the excellent sage Viśravā, the best of sages, born in the family of Prajāpati (Brahmā) and the son of Pulastya. (11)

verses.text:
ईदृशास्ते भविष्यन्ति पुत्राः पुत्रि न संशयः।
तेजसा भास्करसमो तादृशोऽयं धनेश्वरः॥ १२॥
verses.m: ‘O daughter, sons will be born to you equal to the lord of riches, whose lustre is like that of the sun: about this there is no doubt.’ (12)

verses.text:
सा तु तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा कन्यका पितृगौरवात्।
तत्र गत्वा च सा तस्थौ विश्रवा यत्र तप्यते॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Hearing these words, that girl, out of respect for her father, went to the spot where Viśravā was doing Tapas and stood there. (13)

verses.text:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे राम पुलस्त्यतनयो द्विजः।
अग्निहोत्रमुपातिष्ठच्चतुर्थ इव पावकः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “In the meantime, O Rāma, that Brāhmaṇa, the son of Pulastya, resembling a fourth fire, was performing Agnihotra (sacrificial feeding of fire). (14)

verses.text:
अविचिन्त्य तु तां वेलां दारुणां पितृगौरवात्।
उपसृत्याग्रतस्तस्य चरणाधोमुखी स्थिता॥ १५॥
विलिखन्ती मुहुर्भूमिमङ्गुष्ठाग्रेण भामिनी।
स तु तां वीक्ष्य सुश्रोणीं पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम्॥ १६॥
अब्रवीत् परमोदारो दीप्यमानां स्वतेजसा।
भद्रे कस्यासि दुहिता कुतो वा त्वमिहागता॥ १७॥
किं कार्यं कस्य वा हेतोस्तत्त्वतो ब्रूहि शोभने॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Not realizing that the time was inauspicious, out of respect for her father’s words, the young girl went near him and stood in front of him with her face bent downwards and eyes fixed on her feet and repeatedly scratching the ground with the tip of her great toe. Seeing that girl of shapely limbs, whose face resembled the full moon and who was brilliant with her own lustre, that supremely magnanimous sage said: ‘Blessed girl, whose daughter are you, wherefrom and with what motive have you come here and what is your purpose? Tell me the truth, O beautiful one!’ (15—18)

verses.text:
एवमुक्ता तु सा कन्या कृताञ्जलिरथाब्रवीत्।
आत्मप्रभावेण मुने ज्ञातुमर्हसि मे मतम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Addressed thus, that girl forthwith said with folded hands: ‘O sage, you should read my mind by your spiritual insight. (19)

verses.text:
किं तु मां विद्धि ब्रह्मर्षे शासनात् पितुरागताम्।
कैकसी नाम नाम्नाहं शेषं त्वं ज्ञातुमर्हसि॥ २०॥
verses.m: ‘O Brahmarṣi, I am Kaikasī by name; know me to have come at the behest of my father; the rest you should comprehend for yourself.’ (20)

verses.text:
स तु गत्वा मुनिर्ध्यानं वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह।
विज्ञातं ते मया भद्रे कारणं यन्मनोगतम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: The sage went into meditation and said, ‘O auspicious one, I have divined the intention in your mind. (21)

verses.text:
सुताभिलाषो मत्तस्ते मत्तमातङ्गगामिनि।
दारुणायां तु वेलायां यस्मात् त्वं मामुपस्थिता॥ २२॥
शृणु तस्मात् सुतान् भद्रे यादृशाञ्जनयिष्यसि।
दारुणान् दारुणाकारान् दारुणाभिजनप्रियान्॥ २३॥
प्रसविष्यसि सुश्रोणि राक्षसान् क्रूरकर्मणः।
सा तु तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रणिपत्याब्रवीद् वचः॥ २४॥
भगवन्नीदृशान् पुत्रांस्त्वत्तोऽहं ब्रह्मवादिनः।
नेच्छामि सुदुराचारान् प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि॥ २५॥
verses.m: ‘O lady, whose gait is like that of an elephant in rut, you are eager to have sons by me. But since you have approached me at an inauspicious time, know, therefore, the kind of sons you will give birth to; they will be cruel-minded, fierce-looking and fond of people equally cruel. O lady of shapely limbs, you will bring forth Rākṣasas given to cruel deeds.’ Hearing these words of Viśravā, she made obeisance and spoke as follows: ‘O revered sir, from you, who are a Brahmavādī (one who discourses on Brahma), I do not desire such sons, given to heinous deeds; be gracious to me.’ (22—25)

verses.text:
कन्यया त्वेवमुक्तस्तु विश्रवा मुनिपुङ्गवः।
उवाच कैकसीं भूयः पूर्णेन्दुरिव रोहिणीम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: Implored thus by the maiden, Viśravā, the best of sages, who resembled the full moon, for his part spoke again to Kaikasī, who looked like Rohiṇī, (a lunar asterism):(26)

verses.text:
पश्चिमो यस्तव सुतो भविष्यति शुभानने।
मम वंशानुरूपः स धर्मात्मा च न संशयः॥ २७॥
verses.m: ‘O lady with a lovely face, he who will be your last son, will be pious-minded and fully in accord with my family: about this there is no doubt.’ (27)

verses.text:
एवमुक्ता तु सा कन्या राम कालेन केनचित्।
जनयामास बीभत्सं रक्षोरूपं सुदारुणम्॥ २८॥
दशग्रीवं महादंष्ट्रं नीलाञ्जनचयोपमम्।
ताम्रोष्ठं विंशतिभुजं महास्यं दीप्तमूर्धजम्॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Spoken to in these words, O Rāma, that girl in course of time brought forth a hideous child having the form of a Rākṣasa, very cruel, with ten heads, huge teeth, resembling a heap of antimony, having coppery lips, with twenty hands, vast mouths, and fiery hair. (28-29)

verses.text:
तस्मिञ्जाते ततस्तस्मिन् सज्वालकवलाः शिवाः।
क्रव्यादाश्चापसव्यानि मण्डलानि प्रचक्रमुः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “At the time of his birth vixens emitting flames through their mouths, and other carnivorous animals circled from left to right. (30)

verses.text:
ववर्ष रुधिरं देवो मेघाश्च खरनिःस्वनाः।
प्रबभौ न च सूर्यो वै महोल्काश्चापतन् भुवि॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “The rain-god showered blood; clouds thundered fiercely; the sun did not shine brightly; and huge meteors fell on the ground. (31)

verses.text:
चकम्पे जगती चैव ववुर्वाताः सुदारुणाः।
अक्षोभ्यः क्षुभितश्चैव समुद्रः सरितां पतिः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Nay, the earth rocked; and fierce winds blew; the sea, the lord of rivers, which is incapable of being thrown into commotion, was agitated. (32)

verses.text:
अथ नामाकरोत् तस्य पितामहसमः पिता।
दशग्रीवः प्रसूतोऽयं दशग्रीवो भविष्यति॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “His father, equal to the creator, named him Daśagrīva, since he was born with ten heads. (33)

verses.text:
तस्य त्वनन्तरं जातः कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः।
प्रमाणाद् यस्य विपुलं प्रमाणं नेह विद्यते॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “After him was born the exceptionally mighty Kumbhakarṇa, other than whose dimensions no one has greater magnitude on earth. (34)

verses.text:
ततः शूर्पणखा नाम संजज्ञे विकृतानना।
विभीषणश्च धर्मात्मा कैकस्याः पश्चिमः सुतः॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “Then was born Śūrpaṇakhā with an ugly face; the pious-minded Vibhīṣaṇa was the last son of Kaikasī. (35)

verses.text:
तस्मिन् जाते महासत्त्वे पुष्पवर्षं पपात ह।
नभःस्थाने दुन्दुभयो देवानां प्राणदंस्तथा।
वाक्यं चैवान्तरिक्षे च साधु साध्विति तत् तदा॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “When this noble soul was born, flowers, they say, fell in showers on the earth, and kettledrums of the gods sounded in the heavens. ‘Good, excellent!’ were the words spoken in mid heaven. (36)

verses.text:
तौ तु तत्र महारण्ये ववृधाते महौजसौ।
कुम्भकर्णदशग्रीवौ लोकोद्वेगकरौ तदा॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “Then both, Kumbhakarṇa and Daśagrīva, of great strength and tormentors of the world, grew up in that big forest. (37)

verses.text:
कुम्भकर्णः प्रमत्तस्तु महर्षीन् धर्मवत्सलान्।
त्रैलोक्ये नित्यासंतुष्टो भक्षयन् विचचार ह॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “Wanton Kumbhakarṇa, ever discontented, roamed about the three worlds devouring the great sages fond of righteousness. (38)

verses.text:
विभीषणस्तु धर्मात्मा नित्यं धर्मव्यवस्थितः।
स्वाध्यायनियताहार उवास विजितेन्द्रियः॥ ३९॥
verses.m: “The pious-minded Vibhīṣaṇa, who was ever fully established in rectitude and highly self-controlled, lived on a sparse diet, and was given to the study of the Vedas. (39)

verses.text:
अथ वैश्रवणो देवस्तत्र कालेन केनचित्।
आगतः पितरं द्रष्टुं पुष्पकेण धनेश्वरः॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “Now after sometime god Kubera (son of Viśravā), the lord of riches, came in his aerial car to see his father. (40)

verses.text:
तं दृष्ट्वा कैकसी तत्र ज्वलन्तमिव तेजसा।
आगम्य राक्षसी तत्र दशग्रीवमुवाच ह॥ ४१॥
verses.m: “On seeing him, blazing as it were with lustre, the ogress, Kaikasī came up there and said to Daśagrīva: (41)

verses.text:
पुत्र वैश्रवणं पश्य भ्रातरं तेजसा वृतम्।
भ्रातृभावे समे चापि पश्यात्मानं त्वमीदृशम्॥ ४२॥
verses.m: ‘Son, look at your (half-) brother, Vaiśravaṇa (Kubera), full of lustre; look upon yourself, who are so poor, though equal to him as a brother. (42)

verses.text:
दशग्रीव यथा यत्नं कुरुष्वामितविक्रम।
यथा त्वमपि मे पुत्र भवेर्वैश्रवणोपमः॥ ४३॥
verses.m: ‘Make every effort, so that you too become like him, O Daśagrīva! you have limitless prowess, my son.’ (43)

verses.text:
मातुस्तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा दशग्रीवः प्रतापवान्।
अमर्षमतुलं लेभे प्रतिज्ञां चाकरोत् तदा॥ ४४॥
verses.m: “Hearing these words of his mother, the valiant Daśagrīva became immeasurably envious and took the following vow: (44)

verses.text:
सत्यं ते प्रतिजानामि भ्रातृतुल्योऽधिकोऽपि वा।
भविष्याम्योजसा चैव संतापं त्यज हृद्गतम्॥ ४५॥
verses.m: ‘I swear to you truly, I will rise equal to Vaiśravaṇa and even excel him in respect of power; give up grieving in your heart.’ (45)

verses.text:
ततः क्रोधेन तेनैव दशग्रीवः सहानुजः।
चिकीर्षुर्दुष्करं कर्म तपसे धृतमानसः॥ ४६॥
प्राप्स्यामि तपसा काममिति कृत्वाध्यवस्य च।
आगच्छदात्मसिद्ध्यर्थं गोकर्णस्याश्रमं शुभम्॥ ४७॥
verses.m: “Then in a fit of spleen, Daśagrīva, having set his mind on performing Tapas, and seeking to accomplish a difficult task, came to the holy Āśrama at Gokarṇa for achieving success determined to gain his ends by practising austerities with his younger brothers. (46-47)

verses.text:
स राक्षसस्तत्र सहानुजस्तदा
तपश्चचारातुलमुग्रविक्रमः।
अतोषयच्चापि पितामहं विभुं
ददौ स तुष्टश्च वराञ्जयावहान्॥ ४८॥
verses.m: “That Rākṣasa of terrible prowess, in the company of his younger brothers, practised unsurpassed Tapas in that place; thereby he pleased the all-powerful Brahmā who, in the plenitude of his pleasure, granted boons which would bring victory.” (48)

verses.text:
अथाब्रवीन्मुनिं रामः कथं ते भ्रातरो वने।
कीदृशं तु तदा ब्रह्मंस्तपस्तेपुर्महाबलाः॥ १॥
verses.m: “Śrī Rāma then said to the sage, ‘How and in what manner did those brothers of extraordinary might perform Tapas in the forest, O Brāhmaṇa?’ ” (1)

verses.text:
अगस्त्यस्त्वब्रवीत् तत्र रामं सुप्रीतमानसम्।
तांस्तान् धर्मविधींस्तत्र भ्रातरस्ते समाविशन्॥ २॥
verses.m: Agastya for his part told on that occasion Śrī Rāma, who was well-pleased at heart, that the said brothers adopted the religious practices which suited them severally. (2)

verses.text:
कुम्भकर्णस्ततो यत्तो नित्यं धर्मपथे स्थितः।
तताप ग्रीष्मकाले तु पञ्चाग्नीन् परितः स्थितः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Ever steadfast in the path of rectitude and striving hard, Kumbhakarṇa performed Tapas in summer standing in the midst of fires on all the four sides and the sun shining overhead. (3)

verses.text:
मेघाम्बुसिक्तो वर्षासु वीरासनमसेवत।
नित्यं च शिशिरे काले जलमध्यप्रतिश्रयः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “In the rainy season, he sat kneeling on one leg, drenched all over with rainwater and in the winter season he remained always standing in water. (4)

verses.text:
एवं वर्षसहस्राणि दश तस्यापचक्रमुः।
धर्मे प्रयतमानस्य सत्पथे निष्ठितस्य च॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Standing firm in the right path and ever striving for righteousness, he spent ten thousand years. (5)

verses.text:
विभीषणस्तु धर्मात्मा नित्यं धर्मपरः शुचिः।
पञ्चवर्षसहस्राणि पादेनैकेन तस्थिवान्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “The pious-minded Vibhīṣaṇa, pure and always intent on rectitude, for his part stood on one leg for five thousand years. (6)

verses.text:
समाप्ते नियमे तस्य ननृतुश्चाप्सरोगणाः।
पपात पुष्पवर्षं च तुष्टुवुश्चापि देवताः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “When his austerities were over, troupes of Apsarās (celestial nymphs) danced, flowers fell in showers and the gods hymned his praises. (7)

verses.text:
पञ्चवर्षसहस्राणि सूर्यं चैवान्ववर्तत।
तस्थौ चोर्ध्वशिरोबाहुः स्वाध्याये धृतमानसः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Intent on studying the Vedas, he spent another five thousand years with his arms and head raised and worshipped the sun. (8)

verses.text:
एवं विभीषणस्यापि स्वर्गस्थस्येव नन्दने।
दशवर्षसहस्राणि गतानि नियतात्मनः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “In this manner, Vibhīṣaṇa, the disciplined soul, spent ten thousand years as though he stayed in the Nandana Vana (Indra’s pleasure-garden). (9)

verses.text:
दशवर्षसहस्रं तु निराहारो दशाननः।
पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रे तु शिरश्चाग्नौ जुहाव सः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Daśagrīva for his part went without food for ten thousand years and at the end of every thousand years offered one of his heads as a sacrifice into the fire. (10)

verses.text:
एवं वर्षसहस्राणि नव तस्यातिचक्रमुः।
शिरांसि नव चाप्यस्य प्रविष्टानि हुताशनम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Thus he spent nine thousand years and nine of his heads went into the fire. (11)

verses.text:
अथ वर्षसहस्रे तु दशमे दशमं शिरः।
छेत्तुकामे दशग्रीवे प्राप्तस्तत्र पितामहः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “At the end of ten thousand years when Daśagrīva was about to cut off his tenth head, Brahmā appeared before him. (12)

verses.text:
पितामहस्तु सुप्रीतः सार्धं देवैरुपस्थितः।
तव तावद् दशग्रीव प्रीतोऽस्मीत्यभ्यभाषत॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Supremely satisfied, Brahmā for his part stood before him in the company of other gods and said, ‘O Daśagrīva, I am really pleased with you. (13)

verses.text:
शीघ्रं वरय धर्मज्ञ वरो यस्तेऽभिकांक्षितः।
कं ते कामं करोम्यद्य न वृथा ते परिश्रमः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “ ‘Select the boon of your choice without delay, O knower of what is right! What desire of yours shall I fulfil today? Your austerities should not go in vain.’ (14)

verses.text:
अथाब्रवीद् दशग्रीवः प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना।
प्रणम्य शिरसा देवं हर्षगद्गदया गिरा॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Pleased at heart, Daśagrīva bowed down to the god and said in a voice choked with joy: (15)

verses.text:
भगवन् प्राणिनां नित्यं नान्यत्र मरणाद् भयम्।
नास्ति मृत्युसमः शत्रुरमरत्वमहं वृणे॥ १६॥
verses.m: “ ‘O Lord, to living beings the only constant source of fear is death; there is no enemy like unto death. I choose immortality.’ (16)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तदा ब्रह्मा दशग्रीवमुवाच ह।
नास्ति सर्वामरत्वं ते वरमन्यं वृणीष्व मे॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Thus addressed, Brahmā, thereupon said to Daśagrīva, ‘There can be no absolute immortality for you; ask for some other boon of me.’ (17)

verses.text:
एवमुक्ते तदा राम ब्रह्मणा लोककर्तृणा।
दशग्रीव उवाचेदं कृताञ्जलिरथाग्रतः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “O Rāma, Brahmā, the creator of the world, having spoken thus at that time, Daśagrīva, standing in front, submitted as follows with folded hands: (18)

verses.text:
सुपर्णनागयक्षाणां दैत्यदानवरक्षसाम्।
अवध्योऽहं प्रजाध्यक्ष देवतानां च शाश्वत॥ १९॥
verses.m: “ ‘O eternal lord of created beings, I want immunity from death at the hands of Suparṇas (eagles), Nāgas (serpents), Yakṣas, Daityas, Dānavas, Rākṣasas, as also from gods. (19)

verses.text:
नहि चिन्ता ममान्येषु प्राणिष्वमरपूजित।
तृणभूता हि ते मन्ये प्राणिनो मानुषादयः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “ ‘O god, worshipped by the immortals, I have no cause of anxiety from other living beings; for I think of those other creatures such as human beings as mere straw.’ (20)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तु धर्मात्मा दशग्रीवेण रक्षसा।
उवाच वचनं देवः सह देवैः पितामहः॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Addressed thus by Daśagrīva, the Rākṣasa, the pious-minded god Brahmā, who was accompanied by other gods, said as follows: (21)

verses.text:
भविष्यत्येवमेतत् ते वचो राक्षसपुङ्गव।
एवमुक्त्वा तु तं राम दशग्रीवं पितामहः॥ २२॥
शृणु चापि वरो भूयः प्रीतस्येह शुभो मम।
हुतानि यानि शीर्षाणि पूर्वमग्नौ त्वयानघ॥ २३॥
पुनस्तानि भविष्यन्ति तथैव तव राक्षस।
वितरामीह ते सौम्य वरं चान्यं दुरासदम्॥ २४॥
छन्दतस्तव रूपं च मनसा यद् यथेप्सितम्।
एवं पितामहोक्तस्य दशग्रीवस्य रक्षसः॥ २५॥
अग्नौ हुतानि शीर्षाणि पुनस्तान्युत्थितानि वै।
एवमुक्त्वा तु तं राम दशग्रीवं पितामहः॥ २६॥
विभीषणमथोवाच वाक्यं लोकपितामहः।
विभीषण त्वया वत्स धर्मसंहितबुद्धिना॥ २७॥
परितुष्टोऽस्मि धर्मात्मन् वरं वरय सुव्रत।
विभीषणस्तु धर्मात्मा वचनं प्राह साञ्जलिः॥ २८॥
वृतः सर्वगुणैर्नित्यं चन्द्रमा रश्मिभिर्यथा।
भगवन् कृतकृत्योऽहं यन्मे लोकगुरुः स्वयम्॥ २९॥
verses.m: “ ‘O jewel among the Rākṣasas, this request of yours shall be fulfilled.’ Having said this to Daśagrīva, O Rāma, Brahmā added: ‘Hear now of another auspicious boon from me who am pleased, O sinless one, the heads which were previously offered as a sacrifice into the fire, will again appear as before, O ogre. I will give you on this occasion another boon, not easily to be obtained, O dear one! You will assume any form at will.’ So of Daśagrīva, who was thus assured by Brahmā, the heads which were offered as sacrifice into the fire were restored. “Having said as above to Daśagrīva, O Rāma, Brahmā, the grandfather of the universe, spoke as follows to Vibhīṣaṇa: ‘Vibhīṣaṇa, my child, I am highly pleased with you, whose mind is imbued with Dharma, O pious-minded one! Ask for a boon, O ogre of holy vows!’ Vibhīṣaṇa, the Dharmātmā, always endowed with all good qualities like the moon with its rays, said with folded hands, ‘I am Kṛtakṛtya (one who has his life’s purpose accomplished) O venerable sir, in that the ‘Loka-guru’ (the world-teacher) is himself pleased with me. (22—29)

verses.text:
प्रीतेन यदि दातव्यो वरो मे शृणु सुव्रत।
परमापद्गतस्यापि धर्मे मम मतिर्भवेत्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: ‘If you grant a boon to me in your pleasure, O god of holy vows, please give me a hearing: Even when I get into the greatest of difficulties, my mind should remain steady in virtue. (30)

verses.text:
अशिक्षितं च ब्रह्मास्त्रं भगवन् प्रतिभातु मे।
या या मे जायते बुद्धिर्येषु येष्वाश्रमेषु च॥ ३१॥
सा सा भवतु धर्मिष्ठा तं तं धर्मं च पालये।
एष मे परमोदारो वरः परमको मतः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: ‘O Lord, let the knowledge of Brahmāstra (a mystic missile presided over by Brahmā) dawn on me untaught. May all the thoughts that come to me in the various stages of life, be in accord with Dharma. Let me also perform the duties appropriate to each such stage, O supremely magnanimous one, this I consider to be the best boon. (31-32)

verses.text:
नहि धर्माभिरक्तानां लोके किंचन दुर्लभम्।
पुनः प्रजापतिः प्रीतो विभीषणमुवाच ह॥ ३३॥
verses.m: ‘There is nothing in the world which those who are devoted to righteousness find difficult to obtain.’ The Prajāpati, being pleased, further said to Vibhīṣaṇa as follows: (33)

verses.text:
धर्मिष्ठस्त्वं यथा वत्स तथा चैतद् भविष्यति।
यस्माद् राक्षसयोनौ ते जातस्यामित्रनाशन॥ ३४॥
नाधर्मे जायते बुद्धिरमरत्वं ददामि ते।
इत्युक्त्वा कुम्भकर्णाय वरं दातुमवस्थितम्॥ ३५॥
प्रजापतिं सुराः सर्वे वाक्यं प्राञ्जलयोऽब्रुवन्।
न तावत् कुम्भकर्णाय प्रदातव्यो वरस्त्वया॥ ३६॥
जानीषे हि यथा लोकांस्त्रासयत्येष दुर्मतिः।
नन्दनेऽप्सरसः सप्त महेन्द्रानुचरा दश॥ ३७॥
अनेन भक्षिता ब्रह्मन्नृषयो मानुषास्तथा।
अलब्धवरपूर्वेण यत् कृतं राक्षसेन तु॥ ३८॥
यद्येष वरलब्धः स्याद् भक्षयेद् भुवनत्रयम्।
वरव्याजेन मोहोऽस्मै दीयताममितप्रभ॥ ३९॥
verses.m: ‘My son, since you are exceedingly virtuous, it shall be so; O destroyer of your foes, since your mind is not inclined to unrighteousness, even though you are born in the family of Rākṣasas, I make you immortal.’ “When after saying this to Vibhīṣaṇa, the Prajāpati was standing ready to grant a boon to Kumbhakarṇa, all the gods with folded hands said to him: ‘No boon at all should be granted by you to Kumbhakarṇa; for you know how this evil-minded fellow is causing terror in all the three worlds. Seven celestial nymphs (Apsarās) in the Nandana Vana (pleasure-garden of Indra), ten attendants of the mighty Indra as also seers and human beings have been devoured by him, O Brahmā! When so much havoc has been done by this Rākṣasa even when he had received no boons, he will devour all the three worlds if boons are granted to him. Under the pretext of granting boons to him, let a spell of delusion be cast on him, O god of limitless lustre! (34—39)

verses.text:
लोकानां स्वस्ति चैवं स्याद् भवेदस्य च सम्मतिः।
एवमुक्तः सुरैर्ब्रह्माचिन्तयत् पद्मसम्भवः॥ ४०॥
verses.m: ‘The welfare of the world will thus be assured and honour conferred on him.’ “Addressed thus by the gods, Brahmā, the lotus-born, thought of Goddess Saraswatī, his consort. (40)

verses.text:
चिन्तिता चोपतस्थेऽस्य पार्श्वं देवी सरस्वती।
प्राञ्जलिः सा तु पार्श्वस्था प्राह वाक्यं सरस्वती॥ ४१॥
verses.m: “Thought of by him, Goddess Saraswatī came and stood by his side. Standing by his side, she spoke with folded hands as follows: (41)

verses.text:
इयमस्म्यागता देव किं कार्यं करवाण्यहम्।
प्रजापतिस्तु तां प्राप्तां प्राह वाक्यं सरस्वतीम्॥ ४२॥
verses.m: ‘Having arrived I am here, O Lord! What shall I do?’ To Saraswatī, who had come, the Prajāpati for his part, said: (42)

verses.text:
वाणि त्वं राक्षसेन्द्रस्य भव वाग्देवतेप्सिता।
तथेत्युक्त्वा प्रविष्टा सा प्रजापतिरथाब्रवीत्॥ ४३॥
verses.m: ‘O goddess of speech, as the gods desire, you become the speech in the mouth of the chief of ogres, Kumbhakarṇa.’ Saying ‘Be it so’, she entered the mouth of Kumbhakarṇa. Then the Prajāpati said to the latter: (43)

verses.text:
कुम्भकर्ण महाबाहो वरं वरय यो मतः।
कुम्भकर्णस्तु तद्वाक्यं श्रुत्वा वचनमब्रवीत्॥ ४४॥
verses.m: ‘O mighty-armed Kumbhakarṇa, ask the boon of your choice.’ Hearing these words, Kumbhakarṇa said as follows: (44)

verses.text:
स्वप्तुं वर्षाण्यनेकानि देवदेव ममेप्सितम्।
एवमस्त्विति तं चोक्त्वा प्रायाद् ब्रह्मा सुरैःसमम्॥ ४५॥
verses.m: ‘O god of gods, I desire to sleep for many years.’ Having said ‘Be it so’, Brahmā left with the gods. (45)

verses.text:
देवी सरस्वती चैव राक्षसं तं जहौ पुनः।
ब्रह्मणा सह देवेषु गतेषु च नभःस्थलम्॥ ४६॥
विमुक्तोऽसौ सरस्वत्या स्वां संज्ञां च ततो गतः।
कुम्भकर्णस्तु दुष्टात्मा चिन्तयामास दुःखितः॥ ४७॥
verses.m: Goddess Saraswatī also left the Rākṣasa. When the gods alongwith Brahmā had ascended to the heavens, and Saraswatī had left him, the evil-minded Kumbhakarṇa came to himself and thought sorrowfully: (46-47)

verses.text:
ईदृशं किमिदं वाक्यं ममाद्य वदनाच्च्युतम्।
अहं व्यामोहितो देवैरिति मन्ये तदागतैः॥ ४८॥
verses.m: ‘How did words like these come out of my lips? I think I have been deceived by the gods who came at that time.’ (48)

verses.text:
एवं लब्धवराः सर्वे भ्रातरो दीप्ततेजसः।
श्लेष्मातकवनं गत्वा तत्र ते न्यवसन् सुखम्॥ ४९॥
verses.m: “The brothers of shining lustre, having obtained boons in this manner, went to a forest of Śleṣmātaka trees (Cordia myxor) and lived there happily.” (49)

verses.text:
सुमाली वरलब्धांस्तु ज्ञात्वा चैतान् निशाचरान्।
उदतिष्ठद् भयं त्यक्त्वा सानुगः स रसातलात्॥ १॥
verses.m: “Again, coming to know that the aforesaid Rākṣasas had obtained boons from Brahmā, Sumālī shedding his fear, rose up from the netherworld with his followers. (1)

verses.text:
मारीचश्च प्रहस्तश्च विरूपाक्षो महोदरः।
उदतिष्ठन् सुसंरब्धाः सचिवास्तस्य रक्षसः॥ २॥
verses.m: Mārīca and Prahasta, Virūpākṣa and Mahodara, the ministers of that Rākṣasa, also rose up with great fury. (2)

verses.text:
सुमाली सचिवैः सार्धं वृतो राक्षसपुङ्गवैः।
अभिगम्य दशग्रीवं परिष्वज्येदमब्रवीत्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Sumālī accompanied by his ministers and surrounded by other Rākṣasa chieftains, came to Daśagrīva and, embracing him, spoke as follows: (3)

verses.text:
दिष्ट्या ते वत्स सम्प्राप्तश्चिन्तितोऽयं मनोरथः।
यस्त्वं त्रिभुवनश्रेष्ठाल्लब्धवान् वरमुत्तमम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: ‘Child, since you have secured from the great personality of the three worlds, Brahmā, the best of boons, you have fortunately obtained what you were cherishing in your mind. (4)

verses.text:
यत्कृते च वयं लङ्कां त्यक्त्वा याता रसातलम्।
तद्गतं नो महाबाहो महद्विष्णुकृतं भयम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: ‘The great fear inspired in us by Viṣṇu, for which we had to leave Laṅkā and enter the netherworld is now gone, O mighty-armed one! (5)

verses.text:
असकृत् तद्भयाद् भग्नाः परित्यज्य स्वमालयम्।
विद्रुताः सहिताः सर्वे प्रविष्टाः स्म रसातलम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: ‘Dispirited and scared away by fear of Viṣṇu, we all had on many occasions to leave our home, Laṅkā, and enter the netherworld alongwith our followers. (6)

verses.text:
अस्मदीया च लङ्केयं नगरी राक्षसोषिता।
निवेशिता तव भ्रात्रा धनाध्यक्षेण धीमता॥ ७॥
verses.m: ‘The city of Laṅkā which has been occupied by your intelligent half-brother, Kubera, the lord of wealth, really belongs to us and was inhabited by ogres. (7)

verses.text:
यदि नामात्र शक्यं स्यात् साम्ना दानेन वानघ।
तरसा वा महाबाहो प्रत्यानेतुं कृतं भवेत्॥ ८॥
verses.m: ‘If, O sinless and mighty-armed one, it could be taken back by sweet reasonableness or by gift or by force, our work will have been accomplished. (8)

verses.text:
त्वं च लङ्केश्वरस्तात भविष्यसि न संशयः।
त्वया राक्षसवंशोऽयं निमग्नोऽपि समुद्धृतः॥ ९॥
verses.m: ‘Nay, without doubt you will be the ruler of Laṅkā, O dear one! The line of Rākṣasas which had sunk to the grove, has again been lifted up by you. (9)

verses.text:
सर्वेषां नः प्रभुश्चैव भविष्यसि महाबल।
अथाब्रवीद् दशग्रीवो मातामहमुपस्थितम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: ‘O ogre of extraordinary might, you will become the overlord of all of us.’ Daśagrīva then said to his maternal grandfather, who had come in person: (10)

verses.text:
वित्तेशो गुरुरस्माकं नार्हसे वक्तुमीदृशम्।
साम्ना हि राक्षसेन्द्रेण प्रत्याख्यातो गरीयसा॥ ११॥
किंचिन्नाह तदा रक्षो ज्ञात्वा तस्य चिकीर्षितम्।
कस्यचित् त्वथ कालस्य वसन्तं रावणं ततः॥ १२॥
उक्तवन्तं तथा वाक्यं दशग्रीवं निशाचरः।
प्रहस्तः प्रश्रितं वाक्यमिदमाह सकारणम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: ‘You ought not to speak in this strain; for the lord of wealth is our elder brother.’ “The great Rākṣasa, being rebuked in gentle words by the ruler of the ogres, did not say anything further, knowing his (Daśagrīva’s) intention. After sometime the ogre Prahasta addressed the following humble and well-reasoned words to Rāvaṇa, who was still there and who had spoken in the aforesaid manner: (11—13)

verses.text:
दशग्रीव महाबाहो नार्हसे वक्तुमीदृशम्।
सौभ्रात्रं नास्ति शूराणां शृणु चेदं वचो मम॥ १४॥
verses.m: ‘O mighty-armed Daśagrīva, you ought not to speak like this; there is no such thing as brotherly feeling among heroes. Nay, listen to my following words: (14)

verses.text:
अदितिश्च दितिश्चैव भगिन्यौ सहिते हि ते।
भार्ये परमरूपिण्यौ कश्यपस्य प्रजापतेः॥ १५॥
verses.m: ‘The sisters, Aditi and Diti, both highly beautiful, are the mutually loving wives of Kaśyapa, a lord of creation. (15)

verses.text:
अदितिर्जनयामास देवांस्त्रिभुवनेश्वरान्।
दितिस्त्वजनयद् दैत्यान् कश्यपस्यात्मसम्भवान्॥ १६॥
verses.m: ‘Aditi bore the gods, the lords of the worlds; Diti gave birth to the Daityas, both being the progeny of Kaśyapa. (16)

verses.text:
दैत्यानां किल धर्मज्ञ पुरेयं सवनार्णवा।
सपर्वता मही वीर तेऽभवन् प्रभविष्णवः॥ १७॥
verses.m: ‘This earth (filled) with its forests, seas and mountains belonged of yore to the Daityas; for they were all powerful. (17)

verses.text:
निहत्य तांस्तु समरे विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना।
देवानां वशमानीतं त्रैलोक्यमिदमव्ययम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: ‘After killing them in war, all these three worlds were for their part brought under the lasting sway of the gods by the powerful Viṣṇu. (18)

verses.text:
नैतदेको भवानेव करिष्यति विपर्ययम्।
सुरासुरैराचरितं तत् कुरुष्व वचो मम॥ १९॥
verses.m: ‘You are not the only one who will act in opposition to a brother; this was done in the past by the gods and demons alike. Hence, do as I say.’ (19)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तो दशग्रीवः प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना।
चिन्तयित्वा मुहूर्तं वै बाढमित्येव सोऽब्रवीत्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Having been addressed thus, Daśagrīva, pleased at heart, thought for a while and then said, ‘All right’. (20)

verses.text:
स तु तेनैव हर्षेण तस्मिन्नहनि वीर्यवान्।
वनं गतो दशग्रीवः सह तैः क्षणदाचरैः॥ २१॥
verses.m: “With the same joy, the valiant Daśagrīva went to the forest the very day accompanied by the Rākṣasas. (21)

verses.text:
त्रिकूटस्थः स तु तदा दशग्रीवो निशाचरः।
प्रेषयामास दौत्येन प्रहस्तं वाक्यकोविदम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Stationed on Mount Trikūṭa, Daśagrīva, the Rākṣasa, sent Prahasta, skilled in the art of expression, as a messenger, saying: (22)

verses.text:
प्रहस्त शीघ्रं गच्छ त्वं ब्रूहि नैर्ऋतपुङ्गवम्।
वचसा मम वित्तेशं सामपूर्वमिदं वचः॥ २३॥
verses.m: ‘O Prahasta, go quickly and convey to the lord of riches, the foremost of ogres, these words, as coming from me, in a polite manner: (23)

verses.text:
इयं लङ्का पुरी राजन् राक्षसानां महात्मनाम्।
त्वया निवेशिता सौम्य नैतद् युक्तं तवानघ॥ २४॥
verses.m: ‘This city of Laṅkā, O king, which belonged to the mighty Rākṣasas, has been occupied by you. O gentle and sinless one, this is not proper for you. (24)

verses.text:
तद् भवान् यदि नो ह्यद्य दद्यादतुलविक्रम।
कृता भवेन्मम प्रीतिधर्मश्चैवानुपालितः॥ २५॥
verses.m: ‘If you, O hero of peerless strength, could give it back to us now, you will at once have pleased me and done the right thing.’ (25)

verses.text:
स तु गत्वा पुरीं लङ्कां धनदेन सुरक्षिताम्।
अब्रवीत् परमोदारं वित्तपालमिदं वचः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Proceeding to Laṅkā, well-protected by Kubera, Prahasta addressed the following words to the highly magnanimous lord of wealth: (26)

verses.text:
प्रेषितोऽहं तव भ्रात्रा दशग्रीवेण सुव्रत।
त्वत्समीपं महाबाहो सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वर॥ २७॥
verses.m: ‘O pious and best among all those who bear arms, I have been sent by Daśagrīva, your half-brother, to your presence, O mighty-armed one! (27)

verses.text:
तच्छ्रूयतां महाप्राज्ञ सर्वशास्त्रविशारद।
वचनं मम वित्तेश यद् ब्रवीति दशाननः॥ २८॥
verses.m: ‘O lord of wealth, learned in all the Śāstras and highly intelligent, listen to my submission, which is precisely what Daśagrīva says: (28)

verses.text:
इयं किल पुरी रम्या सुमालिप्रमुखैः पुरा।
भुक्तपूर्वा विशालाक्ष राक्षसैर्भीमविक्रमैः॥ २९॥
verses.m: ‘This charming city, O large-eyed one, was previously ruled over by Rākṣasas of terrible might, of whom Sumālī was the foremost. (29)

verses.text:
तेन विज्ञाप्यते सोऽयं साम्प्रतं विश्रवात्मज।
तदेषा दीयतां तात याचतस्तस्य सामतः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: ‘O son of Viśravā, this requisition is being made by him now. Let it be given back to him who is asking for it in a peaceful manner.’ (30)

verses.text:
प्रहस्तादपि संश्रुत्य देवो वैश्रवणो वचः।
प्रत्युवाच प्रहस्तं तं वाक्यं वाक्यविदां वरः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Hearing these words from Prahasta, god Vaiśravaṇa, the best of speakers, replied as follows to Prahasta: (31)

verses.text:
दत्ता ममेयं पित्रा तु लङ्का शून्या निशाचरैः।
निवेशिता च मे रक्षो दानमानादिभिर्गुणैः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “This city of Laṅkā evacuated by the Rākṣasas, was given to me by my father. It then came to be peopled by me by inducements of gifts and honour etc. (32)

verses.text:
ब्रूहि गच्छ दशग्रीवं पुरी राज्यं च यन्मम।
तत्राप्येतन्महाबाहो भुङ्क्ष्व राज्यमकण्टकम्॥ ३३॥
अविभक्तं त्वया सार्धं राज्यं यच्चापि मे वसु।
एवमुक्त्वा धनाध्यक्षो जगाम पितुरन्तिकम्॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “Go and tell Daśagrīva, “my city and kingdom as well belong to you. My kingdom as well as all my wealth stands undivided with you. Enjoy it (with me) without any fear of rivalry.” Having spoken thus, the lord of wealth sought the presence of his father. (33-34)

verses.text:
अभिवाद्य गुरुं प्राह रावणस्य यदीप्सितम्।
एष तात दशग्रीवो दूतं प्रेषितवान् मम॥ ३५॥
दीयतां नगरी लङ्का पूर्वं रक्षोगणोषिता।
मयात्र यदनुष्ठेयं तन्ममाचक्ष्व सुव्रत॥ ३६॥
verses.m: Paying respects to his father, he conveyed Daśagrīva’s desire in the following words: ‘Father, Daśagrīva has just sent an emissary to me saying: “Let Laṅkā, which was previously occupied by the Rākṣasas, be given back to me. Please tell me, O pious one, what I should do in this connection.” (35-36)

verses.text:
ब्रह्मर्षिस्त्वेवमुक्तोऽसौ विश्रवा मुनिपुङ्गवः।
प्राञ्जलिं धनदं प्राह शृणु पुत्र वचो मम॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “Being addressed thus, Viśravā, the Brahmarṣi, the best of sages, told the lord of wealth, who was standing with joined palms, ‘My son, listen to my words. (37)

verses.text:
दशग्रीवो महाबाहुरुक्तवान् मम संनिधौ।
मया निर्भर्त्सितश्चासीद् बहुशोक्तः सुदुर्मतिः॥ ३८॥
स क्रोधेन मया चोक्तो ध्वंससे च पुनः पुनः।
श्रेयोऽभियुक्तं धर्म्यं च शृणु पुत्र वचो मम॥ ३९॥
verses.m: ‘Daśagrīva, the mighty-armed, said the same thing in my presence also. I rebuked him and exhorted that highly evil-minded fellow in several ways. In anger I repeatedly said, You shall be destroyed. Son, listen to my words which will do you good and which are consonant with Dharma. (38-39)

verses.text:
वरप्रदानसम्मूढो मान्यामान्यं सुदुर्मतिः।
न वेत्ति मम शापाच्च प्रकृतिं दारुणां गतः॥ ४०॥
verses.m: ‘This most evil-minded fellow, deluded as he is by the boons that have been granted to him, does not distinguish between people to be respected and those not to be respected. Again, by my curse he is evil-minded by nature. (40)

verses.text:
तस्माद् गच्छ महाबाहो कैलासं धरणीधरम्।
निवेशय निवासार्थं त्यक्त्वा लङ्कां सहानुगः॥ ४१॥
verses.m: ‘Hence, O mighty-armed one, leave Laṅkā and proceed to Mount Kailāsa with your followers and people it for your residence. (41)

verses.text:
तत्र मन्दाकिनी रम्या नदीनामुत्तमा नदी।
काञ्चनैः सूर्यसंकाशैः पङ्कजैः संवृतोदका॥ ४२॥
कुमुदैरुत्पलैश्चैव अन्यैश्चैव सुगन्धिभिः।
तत्र देवाः सगन्धर्वाः साप्सरोरगकिंनराः॥ ४३॥
विहारशीलाः सततं रमन्ते सर्वदाश्रिताः।
नहि क्षमं तवानेन वैरं धनद रक्षसा॥ ४४॥
जानीषे हि यथानेन लब्धः परमको वरः॥ ४५॥
verses.m: ‘The Mandākinī, the best of rivers, whose waters are covered all over with lotus flowers of golden hue and bright like the sun, as also with white water-lilies, blue lotuses and other flowers of sweet fragrance, flows there. Gods with Gandharvas, Apsarās, Nāgas and Kinnaras, all of a sportive nature, always resort to that place and constantly revel there. Since you know how he (Daśagrīva) has obtained an excellent boon, it is not advisable for you to antagonize him.’ (42—45)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तो गृहीत्वा तु तद्वचः पितृगौरवात्।
सदारपुत्रः सामात्यः सवाहनधनो गतः॥ ४६॥
verses.m: Told thus and following his advice out of respect for his father, Kubera left the place with his wife and sons, his ministers, his vehicles and his wealth. (46)

verses.text:
प्रहस्तोऽथ दशग्रीवं गत्वा वचनमब्रवीत्।
प्रहृष्टात्मा महात्मानं सहामात्यं सहानुजम्॥ ४७॥
शून्या सा नगरी लङ्का त्यक्त्वैनां धनदो गतः।
प्रविश्य तां सहास्माभिः स्वधर्मं तत्र पालय॥ ४८॥
verses.m: “Prahasta, overjoyed, sought the mighty Daśagrīva, who was being attended by his ministers and brothers and said, ‘Kubera has left the city of Laṅkā and has gone away. It is now vacant. Entering it now in our company, discharge your duty there.’ ” (47-48)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तो दशग्रीवः प्रहस्तेन महाबलः।
विवेश नगरीं लङ्कां भ्रातृभिः सबलानुगैः॥ ४९॥
verses.m: Told thus by Prahasta, Rāvaṇa of great strength entered Laṅkā alongwith his brothers, forces and other followers. (49)

verses.text:
धनदेन परित्यक्तां सुविभक्तमहापथाम्।
आरुरोह स देवारिः स्वर्गं देवाधिपो यथा॥ ५०॥
verses.m: That enemy of the gods stepped into Laṅkā—whose main streets were well laid out, and which had been evacuated by the god of riches—just as Indra ascended heaven. (50)

verses.text:
स चाभिषिक्तः क्षणदाचरैस्तदा
निवेशयामास पुरीं दशाननः।
निकामपूर्णा च बभूव सा पुरी
निशाचरैर्नीलबलाहकोपमैः ॥ ५१॥
verses.m: Consecrated by the Rākṣasas as its ruler, Daśagrīva peopled that city. It was soon filled to capacity with Rākṣasas, dark as clouds. (51)

verses.text:
धनेश्वरस्त्वथ पितृवाक्यगौरवा-
न्न्यवेशयच्छशिविमले गिरौ पुरीम्।
स्वलंकृतैर्भवनवरैर्विभूषितां
पुरंदरस्येव तदाऽमरावतीम्॥ ५२॥
verses.m: Out of respect for his father’s word, Kubera built on the hill, white as the moon, a city adorned with well-decorated mansions even as Indra laid out Amarāvatī in heaven. (52)

verses.text:
राक्षसेन्द्रोऽभिषिक्तस्तु भ्रातृभिः सहितस्तदा।
ततः प्रदानं राक्षस्या भगिन्याः समचिन्तयत्॥ १॥
verses.m: “After his consecration as the ruler of Laṅkā, Rāvaṇa took counsel with his brothers regarding the marriage of his sister, a Rākṣasī. (1)

verses.text:
स्वसारं कालकेयाय दानवेन्द्राय राक्षसीम्।
ददौ शूर्पणखां नाम विद्युज्जिह्वाय राक्षसः॥ २॥
verses.m: “The Rākṣasa gave away his sister, the ogress Śūrpaṇakhā in marriage to Vidyujjihva, chief of the Dānavas and son of Kālakā. (2)

verses.text:
अथ दत्त्वा स्वयं रक्षो मृगयामटते स्म तत्।
तत्रापश्यत् ततो राम मयं नाम दितेः सुतम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “After giving her away, the Rākṣasa went about sporting in the forest and saw there, O Rāma, Maya, son of Diti. (3)

verses.text:
कन्यासहायं तं दृष्ट्वा दशग्रीवो निशाचरः।
अपृच्छत् को भवानेको निर्मनुष्यमृगे वने॥ ४॥
अनया मृगशावाक्ष्या किमर्थं सह तिष्ठसि।
मयस्तदाब्रवीद् राम पृच्छन्तं तं निशाचरम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Seeing him accompanied by his daughter, Daśagrīva, the Rākṣasa, inquired of him: ‘Who are you and why do you stay in this forest, devoid of human beings and animals, in the company of this girl whose eyes resemble a doe’s?’ O Rāma, Maya then replied to the inquisitive Rākṣasa: (4-5)

verses.text:
श्रूयतां सर्वमाख्यास्ये यथावृत्तमिदं तव।
हेमा नामाप्सरास्तात श्रुतपूर्वा यदि त्वया॥ ६॥
verses.m: ‘I will narrate all the events as they took place. Please listen. There was an Apsarā by name Hemā. You might have heard of her. (6)

verses.text:
दैवतैर्मम सा दत्ता पौलोमीव शतक्रतोः।
तस्यां सक्तमना ह्यासं दशवर्षशतान्यहम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: ‘Just as Paulomi, the daughter of Pulomā, was given in marriage to Indra, even so Hemā was given to me by the gods in marriage. I was deeply attached to her and lived with her for thousands of years. (7)

verses.text:
सा च दैवतकार्येण गता वर्षाश्चतुर्दश।
तस्याः कृते च हेमायाः सर्वं हेममयं पुरम्॥ ८॥
वज्रवैदूर्यचित्रं च मायया निर्मितं मया।
तत्राहमवसं दीनस्तया हीनः सुदुःखितः॥ ९॥
verses.m: ‘It is now fourteen years since she departed to serve the purpose of the gods. For the sake of Hemā, I created this city entirely made of gold by my magical powers and decked it with diamonds and cat’s-eye gems. Bereaved of her, I lived there, dispirited and extremely desolate. (8-9)

verses.text:
तस्माद् पुराद् दुहितरं गृहीत्वा वनमागतः।
इयं ममात्मजा राजंस्तस्याः कुक्षौ विवर्धिता॥ १०॥
verses.m: ‘From that city I came to the forest taking my daughter with me, O king. This is my daughter who grew in her (Hemā’s) womb. (10)

verses.text:
भर्तारमनया सार्धमस्याः प्राप्तोऽस्मि मार्गितुम्।
कन्यापितृत्वं दुःखं हि सर्वेषां मानकांक्षिणाम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: ‘I have come in her company in search of a husband for her; for, to be the father of an unmarried girl is a headache to all parents who hanker after reputation. (11)

verses.text:
कन्या हि द्वे कुले नित्यं संशये स्थाप्य तिष्ठति।
पुत्रद्वयं ममाप्यस्यां भार्यायां सम्बभूव ह॥ १२॥
verses.m: ‘An unmarried girl throws into jeopardy the reputation of two families. Of her (Hemā) two sons, too, were born to me. (12)

verses.text:
मायावी प्रथमस्तात दुन्दुभिस्तदनन्तरः।
एवं ते सर्वमाख्यातं याथातथ्येन पृच्छतः॥ १३॥
verses.m: ‘Of them Māyāvī was the first and Dundubhi, the second. To you who have questioned me, O dear one, I have narrated everything exactly according to facts. (13)

verses.text:
त्वामिदानीं कथं तात जानीयां को भवानिति।
एवमुक्तं तु तद् रक्षो विनीतमिदमब्रवीत्॥ १४॥
अहं पौलस्त्यतनयो दशग्रीवश्च नामतः।
मुनेर्विश्रवसो यस्तु तृतीयो ब्रह्मणोऽभवत्॥ १५॥
verses.m: ‘Now, how can I know you? Who are you?’ “Questioned thus, the Rākṣasa humbly said: ‘I am a grandson of Pulastya and a son of sage Viśravā, who is third in descent from Brahmā himself. I go by the name of Daśagrīva.’ (14-15)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तदा राम राक्षसेन्द्रेण दानवः।
महर्षेस्तनयं ज्ञात्वा मयो हर्षमुपागतः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Spoken to thus, O Rāma, by the lord of the Rākṣasas and coming to know that he was a son of an eminent sage, Viśravā, Maya, the Dānava, became glad. (16)

verses.text:
दातुं दुहितरं तस्मै रोचयामास तत्र वै।
करेण तु करं तस्या ग्राहयित्वा मयस्तदा॥ १७॥
प्रहसन् प्राह दैत्येन्द्रो राक्षसेन्द्रमिदं वचः।
इयं ममात्मजा राजन् हेमयाप्सरसा धृता॥ १८॥
कन्या मन्दोदरी नाम पत्न्यर्थं प्रतिगृह्यताम्।
बाढमित्येव तं राम दशग्रीवोऽभ्यभाषत॥ १९॥
verses.m: Even in that place he resolved to give his daughter to him. Causing her hand to be grasped by his, Maya, the chief of the Daityas, addressed the following words to the chief of the Rākṣasas loudly laughing: ‘O king, this my daughter, was brought up by Hemā, the Apsarā; the name of the maiden is Mandodarī; have her as your wife. To him, O Rāma, Daśagrīva said, ‘All right’. (17—19)

verses.text:
प्रज्वाल्य तत्र चैवाग्निमकरोत् पाणिसंग्रहम्।
स हि तस्य मयो राम शापाभिज्ञस्तपोधनात्॥ २०॥
विदित्वा तेन सा दत्ता तस्य पैतामहं कुलम्।
अमोघां तस्य शक्तिं च प्रददौ परमाद्भुताम्॥ २१॥
परेण तपसा लब्धां जघ्निवाँल्लक्ष्मणं यया।
एवं स कृत्वा दारान् वै लङ्काया ईश्वरः प्रभुः॥ २२॥
गत्वा तु नगरीं भार्ये भ्रातृभ्यां समुपाहरत्।
वैरोचनस्य दौहित्रीं वज्रज्वालेति नामतः॥ २३॥
तां भार्यां कुम्भकर्णस्य रावणः समकल्पयत्।
गन्धर्वराजस्य सुतां शैलूषस्य महात्मनः॥ २४॥
सरमां नाम धर्मज्ञां लेभे भार्यां विभीषणः।
तीरे तु सरसो वै तु संजज्ञे मानसस्य हि॥ २५॥
verses.m: ‘Then kindling a fire, he married her.’ “Though Maya knew that he (Daśagrīva) was under a curse from Viśravā (who was rich in austerities), still, he gave his daughter knowing as he did his descent from Brahmā (the grandfather of the universe). Maya also gave him a most wonderful and infallible javelin obtained by him through hard Tapas and with this he struck Lakṣmaṇa. Having thus married, the mighty lord of Laṅkā went to his city and secured a wife each for his (two) brothers, Rāvaṇa decided upon the grand-daughter (daughter’s daughter) of Bali (son of Virocana), Vajrajwālā by name, as the wife of Kumbhakarṇa. Vibhīṣaṇa obtained as his wife, Saramā, daughter of the noble Gandharva king, Śailūṣa, who knew what is right. She was born on the bank of the Mānasa lake. (20—25)

verses.text:
सरस्तदा मानसं तु ववृधे जलदागमे।
मात्रा तु तस्याः कन्यायाः स्नेहेनाक्रन्दितं वचः॥ २६॥
सरो मा वर्धयस्वेति ततः सा सरमाभवत्।
एवं ते कृतदारा वै रेमिरे तत्र राक्षसाः॥ २७॥
स्वां स्वां भार्यामुपादाय गन्धर्वा इव नन्दने।
ततो मन्दोदरी पुत्रं मेघनादमजीजनत्॥ २८॥
verses.m: “The Mānasa lake was then swelling due to the monsoon. ‘O lake, do not overflow’, (सरो मा वर्धयत) cried the mother of that child out of affection. Hence her child came to be known as Saramā. Having thus married, the three Rākṣasas spent a pleasant time there each in the company of his wife, even as the Gandharvas did in the Nandana grove (the pleasure-garden of Indra). Then Mandodarī gave birth to her son, Meghanāda. (26—28)

verses.text:
स एष इन्द्रजिन्नाम युष्माभिरभिधीयते।
जातमात्रेण हि पुरा तेन रावणसूनुना॥ २९॥
रुदता सुमहान् मुक्तो नादो जलधरोपमः।
जडीकृता च सा लङ्का तस्य नादेन राघव॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “He is the same who is called Indrajit by all of you. Crying as soon as he was born, this son of Rāvaṇa, made a great noise resembling the rumbling of clouds. Laṅkā was stunned by his roar, O Rāghava! (29-30)

verses.text:
पिता तस्याकरोन्नाम मेघनाद इति स्वयम्।
सोऽवर्धत तदा राम रावणान्तःपुरे शुभे॥ ३१॥
रक्ष्यमाणो वरस्त्रीभिश्छन्नः काष्ठैरिवानलः।
मातापित्रोर्महाहर्षं जनयन् रावणात्मजः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Hence his father himself named him Meghanāda. Causing great delight to his mother and father, and being well taken care of by excellent women, that son of Rāvaṇa grew up in the beautiful gynaeceum of Rāvaṇa, O Rāma, like fire concealed under pieces of wood.” (31-32)

verses.text:
अथ लोकेश्वरोत्सृष्टा तत्र कालेन केनचित्।
निद्रा समभवत् तीव्रा कुम्भकर्णस्य रूपिणी॥ १॥
verses.m: “Now after sometime deep sleep, as sent by Brahmā (the lord of the universe), seized Kumbhakarṇa in the form of yawning etc., in Laṅkā. (1)

verses.text:
ततो भ्रातरमासीनं कुम्भकर्णोऽब्रवीद् वचः।
निद्रा मां बाधते राजन् कारयस्व ममालयम्॥ २॥
verses.m: “Thereupon Kumbhakarṇa spoke as follows to his elder brother, who was seated beside him: ‘O king, sleep is troubling me; have a mansion built for me.’ (2)

verses.text:
विनियुक्तास्ततो राज्ञा शिल्पिनो विश्वकर्मवत्।
विस्तीर्णं योजनं स्निग्धं ततो द्विगुणमायतम्॥ ३॥
दर्शनीयं निराबाधं कुम्भकर्णस्य चक्रिरे।
स्फाटिकैः काञ्चनैश्चित्रैः स्तम्भैः सर्वत्र शोभितम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Ordered by the king, architects as good as Viśwakarmā (the architect of gods) built for Kumbhakarṇa a lovely mansion, one Yojana (ten miles) in width and twice as much in length. It had a beautiful appearance and was free from disturbance. It was adorned on all sides with lovely columns of crystal, as well as of gold. (3-4)

verses.text:
वैदूर्यकृतसोपानं किङ्किणीजालकं तथा।
दान्ततोरणविन्यस्तं वज्रस्फटिकवेदिकम्॥ ५॥
मनोहरं सर्वसुखं कारयामास राक्षसः।
सर्वत्र सुखदं नित्यं मेरोः पुण्यां गुहामिव॥ ६॥
verses.m: “The stairways were made of cat’s-eye gems. Its lattice windows were fringed with tiny bells. Its portals were made of ivory. It contained daises built of crystal and diamond. It was not only soul-captivating but the Rākṣasa (Rāvaṇa) provided it with all amenities and made every part of it comfortable in all seasons. It resembled a holy cave of Mount Meru. (5-6)

verses.text:
तत्र निद्रां समाविष्टः कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः।
बहून्यब्दसहस्राणि शयानो न च बुध्यते॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Buried in slumber, the very mighty Kumbhakarṇa lay asleep there, and did not wake up for many thousand years. (7)

verses.text:
निद्राभिभूते तु तदा कुम्भकर्णे दशाननः।
देवर्षियक्षगन्धर्वान् संजघ्ने हि निरङ्कुशः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “While Kumbhakarṇa was thus overpowered by sleep, Daśānana destroyed the gods, the Ṛṣis, the Yakṣas and the Gandharvas without restraint of any kind. (8)

verses.text:
उद्यानानि विचित्राणि नन्दनादीनि यानि च।
तानि गत्वा सुसंक्रुद्धो भिनत्ति स्म दशाननः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “The highly enraged Daśānana overran the Nandana grove (the pleasure-garden of Indra) and other beautiful gardens and laid them waste. (9)

verses.text:
नदीं गज इव क्रीडन् वृक्षान् वायुरिव क्षिपन्।
नगान् वज्र इवोत्सृष्टो विध्वंसयति राक्षसः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Like an elephant at play, the Rākṣasa dissipated the waters of rivers, broke trees as a tempest, and cleaved mountains like the thunderbolt of Indra. (10)

verses.text:
तथावृत्तं तु विज्ञाय दशग्रीवं धनेश्वरः।
कुलानुरूपं धर्मज्ञो वृत्तं संस्मृत्य चात्मनः॥ ११॥
सौभ्रात्रदर्शनार्थं तु दूतं वैश्रवणस्तदा।
लङ्कां सम्प्रेषयामास दशग्रीवस्य वै हितम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Coming to know of the misdeeds of Daśagrīva, and bearing in mind the conduct befitting his family, Vaiśravaṇa, who knew what is right, sent a messenger to Laṅkā to show his brotherly love and specially to promote the good of Rāvaṇa. (11-12)

verses.text:
स गत्वा नगरीं लङ्कामाससाद विभीषणम्।
मानितस्तेन धर्मेण पृष्टश्चागमनं प्रति॥ १३॥
पृष्ट्वा च कुशलं राज्ञो ज्ञातीनां च विभीषणः।
सभायां दर्शयामास तमासीनं दशाननम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Reaching the city of Laṅkā, he (the messenger) went up to Vibhīṣaṇa, who welcomed him according to the rules of propriety, made inquiries regarding his visit, the king (Kubera) and his kinsfolk, asked him the reason for his coming and then showed him Daśānana who was sitting in the assembly. (13-14)

verses.text:
स दृष्ट्वा तत्र राजानं दीप्यमानं स्वतेजसा।
जयेति वाचा सम्पूज्य तूष्णीं समभिवर्तत॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Seeing the king there, effulgent in his own lustre, he greeted him in the words ‘Be victorious!’ and then stood silent. (15)

verses.text:
स तत्रोत्तमपर्यङ्के वरास्तरणशोभिते।
उपविष्टं दशग्रीवं दूतो वाक्यमथाब्रवीत्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Then addressing Daśagrīva, who was seated on an excellent couch overspread with beautiful bedsheets, the messenger spoke the following words: (16)

verses.text:
राजन् वदामि ते सर्वं भ्राता तव यदब्रवीत्।
उभयोः सदृशं वीर वृत्तस्य च कुलस्य च॥ १७॥
verses.m: “ ‘O king, I will tell you all that your brother has said. It is in keeping with good conduct and the traditions of the family. (17)

verses.text:
साधु पर्याप्तमेतावत् कृत्यश्चारित्रसंग्रहः।
साधु धर्मे व्यवस्थानं क्रियतां यदि शक्यते॥ १८॥
verses.m: “ ‘Quite enough of what you have done so long; establish yourself fully, if possible, in better ways. (18)

verses.text:
दृष्टं मे नन्दनं भग्नमृषयो निहताः श्रुताः।
देवतानां समुद्योगस्त्वत्तो राजन् मया श्रुतः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “ ‘I have seen the Nandana grove, the pleasure-garden of Indra, laid waste by you. I have heard of the Ṛṣis who were killed by you. I have also heard of the preparations of the gods against you. (19)

verses.text:
निराकृतश्च बहुशस्त्वयाहं राक्षसाधिप।
सापराधोऽपि बालो हि रक्षितव्यः स्वबान्धवैः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “ ‘O leader of the Rākṣasas, you have repeatedly disregarded me; still it is the duty of relations to save the youngsters even though they misbehave. (20)

verses.text:
अहं तु हिमवत्पृष्ठं गतो धर्ममुपासितुम्।
रौद्रं व्रतं समास्थाय नियतो नियतेन्द्रियः॥ २१॥
verses.m: “ ‘Having undertaken to observe in pursuance of Dharma, a rather fierce vow, I once went to the slopes of the Himālayas with my mind and senses fully under control. (21)

verses.text:
तत्र देवो मया दृष्ट उमया सहितः प्रभुः।
सव्यं चक्षुर्मया दैवात् तत्र देव्यां निपातितम्॥ २२॥
का न्वेषेति महाराज न खल्वन्येन हेतुना।
रूपं चानुपमं कृत्वा रुद्राणी तत्र तिष्ठति॥ २३॥
verses.m: “ ‘There I happened to see the almighty Lord Śiva in the company of Umā. Rudrāṇī (the consort of Rudra) stood there, in her incomparable charm. By chance I cast my left eye on the Devī; my object, O monarch, was just to know who she was and nothing else. (22-23)

verses.text:
देव्या दिव्यप्रभावेण दग्धं सव्यं ममेक्षणम्।
रेणुध्वस्तामिव ज्योतिः पिङ्गलत्वमुपागतम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: “ ‘My left eye got scorched, while the other assumed a grey colour as though soiled by dust, through the supernatural powers of the Devī. (24)

verses.text:
ततोऽहमन्यद् विस्तीर्णं गत्वा तस्य गिरेस्तटम्।
तूष्णीं वर्षशतान्यष्टौ समधारं महाव्रतम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: “ ‘Then I went to another spacious plateau of the Himālayas and observed silently the great vow for eight hundred years. (25)

verses.text:
समाप्ते नियमे तस्मिंस्तत्र देवो महेश्वरः।
ततः प्रीतेन मनसा प्राह वाक्यमिदं प्रभुः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “ ‘When I had completed the observance of that vow, the great Lord Śiva appeared there and, pleased at heart, addressed the following words to me: (26)

verses.text:
प्रीतोऽस्मि तव धर्मज्ञ तपसानेन सुव्रत।
मया चैतद् व्रतं चीर्णं त्वया चैव धनाधिप॥ २७॥
verses.m: “ ‘O Suvrata (one who has successfully observed a vow) and Dharmajña (one who knows Dharma), I am pleased with the Tapas that you have just performed. This was first observed by me and again by you, O lord of riches! (27)

verses.text:
तृतीयः पुरुषो नास्ति यश्चरेद् व्रतमीदृशम्।
व्रतं सुदुष्करं ह्येतन्मयैवोत्पादितं पुरा॥ २८॥
verses.m: “ ‘There is no third person who can observe such a vow. I originated this vow in the past. It is very difficult to observe. (28)

verses.text:
तत्सखित्वं मया सौम्य रोचयस्व धनेश्वर।
तपसा निर्जितश्चैव सखा भव ममानघ॥ २९॥
verses.m: “ ‘Therefore, be pleased to make friends with me, O lord of wealth; I have been conquered by you through your austerities, O sinless one. (29)

verses.text:
देव्या दग्धं प्रभावेण यच्च सव्यं तवेक्षणम्।
पैङ्गल्यं यदवाप्तं हि देव्या रूपनिरीक्षणात्॥ ३०॥
एकाक्षपिङ्गलीत्येव नाम स्थास्यति शाश्वतम्।
एवं तेन सखित्वं च प्राप्यानुज्ञां च शङ्करात्॥ ३१॥
आगतेन मया चैवं श्रुतस्ते पापनिश्चयः।
तदधर्मिष्ठसंयोगान्निवर्त कुलदूषणात्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “ ‘Since your left eye was burnt and the other was turned grey by the supernatural powers of the Devī for just gazing on her beauty, you will be known as Ekākṣapiṅgalī (one who has his one eye turned grey) forever. When having thus secured friendship with Lord Śaṅkara and obtained his leave, I returned, I heard of your sinful resolve. Therefore refrain from this unrighteous conduct which tarnishes the reputation of the family. (30—32)

verses.text:
चिन्त्यते हि वधोपायः सर्षिसङ्घैः सुरैस्तव।
एवमुक्तो दशग्रीवः कोपसंरक्तलोचनः॥ ३३॥
हस्तान् दन्तांश्च सम्पिष्य वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह।
विज्ञातं ते मया दूत वाक्यं यत् त्वं प्रभाषसे॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “ ‘The gods alongwith the hosts of Ṛṣis are considering the way of encompassing your destruction.’ Hearing these words, Daśagrīva wrung his hands and ground his teeth and, his eyes red with anger, spoke as follows: ‘O messenger, I understand the words which you utter. (33-34)

verses.text:
नैव त्वमसि नैवासौ भ्रात्रा येनासि चोदितः।
हितं नैष ममैतद्धि ब्रवीति धनरक्षकः॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “ ‘You will not live nor that brother by whom you have been ordered to speak thus. What the lord of wealth says is not to my good. (35)

verses.text:
महेश्वरसखित्वं तु मूढः श्रावयते किल।
नैवेदं क्षमणीयं मे यदेतद् भाषितं त्वया॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “ ‘That fool evidently tells me of his friendship with Lord Maheśwara. I will not tolerate what you have said. (36)

verses.text:
यदेतावन्मया कालं दूत तस्य तु मर्षितम्।
न हन्तव्यो गुरुर्ज्येष्ठो मयायमिति मन्यते॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “ ‘In the belief that an elder brother is not to be killed, I have put up with all the insults that he has heaped on me, O envoy! (37)

verses.text:
तस्य त्विदानीं श्रुत्वा मे वाक्यमेषा कृता मतिः।
त्रीँल्लोकानपि जेष्यामि बाहुवीर्यमुपाश्रितः॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “ ‘But after hearing these words of his, I have made up my mind to conquer all the three worlds relying on the strength of my arms. (38)

verses.text:
एतन्मुहूर्तमेवाहं तस्यैकस्य तु वै कृते।
चतुरो लोकपालांस्तान् नयिष्यामि यमक्षयम्॥ ३९॥
verses.m: “ ‘This very moment I will send the four Dikpālas (guardians of the four directions) to the abode of Yama just on his account.’ (39)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा तु लङ्केशो दूतं खड्गेन जघ्निवान्।
ददौ भक्षयितुं ह्येनं राक्षसानां दुरात्मनाम्॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “Saying this, the lord of Laṅkā struck down the messenger with his sword and gave the corpse to be eaten by evil-minded Rākṣasas. (40)

verses.text:
ततः कृतस्वस्त्ययनो रथमारुह्य रावणः।
त्रैलोक्यविजयाकांक्षी ययौ यत्र धनेश्वरः॥ ४१॥
verses.m: “Then, after getting Brāhmaṇas to read out benedictory hymns after presentation of offerings with a view to conquering the three worlds, Rāvaṇa ascended his chariot and drove to the abode of the lord of wealth.” (41)

verses.text:
ततः स सचिवैः सार्धं षड्भिर्नित्यबलोद्धतः।
महोदरप्रहस्ताभ्यां मारीचशुकसारणैः॥ १॥
धूम्राक्षेण च वीरेण नित्यं समरगर्द्धिना।
वृतः सम्प्रययौ श्रीमान् क्रोधाल्लोकान् दहन्निव॥ २॥
verses.m: “Accompanied and surrounded by his six ministers—Mahodara and Prahasta, Mārīca, Śuka, Sāraṇa and the hero Dhūmrākṣa, who ever thirsted for battle the glorious Rāvaṇa, who was always proud of his might, set out as if to consume the worlds with his anger. (1-2)

verses.text:
पुराणि स नदीः शैलान् वनान्युपवनानि च।
अतिक्रम्य मुहूर्तेन कैलासं गिरिमागमत्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Marching across cities, rivers, hills, forests and groves, he reached Mount Kailāsa in an hour or so. (3)

verses.text:
संनिविष्टं गिरौ तस्मिन् राक्षसेन्द्रं निशम्य तु।
युद्धेप्सुं तं कृतोत्साहं दुरात्मानं समन्त्रिणम्॥ ४॥
यक्षा न शेकुः संस्थातुं प्रमुखे तस्य रक्षसः।
राज्ञो भ्रातेति विज्ञाय गता यत्र धनेश्वरः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Hearing of the wicked king of the Rākṣasas encamped on the mountain with his ministers, eager for battle and active, the Yakṣas were unable to make a stand against the ogre, knowing that he was a brother of the lord of wealth, they sought the abode of the latter. (4-5)

verses.text:
ते गत्वा सर्वमाचख्युर्भ्रातुस्तस्य चिकीर्षितम्।
अनुज्ञाता ययुर्हृष्टा युद्धाय धनदेन ते॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Going to him, they told him all about the intentions of his brother. Permitted by the lord of wealth, they set out joyously to give battle. (6)

verses.text:
ततो बलानां संक्षोभो व्यवर्धत इवोदधेः।
तस्य नैर्ऋतराजस्य शैलं संचालयन्निव॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Then there arose an excitement in the forces of the king of the Nairṛtas. It was like the agitation of the sea and it seemed to shake the hill. (7)

verses.text:
ततो युद्धं समभवद् यक्षराक्षससंकुलम्।
व्यथिताश्चाभवंस्तत्र सचिवा राक्षसस्य ते॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Between the Yakṣas and the Rākṣasas then started a thick fight in which the said ministers of the Rākṣasa felt alarmed. (8)

verses.text:
स दृष्ट्वा तादृशं सैन्यं दशग्रीवो निशाचरः।
हर्षनादान् बहून् कृत्वा स क्रोधादभ्यधावत॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Seeing his army in that plight, the Rākṣasa, Daśagrīva, rushed out in anger raising many shouts of encouragement. (9)

verses.text:
ये तु ते राक्षसेन्द्रस्य सचिवा घोरविक्रमाः।
तेषां सहस्रमेकैको यक्षाणां समयोधयत्॥ १०॥
verses.m: “The ministers of the king of the Rākṣasas were terribly valiant. Each one of them for his part fought with a thousand Yakṣas. (10)

verses.text:
ततो गदाभिर्मुसलैरसिभिः शक्तितोमरैः।
हन्यमानो दशग्रीवस्तत्सैन्यं समगाहत॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Under an attack of clubs, pestles, swords, javelins and iron clubs, Rāvaṇa entered the enemy’s army. (11)

verses.text:
स निरुच्छ्वासवत् तत्र वध्यमानो दशाननः।
वर्षद्भिरिव जीमूतैर्धाराभिरवरुध्यत॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Being struck with volleys of arrows by the Yakṣas as though with torrents of raining clouds, Daśānana was held up and was unable even to breathe, as it were. (12)

verses.text:
न चकार व्यथां चैव यक्षशस्त्रैः समाहतः।
महीधर इवाम्भोदैर्धाराशतसमुक्षितः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Just as a mountain is not shaken even though drenched by clouds with hundreds of torrents, even so he (Daśagrīva) did not feel tormented though wounded by the weapons shot by the Yakṣas. (13)

verses.text:
स महात्मा समुद्यम्य कालदण्डोपमां गदाम्।
प्रविवेश ततः सैन्यं नयन् यक्षान् यमक्षयम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Lifting up a club, resembling the rod of Death (Kāladaṇḍa), the gigantic Daśagrīva thereupon entered the army, dispatching the Yakṣas to the abode of Yama. (14)

verses.text:
स कक्षमिव विस्तीर्णं शुष्केन्धनमिवाकुलम्।
वातेनाग्निरिवादीप्तो यक्षसैन्यं ददाह तत्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Like a fire ablaze on account of the wind, he burnt the aforesaid army of the Yakṣas, which was spread out as grass and concentrated like dried wood. (15)

verses.text:
तैस्तु तत्र महामात्यैर्महोदरशुकादिभिः।
अल्पावशेषास्ते यक्षाः कृता वातैरिवाम्बुदाः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “By those great ministers, Mahodara, Śuka and others, the Yakṣas were reduced largely in number even as clouds are dispersed by the winds. (16)

verses.text:
केचित् समाहता भग्नाः पतिताः समरे क्षितौ।
ओष्ठांश्च दशनैस्तीक्ष्णैरदशन् कुपिता रणे॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Some of them, badly mutilated when struck in the battle, fell on the ground, while others in anger bit their lips with their sharp teeth on the battlefield. (17)

verses.text:
श्रान्ताश्चान्योन्यमालिङ्ग्य भ्रष्टशस्त्रा रणाजिरे।
सीदन्ति च तदा यक्षाः कूला इव जलेन ह॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Just like the bank of a river eroded by water, some of the Yakṣas, exhausted and embracing one another, sank down on the battlefield, their weapons fallen down. (18)

verses.text:
हतानां गच्छतां स्वर्गं युध्यतामथ धावताम्।
प्रेक्षतामृषिसङ्घानां न बभूवान्तरं दिवि॥ १९॥
verses.m: “The atmosphere was thickly crowded with those who, having lost their lives, were proceeding to heaven, with those who were still fighting, with those who were running away and with the host of Ṛṣis witnessing the fight. (19)

verses.text:
भग्नांस्तु तान् समालक्ष्य यक्षेन्द्रांस्तु महाबलान्।
धनाध्यक्षो महाबाहुः प्रेषयामास यक्षकान्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Seeing those exceptionally mighty leaders of the Yakṣas put to flight, the mighty-armed lord of wealth sent other mighty Yakṣas. (20)

verses.text:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे राम विस्तीर्णबलवाहनः।
प्रेषितो न्यपतद् यक्षो नाम्ना संयोधकण्टकः॥ २१॥
verses.m: “In the meantime, O Rāma, a Yakṣa, Saṁyodhakaṇṭaka by name, with a huge army and a vast number of mounts and vehicles, sallied forth having been sent by the lord of wealth. (21)

verses.text:
तेन चक्रेण मारीचो विष्णुनेव रणे हतः।
पतितो भूतले शैलात् क्षीणपुण्य इव ग्रहः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Struck by him in battle with a discus as by Lord Viṣṇu, Mārīca fell on the ground from the mountain like a star when the merit responsible for its stay in heaven is exhausted. (22)

verses.text:
ससंज्ञस्तु मुहूर्तेन स विश्रम्य निशाचरः।
तं यक्षं योधयामास स च भग्नः प्रदुद्रुवे॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Recovering his consciousness in an hour or so, and having rested awhile, that Rākṣasa fought once more the aforesaid Yakṣa, who having been defeated, took to his heels. (23)

verses.text:
ततः काञ्चनचित्राङ्गं वैदूर्यरजतोक्षितम्।
मर्यादां प्रतिहाराणां तोरणान्तरमाविशत्॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Then Rāvaṇa entered the portals plated all over with gold and inlaid with cat’s-eye gems and silver and which marked the last line guarded by gate-keepers. (24)

verses.text:
तं तु राजन् दशग्रीवं प्रविशन्तं निशाचरम्।
सूर्यभानुरिति ख्यातो द्वारपालो न्यवारयत्॥ २५॥
verses.m: “A gate-keeper, Sūryabhānu by name, stopped Daśagrīva, the Rākṣasa, while he was entering the portal. (25)

verses.text:
स वार्यमाणो यक्षेण प्रविवेश निशाचरः।
यदा तु वारितो राम न व्यतिष्ठत् स राक्षसः॥ २६॥
ततस्तोरणमुत्पाट्य तेन यक्षेण ताडितः।
रुधिरं प्रस्रवन् भाति शैलो धातुस्रवैरिव॥ २७॥
verses.m: “The Rākṣasa, however, made good his entry though stopped by the Yakṣa. When, however, O Rāma, the Rākṣasa did not stop, though prevented by the Yakṣa, he was then struck by the Yakṣa, with a post which he pulled out from the portal. Bleeding profusely, Daśagrīva looked like a hill with streams of molten ochre flowing from it. (26-27)

verses.text:
स शैलशिखराभेण तोरणेन समाहतः।
जगाम न क्षतिं वीरो वरदानात् स्वयम्भुवः॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Though struck with the door-post resembling the crest of a hill, the hero (Daśagrīva) could not be slain, thanks to the boons granted to him by Brahmā (the self-born creator). (28)

verses.text:
तेनैव तोरणेनाथ यक्षस्तेनाभिताडितः।
नादृश्यत तदा यक्षो भस्मीकृततनुस्तदा॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Struck back with the same door-post by him, the Yakṣa was seen no more, his body having been reduced to powder. (29)

verses.text:
ततः प्रदुद्रुवुः सर्वे दृष्ट्वा रक्षःपराक्रमम्।
ततो नदीर्गुहाश्चैव विविशुर्भयपीडिताः।
त्यक्तप्रहरणाः श्रान्ता विवर्णवदनास्तदा॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Seeing the might of the Rākṣasa, all began to run. Exhausted and pale, stricken with fear as they were, they threw away their weapons and entered the rivers or the caves.” (30)

verses.text:
ततस्ताँल्लक्ष्य वित्रस्तान् यक्षेन्द्रांश्च सहस्रशः।
धनाध्यक्षो महायक्षं माणिभद्रमथाब्रवीत्॥ १॥
रावणं जहि यक्षेन्द्र दुर्वृत्तं पापचेतसम्।
शरणं भव वीराणां यक्षाणां युद्धशालिनाम्॥ २॥
एवमुक्तो महाबाहुर्माणिभद्रः सुदुर्जयः।
वृतो यक्षसहस्रैस्तु चतुर्भिः समयोधयत्॥ ३॥
ते गदामुसलप्रासैः शक्तितोमरमुद्गरैः।
अभिघ्नन्तस्तदा यक्षा राक्षसान् समुपाद्रवन्॥ ४॥
कुर्वन्तस्तुमुलं युद्धं चरन्तः श्येनवल्लघु।
बाढं प्रयच्छ नेच्छामि दीयतामिति भाषिणः॥ ५॥
ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वा ऋषयो ब्रह्मवादिनः।
दृष्ट्वा तत् तुमुलं युद्धं परं विस्मयमागमन्॥ ६॥
verses.m: Then the gods, Gandharvas and Ṛṣis who were exponents of the Vedas, were greatly surprised to witness that fierce fight. (6)

verses.text:
यक्षाणां तु प्रहस्तेन सहस्रं निहतं रणे।
महोदरेण चानिन्द्यं सहस्रमपरं हतम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: Prahasta on his part killed in the battle a thousand Yakṣas and Mahodara killed another thousand who were irreproachable heroes. (7)

verses.text:
क्रुद्धेन च तदा राजन् मारीचेन युयुत्सुना।
निमेषान्तरमात्रेण द्वे सहस्रे निपातिते॥ ८॥
verses.m: O king, by the enraged Mārīca, eager for battle, two thousand more Yakṣas were killed in the twinkling of an eye. (8)

verses.text:
क्व च यक्षार्जवं युद्धं क्व च मायाबलाश्रयम्।
रक्षसां पुरुषव्याघ्र तेन तेऽभ्यधिका युधि॥ ९॥
verses.m: Altogether incomparable, O tiger among men, were the straight warfare of the Yakṣas and the deceitful warfare of the Rākṣasas. Hence the Rākṣasas had the upper hand in conflict. (9)

verses.text:
धूम्राक्षेण समागम्य माणिभद्रो महारणे।
मुसलेनोरसि क्रोधात् ताडितो न च कम्पितः॥ १०॥
verses.m: Closing with Dhūmrākṣa in the great struggle, Māṇibhadra was furiously struck in the breast with a pestle by the former, but he did not budge. (10)

verses.text:
ततो गदां समाविध्य माणिभद्रेण राक्षसः।
धूम्राक्षस्ताडितो मूर्ध्नि विह्वलः स पपात ह॥ ११॥
verses.m: Then Māṇibhadra whirled his club and struck the Rākṣasa, Dhūmrākṣa, on the head; he fell down confused. (11)

verses.text:
धूम्राक्षं ताडितं दृष्ट्वा पतितं शोणितोक्षितम्।
अभ्यधावत संग्रामे माणिभद्रं दशाननः॥ १२॥
verses.m: Seeing Dhūmrākṣa struck and fallen bathed in blood, Daśānana rushed towards Māṇibhadra in the battle. (12)

verses.text:
संक्रुद्धमभिधावन्तं माणिभद्रो दशाननम्।
शक्तिभिस्ताडयामास तिसृभिर्यक्षपुङ्गवः॥ १३॥
verses.m: Seeing the enraged Daśānana rushing towards him, Māṇibhadra, the best of Yakṣas, struck him with three javelins. (13)

verses.text:
ताडितो माणिभद्रस्य मुकुटे प्राहरद् रणे।
तस्य तेन प्रहारेण मुकुटं पार्श्वमागतम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: When struck on the field of battle Rāvaṇa dealt a blow at Māṇibhadra’s diadem; as a result of that blow of Rāvaṇa, Māṇibhadra’s diadem turned to one side. (14)

verses.text:
ततः प्रभृति यक्षोऽसौ पार्श्वमौलिरभूत् किल।
तस्मिंस्तु विमुखीभूते माणिभद्रे महात्मनि।
संनादः सुमहान् राजंस्तस्मिन् शैले व्यवर्धत॥ १५॥
verses.m: From that day onward Māṇibhadra, the Yakṣa, came to be known as Pārśwamauli (one whose diadem has turned to one side). When the colossal Māṇibhadra turned his face away (from the battlefield), there arose, O king, a great clamour of the Rākṣasas on that hill. (15)

verses.text:
ततो दूरात् प्रददृशे धनाध्यक्षो गदाधरः।
शुक्रप्रौष्ठपदाभ्यां च पद्मशङ्खसमावृतः॥ १६॥
verses.m: There came to view from afar the lord of wealth, who was holding a club and was accompanied by Śukra and Prauṣṭhapada, his two ministers, and by the deities presiding over two of his treasures, Padma and Śaṅkha. (16)

verses.text:
स दृष्ट्वा भ्रातरं संख्ये शापाद् विभ्रष्टगौरवम्।
उवाच वचनं धीमान् युक्तं पैतामहे कुले॥ १७॥
verses.m: Seeing on the battlefield his brother (Rāvaṇa) who had lost his sense of respect (for elders) by reason of the curse, that wise man tendered the following advice worthy of the House of Brahmā (the grandfather of the universe): (17)

verses.text:
यन्मया वार्यमाणस्त्वं नावगच्छसि दुर्मतेः।
पश्चादस्य फलं प्राप्य ज्ञास्यसे निरयं गतः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “O fool, though being warned by me, you do not listen; you will, however, come to your senses later when, as a result of your misdeeds, you go to hell. (18)

verses.text:
यो हि मोहाद् विषं पीत्वा नावगच्छति दुर्मतिः।
स तस्य परिणामान्ते जानीते कर्मणः फलम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: “The fool who, out of delusion, drinks poison and does not recognize it as such, will come to know the result of that action when he reaps its fruit. (19)

verses.text:
दैवतानि न नन्दन्ति धर्मयुक्तेन केनचित्।
येन त्वमीदृशं भावं नीतस्तच्च न बुद्ध्यसे॥ २०॥
verses.m: “The gods will not be pleased even with an act which is righteous in your eyes. Deluded by that displeasure (of the gods) you have been led to this violence; yet you do not understand that. (20)

verses.text:
मातरं पितरं विप्रमाचार्यं चावमन्यते।
स पश्यति फलं तस्य प्रेतराजवशं गतः॥ २१॥
verses.m: “He who insults his mother, father, teacher and a Brāhmaṇa will reap the consequence when he has fallen under the sway of Yama (the king of the departed). (21)

verses.text:
अध्रुवे हि शरीरे यो न करोति तपोऽर्जनम्।
स पश्चात् तप्यते मूढो मृतो गत्वाऽऽत्मनो गतिम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: “The fool who does not practise austerities with his transient body will repent when he meets with his destiny after death. (22)

verses.text:
धर्माद् राज्यं धनं सौख्यमधर्माद् दुःखमेव च।
तस्माद् धर्मं सुखार्थाय कुर्यात् पापं विसर्जयेत्॥ २३॥
verses.m: From virtue follow sovereignty, wealth and happiness; misery alone results from unrighteousness. Hence to secure happiness one should practise virtue and abjure sin. (23)

verses.text:
पापस्य हि फलं दुःखं तद् भोक्तव्यमिहात्मना।
तस्मादात्मापघातार्थं मूढः पापं करिष्यति॥ २४॥
verses.m: “The fruit of sin is misery and it must be reaped by the sinner himself; hence a fool commits sin for his own destruction. (24)

verses.text:
कस्यचिन्न हि दुर्बुद्धेश्छन्दतो जायते मतिः।
यादृशं कुरुते कर्म तादृशं फलमश्नुते॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Sense does not dawn on an evil-minded man of its own accord. As he sows so he reaps. (25)

verses.text:
ऋदिं्ध रूपं बलं पुत्रान् वित्तं शूरत्वमेव च।
प्राप्नुवन्ति नरा लोके निर्जितं पुण्यकर्मभिः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “People attain in this world prosperity, personality, strength, sons, wealth and valour as earned by their meritorious deeds. (26)

verses.text:
एवं निरयगामी त्वं यस्य ते मतिरीदृशी।
न त्वां समभिभाषिष्येऽसद्वृत्तेष्वेव निर्णयः॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Thus you will go to hell since your mind is disposed to evil. I shall speak to you no more. This is the rule laid down in regard to men of bad conduct.” (27)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तास्ततस्तेन तस्यामात्याः समाहताः।
मारीचप्रमुखाः सर्वे विमुखा विप्रदुद्रुवुः॥ २८॥
verses.m: Admonished in such words and hit hard by Kubera, the ministers of Rāvaṇa, headed by Mārīca, thereupon lost their enthusiasm and fled. (28)

verses.text:
ततस्तेन दशग्रीवो यक्षेन्द्रेण महात्मना।
गदयाभिहतो मूर्ध्नि न च स्थानात् प्रकम्पितः॥ २९॥
verses.m: Then Rāvaṇa was struck on the head by the noble leader of the Yakṣas with his club, but he did not budge from his position. (29)

verses.text:
ततस्तौ राम निघ्नन्तौ तदान्योन्यं महामृधे।
न विह्वलौ न च श्रान्तौ तावुभौ यक्षराक्षसौ॥ ३०॥
verses.m: The Yakṣa and the Rākṣasa thereafter exchanged blows in the course of the great conflict, but, O Rāma, neither of them felt afflicted or exhausted. (30)

verses.text:
आग्नेयमस्त्रं तस्मै स मुमोच धनदस्तदा।
राक्षसेन्द्रो वारुणेन तदस्त्रं प्रत्यवारयत्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “The lord of wealth then shot at Rāvaṇa an Āgneyāstra (a missile presided over by the god of fire), which missile the king of the Rākṣasas countered with a Vāruṇāstra, a missile presided over by Varuṇa, the god of water. (31)

verses.text:
ततो मायां प्रविष्टोऽसौ राक्षसीं राक्षसेश्वरः।
रूपाणां शतसाहस्रं विनाशाय चकार च॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Then the king of the Rākṣasas fell back upon conjuring tricks natural to ogres and assumed myriads of forms to bring about the destruction of the Yakṣas. (32)

verses.text:
व्याघ्रो वराहो जीमूतः पर्वतः सागरो द्रुमः।
यक्षो दैत्यस्वरूपी च सोऽदृश्यत दशाननः॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “He, Daśānana, appeared as a tiger, a boar, a cloud, a hill, a sea, a tree, a Yakṣa and a Daitya. (33)

verses.text:
बहूनि च करोति स्म दृश्यन्ते न त्वसौ ततः।
प्रतिगृह्य ततो राम महदस्त्रं दशाननः॥ ३४॥
जघान मूर्ध्नि धनदं व्याविद्ध्य महतीं गदाम्।
एवं स तेनाभिहतो विह्वलः शोणितोक्षितः॥ ३५॥
कृत्तमूल इवाशोको निपपात धनाधिपः।
ततः पद्मादिभिस्तत्र निधिभिः स तदा वृतः॥ ३६॥
धनदोच्छ्वासितस्तैस्तु वनमानीय नन्दनम्।
निर्जित्य राक्षसेन्द्रस्तं धनदं हृष्टमानसः॥ ३७॥
पुष्पकं तस्य जग्राह विमानं जयलक्षणम्।
काञ्चनस्तम्भसंवीतं वैदूर्यमणितोरणम्॥ ३८॥
मुक्ताजालप्रतिच्छन्नं सर्वकालफलद्रुमम्।
मनोजवं कामगमं कामरूपं विहंगमम्॥ ३९॥
मणिकाञ्चनसोपानं तप्तकाञ्चनवेदिकम्।
देवोपवाह्यमक्षय्यं सदा दृष्टिमनःसुखम्॥ ४०॥
बह्वाश्चर्यं भक्तिचित्रं ब्रह्मणा परिनिर्मितम्।
निर्मितं सर्वकामैस्तु मनोहरमनुत्तमम्॥ ४१॥
न तु शीतं न चोष्णं च सर्वर्तुसुखदं शुभम्।
स तं राजा समारुह्य कामगं वीर्यनिर्जितम्॥ ४२॥
जितं त्रिभुवनं मेने दर्पोत्सेकात् सुदुर्मतिः।
जित्वा वैश्रवणं देवं कैलासात् समवातरत्॥ ४३॥
verses.m: “Nay, he appeared in many guises but he could not be seen. Then seizing hold of a mighty weapon, a huge club, and whirling it, Daśānana struck the lord of wealth on the head, O Rāma ! Knocked senseless when struck by him in this way and bathed in blood, the lord of wealth fell on the ground like an Aśoka tree cut at the root. Surrounded there at that time by the deities presiding over the treasures like Padma and others, the aforesaid lord of riches was brought to the Nandana grove and restored to his senses. Having vanquished the said lord of wealth, the king of the Rākṣasas, pleased at heart, seized his aerial car, the Puṣpaka, as a token of his victory. “The aerial car was furnished with pillars made of gold; its portals were made of cat’s-eye gems; it was hung with nets of pearls and planted with trees bearing fruit in all the seasons; it had the speed of the mind; it could go wherever one wanted to go; it could assume any form as desired; it had stairways of gems and gold and daises of refined gold; it was a celestial vehicle and was not subject to wear and tear; it was a perpetual joy to the eyes and the mind; it contained numerous curios of art; it looked picturesque with its compartments and had been constructed by Viśwakarmā, the architect of gods; it was provided with all objects of desire, was soul-captivating and unsurpassed in charm; it was neither too cool nor too hot; it was comfortable in all seasons and was splendid. Ascending the car, which had been won by his prowess and which could go wherever he wanted to go, that most evil-minded king thought in the height of his arrogance that he had conquered all the three worlds. Having vanquished God Vaiśravaṇa (Kubera), he descended from Kailāsa. (34—43)

verses.text:
स तेजसा विपुलमवाप्य तं जयं
प्रतापवान् विमलकिरीटहारवान्।
रराज वै परमविमानमास्थितो
निशाचरः सदसि गतो यथानलः॥ ४४॥
