verses.m: “Having scored that great victory by dint of his valour and seated in his excellent aerial car, that glorious ranger of the night, who wore a brilliant diadem on his head and a necklace of pearls on his breast, shone like fire in a sacrificial hall.” (44)

verses.text:
स जित्वा धनदं राम भ्रातरं राक्षसाधिपः।
महासेनप्रसूतिं तद् ययौ शरवणं महत्॥ १॥
verses.m: “Having vanquished his brother, Kubera, the king of the Rākṣasas sought the well-known thicket of reeds ‘Śaravaṇa’ where Lord Kārtikeya was born, O Rāma ! (1)

verses.text:
अथापश्यद् दशग्रीवो रौक्मं शरवणं महत्।
गभस्तिजालसंवीतं द्वितीयमिव भास्करम्॥ २॥
verses.m: “Now Daśagrīva saw the large golden-hued expanse of reeds bright like a second sun surrounded by rays. (2)

verses.text:
स पर्वतं समारुह्य कंचिद् रम्यवनान्तरम्।
प्रेक्षते पुष्पकं तत्र राम विष्टम्भितं तदा॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Ascending a mountain clothed with a lovely grove, he found the Puṣpaka brought to a standstill on that spot on that occasion, O Rāma! (3)

verses.text:
विष्टब्धं किमिदं कस्मान्नागमत् कामगं कृतम्।
अचिन्तयद् राक्षसेन्द्रः सचिवैस्तैः समावृतः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Surrounded by his aforesaid ministers, the king of the Rākṣasas reflected, “How has this aerial car, which had been designed in such a way as to be able to follow its master’s will, been rendered motionless? Why does it not move? (4)

verses.text:
किंनिमित्तमिच्छया मे नेदं गच्छति पुष्पकम्।
पर्वतस्योपरिष्ठस्य कर्मेदं कस्यचिद् भवेत्॥ ५॥
verses.m: “What may be the reason for the Puṣpaka not proceeding according to my wishes? It must be the act of someone who resides on this hill.” (5)

verses.text:
ततोऽब्रवीत् तदा राम मारीचो बुद्धिकोविदः।
नेदं निष्कारणं राजन् पुष्पकं यन्न गच्छति॥ ६॥
verses.m: “O Rāma, the astute Mārīca thereupon said on that occasion: ‘O king, it cannot be without a reason that this aerial car, Puṣpaka, does not move. (6)

verses.text:
अथवा पुष्पकमिदं धनदान्नान्यवाहनम्।
अतो निस्पन्दमभवद् धनाध्यक्षविनाकृतम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “ ‘Maybe, the aerial car, Puṣpaka, will not carry anyone other than Kubera, the god of riches. Therefore, even as it has been disunited from him, it has become motionless.’ (7)

verses.text:
इति वाक्यान्तरे तस्य करालः कृष्णपिङ्गलः।
वामनो विकटो मुण्डी नन्दी ह्रस्वभुजो बली॥ ८॥
ततः पार्श्वमुपागम्य भवस्यानुचरोऽब्रवीत्।
नन्दीश्वरो वचश्चेदं राक्षसेन्द्रमशङ्कितः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Interrupting his speech, and approaching him, Nandīśwara, an attendant of Lord Śiva, dreadful, of yellowish dark complexion, dwarfish, misshapen, with his head clean shaved, of short arms and very strong, and ever full of joy, fearlessly spoke the following words to the king of the Rākṣasas: (8-9)

verses.text:
निवर्तस्व दशग्रीव शैले क्रीडति शंकरः।
सुपर्णनागयक्षाणां देवगन्धर्वरक्षसाम्॥ १०॥
सर्वेषामेव भूतानामगम्यः पर्वतः कृतः।
इति नन्दिवचः श्रुत्वा क्रोधात् कम्पितकुण्डलः॥ ११॥
रोषात् तु ताम्रनयनः पुष्पकादवरुह्य सः।
कोऽयं शङ्कर इत्युक्त्वा शैलमूलमुपागतः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “ ‘Turn back, O Daśagrīva ! Lord Śaṅkara is sporting on this hill; hence it has been rendered inaccessible even to Suparṇas, Nāgas, Yakṣas, gods, Gandharvas and Rākṣasas, nay, to all created beings.’ Hearing these words of Nandī and alighting from the Puṣpaka, and his earrings shaking on account of his wrath and his eyes coppery through indignation, Rāvaṇa sought the foot of the hill, saying, ‘Who is this Śaṅkara?’ (10—12)

verses.text:
सोऽपश्यन्नन्दिनं तत्र देवस्यादूरतः स्थितम्।
दीप्तं शूलमवष्टभ्य द्वितीयमिव शङ्करम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “There he beheld Nandī standing near the Lord, holding a flaming pike and appearing like a second Śaṅkara. (13)

verses.text:
तं दृष्ट्वा वानरमुखमवज्ञाय स राक्षसः।
प्रहासं मुमुचे तत्र सतोय इव तोयदः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Seeing him endowed with the head of a monkey, and disregarding him, the said Rākṣasa laughed loudly thundering like a cloud laden with water. (14)

verses.text:
तं क्रुद्धो भगवान् नन्दी शङ्करस्यापरा तनुः।
अब्रवीत् तत्र तद् रक्षो दशाननमुपस्थितम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Provoked to anger, the divine Nandī, an alter ego of Lord Śaṅkara, spoke to the said ogre, Daśānana, who was standing there closeby: (15)

verses.text:
यस्माद् वानररूपं मामवज्ञाय दशानन।
अशनीपातसंकाशमपहासं प्रमुक्तवान्॥ १६॥
तस्मान्मद्वीर्यसंयुक्ता मद्रूपसमतेजसः।
उत्पत्स्यन्ति वधार्थं हि कुलस्य तव वानराः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “ ‘O Daśānana, since, deriding me in my monkey-form, you burst into a loud laughter resembling a stroke of lightning, therefore, monkeys will be born to destroy your race. They will possess my valour; they will have a lustrous form like mine. (16-17)

verses.text:
नखदंष्ट्रायुधाः क्रूर मनःसम्पातरंहसः।
युद्धोन्मत्ता बलोद्रिक्ताः शैला इव विसर्पिणः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “ ‘They will have claws and teeth for their weapons; they will have the speed of the mind; they will be frantic in fight; they will be proud of their might; they will look like moving mountains, O cruel one! (18)

verses.text:
ते तव प्रबलं दर्पमुत्सेधं च पृथग्विधम्।
व्यपनेष्यन्ति सम्भूय सहामात्यसुतस्य च॥ १९॥
verses.m: “ ‘Gathering together, they will take away your excessive arrogance and pride of physical superiority alongwith that of your ministers and sons. (19)

verses.text:
किं त्विदानीं मया शक्यं हन्तुं त्वां हे निशाचर।
न हन्तव्यो हतस्त्वं हि पूर्वमेव स्वकर्मभिः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “ ‘O Rākṣasa, I can kill you even now; but you shall not be killed inasmuch as you are already killed by your own misdeeds.’ (20)

verses.text:
इत्युदीरितवाक्ये तु देवे तस्मिन् महात्मनि।
देवदुन्दुभयो नेदुः पुष्पवृष्टिश्च खाच्च्युता॥ २१॥
verses.m: “When that high-souled divine being uttered these words, the kettledrums of the gods for their part sounded and a shower of flowers fell from the heavens. (21)

verses.text:
अचिन्तयित्वा स तदा नन्दिवाक्यं महाबलः।
पर्वतं तु समासाद्य वाक्यमाह दशाननः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Not minding the utterance of Nandī, and approaching the hill, Daśānana, that very mighty ogre, however, said on that occasion: (22)

verses.text:
पुष्पकस्य गतिश्छिन्ना यत्कृते मम गच्छतः।
तमिमं शैलमुन्मूलं करोमि तव गोपते॥ २३॥
verses.m: “ ‘O master of a bull, I shall pull up by the roots this hill on whose account the course of Puṣpaka in which I was travelling has been arrested. (23)

verses.text:
केन प्रभावेण भवो नित्यं क्रीडति राजवत्।
विज्ञातव्यं न जानीते भयस्थानमुपस्थितम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: “ ‘By virtue of what power does Śiva continually sport like a king? He does not seem to understand what should be known to him, viz., that danger has come to him.’ (24)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा ततो राम भुजान् विक्षिप्य पर्वते।
तोलयामास तं शीघ्रं स शैलः समकम्पत॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Having said so, O Rāma, he put his hands below the hill and lifted it up in no time so that, the hill shook violently. (25)

verses.text:
चालनात् पर्वतस्यैव गणा देवस्य कम्पिताः।
चचाल पार्वती चापि तदाश्लिष्टा महेश्वरम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: “By the shaking of the hill the attendants of the Lord trembled; Pārvatī also slipped and clung to Maheśwara at that moment. (26)

verses.text:
ततो राम महादेवो देवानां प्रवरो हरः।
पादाङ्गुष्ठेन तं शैलं पीडयामास लीलया॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Then, O Rāma, Mahādeva, the foremost of the gods, also known as Hara, the Destroyer, sportively pressed the hill with His great toe. (27)

verses.text:
पीडितास्तु ततस्तस्य शैलस्तम्भोपमा भुजाः।
विस्मिताश्चाभवंस्तत्र सचिवास्तस्य रक्षसः॥ २८॥
verses.m: “His (Daśānana’s) arms, which resembled pillars supporting the hill, were then crushed; and the ministers of the Rākṣasa standing there were surprised. (28)

verses.text:
रक्षसा तेन रोषाच्च भुजानां पीडनात् तथा।
मुक्तो विरावः सहसा त्रैलोक्यं येन कम्पितम्॥ २९॥
verses.m: “When his arms were thus crushed, the Rākṣasa in fury raised a cry all of a sudden. All the three worlds were shaken by it. (29)

verses.text:
मेनिरे वज्रनिष्पेषं तस्यामात्या युगक्षये।
तदा वर्त्मसु चलिता देवा इन्द्रपुरोगमाः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “His ministers took it to be a crash of thunder, which takes place at the end of the world-period. At that time even the gods, with Indra at their head, stumbled on their way. (30)

verses.text:
समुद्राश्चापि संक्षुब्धाश्चलिताश्चापि पर्वताः।
यक्षा विद्याधराः सिद्धाः किमेतदिति चाब्रुवन्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Even the oceans became turbulent and the mountains also shook; nay, the Yakṣas, Vidyādharas and Siddhas cried out, “What is this?” (31)

verses.text:
तोषयस्व महादेवं नीलकण्ठमुमापतिम्।
तमृते शरणं नान्यं पश्यामोऽत्र दशानन॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “ ‘Propitiate Mahādeva, the blue-necked God, and the husband of Umā; O Daśānana, we do not see any protector other than Him. (32)

verses.text:
स्तुतिभिः प्रणतो भूत्वा तमेव शरणं व्रज।
कृपालुः शङ्करस्तुष्टः प्रसादं ते विधास्यति॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “ ‘In all humility seek refuge in Him by singing His praises. Śaṅkara is compassionate and will become gracious to you when gratified.’ (33)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तदामात्यैस्तुष्टाव वृषभध्वजम्।
सामभिर्विविधैः स्तोत्रैः प्रणम्य स दशाननः।
संवत्सरसहस्रं तु रुदतो रक्षसो गतम्॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “Respectfully bowing to Him when advised thus by his ministers, Daśānana glorified the God, whose standard bears the ensign of a bull, by singing psalms from the Sāmaveda and other hymns. A thousand years elapsed while the Rākṣasa went on crying in this manner. (34)

verses.text:
ततः प्रीतो महादेवः शैलाग्रे विष्ठितः प्रभुः।
मुक्त्वा चास्य भुजान् राम प्राह वाक्यं दशाननम्॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “Relieving his hands of the pressure, when pleased with his eulogy, while remaining seated on a peak of the hill, Lord Mahādeva, O Rāma, then spoke to Daśānana as follows: (35)

verses.text:
प्रीतोऽस्मि तव वीरस्य शौटीर्याच्च दशानन।
शैलाक्रान्तेन यो मुक्तस्त्वया रावः सुदारुणः॥ ३६॥
यस्माल्लोकत्रयं चैतद् रावितं भयमागतम्।
तस्मात् त्वं रावणो नाम नाम्ना राजन् भविष्यसि॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “ ‘O Daśānana, I am pleased with your manliness, a hero as you are, as well as with your encomium. Since the denizens of all the three worlds were set acrying, seized as they were with fear by the fierce cry which was set forth by you when you were crushed by the hill. Therefore, O king, you will go by the name of Rāvaṇa. (36-37)

verses.text:
देवता मानुषा यक्षा ये चान्ये जगतीतले।
एवं त्वामभिधास्यन्ति रावणं लोकरावणम्॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “ ‘The gods, human beings, Yakṣas and whatever other beings exist on the earth’s surface will, henceforth call you by the name of Rāvaṇa because you thus set the world acrying. (38)

verses.text:
गच्छ पौलस्त्य विस्रब्धं पथा येन त्वमिच्छसि।
मया चैवाभ्यनुज्ञातो राक्षसाधिप गम्यताम्॥ ३९॥
verses.m: “ ‘O grandson of Pulastya, proceed without fear by whichever path you wish to take. Permitted by Me, O suzerain lord of ogres, you may go.’ (39)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तु लङ्केशः शम्भुना स्वयमब्रवीत्।
प्रीतो यदि महादेव वरं मे देहि याचतः॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “When spoken to in these words by Lord Śambhu Himself, the king of Laṅkā said, ‘O Mahādeva, if you are pleased with me, kindly vouchsafe a boon to me, who beg for the same. (40)

verses.text:
अवध्यत्वं मया प्राप्तं देवगन्धर्वदानवैः।
राक्षसैर्गुह्यकैर्नागैर्ये चान्ये बलवत्तराः॥ ४१॥
verses.m: “ ‘I have already secured immunity from death at the hands of gods, Gandharvas and Dānavas, Rākṣasas, Guhyakas, Nāgas and others who are mightier than these. (41)

verses.text:
मानुषान् न गणे देव स्वल्पास्ते मम सम्मताः।
दीर्घमायुश्च मे प्राप्तं ब्रह्मणस्त्रिपुरान्तक॥ ४२॥
वाञ्छितं चायुषः शेषं शस्त्रं त्वं च प्रयच्छ मे।
एवमुक्तस्ततस्तेन रावणेन स शङ्करः॥ ४३॥
ददौ खड्गं महादीप्तं चन्द्रहासमिति श्रुतम्।
आयुषश्चावशेषं च ददौ भूतपतिस्तदा॥ ४४॥
verses.m: “ ‘I do not reckon the human beings, O Lord, because they are regarded by me as very insignificant. A boon of long life has been secured by me from Brahmā, O destroyer of Tripura ! Give me the remaining lease of life sought by me and give me also a weapon.’ Requested thus by the aforesaid Rāvaṇa, the well-known Lord Śaṅkara gifted to him the highly shining sword known as Candrahāsa. The Lord of spirits granted to him also the remaining lease of life on that occasion. (42—44)

verses.text:
दत्त्वोवाच ततः शम्भुर्नावज्ञेयमिदं त्वया।
अवज्ञातं यदि हि ते मामेवैष्यत्यसंशयः॥ ४५॥
verses.m: “Bestowing it on him, He said, ‘This sword is not to be despised by you; if it is disregarded by you, it shall doubtless return to me.’ (45)

verses.text:
एवं महेश्वरेणैव कृतनामा स रावणः।
अभिवाद्य महादेवमारुरोहाथ पुष्पकम्॥ ४६॥
verses.m: “Having thus been named by the supreme Deity Śiva, greeting Mahādeva, the said Rāvaṇa re-ascended Puṣpaka. (46)

verses.text:
ततो महीतलं राम पर्यक्रामत रावणः।
क्षत्रियान् सुमहावीर्यान् बाधमानस्ततस्ततः॥ ४७॥
verses.m: “Thereafter, O Rāma, Rāvaṇa ranged over the earth’s surface oppressing Kṣatriyas possessed of exceeding valour here and there. (47)

verses.text:
केचित् तेजस्विनः शूराः क्षत्रिया युद्धदुर्मदाः।
तच्छासनमकुर्वन्तो विनेशुः सपरिच्छदाः॥ ४८॥
verses.m: “Disobeying his command some valiant Kṣatriyas, who were full of martial ardour and ferocious in battle, perished alongwith their followers. (48)

verses.text:
अपरे दुर्जयं रक्षो जानन्तः प्राज्ञसम्मताः।
जिताः स्म इत्यभाषन्त राक्षसं बलदर्पितम्॥ ४९॥
verses.m: “Others, who were recognized as prudent, and who knew the Rākṣasa to be difficult to conquer, submitted to the ogre, who was proud of his strength, ‘We stand vanquished.’ ” (49)

verses.text:
अथ राजन् महाबाहुर्विचरन् पृथिवीतले।
हिमवद्वनमासाद्य परिचक्राम रावणः॥ १॥
verses.m: “While ranging over the earth’s surface, the mighty-armed Rāvaṇa, O king, arrived at a forest in the region of the Himālayas and was roving in it. (1)

verses.text:
तत्रापश्यत् स वै कन्यां कृष्णाजिनजटाधराम्।
आर्षेण विधिना चैनां दीप्यन्तीं देवतामिव॥ २॥
verses.m: “There he saw a maiden, wearing the skin of a black antelope and matted locks, rich in austerities befitting a Ṛṣi (a seer of Vedic Mantras) and glowing like a deity. (2)

verses.text:
स दृष्ट्वा रूपसम्पन्नां कन्यां तां सुमहाव्रताम्।
काममोहपरीतात्मा पप्रच्छ प्रहसन्निव॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Seeing her, endowed with comeliness and observing a great vow, and overpowered by infatuation born of lust, Rāvaṇa asked her as though laughing: (3)

verses.text:
किमिदं वर्तसे भद्रे विरुद्धं यौवनस्य ते।
नहि युक्ता तवैतस्य रूपस्यैवं प्रतिक्रिया॥ ४॥
verses.m: “ ‘O blessed one, what are you doing here? It is incompatible with your youth. Such a conduct fits ill with one of your beauty. (4)

verses.text:
रूपं तेऽनुपमं भीरु कामोन्मादकरं नृणाम्।
न युक्तं तपसि स्थातुं निर्गतो ह्येष निर्णयः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “ ‘O Bhīru (one who easily gets afraid), your unrivalled beauty generates madness born of lust in the minds of men. It is not proper for you to perform Tapas; this is the conclusion which has emerged from my mind. (5)

verses.text:
कस्यासि किमिदं भद्रे कश्च भर्ता वरानने।
येन सम्भुज्यसे भीरु स नरः पुण्यभाग् भुवि॥ ६॥
verses.m: “ ‘O auspicious one, to whom do you belong? What are you doing here? Who is your husband, O lady with a comely face? He who enjoys you, O timid one, is indeed a very fortunate person in this world. (6)

verses.text:
पृच्छतः शंस मे सर्वं कस्य हेतोः परिश्रमः।
एवमुक्ता तु सा कन्या रावणेन यशस्विनी॥ ७॥
अब्रवीद् विधिवत् कृत्वा तस्यातिथ्यं तपोधना।
कुशध्वजो नाम पिता ब्रह्मर्षिरमितप्रभः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “ ‘Relate everything to me, who am inquisitive. For whose sake is all this effort?’ Questioned thus by Rāvaṇa, that illustrious maiden, whose wealth was Tapas, played the host according to rule and then said, ‘My father’s name is Kuśadhwaja. He was a Brahmarṣi endowed with immense lustre. (7-8)

verses.text:
बृहस्पतिसुतः श्रीमान् बुद्ध्या तुल्यो बृहस्पतेः।
तस्याहं कुर्वतो नित्यं वेदाभ्यासं महात्मनः॥ ९॥
सम्भूता वाङ्मयी कन्या नाम्ना वेदवती स्मृता।
ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वा यक्षराक्षसपन्नगाः॥ १०॥
ते चापि गत्वा पितरं वरणं रोचयन्ति मे।
न च मां स पिता तेभ्यो दत्तवान् राक्षसेश्वर॥ ११॥
verses.m: “ ‘That glorious sage was a son of Bṛhaspati and equal to him in respect of intelligence. Of that magnanimous soul, who was always engaged in reciting the Vedas, I was born as an incarnation of the Vedas. I am, therefore, known as Vedavatī. O king of the Rākṣasas, gods with Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas and Pannagas (Nāgas) approached my father and sought my hand in marriage; but my aforesaid father did not give me to any of them. (9—11)

verses.text:
कारणं तद् वदिष्यामि निशामय महाभुज।
पितुस्तु मम जामाता विष्णुः किल सुरेश्वरः॥ १२॥
अभिप्रेतस्त्रिलोकेशस्तस्मान्नान्यस्य मे पिता।
दातुमिच्छति तस्मै तु तच्छ्रुत्वा बलदर्पितः॥ १३॥
शम्भुर्नाम ततो राजा दैत्यानां कुपितोऽभवत्।
तेन रात्रौ शयानो मे पिता पापेन हिंसितः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “ ‘O mighty-armed one, I will tell you the reason behind it. Please listen. Viṣṇu, the Lord of gods and the Ruler of the three worlds, indeed was acceptable to my father as a son-in-law. My father would not give me to anyone other than Him. Hearing this, Śambhu, the king of the Daityas, who was proud of his might, became angry. While asleep at night, my father was killed by that sinful one. (12—14)

verses.text:
ततो मे जननी दीना तच्छरीरं पितुर्मम।
परिष्वज्य महाभागा प्रविष्टा हव्यवाहनम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “ ‘Thereupon my mother, of great merit, who had become very depressed, entered the fire, taking that body of my father in her arms. (15)

verses.text:
ततो मनोरथं सत्यं पितुर्नारायणं प्रति।
करोमीति तमेवाहं हृदयेन समुद्वहे॥ १६॥
verses.m: “ ‘Thenceforward I have installed Nārāyaṇa in my heart so that I may implement the desire of my father with regard to Him. (16)

verses.text:
इति प्रतिज्ञामारुह्य चरामि विपुलं तपः।
एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं मया राक्षसपुङ्गव॥ १७॥
verses.m: “ ‘Having taken this vow, I am performing severe Tapas; O best of Rākṣasas, I have told you all this. (17)

verses.text:
नारायणो मम पतिर्न त्वन्यः पुरुषोत्तमात्।
आश्रये नियमं घोरं नारायणपरीप्सया॥ १८॥
verses.m: “ ‘Nārāyaṇa is my husband and no one other than that Puruṣottama. Desiring to secure the hand of Nārāyaṇa I am observing this hard penance. (18)

verses.text:
विज्ञातस्त्वं हि मे राजन् गच्छ पौलस्त्यनन्दन।
जानामि तपसा सर्वं त्रैलोक्ये यद्धि वर्तते॥ १९॥
verses.m: “ ‘O king, by dint of my Tapas I know everything that exists in the three worlds. I have come to know who you are. You may go, O son of Viśravā!’ (19)

verses.text:
सोऽब्रवीद् रावणो भूयस्तां कन्यां सुमहाव्रताम्।
अवरुह्य विमानाग्रात् कन्दर्पशरपीडितः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Descending from the aerial car, Rāvaṇa, who was smitten with darts of love, spoke again to that maiden, who was observing a great vow: (20)

verses.text:
अवलिप्तासि सुश्रोणि यस्यास्ते मतिरीदृशी।
वृद्धानां मृगशावाक्षि भ्राजते पुण्यसंचयः॥ २१॥
verses.m: “ ‘O lady of shapely limbs, you are presumptuous in that you have made such a resolve. Your endeavour to acquire merit through Tapas befits only old women, O lady possessing the eyes of a fawn ! (21)

verses.text:
त्वं सर्वगुणसम्पन्ना नार्हसे वक्तुमीदृशम्।
त्रैलोक्यसुन्दरी भीरु यौवनं तेऽतिवर्तते॥ २२॥
verses.m: “ ‘You, who are endowed with all good qualities, ought not to speak like this. You are beautiful in all the three worlds, O timid one, your youth is passing away. (22)

verses.text:
अहं लङ्कापतिर्भद्रे दशग्रीव इति श्रुतः।
तस्य मे भव भार्या त्वं भुङ् क्ष्व भोगान् यथासुखम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: “ ‘O blessed one, I am the king of Laṅkā, known as Daśagrīva. Become my wife and enjoy all sense-delights as it suits your pleasure. (23)

verses.text:
कश्च तावदसौ यं त्वं विष्णुरित्यभिभाषसे।
वीर्येण तपसा चैव भोगेन च बलेन च॥ २४॥
स मया नो समो भद्रे यं त्वं कामयसेऽङ्गने।
इत्युक्तवति तस्मिंस्तु वेदवत्यथ साब्रवीत्॥ २५॥
मा मैवमिति सा कन्या तमुवाच निशाचरम्।
त्रैलोक्याधिपतिं विष्णुं सर्वलोकनमस्कृतम्॥ २६॥
त्वदृते राक्षसेन्द्रान्यः कोऽवमन्येत बुद्धिमान्।
एवमुक्तस्तया तत्र वेदवत्या निशाचरः॥ २७॥
मूर्धजेषु तदा कन्यां कराग्रेण परामृशत्।
ततो वेदवती क्रुद्धा केशान् हस्तेन साच्छिनत्॥ २८॥
verses.m: “ ‘By the way, who is that whom you speak of as Viṣṇu? He whom you wish to secure, O good lady, is not equal to me in valour, Tapas, enjoyment and strength.’ When he had spoken thus, the aforesaid Vedavatī for her part thereupon replied as follows: ‘Don’t speak thus, don’t speak thus!’ She told the ranger of the night, ‘What sensible man, other than you, O king of the Rākṣasas, will speak thus disparagingly of Viṣṇu, who is the lord of the three worlds and who is universally respected.’ Spoken to in these words on that spot by the aforesaid Vedavatī, the Rākṣasa then seized hold of the maiden by her hair with his hand. Provoked to anger, Vedavatī cut off her hair with her hand. (24—28)

verses.text:
असिर्भूत्वा करस्तस्याः केशांश्छिन्नांस्तदाकरोत्।
सा ज्वलन्तीव रोषेण दहन्तीव निशाचरम्॥ २९॥
उवाचाग्निं समाधाय मरणाय कृतत्वरा।
धर्षितायास्त्वयानार्य न मे जीवितमिष्यते॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Getting transformed her hand into sword, she then cut off her hair. Hastening to put an end to her life, she kindled a fire. Burning, as it were, with anger, she spoke to the Rākṣasa as if she would burn him: ‘Insulted by you, O ignoble man, I no longer desire to live. (29-30)

verses.text:
रक्षस्तस्मात् प्रवेक्ष्यामि पश्यतस्ते हुताशनम्।
यस्मात् तु धर्षिता चाहं त्वया पापात्मना वने॥ ३१॥
तस्मात् तव वधार्थं हि समुत्पत्स्ये ह्यहं पुनः।
नहि शक्यः स्त्रिया हन्तुं पुरुषः पापनिश्चयः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “ ‘I will, therefore, enter the fire before your very eyes, O ogre ! As I have been insulted in this forest by you, O sinner, therefore, I will be born again for your destruction. It is not possible for a woman to kill a man of sinful resolve. (31-32)

verses.text:
शापे त्वयि मयोत्सृष्टे तपसश्च व्ययो भवेत्।
यदि त्वस्ति मया किंचित् कृतं दत्तं हुतं तथा॥ ३३॥
तस्मात् त्वयोनिजा साध्वी भवेयं धर्मिणः सुता।
एवमुक्त्वा प्रविष्टा सा ज्वलितं जातवेदसम्॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “ ‘And if I pronounce a curse on you, my reserve of Tapas will be lost. If I have done anything meritorious or have given gifts or tended the sacred fire, I will surely appear as Ayonijā (not born of the womb), the pious daughter of a virtuous man.’ Having said thus, she entered the kindled fire. (33-34)

verses.text:
पपात च दिवो दिव्या पुष्पवृष्टिः समन्ततः।
पुनरेव समुद्भूता पद्मे पद्मसमप्रभा॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “Nay, a rain of celestial flowers fell from the heaven on all sides. She appeared again from a lotus with the radiance of a lotus. (35)

verses.text:
तस्मादपि पुनः प्राप्ता पूर्ववत् तेन रक्षसा।
कन्यां कमलगर्भाभां प्रगृह्य स्वगृहं ययौ॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “As on the previous occasion, she was again taken hold of by the Rākṣasa from her birth-place. Taking hold of the maiden, who had the lustre of the interior of a lotus, he went home. (36)

verses.text:
प्रगृह्य रावणस्त्वेतां दर्शयामास मन्त्रिणे।
लक्षणज्ञो निरीक्ष्यैव रावणं चैवमब्रवीत्॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “Taking her by the hand, Rāvaṇa showed her to his minister. Scanning her very features, the minister, who was well-versed in physiognomy, said to Rāvaṇa:(37)

verses.text:
गृहस्थैषा हि सुश्रोणी त्वद्वधायैव दृश्यते।
एतच्छ्रुत्वार्णवे राम तां प्रचिक्षेप रावणः॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “ ‘If this woman of shapely limbs stays in your house, she will prove to be your destroyer.’ Hearing this, O Rāma, Rāvaṇa threw her into the sea. (38)

verses.text:
सा चैव क्षितिमासाद्य यज्ञायतनमध्यगा।
राज्ञो हलमुखोत्कृष्टा पुनरप्युत्थिता सती॥ ३९॥
verses.m: “Reaching the shore she came to the middle of a sacrificial ground. Dug out by the ploughshare of the king, Janaka, she came up again. (39)

verses.text:
सैषा जनकराजस्य प्रसूता तनया प्रभो।
तव भार्या महाबाहो विष्णुस्त्वं हि सनातनः॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “O Lord, the same Vedavatī reborn as the daughter of King Janaka, is Your wife now. O mighty-armed Lord, You are indeed Viṣṇu, the ancient one. (40)

verses.text:
पूर्वं क्रोधहतः शत्रुर्ययासौ निहतस्तया।
उपाश्रयित्वा शैलाभस्तव वीर्यममानुषम्॥ ४१॥
verses.m: “Falling back upon Your superhuman prowess, the same lady by whom Your mountain-like enemy was consumed by her wrath, in her former birth, actually killed him. (41)

verses.text:
एवमेषा महाभागा मर्त्येषूत्पत्स्यते पुनः।
क्षेत्रे हलमुखोत्कृष्टे वेद्यामग्निशिखोपमा॥ ४२॥
verses.m: “In this manner this highly meritorious lady will continue to appear again among mortals (in the following cycles), drawn out by a ploughshare in a furrowed field, like a fire on an altar. (42)

verses.text:
एषा वेदवती नाम पूर्वमासीत् कृते युगे।
त्रेतायुगमनुप्राप्य वधार्थं तस्य रक्षसः॥ ४३॥
उत्पन्ना मैथिलकुले जनकस्य महात्मनः।
सीतोत्पन्ना तु सीतेति मानुषैः पुनरुच्यते॥ ४४॥
verses.m: “She who was known as Vedavatī in her former birth in Kṛtayuga, appeared again in the Tretāyuga as a daughter of the high-souled Janaka in the line of the kings of Mithilā for bringing about the destruction of that Rākṣasa. Since she came out of a furrow (Sītā), she is called ‘Sītā’ by human beings.” (43-44)

verses.text:
प्रविष्टायां हुताशं तु वेदवत्यां स रावणः।
पुष्पकं तु समारुह्य परिचक्राम मेदिनीम्॥ १॥
verses.m: “Ascending the Puṣpaka, when Vedavatī had entered the fire, Rāvaṇa ranged the earth once more. (1)

verses.text:
ततो मरुत्तं नृपतिं यजन्तं सह दैवतैः।
उशीरबीजमासाद्य ददर्श स तु रावणः॥ २॥
verses.m: “Reaching Uśīrabīja, Rāvaṇa for his part saw king Marutta performing a sacrifice in the company of gods. (2)

verses.text:
संवर्तो नाम ब्रह्मर्षिः साक्षाद् भ्राता बृहस्पतेः।
याजयामास धर्मज्ञः सर्वैर्देवगणैर्वृतः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Surrounded by the hosts of gods, a Brahmarṣi, Saṁvarta by name, a brother of Sage Bṛhaspati himself and a knower of Dharma, was conducting the sacrifice. (3)

verses.text:
दृष्ट्वा देवास्तु तद् रक्षो वरदानेन दुर्जयम्।
तिर्यग्योनिं समाविष्टास्तस्य धर्षणभीरवः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Seeing that Rākṣasa, who was hard to vanquish on account of the boons (granted to him), the gods, afraid of his attack, took cover in the bodies of animals. (4)

verses.text:
इन्द्रो मयूरः संवृत्तो धर्मराजस्तु वायसः।
कृकलासो धनाध्यक्षो हंसश्च वरुणोऽभवत्॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Indra became a peacock; Yama, a crow; Kubera, a chameleon and Varuṇa, a swan. (5)

verses.text:
अन्वेष्वपि गतेष्वेवं देवेष्वरिनिषूदन।
रावणः प्राविशद् यज्ञं सारमेय इवाशुचिः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “In this manner when the other gods too had transformed themselves, O scourge of Your foes, Rāvaṇa entered the sacrificial ground like an unclean dog. (6)

verses.text:
तं च राजानमासाद्य रावणो राक्षसाधिपः।
प्राह युद्धं प्रयच्छेति निर्जितोऽस्मीति वा वद॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Approaching the king, Rāvaṇa, the suzerain lord of the Rākṣasas, said, ‘Give battle to me or admit that you stand vanquished.’ (7)

verses.text:
ततो मरुत्तो नृपतिः को भवानित्युवाच तम्।
अवहासं ततो मुक्त्वा रावणो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Thereupon King Marutta said to him: ‘Who are you?’ Uttering a derisive laugh, Rāvaṇa then spoke the following words: (8)

verses.text:
अकुतूहलभावेन प्रीतोऽस्मि तव पार्थिव।
धनदस्यानुजं यो मां नावगच्छसि रावणम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “ ‘I am pleased with your equanimity, O king, who do not know me as Rāvaṇa, a younger (half-) brother of Kubera. (9)

verses.text:
त्रिषु लोकेषु कोऽन्योऽस्ति यो न जानाति मेबलम्।
भ्रातरं येन निर्जित्य विमानमिदमाहृतम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: ‘Who else is there in the three worlds, who does not know my might who snatched away this aerial car, after vanquishing my said brother?’ (10)

verses.text:
ततो मरुत्तः स नृपस्तं रावणमथाब्रवीत्।
धन्यः खलु भवान् येन ज्येष्ठो भ्राता रणे जितः॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Thereupon the aforesaid King Marutta forthwith answered Rāvaṇa (as follows): ‘You are praiseworthy, indeed, in that you conquered in combat your own elder brother. (11)

verses.text:
न त्वया सदृशः श्लाघ्यस्त्रिषु लोकेषु विद्यते।
कं त्वं प्राक् केवलं धर्मं चरित्वा लब्धवान् वरम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “ ‘In all the three worlds there is no one who is as praiseworthy as you. Practising what unique virtue did you secure boons in the past? (12)

verses.text:
श्रुतपूर्वं हि न मया भाषसे यादृशं स्वयम्।
तिष्ठेदानीं न मे जीवन् प्रतियास्यसि दुर्मते॥ १३॥
verses.m: “ ‘Nothing like what you say has been heard of by me before. O evil-minded one, tarry awhile; now you will not get back alive. (13)

verses.text:
अद्य त्वां निशितैर्बाणैः प्रेषयामि यमक्षयम्।
ततः शरासनं गृह्य सायकांश्च नराधिपः॥ १४॥
रणाय निर्ययौ क्रुद्धः संवर्तो मार्गमावृणोत्।
सोऽब्रवीत् स्नेहसंयुक्तं मरुत्तं तं महानृषिः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “ ‘With my sharp arrows I will dispatch you to the abode of Yama, the god of death.’ Seizing hold of his bow and arrows, the king thereupon rushed in anger for combat, but Saṁvarta blocked his way. That great sage addressed the following loving words to the said Marutta: (14-15)

verses.text:
श्रोतव्यं यदि मद्वाक्यं सम्प्रहारो न ते क्षमः।
माहेश्वरमिदं सत्रमसमाप्तं कुलं दहेत्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “ ‘If you heed my advice, an encounter is not advisable for you. If left unfinished, this sacrifice, which is intended to propitiate Maheśwara, will consume your race. (16)

verses.text:
दीक्षितस्य कुतो युद्धं क्रोधित्वं दीक्षिते कुतः।
संशयश्च जये नित्यं राक्षसश्च सुदुर्जयः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “ ‘An encounter is out of the question for one who stands consecrated for a sacrificial performance, and temper is also out of the question for such a one; moreover, victory is uncertain in a battle and the Rākṣasa is very hard to vanquish.’ ” (17)

verses.text:
स निवृत्तो गुरोर्वाक्यान्मरुत्तः पृथिवीपतिः।
विसृज्य सशरं चापं स्वस्थो मखमुखोऽभवत्॥ १८॥
verses.m: Bowing to his preceptor’s remonstrance, King Marutta withdrew; throwing away his bow and arrows, he became self-poised and addressed himself to the performance of the sacrifice. (18)

verses.text:
ततस्तं निर्जितं मत्वा घोषयामास वै शुकः।
रावणो जयतीत्युच्चैर्हर्षान्नादं विमुक्तवान्॥ १९॥
verses.m: Taking him to be vanquished, Śuka thereupon raised in glee a shout in a high pitch, saying, “Rāvaṇa has triumphed !” (19)

verses.text:
तान् भक्षयित्वा तत्रस्थान् महर्षीन् यज्ञमागतान्।
वितृप्तो रुधिरैस्तेषां पुनः सम्प्रययौ महीम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: Having devoured the celebrated and great sages who had come to the sacrifice and who were still there, and fully sated with their blood, Rāvaṇa ranged the earth once more. (20)

verses.text:
रावणे तु गते देवाः सेन्द्राश्चैव दिवौकसः।
ततः स्वां योनिमासाद्य तानि सत्त्वानि चाब्रुवन्॥ २१॥
verses.m: When Rāvaṇa had left, the gods and other denizens of heaven including Indra resumed their original form and spoke to these animals. (21)

verses.text:
हर्षात् तदाब्रवीदिन्द्रो मयूरं नीलबर्हिणम्।
प्रीतोऽस्मि तव धर्मज्ञ भुजङ्गाद्धि न ते भयम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: In joy Indra then said to the peacock with a blue tail: “O knower of Dharma, I am pleased with you; there will be no fear for you from the snakes. (22)

verses.text:
इदं नेत्रसहस्रं तु यत् तद् बर्हे भविष्यति।
वर्षमाणे मयि मुदं प्राप्स्यसे प्रीतिलक्षणाम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: Spots resembling these thousand eyes (of mine) will appear in your tail. Nay, when I send down a shower of rain, you will rejoice as a token of love (you cherish for me).”(23)

verses.text: एवमिन्द्रो वरं प्रादान्मयूरस्य सुरेश्वरः॥ २४॥
verses.m: In this way, Indra, the ruler of gods, conferred boons on the peacock. (24)

verses.text:
नीलाः किल पुरा बर्हा मयूराणां नराधिप।
सुराधिपाद् वरं प्राप्य गताः सर्वेऽपि बर्हिणः॥ २५॥
verses.m: Formerly the tails of peacocks were plain blue alone, O suzerain lord of men; after obtaining boons from the lord of the gods, the whole body of the peacocks left. (25)

verses.text:
धर्मराजोऽब्रवीद् राम प्राग्वंशे वायसं प्रति।
पकिं्षस्तवास्मि सुप्रीतः प्रीतस्य वचनं शृणु॥ २६॥
verses.m: Yama, O Rāma ! said to the crow perched on the Prāgvaṁśa* in front of him: “O bird, I am greatly pleased with you; listen to my words which I am addressing to you out of gratification: (26)

verses.text:
यथान्ये विविधै रोगैः पीड्यन्ते प्राणिनो मया।
ते न ते प्रभविष्यन्ति मयि प्रीते न संशयः॥ २७॥
verses.m: ‘As I am pleased with you, the various diseases with which other living beings are tormented by me, shall have no effect on you. There is no doubt about this. (27)

verses.text:
मृत्युतस्ते भयं नास्ति वरान् मम विहङ्गम।
यावत् त्वां न वधिष्यन्ति नरास्तावद् भविष्यसि॥ २८॥
verses.m: ‘In consequence of the boon granted by me, O bird, there is no fear for you from Death. You will live so long as people do not kill you. (28)

verses.text:
ये च मद्विषयस्था वै मानवाः क्षुधयार्दिताः।
त्वयि भुक्ते सुतृप्तास्ते भविष्यन्ति सबान्धवाः॥ २९॥
verses.m: ‘When you have been fed, the people who are in my domain and who are afflicted with hunger, will feel perfectly sated alongwith their relations.’ (29)

verses.text:
वरुणस्त्वब्रवीद्धंसं गङ्गातोयविचारिणम्।
श्रूयतां प्रीतिसंयुक्तं वचः पत्ररथेश्वर॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Varuṇa for his part said to the swan, swimming about in the waters of the Gaṅgā: “O ruler of birds, listen to my words full of love. (30)

verses.text:
वर्णो मनोरमः सौम्यश्चन्द्रमण्डलसंनिभः।
भविष्यति तवोदग्रः शुद्धफेनसमप्रभः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: ‘Your colour will be pleasing to the mind and delightful like that of the orb of the pure moon. It will be white as foam and it will be unique to you. (31)

verses.text:
मच्छरीरं समासाद्य कान्तो नित्यं भविष्यसि।
प्राप्स्यसे चातुलां प्रीतिमेतन्मे प्रीतिलक्षणम्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: ‘Coming into contact with water (which constitutes my body), you will ever look charming and enjoy unequalled delight. This will be a mark of my pleasure.’ (32)

verses.text:
हंसानां हि पुरा राम न वर्णः सर्वपाण्डुरः।
पक्षा नीलाग्रसंवीताः क्रोडाः शष्पाग्रनिर्मलाः॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “O Rāma, in the past the colour of swans was not white all over the body; their wings were dark at the tips, while their breasts were dark-brown like the tips of the panic grass.” (33)

verses.text:
अथाब्रवीद् वैश्रवणः कृकलासं गिरौ स्थितम्।
हैरण्यं सम्प्रयच्छामि वर्णं प्रीतस्तवाप्यहम्॥ ३४॥
verses.m: ‘Then Kubera (son of Viśravā) said to the chameleon, which was resting on a rock: “Pleased with you too, I will confer on you a golden hue. (34)

verses.text:
सद्रव्यं च शिरो नित्यं भविष्यति तवाक्षयम्।
एष काञ्चनको वर्णो मत्प्रीत्या ते भविष्यति॥ ३५॥
verses.m: ‘Your head will always have the imperishable golden colour. Due to my pleasure, your dark colour will be transformed into a golden hue.’ (35)

verses.text:
एवं दत्त्वा वरांस्तेभ्यस्तस्मिन् यज्ञोत्सवे सुराः।
निवृत्ते सह राज्ञा ते पुनः स्वभवनं गताः॥ ३६॥
verses.m: Having granted boons in this manner to the aforesaid animals, the gods, at the completion of the sacrificial ceremony, returned each to his abode alongwith their king, Indra. (36)

verses.text:
अथ जित्वा मरुत्तं स प्रययौ राक्षसाधिपः।
नगराणि नरेन्द्राणां युद्धकाङ्क्षी दशाननः॥ १॥
verses.m: Having conquered Marutta, and thirsting for combat, the notorious Daśānana, the suzerain lord of the Rākṣasas, now sought the capital cities of kings. (1)

verses.text:
समासाद्य तु राजेन्द्रान् महेन्द्रवरुणोपमान्।
अब्रवीद् राक्षसेन्द्रस्तु युद्धं मे दीयतामिति॥ २॥
निर्जिताः स्मेति वा ब्रूत एष मे हि सुनिश्चयः।
अन्यथा कुर्वतामेवं मोक्षो नैवोपपद्यते॥ ३॥
verses.m: Approaching the King of kings, who compared with the mighty Indra (the ruler of gods) and Varuṇa (the god presiding over the waters), Rāvaṇa (the ruler of ogres) actually said to them: “Give me battle or declare that you are defeated. This is my ultimatum to you. No escape is possible for those who act otherwise.” (2-3)

verses.text:
ततस्त्वभीरवः प्राज्ञाः पार्थिवा धर्मनिश्चयाः।
मन्त्रयित्वा ततोऽन्योन्यं राजानः सुमहाबलाः॥ ४॥
निर्जिताः स्मेत्यभाषन्त ज्ञात्वा वरबलं रिपोः।
दुष्यन्तः सुरथो गाधिर्गयो राजा पुरूरवाः॥ ५॥
एते सर्वेऽब्रुवंस्तात निर्जिताः स्मेति पार्थिवाः।
अथायोध्यां समासाद्य रावणो राक्षसाधिपः॥ ६॥
सुगुप्तामनरण्येन शक्रेणेवामरावतीम्।
स तं पुरुषशार्दूलं पुरंदरसमं बले॥ ७॥
प्राह राजानमासाद्य युद्धं देहीति रावणः।
निर्जितोऽस्मीति वा ब्रूहि त्वमेवं मम शासनम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: Consulting one another, the kings for their part, though fearless, highly intelligent, exceedingly mighty and pious of resolve, and recognizing the enemy’s strength which he had derived from boons, then admitted that they stood defeated. Duṣyanta, Suratha, Gādhi, Gaya and King Purūravā—all these monarchs, O beloved Rāma, said, ‘We are defeated.’ Then, duly reaching Ayodhyā, well-protected by Anaraṇya, as Amarāvatī is by Indra, and approaching the monarch, who was a tiger among men and equal to Indra in might, the notorious Rāvaṇa, the suzerain lord of the Rākṣasas, said to him, “Give me fight or say ‘I stand defeated.’ Such is my mandate.” (4—8)

verses.text:
अयोध्याधिपतिस्तस्य श्रुत्वा पापात्मनो वचः।
अनरण्यस्तु संक्रुद्धो राक्षसेन्द्रमथाब्रवीत्॥ ९॥
verses.m: Enraged to hear the command of that sinful-minded fellow, Anaraṇya, the king of Ayodhyā, now said to the king of the Rākṣasas: (9)

verses.text:
दीयते द्वन्द्वयुद्धं ते राक्षसाधिपते मया।
संतिष्ठ क्षिप्रमायत्तो भव चैवं भवाम्यहम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: “O king of the Rākṣasas, I allow you to fight a duel with me, tarry awhile and get ready quickly; I am also getting ready.” (10)

verses.text:
अथ पूर्वं श्रुतार्थेन निर्जितं सुमहद् बलम्।
निष्क्रामत् तन्नरेन्द्रस्य बलं रक्षोवधोद्यतम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: Since Anaraṇya had previous information, he had gathered a huge force. Intent on killing the Rākṣasa, the said army of the king sallied forth. (11)

verses.text:
नागानां दशसाहस्रं वाजिनां नियुतं तथा।
रथानां बहुसाहस्रं पत्तीनां च नरोत्तम॥ १२॥
महीं संछाद्य निष्क्रान्तं सपदातिरथं रणे।
ततः प्रवृत्तं सुमहद् युद्धं युद्धविशारद॥ १३॥
अनरण्यस्य नृपते राक्षसेन्द्रस्य चाद्भुतम्।
तद् रावणबलं प्राप्य बलं तस्य महीपतेः॥ १४॥
प्राणश्यत तदा सर्वं हव्यं हुतमिवानले।
युद्ध्वा च सुचिरं कालं कृत्वा विक्रममुत्तमम्॥ १५॥
प्रज्वलन्तं तमासाद्य क्षिप्रमेवावशेषितम्।
प्राविशत् संकुलं तत्र शलभा इव पावकम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: O jewel among men, ten thousand elephants and a lakh of horses, nay, several thousands of chariots as well as of foot-soldiers then came out on the battlefield, entirely covering the land, inclusive of foot-soldiers and chariots. Then ensued, O warrior skilled in warfare, a very fierce battle between King Anaraṇya, and the king of the Rākṣasas. Encountering the forces of Rāvaṇa, and having fought for a pretty long time and exhibited supreme valour, the entire army of that ruler of the earth was fully consumed like oblations poured into a sacrificial fire. Attenuated in no time on coming in contact with the inflamed Rāvaṇa, the army perished in a body like moths on entering fire. (12—16)

verses.text:
सोऽपश्यत् तन्नरेन्द्रस्तु नश्यमानं महाबलम्।
महार्णवं समासाद्य वनापगशतं यथा॥ १७॥
verses.m: That aforesaid monarch, for his part saw that huge army perishing like hundreds of streams full of water disappearing on reaching the ocean. (17)

verses.text:
ततः शक्रधनुःप्रख्यं धनुर्विस्फारयन् स्वयम्।
आससाद नरेन्द्रस्तं रावणं क्रोधमूर्च्छितः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Then beside himself with rage and twanging his bow, resembling the bow of Indra, the king came up to the notorious Rāvaṇa. (18)

verses.text:
अनरण्येन तेऽमात्या मारीचशुकसारणाः।
प्रहस्तसहिता भग्ना व्यद्रवन्त मृगा इव॥ १९॥
verses.m: The said ministers, Mārīca, Śuka and Sāraṇa alongwith Prahasta, were badly beaten by Anaraṇya and fled like deer. (19)

verses.text:
ततो बाणशतान्यष्टौ पातयामास मूर्धनि।
तस्य राक्षसराजस्य इक्ष्वाकुकुलनन्दनः॥ २०॥
verses.m: Thereupon Anaraṇya (the delight of Ikṣwāku’s race) shot eight hundred arrows on the head of the king of the Rākṣasas. (20)

verses.text:
तस्य बाणाः पतन्तस्ते चक्रिरे न क्षतं क्वचित्।
वारिधारा इवाभ्रेभ्यः पतन्त्यो गिरिमूर्धनि॥ २१॥
verses.m: Though falling on the head of Rāvaṇa, the aforesaid arrows of Anaraṇya did not cause any injury anywhere any more than torrents of water falling from clouds on the top of a hill. (21)

verses.text:
ततो राक्षसराजेन क्रुद्धेन नृपतिस्तदा।
तलेनाभिहतो मूर्ध्नि स रथान्निपपात ह॥ २२॥
verses.m: Then, struck on the head by the enraged king of the Rākṣasas with his palm, the aforesaid king fell from the chariot: so the tradition goes. (22)

verses.text:
स राजा पतितो भूमौ विह्वलः प्रविवेपितः।
वज्रदग्ध इवारण्ये सालो निपतितो यथा॥ २३॥
verses.m: Confused and completely shaken, the said king fell on the ground like a sal tree struck by lightning in a forest. (23)

verses.text:
तं प्रहस्याब्रवीद् रक्ष इक्ष्वाकुं पृथिवीपतिम्।
किमिदानीं फलं प्राप्तं त्वया मां प्रति युध्यता॥ २४॥
verses.m: Making fun of that ruler of Ikṣwāku’s dynasty, Rāvaṇa said, “What have you gained by encountering me, on this occasion? (24)

verses.text:
त्रैलोक्ये नास्ति यो द्वन्द्वं मम दद्यान्नराधिप।
शङ्के प्रसक्तो भोगेषु न शृणोषि बलं मम॥ २५॥
verses.m: “There is none in all the three worlds who can give battle to me, O Lord of men! Deeply addicted (as you were) to sense-enjoyments, I imagine, you did not hear of my might.” (25)

verses.text:
तस्यैवं ब्रुवतो राजा मन्दासुर्वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
किं शक्यमिह कर्तुं वै कालो हि दुरतिक्रमः॥ २६॥
verses.m: To him who was speaking thus, the king, whose life was sinking, replied as follows: “What can be done by me now? For, death is inviolable, indeed. (26)

verses.text:
नह्यहं निर्जितो रक्षस्त्वया चात्मप्रशंसिना।
कालेनैव विपन्नोऽहं हेतुभूतस्तु मे भवान्॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Surely, I have not been vanquished by you, O ogre, who are indulging in self-praise; I stand destroyed by Fate alone and you are a mere instrument in the hands of Death. (27)

verses.text:
किं त्विदानीं मया शक्यं कर्तुं प्राणपरिक्षये।
नह्यहं विमुखी रक्षो युद्ध्यमानस्त्वया हतः॥ २८॥
verses.m: “What can be done by me precisely at this moment when my life is coming to an end? Thank God, I have not been averse to fighting, O ogre, and have been killed while fighting. (28)

verses.text:
इक्ष्वाकुपरिभावित्वाद् वचो वक्ष्यामि राक्षस।
यदि दत्तं यदि हुतं यदि मे सुकृतं तपः।
यदि गुप्ताः प्रजाः सम्यक् तदा सत्यं वचोऽस्तु मे॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Since you have insulted the race of Ikṣwāku, I shall pronounce a curse (on you), O ogre! If a gift has ever been bestowed, an oblation has ever been poured into the sacred fire, and austerities have been practised well and if the people have been well protected by me, let my words prove to be true. (29)

verses.text:
उत्पत्स्यते कुले ह्यस्मिन्निक्ष्वाकूणां महात्मनाम्।
रामो दाशरथिर्नाम स ते प्राणान् हरिष्यति॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Indeed, in this race of high-souled Ikṣwākus will be born a son of Daśaratha, Śrī Rāma by name; He will take your life”. (30)

verses.text:
ततो जलधरोदग्रस्ताडितो देवदुन्दुभिः।
तस्मिन्नुदाहृते शापे पुष्पवृष्टिश्च खाच्च्युता॥ ३१॥
verses.m: When that curse was pronounced, the kettledrum of the gods was sounded at a high pitch like the roar of thunder and an abundance—of flowers were showered from the heavens. (31)

verses.text:
ततः स राजा राजेन्द्र गतः स्थानं त्रिविष्टपम्।
स्वर्गते च नृपे तस्मिन् राक्षसः सोऽपसर्पत॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Then that king, O ruler of rulers, ascended to the realm of heaven. And when the said king ascended to heaven, the ogre left. (32)

verses.text:
ततो वित्रासयन् मर्त्यान् पृथिव्यां राक्षसाधिपः।
आससाद घने तस्मिन् नारदं मुनिपुङ्गवम्॥ १॥
verses.m: While terrorizing the mortals on the earth, Rāvaṇa (the suzerain lord of the ogres) met Nārada one day in the midst of clouds while coursing in the heavens. (1)

verses.text:
तस्याभिवादनं कृत्वा दशग्रीवो निशाचरः।
अब्रवीत् कुशलं पृष्ट्वा हेतुमागमनस्य च॥ २॥
verses.m: Having greeted him and made inquiries regarding his welfare, Daśagrīva, the Rākṣasa, asked him the reason of his visit to the terrestrial region. (2)

verses.text:
नारदस्तु महातेजा देवर्षिरमितप्रभः।
अब्रवीन्मेघपृष्ठस्थो रावणं पुष्पके स्थितम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Sailing on a cloud, Nārada, the Devarṣi of immeasurable effulgence, said to Rāvaṇa who was seated in his aerial car, the Puṣpaka: (3)

verses.text:
राक्षसाधिपते सौम्य तिष्ठ विश्रवसः सुत।
प्रीतोऽस्म्यभिजनोपेत विक्रमैरूर्जितैस्तव॥ ४॥
verses.m: “O suzerain lord of the Rākṣasas and son of Viśravā, O my friend, of noble descent, wait awhile; I am pleased with your noble exploits. (4)

verses.text:
विष्णुना दैत्यघातैश्च गन्धर्वोरगधर्षणैः।
त्वया समं विमर्दैश्च भृशं हि परितोषितः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Indeed, I stand highly gratified by Lord Viṣṇu through encounters killing the Daityas and equally by you through conflicts overcoming the Gandharvas and Nāgas. (5)

verses.text:
किंचिद् वक्ष्यामि तावत् तु श्रोतव्यं श्रोष्यसे यदि।
तन्मे निगदतस्तात समाधिं श्रवणे कुरु॥ ६॥
verses.m: “I, however, O friend, shall presently tell you something which is worth listening to, if you are willing to listen. Pray, concentrate on listening as I speak, O dear son! (6)

verses.text:
किमयं वध्यते तात त्वयावध्येन दैवतैः।
हत एव ह्ययं लोको यदा मृत्युवशं गतः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “What for is this world of mortals being destroyed by you, who cannot be killed even by the gods, O my child? For this world stands virtually destroyed in that it is in the grip of Death. (7)

verses.text:
देवदानवदैत्यानां यक्षगन्धर्वरक्षसाम्।
अवध्येन त्वया लोकः क्लेष्टुं योग्यो न मानुषः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “The world of humans does not deserve to be tormented by you, who cannot be killed even by the gods, the Dānavas and the Daityas, much less by the Yakṣas, the Gandharvas and the Rākṣasas. (8)

verses.text:
नित्यं श्रेयसि सम्मूढं महद्भिर्व्यसनैर्वृतम्।
हन्यात् कस्तादृशं लोकं जराव्याधिशतैर्युतम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Who would destroy people who are utterly ignorant of their higher interests, are surrounded by major calamities and who are subject to old age and hundreds of diseases? (9)

verses.text:
तैस्तैरनिष्टोपगमैरजस्रं यत्र कुत्र कः।
मतिमान् मानुषे लोके युद्धेन प्रणयी भवेत्॥ १०॥
verses.m: “What wise man would love to sow destruction through warfare in the world of human beings, which is constantly afflicted with adverse contingencies here, there and everywhere? (10)

verses.text:
क्षीयमाणं दैवहतं क्षुत्पिपासाजरादिभिः।
विषादशोकसम्मूढं लोकं त्वं क्षपयस्व मा॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Pray! do not destroy people who are being preyed upon by hunger, thirst, old age, and so on, doomed as they are by Fate, and stand bewildered by melancholy and sorrow. (11)

verses.text:
पश्य तावन्महाबाहो राक्षसेश्वर मानुषम्।
मूढमेवं विचित्रार्थं यस्य न ज्ञायते गतिः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “O mighty-armed lord of the Rākṣasas, just look at this world of human beings, who though ignorant are yet addicted to diverse pursuits and to whom what is in store for them is not known. (12)

verses.text:
क्वचिद् वादित्रनृत्यादि सेव्यते मुदितैर्जनैः।
रुद्यते चापरैरार्तैर्धाराश्रुनयनाननैः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “At places instrumental music and dance etc., is enjoyed by men full of delight, while others in distress are crying with tears streaming from their eyes and along their faces. (13)

verses.text:
मातापितृसुतस्नेहभार्याबन्धुमनोरमैः।
मोहितोऽयं जनो ध्वस्तः क्लेशं स्वं नावबुध्यते॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Deluded by fondness for their mother, father and son, and airy projects relating to their wife and other relatives, and fallen from virtue, man does not foresee his own suffering. (14)

verses.text:
तत्किमेवं परिक्लिश्य लोकं मोहनिराकृतम्।
जित एव त्वया सौम्य मर्त्यलोको न संशयः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Therefore, what will you gain by harassing as you do this world of mortals which is already undone by delusion? O friend, the world of mortals stands already conquered by you; there is no doubt about it. (15)

verses.text:
अवश्यमेभिः सर्वैश्च गन्तव्यं यमसादनम्।
तन्निगृह्णीष्व पौलस्त्य यमं परपुरंजय॥ १६॥
verses.m: “All these beings need must seek the abode of Yama; therefore, O scion of Pulastya, subdue Yama, O conqueror of hostile cities! (16)

verses.text:
तस्मिञ्जिते जितं सर्वं भवत्येव न संशयः।
एवमुक्तस्तु लङ्केशो दीप्यमानं स्वतेजसा॥ १७॥
अब्रवीन्नारदं तत्र सम्प्रहस्याभिवाद्य च।
महर्षे देवगन्धर्वविहार समरप्रिय॥ १८॥
अहं समुद्यतो गन्तुं विजयार्थं रसातलम्।
ततो लोकत्रयं जित्वा स्थाप्य नागान् सुरान् वशे॥ १९॥
समुद्रममृतार्थं च मथिष्यामि रसालयम्।
अथाब्रवीद् दशग्रीवं नारदो भगवानृषिः॥ २०॥
क्व खल्विदानीं मार्गेण त्वयेहान्येन गम्यते।
अयं खलु सुदुर्गम्यः प्रेतराजपुरं प्रति॥ २१॥
मार्गो गच्छति दुर्धर्ष यमस्यामित्रकर्शन।
स तु शारदमेघाभं हासं मुक्त्वा दशाननः॥ २२॥
उवाच कृतमित्येव वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्।
तस्मादेवमहं ब्रह्मन् वैवस्वतवधोद्यतः॥ २२॥
गच्छामि दक्षिणामाशां यत्र सूर्यात्मजो नृपः।
मया हि भगवन् क्रोधात् प्रतिज्ञातं रणार्थिना॥ २४॥
अवजेष्यामि चतुरो लोकपालानिति प्रभो।
तदिह प्रस्थितोऽहं वै पितृराजपुरं प्रति॥ २५॥
प्राणिसंक्लेशकर्तारं योजयिष्यामि मृत्युना।
एवमुक्त्वा दशग्रीवो मुनिं तमभिवाद्य च॥ २६॥
प्रययौ दक्षिणामाशां प्रविष्टः सह मन्त्रिभिः।
नारदस्तु महातेजा मुहूर्तं ध्यानमास्थितः॥ २७॥
चिन्तयामास विप्रेन्द्रो विधूम इव पावकः।
येन लोकास्त्रयः सेन्द्राः क्लिश्यन्ते सचराचराः॥ २८॥
क्षीणे चायुषि धर्मेण स कालो जेष्यते कथम्।
स्वदत्तकृतसाक्षी यो द्वितीय इव पावकः॥ २९॥
लब्धसंज्ञा विचेष्टन्ते लोका यस्य महात्मनः।
यस्य नित्यं त्रयो लोका विद्रवन्ति भयार्दिताः॥ ३०॥
तं कथं राक्षसेन्द्रोऽसौ स्वयमेव गमिष्यति।
यो विधाता च धाता च सुकृतं दुष्कृतं तथा॥ ३१॥
त्रैलोक्यं विजितं येन तं कथं विजयिष्यते।
अपरं किं तु कृत्वैवं विधानं संविधास्यति॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “When he is conquered, all stands automatically conquered : there is no doubt about it.” Heartily laughing and greeting Nārada, who was flaming with effulgence, when spoken to in these words, the king of Laṅkā for his part, replied to him as follows: “O great Ṛṣi, who find delight in the company of the gods and the Gandharvas, who are fond of witnessing a conflict, I am fully prepared to proceed to the nether world known as Rasātala with a view to conquering it. Then after conquering all the three worlds and placing the Nāgas and the gods under my yoke, I will churn up the ocean, which is the seat of nectar, for nectar.” The revered Sage Nārada then said to Daśagrīva: “Where, then, are you proceeding to along a different path? Indeed, this path which is extremely difficult to tread, leads to the city of Yama (the king of the departed), O scourge of your foes, who are so difficult to assail.” Uttering a laugh resembling the rumbling of an autumnal cloud, the notorious Rāvaṇa (the ten-headed monster) said: “It is as good as accomplished!” and added the following: “Resolved to make short work of Yama (son of the sun-god), O Brāhmaṇa, I accordingly proceed to the southern quarter, where its ruler, the son of the sun-god resides. Thirsting for an encounter, O Revered Sir, I have actually taken a vow in rage that I shall conquer the four guardians of the world, my lord ! Having now actually set out on my journey to the city of Yama (the king of the departed), I shall accordingly put an end to the torment of living beings.” Having spoken as above, and greeted the aforesaid sage, Rāvaṇa (the ten-headed monster) departed and entered the southern quarter, accompanied by his ministers. Plunged in meditation for a while, Nārada, the foremost of Brāhmaṇas, who was clothed with great effulgence like a smokeless fire, for his part reflected as follows: “How will Death (the Time-Spirit), by whom all the three worlds including the mobile and immobile creation as well as Indra (their ruler) are afflicted in accordance with righteousness when their life has come to an end, be conquered (by Rāvaṇa)? How will that ruler of the ogres approach of his own accord that exalted soul who is like a second fire in brilliance, who is aware of the gifts as well as of the doings of all creatures, through whose energy all created beings derive their consciousness and varied activity and before whom all the three worlds ever recoil fear-stricken? How will Rāvaṇa subjugate him who is the sustainer of the universe and the dispenser of the fruit of their good and evil deeds and by whom all the three worlds stand subjugated? Again, after adopting such a course of conduct (viz., subjugating Yama), what other order will he establish?(17—32)

verses.text:
कौतूहलं समुत्पन्नो यास्यामि यमसादनम्।
विमर्दं द्रष्टुमनयोर्यमराक्षसयोः स्वयम्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “Curiosity having been aroused in me, I shall personally seek the abode of Yama (the god of retribution) in order to witness the encounter of these two heroes, Yama and the ogre, Rāvaṇa.” (33)

verses.text:
एवं संचिन्त्य विप्रेन्द्रो जगाम लघुविक्रमः।
आख्यातुं तद् यथावृत्तं यमस्य सदनं प्रति॥ १॥
verses.m: Having contemplated thus, Nārada (the foremost of Brāhmaṇas), swift of pace, proceeded towards the domain of Yama in order to relate the story as it came to be. (1)

verses.text:
अपश्यत् स यमं तत्र देवमग्निपुरस्कृतम्।
विधानमनुतिष्ठन्तं प्राणिनो यस्य यादृशम्॥ २॥
verses.m: There he saw god Yama, with the (all-witnessing) fire placed before him and dealing out justice to every living being according to the nature of its doing. (2)

verses.text:
स तु दृष्ट्वा यमः प्राप्तं महर्षिं तत्र नारदम्।
अब्रवीत् सुखमासीनमर्घ्यमावेद्य धर्मतः॥ ३॥
verses.m: Offering water to wash his hands with according to the rules of conduct on seeing the eminent Sage Nārada arrived there, Yama for his part said to him when he was seated comfortably: (3)

verses.text:
कच्चित् क्षेमं नु देवर्षे कच्चिद् धर्मो न नश्यति।
किमागमनकृत्यं ते देवगन्धर्वसेवित॥ ४॥
verses.m: “O celestial sage, waited upon by gods and Gandharvas, I hope all is well (with you). I hope righteousness is not wanting. What may be the object of your visit?” (4)

verses.text:
अब्रवीत् तु तदा वाक्यं नारदो भगवानृषिः।
श्रूयतामभिधास्यामि विधानं च विधीयताम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: The revered Sage Nārada for his part then replied as follows: “Listen, I shall presently tell you the object of my visit. And let the necessary remedial measures be taken. (5)

verses.text:
एष नाम्ना दशग्रीवः पितृराज निशाचरः।
उपयाति वशं नेतुं विक्रमैस्त्वां सुदुर्जयम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “O King of the Manes, the ranger of the night, Daśagrīva by name, is presently coming here to subdue you, even though you are hard to vanquish, by his exploits. (6)

verses.text:
एतेन कारणेनाहं त्वरितो ह्यागतः प्रभो।
दण्डप्रहरणस्याद्य तव किं नु भविष्यति॥ ७॥
verses.m: “For this very reason I have come here with all speed, my lord ! I wonder what is going to happen to you now, who hold the rod of punishment for your weapon.” (7)

verses.text:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे दूरादंशुमन्तमिवोदितम्।
ददृशुर्दीप्तमायान्तं विमानं तस्य रक्षसः॥ ८॥
verses.m: In the meantime they saw from a distance the aerial car of that ogre, bright like the rising sun, approaching. (8)

verses.text:
तं देशं प्रभया तस्य पुष्पकस्य महाबलः।
कृत्वा वितिमिरं सर्वं समीपमभ्यवर्तत॥ ९॥
verses.m: Dispelling the darkness of that entire region by the brilliance of the aforesaid Puṣpaka, that very mighty ogre (Rāvaṇa) arrived near. (9)

verses.text:
सोऽपश्यत् स महाबाहुर्दशग्रीवस्ततस्ततः।
प्राणिनः सुकृतं चैव भुञ्जानांश्चैव दुष्कृतम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: That mighty-armed ogre, Daśagrīva, saw everywhere living beings reaping the fruit of their good as well as of their evil deeds. (10)

verses.text:
अपश्यत् सैनिकांश्चास्य यमस्यानुचरैः सह।
यमस्य पुरुषैरुग्रैर्घोररूपैर्भयानकैः॥ ११॥
ददर्श वध्यमानांश्च क्लिश्यमानांश्च देहिनः।
क्रोशतश्च महानादं तीव्रनिष्टनतत्परान्॥ १२॥
verses.m: He also saw the soldiers of Yama alongwith his attendants. He also perceived embodied souls being struck and tortured by Yama’s violent and fierce servants of hideous aspect, and screaming with a bellowing sound and emitting shrill cries. (11-12)

verses.text:
कृमिभिर्भक्ष्यमाणांश्च सारमेयैश्च दारुणैः।
श्रोत्रायासकरा वाचो वदतश्च भयावहाः॥ १३॥
संतार्यमाणान् वैतरणीं बहुशः शोणितोदकाम्।
वालुकासु च तप्तासु तप्यमानान् मुहुर्मुहुः॥ १४॥
असिपत्रवने चैव भिद्यमानानधार्मिकान्।
रौरवे क्षारनद्यां च क्षुरधारासु चैव हि॥ १५॥
पानीयं याचमानांश्च तृषितान् क्षुधितानपि।
शवभूतान् कृशान् दीनान् विवर्णान् मुक्तमूर्धजान्॥ १६॥
मलपङ्कधरान् दीनान् रुक्षांश्च परिधावतः।
ददर्श रावणो मार्गे शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥ १७॥
verses.m: On the way Rāvaṇa saw in hundreds and thousands people being eaten up by worms and fierce dogs and uttering words painful to the ear and causing fright, others being made to cross many times the Vaitaraṇī, the river which flowed with blood, still others suffering pain while being made to tread again and again on burning sands; many more unrighteous souls being split in a grove with sword-like sharp leaves; others being immersed in streams of brackish waters and made to tread on razor blades; others seized with thirst and hunger and begging for water; others no better than corpses, emaciated, wretched and pale, their hair in disarray, bearing dirt and mud on their bodies, helpless and running hither and thither unanointed. (13—17)

verses.text:
कांश्चिच्च गृहमुख्येषु गीतवादित्रनिःस्वनैः।
प्रमोदमानानद्राक्षीद् रावणः सुकृतैः स्वकैः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Rāvaṇa, also saw some people feeling delighted in the best of houses with the sound of vocal and instrumental music by virtue of their own meritorious deeds. (18)

verses.text:
गोरसं गोप्रदातारो ह्यन्नं चैवान्नदायिनः।
गृहांश्च गृहदातारः स्वकर्मफलमश्नतः॥ १९॥
सुवर्णमणिमुक्ताभिः प्रमदाभिरलंकृतान्।
धार्मिकानपरांस्तत्र दीप्यमानान् स्वतेजसा॥ २०॥
ददर्श स महाबाहू रावणो राक्षसाधिपः।
ततस्तान् भिद्यमानांश्च कर्मभिर्दुष्कृतैः स्वकैः॥ २१॥
रावणो मोचयामास विक्रमेण बलाद् बली।
प्राणिनो मोक्षितास्तेन दशग्रीवेण रक्षसा॥ २२॥
सुखमापुर्मुहूर्तं ते ह्यतर्कितमचिन्तितम्।
प्रेतेषु मुच्यमानेषु राक्षसेन महीयसा॥ २३॥
प्रेतगोपाः सुसंक्रुद्धा राक्षसेन्द्रमभिद्रवन्।
ततो हलहलाशब्दः सर्वदिग्भ्यः समुत्थितः॥ २४॥
धर्मराजस्य योधानां शूराणां सम्प्रधावताम्।
ते प्रासैः परिघैः शूलैर्मुसलैः शक्तितोमरैः॥ २५॥
पुष्पकं समधर्षन्त शूराः शतसहस्रशः।
तस्यासनानि प्रासादान् वेदिकास्तोरणानि च॥ २६॥
पुष्पकस्य बभञ्जुस्ते शीघ्रं मधुकरा इव।
देवनिष्ठानभूतं तद् विमानं पुष्पकं मृधे॥ २७॥
भज्यमानं तथैवासीदक्षयं ब्रह्मतेजसा।
असंख्या सुमहत्यासीत् तस्य सेना महात्मनः॥ २८॥
शूराणामग्रयातॄणां सहस्राणि शतानि च।
ततो वृक्षैश्च शैलैश्च प्रासादानां शतैस्तथा॥ २९॥
ततस्ते सचिवास्तस्य यथाकामं यथाबलम्।
अयुध्यन्त महावीराः स च राजा दशाननः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Rāvaṇa, the mighty-armed suzerain lord of the Rākṣasas, saw those, who had gifted cows, drinking milk; others who had gifted food eating food; and still others who had gifted houses residing in houses as the reward of their meritorious doings, and other pious souls decked with gold, gems and pearls and shining in their own lustre in the company of youthful women. By dint of his prowess the mighty Rāvaṇa forcibly liberated those who were being tortured because of their own sinful deeds. The aforesaid living beings liberated by the said ogre, Daśagrīva, enjoyed for a while happiness which was altogether unexpected and unthought of. While the departed were being liberated in this way by the exceptionally mighty Rāvaṇa, the guardians of the dead rushed at the king of the Rākṣasas highly enraged. A great clamour then distinctly arose from all sides among the valiant soldiers of Yama (the king who deals out justice), who ran with all speed (to check the disorder). The said heroes duly assailed the Puṣpaka in hundreds and thousands with spears, iron bars, pikes, pestles, javelins and iron clubs. Like black bees they rapidly demolished the seats, the mansions, the daises and the portals of the Puṣpaka. Though being demolished in combat, that aerial car, the Puṣpaka, which was the seat of gods remained intact by the power of Brahmā, imperishable as it was. The army of that high-souled god was a very huge one; it was past counting; of the heroes who formed the advance guard there were hundreds and thousands. Thereupon the aforesaid ministers of Rāvaṇa, who were all great heroes, as well as the notorious King Rāvaṇa, fought each according to his will and strength with trees and mountains as well as with hundreds of house-tops. (19—30)

verses.text:
ते तु शोणितदिग्धाङ्गाः सर्वशस्त्रसमाहताः।
अमात्या राक्षसेन्द्रस्य चक्रुरायोधनं महत्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: Though all their limbs were smeared with blood, and lacerated by all kinds of weapons, the ministers of Rāvaṇa put forth a major conflict. (31)

verses.text:
अन्योन्यं ते महाभागा जघ्नुः प्रहरणैर्भृशम्।
यमस्य च महाबाहो रावणस्य च मन्त्रिणः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Those glorious ministers of Yama as well as those of Rāvaṇa, O mighty-armed one, struck each of the other party violently with weapons. (32)

verses.text:
अमात्यांस्तांस्तु संत्यज्य यमयोधा महाबलाः।
तमेव चाभ्यधावन्त शूलवर्षैर्दशाननम्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: Leaving alone the said ministers, the exceptionally mighty soldiers of Yama for their part attacked the notorious Rāvaṇa himself with a shower of arrows. (33)

verses.text:
ततः शोणितदिग्धाङ्गः प्रहारैर्जर्जरीकृतः।
फुल्लाशोक इवाभाति पुष्पके राक्षसाधिपः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: Shattered by the adversaries’ blows and his limbs smeared with blood, the suzerain lord of the Rākṣasas in the Puṣpaka thereupon looked like an Aśoka tree in flower. (34)

verses.text:
स तु शूलगदाप्रासाञ्छक्तितोमरसायकान्।
मुसलानि शिलावृक्षान् मुमोचास्त्रबलाद् बली॥ ३५॥
verses.m: That mighty warrior for his part hurled pikes, clubs and spears, javelins, iron clubs and arrows, pestles, rocks and trees by dint of his knowledge of mystic missiles. (35)

verses.text:
तरूणां च शिलानां च शस्त्राणां चातिदारुणम्।
यमसैन्येषु तद् वर्षं पपात धरणीतले॥ ३६॥
verses.m: That most formidable shower of trees and rocks and weapons too fell on the troops of Yama standing on the ground. (36)

verses.text:
तांस्तु सर्वान् विनिर्भिद्य तदस्त्रमपहत्य च।
जघ्नुस्ते राक्षसं घोरमेकं शतसहस्रशः॥ ३७॥
verses.m: Having destroyed all those weapons and repelled the mystic missile itself, they (the soldiers of Yama) struck that redoubtable single warrior, Rāvaṇa, in their hundreds of thousands. (37)

verses.text:
परिवार्य च तं सर्वे शैलं मेघोत्करा इव।
भिन्दिपालैश्च शूलैश्च निरुछ्वासमपोथयन्॥ ३८॥
verses.m: Surrounding him even as masses of clouds would encircle a hill, they assailed him with Bhindipālas and darts so as to suffocate him. (38)

verses.text:
विमुक्तकवचः क्रुद्धः सिक्तः शोणितविस्रवैः।
ततः स पुष्पकं त्यक्त्वा पृथिव्यामवतिष्ठत॥ ३९॥
verses.m: His armour having been severed, nay, bathed in streams of blood and, leaving the Puṣpaka, Rāvaṇa, who was provoked to anger, stood on the ground. (39)

verses.text:
ततः स कार्मुकी बाणी समरे चाभिवर्धत।
लब्धसंज्ञो मुहूर्तेन क्रुद्धस्तस्थौ यथान्तकः॥ ४०॥
verses.m: Regaining his consciousness in a short while, and furnished with his bow and arrows, he thereupon rose in spirit on the battlefield and stood enraged like Death. (40)

verses.text:
ततः पाशुपतं दिव्यमस्त्रं संधाय कार्मुके।
तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति तानुक्त्वा तच्चापं व्यपकर्षत॥ ४१॥
verses.m: Then fitting the divine missile presided over by Lord Śiva to his bow, and saying: “Wait, wait!”, he stretched the bow-string. (41)

verses.text:
आकर्णात् स विकृष्याथ चापमिन्द्रारिराहवे।
मुमोच तं शरं क्रुद्धस्त्रिपुरे शंकरो यथा॥ ४२॥
verses.m: Stretching the bow-string up to his ear, that enemy of Indra forthwith shot the said arrow in rage even as Śaṅkara did at Tripura. (42)

verses.text:
तस्य रूपं शरस्यासीत् सधूमज्वालमण्डलम्।
वनं दहिष्यतो घर्मे दावाग्नेरिव मूर्च्छतः॥ ४३॥
verses.m: With its circle of smoke and flames the said arrow looked like a sylvan fire growing in summer in order to consume a wood. (43)

verses.text:
ज्वालामाली स तु शरः क्रव्यादानुगतो रणे।
मुक्तो गुल्मान् द्रुमांश्चापि भस्म कृत्वा प्रधावति॥ ४४॥
verses.m: Having reduced bushes as well as trees to ashes, when discharged, that arrow for its part with its crown of flames coursed through the field of battle followed by carnivorous animals. (44)

verses.text:
ते तस्य तेजसा दग्धाः सैन्या वैवस्वतस्य तु।
रणे तस्मिन् निपतिता माहेन्द्रा इव केतवः॥ ४५॥
verses.m: Consumed by the blaze of that shaft, the troops of Yama (son of the sun-god) for their part fell on the battlefield like the standards of the mighty Indra. (45)

verses.text:
ततस्तु सचिवैः सार्धं राक्षसो भीमविक्रमः।
ननाद सुमहानादं कम्पयन्निव मेदिनीम्॥ ४६॥
verses.m: Thereupon the ogre of terrible prowess for his part with his ministers uttered a great roar convulsing the earth, as it were. (46)

verses.text:
स तस्य तु महानादं श्रुत्वा वैवस्वतः प्रभुः।
शत्रुं विजयिनं मेने स्वबलस्य च संक्षयम्॥ १॥
verses.m: Hearing that great roar of Rāvaṇa, Lord Yama (son of the sun-god) for his part concluded the enemy to have got the upper hand and that his own forces having perished. (1)

verses.text:
स हि योधान् हतान् मत्वा क्रोधसंरक्तलोचनः।
अब्रवीत् त्वरितः सूतं रथो मे उपनीयताम्॥ २॥
verses.m: Assuming that his own soldiers had been killed, his eyes blood-red with anger, Yama hastily said to his charioteer, ‘Let my chariot be brought.’ (2)

verses.text:
तस्य सूतस्तदा दिव्यमुपस्थाप्य महारथम्।
स्थितः स च महातेजा अध्यारोहत तं रथम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Having brought his huge celestial car, the charioteer stood before him and that god of exceeding energy, ascended the said chariot. (3)

verses.text:
प्रासमुद्गरहस्तश्च मृत्युस्तस्याग्रतः स्थितः।
येन संक्षिप्यते सर्वं त्रैलोक्यमिदमव्ययम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Nay, with a lance and mallet in his hand, the god of death by whom all these three worlds, which are imperishable (in the sense that they spring up and disappear in regular succession) are destroyed, stood in front of him (Yama). (4)

verses.text:
कालदण्डस्तु पार्श्वस्थो मूर्तिमानस्य चाभवत्।
यमप्रहरणं दिव्यं तेजसा ज्वलदग्निवत्॥ ५॥
verses.m: Kāladaṇḍa, the rod of universal destruction, the celestial weapon of Yama, stood at his side in a personal form, blazing with effulgence like a fire. (5)

verses.text:
तस्य पार्श्वेषु निश्छिद्राः कालपाशाः प्रतिष्ठिताः।
पावकस्पर्शसंकाशः स्थितो मूर्तश्च मुद्गरः॥ ६॥
verses.m: On all his (four) sides were installed the nooses of Death which had no rents or holes and there also stood in a personal form a mallet whose impact was like that of fire. (6)

verses.text:
ततो लोकत्रयं क्षुब्धमकम्पन्त दिवौकसः।
कालं दृष्ट्वा तथा क्रुद्धं सर्वलोकभयावहम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: Beholding the Time-Spirit, the terror of all the three worlds, thus provoked to anger, all the three worlds thereupon felt agitated and the denizens of heaven began to tremble. (7)

verses.text:
ततस्त्वचोदयत् सूतस्तानश्वान् रुचिरप्रभान्।
प्रययौ भीमसंनादो यत्र रक्षःपतिः स्थितः॥ ८॥
verses.m: Then the charioteer urged on those steeds which were possessed of a bright lustre, and the chariot advanced with a terrible noise to the spot where the king of ogres stood. (8)

verses.text:
मुहूर्तेन यमं ते तु हया हरिहयोपमाः।
प्रापयन् मनसस्तुल्या यत्र तत् प्रस्तुतं रणम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: In an instant those horses, which resembled those of Indra and were quick as thought, brought, Yama to the spot where the battle was already going on. (9)

verses.text:
दृष्ट्वा तथैव विकृतं रथं मृत्युसमन्वितम्।
सचिवा राक्षसेन्द्रस्य सहसा विप्रदुद्रुवुः॥ १०॥
verses.m: Beholding the said chariot, which was occupied by the god of death and was equally hideous, the ministers of Rāvaṇa (the king of ogres) at once took to their heels. (10)

verses.text:
लघुसत्त्वतया ते हि नष्टसंज्ञा भयार्दिताः।
नेह योद्धुं समर्थाः स्म इत्युक्त्वा प्रययुर्दिशः॥ ११॥
verses.m: Having lost their consciousness, stricken as they were with fear, because of their meagre strength, they actually fled in different directions, unable to fight at this juncture. (11)

verses.text:
स तु तं तादृशं दृष्ट्वा रथं लोकभयावहम्।
नाक्षुभ्यत दशग्रीवो न चापि भयमाविशत्॥ १२॥
verses.m: Even on seeing such a chariot, which was causing fright to the world, that ten-headed monster, Rāvaṇa, however, did not feel agitated nor did fear enter his mind. (12)

verses.text:
स तु रावणमासाद्य व्यसृजच्छक्तितोमरान्।
यमो मर्माणि संक्रुद्धो रावणस्य न्यकृन्तत॥ १३॥
verses.m: Approaching Rāvaṇa, full of rage, Yama for his part hurled javelins and iron clubs and pierced his vulnerable parts. (13)

verses.text:
रावणस्तु ततः स्वस्थः शरवर्षं मुमोच ह।
तस्मिन् वैवस्वतरथे तोयवर्षमिवाम्बुदः॥ १४॥
verses.m: Rāvaṇa, however, who was self-poised, they say, let fly a hail of arrows on that chariot of Yama (son of the sun-god) as a cloud would pour a shower. (14)

verses.text:
ततो महाशक्तिशतैः पात्यमानैर्महोरसि।
नाशक्नोत् प्रतिकर्तुं स राक्षसः शल्यपीडितः॥ १५॥
verses.m: The said ogre, who felt afflicted by the darts while hundreds of huge javelins were being hurled on his mighty breast, was thereupon unable to hit back. (15)

verses.text:
एवं नानाप्रहरणैर्यमेनामित्रकर्षिणा।
सप्तरात्रं कृतः संख्ये विसंज्ञो विमुखो रिपुः॥ १६॥
verses.m: In this way, in the course of a conflict which raged for seven nights continuously the enemy was rendered unconscious and averse to fighting by Yama, the scourge of his foes, who fought with various weapons. (16)

verses.text:
तदाऽऽसीत् तुमुलं युद्धं यमराक्षसयोर्द्वयोः।
जयमाकांक्षतोर्वीर समरेष्वनिवर्तिनोः॥ १७॥
verses.m: Then ensued, O hero, a tumultuous duel between the two warriors, Yama and the ogre (Rāvaṇa), both seeking victory and both not retreating in combat. (17)

verses.text:
ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः।
प्रजापतिं पुरस्कृत्य समेतास्तद्रणाजिरे॥ १८॥
verses.m: Thereupon gods, accompanied by Gandharvas, Siddhas and the highest Ṛṣis, assembled on that battlefield, placing Prajāpati, the creator, at their head. (18)

verses.text:
संवर्त इव लोकानां युध्यतोरभवत् तदा।
राक्षसानां च मुख्यस्य प्रेतानामीश्वरस्य च॥ १९॥
verses.m: While Rāvaṇa (the foremost of the Rākṣasas) and Yama (the lord of the departed) were contending with each other on that occasion, the dissolution of the world appeared imminent. (19)

verses.text:
राक्षसेन्द्रोऽपि विस्फार्य चापमिन्द्राशनिप्रभम्।
निरन्तरमिवाकाशं कुर्वन् बाणांस्ततोऽसृजत्॥ २०॥
verses.m: Stretching his bow, which shone like the thunderbolt of Indra, Rāvaṇa (the ruler of ogres) thereupon discharged arrows, filling the entire space, as it were. (20)

verses.text:
मृत्युं चतुर्भिर्विशिखैः सूतं सप्तभिरार्दयत्।
यमं शतसहस्रेण शीघ्रं मर्मस्वताडयत्॥ २१॥
verses.m: He struck the god of Death with four arrows and the charioteer with seven; with a hundred thousand arrows he swiftly pierced Yama in his vital parts. (21)

verses.text:
ततः क्रुद्धस्य वदनाद् यमस्य समजायत।
ज्वालामाली सनिश्वासः सधूमः कोपपावकः॥ २२॥
verses.m: Then arose from the mouth of the angered Yama, the fire of anger with a crown of flames, accompanied by breath and smoke. (22)

verses.text:
तदाश्चर्यमथो दृष्ट्वा देवदानवसंनिधौ।
प्रहर्षितौ सुसंरब्धौ मृत्युकालौ बभूवतुः॥ २३॥
verses.m: Beholding that marvel in the presence of the gods and the demons, the god of death and Kāla (the Time-Spirit), who were highly enraged were filled with great enthusiasm for the contest. (23)

verses.text:
ततो मृत्युः क्रुद्धतरो वैवस्वतमभाषत।
मुञ्च मां समरे यावद्धन्मीमं पापराक्षसम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: Feeling greatly angered, the god of death said to Vaivaswata Yama (son of the sun-god): “Leave me alone on the field of battle till I make short work of this sinful ogre. (24)

verses.text:
नैषा रक्षो भवेदद्य मर्यादा हि निसर्गतः।
हिरण्यकशिपुः श्रीमान् नमुचिः शम्बरस्तथा॥ २५॥
निसन्दिर्धूमकेतुश्च बलिर्वैरोचनोऽपि च।
शम्भुर्दैत्यो महाराजो वृत्रो बाणस्तथैव च॥ २६॥
राजर्षयः शास्त्रविदो गन्धर्वाः समहोरगाः।
ऋषयः पन्नगा दैत्या यक्षाश्च ह्यप्सरोगणाः॥ २७॥
युगान्तपरिवर्ते च पृथिवी समहार्णवा।
क्षयं नीता महाराज सपर्वतसरिद्द्रुमा॥ २८॥
verses.m: “The ogre would not survive today (on closing with me); such is the natural law. The glorious Hiraṇyakaśipu, Namuci and Śambara, Nisandi and Dhūmaketu as well as Bali, son of Virocana, the giant Śambhu, the great king Vṛtra as well as Vāṇa, royal sages versed in the scriptures, Gandharvas and mighty Nāgas, seers of Vedic Mantras, serpents, (other) giants, Yakṣas as well as hosts of celestial nymphs, nay, (even) this earth including the ocean, mountains, rivers and trees was brought to an end by me, O great king, at the end of the world-cycle. (25—28)

verses.text:
एते चान्ये च बहवो बलवन्तो दुरासदाः।
विनिपन्ना मया दृष्टाः किमुतायं निशाचरः॥ २९॥
verses.m: “These above named as well as numerous other mighty warriors, who were difficult to approach were utterly destroyed as soon as seen by me, to say nothing of this ranger of the night. (29)

verses.text:
मुञ्च मां साधु धर्मज्ञ यावदेनं निहन्म्यहम्।
नहि कश्चिन्मया दृष्टो बलवानपि जीवति॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Leave me perfectly alone, O knower of what is right, till I make short work of this fellow. None who is seen by me, however mighty he may be, can survive. (30)

verses.text:
बलं मम न खल्वेतन्मर्यादैषा निसर्गतः।
स दृष्टो न मया काल मुहूर्तमपि जीवति॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Seen by me, O Time-Spirit, this fellow will not survive even for a short while. This indeed is no power of mine; such, however, is the natural law.” (31)

verses.text:
तस्यैवं वचनं श्रुत्वा धर्मराजः प्रतापवान्।
अब्रवीत् तत्र तं मृत्युं त्वं तिष्ठैनं निहन्म्यहम्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Hearing this utterance of Death, the glorious Yama (the Lord of Justice), on that occasion said to the celebrated god of death, “You stand alone, I will kill this fellow.” (32)

verses.text:
ततः संरक्तनयनः क्रुद्धो वैवस्वतः प्रभुः।
कालदण्डममोघं तु तोलयामास पाणिना॥ ३३॥
यस्य पार्श्वेषु निहिताः कालपाशाः प्रतिष्ठिताः।
पावकाशनिसंकाशो मुद्गरो मूर्तिमान् स्थितः॥ ३४॥
दर्शनादेव यः प्राणान् प्राणिनामपि कर्षति।
किं पुनः स्पृशमानस्य पात्यमानस्य वा पुनः॥ ३५॥
verses.m: Thereupon Lord Yama (son of the sun-god) for his part, his eyes blood-red with anger, lifted with his hand his unfailing rod of punishment, on the four sides of which were installed the snares of destruction and there also stood in a personal form a mallet brilliant as a fire and the thunderbolt, and which extracts the life out of living beings by its very sight, much more of the one who is touched or dashed down by it. (33—35)

verses.text:
स ज्वालापरिवारस्तु निर्दहन्निव राक्षसम्।
तेन स्पृष्टो बलवता महाप्रहरणोऽस्फुरत्॥ ३६॥
verses.m: Touched by that mighty god, Yama, that great weapon for its part with its circle of flames shone as if it were going to consume the ogre. (36)

verses.text:
ततो विदुद्रुवुः सर्वे तस्मात् त्रस्ता रणाजिरे।
सुराश्च क्षुभिताः सर्वे दृष्ट्वा दण्डोद्यतं यमम्॥ ३७॥
verses.m: Afraid of him, all the ogres on the battlefield fled from that place. Seeing Yama with his rod of punishment uplifted, all the gods too felt disturbed through fear. (37)

verses.text:
तस्मिन् प्रहर्तुकामे तु यमे दण्डेन रावणम्।
यमं पितामहः साक्षाद् दर्शयित्वेदमब्रवीत्॥ ३८॥
verses.m: Manifesting himself personally when Yama for his part was inclined to smite Rāvaṇa with his rod, Brahmā (the grandfather of the entire creation) spoke to him as follows: (38)

verses.text:
वैवस्वत महाबाहो न खल्वमितविक्रम।
न हन्तव्यस्त्वयैतेन दण्डेनैष निशाचरः॥ ३९॥
verses.m: “O mighty-armed son of the sun-god, O god with immeasurable prowess, surely this ranger of the night is not to be killed by you with this rod. (39)

verses.text:
वरः खलु मयैतस्मै दत्तस्त्रिदशपुङ्गव।
स त्वया नानृतः कार्यो यन्मया व्याहृतं वचः॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “Indeed, a boon has been conferred on this ogre by me, O bull among the gods ! That boon, the pledge which has been given by me, ought not to be rendered void. (40)

verses.text:
यो हि मामनृतं कुर्याद् देवो वा मानुषोऽपि वा।
त्रैलोक्यमनृतं तेन कृतं स्यान्नात्र संशयः॥ ४१॥
verses.m: “By him, be he a man or a god, who proved me to be a liar, all the three worlds indeed would be accused of lying; there is no doubt about it. (41)

verses.text:
क्रुद्धेन विप्रमुक्तोऽयं निर्विशेषं प्रियाप्रिये।
प्रजाः संहरते रौद्रो लोकत्रयभयावहः॥ ४२॥
verses.m: If discharged by you in anger, this terrible weapon, which is the terror of all the three worlds will destroy all created beings, regardless of those who are dear to you or otherwise. (42)

verses.text:
अमोघो ह्येष सर्वेषां प्राणिनाममितप्रभः।
कालदण्डो मया सृष्टः पूर्वं मृत्युपुरस्कृतः॥ ४३॥
verses.m: “Indeed, this rod of destruction of immeasurable splendour, which is unfailing in relation to all beings, and is attended with death, was created by me of yore. (43)

verses.text:
तन्न खल्वेष ते सौम्य पात्यो रावणमूर्धनि।
नह्यस्मिन् पतिते कश्चिन्मुहूर्तमपि जीवति॥ ४४॥
verses.m: “Therefore, O gentle one, this rod must not be hurled on Rāvaṇa’s head by you; for, in the event of its falling, none will survive even for a little while. (44)

verses.text:
यदि ह्यस्मिन् निपतिते न म्रियेतैष राक्षसः।
म्रियते वा दशग्रीवस्तदाप्युभयतोऽनृतम्॥ ४५॥
verses.m: “In both cases—even if this ten-headed ogre dies or fails to die in the event of this rod falling on him, falsity of my boons will be the result. (45)

verses.text:
तन्निवर्तय लङ्केशाद् दण्डमेतं समुद्यतम्।
सत्यं च मां कुरुष्वाद्य लोकांस्त्वं यद्यवेक्षसे॥ ४६॥
verses.m: “Hence turn aside this uplifted rod from the king of Laṅkā, and thereby vindicate my truthfulness today if you have regard for the worlds.” (46)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तु धर्मात्मा प्रत्युवाच यमस्तदा।
एष व्यावर्तितो दण्डः प्रभविष्णुर्हि नो भवान्॥ ४७॥
verses.m: Spoken to in these words, the pious-minded Yama for his part then said in reply: ”The rod stands diverted hereby, since you are our master. (47)

verses.text:
किं त्विदानीं मया शक्यं कर्तुं रणगतेन हि।
न मया यद्ययं शक्यो हन्तुं वरपुरस्कृतः॥ ४८॥
verses.m: “If this fellow who stands protected by your boon cannot be killed by me, what can be accomplished by me now by continuing on the field of battle ! (48)

verses.text:
एष तस्मात् प्रणश्यामि दर्शनादस्य रक्षसः।
इत्युक्त्वा सरथः साश्वस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत॥ ४९॥
verses.m: “I, therefore, hereby disappear from the view of this ogre.” Saying so he disappeared then and there—chariot, horses and all. (49)

verses.text:
दशग्रीवस्तु तं जित्वा नाम विश्राव्य चात्मनः।
आरुह्य पुष्पकं भूयो निष्क्रान्तो यमसादनात्॥ ५०॥
verses.m: Having conquered Yama, and proclaimed his name, and remounting the Puṣpaka, Rāvaṇa (the ten-headed, monster) emerged from the domain of Yama. (50)

verses.text:
स तु वैवस्वतो देवैः सह ब्रह्मपुरोगमैः।
जगाम त्रिदिवं हृष्टो नारदश्च महामुनिः॥ ५१॥
verses.m: God Yama (son of the sun-god) for his part, as well as the eminent sage Nārada joyously rose to heaven alongwith the gods headed by Brahmā. (51)

verses.text:
ततो जित्वा दशग्रीवो यमं त्रिदशपुङ्गवम्।
रावणस्तु रणश्लाघी स्वसहायान् ददर्श ह॥ १॥
verses.m: Having conquered Yama, the foremost of gods, Rāvaṇa, the ten-headed monster, for his part who boasted of his fighting, then saw his associates in war : so the tradition goes. (1)

verses.text:
ततो रुधिरसिक्ताङ्गं प्रहारैर्जर्जरीकृतम्।
रावणं राक्षसा दृष्ट्वा विस्मयं समुपागमन्॥ २॥
verses.m: Thereupon the ogres felt amazed to see Rāvaṇa bathed all over with blood and shattered by blows. (2)

verses.text:
जयेन वर्धयित्वा च मारीचप्रमुखास्ततः।
पुष्पकं भेजिरे सर्वे सान्त्विता रावणेन तु॥ ३॥
verses.m: Having felicitated him on his victory, and reassured by him in their turn, all the ministers headed by Mārīca then remounted the Puṣpaka. (3)

verses.text:
ततो रसातलं रक्षः प्रविष्टः पयसां निधिम्।
दैत्योरगगणाध्युष्टं वरुणेन सुरक्षितम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: In order to reach Rasātala (the penultimate subterranean region) the ogre then entered the ocean (the repository of waters) inhabited by giants and the hosts of Nāgas (semi-divine beings having the face of a man and the tail of a serpent) and duly protected by Varuṇa (the god of water). (4)

verses.text:
स तु भोगवतीं गत्वा पुरीं वासुकिपालिताम्।
कृत्वा नागान् वशे हृष्टो ययौ मणिमयीं पुरीम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: Proceeding to the city of Bhogavatī, ruled by Vāsuki (the ruler of the Nāgas) and having subdued the Nāgas, he for his part joyously went to the city of Maṇimayī (made of gems). (5)

verses.text:
निवातकवचास्तत्र दैत्या लब्धवरा वसन्।
राक्षसस्तान् समागम्य युद्धाय समुपाह्वयत्॥ ६॥
verses.m: In that city lived a race of giants, known as the Nivātakavacas, who had obtained boons (from Brahmā). Approaching them, the ogre challenged them to a combat. (6)

verses.text:
ते तु सर्वे सुविक्रान्ता दैतेया बलशालिनः।
नानाप्रहरणास्तत्र प्रहृष्टा युद्धदुर्मदाः॥ ७॥
verses.m: The said mighty sons of Diti for their part, who were all exceedingly valiant, were armed with all sorts of weapons and were ferocious in combat, were transported with joy on getting this god-sent opportunity for fighting. (7)

verses.text:
शूलैस्त्रिशूलैः कुलिशैः पट्टिशासिपरश्वधैः।
अन्योन्यं बिभिदुः क्रुद्धा राक्षसा दानवास्तथा॥ ८॥
verses.m: Provoked to anger, the ogres as well as the Dānavas pierced each his opponent with pikes, tridents, thunderbolts, sharp-edged spears, swords and battle-axes. (8)

verses.text:
तेषां तु युध्यमानानां साग्रः संवत्सरो गतः।
न चान्यतरतस्तत्र विजयो वा क्षयोऽपि वा॥ ९॥
verses.m: When they were fighting thus, more then a year actually elapsed and there was neither victory nor defeat for any of the two sides. (9)

verses.text:
ततः पितामहस्तत्र त्रैलोक्यगतिरव्ययः।
आजगाम द्रुतं देवो विमानवरमास्थितः॥ १०॥
verses.m: Seated in his excellent aerial car, the immortal Lord Brahmā, the refuge of the three worlds, then hurriedly came there. (10)

verses.text:
निवातकवचानां तु निवार्य रणकर्म तत्।
वृद्धः पितामहो वाक्यमुवाच विदितार्थवत्॥ ११॥
verses.m: Stopping the said bellicose activity of the Nivātakavacas, the ancient grandfather (of the creation) for his part spoke the following explicit words to them: (11)

verses.text:
नह्ययं रावणो युद्धे शक्यो जेतुं सुरासुरैः।
न भवन्तः क्षयं नेतुमपि सामरदानवैः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Neither can this Rāvaṇa be got the better of in a conflict jointly by the gods and the demons nor can you be exterminated by the Dānavas including the gods. (12)

verses.text:
राक्षसस्य सखित्वं च भवद्भिः सह रोचते।
अविभक्ताश्च सर्वार्थाः सुहृदां नात्र संशयः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Nay, the friendship of the ogre with you finds favour with me. All blessings are held in common by friends : there is no doubt about it.” (13)

verses.text:
ततोऽग्निसाक्षिकं सख्यं कृतवांस्तत्र रावणः।
निवातकवचैः सार्धं प्रीतिमानभवत् तदा॥ १४॥
verses.m: Thereupon Rāvaṇa concluded an alliance with the Nivātakavacas in the presence of the sacred fire then and there and was much pleased. (14)

verses.text:
अर्चितस्तैर्यथान्यायं संवत्सरमथोषितः।
स्वपुरान्निर्विशेषं च प्रियं प्राप्तो दशाननः॥ १५॥
verses.m: Honoured by them according to the rules of propriety, Rāvaṇa (the ten-headed monster) then stayed there for a year and enjoyed pleasures indistinguishable from those of his own city. (15)

verses.text:
तत्रोपधार्य मायानां शतमेकं समाप्तवान्।
