verses.m: In his fury, they say, the ogre, who was so difficult to overcome, spoke as follows to his charioteer, who was still on the chariot: “Take me through the enemy ranks to the place where the other end exists. (6)

verses.text:
अद्यैतान् त्रिदशान् सर्वान् विक्रमैः समरे स्वयम्।
नानाशस्त्रमहासारैर्नयामि यमसादनम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “This very day through feats of valour I shall myself dispatch in combat all the gods to the abode of Death by thick showers of all kinds of weapons. (7)

verses.text:
अहमिन्द्रं वधिष्यामि धनदं वरुणं यमम्।
त्रिदशान् विनिहत्याशु स्वयं स्थास्याम्यथोपरि॥ ८॥
verses.m: “I shall kill Indra, Kubera (the bestower of riches), Varuṇa (the god of water) and Yama (the god of retribution): nay, having destroyed the aforesaid gods in no time, I shall then abide in heaven myself. (8)

verses.text:
विषादो नैव कर्तव्यः शीघ्रं वाहय मे रथम्।
द्विः खलु त्वां ब्रवीम्यद्य यावदन्तं नयस्व माम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Despondency should not be had recourse to in any case; drive my chariot without loss of time; indeed I repeat it to you today, take me to the other end of the army. (9)

verses.text:
अयं स नन्दनोद्देशो यत्र वर्तावहे वयम्।
नय मामद्य तत्र त्वमुदयो यत्र पर्वतः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “The place where we stand just now is a part of the Nandana grove, Indra’s pleasure-garden; take me today to the place where the Udaya (eastern) mountain is. (The celestial host extended from the Nandana grove to the Udaya mountain).” (10)

verses.text:
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा तुरगान् स मनोजवान्।
आदिदेशाथ शत्रूणां मध्येनैव च सारथिः॥ ११॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid command of Rāvaṇa, the said charioteer forthwith drove the horses, which were swift as thought, right through the enemy ranks. (11)

verses.text:
तस्य तं निश्चयं ज्ञात्वा शक्रो देवेश्वरस्तदा।
रथस्थः समरस्थस्तान् देवान् वाक्यमथाब्रवीत्॥ १२॥
verses.m: Coming to know of this resolve of Rāvaṇa, Indra, the ruler of gods, seated in his chariot on the battlefield, forthwith spoke as follows on that occasion to the gods present on the battlefield: (12)

verses.text:
सुराः शृणुत मद्वाक्यं यत् तावन्मम रोचते।
जीवन्नेव दशग्रीवः साधु रक्षो निगृह्यताम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “O gods, listen to my words; what finds favour with me just at this moment is that the ten-headed ogre had better be captured even while alive. (13)

verses.text:
एष ह्यतिबलः सैन्ये रथेन पवनौजसा।
गमिष्यति प्रवृद्धोर्मिः समुद्र इव पर्वणि॥ १४॥
verses.m: “In his chariot, which has the speed of the wind, this very mighty ogre will actually rush through our army like the sea with its swollen waves on the day of the full moon. (14)

verses.text:
नह्येष हन्तुं शक्योऽद्य वरदानात् सुनिर्भयः।
तद् ग्रहीष्यामहे रक्षो यत्ता भवत संयुगे॥ १५॥
verses.m: “He cannot be killed this day in that he has grown utterly fearless due to the conferment of a boon on him by Brahmā; hence we shall capture the ogre; be prepared for this on the field of battle. (15)

verses.text:
यथा बलौ निरुद्धे च त्रैलोक्यं भुज्यते मया।
एवमेतस्य पापस्य निरोधो मम रोचते॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Even as the three worlds are being ruled over by me only because of the demon Bali having been taken captive by Lord Viṣṇu, the incarceration of this sinful ogre finds favour with me likewise.” (16)

verses.text:
ततोऽन्यं देशमास्थाय शक्रः संत्यज्य रावणम्।
अयुध्यत महाराज राक्षसांस्त्रासयन् रणे॥ १७॥
verses.m: Having said so and leaving Rāvaṇa alone, and moving to a different place, Indra fought there causing terror to the ogres on the field of battle, O monarch. (17)

verses.text:
उत्तरेण दशग्रीवः प्रविवेशानिवर्तकः।
दक्षिणेन तु पार्श्वेन प्रविवेश शतक्रतुः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Rāvaṇa (the ten-headed monster), who never retreated from the battlefield, penetrated into the army of gods from the northern side; while Indra (who is supposed to have performed a hundred horse-sacrifices in his past lives as a condition precedent for obtaining the office of Indra) made his way into the army of ogres from the southern side. (18)

verses.text:
ततः स योजनशतं प्रविष्टो राक्षसाधिपः।
देवतानां बलं सर्वं शरवर्षैरवाकिरत्॥ १९॥
verses.m: Having penetrated a hundred Yojanas (or eight hundred miles) deep, the suzerain lord of ogres covered the entire army of gods with showers of arrows. (19)

verses.text:
ततः शक्रो निरीक्ष्याथ प्रणष्टं तु स्वकं बलम्।
न्यवर्तयदसम्भ्रान्तः समावृत्य दशाननम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: Surrounding Rāvaṇa (the ten-headed monster) on perceiving his own army completely destroyed, Indra for his part, who was not the least agitated, thereupon forthwith compelled Rāvaṇa to retreat. (20)

verses.text:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे नादो मुक्तो दानवराक्षसैः।
हा हताः स्म इति ग्रस्तं दृष्ट्वा शक्रेण रावणम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: In the meantime, on seeing Rāvaṇa overcome by Indra, an outcry was raised by the Dānavas and the ogres, saying: “Alas, we are all undone?” (21)

verses.text:
ततो रथं समास्थाय रावणिः क्रोधमूर्च्छितः।
तत् सैन्यमतिसंक्रुद्धः प्रविवेश सुदारुणम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: Taking his seat in a chariot, Meghanāda, son of Rāvaṇa, who felt greatly enraged, nay, who was beside himself with anger, then penetrated deep into the fierce army of gods. (22)

verses.text:
तां प्रविश्य महामायां प्राप्तां पशुपतेः पुरा।
प्रविवेश सुसंरब्धस्तत् सैन्यं समभिद्रवत्॥ २३॥
verses.m: Taking cover under the mighty power of illusion obtained by him in the past as a boon from Lord Śiva, he penetrated deep into the army of gods in fury and completely dispersed the army of gods. (23)

verses.text:
स सर्वा देवतास्त्यक्त्वा शक्रमेवाभ्यधावत।
महेन्द्रश्च महातेजा नापश्यच्च सुतं रिपोः॥ २४॥
verses.m: Leaving all the other gods alone, he rushed on Indra himself; but the mighty Indra, though endowed with extraordinary energy, could not perceive the enemy’s son. (24)

verses.text:
विमुक्तकवचस्तत्र वध्यमानोऽपि रावणिः।
त्रिदशैः सुमहावीर्यैर्न चकार च किंचन॥ २५॥
verses.m: His armour having fallen off on the battlefield, while he was being struck by the gods, who were endowed with exceptional prowess, the son of Rāvaṇa did not entertain the least fear. (25)

verses.text:
स मातलिं समायान्तं ताडयित्वा शरोत्तमैः।
महेन्द्रं बाणवर्षेण भूय एवाभ्यवाकिरत्॥ २६॥
verses.m: Having hit Mātali, who was advancing, with the best of arrows, he then covered the mighty Indra with a shower of arrows. (26)

verses.text:
ततस्त्यक्त्वा रथं शक्रो विससर्ज च सारथिम्।
ऐरावतं समारुह्य मृगयामास रावणिम्॥ २७॥
verses.m: Leaving the chariot, Indra thereupon dismissed the charioteer and, duly mounting the elephant, Airāvata, he began to search for Meghanāda (son of Rāvaṇa). (27)

verses.text:
स तत्र मायाबलवानदृश्योऽथान्तरिक्षगः।
इन्द्रं मायापरिक्षिप्तं कृत्वा स प्राद्रवच्छरैः॥ २८॥
verses.m: Confounding Indra by means of his Māyā (conjuring tricks) while remaining invisible and moving in the air, endowed as he was with the power of Māyā, the notorious Meghanāda assailed him with arrows. (28)

verses.text:
स तं यदा परिश्रान्तमिन्द्रं जज्ञेऽथ रावणिः।
तदैनं मायया बद्ध्वा स्वसैन्यमभितोऽनयत्॥ २९॥
verses.m: Having bound Indra by dint of Māyā the moment he came to know of the former having been worn out, Meghanāda (son of Rāvaṇa) forthwith took him to the flank of his army. (29)

verses.text:
तं तु दृष्ट्वा बलात् तेन नीयमानं महारणात्।
महेन्द्रममराः सर्वे किं नु स्यादित्यचिन्तयन्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Seeing him, the mighty Indra, being borne away by force from the great fight, all the gods for their part wondered what was actually going to happen. (30)

verses.text:
दृश्यते न स मायावी शक्रजित् समितिंजयः।
विद्यावानपि येनेन्द्रो माययापहृतो बलात्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “The notorious Meghanāda, the conqueror of Indra”, they added, “who is an adept in conjuring tricks and has come out victorious in battle and by whom Indra, though skilled in dispelling Māyā, has been borne away by force by dint of conjuring tricks, cannot be perceived.” (31)

verses.text:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे क्रुद्धाः सर्वे सुरगणास्तदा।
रावणं विमुखीकृत्य शरवर्षैरवाकिरन्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: In the meantime, compelling Rāvaṇa to turn his face away (from the field of battle), all the hosts of gods, who were provoked to anger, then covered him with showers of shafts. (32)

verses.text:
रावणस्तु समासाद्य आदित्यांश्च वसूंस्तदा।
न शशाक स संग्रामे योद्धुं शत्रुभिरर्दितः॥ ३३॥
verses.m: Having duly reached the twelve sons of Aditi and the eight Vasus on that occasion, Rāvaṇa failed to encounter them on the field of battle, hard pressed as he was by the enemies. (33)

verses.text:
स तं दृष्ट्वा परिम्लानं प्रहारैर्जर्जरीकृतम्।
रावणिः पितरं युद्धेऽदर्शनस्थोऽब्रवीदिदम्॥ ३४॥
verses.m: Seeing his father languid and shattered by blows in the encounter, Meghanāda (son of Rāvaṇa) spoke to him as follows, remaining invisible all the while: (34)

verses.text:
आगच्छ तात गच्छामो रणकर्म निवर्तताम्।
जितं नो विदितं तेऽस्तु स्वस्थो भव गतज्वरः॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “Come, dear father, we retire. Let the act of fighting come to an end. Let our victory be known to you. Be at ease and free from anxiety. (35)

verses.text:
अयं हि सुरसैन्यस्य त्रैलोक्यस्य च यः प्रभुः।
स गृहीतो देवबलाद् भग्नदर्पाः सुराः कृताः॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “Since the yonder Indra, who was till now the master of the army of gods as well as the lord of all the three worlds, has been captured from the midst of the army of gods, the vanity of the gods has thereby been crushed. (36)

verses.text:
यथेष्टं भुङ्क्ष्व लोकांस्त्रीन् निगृह्यारातिमोजसा।
वृथा किं ते श्रमेणेह युद्धमद्य तु निष्फलम्॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “Having captured the enemy by dint of your might, rule all the three worlds as you please; what will you gain by needlessly exerting yourself any more; fighting is now fruitless.” (37)

verses.text:
ततस्ते दैवतगणा निवृत्ता रणकर्मणः।
तच्छ्रुत्वा रावणेर्वाक्यं शक्रहीनाः सुरा गताः॥ ३८॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid observation of Meghanāda (son of Rāvaṇa), the hosts of gods thereupon desisted from the act of fighting and, deprived of Indra, left for heaven. (38)

verses.text:
अथ रणविगतः स उत्तमौजा-
स्त्रिदशरिपुः प्रथितो निशाचरेन्द्रः।
स्वसुतवचनमादृतः प्रियं तत्
समनुनिशम्य जगाद चैव सूनुम्॥ ३९॥
verses.m: Listening with deference to that agreeable counsel of his son, Rāvaṇa, the ruler of ogres, that notorious enemy of gods, who was endowed with surpassing might, retired from the field of battle and spoke to his son as follows: (39)

verses.text:
अतिबलसदृशैः पराक्रमैस्त्वं
मम कुलवंशविवर्धनः प्रभो।
यदयमतुल्यबलस्त्वयाद्य वै
त्रिदशपतिस्त्रिदशाश्च निर्जिताः॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “You are the promoter of my race, my powerful son, in that the yonder ruler of gods, who was endowed with unequalled might, as well as the other gods, have been actually conquered by you today through exploits which were becoming of your superior might. (40)

verses.text:
नय रथमधिरोप्य वासवं
नगरमितो व्रज सेनया वृतस्त्वम्।
अहमपि तव पृष्ठतो द्रुतं
सह सचिवैरनुयामि हृष्टवत्॥ ४१॥
verses.m: “Placing Indra in the chariot, take him to the city of Laṅkā and, surrounded by your army, depart you from this region. Accompanied by my ministers, I too will follow at your heels with all speed joyfully.” (41)

verses.text:
अथ स बलवृतः सवाहन-
स्त्रिदशपतिं परिगृह्य रावणिः।
स्वभवनमधिगम्य वीर्यवान्
कृतसमरान् विससर्ज राक्षसान्॥ ४२॥
verses.m: Having reached his own abode followed by his army and conveyances and taking with him the ruler of gods, the powerful son of Rāvaṇa dismissed the ogres, who had carried on the operations. (42)

verses.text:
जिते महेन्द्रेऽतिबले रावणस्य सुतेन वै।
प्रजापतिं पुरस्कृत्य ययुर्लङ्कां सुरास्तदा॥ १॥
verses.m: Placing Brahmā, the lord of created beings, at their head, when the mighty Indra, who was endowed with surpassing strength, had been actually conquered by Meghanāda (son of Rāvaṇa), the gods then proceeded to Laṅkā. (1)

verses.text:
तत्र रावणमासाद्य पुत्रभ्रातृभिरावृतम्।
अब्रवीद् गगने तिष्ठन् सामपूर्वं प्रजापतिः॥ २॥
verses.m: Approaching Rāvaṇa, surrounded by his sons and brothers, Brahmā (the lord of created beings), while remaining in the air, spoke (as follows) in conciliatory tones: (2)

verses.text:
वत्स रावण तुष्टोऽस्मि पुत्रस्य तव संयुगे।
अहोऽस्य विक्रमौदार्यं तव तुल्योऽधिकोऽपि वा॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Dear Rāvaṇa, I am pleased with your son’s bearing on the battlefield. Wonderful is the greatness of his prowess. He is thus your equal or even superior to you. (3)

verses.text:
जितं हि भवता सर्वं त्रैलोक्यं स्वेन तेजसा।
कृता प्रतिज्ञा सफला प्रीतोऽस्मि ससुतस्य ते॥ ४॥
verses.m: “By dint of your own energy all the three worlds have actually been conquered by you and your vow stands fulfilled. I am accordingly pleased with you as well as with your son. (4)

verses.text:
अयं च पुत्रोऽतिबलस्तव रावण वीर्यवान्।
जगतीन्द्रजिदित्येव परिख्यातो भविष्यति॥ ५॥
verses.m: “This son of yours, O Rāvaṇa, is exceedingly mighty and powerful, and will henceforth be widely known in the world by the name of Indrajit, the conqueror of Indra. (5)

verses.text:
बलवान् दुर्जयश्चैव भविष्यत्येव राक्षसः।
यं समाश्रित्य ते राजन् स्थापितास्त्रिदशा वशे॥ ६॥
verses.m: “This ogre, relying on whom, O king, you have brought the gods under your subjugation, will surely become powerful and difficult to conquer. (6)

verses.text:
तन्मुच्यतां महाबाहो महेन्द्रः पाकशासनः।
किं चास्य मोक्षणार्थाय प्रयच्छन्तु दिवौकसः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Therefore, let the mighty Indra, the tamer of the demon Pāka, be set free. Again, what should the gods (lit., denizens of heaven) pay to you in consideration for his liberation?”(7)

verses.text:
अथाब्रवीन्महातेजा इन्द्रजित् समितिञ्जयः।
अमरत्वमहं देव वृणे यद्येष मुच्यते॥ ८॥
verses.m: Indrajit, who was victorious in battle and was endowed with extraordinary energy, thereupon replied, “I seek immortality from you, O lord, if he is set free.” (8)

verses.text:
ततोऽब्रवीन्महातेजा मेघनादं प्रजापतिः।
नास्ति सर्वामरत्वं हि कस्यचित् प्राणिनो भुवि॥ ९॥
चतुष्पदां खेचराणामन्येषां च महौजसाम्।
श्रुत्वा पितामहेनोक्तमिन्द्रजित् प्रभुणाव्ययम्॥ १०॥
अथाब्रवीत् स तत्रस्थं मेघनादो महाबलः।
श्रूयतां या भवेत् सिद्धिः शतक्रतुविमोक्षणे॥ ११॥
verses.m: Thereupon Brahmā (the lord of created beings), who was endowed with extraordinary energy, replied as follows to Meghanāda: “There is no immunity from death at the hands of any for any living being whatsoever on earth, for a bird or a quadruped or for other created beings, though endowed with extraordinary might.” Hearing the observation made by Lord Brahmā (the grandfather of the creation), the exceptionally mighty Meghanāda, the notorious conqueror of Indra, forthwith replied to the imperishable Brahmā, who was standing there: “The alternative consummation which may be acceptable to me in consideration for the release of Indra (who is pre-supposed to have performed a hundred horse-sacrifices as a condition precedent for attaining Indrahood) may be known from me. (9—11)

verses.text:
ममेष्टं नित्यशो हव्यैर्मन्त्रैः सम्पूज्य पावकम्।
संग्राममवतर्तुं च शत्रुनिर्जयकाङ्क्षिणः॥ १२॥
अश्वयुक्तो रथो मह्यमुत्तिष्ठेत् तु विभावसोः।
तत्स्थस्यामरता स्यान्मे एष मे निश्चितो वरः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “What is sought by me is that whenever, seeking the utter discomfiture of my enemies, I wish to engage in a fight after duly propitiating the sacred fire through oblations daily while chanting the sacred texts, a huge chariot harnessed to steeds should emerge from the sacred fire before me and immunity from death should be insured for me so long as I remain seated in that chariot. This is the avowed boon sought by me. (12-13)

verses.text:
तस्मिन् यद्यसमाप्ते च जप्यहोमे विभावसौ।
युध्येयं देव संग्रामे तदा मे स्याद् विनाशनम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: “If, O lord, I should engage in fight on the battlefield before the muttering of prayers, and the pouring of oblations into the sacred fire is completed, my death should take place then and then alone. (14)

verses.text:
सर्वो हि तपसा देव वृणोत्यमरतां पुमान्।
विक्रमेण मया त्वेतदमरत्वं प्रवर्तितम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Every person, O lord, seeks immortality through askesis alone. By me, however, such immunity from death is being sought through prowess.” (15)

verses.text:
एवमस्त्विति तं चाह वाक्यं देवः पितामहः।
मुक्तश्चेन्द्रजिता शक्रो गताश्च त्रिदिवं सुराः॥ १६॥
verses.m: Lord Brahmā now gave him the assurance: “Be it so!” Nay, Indra was set at liberty by Indrajit, and the gods returned to heaven. (16)

verses.text:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे राम दीनो भ्रष्टामरद्युतिः।
इन्द्रश्चिन्तापरीतात्मा ध्यानतत्परतां गतः॥ १७॥
verses.m: In the meanwhile, O Rāma, the wretched Indra, whose divine lustre had disappeared, and whose mind was plunged in thought, was lost in contemplation. (17)

verses.text:
तं तु दृष्ट्वा तथा भूतं प्राह देवः पितामहः।
शतक्रतो किमु पुरा करोति स्म सुदुष्कृतम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: Seeing him in that (wretched) plight, Lord Brahmā (the grandfather of the entire creation) said, “O Indra, why did you perpetrate a heinous sin in the past? (18)

verses.text:
अमरेन्द्र मया बुद्ध्या प्रजाः सृष्टास्तथा प्रभो।
एकवर्णाः समाभाषा एकरूपाश्च सर्वशः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Created beings were so evolved by me in my wisdom, O ruler of gods, that they had the same complexion, the same voice and the same form in everyway, O king! (19)

verses.text:
तासां नास्ति विशेषो हि दर्शने लक्षणेऽपि वा।
ततोऽहमेकाग्रमनास्ताः प्रजाः समचिन्तयम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “There was no difference whatsoever in their appearance or even in their distinguishing marks. Hence with a concentrated mind I duly thought of introducing differences in those created beings. (20)

verses.text:
सोऽहं तासां विशेषार्थं स्त्रियमेकां विनिर्ममे।
यद् यत् प्रजानां प्रत्यङ्गं विशिष्टं तत् तदुद्धृतम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “As such in order to make a distinction between them, I evolved a woman. Whatever was striking in every limb of the created beings was reproduced in her. (21)

verses.text:
ततो मया रूपगुणैरहल्या स्त्री विनिर्मिता।
हलं नामेह वैरूप्यं हल्यं तत्प्रभवं भवेत्॥ २२॥
verses.m: “With those features and excellences was created by me, the woman Ahalyā. ‘Hala’ stands here for ugliness and the reproachability following from it is ‘Halya’. (22)

verses.text:
यस्या न विद्यते हल्यं तेनाहल्येति विश्रुता।
अहल्येत्येव च मया तस्या नाम प्रकीर्तितम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: “The woman was widely known as ‘Ahalyā’ in that there was no reproachability in her. Nay, ‘Ahalyā’ itself was proclaimed by me as her name. (23)

verses.text:
निर्मितायां च देवेन्द्र तस्यां नार्यां सुरर्षभ।
भविष्यतीति कस्यैषा मम चिन्ता ततोऽभवत्॥ २४॥
verses.m: “On that woman having been evolved, O ruler of gods, and a jewel among the gods, the thought now haunted me: ‘Whose partner should she be?’ (24)

verses.text:
त्वं तु शक्र तदा नारीं जानीषे मनसा प्रभो।
स्थानाधिकतया पत्नी ममैषेति पुरंदर॥ २५॥
verses.m: “You, however, O mighty Indra, the destroyer of citadels, began to entertain the thought in your mind about that woman: ‘She must be my consort in view of the superiority of my position.’ (25)

verses.text:
सा मया न्यासभूता तु गौतमस्य महात्मनः।
न्यस्ता बहूनि वर्षाणि तेन निर्यातिता च ह॥ २६॥
verses.m: “She was, however, kept by me as a sacred trust in the charge of the high-souled, Sage Gautama, for many years, and was eventually returned by him. (26)

verses.text:
ततस्तस्य परिज्ञाय महास्थैर्यं महामुनेः।
ज्ञात्वा तपसि सिद्धिं च पत्न्यर्थं स्पर्शिता तदा॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Having then tested the extraordinary self-control of that eminent sage and coming to know of the successful conclusion of his austerities, I gave her away to him for being taken to wife on that occasion : (27)

verses.text:
स तया सह धर्मात्मा रमते स्म महामुनिः।
आसन्निराशा देवास्तु गौतमे दत्तया तया॥ २८॥
verses.m: “That eminent and pious-minded sage lived happily with her; on her having been given away to Gautama, however, the gods became despondent. (28)

verses.text:
त्वं क्रुद्धस्त्विह कामात्मा गत्वा तस्याश्रमं मुनेः।
दृष्टवांश्च तदा तां स्त्रीं दीप्तामग्निशिखामिव॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Proceeding to the hermitage of that sage, angry as you were at this, your mind given over to lust, you saw at that time the said woman bright like a tongue of fire. (29)

verses.text:
सा त्वया धर्षिता शक्र कामार्तेन समन्युना।
दृष्टस्त्वं स तदा तेन आश्रमे परमर्षिणा॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “She, O Indra, was violated by you, love-stricken as you were and full of anger. Nay, you were seen on that occasion by the eminent Ṛṣi (a seer of Vedic Mantras) in his hermitage. (30)

verses.text:
ततः क्रुद्धेन तेनासि शप्तः परमतेजसा।
गतोऽसि येन देवेन्द्र दशाभागविपर्ययम्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Thereupon you were execrated in the following words by that supremely powerful sage who was provoked to anger, due to which, O ruler of gods, you had to undergo a reversal of fortune: (31)

verses.text:
यस्मान्मे धर्षिता पत्नी त्वया वासव निर्भयात्।
तस्मात् त्वं समरे शक्र शत्रुहस्तं गमिष्यसि॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “ ‘Since my wife, O chief of the Vasus, was audaciously violated by you, therefore, O Indra, you will fall into the hands of your enemy in war. (32)

verses.text:
अयं तु भावो दुर्बुद्धे यस्त्वयेह प्रवर्तितः।
मानुषेष्वपि लोकेषु भविष्यति न संशयः॥ ३३॥
verses.m: ‘The way of life which you for your part have introduced into this world, O god of perverse intellect, will gain ground even among human beings: there is no doubt about it. (33)

verses.text:
तत्रार्धं तस्य यः कर्ता त्वय्यर्धं निपतिष्यति।
न च ते स्थावरं स्थानं भविष्यति न संशयः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: ‘On him who perpetrates such a sin, only one-half of it will fall to his lot and the other half will accrue to you. Nor will your position be stable: there is no doubt about it. (34)

verses.text:
यश्च यश्च सुरेन्द्रः स्याद् ध्रुवः स न भविष्यति।
एष शापो मया मुक्त इत्यसौ त्वां तदाब्रवीत्॥ ३५॥
verses.m: ‘Whosoever comes to be the ruler of gods shall not endure. This is the curse pronounced by me.’ This is what he said to you at that time. (35)

verses.text:
तां तु भार्यां सुनिर्भर्त्स्य सोऽब्रवीत् सुमहातपाः।
दुर्विनीते विनिध्वंस ममाश्रमसमीपतः॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “Severely reproaching his aforesaid wife, the sage for his part, who was practising rigorous austerities, said, ‘O impudent woman, live unseen in the precincts of my hermitage. (36)

verses.text:
रूपयौवनसम्पन्ना यस्मात् त्वमनवस्थिता।
तस्माद् रूपवती लोके न त्वमेका भविष्यति॥ ३७॥
verses.m: ‘Since you have proved inconstant, though rich in comeliness and youth, you will accordingly no longer be the only comely woman. (37)

verses.text:
रूपं च ते प्रजाः सर्वा गमिष्यन्ति न संशयः।
यत् तदेकं समाश्रित्य विभ्रमोऽयमुपस्थितः॥ ३८॥
verses.m: ‘Nay, all created beings shall henceforth undoubtedly share your comeliness inasmuch as this perversity (occasioned by concupiscence) appeared in the mind of Indra due to that singular comeliness of yours.’ (38)

verses.text:
तदाप्रभृति भूयिष्ठं प्रजा रूपसमन्विता।
सा तं प्रसादयामास महर्षिं गौतमं तदा॥ ३९॥
verses.m: From that time onwards the creation was mostly endowed with comeliness. Ahalyā at that time sought to propitiate that eminent seer of Vedic Mantras as follows: (39)

verses.text:
अज्ञानाद् धर्षिता विप्र त्वद्रूपेण दिवौकसा।
न कामकाराद् विप्रर्षे प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि॥ ४०॥
verses.m: ‘I was unwittingly violated by the god (lit., a denizen of heaven) appearing in your guise, and not according to my own free will, O Brahmarṣi; you ought, therefore, to extend your grace to me.’ (40)

verses.text:
अहल्यया त्वेवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच स गौतमः।
उत्पत्स्यति महातेजा इक्ष्वाकूणां महारथः॥ ४१॥
रामो नाम श्रुतो लोके वनं चाप्युपयास्यति।
ब्राह्मणार्थे महाबाहुर्विष्णुर्मानुषविग्रहः॥ ४२॥
verses.m: Supplicated in these words by Ahalyā, the celebrated Gautama for his part replied as follows: ‘Among the scions of Ikṣwāku will be born a mighty-armed great car-warrior, endowed with extraordinary energy, known in the world by the name of Rāma, and he will proceed to the forest for the sake of a Brāhmaṇa (Sage Viśwāmitra). He will be no other than Lord Viṣṇu in human semblance. (41-42)

verses.text:
तं द्रक्ष्यसि यदा भद्रे ततः पूता भविष्यसि।
स हि पावयितुं शक्तस्त्वया यद् दुष्कृतं कृतम्॥ ४३॥
verses.m: ‘When you will see him, O blessed one, then you will get purified; for he alone is able to eradicate the misdeed that has been done by you. (43)

verses.text:
तस्यातिथ्यं च कृत्वा वै मत्समीपं गमिष्यसि।
वत्स्यसि त्वं मया सार्धं तदा हि वरवर्णिनि॥ ४४॥
verses.m: ‘Nay, after offering hospitality to him, you shall surely return to my presence. Then only, O lady of fair complexion, you will continue to live with me.’ (44)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा तु विप्रर्षिराजगाम स्वमाश्रमम्।
तपश्चचार सुमहत् सा पत्नी ब्रह्मवादिनः॥ ४५॥
verses.m: Having spoken as aforesaid, that Brahmarṣi (a seer of Vedic Mantras) re-entered his hermitage, while the said consort of that teacher of the Vedas practised exceptionally rigid austerities. (45)

verses.text:
शापोत्सर्गाद्धि तस्येदं मुनेः सर्वमुपस्थितम्।
तत् स्मर त्वं महाबाहो दुष्कृतं यत् त्वया कृतम्॥ ४६॥
verses.m: “All this has followed in consequence of the utterance of a curse by that sage. Recall (now), O mighty-armed one, the misdeed which was committed by you. (46)

verses.text:
तेन त्वं ग्रहणं शत्रोर्यातो नान्येन वासव।
शीघ्रं वै यज यज्ञं त्वं वैष्णवं सुसमाहितः॥ ४७॥
verses.m: “Through that curse alone and for no other reason, O Indra, did you fall into the clutches of your enemy. Therefore, perform you with full attention without delay the sacrifice intended to propitiate Lord Viṣṇu. (47)

verses.text:
पावितस्तेन यज्ञेन यास्यसे त्रिदिवं ततः।
पुत्रश्च तव देवेन्द्र न विनष्टो महारणे॥ ४८॥
verses.m: “Purified by that sacrifice you shall return to heaven from the sacrificial ground itself. Your son, too, O ruler of gods, was not destroyed in the great conflict. (48)

verses.text:
नीतः संनिहितश्चैव आर्यकेण महोदधौ।
एतच्छ्रुत्वा महेन्द्रस्तु यज्ञमिष्ट्वा च वैष्णवम्॥ ४९॥
पुनस्त्रिदिवमाक्रामदन्वशासच्च देवराट्।
एतदिन्द्रजितो नाम बलं यत् कीर्तितं मया॥ ५०॥
verses.m: “He was borne away by his maternal grandfather, Pulomā, and has been lodged near him in the ocean.” Hearing this, and having performed a sacrifice intended to propitiate Lord Viṣṇu, the mighty Indra, the ruler of gods, re-ascended to heaven and ruled as before. Such was the might of Indrajit, which has been recounted by me. (49-50)

verses.text:
निर्जितस्तेन देवेन्द्रः प्राणिनोऽन्ये तु किं पुनः।
आश्चर्यमिति रामश्च लक्ष्मणश्चाब्रवीत् तदा॥ ५१॥
अगस्त्यवचनं श्रुत्वा वानरा राक्षसास्तदा।
विभीषणस्तु रामस्य पार्श्वस्थो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ ५२॥
verses.m: By him was conquered the ruler of gods himself. What wonder, then, if other living beings were so conquered? Hearing the narration of Agastya, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa too exclaimed as also the monkeys and the ogres present on that occasion: “Wonderful!” Vibhīṣaṇa for his part who sat beside Śrī Rāma, spoke as follows: (51-52)

verses.text:
आश्चर्यं स्मारितोऽस्म्यद्य यत् तद् दृष्टं पुरातनम्।
अगस्त्यं त्वब्रवीद् रामः सत्यमेतच्छ्रुतं च मे॥ ५३॥
verses.m: “I have been put in mind today of the past miracle which was witnessed by me.” Śrī Rāma too said to Sage Agastya, “This is quite true. Nay, it was heard by me even before from Vibhīṣaṇa.” (53)

verses.text:
एवं राम समुद्भूतो रावणो लोककण्टकः।
सपुत्रो येन संग्रामे जितः शक्रः सुरेश्वरः॥ ५४॥
verses.m: Thus, O Rāma, was born Rāvaṇa, who with his son was a thorn in the side of the worlds, by whom was conquered Indra, the ruler of gods, in an encounter. (54)

verses.text:
ततो रामो महातेजा विस्मयात् पुनरेव हि।
उवाच प्रणतो वाक्यमगस्त्यमृषिसत्तमम्॥ १॥
verses.m: In surprise indeed Śrī Rāma, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, once more thereupon submissively addressed the following words to Agastya, the foremost of sages: (1)

verses.text:
भगवन् राक्षसः क्रूरो यदाप्रभृति मेदिनीम्।
पर्यटत् किं तदा लोकाः शून्या आसन् द्विजोत्तम॥ २॥
verses.m: “Ever since, O revered sir, the cruel ogre, Rāvaṇa, ranged over the earth, were the people (on earth) devoid of manliness at that time, O jewel among the twiceborn? (2)

verses.text:
राजा वा राजमात्रो वा किं तदा नात्र कश्चन।
धर्षणं यत्र न प्राप्तो रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Was there no Kṣatriya king or non-Kṣatriya ruler at that time on the earth, since Rāvaṇa, the ruler of ogres, did not meet with any rebuff? (3)

verses.text:
उताहो हतवीर्यास्ते बभूवुः पृथिवीक्षितः।
बहिष्कृता वरास्त्रैश्च बहवो निर्जिता नृपाः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Or, was it that the said rulers of the earth were lacking in manliness or that they were deprived of good weapons, so that many rulers of men were conquered by him?” (4)

verses.text:
राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा अगस्त्यो भगवानृषिः।
उवाच रामं प्रहसन् पितामह इवेश्वरम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: Hearing the question of Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), the glorious Sage Agastya laughingly replied to Śrī Rāma even as Brahmā would to Lord Śiva: (5)

verses.text:
इत्येवं बाधमानस्तु पार्थिवान् पार्थिवर्षभ।
चचार रावणो राम पृथिवीं पृथिवीपते॥ ६॥
verses.m: “In this way, O jewel among the rulers of the earth, did Rāvaṇa range over the world harassing the kings, O lord of the earth! (6)

verses.text:
ततो माहिष्मतीं नाम पुरीं स्वर्गपुरीप्रभाम्।
सम्प्राप्तो यत्र सांनिध्यं सदासीद् वसुरेतसः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Thereupon he reached the city named Māhiṣmatī, which possessed the splendour of Amarāvatī (the city of Indra) where there was the constant presence of the god of fire. (7)

verses.text:
तुल्य आसीन्नृपस्तस्य प्रभावाद् वसुरेतसः।
अर्जुनो नाम यत्राग्निः शरकुण्डेशयः सदा॥ ८॥
verses.m: “A king, Arjuna by name, who was a compeer of the god of fire in effulgence through the latter’s grace, ruled in that city, where the sacred fire remained ever enshrined in a pit covered with sacred Kuśa grass.” (8)

verses.text:
तमेव दिवसं सोऽथ हैहयाधिपतिर्बली।
अर्जुनो नर्मदां रन्तुं गतः स्त्रीभिः सहेश्वरः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “The same day Arjuna, that mighty and powerful lord of the Haihayas, had just gone to the Narmadā to sport with his womenfolk. (9)

verses.text:
तमेव दिवसं सोऽथ रावणस्तत्र आगतः।
रावणो राक्षसेन्द्रस्तु तस्यामात्यानपृच्छत॥ १०॥
verses.m: “The notorious Rāvaṇa arrived there that very day. Rāvaṇa, the ruler of ogres, for his part spoke to his (Arjuna’s) ministers as follows: (10)

verses.text:
क्वार्जुनो नृपतिः शीघ्रं सम्यगाख्यातुमर्हथ।
रावणोऽहमनुप्राप्तो युद्धेप्सुर्नृवरेण ह॥ ११॥
verses.m: ‘Where is king Arjuna? You ought to point this out accurately without delay. I, Rāvaṇa, have come seeking a trial of strength with Arjuna, the foremost of human kings. (11)

verses.text:
ममागमनमप्यग्रे युष्माभिः संनिवेद्यताम्।
इत्येवं रावणेनोक्तास्तेऽमात्याः सुविपश्चितः॥ १२॥
अब्रुवन् राक्षसपतिमसांनिध्यं महीपतेः।
श्रुत्वा विश्रवसः पुत्रः पौराणामर्जुनं गतम्॥ १३॥
अपसृत्यागतो विन्ध्यं हिमवत्संनिभं गिरिम्।
स तमभ्रमिवाविष्टमुद्भ्रान्तमिव मेदिनीम्॥ १४॥
अपश्यद् रावणो विन्ध्यमालिखन्तमिवाम्बरम्।
सहस्रशिखरोपेतं सिंहाध्युषितकन्दरम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Let my arrival be duly made known to him in advance by you.’ Spoken to as aforesaid by Rāvaṇa, the said ministers (of Arjuna), who were all very wise, told the ruler of ogres of the king’s absence from the capital. Withdrawing from that place on hearing, from the mouth of the citizens, of Arjuna having left the city, Rāvaṇa (son of Viśravā) sought the Vindhya mountain, which closely resembled the Himālayas in height. “Rāvaṇa saw the Vindhya mountain which having penetrated into the clouds as it were and having as though burst forth from the earth, seemed to scrape the skies. It had thousands of peaks, and its caves were infested with lions. (12—15)

verses.text:
प्रपातपतितैः शीतैः साट्टहासमिवाम्बुभिः।
देवदानवगन्धर्वैः साप्सरोभिः सकिंनरैः॥ १६॥
स्वस्त्रीभिः क्रीडमानैश्च स्वर्गभूतं महोच्छ्रयम्।
नदीभिः स्यन्दमानाभिः स्फटिकप्रतिमं जलम्॥ १७॥
फणाभिश्चलजिह्वाभिरनन्तमिव विष्ठितम्।
उत्क्रामन्तं दरीवन्तं हितवत्संनिभं गिरिम्॥ १८॥
पश्यमानस्ततो विन्ध्यं रावणो नर्मदां ययौ।
चलोपलजलां पुण्यां पश्चिमोदधिगामिनीम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: “With cool waters fallen from the hills, it seemed to utter a horse-laugh. With gods, Dānavas and Gandharvas, accompanied by Apsarās (celestial nymphs) and Kinnaras, and sporting with their womenfolk, the mountain, which was exceptionally high, had turned into heaven. With its rivers carrying crystal-clear waters the mountain stood rooted like the serpent-god Śeṣa with his thousand hoods distinguished by restless tongues. Beholding the Vindhya mountain, which was moving upwards, as it were, which abounded in caves and closely resembled the Himalayan range, Rāvaṇa sought the holy river Narmadā, whose waters flowed over a bed of rocks and which ran towards the western sea. (16—19)

verses.text:
महिषैः सृमरैः सिंहैः शार्दूलर्क्षगजोत्तमैः।
उष्णाभितप्तैस्तृषितैः संक्षोभितजलाशयाम्॥ २०॥
चक्रवाकैः सकारण्डैः सहंसजलकुक्कुटैः।
सारसैश्च सदा मत्तैः कूजद्भिः सुसमावृताम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “The ponds forming a part of the river were ruffled by buffaloes, young deer, lions, bears and lordly elephants scorched by heat, and seized with thirst and the river was thickly crowded with ruddy geese accompanied by wild ducks, swans and water-fowls as well as with cranes ever in heat and screaming. (20-21)

verses.text:
फुल्लद्रुमकृतोत्तंसां चक्रवाकयुगस्तनीम्।
विस्तीर्णपुलिनश्रोणीं हंसावलिसुमेखलाम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: “The river had trees in blossom for its diadem, a pair of Cakrawāka birds for its breasts, extensive sandy banks for its hips, rows of swans for its lovely girdle. (22)

verses.text:
पुष्परेण्वनुलिप्ताङ्गीं जलफेनामलांशुकाम्।
जलावगाहसुस्पर्शां फुल्लोत्पलशुभेक्षणाम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: “It had its limbs powdered with the pollen of flowers, it had the foam for its immaculate robe; a dip into its waters constituted its thrilling contact and it had full-blown lotuses for its charming eyes. (23)

verses.text:
पुष्पकादवरुह्याशु नर्मदां सरितां वराम्।
इष्टामिव वरां नारीमवगाह्य दशाननः॥ २४॥
स तस्याः पुलिने रम्ये नानामुनिनिषेविते।
उपोपविष्टः सचिवैः सार्धं राक्षसपुङ्गवः॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Quickly alighting from the Puṣpaka car, and taking a dip in the Narmadā, the foremost of rivers, which thus resembled an excellent and agreeable woman, that ten-headed bull among the ogres, sat down in the company of his ministers on its lovely bank, frequented by sages. (24-25)

verses.text:
प्रख्याय नर्मदां सोऽथ गङ्गेयमिति रावणः।
नर्मदादर्शने हर्षमाप्तवान् स दशाननः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Complimenting the Narmadā in the words ‘Here is the holy Gaṅgā,’ the notorious Rāvaṇa, that ten-headed monster, forthwith experienced delight at the sight of the Narmadā. (26)

verses.text:
उवाच सचिवांस्तत्र सलीलं शुकसारणौ।
एष रश्मिसहस्रेण जगत् कृत्वेव काञ्चनम्॥ २७॥
तीक्ष्णतापकरः सूर्यो नभसो मध्यमास्थितः।
मामासीनं विदित्वैव चन्द्रायति दिवाकरः॥ २८॥
verses.m: “He playfully said to his ministers, as well as to Śuka and Sāraṇa ‘Having turned the world golden-coloured as it were by its myriad rays, the yonder sun, the maker of the day, which should generate intense heat, its position being located in mid heavens, has grown cool as the moon merely on perceiving me seated on this spot. (27-28)

verses.text:
नर्मदाजलशीतश्च सुगन्धिः श्रमनाशनः।
मद्भयादनिलो ह्येष वात्यसौ सुसमाहितः॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Cooled by its contact with the waters of the Narmadā, fragrant and relieving fatigue, this breeze is blowing softly indeed due to fear of me. (29)

verses.text:
इयं वापि सरिच्छ्रेष्ठा नर्मदा नर्मवर्धिनी।
नक्रमीनविहंगोर्मिः सभयेवाङ्गना स्थिता॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Bearing crocodiles, fishes and birds on its waves, this Narmadā, the foremost of rivers, too, which heightens my merriment, looks like a timid girl. (30)

verses.text:
तद्भवन्तः क्षताः शस्त्रैर्नृपैरिन्द्रसमैर्युधि।
चन्दनस्य रसेनेव रुधिरेण समुक्षिताः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “You stand pierced with weapons by kings vying with Indra on the field of battle and bathed in blood as though sprinkled all over with the sap of a red sandal tree. (31)

verses.text:
ते यूयमवगाहध्वं नर्मदां शर्मदां शुभाम्।
सार्वभौममुखा मत्ता गङ्गामिव महागजाः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “As such take you a dip in the lovely and delightful Narmadā even as huge elephants (guarding the quarters) in rut—Sārvabhauma and others—take a dip in the Gaṅgā. (32)

verses.text:
अस्यां स्नात्वा महानद्यां पाप्मनो विप्रमोक्ष्यथ।
अहमप्यद्य पुलिने शरदिन्दुसमप्रभे॥ ३३॥
पुष्पोपहारं शनकैः करिष्यामि कपर्दिनः।
रावणेनैवमुक्तास्तु प्रहस्तशुकसारणाः॥ ३४॥
समहोदरधूम्राक्षा नर्मदां विजगाहिरे।
राक्षसेन्द्रगजैस्तैस्तु क्षोभिता नर्मदा नदी॥ ३५॥
वामनाञ्जनपद्माद्यैर्गङ्गा इव महागजैः।
ततस्ते राक्षसाः स्नात्वा नर्मदायां महाबलाः॥ ३६॥
उत्तीर्य पुष्पाण्याजह्रुर्बल्यर्थं रावणस्य तु।
नर्मदापुलिने हृद्ये शुभ्राभ्रसदृशप्रभे॥ ३७॥
राक्षसैस्तु मुहूर्तेन कृतः पुष्पमयो गिरिः।
पुष्पेषूपहृतेष्वेवं रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः॥ ३८॥
अवतीर्णो नदीं स्नातुं गङ्गामिव महागजः।
तत्र स्नात्वा च विधिवज्जप्त्वा जप्यमनुत्तमम्॥ ३९॥
नर्मदासलिलात् तस्मादुत्ततार स रावणः।
ततः क्लिन्नाम्बरं त्यक्त्वा शुक्लवस्त्रसमावृतः॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “Bathing in this great river, you will be completely rid of your sin. I too shall presently offer flowers slowly to Lord Śiva (who wears matted locks on His head) on this sandy bank, shining like the autumnal moon.” Commanded in these words by Rāvaṇa, Prahasta, Śuka and Sāraṇa for their part, accompanied by Mahodara and Dhūmrākṣa, took a dip in the Narmadā. The river Narmadā for its part was ruffled by those elephants of Rāvaṇa (the ruler of ogres) even as the Gaṅgā by the mighty elephants (guarding the quarters), Vāmana, Añjana, Padma and others. Emerging after taking a dip in the Narmadā, these exceptionally mighty ogres for their part fetched flowers for Rāvaṇa’s worship of Lord Śiva. On the delightful sandy bank of the Narmadā, shining like a white cloud, a mountain of flowers was raised in less than an hour by the ogres. When flowers had been collected in this way, Rāvaṇa, the king of ogres, descended into the river to bathe even as a huge elephant would into the Gaṅgā. Having bathed in the river and muttered the most excellent text, the Gāyatrī Mantra, with due ceremony, the notorious Rāvaṇa came out of the well-known waters of the Narmadā. Then putting off the wet clothes, he was duly covered with a white robe. (33—40)

verses.text:
रावणं प्राञ्जलिं यान्तमन्वयुः सर्वराक्षसाः।
तद्गतीवशमापन्ना मूर्तिमन्त इवाचलाः॥ ४१॥
verses.m: Like incarnate mountains swayed by his motion, all the other ogres followed him even as he proceeded with joined palms to offer flowers to Lord Śiva. (41)

verses.text:
यत्र यत्र च याति स्म रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः।
जाम्बूनदमयं लिङ्गं तत्र तत्र स्म नीयते॥ ४२॥
verses.m: Wherever Rāvaṇa, the ruler of ogres, went, a golden emblem of Lord Śiva was borne there. (42)

verses.text:
वालुकावेदिमध्ये तु तल्लिङ्गं स्थाप्य रावणः।
अर्चयामास गन्धैश्च पुष्पैश्चामृतगन्धिभिः॥ ४३॥
verses.m: Placing the said emblem in the middle of an altar of sand, Rāvaṇa for his part worshipped it with sandal-pastes (of various kinds) and flowers, of undying fragrance. (43)

verses.text:
ततः सतामार्तिहरं परं वरं
वरप्रदं चन्द्रमयूखभूषणम्।
समर्चयित्वा स निशाचरो जगौ
प्रसार्य हस्तान् प्रणनर्त चाग्रतः॥ ४४॥
verses.m: Having duly worshipped the supreme and most excellent Lord Śiva (who bears moonbeams on His head as an ornament), the reliever of the agony of the virtuous and the bestower of boons, the said ranger of the night sang and, stretching his arms gaily danced before Him. (44)

verses.text:
नर्मदापुलिने यत्र राक्षसेन्द्रः स दारुणः।
पुष्पोपहारं कुरुते तस्माद् देशाददूरतः॥ १॥
अर्जुनो जयतां श्रेष्ठो माहिष्मत्याः पतिः प्रभुः।
क्रीडते सह नारीभिर्नर्मदातोयमाश्रितः॥ २॥
verses.m: Not far from the place where, on the sandy bank of the Narmadā, the dread king of ogres was offering flowers to Lord Śiva, Arjuna, the powerful ruler of Māhiṣmatī and the foremost of conquerors, was sporting with his womenfolk in the waters of the Narmadā. (1-2)

verses.text:
तासां मध्यगतो राजा रराज च तदार्जुनः।
करेणूनां सहस्रस्य मध्यस्थ इव कुञ्जरः॥ ३॥
verses.m: Standing in their midst, King Arjuna shone at the moment like an elephant in the midst of a thousand of she-elephants. (3)

verses.text:
जिज्ञासुः स तु बाहूनां सहस्रस्योत्तमं बलम्।
रुरोध नर्मदावेगं बाहुभिर्बहुभिर्वृतः॥ ४॥
verses.m: Seeking to know the maximum strength of his thousand arms, Arjuna for his part, who was endowed with numerous arms, blocked the Narmadā. (4)

verses.text:
कार्तवीर्यभुजासक्तं तज्जलं प्राप्य निर्मलम्।
कूलोपहारं कुर्वाणं प्रतिस्रोतः प्रधावति॥ ५॥
verses.m: Reaching Rāvaṇa, who was offering flowers to Lord Śiva on a sandy bank of the Narmadā, when held up by the arms of Arjuna (son of Kṛtavīrya), the transparent waters of the Narmadā began to flow rapidly upstream. (5)

verses.text:
समीननक्रमकरः सपुष्पकुशसंस्तरः।
स नर्मदाम्भसो वेगः प्रावृट्काल इवाबभौ॥ ६॥
verses.m: The vehemence of the Narmadā, flowing as it did with its fishes, crocodiles and alligators as also with its flowers and layers of sacred Kuśa grass (spread out at a sacrifice), looked as it did during the monsoon. (6)

verses.text:
स वेगः कार्तवीर्येण सम्प्रेषित इवाम्भसः।
पुष्पोपहारं सकलं रावणस्य जहार ह॥ ७॥
verses.m: That rapid flow of water, as though impelled by Arjuna (son of Kṛtavīrya), they say, swept away all the flowers that had been collected for being offered to Lord Śiva by Rāvaṇa. (7)

verses.text:
रावणोऽर्धसमाप्तं तमुत्सृज्य नियमं तदा।
नर्मदां पश्यते कान्तां प्रतिकूलां यथा प्रियाम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: Leaving the observance when it was only half-way through, Rāvaṇa looked at the Narmadā as if one would look upon one’s beloved wife turned refractory. (8)

verses.text:
पश्चिमेन तु तं दृष्ट्वा सागरोद्गारसंनिभम्।
वर्धन्तमम्भसो वेगं पूर्वामाशां प्रविश्य तु॥ ९॥
ततोऽनुद्भ्रान्तशकुनां स्वभावे परमे स्थिताम्।
निर्विकाराङ्गनाभासामपश्यद् रावणो नदीम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: Surveying the rapid flow of water from the west gathering force on entering the east like the flood-tide in a sea, Rāvaṇa for his part found the river existing in its absolutely natural state, as was evident from the fact that the birds did not feel the least bewildered and thus resembling a lady free from agitation. (9-10)

verses.text:
सव्येतरकराङ्गुल्या ह्यशब्दास्यो दशाननः।
वेगप्रभवमन्वेष्टुं सोऽदिशच्छुकसारणौ॥ ११॥
verses.m: Without uttering a word with his mouth, that ten-headed monster directed with a finger of his right hand Śuka and Sāraṇa to seek out the cause of the rapid flow. (11)

verses.text:
तौ तु रावणसंदिष्टौ भ्रातरौ शुकसारणौ।
व्योमान्तरगतौ वीरौ प्रस्थितौ पश्चिमामुखौ॥ १२॥
verses.m: Commanded by Rāvaṇa, the two heroic brothers, Śuka and Sāraṇa, set out with their faces turned towards the west, coursing through the airspace. (12)

verses.text:
अर्धयोजनमात्रं तु गत्वा तौ रजनीचरौ।
पश्येतां पुरुषं तोये क्रीडन्तं सहयोषितम्॥ १३॥
बृहत्सालप्रतीकाशं तोयव्याकुलमूर्धजम्।
मदरक्तान्तनयनं मदव्याकुलचेतसम्॥ १४॥
नदीं बाहुसहस्रेण रुन्धन्तमरिमर्दनम्।
गिरिं पादसहस्रेण रुन्धन्तमिव मेदिनीम्॥ १५॥
बालानां वरनारीणां सहस्रेण समावृतम्।
समदानां करेणूनां सहस्रेणेव कुञ्जरम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: Advancing half a Yojana (four miles) only, the aforesaid rangers of the night saw sporting with women in the waters a man resembling a huge sal tree, his hair tossed about in the waters, the corners of his eyes red through inebriety and his mind distracted through intoxication, and capable of crushing his enemy, blocking the river with his thousand arms, even as a mountain would block the earth with its thousand offshoots, and surrounded by a thousand comely young women like an elephant surrounded by a thousand she-elephants in rut. (13—16)

verses.text:
तमद्भुततरं दृष्ट्वा राक्षसौ शुकसारणौ।
संनिवृत्तावुपागम्य रावणं तमथोचतुः॥ १७॥
verses.m: Beholding that highly prodigious man, the ogres, Śuka and Sāraṇa turned back and, approaching Rāvaṇa, spoke to him as follows: (17)

verses.text:
बृहत्सालप्रतीकाशः कोऽप्यसौ राक्षसेश्वर।
नर्मदां रोधवद् रुद्ध्वा क्रीडापयति योषितः॥ १८॥
verses.m: ‘Blocking the Narmadā like a dyke, O ruler of ogres, an unknown person, resembling an enormous sal tree, is providing amusement to women. (18)

verses.text:
तेन बाहुसहस्रेण संनिरुद्धजला नदी।
सागरोद्गारसंकाशानुद्गारान् सृजते मुहुः॥ १९॥
verses.m: ‘With its waters blocked by him with his thousand arms, the river is repeatedly disgorging volumes of water resembling the flood-tide in a sea.’ (19)

verses.text:
इत्येवं भाषमाणौ तौ निशम्य शुकसारणौ।
रावणोऽर्जुन इत्युक्त्वा स ययौ युद्धलालसः॥ २०॥
verses.m: Saying “So it is!” Arjuna, on hearing the aforesaid Śuka and Sāraṇa speaking as above, the notorious Rāvaṇa sallied forth, thirsting for an encounter. (20)

verses.text:
अर्जुनाभिमुखे तस्मिन् रावणे राक्षसाधिपे।
चण्डः प्रवाति पवनः सनादः सरजस्तथा॥ २१॥
verses.m: When Rāvaṇa, the suzerain lord of ogres, set forth with his face directed towards Arjuna, the wind blew furiously with a noise and dust. (21)

verses.text:
सकृदेव कृतो रावः सरक्तपृषतो घनैः।
महोदरमहापार्श्वधूम्राक्षशुकसारणैः ॥ २२॥
संवृतो राक्षसेन्द्रस्तु तत्रागाद् यत्र चार्जुनः।
अदीर्घेणैव कालेन स तदा राक्षसो बली॥ २३॥
तं नर्मदाह्रदं भीममाजगामाञ्जनप्रभः।
स तत्र स्त्रीपरिवृतं वासिताभिरिव द्विपम्॥ २४॥
नरेन्द्रं पश्यते राजा राक्षसानां तदार्जुनम्।
स रोषाद् रक्तनयनो राक्षसेन्द्रो बलोद्धतः॥ २५॥
इत्येवमर्जुनामात्यानाह गम्भीरया गिरा।
अमात्याः क्षिप्रमाख्यात हैहयस्य नृपस्य वै॥ २६॥
युद्धार्थं समनुप्राप्तो रावणो नाम नामतः।
रावणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा मन्त्रिणोऽथार्जुनस्य ते॥ २७॥
उत्तस्थुः सायुधास्तं च रावणं वाक्यमब्रुवन्।
युद्धस्य कालो विज्ञातः साधु भो साधु रावण॥ २८॥
यः क्षीबं स्त्रीगतं चैव योद्धुमुत्सहसे नृपम्।
स्त्रीसमक्षगतं यत् त्वं योद्धुमुत्सहसे नृप॥ २९॥
वासितामध्यगं मत्तं शार्दूल इव कुञ्जरम्।
क्षमस्वाद्य दशग्रीव उष्यतां रजनी त्वया।
युद्धे श्रद्धा तु यद्यस्ति श्वस्तात समरेऽर्जुनम्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: A peal of thunder was emitted by the clouds with drops of blood. Nay, protected by Mahodara, Mahāpārśwa, Dhūmrākṣa, Śuka and Sāraṇa, the ruler of ogres for his part arrived at the place where Arjuna was sporting. In a short time that mighty ogre, who shone as antimony, reached the frightful pool forming part of the Narmadā. There the king of ogres saw at that moment King Arjuna surrounded by women as an elephant by she-elephants. His eyes red through anger, that ruler of ogres, who was arrogant by reason of his might, spoke as follows to the ministers of Arjuna in a deep tone: “O ministers, make it known quickly to the king of the Haihayas that a warrior, Rāvaṇa by name, has actually come to him for an encounter.” Hearing the challenge of Rāvaṇa, the aforesaid ministers of Arjuna forthwith sprang on their feet, armed with weapons, and submitted as follows to the notorious Rāvaṇa: “Well! The time suitable for a trial of strength is indeed well-known to you, O Rāvaṇa, in that you feel inclined to enter into a combat with a prince who is drunk and in the company of women! Since, O king, you seek to fight with one who stands in the presence of womenfolk, even as a tiger would seek to fight with an elephant in rut standing in the midst of she-elephants. Have patience today, O ten-headed monster, and let the night be spent here by you; if there is keenness in you for a combat, fight Arjuna tomorrow, O dear friend! (22—30)

verses.text:
यदि वापि त्वरा तुभ्यं युद्धतृष्णासमावृता।
निपात्यास्मान् रणे युद्धमर्जुनेनोपयास्यसि॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “If, however, you are in a hurry, O warrior seized with a thirst for combat, you will have an opportunity for an encounter with Arjuna only after overthrowing us in combat.” (31)

verses.text:
ततस्तै रावणामात्यैरमात्यास्ते नृपस्य तु।
सूदिताश्चापि ते युद्धे भक्षिताश्च बुभुक्षितैः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: The aforesaid ministers of King Arjuna for their part were thereupon killed in combat and devoured by the said ministers of Rāvaṇa who were all seized with hunger. (32)

verses.text:
ततो हलहलाशब्दो नर्मदातीरगो बभौ।
अर्जुनस्यानुयात्राणां रावणस्य च मन्त्रिणाम्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: An uproar then arose on the bank of the Narmadā among the followers of King Arjuna and the ministers of Rāvaṇa. (33)

verses.text:
इषुभिस्तोमरैः प्रासैस्त्रिशूलैर्वज्रकर्षणैः।
सरावणानर्दयन्तः समन्तात् समभिद्रुताः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: The ministers of Arjuna rushed on all sides hitting the intruders including Rāvaṇa with arrows, iron-clubs, lances and tridents which tore up the skin like the thunderbolt. (34)

verses.text:
हैहयाधिपयोधानां वेग आसीत् सुदारुणः।
सनक्रमीनमकरसमुद्रस्येव निःस्वनः॥ ३५॥
verses.m: The onrush of the warriors of the king of the Haihayas was fierce like the roar of a sea infested with crocodiles, fishes and alligators. (35)

verses.text:
रावणस्य तु तेऽमात्याः प्रहस्तशुकसारणाः।
कार्तवीर्यबलं क्रुद्धा निहन्ति स्म स्वतेजसा॥ ३६॥
verses.m: Provoked to anger, the aforesaid ministers of Rāvaṇa—Prahasta, Śuka and Sāraṇa, however, began to exterminate the army of Arjuna (son of Kṛtavīrya) with their might. (36)

verses.text:
अर्जुनाय तु तत्कर्म रावणस्य समन्त्रिणः।
क्रीडमानाय कथितं पुरुषैर्भयविह्वलैः॥ ३७॥
verses.m: The aforesaid doing of Rāvaṇa accompanied by his ministers was, however, reported to the sporting Arjuna by his men, who were beside themselves through fear. (37)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा न भेतव्यमिति स्त्रीजनं स तदार्जुनः।
उत्ततार जलात् तस्माद् गङ्गातोयादिवाञ्जनः॥ ३८॥
verses.m: Saying to the womenfolk, “You need not be afraid,” on hearing the report, the celebrated Arjuna then emerged from the waters of the Narmadā even as Añjana (one of the elephants guarding the quarters) would emerge from waters of the Gaṅgā. (38)

verses.text:
क्रोधदूषितनेत्रस्तु स तदार्जुनपावकः।
प्रजज्वाल महाघोरो युगान्त इव पावकः॥ ३९॥
verses.m: His eyes coloured through anger, the fiery Arjuna flared up like the most dreadful fire at the end of a world-cycle. (39)

verses.text:
स तूर्णतरमादाय वरहेमाङ्गदो गदाम्।
अभिदुद्राव रक्षांसि तमांसीव दिवाकरः॥ ४०॥
verses.m: Seizing hold with all speed of a mace, Arjuna, who was adorned with a pair of excellent golden armlets, drove away the ogres even as the sun would dispel darkness. (40)

verses.text:
बाहुविक्षेपकरणां समुद्यम्य महागदाम्।
गारुडं वेगमास्थाय आपपातैव सोऽर्जुनः॥ ४१॥
verses.m: Holding up his huge mace, which could be spun with one’s arms, and assuming the speed of Garuḍa (the king of birds), the celebrated Arjuna immediately rushed on the ogres. (41)

verses.text:
तस्य मार्गं समारुद्ध्य विन्ध्योऽर्कस्येव पर्वतः।
स्थितो विन्ध्य इवाकम्प्यः प्रहस्तो मुसलायुधः॥ ४२॥
verses.m: Barring his path, even as the Vindhya mountain intercepted the orbit of the sun of yore, Prahasta stood unshakable like the Vindhya, pestle in hand. (42)

verses.text:
ततोऽस्य मुसलं घोरं लोहबद्धं मदोद्धतः।
प्रहस्तः प्रेषयन् क्रुद्धो ररास च यथान्तकः॥ ४३॥
verses.m: Inflated with arrogance and provoked to anger, Prahasta thereupon hurled the dreadful copper-bound pestle at Arjuna and roared like Death. (43)

verses.text:
तस्याग्रे मुसलस्याग्निरशोकापीडसंनिभः।
प्रहस्तकरमुक्तस्य बभूव प्रदहन्निव॥ ४४॥
verses.m: At the tip of the pestle shot by the hand of Prahasta appeared a fire resembling the point of an Aśoka flower, which seemed to consume its Target. (44)

verses.text:
आधावमानं मुसलं कार्तवीर्यस्तदार्जुनः।
निपुणं वञ्चयामास गदया गतविक्लवः॥ ४५॥
verses.m: Not the least perplexed, Arjuna, son of Kṛtavīrya, at that time completely confronted the pestle, which was coming with great speed, by means of his mace. (45)

verses.text:
ततस्तमभिदुद्राव सगदो हैहयाधिपः।
भ्रामयाणो गदां गुर्वीं पञ्चबाहुशतोच्छ्रयाम्॥ ४६॥
verses.m: Whirling his massive mace, which was thrown with five hundred arms, the king of the Haihayas, who was still armed with a mace, thereupon rushed on Prahasta. (46)

verses.text:
ततो हतोऽतिवेगेन प्रहस्तो गदया तदा।
निपपात स्थितः शैलो वज्रिवज्रहतो यथा॥ ४७॥
verses.m: Struck with great vehemence by the mace at that time, Prahasta, who stood erect, thereupon fell prostrate like a hill struck by the thunderbolt of Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt. (47)

verses.text:
प्रहस्तं पतितं दृष्ट्वा मारीचशुकसारणाः।
समहोदरधूम्राक्षा अपसृष्टा रणाजिरात्॥ ४८॥
verses.m: Seeing Prahasta fallen, Mārīca, Śuka and Sāraṇa alongwith Mahodara and Dhūmrākṣa slipped away from the field of battle. (48)

verses.text:
अपक्रान्तेष्वमात्येषु प्रहस्ते च निपातिते।
रावणोऽभ्यद्रवत् तूर्णमर्जुनं नृपसत्तमम्॥ ४९॥
verses.m: The ministers having fled away and Prahasta having been struck down, Rāvaṇa rushed with all speed towards Arjuna, the foremost of kings. (49)

verses.text:
सहस्रबाहोस्तद् युद्धं विंशद्बाहोश्च दारुणम्।
नृपराक्षसयोस्तत्र आरब्धं रोमहर्षणम्॥ ५०॥
verses.m: Then commenced a fierce fight, which caused one’s hair to stand on end, between the thousand-armed king and the twenty-armed ogre. (50)

verses.text:
सागराविव संक्षुब्धौ चलमूलाविवाचलौ।
तेजोयुक्ताविवादित्यौ प्रदहन्ताविवानलौ॥ ५१॥
बलोद्धतौ यथा नागौ वासितार्थे यथा वृषौ।
मेघाविव विनर्दन्तौ सिंहाविव बलोत्कटौ॥ ५२॥
रुद्रकालाविव क्रुद्धौ तौ तदा राक्षसार्जुनौ।
परस्परं गदां गृह्य ताडयामासतुर्भृशम्॥ ५३॥
verses.m: Seizing hold of a mace each, the ogre and King Arjuna, who looked at that time like two seas which were greatly ruffled, two mountains with moving bases, a pair of suns full of martial ardour, a couple of blazing fires, two elephants intoxicated with might, two bulls contending for a cow in heat, two thundering clouds, two lions proud of their might, like Rudra, the god of destruction, and Kāla, the Time-Spirit, provoked to anger, struck each other violently. (51—53)

verses.text:
वज्रप्रहारानचला यथा घोरान् विषेहिरे।
गदाप्रहारांस्तौ तत्र सेहाते नरराक्षसौ॥ ५४॥
verses.m: Even as the mountains withstood the formidable strokes of lightning at the beginning of creation, so did the two warriors, the human being, Arjuna, and the ogre, Rāvaṇa, endure the blows of each other’s mace. (54)

verses.text:
यथाशनिरवेभ्यस्तु जायतेऽथ प्रतिश्रुतिः।
तथा तयोर्गदापोथैर्दिशः सर्वाः प्रतिश्रुताः॥ ५५॥
verses.m: Even as reverberations emanate from the peals of thunder, so did all the quarters resound with the clashes of their maces. (55)

verses.text:
अर्जुनस्य गदा सा तु पात्यमानाऽहितोरसि।
काञ्चनाभं नभश्चक्रे विद्युत्सौदामनी यथा॥ ५६॥
verses.m: While being directed against the enemy’s breast, the well-known mace of Arjuna for its part rendered it golden even as a flash of lightning makes the sky assume a golden hue. (56)

verses.text:
तथैव रावणेनापि पात्यमाना मुहुर्मुहुः।
अर्जुनोरसि निर्भाति गदोल्केव महागिरौ॥ ५७॥
verses.m: Being repeatedly directed against the breast of Arjuna by Rāvaṇa too, his mace likewise shone brightly like a meteor descending on a huge mountain. (57)

verses.text:
नार्जुनः खेदमायाति न राक्षसगणेश्वरः।
सममासीत् तयोर्युद्धं यथा पूर्वं बलीन्द्रयोः॥ ५८॥
verses.m: Neither Arjuna nor the ruler of the hordes of ogres grew weary. Well-matched was their duel as that which took place between Bali and Indra of yore. (58)

verses.text:
शृङ्गैरिव वृषायुध्यन् दन्ताग्रैरिव कुञ्जरौ।
परस्परं विनिघ्नन्तौ नरराक्षससत्तमौ॥ ५९॥
verses.m: Striking each other violently with full force, the foremost of human beings as well as the jewel among the ogres fought even as a pair of bulls would do with their horns, or two elephants with their tusks. (59)

verses.text:
ततोऽर्जुनेन क्रुद्धेन सर्वप्राणेन सा गदा।
स्तनयोरन्तरे मुक्ता रावणस्य महोरसि॥ ६०॥
verses.m: The said mace was then hurled with all his strength by the enraged Arjuna on the mighty chest of Rāvaṇa. (60)

verses.text:
वरदानकृतत्राणे सा गदा रावणोरसि।
दुर्बलेव यथावेगं द्विधाभूतापतत् क्षितौ॥ ६१॥
verses.m: Though hurled with full force on the breast of Rāvaṇa, which was protected by the bestowal of boons by Brahmā, the said mace fell on the ground, broken in two as though it were of meagre strength. (61)

verses.text:
स त्वर्जुनप्रयुक्तेन गदाघातेन रावणः।
अपासर्पद् धनुर्मात्रं निषसाद च निष्टनन्॥ ६२॥
verses.m: Under the blow of the mace directed by Arjuna, however, the notorious Rāvaṇa receded a bow’s length and sank down crying. (62)

verses.text:
स विह्वलं तदालक्ष्य दशग्रीवं ततोऽर्जुनः।
सहसोत्पत्य जग्राह गरुत्मानिव पन्नगम्॥ ६३॥
verses.m: Springing forward all of a sudden on seeing Rāvaṇa (the ten-headed monster) confused at that time, Arjuna thereupon caught hold of him as Garuḍa (the king of birds) would seize a serpent. (63)

verses.text:
स तु बाहुसहस्रेण बलाद् गृह्य दशाननम्।
बबन्ध बलवान् राजा बलिं नारायणो यथा॥ ६४॥
verses.m: Forcibly laying hold of Rāvaṇa with his thousand arms, the mighty king bound him even as Lord Nārāyaṇa in His descent as Vāmana bound Bali. (64)

verses.text:
बध्यमाने दशग्रीवे सिद्धचारणदेवताः।
साध्वीति वादिनः पुष्पैः किरन्त्यर्जुनमूर्धनि॥ ६५॥
verses.m: While Rāvaṇa (the ten-headed monster) was being bound, the Siddhas (a class of semi-divine beings credited with supernatural powers by virtue of their very birth), Cāraṇas (celestial bards) and gods (witnessing the scene from the skies) covered the airspace over the head of Arjuna with flowers, saying “Well done!” (65)

verses.text:
व्याघ्रो मृगमिवादाय मृगराडिव कुञ्जरम्।
ररास हैहयो राजा हर्षादम्बुदवन्मुहुः॥ ६६॥
verses.m: Having captured Rāvaṇa even as a tiger would seize a deer or a lion would lay hold of an elephant, King Arjuna (the ruler of the Haihayas) thundered like a cloud again and again. (66)

verses.text:
प्रहस्तस्तु समाश्वस्तो दृष्ट्वा बद्धं दशाननम्।
सहसा राक्षसः क्रुद्धो ह्यभिदुद्राव हैहयम्॥ ६७॥
verses.m: Provoked to anger on seeing Rāvaṇa (the ten-headed monster) bound, when fully restored to consciousness, the ogre Prahasta for his part rapidly rushed headlong on Arjuna. (67)

verses.text:
नक्तंचराणां वेगस्तु तेषामापततां बभौ।
उद्भूत आतपापाये पयोदानामिवाम्बुधौ॥ ६८॥
verses.m: The onrush of those assailing night-rangers grew in violence as that of clouds appearing on the sea at the end of summer. (68)

verses.text:
मुञ्चमुञ्चेति भाषन्तस्तिष्ठतिष्ठेति चासकृत्।
मुसलानि च शूलानि सोत्ससर्ज तदा रणे॥ ६९॥
verses.m: The ogres rushed forth, repeatedly crying “Hurl the weapon! Hurl the weapon” and “Stay awhile, Stay awhile” and he (Prahasta) hurled pestles and darts on the battlefield. (69)

verses.text:
अप्राप्तान्येव तान्याशु असम्भ्रान्तस्तदार्जुनः।
आयुधान्यमरारीणां जग्राहारिनिषूदनः॥ ७०॥
verses.m: Not at all confused, Arjuna, the destroyer of his foes, at that time speedily took hold of those weapons of the enemies of gods even before they reached him. (70)

verses.text:
ततस्तैरेव रक्षांसि दुर्धरैः प्रवरायुधैः।
भित्त्वा विद्रावयामास वायुरम्बुधरानिव॥ ७१॥
verses.m: Piercing the ogres with those very weapons, which were most excellent and difficult even to hold, Arjuna drove them away even as the wind disperses clouds. (71)

verses.text:
राक्षसांस्त्रासयामास कार्तवीर्यार्जुनस्तदा।
रावणं गृह्य नगरं प्रविवेश सुहृद्वृतः॥ ७२॥
verses.m: Arjuna, son of Kṛtavīrya, frightened the ogres at that time. Nay taking Rāvaṇa and surrounded by his friends, he entered the city. (72)

verses.text:
स कीर्यमाणः कुसुमाक्षतोत्करै-
र्द्विजैः सपौरैः पुरुहूतसंनिभः।
ततोऽर्जुनः स्वां प्रविवेश तां पुरीं
बलिं निगृह्येव सहस्रलोचनः॥ ७३॥
verses.m: Being covered with heaps of flowers and unbroken grains of rice by Brāhmaṇas (the twice-born) and other citizens on capturing Rāvaṇa, Arjuna, who closely resembled Indra (who is invoked by many), thereupon entered his well-known city even as Indra (the thousand-eyed god) entered his city after capturing Bali. (73)

verses.text:
रावणग्रहणं तत् तु वायुग्रहणसंनिभम्।
ततः पुलस्त्यः शुश्राव कथितं दिवि दैवतैः॥ १॥
verses.m: Pulastya thereupon heard as narrated by the gods in heaven the story of Rāvaṇa’s aforesaid capture, which was much like capturing the air. (1)

verses.text:
ततः पुत्रकृतस्नेहात् कम्पमानो महाधृतिः।
माहिष्मतीपतिं द्रष्टुमाजगाम महानृषिः॥ २॥
verses.m: Feeling commiseration (for Rāvaṇa) due to affection for his son (grandson), though highly self-possessed, the great Ṛṣi (seer of Vedic Mantras) came all the way to see the ruler of Māhiṣmatī. (2)

verses.text:
स वायुमार्गमास्थाय वायुतुल्यगतिर्द्विजः।
पुरीं माहिष्मतीं प्राप्तो मनःसम्पातविक्रमः॥ ३॥
verses.m: Travelling by the aerial route, the Brāhmaṇa, whose speed equalled that of the wind, reached the city of Māhiṣmatī with the swiftness of thought. (3)

verses.text:
सोऽमरावतिसंकाशां हृष्टपुष्टजनावृताम्।
प्रविवेश पुरीं ब्रह्मा इन्द्रस्येवामरावतीम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Like Brahmā entering Amarāvatī, the city of Indra, he penetrated deep into the city, which was crowded with happy and prosperous people and which closely resembled Amarāvatī. (4)

verses.text:
पादचारमिवादित्यं निष्पतन्तं सुदुर्दृशम्।
ततस्ते प्रत्यभिज्ञाय अर्जुनाय न्यवेदयन्॥ ५॥
verses.m: Recognizing the sage, who looked like the sun-god coming on foot, extremely difficult as he was to gaze on, even while he was descending from the heavens, the counsellors of Arjuna thereupon reported his arrival to him. (5)

verses.text:
पुलस्त्य इति विज्ञाय वचनाद्धैहयाधिपः।
शिरस्यञ्जलिमाधाय प्रत्युद्गच्छत् तपस्विनम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: Placing his joined palms above his head on coming to know from their report that he was no other than Sage Pulastya, Arjuna (the suzerain lord of the Haihayas) went forward to meet the ascetic. (6)

verses.text:
पुरोहितोऽस्य गृह्यार्घ्यं मधुपर्कं तथैव च।
पुरस्तात् प्रययौ राज्ञः शक्रस्येव बृहस्पतिः॥ ७॥
verses.m: Taking with him Arghya (water to wash one’s hands with) as well as Madhuparka (a mixture of honey and curds), his family-priest preceded the king even as Sage Bṛhaspati, the preceptor of gods, would walk ahead of Indra. (7)

verses.text:
ततस्तमृषिमायान्तमुद्यन्तमिव भास्करम्।
अर्जुनो दृश्य सम्भ्रान्तो ववन्देन्द्र इवेश्वरम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: Overawed to see the aforesaid Ṛṣi (the seer of Vedic Mantras) coming like the rising sun, Arjuna thereupon saluted him even as Indra, the ruler of gods, would salute the Supreme (Brahma). (8)

verses.text:
स तस्य मधुपर्कं गां पाद्यमर्घ्यं निवेद्य च।
पुलस्त्यमाह राजेन्द्रो हर्षगद्गदया गिरा॥ ९॥
verses.m: Having offered Madhuparka, a cow and water to wash his feet and hands (respectively) with, Arjuna, the king of kings, submitted as follows to Sage Pulastya in a voice choked with delight: (9)

verses.text:
अद्यैवममरावत्या तुल्या माहिष्मती कृता।
अद्याहं तु द्विजेन्द्र त्वां यस्मात् पश्यामि दुर्दृशम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Māhiṣmatī has in this way been placed on a par with Amarāvatī (the city of Indra) this day in that I see today, O prince of the twice-born, you, who are really so difficult to behold. (10)

verses.text:
अद्य मे कुशलं देव अद्य मे कुशलं व्रतम्।
अद्य मे सफलं जन्म अद्य मे सफलं तपः॥ ११॥
यत् ते देवगणैर्वन्द्यौ वन्देऽहं चरणौ तव।
इदं राज्यमिमे पुत्रा इमे दारा इमे वयम्।
ब्रह्मन् किं कुर्मि किं कार्यमाज्ञापयतु नो भवान्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Prosperity attends on me today, O revered one! My vow too stands fulfilled today; my birth too stands consummated today and my askesis too have borne fruit today in that I salute your holy feet, which deserve to be saluted by gods. This kingdom, these sons and these consorts of mine, nay, even ourselves stand at your service. What should we do? Pray, command us what should be done by us.” (11-12)

verses.text:
तं धर्मेऽग्निषु पुत्रेषु शिवं पृष्ट्वा च पार्थिवम्।
पुलस्त्योवाच राजानं हैहयानां तथार्जुनम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: Having inquired of the king about his welfare concerning religious practices, sacrificial fires and sons, Sage Pulastya spoke as follows to Arjuna, the ruler of the Haihayas: (13)

verses.text:
नरेन्द्राम्बुजपत्राक्ष पूर्णचन्द्रनिभानन।
अतुलं ते बलं येन दशग्रीवस्त्वया जितः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Matchless is your might by dint of which Rāvaṇa stands conquered by you, O ruler of men whose eyes resemble the lotus-petals and whose countenance shines as the full moon. ` (14)

verses.text:
भयाद् यस्योपतिष्ठेतां निष्पन्दौ सागरानिलौ।
सोऽयं मृधे त्वया बद्धः पौत्रो मे रणदुर्जयः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “That very grandson of mine, who was hard to conquer, and for fear of whom the ocean as well as the wind stood motionless in attendance, was made captive by you on the battlefield. (15)

verses.text:
पुत्रकस्य यशः पीतं नाम विश्रावितं त्वया।
मद्वाक्याद् याच्यमानोऽद्य मुञ्च वत्स दशाननम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “The glory of my beloved child stands swallowed up by you and your own name has been made widely known by you. Being solicited by me today, pray, set my child, Rāvaṇa, free at my intercession.” (16)

verses.text:
पुलस्त्याज्ञां प्रगृह्योचे न किंचन वचोऽर्जुनः।
मुमोच वै पार्थिवेन्द्रो राक्षसेन्द्रं प्रहृष्टवत्॥ १७॥
verses.m: Arjuna did not utter a word in reply. Bowing to the command of Pulastya, however, the king of kings joyously set free the ruler of ogres. (17)

verses.text:
स तं प्रमुच्य त्रिदशारिमर्जुनः
प्रपूज्य दिव्याभरणस्रगम्बरैः।
अहिंसकं सख्यमुपेत्य साग्निकं
प्रणम्य तं ब्रह्मसुतं गृहं ययौ॥ १८॥
verses.m: Having unconditionally released the enemy of gods and duly honoured him with celestial ornaments, garlands and raiment, nay, contracted with him in the presence of fire an alliance which involved no destruction to each other and, respectfully bowing down to the aforesaid son of Brahmā (the creator), the celebrated Arjuna entered his palace. (18)

verses.text:
पुलस्त्येनापि संत्यक्तो राक्षसेन्द्रः प्रतापवान्।
परिष्वक्तः कृतातिथ्यो लज्जमानो विनिर्जितः॥ १९॥
verses.m: Though unconditionally released by Arjuna after being hospitably treated, and lovingly embraced by his grandfather, Pulastya, the glorious Rāvaṇa felt shy due to his having been utterly vanquished. (19)

verses.text:
पितामहसुतश्चापि पुलस्त्यो मुनिपुङ्गवः।
मोचयित्वा दशग्रीवं ब्रह्मलोकं जगाम ह॥ २०॥
verses.m: Having secured the deliverance of Rāvaṇa (the ten-headed monster), they say, Pulastya too, (a mind-born) son of Brahmā ( the grandfather of the entire creation) and the foremost of ascetics, went back to the realm of Brahmā (the creator). (20)

verses.text:
एवं स रावणः प्राप्तः कार्तवीर्यात् प्रधर्षणम्।
पुलस्त्यवचनाच्चापि पुनर्मुक्तो महाबलः॥ २१॥
verses.m: In this way the notorious and highly powerful Rāvaṇa sustained defeat at the hands of Arjuna (son of Kṛtavīrya) and was then also set at liberty once more at the intercession of Pulastya. (21)

verses.text:
एवं बलिभ्यो बलिनः सन्ति राघवनन्दन।
नावज्ञा हि परे कार्या य इच्छेच्छ्रेय आत्मनः॥ २२॥
verses.m: Thus, O delight of the scions of Raghu, there are warriors mightier than the mighty; hence by him who seeks his own welfare no disrespect should be shown to his enemy. (22)

verses.text:
ततः स राजा पिशिताशनानां
सहस्रबाहोरुपलभ्य मैत्रीम्।
पुनर्नृपाणां कदनं चकार
चकार सर्वां पृथिवीं च दर्पात्॥ २३॥
verses.m: Having secured the alliance of Arjuna (the thousand-armed prince), the said king of ogres (lit., flesh-eaters) resumed the destruction of rulers of men and arrogantly ranged over the entire globe. (23)

verses.text:
अर्जुनेन विमुक्तस्तु रावणो राक्षसाधिपः।
चचार पृथिवीं सर्वामनिर्विण्णस्तथा कृतः॥ १॥
verses.m: Having been set free by Arjuna, and thus rendered free from all causes of despondency, Rāvaṇa, the suzerain lord of ogres, for his part ranged over the entire globe. (1)

verses.text:
राक्षसं वा मनुष्यं वा शृणुते यं बलाधिकम्।
रावणस्तं समासाद्य युद्धे ह्वयति दर्पितः॥ २॥
verses.m: Approaching whomsoever he heard of as superior in might, irrespective of whether he was an ogre or a human being, Rāvaṇa, full of arrogance, challenged him to a duel. (2)

verses.text:
ततः कदाचित् किष्किन्धां नगरीं वालिपालिताम्।
गत्वाऽऽह्वयति युद्धाय वालिनं हेममालिनम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Making his way to the city of Kiṣkindhā, ruled over by Vālī, on a certain day, he then challenged Vālī, who was adorned with a gold necklace, to a duel. (3)

verses.text:
ततस्तु वानरामात्यास्तारस्तारापिता प्रभुः।
उवाच वानरो वाक्यं युद्धप्रेप्सुमुपागतम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Thereupon Tāra, a minister of Vālī (the chief of monkeys), Suṣeṇa (father of Tārā, Vālī’s consort), Aṅgada (the Crown prince) and Sugrīva (the junior monkey chief) spoke as follows to Rāvaṇa, who had come seeking combat: (4)

verses.text:
राक्षसेन्द्र गतो वाली यस्ते प्रतिबलो भवेत्।
कोऽन्यः प्रमुखतः स्थातुं तव शक्तः प्लवङ्गमः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Vālī, O ruler of ogres, who may be a match for you, has gone out. What other monkey is capable of standing before you? (5)

verses.text:
चतुर्भ्योऽपि समुद्रेभ्यः संध्यामन्वास्य रावण।
इदं मुहूर्तमायाति वाली तिष्ठ मुहूर्तकम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “After saying his Sandhyā prayers on the shore of all the four oceans, O Rāvaṇa, Vālī must be returning this very hour. Pray, wait awhile. (6)

verses.text:
एतानस्थिचयान् पश्य य एते शङ्खपाण्डुराः।
युद्धार्थिनामिमे राजन् वानराधिपतेजसा॥ ७॥
verses.m: Behold these heaps of bones, which are white as a conch. These are the bones of those who sought combat with Vālī and were crushed by the might of Vālī, the suzerain lord of monkeys, O King! (7)

verses.text:
यद्वामृतरसः पीतस्त्वया रावण राक्षस।
तदा वालिनमासाद्य तदन्तं तव जीवितम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Or, even if the drink of immortality has been imbibed by you, O Rāvaṇa, your life will have reached its end the moment you encounter Vālī, O ogre! (8)

verses.text:
पश्येदानीं जगच्चित्रमिमं विश्रवसः सुत।
इदं मुहूर्तं तिष्ठस्व दुर्लभं ते भविष्यति॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Presently behold this marvel of the world, O son of Viśravā! Wait till this hour. Your life will be difficult to retain any more. (9)

verses.text:
अथवा त्वरसे मर्तुं गच्छ दक्षिणसागरम्।
वालिनं द्रक्ष्यसे तत्र भूमिष्ठमिव पावकम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Or, if you are in a hurry to breathe your last, proceed to the southern sea. There you will see Vālī like the god of fire staying on earth.” (10)

verses.text:
स तु तारं विनिर्भर्त्स्य रावणो लोकरावणः।
पुष्पकं तत् समारुह्य प्रययौ दक्षिणार्णवम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: Severely scolding Tāra, the notorious Rāvaṇa, who made people cry, flew to the southern sea, getting on his well-known Puṣpaka car. (11)

verses.text:
तत्र हेमगिरिप्रख्यं तरुणार्कनिभाननम्।
रावणो वालिनं दृष्ट्वा संध्योपासनतत्परम्॥ १२॥
पुष्पकादवरुह्याथ रावणोऽञ्जनसंनिभः।
ग्रहीतुं वालिनं तूर्णं निःशब्दपदमव्रजत्॥ १३॥
verses.m: Alighting from the Puṣpaka on seeing Vālī, who resembled a mountain of gold and whose countenance shone like the newly risen sun, absorbed in saying the Sandhyā prayers, Rāvaṇa who had the hue of collyrium, proceeded hastily with silent steps in order to capture him. (12-13)

verses.text:
यदृच्छया तदा दृष्टो वालिनापि स रावणः।
पापाभिप्रायकं दृष्ट्वा चकार न तु सम्भ्रमम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: By chance the notorious Rāvaṇa too was espied by Vālī. The latter, however, did not feel perturbed even on seeing him of sinful intent. (14)

verses.text:
शशमालक्ष्य सिंहो वा पन्नगं गरुडो यथा।
न चिन्तयति तं वाली रावणं पापनिश्चयम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Vālī did not feel worried even on perceiving Rāvaṇa of sinful resolve any more than a lion would on seeing a hare or Garuḍa (the king of birds) on seeing a serpent. (15)

verses.text:
जिघृक्षमाणमायान्तं रावणं पापचेतसम्।
कक्षावलम्बिनं कृत्वा गमिष्ये त्रीन् महार्णवान्॥ १६॥
verses.m: (Vālī said to himself:) “Pressing in my arm-pit the sinful-minded Rāvaṇa as soon as he approaches with intent to catch hold of me and leaving him hanging there, I shall visit the three remaining oceans too. (16)

verses.text:
द्रक्ष्यन्त्यरिं ममाङ्कस्थं स्रंसदूरुकराम्बरम्।
लम्बमानं दशग्रीवं गरुडस्येव पन्नगम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “People will see my enemy, Rāvaṇa (the ten-headed monster), hanging from my arm-pit with his thighs, hands and raiment dangling, like a serpent in the claws of Garuḍa.” (17)

verses.text:
इत्येवं मतिमास्थाय वाली मौनमुपास्थितः।
जपन् वै नैगमान् मन्त्रांस्तस्थौ पर्वतराडिव॥ १८॥
verses.m: Making up his mind thus, Vālī remained standing like the king of mountains, silently repeating Vedic Mantras. (18)

verses.text:
तावन्योन्यं जिघृक्षन्तौ हरिराक्षसपार्थिवौ।
प्रयत्नवन्तौ तत् कर्म ईहतुर्बलदर्पितौ॥ १९॥
verses.m: Each seeking to lay his hands on the other, the two warriors, the king of monkeys and the lord of ogres, both conceited by reason of their might, strove diligently to accomplish that end. (19)

verses.text:
हस्तग्राहं तु तं मत्वा पादशब्देन रावणम्।
पराङ् मुखोऽपि जग्राह वाली सर्पमिवाण्डजः॥ २०॥
verses.m: Concluding from his footfalls Rāvaṇa to be ready to catch hold of himself, Vālī, though having his back turned upon him, caught hold of him even as Garuḍa (a bird) would seize a serpent. (20)

verses.text:
ग्रहीतुकामं तं गृह्य रक्षसामीश्वरं हरिः।
खमुत्पपात वेगेन कृत्वा कक्षावलम्बिनम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: Having captured the said ruler of ogres, who sought to capture Vālī, and pressing him in his arm-pit and leaving him hanging there, Vālī, monkey-chief, sprang up with speed in the airspace. (21)

verses.text:
तं च पीडयमानं तु वितुदन्तं नखैर्मुहुः।
जहार रावणं वाली पवनस्तोयदं यथा॥ २२॥
verses.m: Even though Rāvaṇa repeatedly oppressed and pinched Vālī with his nails, the latter bore away Rāvaṇa just as the wind would sweep away a cloud. (22)

verses.text:
अथ ते राक्षसामात्या ह्रियमाणे दशानने।
मुमोक्षयिषवो वालिं रवमाणा अभिद्रुताः॥ २३॥
verses.m: While Rāvaṇa, the ten-headed monster, was being borne away, the said ministers of Rāvaṇa forthwith rushed upon Vālī, with a view to securing his release, emitting loud cries. (23)

verses.text:
अन्वीयमानस्तैर्वाली भ्राजतेऽम्बरमध्यगः।
अन्वीयमानो मेघौघैरम्बरस्थ इवांशुमान्॥ २४॥
verses.m: Being pursued by them in mid heavens, Vālī shone like the sun being followed by multitudes of clouds in space. (24)

verses.text:
तेऽशक्नुवन्तः सम्प्राप्तुं वालिनं राक्षसोत्तमाः।
तस्य बाहूरुवेगेन परिश्रान्ता व्यवस्थिताः॥ २५॥
verses.m: Failing to approach Vālī, the aforesaid jewels among the ogres stood exhausted by the onrush of his hands and thighs. (25)

verses.text:
वालिमार्गादपाक्रामन् पर्वतेन्द्रापि गच्छतः।
किं पुनर्जीवनप्रेप्सुर्बिभ्रद् वै मांसशोणितम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: Even the foremost of mountains receded from the path of Vālī as he rushed forth, what wonder, then, that one having a body composed of flesh and blood and seeking to live should do so. (26)

verses.text:
अपक्षिगणसम्पातान् वानरेन्द्रो महाजवः।
क्रमशः सागरान् सर्वान् संध्याकालमवन्दत॥ २७॥
verses.m: Vālī (the ruler of monkeys), who moved with extraordinary speed, paid homage to the goddess presiding over the morning and evening twilights reaching one after another the four seas which could not be visited even by flocks of fast-moving birds. (27)

verses.text:
सम्पूज्यमानो यातस्तु खचरैः खचरोत्तमः।
पश्चिमं सागरं वाली आजगाम सरावणः॥ २८॥
verses.m: Being duly honoured on the way by winged creatures, Vālī, the foremost of those moving in the air, reached the western sea with Rāvaṇa tightly held in his armpit. (28)

verses.text:
तस्मिन् संध्यामुपासित्वा स्नात्वा जप्त्वा च वानरः।
उत्तरं सागरं प्रायाद् वहमानो दशाननम्॥ २९॥
verses.m: After taking a plunge in it, saying his Sandhyā prayers and muttering the sacred formula, the monkey moved to the northern sea carrying the ten-headed monster tucked in his armpit. (29)

verses.text:
बहुयोजनसाहस्रं वहमानो महाहरिः।
वायुवच्च मनोवच्च जगाम सह शत्रुणा॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Carrying him across many thousands of Yojanas, the mighty monkey moved with his adversary with the speed of the wind and thought. (30)

verses.text:
उत्तरे सागरे संध्यामुपासित्वा दशाननम्।
वहमानोऽगमद् वाली पूर्वं वै स महोदधिम्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: Having said his Sandhyā prayers at the northern ocean, the said Vālī actually proceeded to the eastern sea, carrying Rāvaṇa (the ten-headed monster). (31)

verses.text:
तत्रापि संध्यामन्वास्य वासविः स हरीश्वरः।
किष्किन्धामभितो गृह्य रावणं पुनरागमत्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Having said his Sandhyā prayers there also, the aforesaid Vālī (sprung from the loins of Indra), the ruler of monkeys, returned to the precincts of Kiṣkindhā, taking with him Rāvaṇa held in his armpit. (32)

verses.text:
चतुर्ष्वपि समुद्रेषु संध्यामन्वास्य वानरः।
रावणोद्वहनश्रान्तः किष्किन्धोपवनेऽपतत्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: Having said his Sandhyā prayers at all the four seas, the monkey chief (Vālī), who had been worn out on account of carrying Rāvaṇa all the way, landed in a park adjoining Kiṣkindhā. (33)

verses.text:
रावणं तु मुमोचाथ स्वकक्षात् कपिसत्तमः।
कुतस्त्वमिति चोवाच प्रहसन् रावणं मुहुः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: Vālī (the foremost of monkeys) for his part disengaged Rāvaṇa from his armpit, and loudly laughing again and again, questioned Rāvaṇa as follows: “Whence are you?” (34)

verses.text:
विस्मयं तु महद् गत्वा श्रमलोलनिरीक्षणः।
राक्षसेन्द्रो हरीन्द्रं तमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ ३५॥
verses.m: Feeling great surprise, his eyes rolling on account of weariness, the ruler of ogres replied as follows to the aforesaid ruler of monkeys: (35)

verses.text:
वानरेन्द्र महेन्द्राभ राक्षसेन्द्रोऽस्मि रावणः।
युद्धेप्सुरिह सम्प्राप्तः स चाद्यासादितस्त्वया॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “I am Rāvaṇa, the ruler of ogres, O king of monkeys, a compeer of the mighty Indra, come here seeking an encounter with you and I was consequently captured by you today. (36)

verses.text:
अहो बलमहो वीर्यमहो गाम्भीर्यमेव च।
येनाहं पशुवद् गृह्य भ्रामितश्चतुरोऽर्णवान्॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “Astounding is the strength, marvellous is the prowess and wonderful is the profundity too in you, by whom, after seizing me I was taken like an animal round the four seas! (37)

verses.text:
एवमश्रान्तवद् वीर शीघ्रमेव च वानर।
मां चैवोद्वहमानस्तु कोऽन्यो वीरो भविष्यति॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “What other hero would carry me so unweariedly and fast as you did, O valiant monkey? (38)

verses.text:
त्रयाणामेव भूतानां गतिरेषा प्लवङ्गम।
मनोऽनिलसुपर्णानां तव चात्र न संशयः॥ ३९॥
verses.m: “Such a marvellous speed exists in three created entities alone—the mind, the wind-god and Garuḍa (lit., the bird with beautiful wings) as well as in you: there is no doubt about it, O monkey! (39)

verses.text:
सोऽहं दृष्टबलस्तुभ्यमिच्छामि हरिपुङ्गव।
त्वया सह चिरं सख्यं सुस्निग्धं पावकाग्रतः॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “Having witnessed your might, O jewel among the monkeys, I seek to enter into an enduring and exceedingly loving friendship with you in the presence of fire. (40)

verses.text:
दाराः पुत्राः पुरं राष्ट्रं भोगाच्छादनभोजनम्।
सर्वमेवाविभक्तं नौ भविष्यति हरीश्वर॥ ४१॥
verses.m: “Our consorts, sons, cities, kingdoms, luxuries, raiment and food—all will be jointly held by us two, O lord of monkeys!” (41)

verses.text:
ततः प्रज्वालयित्वाग्निं तावुभौ हरिराक्षसौ।
भ्रातृत्वमुपसम्पन्नौ परिष्वज्य परस्परम्॥ ४२॥
verses.m: Then, lighting a fire, both the said warriors, the monkey chief and the lord of ogres, entered into fraternity, after embracing each other. (42)

verses.text:
अन्योन्यं लम्बितकरौ ततस्तौ हरिराक्षसौ।
किष्किन्धां विशतुर्हृष्टौ सिंहौ गिरिगुहामिव॥ ४३॥
verses.m: With their hands clasped together, the two warriors, the monkey chief and the king of ogres, thereupon joyously entered Kiṣkindhā like two lions entering a rock cavern. (43)

verses.text:
स तत्र मासमुषितः सुग्रीव इव रावणः।
अमात्यैरागतैर्नीतस्त्रैलोक्योत्सादनार्थिभिः ॥ ४४॥
verses.m: Rāvaṇa lived there for a month like Sugrīva. He was then led away by his ministers who had come and who were desirous of exterminating the three worlds. (44)

verses.text:
एवमेतत् पुरा वृत्तं वालिना रावणः प्रभो।
धर्षितश्च वृतश्चापि भ्राता पावकसंनिधौ॥ ४५॥
verses.m: This is how it happened in the past, how Rāvaṇa, my lord, was overpowered by Vālī and was then accepted as a brother in the presence of fire. (45)

verses.text:
बलमप्रतिमं राम वालिनोऽभवदुत्तमम्।
सोऽपि त्वया विनिर्दग्धः शलभो वह्निना यथा॥ ४६॥
verses.m: Matchless and unsurpassed was the strength of Vālī. Even he was consumed by You as a moth is consumed by fire. (46)

verses.text:
अपृच्छत तदा रामो दक्षिणाशाश्रयं मुनिम्।
प्राञ्जलिर्विनयोपेत इदमाह वचोऽर्थवत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma then questioned the sage having his abode in the southern quarter; and full of humility, with joined palms, He addressed the following significant words to him: (1)

verses.text:
अतुलं बलमेतद् वै वालिनो रावणस्य च।
न त्वेताभ्यां हनुमता समं त्विति मतिर्मम॥ २॥
verses.m: “Incomparable indeed was the aforesaid might of Vālī and Rāvaṇa. The might of the aforesaid two warriors was, however, not equal to the strength of Hanumān: such indeed is my opinion. (2)

verses.text:
शौर्यं दाक्ष्यं बलं धैर्यं प्राज्ञता नयसाधनम्।
विक्रमश्च प्रभावश्च हनूमति कृतालयाः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Heroism, deligence, strength, firmness, sagacity, prudence and prowess and power have taken up their abode in Hanūmān. (3)

verses.text:
दृष्ट्वैव सागरं वीक्ष्य सीदन्तीं कपिवाहिनीम्।
समाश्वास्य महाबाहुर्योजनानां शतं प्लुतः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Perceiving the army of the monkeys sinking into despondency at the very sight of the sea, and reassuring it, the mighty-armed Hanumān leapt across the sea covering a hundred Yojanas (or eight hundred miles). (4)

verses.text:
धर्षयित्वा पुरीं लङ्कां रावणान्तःपुरं तदा।
दृष्टा सम्भाषिता चापि सीता ह्याश्वासिता तथा॥ ५॥
verses.m: “After overpowering the ogress presiding over the city of Laṅkā and stealing into the gynaeceum of Rāvaṇa, Sītā was discovered and spoken to as well and actually comforted by him. (5)

verses.text:
सेनाग्रगा मन्त्रिसुताः किंकरा रावणात्मजः।
एते हनुमता तत्र एकेन विनिपातिताः॥ ६॥
verses.m: The leaders of Rāvaṇa’s army the sons of his counsellors, his own servants and his son—all these were struck down there by Hanumān single-handed. (6)

verses.text:
भूयो बन्धाद् विमुक्तेन भाषयित्वा दशाननम्।
लङ्का भस्मीकृता येन पावकेनेव मेदिनी॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Then, after speaking to Rāvaṇa (the ten-headed monster), when he was entirely free from bondage, Laṅkā was reduced to ashes by him even as the terrestrial globe by the fire of dissolution. (7)

verses.text:
न कालस्य न शक्रस्य न विष्णोर्वित्तपस्य च।
कर्माणि तानि श्रूयन्ते यानि युद्धे हनूमतः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Feats similar to those which were performed in war by Hanūmān are not known to have been performed either by Kāla (the Time-Spirit) or by Indra or again by the god of fire or Kubera, the lord of riches. (8)

verses.text:
एतस्य बाहुवीर्येण लङ्का सीता च लक्ष्मणः।
प्राप्ता मया जयश्चैव राज्यं मित्राणि बान्धवाः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “By the prowess of his arms alone were Laṅkā and victory attained and Sītā, Lakṣmaṇa, sovereignty, friends and kinsfolk too regained by me. (9)

verses.text:
