हनूमान् यदि मे न स्याद् वानराधिपतेः सखा।
प्रवृत्तिमपि को वेत्तुं जानक्याः शक्तिमान् भवेत्॥ १०॥
verses.m: “If Hanūmān, the friend of Sugrīva (the suzerain lord of monkeys), were not with Me, who else would have been able to get the news about Sītā (Janaka’s daughter)? (10)

verses.text:
किमर्थं वाली चैतेन सुग्रीवप्रियकाम्यया।
तदा वैरे समुत्पन्ने न दग्धो वीरुधो यथा॥ ११॥
verses.m: “I wonder wherefore, when hostility sprang up between Sugrīva and Vālī, Vālī was not consumed as a tree by fire by Hanumān, with a desire to please Sugrīva. (11)

verses.text:
नहि वेदितवान् मन्ये हनूमानात्मनो बलम्।
यद् दृष्टवाञ्जीवितेष्टं क्लिश्यन्तं वानराधिपम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “I think Hanūmān was not conscious of his own might in that he simply watched Sugrīva (now the supreme ruler of the monkeys), who was dearer to him than his life, suffering hardships in exile. (12)

verses.text:
एतन्मे भगवन् सर्वं हनूमति महामुने।
विस्तरेण यथातत्त्वं कथयामरपूजित॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Tell me, Revered Sir, in extenso according to facts all this about Hanūmān, O great sage, adored by gods!” (13)

verses.text:
राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा हेतुयुक्तमृषिस्ततः।
हनूमतः समक्षं तमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ १४॥
verses.m: Hearing this reasonable submission of Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), the seer of Vedic Mantras thereupon replied to him as follows in the presence of Hanūmān: (14)

verses.text:
सत्यमेतद् रघुश्रेष्ठ यद् ब्रवीषि हनूमति।
न बले विद्यते तुल्यो न गतौ न मतौ परः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “What you say regarding Hanūmān is true, O jewel among the Raghus! None else is equal to him in might, speed or intelligence. (15)

verses.text:
अमोघशापैः शापस्तु दत्तोऽस्य मुनिभिः पुरा।
न वेत्ता हि बलं सर्वं बली सन्नरिमर्दन॥ १६॥
verses.m: “An imprecation was, however, pronounced on him in the past by ascetics whose curse never went in vain, that, though mighty he would not be aware of his entire strength, O scourge of your enemies! (16)

verses.text:
बाल्येऽप्येतेन यत् कर्म कृतं राम महाबल।
तन्न वर्णयितुं शक्यमिति बाल्यतयास्यते॥ १७॥
verses.m: “It is not possible to recount the feat which was performed by him even in his very childhood, O Rāma, who are endowed with extraordinary might! Hence he remained ignorant of his might as a child. (17)

verses.text:
यदि वास्ति त्वभिप्रायः संश्रोतुं तव राघव।
समाधाय मतिं राम निशामय वदाम्यहम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “If, however, you have a mind to listen, O scion of Raghus, hearken, O Rāma, after concentrating your mind, I proceed to narrate. (18)

verses.text:
सूर्यदत्तवरस्वर्णः सुमेरुर्नाम पर्वतः।
यत्र राज्यं प्रशास्त्यस्य केसरी नाम वै पिता॥ १९॥
verses.m: “There is a mountain, Sumeru by name, rendered golden by virtue of a boon bestowed on it by the sun-god, where reigns Hanumān’s father, Kesarī by name, they say. (19)

verses.text:
तस्य भार्या बभूवेष्टा अञ्जनेति परिश्रुता।
जनयामास तस्यां वै वायुरात्मजमुत्तमम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: Kesarī’s beloved wife was widely known by the name of Añjanā. The wind-god procreated an excellent son through her, they say. (20)

verses.text:
शालिशूकनिभाभासं प्रासूतेमं तदाञ्जना।
फलान्याहर्तुकामा वै निष्क्रान्ता गहनेचरा॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Añjanā then gave birth to Hanumān, who possessed the hue of paddy awns. Desiring to get excellent fruits, the belle actually went out into the forest. (21)

verses.text:
एष मातुर्वियोगाच्च क्षुधया च भृशार्दितः।
रुरोद शिशुरत्यर्थं शिशुः शरवणे यथा॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Due to separation from his mother and sore stricken with hunger, the babe cried aloud as did Kārtikeya in the thicket of reeds (where he was born). (22)

verses.text:
तदोद्यन्तं विवस्वन्तं जपापुष्पोत्करोपमम्।
ददर्श फललोभाच्च ह्युत्पपात रविं प्रति॥ २३॥
verses.m: “That very moment he espied the rising sun having the hue of a heap of Japā (China rose) flowers and in his eager desire to get at it, thinking it to be a fruit, he sprang towards the sun. (23)

verses.text:
बालार्काभिमुखो बालो बालार्क इव मूर्तिमान्।
ग्रहीतुकामो बालार्कं प्लवतेऽम्बरमध्यगः॥ २४॥
verses.m: “With his face turned towards the sun, the babe, which looked like the rising sun incarnate, continued to shoot up in mid heavens with intent to catch hold of the rising sun. (24)

verses.text:
एतस्मिन् प्लवमाने तु शिशुभावे हनूमति।
देवदानवयक्षाणां विस्मयः सुमहानभूत्॥ २५॥
verses.m: “While the yonder Hanūmān in his childlike simplicity was shooting up in this manner, the gods, Dānavas and Yakṣas felt extremely astonished. (25)

verses.text:
नाप्येवं वेगवान् वायुर्गरुडो न मनस्तथा।
यथायं वायुपुत्रस्तु क्रमतेऽम्बरमुत्तमम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: They said to themselves: ‘Neither the wind-god nor Garuḍa (the king of birds, the mount of Lord Viṣṇu), nor even the mind moves so swiftly as does this son of the wind-god course through the high skies. (26)

verses.text:
यदि तावच्छिशोरस्य ईदृशो गतिविक्रमः।
यौवनं बलमासाद्य कथं वेगो भविष्यति॥ २७॥
verses.m: “When such is his speed and prowess as a mere babe, what will be his speed when he has attained the vigour of youth?’ (27)

verses.text:
तमनुप्लवते वायुः प्लवन्तं पुत्रमात्मनः।
सूर्यदाहभयाद् रक्षंस्तुषारचयशीतलः॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Cool to the touch like a mass of snow, the wind-god too followed his son in his flight, protecting him from the danger of getting scorched by the sun. (28)

verses.text:
बहुयोजनसाहस्रं क्रमन्नेव गतोऽम्बरम्।
पितुर्बलाच्च बाल्याच्च भास्कराभ्याशमागतः॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Shooting up through the heavens for many thousands of Yojanas by virtue of his father’s might and his own childlike simplicity, he drew near to the sun. (29)

verses.text:
शिशुरेष त्वदोषज्ञ इति मत्वा दिवाकरः।
कार्यं चास्मिन् समायत्तमित्येवं न ददाह सः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Realizing that he was a mere innocent child and also that a great purpose (of Śrī Rāma) waited to be accomplished by him, the said sun-god did not consume him. (30)

verses.text:
यमेव दिवसं ह्येष ग्रहीतुं भास्करं प्लुतः।
तमेव दिवसं राहुर्जिघृक्षति दिवाकरम्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Rāhu (the demon who is traditionally believed to devour the orb of the sun during an eclipse) sought to seize the sun the same day on which Hanumān actually sprang in the sky to catch hold of the sun. (31)

verses.text:
अनेन च परामृष्टो राहुः सूर्यरथोपरि।
अपक्रान्तस्ततस्त्रस्तो राहुश्चन्द्रार्कमर्दनः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Nay, Rāhu was laid hands on by Hanumān on the solar chariot. Thereupon Rāhu, the scourge of the sun-god and the moon-god, slipped away from that place, frightened. (32)

verses.text:
इन्द्रस्य भवनं गत्वा सरोषः सिंहिकासुतः।
अब्रवीद् भ्रुकुटिं कृत्वा देवं देवगणैर्वृतम्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “Knitting his eyebrows after proceeding to the abode of Indra, Rāhu (son of Siṁhikā) angrily spoke as follows to the deity surrounded by hosts of gods: (33)

verses.text:
बुभुक्षापनयं दत्त्वा चन्द्रार्कौ मम वासव।
किमिदं तत् त्वया दत्तमन्यस्य बलवृत्रहन्॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “ ‘Having allotted to me the moon and the sun as a means of appeasing my hunger, O Indra, how is it that my aforesaid share has been given over by you to another, O destroyer of the demons Bala and Vṛtra? (34)

verses.text:
अद्याहं पर्वकाले तु जिघृक्षुः सूर्यमागतः।
अथान्यो राहुरासाद्य जग्राह सहसा रविम्॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “ ‘Today at the conjunction of the moonless night and the new moon day I for my part came to lay hold of the sun. Meanwhile, approaching the sun, another Rāhu seized it all at once.’ (35)

verses.text:
स राहोर्वचनं श्रुत्वा वासवः सम्भ्रमान्वितः।
उत्पपातासनं हित्वा उद्वहन् काञ्चनीं स्रजम्॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “Leaving his seat on hearing the grievance of Rāhu, Indra, full of awe, sprang on his feet, holding up his gold necklace. (36)

verses.text:
ततः कैलासकूटाभं चतुर्दन्तं मदस्रवम्।
शृङ्गारधारिणं प्रांशुं स्वर्णघण्टाट्टहासिनम्॥ ३७॥
इन्द्रः करीन्द्रमारुह्य राहुं कृत्वा पुरःसरम्।
प्रायाद् यत्राभवत् सूर्यः सहानेन हनूमता॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “Mounting Airāvata (the king of elephants), who was tall like a peak of Mount Kailāsa, was distinguished by four tusks, nay, who (being in heat) was exuding temple-juice, was richly decorated, and was uttering a horse-laugh in the form of the ringing of a gold bell, and placing Rāhu before him, Indra marched to the spot where the sun-god was with the yonder Hanūmān. (37-38)

verses.text:
अथातिरभसेनागाद् राहुरुत्सृज्य वासवम्।
अनेन च स वै दृष्टः प्रधावन् शैलकूटवत्॥ ३९॥
verses.m: “Meanwhile, leaving Indra behind, Rāhu advanced with great speed and he was actually seen by Hanumān running fast like a mountain-peak in motion. (39)

verses.text:
ततः सूर्यं समुत्सृज्य राहुं फलमवेक्ष्य च।
उत्पपात पुनर्व्योम ग्रहीतुं सिंहिकासुतम्॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “Leaving the sun and visualizing Rāhu to be a fruit, Hanumān thereupon again bounded in the skies to take hold of the son of Siṁhikā. (40)

verses.text:
उत्सृज्यार्कमिमं राम प्रधावन्तं प्लवङ्गमम्।
अवेक्ष्यैवं परावृत्तो मुखशेषः पराङ्मुखः॥ ४१॥
verses.m: “Clearly perceiving this monkey, Hanumān, running with all speed towards him leaving the sun alone, O Rāma, Rāhu, who had such huge proportions and of whom the head alone remained* retraced his steps with his face turned in the opposite direction. (41)

verses.text:
इन्द्रमाशंसमानस्तु त्रातारं सिंहिकासुतः।
इन्द्र इन्द्रेति संत्रासान्मुहुर्मुहुरभाषत॥ ४२॥
verses.m: “Looking forward to Indra as his protector, Rāhu (the son of Siṁhikā) for his part repeatedly cried out in his terror ‘Indra!’ ‘Indra!’ (42)

verses.text:
राहोर्विक्रोशमानस्य प्रागेवालक्षितं स्वरम्।
श्रुत्वेन्द्रोवाच मा भैषीरहमेनं निषूदये॥ ४३॥
verses.m: “Hearing the voice of the screaming Rāhu, which was already known to him, Indra said, ‘Don’t be afraid, I shall presently make short work of him.’ (43)

verses.text:
ऐरावतं ततो दृष्ट्वा महत्तदिदमित्यपि।
फलं तं हस्तिराजानमभिदुद्राव मारुतिः॥ ४४॥
verses.m: “Espying after that Airāvata and taking the king of elephants too to be some enormous fruit, Hanumān, son of the wind-god, rushed at him. (44)

verses.text:
तथास्य धावतो रूपमैरावतजिघृक्षया।
मुहूर्तमभवद् घोरमिन्द्राग्न्योरिव भास्वरम्॥ ४५॥
verses.m: “Nay, the form of Hanumān, even as he was rushing at Airāvata with intent to catch hold of him, turned for a while fearful and splendid like those of Indra and the god of fire. (45)

verses.text:
एवमाधावमानं तु नातिक्रुद्धः शचीपतिः।
हस्तान्तादतिमुक्तेन कुलिशेनाभ्यताडयत्॥ ४६॥
verses.m: “Though not highly provoked, Indra (the consort of Śacī) struck Hanumān, who was rushing towards him, with the thunderbolt hurled from the extremities of his hand. (46)

verses.text:
ततो गिरौ पपातैष इन्द्रवज्राभिताडितः।
पतमानस्य चैतस्य वामा हनुरभज्यत॥ ४७॥
verses.m: “Hit by the thunderbolt of Indra, Hanumān thereupon fell on a mountain; and as he fell his left jaw was broken. (47)

verses.text:
तस्मिंस्तु पतिते चापि वज्रताडनविह्वले।
चुक्रोधेन्द्राय पवनः प्रजानामहिताय सः॥ ४८॥
verses.m: “Nay, Hanumān for his part having fallen and getting confused too under the stroke of the thunderbolt, the celebrated wind-god got angry with Indra to the detriment of created beings. (48)

verses.text:
प्रचारं स तु संगृह्य प्रजास्वन्तर्गतः प्रभुः।
गुहां प्रविष्टः स्वसुतं शिशुमादाय मारुतः॥ ४९॥
verses.m: “Withdrawing his movement in the form of respiration, though abiding in all living beings, the celebrated and all-powerful wind-god penetrated deep into a cave, taking his infant son with him. (49)

verses.text:
विण्मूत्राशयमावृत्य प्रजानां परमार्तिकृत्।
रुरोध सर्वभूतानि यथा वर्षाणि वासवः॥ ५०॥
verses.m: “Causing extreme suffering to created beings by obstructing their bowels and bladder, the wind-god rendered all created beings motionless even as Indra holds up the rains. (50)

verses.text:
वायुप्रकोपाद् भूतानि निरुच्छ्वासानि सर्वतः।
संधिभिर्भिद्यमानैश्च काष्ठभूतानि जज्ञिरे॥ ५१॥
verses.m: “Due to the wrath of the wind-god living beings everywhere felt choked and turned stiff like wood, as it were, due to their joints getting disrupted. (51)

verses.text:
निःस्वाध्यायवषट्कारं निष्क्रियं धर्मवर्जितम्।
वायुप्रकोपात् त्रैलोक्यं निरयस्थमिवाभवत्॥ ५२॥
verses.m: “Bereft of study of the Vedas and sacrificial performances, and devoid of rituals and the practice of virtue as a result of the displeasure of the wind-god, all the three worlds felt as if they had sunk into hell. (52)

verses.text:
ततः प्रजाः सगन्धर्वाः सदेवासुरमानुषाः।
प्रजापतिं समाधावन् दुःखिताश्च सुखेच्छया॥ ५३॥
verses.m: “Feeling afflicted, all created beings including the Gandharvas (celestial musicians), gods, demons and human beings hurried to Brahmā (the lord of creation) with intent to obtain relief. (53)

verses.text:
ऊचुः प्राञ्जलयो देवा महोदरनिभोदराः।
त्वया तु भगवन् सृष्टाः प्रजा नाथ चतुर्विधाः॥ ५४॥
verses.m: “With bloated bellies resembling the bellies of those suffering from the disease of dropsy, the gods submitted with joined palms: ‘By you, indeed, O lord! our master, the four types of created beings 1. viviparous, 2. oviparous, 3. the sweat-born and 4. those sprouting from the earth were evolved. (54)

verses.text:
त्वया दत्तोऽयमस्माकमायुषः पवनः पतिः।
सोऽस्मान् प्राणेश्वरो भूत्वा कस्मादेषोऽद्य सत्तम॥ ५५॥
रुरोध दुःखं जनयन्नन्तःपुर इव स्त्रियः।
तस्मात् त्वां शरणं प्राप्ता वायुनोपहता वयम्॥ ५६॥
verses.m: “ ‘The wind-god was bestowed on us by you as the lord of our lives. Wherefore, O prince of the virtuous, has he, even though being the controller of our vital breaths, suffocated us today, even as a king would confine his womenfolk in a gynaeceum, thereby causing affliction to us? Afflicted by the wind-god, we have accordingly sought you as our shelter. (55-56)

verses.text:
वायुसंरोधजं दुःखमिदं नो नुद दुःखहन्।
एतत् प्रजानां श्रुत्वा तु प्रजानाथः प्रजापतिः॥ ५७॥
कारणादिति चोक्त्वासौ प्रजाः पुनरभाषत।
यस्मिंश्च कारणे वायुश्चुक्रोध च रुरोध च॥ ५८॥
प्रजाः शृणुध्वं तत् सर्वं श्रोतव्यं चात्मनः क्षमम्।
पुत्रस्तस्यामरेशेन इन्द्रेणाद्य निपातितः॥ ५९॥
राहोर्वचनमास्थाय ततः स कुपितोऽनिलः।
अशरीरः शरीरेषु वायुश्चरति पालयन्॥ ६०॥
verses.m: “ ‘Pray, relieve this suffering of ours caused by the obstruction of the wind, O allayer of suffering!’ “Hearing this petition of the created beings, and saying, ‘This has happened due to some reason’, the lord of creation, the protector of all created beings, for his part continued as follows: ‘Hear, O created beings, for what reason the wind-god got angry and held up his movement; all that deserves to be listened to by you and is justifiable too. In response to the appeal of Rāhu, the son of the wind-god has been struck down today by Indra, the ruler of gods; hence the said wind-god got angry. Going without a body, the wind-god moves in all bodies preserving them. (57—60)

verses.text:
शरीरं हि विना वायुं समतां याति दारुभिः।
वायुः प्राणः सुखं वायुर्वायुः सर्वमिदं जगत्॥ ६१॥
verses.m: “Devoid of the wind, a body attains similarity to blocks of wood. Air is life, air is happiness, the air constitutes all this universe. (61)

verses.text:
वायुना सम्परित्यक्तं न सुखं विन्दते जगत्।
अद्यैव च परित्यक्तं वायुना जगदायुषा॥ ६२॥
verses.m: “Entirely devoid of the air, the world does not attain happiness. The world has just now been forsaken by the wind, which is its very life. (62)

verses.text:
अद्यैव ते निरुच्छ्वासाः काष्ठकुड्योपमाः स्थिताः।
तद् यामस्तत्र यत्रास्ते मारुतो रुक्प्रदो हि नः।
मा विनाशं गमिष्याम अप्रसाद्यादितेः सुताः॥ ६३॥
verses.m: “ ‘Being unable to breathe, all created beings stand no better than the blocks of wood or walls. Therefore, we shall actually proceed to that place where the wind-god who is causing pain to us, is present; let us not go to ruin by not placating him, O sons of Aditi!’ (63)

verses.text:
ततः प्रजाभिः सहितः प्रजापतिः
सदेवगन्धर्वभुजङ्गगुह्यकैः।
जगाम तत्रास्यति यत्र मारुतः
सुतं सुरेन्द्राभिहतं प्रगृह्य सः॥ ६४॥
verses.m: “Accompanied by all created beings including gods, the Gandharvas (celestial musicians), serpents and Guhyakas (Yakṣas), Brahmā (the lord of creation) thereupon moved to the place where the said wind-god sat, taking hold of his son who had been struck down by Indra. (64)

verses.text:
ततोऽर्कवैश्वानरकाञ्चनप्रभं
सुतं तदोत्सङ्गगतं सदागतेः।
चतुर्मुखो वीक्ष्य कृपामथाकरोत्
सदेवगन्धर्वऋषियक्षराक्षसैः ॥ ६५॥
verses.m: “Perceiving at that time the son of the wind-god (who is perpetually in motion), radiant as the sun, fire and gold, in his lap, Brahmā (the four-faced god) accompanied by Gandharvas, Ṛṣis (the seers of Vedic Mantras), Yakṣas and ogres, including gods, thereupon immediately took pity on the child.” (65)

verses.text:
ततः पितामहं दृष्ट्वा वायुः पुत्रवधार्दितः।
शिशुकं तं समादाय उत्तस्थौ धातुरग्रतः॥ १॥
verses.m: “On seeing Brahmā (the grandfather of the entire creation, which is evolved by his ten mind-born sons), the wind-god, who was tormented by the death of his son, stood in front of the creator, bearing that child in his arms. (1)

verses.text:
चलकुण्डलमौलिस्रक् तपनीयविभूषणः।
पादयोर्न्यपतद् वायुस्त्रिरुपस्थाय वेधसे॥ २॥
verses.m: “Standing thrice submissively before the creator, the wind-god with swinging earrings, nay, adorned with a diadem and garland, and ornaments of gold, fell at the former’s feet. (2)

verses.text:
तं तु वेदविदा तेन लम्बाभरणशोभिना।
वायुमुत्थाप्य हस्तेन शिशुं तं परिमृष्टवान्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Lifting up the wind-god, Brahmā (the knower of the Vedas) stroked that child with his long, outstretched and adorned hand. (3)

verses.text:
स्पृष्टमात्रस्ततः सोऽथ सलीलं पद्मजन्मना।
जलसिक्तं यथा सस्यं पुनर्जीवितमाप्तवान्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “The moment Hanumān was sportingly touched by Brahmā (the lotus-born), he thereupon forthwith came back to life like a crop which has been watered. (4)

verses.text:
प्राणवन्तमिमं दृष्ट्वा प्राणो गन्धवहो मुदा।
चचार सर्वभूतेषु संनिरुद्धं यथा पुरा॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Seeing Hanumān restored to life, the wind-god, constituting the vital breath of the entire creation, began once more to circulate inwardly as before in all creatures. (5)

verses.text:
मरुद्रोधाद् विनिर्मुक्तास्ताः प्रजा मुदिताऽभवन्।
शीतवातविनिर्मुक्ताः पद्मिन्य इव साम्बुजाः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Completely freed from the obstruction caused by the wind-god, all those created beings became joyful again like lakes spotted with lotus flowers when rid of cold winds. (6)

verses.text:
ततस्त्रियुग्मस्त्रिककुत् त्रिधामा त्रिदशार्चितः।
उवाच देवता ब्रह्मा मारुतप्रियकाम्यया॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Thereupon Brahmā, who is endowed with three pairs of divine properties (viz., glory and prowess, power and wealth, wisdom and dispassion), who appears in three forms (viz., Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva), who has His abode in all the three worlds, and who is worshipped by all the gods (lit., those who pass through only three stages in life, viz., infancy, boyhood and prime of youth) spoke as follows to the gods with intent to oblige the wind-god: (7)

verses.text:
भो महेन्द्राग्निवरुणा महेश्वरधनेश्वराः।
जानतामपि वः सर्वं वक्ष्यामि श्रूयतां हितम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: “ ‘O mighty Indra, Agni (the god of fire), Varuṇa (the god presiding over the waters), Lord Śiva (the Supreme Ruler) and Kubera (the god of riches) to you, even though you know everything, I will tell you what is conducive to your good; please listen. (8)

verses.text:
अनेन शिशुना कार्यं कर्तव्यं वो भविष्यति।
तद् ददध्वं वरान् सर्वे मारुतस्यास्य तुष्टये॥ ९॥
verses.m: “ ‘Your purpose shall be accomplished by this infant. Therefore, grant him boons all of you with a view to the appeasement of the wind-god.’ (9)

verses.text:
ततः सहस्रनयनः प्रीतियुक्तः शुभाननः।
कुशेशयमयीं मालामुत्क्षेप्येदं वचोऽब्रवीत्॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Taking off his wreath of lotus flowers and placing it round the neck of Hanumān, Indra (the thousand-eyed god), who had a charming countenance, uttered the following words: (10)

verses.text:
मत्करोत्सृष्टवज्रेण हनुरस्य यथा हतः।
नाम्ना वै कपिशार्दूलो भविता हनुमानिति॥ ११॥
verses.m: “ ‘Inasmuch as the chin of this infant was broken by the thunderbolt hurled from my hand, this tiger among the monkeys will surely go by the name of Hanumān. (11)

verses.text:
अहमस्य प्रदास्यामि परमं वरमद्भुतम्।
इतः प्रभृति वज्रस्य ममावध्यो भविष्यति॥ १२॥
verses.m: “ ‘I hereby grant him the supreme and wonderful boon that from this day onwards he will be invulnerable to my thunderbolt.’ (12)

verses.text:
मार्तण्डस्त्वब्रवीत् तत्र भगवांस्तिमिरापहः।
तेजसोऽस्य मदीयस्य ददामि शतिकां कलाम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “The glorious sun-god, the dispeller of darkness, for his part said on that occasion, ‘I bestow upon him a hundredth part of my brilliance. (13)

verses.text:
यदा च शास्त्राण्यध्येतुं शक्तिरस्य भविष्यति।
तदास्य शास्त्रं दास्यामि येन वाग्मी भविष्यति।
न चास्य भविता कश्चित् सदृशः शास्त्रदर्शने॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Again, when the ability to study the Śāstras (the various branches of learning) appears in him, then I shall impart to him the knowledge of the Śāstras, whereby he will become a good speaker. Nay, none shall vie with him in the knowledge of the Śāstras.’ (14)

verses.text:
वरुणश्च वरं प्रादान्नास्य मृत्युर्भविष्यति।
वर्षायुतशतेनापि मत्पाशादुदकादपि॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Nay, Varuṇa conferred on him the boon that his death will not occur even in millions of years from his noose or from water either. (15)

verses.text:
यमो दण्डादवध्यत्वमरोगत्वं च दत्तवान्।
वरं ददामि संतुष्ट अविषादं च संयुगे॥ १६॥
गदेयं मामिका नैनं संयुगेषु वधिष्यति।
इत्येवं धनदः प्राह तदा ह्येकाक्षिपिङ्गलः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Yama granted him invulnerability to his rod and freedom from ailment. Then Kubera (the bestower of riches), who was brown of one eye, actually said, ‘Highly pleased, I grant him the boon that this mace of mine shall not cause his death in conflicts and further vouchsafe him unweariness in war.’ (16-17)

verses.text:
मत्तो मदायुधानां च अवध्योऽयं भविष्यति।
इत्येवं शङ्करेणापि दत्तोऽस्य परमो वरः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “The supreme boon that ‘This child shall be immune from death at My hands as well as from death caused by My weapons’ was bestowed on him by Lord Śaṅkara, the Bestower of happiness. (18)

verses.text:
विश्वकर्मा च दृष्ट्वेमं बालसूर्योपमं शिशुम्।
शिल्पिनां प्रवरः प्रादाद् वरमस्य महामतिः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Nay, beholding that infant, who vied with the rising sun, the highly intelligent Viśwakarmā, the foremost among the builders, granted him the following boon: (19)

verses.text:
मत्कृतानि च शस्त्राणि यानि दिव्यानि तानि च।
तैरवध्यत्वमापन्नश्चिरजीवी भविष्यति॥ २०॥
verses.m: ‘Having acquired invulnerability to celestial weapons that have been forged by me as well as to those which exist in my mind, he shall be long-lived.’ (20)

verses.text:
दीर्घायुश्च महात्मा च ब्रह्मा तं प्राब्रवीद् वचः।
सर्वेषां ब्रह्मदण्डानामवध्योऽयं भविष्यति॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Brahmā made the following augury concerning the infant: ‘This infant shall be long-lived and magnanimous and shall be invulnerable to all rods of punishment connected with Brahmā (the creator) or to the imprecations pronounced by the Brāhmaṇas.” (21)

verses.text:
ततः सुराणां तु वरैर्दृष्ट्वा ह्येनमलङ्कृतम्।
चतुर्मुखस्तुष्टमना वायुमाह जगद्गुरुः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Gratified to see the infant enriched by the boons granted by the gods, Brahmā (the four-faced god), the teacher of the world, spoke to the wind-god as follows: (22)

verses.text:
अमित्राणां भयकरो मित्राणामभयंकरः।
अजेयो भविता पुत्रस्तव मारुत मारुतिः॥ २३॥
verses.m: “ ‘Your son, Hanumān, O wind-god, will prove to be a terror to his foes, will vouchsafe immunity from fear to his friends and will prove invincible. (23)

verses.text:
कामरूपः कामचारी कामगः प्लवतां वरः।
भवत्यव्याहतगतिः कीर्तिमांश्च भविष्यति॥ २४॥
verses.m: “ ‘This jewel among the monkeys shall be able to change his form at will, and go wheresoever he pleases at the speed of his choice; his movements will remain unimpeded and everywhere he shall turn out glorious. (24)

verses.text:
रावणोत्सादनार्थानि रामप्रीतिकराणि च।
रोमहर्षकराण्येव कर्ता कर्माणि संयुगे॥ २५॥
verses.m: “ ‘In the war he shall accomplish feats intended to uproot Rāvaṇa, pleasing to Śrī Rāma and causing one’s hair to stand on end.’ (25)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा तमामन्त्र्य मारुतं त्वमरैः सह।
यथागतं ययुः सर्वे पितामहपुरोगमाः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Saying so and taking leave of the well-known wind-god, all the petitioners including the gods, with Brahmā (the grandfather of the entire creation) at their head, returned even as they had come.(26)

verses.text:
सोऽपि गन्धवहः पुत्रं प्रगृह्य गृहमानयत्।
अञ्जनायास्तमाख्याय वरदत्तं विनिर्गतः॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Taking his son with him, the wind-god (the wafter of smells), brought the child home and, telling Añjanā of the child having been granted boons by the gods, departed. (27)

verses.text:
प्राप्य राम वरानेष वरदानबलान्वितः।
जवेनात्मनि संस्थेन सोऽसौ पूर्ण इवार्णवः॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Having obtained boons from the gods, and enriched by the strength which accrued from the bestowal of boons, O Rāma, this celebrated Hanumān replete with his native velocity, resembled the ocean. (28)

verses.text:
तरसा पूर्यमाणोऽपि तदा वानरपुङ्गवः।
आश्रमेषु महर्षीणामपराध्यति निर्भयः॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Overflowing with vigour, Hanumān (a bull among the monkeys) fearlessly began to offend even against the sanctity of the hermitages of eminent Ṛṣis seers of Vedic Mantras at that time. (29)

verses.text:
स्रुग्भाण्डान्यग्निहोत्राणि वल्कलानां च संचयान्।
भग्नविच्छिन्नविध्वस्तान् संशान्तानां करोत्ययम्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “He broke the sacrificial ladles and vessels, interrupted the pouring of oblations into the sacred fires and tore to shreds the piles of bark belonging to the perfectly tranquil ascetics living in the hermitages. (30)

verses.text:
एवंविधानि कर्माणि प्रावर्तत महाबलः।
सर्वेषां ब्रह्मदण्डानामवध्यः शम्भुना कृतः॥ ३१॥
जानन्त ऋषयः सर्वे सहन्ते तस्य शक्तितः।
तथा केसरिणा त्वेष वायुना सोऽञ्जनीसुतः॥ ३२॥
प्रतिषिद्धोऽपि मर्यादां लङ्घयत्येव वानरः।
ततो महर्षयः क्रुद्धा भृग्वङ्गिरसवंशजाः॥ ३३॥
शेपुरेनं रघुश्रेष्ठ नातिक्रुद्धातिमन्यवः।
बाधसे यत् समाश्रित्य बलमस्मान् प्लवङ्गम॥ ३४॥
तद् दीर्घकालं वेत्तासि नास्माकं शापमोहितः।
यदा ते स्मार्यते कीर्तिस्तदा ते वर्धते बलम्॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “Hanumān, who was endowed with extraordinary might, freely indulged in such pranks. Knowing that he had been rendered immune by Brahmā (the source of happiness) from death caused by all kinds of curses pronounced by Brāhmaṇas, all those Ṛṣis (seers of Vedic Mantras), put up with them because of the power derived from the boons. Even though prohibited by Kesarī (Añjanā’s husband and Hanumān’s foster-father) as well as by the wind-god, the yonder monkey, the son of Añjanā, for his part continued to exceed the bounds of propriety. Provoked to anger, the eminent sages, born in the line of Bhṛgu and Aṅgirā (the mind-born sons of Brahmā), who were really speaking neither enraged nor highly indignant, thereupon cursed him as follows, O jewel among Raghus: “ ‘Bewitched by our imprecation, you will remain unconscious for a long time of the power, banking on which you are harassing us, O monkey! You will become aware of your mighty prowess when someone reminds you of your glory.’ (31—35)

verses.text:
ततस्तु हृततेजौजा महर्षिवचनौजसा।
एषोऽऽश्रमाणि तान्येव मृदुभावं गतोऽचरत्॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “Deprived of the knowledge of his energy and vigour by the strength of the execration pronounced by the eminent sages, Hanumān, for his part, thereupon ranged over those very hermitages in a placid mood. (36)

verses.text:
अथर्क्षरजसो नाम वालिसुग्रीवयोः पिता।
सर्ववानरराजासीत् तेजसा इव भास्करः॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “At that time, the father of Vālī and Sugrīva, Ṛkṣarajā by name, who resembled the sun in splendour, was the ruler of all the monkeys. (37)

verses.text:
स तु राज्यं चिरं कृत्वा वानराणां महेश्वरः।
ततस्त्वर्क्षरजा नाम कालधर्मेण योजितः॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “Having ruled for a long time, that suzerain lord of the monkeys, Ṛkṣarajā by name, for his part, was subjected to the natural law of Time. (38)

verses.text:
तस्मिन्नस्तमिते चाथ मन्त्रिभिर्मन्त्रकोविदैः।
पित्र्ये पदे कृतो वाली सुग्रीवो वालिनः पदे॥ ३९॥
verses.m: “He having met his death, Vālī was forthwith installed in the position of his father and Sugrīva in the position of Vālī (the Crown prince) by his counsellors, who were expert in counselling. (39)

verses.text:
सुग्रीवेण समं त्वस्य अद्वैधं छिद्रवर्जितम्।
आबाल्यं सख्यमभवदनिलस्याग्निना यथा॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “From his very boyhood Vāli developed with Sugrīva an unwarying and unbroken brotherhood, similar to that of the wind with fire. (40)

verses.text:
एष शापवशादेव न वेद बलमात्मनः।
वालिसुग्रीवयोर्वैरं यदा राम समुत्थितम्॥ ४१॥
न ह्येष राम सुग्रीवो भ्राम्यमाणोऽपि वालिना।
देव जानाति न ह्येष बलमात्मनि मारुतिः॥ ४२॥
verses.m: “By reason of that very curse, Hanumān was not conscious of his might. When hostility arose between Vālī and Sugrīva, O Rāma, neither the yonder Sugrīva, even while he was being forced to wander from place to place, O Lord Rāma, nor this son of the wind-god, Hanumān, was actually aware of the strength which existed in him. (41-42)

verses.text:
ऋषिशापाहृतबलस्तदैव कपिसत्तमः।
सिंहः कुञ्जररुद्धो वा आस्थितः सहितो रणे॥ ४३॥
verses.m: “Deprived of the knowledge of his own might by the curse of the sages, Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys, remained standing by the side of Sugrīva during that very period like a lion kept back by an elephant, in the course of the latter’s combat with Vālī. (43)

verses.text:
पराक्रमोत्साहमतिप्रताप-
सौशील्यमाधुर्यनयानयैश्च।
गाम्भीर्यचातुर्यसुवीर्यधैर्यै-
र्हनूमतः कोऽप्यधिकोऽस्ति लोके॥ ४४॥
verses.m: “Who is there in the world superior to Hanumān in respect of prowess, energy, extraordinary glory, amiability, sweetness of temper and the knowledge of what is prudent or otherwise, as well as of profundity, cleverness, extraordinary virility and firmness? (44)

verses.text:
असौ पुनर्व्याकरणं ग्रहीष्यन्
सूर्योन्मुखः प्रष्टुमनाः कपीन्द्रः।
उद्यद्गिरेरस्तगिरिं जगाम
ग्रन्थं महद्धारयनप्रमेयः॥ ४५॥
verses.m: “With his face turned towards the sun-god with a view to learn grammar and desiring to put questions to him, (in order to remove his doubts) the yonder chief of monkeys, of immeasurable energy, journeyed from the hill where the sun rises to the hill where it sets, with intent to master the great work on grammar. (45)

verses.text:
ससूत्रवृत्त्यर्थपदं महार्थं
ससंग्रहं सिद्ध्यति वै कपीन्द्रः।
नह्यस्य कश्चित् सदृशोऽस्ति शास्त्रे
वैशारदे छन्दगतौ तथैव॥ ४६॥
verses.m: “Hanumān (the chief of monkeys) has mastered the great gloss on the aphorisms including the aphorisms of grammar as well as the Vṛtti (comment), the Vārtīka (annotation) on the aphorisms and also the monographs on the subject. Indeed there is none like him in the knowledge of other branches of learning as well as in prosody. (46)

verses.text:
सर्वासु विद्यासु तपोविधाने
प्रस्पर्धतेऽयं हि गुरुं सुराणाम्।
सोऽयं नवव्याकरणार्थवेत्ता
ब्रह्मा भविष्यत्यपि ते प्रसादात्॥ ४७॥
verses.m: “He actually rivals Sage Bṛhaspati (the preceptor of gods) in all the branches of learning as well as in the practice of austerities. Well-versed in the subject-matter of the nine systems of grammar, the yonder Hanumān shall prove to be a very Brahmā by Your grace. (47)

verses.text:
प्रवीविवक्षोरिव सागरस्य
लोकान् दिधक्षोरिव पावकस्य।
लोकक्षयेष्वेव यथान्तकस्य
हनूमतः स्थास्यति कः पुरस्तात्॥ ४८॥
verses.m: “Who can stand face to face with Hanūmān, who resembles the ocean threatening (at the time of final dissolution) to corrode the earth or the fire which (at the end of the world-period) is out to consume the universe and who resembles Death on the occasion of the destruction of the world? (48)

verses.text:
एषेव चान्ये च महाकपीन्द्राः
सुग्रीवमैन्दद्विविदाः सनीलाः।
सतारतारेयनलाः सरम्भा-
स्त्वत्कारणाद् राम सुरैर्हि सृष्टाः॥ ४९॥
verses.m: “Like him, other great leaders of monkeys too, viz., Sugrīva, Mainda and Dwivida including Nīla, Tāra, Aṅgada (son of Tārā) and Nala as also Rambha were actually procreated by the gods for your sake, O Rāma! (49)

verses.text:
गजो गवाक्षो गवयः सुदंष्ट्रो
मैन्दः प्रभो ज्योतिमुखो नलश्च।
एते च ऋक्षाः सह वानरेन्द्रै-
स्त्वत्कारणाद् राम सुरैर्हि सृष्टाः॥ ५०॥
verses.m: “Nay, alongwith the aforesaid leaders of monkeys, Gaja, Gavākṣa, Gavaya, Sudaṁṣṭra, Mainda, Prabha, Jyotimukha and Nala—these bears too were actually procreated by the gods for your sake only, O Rāma! (50)

verses.text:
तदेतत् कथितं सर्वं यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि।
हनूमतो बालभावे कर्मैतत् कथितं मया॥ ५१॥
verses.m: “All that you asked me has hereby been related by me. The feats performed by Hanumān in his childhood have also been recounted by me.” (51)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वागस्त्यस्य कथितं रामः सौमित्रिरेव च।
विस्मयं परमं जग्मुर्वानरा राक्षसैः सह॥ ५२॥
verses.m: Hearing the tale of Agastya, Śrī Rāma as well as Lakṣmaṇa, as also the monkeys alongwith the ogres experienced great wonder. (52)

verses.text:
अगस्त्यस्त्वब्रवीद् रामं सर्वमेतच्छ्रुतं त्वया।
दृष्टः सम्भाषितश्चासि राम गच्छामहे वयम्॥ ५३॥
verses.m: Agastya for his part said to Śrī Rāma, “All this has been listened to by You. You have also been seen and spoken to by us, O Rāma! We now depart.” (53)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वैतद् राघवो वाक्यमगस्त्यस्योग्रतेजसः।
प्राञ्जलिः प्रणतश्चापि महर्षिमिदमब्रवीत्॥ ५४॥
verses.m: Hearing this statement of Agastya of formidable lustre, Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) submissively replied as follows with joined palms to the great sage: (54)

verses.text:
अद्य मे देवतास्तुष्टाः पितरः प्रपितामहाः।
युष्माकं दर्शनादेव नित्यं तुष्टाः सबान्धवाः॥ ५५॥
verses.m: “The gods, the eternal manes as well as the souls of My departed ancestors are pleased with Me today. As for ourselves we stand ever gratified with our kinsfolk through your very sight. (55)

verses.text:
विज्ञाप्यं तु ममैतद्धि यद् वदाम्यागतस्पृहः।
तद् भवद्भिर्मम कृते कर्तव्यमनुकम्पया॥ ५६॥
verses.m: “Here is something actually worth bringing to your notice. Seized with a longing, that which I submit to you must be carried out by you out of compassion to Me. (56)

verses.text:
पौरजानपदान् स्थाप्य स्वकार्येष्वहमागतः।
क्रतूनहं करिष्यामि प्रभावाद् भवतां सताम्॥ ५७॥
verses.m: “After appointing the citizens as well as the people of the countryside to their respective duties, now that I have returned from My exile in the forest, I intend to perform sacrifices through the goodwill of saintly persons like you. (57)

verses.text:
सदस्या मम यज्ञेषु भवन्तो नित्यमेव तु।
भविष्यथ महावीर्या ममानुग्रहकांक्षिणः॥ ५८॥
verses.m: “Longing, as you do, to bless Me, you, for your part, who are endowed with extraordinary prowess born of asceticism, should constantly act as superintending priests at My sacrificial performances. (58)

verses.text:
अहं युष्मान् समाश्रित्य तपोनिर्धूतकल्मषान्।
अनुगृहीतः पितृभिर्भविष्यामि सुनिर्वृतः॥ ५९॥
verses.m: “Fully depending on you, who have shaken off all sins through asceticism, I shall be blessed by My ancestors and feel exceedingly happy. (59)

verses.text:
तदागन्तव्यमनिशं भवद्भिरिह संगतैः।
अगस्त्याद्यास्तु तच्छ्रुत्वा ऋषयः संशितव्रताः॥ ६०॥
एवमस्त्विति तं प्रोच्य प्रयातुमुपचक्रमुः।
एवमुक्त्वा गताः सर्वे ऋषयस्ते यथागतम्॥ ६१॥
verses.m: “You all should always come here in a body at the time when the sacrifice has commenced.” Hearing the aforesaid request and saying “Amen” to Him, the sages of rigid vows, the foremost of whom was Agastya, began to depart. Saying so, all the aforesaid sages left as they came. (60-61)

verses.text:
राघवश्च तमेवार्थं चिन्तयामास विस्मितः।
ततोऽस्तं भास्करे याते विसृज्य नृपवानरान्॥ ६२॥
संध्यामुपास्य विधिवत् तदा नरवरोत्तमः।
प्रवृत्तायां रजन्यां तु सोऽन्तःपुरचरोऽभवत्॥ ६३॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma too pondered in amazement over that very subject of performing sacrifices. Having seen off the assembled kings and monkeys on the sun having set, and performed the Sandhyā devotions with due ceremony, Śrī Rāma, the foremost of jewels among men, for His part retired into the gynaeceum when the night had set in. (62-63)

verses.text:
अभिषिक्ते तु काकुत्स्थे धर्मेण विदितात्मनि।
व्यतीता या निशा पूर्वा पौराणां हर्षवर्धिनी॥ १॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma (a scion of Kakutstha), who understood the nature of the soul, having been consecrated on the throne of Ayodhyā in accordance with the prescribed rule, the first night, which enhanced the delight of the citizens of Ayodhyā, passed. (1)

verses.text:
तस्यां रजन्यां व्युष्टायां प्रातर्नृपतिबोधकाः।
वन्दिनः समुपातिष्ठन् सौम्या नृपतिवेश्मनि॥ २॥
verses.m: The said night having ended, the following morning the gentle bards who were charged with the duty of waking the king assembled at the royal palace. (2)

verses.text:
ते रक्तकण्ठिनः सर्वे किन्नरा इव शिक्षिताः।
तुष्टुवुर्नृपतिं वीरं यथावत् सम्प्रहर्षिणः॥ ३॥
verses.m: Sweet-voiced as they were and trained in the art of singing like the Kinnaras (celestial minstrels), they all, full of excessive joy, began duly to extol the heroic king as follows: (3)

verses.text:
वीर सौम्य प्रबुध्यस्व कौसल्याप्रीतिवर्धन।
जगद्धि सर्वं स्वपिति त्वयि सुप्ते नराधिप॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Awake, O gentle hero, the enhancer of the delight of mother Kausalyā! Indeed the whole world remains buried in sleep while you are asleep, O suzerain lord of men! (4)

verses.text:
विक्रमस्ते यथा विष्णो रूपं चैवाश्विनोरिव।
बुद्ध्या बृहस्पतेस्तुल्यः प्रजापतिसमो ह्यसि॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Your prowess is like that of Lord Viṣṇu, and your comeliness is like that of the twin-born Aświns, the physicians of gods. You are a compeer of Sage Bṛhaspati (the preceptor of gods) in intelligence, and in ruling over the people you are the equal to Brahmā, the lord of creation. (5)

verses.text:
क्षमा ते पृथिवीतुल्या तेजसा भास्करोपमः।
वेगस्ते वायुना तुल्यो गाम्भीर्यमुदधेरिव॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Your forbearance is unshaken like the earth; in glory you are a compeer of the sun. Your onrush vies with the wind, while your profundity is like that of the deep ocean. (6)

verses.text:
अप्रकम्प्यो यथा स्थाणुश्चन्द्रे सौम्यत्वमीदृशम्।
नेदृशाः पार्थिवाः पूर्वं भवितारो नराधिप॥ ७॥
verses.m: “You are unshakable in conflict like Lord Śiva such delightfulness as exists in you is found in the moon. Kings such as you, never existed in the past nor will they be hereafter, O suzerain lord of human beings! (7)

verses.text:
यथा त्वमसि दुर्धर्षो धर्मनित्यः प्रजाहितः।
न त्वां जहाति कीर्तिश्च लक्ष्मीश्च पुरुषर्षभ॥ ८॥
verses.m: “You are difficult to overpower in the true sense of the term, constant as you are in virtue and friendly to the people. Nay, glory does not forsake you, much less fortune, O jewel among men! (8)

verses.text:
श्रीश्च धर्मश्च काकुत्स्थ त्वयि नित्यं प्रतिष्ठितौ।
एताश्चान्याश्च मधुरा वन्दिभिः परिकीर्तिताः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Fortune and piety are constantly established in you, O Rāma (a scion of Kakutstha)!” These and other sweet encomia too were chanted by the bards. (9)

verses.text:
सूताश्च संस्तवैर्दिव्यैर्बोधयन्ति स्म राघवम्।
स्तुतिभिः स्तूयमानाभिः प्रत्यबुध्यत राघवः॥ १०॥
verses.m: Panegyrists too woke up Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) by means of wonderful panegyrics. Śrī Rāma awoke while praises were being sung. (10)

verses.text:
स तद्विहाय शयनं पाण्डुराच्छादनास्तृतम्।
उत्तस्थौ नागशयनाद्धरिर्नारायणो यथा॥ ११॥
verses.m: Quitting his well-known couch overspread with a bed covered by a white sheet, he got up as would Lord Nārāyaṇa, the Destroyer of sins, from His couch consisting of a serpent (Śeṣa). (11)

verses.text:
तमुत्थितं महात्मानं प्रह्वाः प्राञ्जलयो नराः।
सलिलं भाजनैः शुभ्रैरुपतस्थुः सहस्रशः॥ १२॥
verses.m: Attendants in thousands bowing with joined palms brought water in shining ewers for the use of the high-souled monarch who had just risen. (12)

verses.text:
कृतोदकः शुचिर्भूत्वा काले हुतहुताशनः।
देवागारं जगामाशु पुण्यमिक्ष्वाकुसेवितम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: Having bathed and getting thus purified and having propitiated the sacred fire through oblations in time, he repaired with quick steps to the holy temple of the Ikṣwākus. (13)

verses.text:
तत्र देवान् पितॄन् विप्रानर्चयित्वा यथाविधि।
बाह्यकक्षान्तरं रामो निर्जगाम जनैर्वृतः॥ १४॥
verses.m: Having duly worshipped there the gods, the manes and the Brāhmaṇas, Śrī Rāma, surrounded by men, sought the interior of the outer chamber. (14)

verses.text:
उपतस्थुर्महात्मानो मन्त्रिणः सपुरोहिताः।
वसिष्ठप्रमुखाः सर्वे दीप्यमाना इवाग्नयः॥ १५॥
verses.m: Like blazing fires, all the high-souled counsellors including priests, Vasiṣṭha being the foremost among them, presented themselves. (15)

verses.text:
क्षत्रियाश्च महात्मानो नानाजनपदेश्वराः।
रामस्योपाविशन् पार्श्वे शक्रस्येव यथामराः॥ १६॥
verses.m: Magnanimous Kṣatriyas, rulers of various parts of the country, sat at the side of Śrī Rāma even as gods would by Indra. (16)

verses.text:
भरतो लक्ष्मणश्चात्र शत्रुघ्नश्च महायशाः।
उपासांचक्रिरे हृष्टा वेदास्त्रय इवाध्वरम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: Like the three Vedas (Ṛgveda, Yajurveda and Sāmaveda) waiting upon a sacrificial performance, Bharata, Lakṣmaṇa as also Śatrughna of great renown waited, full of joy, on Śrī Rāma. (17)

verses.text:
याताः प्राञ्जलयो भूत्वा किंकरा मुदिताननाः।
मुदिता नाम पार्श्वस्था बहवः समुपाविशन्॥ १८॥
verses.m: With joined palms and a cheerful countenance many a servant known by the class name of Muditas walked and sat comfortably at his side. (18)

verses.text:
वानराश्च महावीर्या विंशतिः कामरूपिणः।
सुग्रीवप्रमुखा राममुपासन्ते महौजसः॥ १९॥
verses.m: Nay, endowed with great prowess and extraordinary strength the twenty monkeys*, Sugrīva being the foremost among them, who were able to change their form at will, sat at the side of Śrī Rāma. (19)

verses.text:
विभीषणश्च रक्षोभिश्चतुर्भिः परिवारितः।
उपासते महात्मानं धनेशमिव गुह्यकः॥ २०॥
verses.m: Like a Yakṣa attending on Kubera (the god of riches), Vibhīṣaṇa, surrounded by four ogres (his ministers), waited on the high-souled Śrī Rāma. (20)

verses.text:
तथा निगमवृद्धाश्च कुलीना ये च मानवाः।
शिरसा वन्द्य राजानमुपासन्ते विचक्षणाः॥ २१॥
verses.m: Bowing with their heads bent low, sagacious human beings too, who were superior in the knowledge of the Vedas and of noble descent also, likewise sat at his side. (21)

verses.text:
तथा परिवृतो राजा श्रीमद्भिर्ऋषिभिर्वरैः।
राजभिश्च महावीर्यैर्वानरैश्च सराक्षसैः॥ २२॥
verses.m: The king was similarly surrounded by glorious and eminent Ṛṣis (seers of Vedic Mantras) as well as by kings endowed with extraordinary prowess and the aforesaid monkeys alongwith the ogres. (22)

verses.text:
यथा देवेश्वरो नित्यमृषिभिः समुपास्यते।
अधिकस्तेन रूपेण सहस्राक्षाद् विरोचते॥ २३॥
verses.m: Just as Indra, the ruler of gods, is duly waited upon by Ṛṣis everyday, Śrī Rāma shone brightly even more than Indra (the thousand-eyed god) in that seemingly human form. (23)

verses.text:
तेषां समुपविष्टानां तास्ताः सुमधुराः कथाः।
कथ्यन्ते धर्मसंयुक्ताः पुराणज्ञैर्महात्मभिः॥ २४॥
verses.m: In their presence when they were all comfortably seated, different stories, exceedingly sweet and full of piety, were recited by high-souled persons well-versed in the Purāṇas.* (24)

verses.text:
एवमास्ते महाबाहुरहन्यहनि राघवः।
प्रशासत् सर्वकार्याणि पौरजानपदेषु च॥ १॥
verses.m: In this way the mighty-armed Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) continued from day to day to administer all the affairs of the citizens as well as of the people of the outlying districts. (1)

verses.text:
ततः कतिपयाहःसु वैदेहं मिथिलाधिपम्।
राघवः प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह॥ २॥
verses.m: Then after some days Śrī Rāma with joined palms addressed the following submission to King Janaka, ruler of the Videha territory, and the suzerain lord of Mithilā, so the tradition goes: (2)

verses.text:
भवान् हि गतिरव्यग्रा भवता पालिता वयम्।
भवतस्तेजसोग्रेण रावणो निहतो मया॥ ३॥
verses.m: “You indeed are our permanent support; we stand fostered by you. By virtue of the formidable prowess alone, born of your austerities, was Rāvaṇa killed by me. (3)

verses.text:
इक्ष्वाकूणां च सर्वेषां मैथिलानां च सर्वशः।
अतुलाः प्रीतयो राजन् सम्बन्धकपुरोगमाः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Bonds of affection which have followed from a matrimonial alliance and stand unequalled have existed between all the Ikṣwākus, on the one hand, and all the rulers of Mithilā, on the other, O king! (4)

verses.text:
तद् भवान् स्वपुरं यातु रत्नान्यादाय पार्थिव।
भरतश्च सहायार्थं पृष्ठतश्चानुयास्यति॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Accepting the valuable presents, which are being respectfully offered by me, therefore, proceed you to your own city, O king Bharata and alongwith him Śatrughna too will follow at your heels for escorting you.” (5)

verses.text:
स तथेति ततः कृत्वा राघवं वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
प्रीतोऽस्मि भवता राजन् दर्शनेन नयेन च॥ ६॥
verses.m: Saying ‘Amen’, King Janaka thereupon made the following reply to Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu: “I feel gratified, O king, with your sight and polity. (6)

verses.text:
यान्येतानि तु रत्नानि मदर्थं संचितानि वै।
दुहित्रे तान्यहं राजन् सर्वाण्येव ददामि वै॥ ७॥
verses.m: “I for my part hereby bestow all these valuable presents which have been actually got together for my sake, O king, on my daughter, Empress Sītā.” (7)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा तु काकुत्स्थं जनको हृष्टमानसः।
प्रययौ मिथिलां श्रीमांस्तमनुज्ञाय राघवम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: Having spoken as above to Śrī Rāma (a scion of Kakutstha) and taking leave of the said scion of Raghu, the glorious King Janaka proceeded to Mithilā, delighted in mind. (8)

verses.text:
ततः प्रयाते जनके केकयं मातुलं प्रभुम्।
राघवः प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा विनयाद् वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ ९॥
verses.m: Janaka having departed, Śrī Rāma with joined palms submitted in all humility as follows to his maternal uncle, the Kekaya king, Yudhājit: (9)

verses.text:
इदं राज्यमहं चैव भरतश्च सलक्ष्मणः।
आयत्तस्त्वं हि नो राजन् गतिश्च पुरुषर्षभ॥ १०॥
verses.m: “This kingdom of Ayodhyā, myself, as also Bharata and Śatrughna, including Lakṣmaṇa, are at your disposal; nay,you are our very mainstay, O king, a jewel among men! (10)

verses.text:
राजा हि वृद्धः संतापं त्वदर्थमुपयास्यति।
तस्माद् गमनमद्यैव रोचते तव पार्थिव॥ ११॥
verses.m: “The king, being aged, will feel afflicted on your account; hence, O king, your leaving this very day for your city finds favour with me. (11)

verses.text:
लक्ष्मणेनानुयात्रेण पृष्ठतोऽनुगमिष्यते।
धनमादाय बहुलं रत्नानि विविधानि च॥ १२॥
verses.m: “You will be followed by Lakṣmaṇa marching at your heels, taking with him abundant wealth and precious stones of various kinds for you.” (12)

verses.text:
युधाजित् तु तथेत्याह गमनं प्रति राघव।
रत्नानि च धनं चैव त्वय्येवाक्षय्यमस्त्विति॥ १३॥
verses.m: Yudhājit for his part said, “Be it so!” with reference to his departure, adding, “O scion of Raghu, let the precious stones as well as the gold remain eternally with you.” (13)

verses.text:
प्रदक्षिणं च राजानं कृत्वा केकयवर्धनः।
रामेण च कृतः पूर्वमभिवाद्य प्रदक्षिणम्॥ १४॥
लक्ष्मणेन सहायेन प्रयातः केकयेश्वरः।
हतेऽसुरे यथा वृत्रे विष्णुना सह वासवः॥ १५॥
verses.m: Nay, having walked clockwise as a mark of respect around the king, Śrī Rāma, the king of the Kekayas, who was also the promoter of the Kekayas, nay, who had already been circumambulated clockwise by Śrī Rāma after greeting him, departed with Lakṣmaṇa as his escort, even as Indra did (for Amarāvatī) on the demon Vṛtra having been killed, with Lord Viṣṇu descended as his younger brother. (14-15)

verses.text:
तं विसृज्य ततो रामो वयस्यमकुतोभयम्।
प्रतर्दनं काशिपतिं परिष्वज्येदमब्रवीत्॥ १६॥
verses.m: Having sent him away and embraced his friend Pratardana, the ruler of Kāśī, who was a friend and who entertained no fear from any quarter, Śrī Rāma then spoke as follows to him: (16)

verses.text:
दर्शिता भवता प्रीतिर्दर्शितं सौहृदं परम्।
उद्योगश्च त्वया राजन् भरतेन कृतः सह॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Endeavour was made by you in co-operation with Bharata in my coronation*, O king, and affection and great amity was thereby shown by you. (17)

verses.text:
तद् भवानद्य काशेय पुरीं वाराणसीं व्रज।
रमणीयां त्वया गुप्तां सुप्राकारां सुतोरणाम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Therefore, O king of Kāśī, return you today to the enchanting city of Vārāṇasī, which stands enclosed with a strong wall provided with magnificent gateways and protected by you.” (18)

verses.text:
एतावदुक्त्वा चोत्थाय काकुत्स्थः परमासनात्।
पर्यष्वजत धर्मात्मा निरन्तरमुरोगतम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: Having spoken as above, and rising from his magnificent throne, Śrī Rāma (a scion of Kakutstha), whose mind was set on righteousness, tightly clasped Pratardana, who had clung to his bosom. (19)

verses.text:
विसर्जयामास तदा कौसल्याप्रीतिवर्धनः।
राघवेण कृतानुज्ञः काशेयो ह्यकुतोभयः॥ २०॥
वाराणसीं ययौ तूर्णं राघवेण विसर्जितः।
विसृज्य तं काशिपतिं त्रिशतं पृथिवीपतीन्॥ २१॥
प्रहसन् राघवो वाक्यमुवाच मधुराक्षरम्।
भवतां प्रीतिरव्यग्रा तेजसा परिरक्षिता॥ २२॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma (who enhanced the joy of Kausalyā) then bid farewell to the king of Kāśī. Permitted by Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), the ruler of Kāśī, who actually entertained fear from none, proceeded with all speed to Vārāṇasī when sent off by Śrī Rāma. Having sent away the said ruler of Kāśī, Śrī Rāma laughingly spoke in sweet accents as follows to the three hundred princes assembled there: “Your unflinching devotion to Me stands vindicated by your glory. (20—22)

verses.text:
धर्मश्च नियतो नित्यं सत्यं च भवतां सदा।
युष्माकं चानुभावेन तेजसा च महात्मनाम्॥ २३॥
हतो दुरात्मा दुर्बुद्धी रावणो राक्षसाधमः।
हेतुमात्रमहं तत्र भवतां तेजसा हतः॥ २४॥
रावणः सगणो युद्धे सपुत्रामात्यबान्धवः।
भवन्तश्च समानीता भरतेन महात्मना॥ २५॥
श्रुत्वा जनकराजस्य काननात् तनयां हृताम्।
उद्युक्तानां च सर्वेषां पार्थिवानां महात्मनाम्॥ २६॥
कालोऽप्यतीतः सुमहान् गमनं रोचयाम्यतः।
प्रत्यूचुस्तं च राजानो हर्षेण महता वृताः॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Virtue is constant and truthfulness too ever exists invariably in you. Nay, through the majesty and glory alone of you, exalted souls, was the evil-minded and perverse Rāvaṇa, the vilest among the ogres, killed. I was a mere instrument in encompassing his death. Truly speaking, Rāvaṇa with his followers, as also his sons, ministers and kinsfolk—was made short work of through your glory alone. You too were called together by the high-souled Bharata on hearing of Sītā (the daughter of king Janaka) having been borne away from the forest. Nay, a pretty long time has gone by while all of you high-souled kings have been zealously active all these days in my interest. Hence I deem it proper that you should depart.” Nay, filled with great joy, the kings answered him thus: (23—27)

verses.text:
दिष्ट्या त्वं विजयी राम स्वराज्येऽपि प्रतिष्ठितः।
दिष्ट्या प्रत्याहृता सीता दिष्ट्या शत्रुः पराजितः॥ २८॥
verses.m: “By our good luck, O Rāma, you have come out victorious and also stand secure in your own sovereignty. By our good fortune Sītā has been recovered and, thank God, the enemy has been vanquished. (28)

verses.text:
एष नः परमः काम एषा नः प्रीतिरुत्तमा।
यत् त्वां विजयिनं राम पश्यामो हतशात्रवम्॥ २९॥
verses.m: “This was our highest ambition, and this constitutes our greatest satisfaction, that we see you having killed your enemy and come out victorious, O Rāma. (29)

verses.text:
एतत् त्वय्युपपन्नं च यदस्मांस्त्वं प्रशंससे।
प्रशंसार्ह न जानीमः प्रशंसां वक्तुमीदृशीम्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Nay, it is but proper for you that you compliment us, O king worthy of tribute! We, however, do not know how to pay such a compliment. (30)

verses.text:
आपृच्छामो गमिष्यामो हृदिस्थो नः सदा भवान्।
वर्तामहे महाबाहो प्रीत्यात्र महता वृताः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “We now take leave of you and shall depart. Even as you ever remain enshrined in our heart, so filled with great devotion to you, we too may abide in the heart of yours, O mighty-armed one! (31)

verses.text:
भवेच्च ते महाराज प्रीतिरस्मासु नित्यदा।
बाढमित्येव राजानो हर्षेण परमान्विताः॥ ३२॥
ऊचुः प्राञ्जलयः सर्वे राघवं गमनोत्सुकाः।
पूजितास्ते च रामेण जग्मुर्देशान् स्वकान् स्वकान्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “And let your affection ever be for us, O monarch!” Answered by Śrī Rāma in the words “All right!”, all the kings, transported with joy and ready to depart, said to Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) with joined palms, “We are leaving”. Nay, honoured by Śrī Rāma, they all returned to their respective territories. (32-33)

verses.text:
ते प्रयाता महात्मानः पार्थिवास्ते प्रहृष्टवत्।
गजवाजिसहस्रौघैः कम्पयन्तो वसुंधराम्॥ १॥
verses.m: Those well-known and high-souled princes joyously departed, shaking the earth with their contingents consisting of thousands of elephants and horses. (1)

verses.text:
अक्षौहिण्यो हि तत्रासन् राघवार्थे समुद्यताः।
भरतस्याज्ञयानेकाः प्रहृष्टबलवाहनाः॥ २॥
verses.m: More than one Akṣauhiṇī (or units of army, consisting of 21,870 elephants, the same number of chariots, 65,610 horses and 109,350 infantry) stood garrisoned there under the orders of Bharata, fully equipped for the sake of Śrī Rāma (in his conflict with Rāvaṇa, if need be) and full of highly delighted troops and mounts. (2)

verses.text:
ऊचुस्ते च महीपाला बलदर्पसमन्विताः।
न राम रावणं युद्धे पश्यामः पुरतः स्थितम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Nay, fully possessed with pride of might, the aforesaid kings said to one another, “We do not see Śrī Rāma and Rāvaṇa standing face to face on the field of battle. (3)

verses.text:
भरतेन वयं पश्चात् समानीता निरर्थकम्।
हता हि राक्षसाः क्षिप्रं पार्थिवैः स्युर्न संशयः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “We were uselessly brought together by Bharata when the war was over. The ogres would have surely been killed in no time by the kings had they been summoned in time; there is no doubt about it. (4)

verses.text:
रामस्य बाहुवीर्येण रक्षिता लक्ष्मणस्य च।
सुखं पारे समुद्रस्य युध्येम विगतज्वराः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Protected by the might of arms of Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa we could have fought at ease on the other side of the sea (dividing the island of Laṅkā from the mainland), free from anxiety.” (5)

verses.text:
एताश्चान्याश्च राजानः कथास्तत्र सहस्रशः।
कथयन्तः स्वराज्यानि जग्मुर्हर्षसमन्विताः॥ ६॥
verses.m: Saying these and other things in thousands on the way, the kings returned to their respective dominions, full of joy. (6)

verses.text:
स्वानि राज्यानि मुख्यानि ऋद्धानि मुदितानि च।
समृद्धधनधान्यानि पूर्णानि वसुमन्ति च॥ ७॥
यथापुराणि ते गत्वा रत्नानि विविधान्यथ।
रामस्य प्रियकामार्थमुपहारं नृपा ददुः॥ ८॥
अश्वान् यानानि रत्नानि हस्तिनश्च मदोत्कटान्।
चन्दनानि च मुख्यानि दिव्यान्याभरणानि च॥ ९॥
मणिमुक्ताप्रवालांस्तु दास्यो रूपसमन्विताः।
अजाविकं च विविधं रथांस्तु विविधान् बहून्॥ १०॥
verses.m: Duly reaching their own well-known kingdoms, which were prosperous and happy, with plentiful gold and grains, self-contained and full of treasures, and then to their respective cities, the aforesaid rulers of men forthwith bestowed on the escorts accompanying them as representatives of Śrī Rāma by way of so many presents for the gratification of Śrī Rāma, valuable things of various kinds, horses, vehicles, precious stones and elephants excited by passion, also excellent pieces of sandalwood and brilliant ornaments, gems, pearls and coral, nay, servant-maids richly endowed with comeliness, she-goats and sheep of different species and numerous chariots of every description. (7—10)

verses.text:
भरतो लक्ष्मणश्चैव शत्रुघ्नश्च महाबलः।
आदाय तानि रत्नानि स्वां पुरीं पुनरागताः॥ ११॥
verses.m: Taking the aforesaid valuable presents, Bharata as well as Lakṣmaṇa and Śatrughna, who was endowed with extraordinary might, returned to their own city, Ayodhyā. (11)

verses.text:
आगम्य च पुरीं रम्यामयोध्यां पुरुषर्षभाः।
तानि रत्नानि चित्राणि रामाय समुपानयन्॥ १२॥
verses.m: Nay, reaching the delightful city of Ayodhyā, the jewels among men handed those wonderful objects to Śrī Rāma. (12)

verses.text:
प्रतिगृह्य च तत् सर्वं रामः प्रीतिसमन्वितः।
सुग्रीवाय ददौ राज्ञे महात्मा कृतकर्मणे॥ १३॥
विभीषणाय च ददौ तथान्येभ्योऽपि राघवः।
राक्षसेभ्यः कपिभ्यश्च यैर्वृतो जयमाप्तवान्॥ १४॥
verses.m: Accepting all that, the high-souled Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, full of joy bestowed them on King Sugrīva, who had done his duty to Śrī Rāma, as well as on Vibhīṣaṇa and on other monkeys and ogres, surrounded by whom He had scored a victory over Rāvaṇa. (13-14)

verses.text:
ते सर्वे रामदत्तानि रत्नानि कपिराक्षसाः।
शिरोभिर्धारयामासुर्भुजेषु च महाबलाः॥ १५॥
verses.m: All the aforesaid monkeys and ogres, who were endowed with extraordinary might, wore the precious stones bestowed on them by Śrī Rāma, on their heads as well as around their arms. (15)

verses.text:
हनूमन्तं च नृपतिरिक्ष्वाकूणां महारथः।
अङ्गदं च महाबाहुमङ्कमारोप्य वीर्यवान्॥ १६॥
रामः कमलपत्राक्षः सुग्रीवमिदमब्रवीत्।
अङ्गदस्ते सुपुत्रोऽयं मन्त्री चाप्यनिलात्मजः॥ १७॥
सुग्रीवमन्त्रिते युक्तौ मम चापि हिते रतौ।
अर्हतो विविधां पूजां त्वत्कृते वै हरीश्वर॥ १८॥
verses.m: Placing Hanūmān and Aṅgada too in His lap, Śrī Rāma, the powerful king of the Ikṣwākus, a great chariot-warrior, whose eyes resembled the petals of a lotus, spoke as follows to Sugrīva: “This Aṅgada, your worthy son (nephew) and your minister, the son of the wind-god, too, O Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys, who have both remained engaged in giving counsel to you and have been devoted to My interests, too, actually merit every kind of honour.” (16—18)

verses.text:
इत्युक्त्वा व्यवमुच्याङ्गाद् भूषणानि महायशाः।
स बबन्ध महार्हाणि तदाङ्गदहनूमतोः॥ १९॥
verses.m: Saying so, and taking off ornaments of great value from His body, the illustrious One fastened them on the person of Aṅgada and Hanumān. (19)

verses.text:
आभाष्य च महावीर्यान् राघवो यूथपर्षभान्।
नीलं नलं केसरिणं कुमुदं गन्धमादनम्॥ २०॥
सुषेणं पनसं वीरं मैन्दं द्विविदमेव च।
जाम्बवन्तं गवाक्षं च विनतं धूम्रमेव च॥ २१॥
बलीमुखं प्रजङ्घं च संनादं च महाबलम्।
दरीमुखं दधिमुखमिन्द्रजानुं च यूथपम्॥ २२॥
मधुरं श्लक्ष्णया वाचा नेत्राभ्यामापिबन्निव।
सुहृदो मे भवन्तश्च शरीरं भ्रातरस्तथा॥ २३॥
युष्माभिरुद्धृतश्चाहं व्यसनात् काननौकसः।
धन्यो राजा च सुग्रीवो भवद्भिः सुहृदां वरैः॥ २४॥
एवमुक्त्वा ददौ तेभ्यो भूषणानि यथार्हतः।
वज्राणि च महार्हाणि सस्वजे च नरर्षभः॥ २५॥
verses.m: Nay, sweetly accosting the foremost of His troop-commanders, who were all endowed with extraordinary prowess, viz., Nīla, Nala, Kesarī, Kumuda, Gandhamādana, Suṣeṇa, Panasa, the valiant Mainda as well as Dwivida, Jāmbavān and Gavākṣa, Vinata and Dhūmra too, Balīmukha and Prajaṅgha, as well as the exceptionally mighty Sannāda, Darīmukha, Dadhimukha and the troop-commander Indrajānu in a soft tone, as though He would drink them up with His eyes, and saying, “you are My friends, nay, My other self, as also My brothers. By you alone was I delivered from misfortune, O dwellers in the woods! Nay, King Sugrīva is blessed because of you, the foremost among his friends,” Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), the foremost of human beings, bestowed on them, according to their deserts, ornaments and diamonds of great value and embraced them. (20—25)

verses.text:
ते पिबन्तः सुगन्धीनि मधूनि मधुपिङ्गलाः।
मांसानि च सुमृष्टानि मूलानि च फलानि च॥ २६॥
verses.m: The monkeys (who were reddish brown as honey) stayed there, quaffing fragrant honeys, and subsisting on royal dishes, roots and fruits. (26)

verses.text:
एवं तेषां निवसतां मासः साग्रो ययौ तदा।
मुहूर्तमिव ते सर्वे रामभक्त्या च मेनिरे॥ २७॥
verses.m: More than a month elapsed on that occasion while they stayed at Ayodhyā as aforesaid. Nay, because of their devotion to Śrī Rāma, they all felt it to be less than an hour. (27)

verses.text:
रामोऽपि रेमे तैः सार्धं वानरैः कामरूपिभिः।
राक्षसैश्च महावीर्यैर्ऋक्षैश्चैव महाबलैः॥ २८॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma too spent his time happily in the company of those aforesaid monkeys, who could change their form at will, as also with the ogres, who were endowed with extraordinary prowess, as well as with bears who were exceptionally mighty. (28)

verses.text:
एवं तेषां ययौ मासो द्वितीयः शिशिरः सुखम्।
वानराणां प्रहृष्टानां राक्षसानां च सर्वशः॥ २९॥
इक्ष्वाकुनगरे रम्ये परां प्रीतिमुपासताम्।
रामस्य प्रीतिकरणैः कालस्तेषां सुखं ययौ॥ ३०॥
verses.m: In this way the second month, Phālguna, of the extreme cold season also passed happily with the monkeys and the ogres, who felt highly rejoiced in every way and enjoyed supreme gratification through the hospitality of Śrī Rāma. Their time passed merrily in the delightful city of the Ikṣwākus. (29-30)

verses.text:
तथा स्म तेषां वसतामृक्षवानररक्षसाम्।
राघवस्तु महातेजाः सुग्रीवमिदमब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Of the aforesaid bears, monkeys and ogres sojourning with Him, Śrī Rāma for his part, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, spoke as follows to Sugrīva: (1)

verses.text:
गम्यतां सौम्य किष्किन्धां दुराधर्षां सुरासुरैः।
पालयस्व सहामात्यै राज्यं निहतकण्टकम्॥ २॥
verses.m: “Return, O gentle one, to Kiṣkindhā, which cannot easily be assailed by the gods and the demons alike; and rule with your ministers the kingdom, all of whose enemies have been exterminated. (2)

verses.text:
अङ्गदं च महाबाहो प्रीत्या परमया युतः।
पश्य त्वं हनुमन्तं च नलं च सुमहाबलम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Nay, regard you with supreme affection, O mighty-armed one, Aṅgada and Hanumān as also the exceptionally mighty Nala. (3)

verses.text:
सुषेणं श्वशुरं वीरं तारं च बलिनां वरम्।
कुमुदं चैव दुर्धर्षं नीलं चैव महाबलम्॥ ४॥
वीरं शतबलिं चैव मैन्दं द्विविदमेव च।
गजं गवाक्षं गवयं शरभं च महाबलम्॥ ५॥
ऋक्षराजं च दुर्धर्षं जाम्बवन्तं महाबलम्।
पश्य प्रीतिसमायुक्तो गन्धमादनमेव च॥ ६॥
ऋषभं च सुविक्रान्तं प्लवङ्गं च सुपाटलम्।
केसरिं शरभं शुम्भं शङ्खचूडं महाबलम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Replete with love, cast your look on your father-in-law, the heroic Suṣeṇa and Tāra, the foremost of the mighty, as well as on Kumuda, who is so difficult to assail as also on Nīla, who is endowed with extraordinary might, on the valiant Śatabali, as also on Mainda as well as on Dwivida, Gaja, Gavākṣa, Gavaya and the exceptionally mighty Śarabha, on the very mighty Jāmbavān, the king of bears, who is so difficult to assail, as also on Gandhamādana, and on the highly valiant Ṛṣabha and on the monkey Supāṭala, on Kesarī, Śarabha, Śumbha and on the exceptionally mighty Śaṅkhacūḍa. (4—7)

verses.text:
ये ये च सुमहात्मानो मदर्थे त्यक्तजीविताः।
पश्य त्वं प्रीतिसंयुक्तो मा चैषां विप्रियं कृथाः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Nay, full of affection, cast your eyes on all the high-souled monkeys who risked their lives for My sake. Never do anything displeasing to them.” (8)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा च सुग्रीवमाश्लिष्य च पुनः पुनः।
विभीषणमुवाचाथ रामो मधुरया गिरा॥ ९॥
verses.m: Having spoken as aforesaid to Sugrīva and embraced him again and again, Śrī Rāma then spoke as follows to Vibhīṣaṇa in a sweet tone: (9)

verses.text:
लङ्कां प्रशाधि धर्मेण धर्मज्ञस्त्वं मतो मम।
पुरस्य राक्षसानां च भ्रातुर्वैश्रवणस्य च॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Rule Laṅkā with righteousness; you are held to be a knower of what is right by Me, by the city of Laṅkā, by the ogres as a whole and by your eldest brother, Kubera, son of Viśravā. (10)

verses.text:
मा च बुद्धिमधर्मे त्वं कुर्या राजन् कथंचन।
बुद्धिमन्तो हि राजानो ध्रुवमश्नन्ति मेदिनीम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Nay, never set your mind in any case on unrighteousness, O king! Prudent kings do rule the earth firmly. (11)

verses.text:
अहं च नित्यशो राजन् सुग्रीवसहितस्त्वया।
स्मर्तव्यः परया प्रीत्या गच्छ त्वं विगतज्वरः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Nay, alongwith Sugrīva I should be constantly cherished in memory by you with supreme affection, O king! Depart you free from anxiety.” (12)

verses.text:
रामस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा ऋक्षवानरराक्षसाः।
साधुसाध्विति काकुत्स्थं प्रशशंसुः पुनः पुनः॥ १३॥
verses.m: Hearing the speech of Śrī Rāma, the bears, monkeys and ogres repeatedly applauded Śrī Rāma (a scion of Kakutstha), saying: “Well said! Excellent!! (13)

verses.text:
तव बुद्धिर्महाबाहो वीर्यमद्भुतमेव च।
माधुर्यं परमं राम स्वयम्भोरिव नित्यदा॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Wonderful is Your wisdom, O mighty-armed one, and your prowess too. Your supreme geniality too, O Rāma, ever vies with that of Brahmā (the self-born).” (14)

verses.text:
तेषामेवं ब्रुवाणानां वानराणां च रक्षसाम्।
हनूमान् प्रणतो भूत्वा राघवं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Remaining inclined while the monkeys and ogres were speaking as aforesaid, Hanūmān submitted as follows to Śrī Rāma: (15)

verses.text:
स्नेहो मे परमो राजंस्त्वयि तिष्ठतु नित्यदा।
भक्तिश्च नियता वीर भावो नान्यत्र गच्छतु॥ १६॥
verses.m: “May my supreme affection for You stand forever, O Lord! May my devotion be constant to You, O valiant prince! Let not my love be diverted to anyone else. (16)

verses.text:
यावद् रामकथा वीर चरिष्यति महीतले।
तावच्छरीरे वत्स्यन्तु प्राणा मम न संशयः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “May life continue in my body without doubt so long as Your story remains current on the surface of the earth, O heroic Śrī Rāma! (17)

verses.text:
यच्चैतच्चरितं दिव्यं कथा ते रघुनन्दन।
तन्ममाप्सरसो राम श्रावयेयुर्नरर्षभ॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Let the celestial nymphs, O Rāma, recount to me in musical notes, O jewel among the human beings, that which passes as Your divine life exploits, Your story, O delight of the Raghus! (18)

verses.text:
तच्छ्रुत्वाहं ततो वीर तव चर्यामृतं प्रभो।
उत्कण्ठां तां हरिष्यामि मेघलेखामिवानिलः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Imbibing with my ears the nectar in the form of Your lifestory, My heroic lord, I shall thereby be able to allay my longing for Your sight even as the wind disperses a line of clouds.” (19)

verses.text:
एवं ब्रुवाणं रामस्तु हनूमन्तं वरासनात्।
उत्थाय सस्वजे स्नेहाद् वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह॥ २०॥
verses.m: Rising from his excellent seat, Śrī Rāma hugged with affection Hanūmān while he was submitting as above, and made the following reply: so the tradition goes: (20)

verses.text:
एवमेतत् कपिश्रेष्ठ भविता नात्र संशयः।
चरिष्यति कथा यावदेषा लोके च मामिका॥ २१॥
तावत् ते भविता कीर्तिः शरीरेऽप्यसवस्तथा।
लोका हि यावत्स्थास्यन्ति तावत् स्थास्यन्ति मे कथाः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “So shall it be, O prince of monkeys; there is no doubt about it. Your fame will endure and life too will continue in your body so long as this story of Mine will remain current in the world. Nay, My stories will surely abide so long as the worlds will last. (21-22)

verses.text:
एकैकस्योपकारस्य प्राणान् दास्यामि ते कपे।
शेषस्येहोपकाराणां भवाम ऋणिनो वयम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: “I would give up My life for every single service rendered by you here and we shall remain in debt to you for the rest of your services, O monkey! (23)

verses.text:
मदङ्गे जीर्णतां यातु यत् त्वयोपकृतं कपे।
नरः प्रत्युपकाराणामापत्स्वायाति पात्रताम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Let My obligation to you stand in My heart forever, O monkey! (Let there be no occasion for Me to repay your services); for one deserves to be requited for services rendered only when one is in straits.” (24)

verses.text:
ततोऽस्य हारं चन्द्राभं मुच्य कण्ठात् स राघवः।
वैदूर्यतरलं कण्ठे बबन्ध च हनूमतः॥ २५॥
verses.m: Taking off from his neck a string of pearls, shining as the moon, with a cat’s-eye gem in the centre, the celebrated Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) then fastened it about the neck of the said Hanūmān. (25)

verses.text:
तेनोरसि निबद्धेन हारेण महता कपिः।
रराज हेमशैलेन्द्रश्चन्द्रेणाक्रान्तमस्तकः॥ २६॥
verses.m: With that big necklace fastened on his breast, the monkey shone as the lordly Mount Meru (the golden mountain) with its summit topped over by the moon. (26)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा तु राघवस्यैतदुत्थायोत्थाय वानराः।
प्रणम्य शिरसा पादौ निर्जग्मुस्ते महाबलाः॥ २७॥
verses.m: Rising one after another on hearing this speech of Śrī Rāma, and bowing down at his feet with their heads bent low, the aforesaid monkeys of extraordinary might for their part departed. (27)

verses.text:
सुग्रीवः स च रामेण निरन्तरमुरोगतः।
विभीषणश्च धर्मात्मा सर्वे ते बाष्पविक्लवाः॥ २८॥
verses.m: The celebrated Sugrīva as well as the pious-minded Vibhīṣaṇa were tightly clasped to his bosom by Śrī Rāma; all the monkeys were overcome with emotions and shed tears. (28)

verses.text:
सर्वे च ते बाष्पकलाः साश्रुनेत्रा विचेतसः।
सम्मूढा इव दुःखेन त्यजन्तो राघवं तदा॥ २९॥
verses.m: While leaving Śrī Rāma at that time, they all spoke indistinctly, their throats being choked with tears; nay, their eyes too were full of tears, they felt confused and stupefied as it were through agony. (29)

verses.text:
कृतप्रसादास्तेनैवं राघवेण महात्मना।
जग्मुः स्वं स्वं गृहं सर्वे देही देहमिव त्यजन्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Having been favoured with gifts as aforesaid by that high-souled scion of Raghu, they returned each to his home, (feeling agonized) even as an embodied soul would, while leaving the body (tenanted by it). (30)

verses.text:
ततस्तु ते राक्षसऋक्षवानराः
प्रणम्य रामं रघुवंशवर्धनम्।
वियोगजाश्रुप्रतिपूर्णलोचनाः
प्रतिप्रयातास्तु यथा निवासिनः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: Having respectfully bowed down to Śrī Rāma, the promoter of Raghu’s race, the said ogres, bears and monkeys for their part returned to their respective abodes with their eyes full of tears (born of their separation from Śrī Rāma). (31)

verses.text:
विसृज्य च महाबाहुर्ऋक्षवानरराक्षसान्।
भ्रातृभिः सहितो रामः प्रमुमोद सुखं सुखी॥ १॥
verses.m: After sending away the bears, the monkeys and the ogres, the mighty-armed Śrī Rāma, who was ever happy, intrinsically felt highly rejoiced alongwith his brothers. (1)

verses.text:
अथापराह्णसमये भ्रातृभिः सह राघवः।
शुश्राव मधुरां वाणीमन्तरिक्षान्महाप्रभुः॥ २॥
सौम्य राम निरीक्षस्व सौम्येन वदनेन माम्।
कुबेरभवनात् प्राप्तं विद्धि मां पुष्पकं प्रभो॥ ३॥
verses.m: After sometime in the afternoon the mighty Lord Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), heard, alongwith his brothers, a sweet voice coming from the sky as follows: “Dear Rāma, look on me with affection beaming from your face; know me, O Lord, to be the Puṣpaka, come from the mansion of Kubera. (2-3)

verses.text:
तव शासनमाज्ञाय गतोऽस्मि भवनं प्रति।
उपस्थातुं नरश्रेष्ठ स च मां प्रत्यभाषत॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Obeying Your command, O best of men, I went home to wait on him (Kubera), but he said to me: (4)

verses.text:
निर्जितस्त्वं नरेन्द्रेण राघवेण महात्मना।
निहत्य युधि दुर्धर्षं रावणं राक्षसेश्वरम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: “ ‘Having killed in battle the unassailable Rāvaṇa, the king of the Rākṣasas, Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), the high-souled king of men, has won possession over you. (5)

verses.text:
ममापि परमा प्रीतिर्हते तस्मिन् दुरात्मनि।
रावणे सगणे चैव सपुत्रे सहबान्धवे॥ ६॥
verses.m: “ ‘A great delight has fallen to my lot too on that wicked Rāvaṇa having been killed alongwith his hosts, with his sons and other relations. (6)

verses.text:
स त्वं रामेण लङ्कायां निर्जितः परमात्मना।
वह सौम्य तमेव त्वमहमाज्ञापयामि ते॥ ७॥
verses.m: “ ‘As such you have been won in Laṅkā by Śrī Rāma, who is the Highest Being. O gentle one! You carry Him indeed: I command you. (7)

verses.text:
परमो ह्येष मे कामो यत् त्वं राघवनन्दनम्।
वहेर्लोकस्य संयानं गच्छस्व विगतज्वरः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “ ‘It is my highest desire that you serve as a carriage of Śrī Rāma (the delight of Raghu’s race) who is the support of the entire world: go without qualms.’ (8)

verses.text:
सोऽहं शासनमाज्ञाय धनदस्य महात्मनः।
त्वत्सकाशमनुप्राप्तो निर्विशङ्कः प्रतीच्छ माम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “I, who was ordered thus, have come to your presence abiding by the command of the high-souled Kubera; accept me kindly without any hitch. (9)

verses.text:
अधृष्यः सर्वभूतानां सर्वेषां धनदाज्ञया।
चराम्यहं प्रभावेण तवाज्ञां परिपालयन्॥ १०॥
verses.m: “By virtue of my power I am unassailable by the entire range of created beings. By Kubera’s order I shall move through all the spheres carrying out your behest.” (10)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तदा रामः पुष्पकेण महाबलः।
उवाच पुष्पकं दृष्ट्वा विमानं पुनरागतम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: Thus addressed by Puṣpaka, Śrī Rāma of great strength then spoke as follows, casting a benign look on the aerial car known as Puṣpaka, which had come back: (11)

verses.text:
यद्येवं स्वागतं तेऽस्तु विमानवर पुष्पक।
आनुकूल्याद् धनेशस्य वृत्तदोषो न नो भवेत्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “If it is so, you are welcome, O Puṣpaka, the best of aerial cars! On account of this favour of Kubera, the charge of unfair dealing will not be laid at our doors.” (12)

verses.text:
लाजैश्चैव तथा पुष्पैर्धूपैश्चैव सुगन्धिभिः।
पूजयित्वा महाबाहू राघवः पुष्पकं तदा॥ १३॥
verses.m: Having worshipped Puṣpaka after that with fried grains of rice and flowers as well as incenses and also sandal-pastes, the mighty-armed Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), spoke as follows: (13)

verses.text:
गम्यतामिति चोवाच आगच्छ त्वं स्मरे यदा।
सिद्धानां च गतौ सौम्य मा विषादेन योजय॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Depart for the present. You should come whenever I recall you. Vanishing in thin air, the dwelling place of the Siddhas, be not oppressed by grief at my separation. (14)

verses.text:
प्रतिघातश्च ते मा भूद् यथेष्टं गच्छतो दिशः।
एवमस्त्विति रामेण पूजयित्वा विसर्जितम्॥ १५॥
अभिप्रेतां दिशं तस्मात् प्रायात् तत् पुष्पकं तदा।
एवमन्तर्हिते तस्मिन् पुष्पके सुकृतात्मनि॥ १६॥
भरतः प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यमुवाच रघुनन्दनम्।
विबुधात्मनि दृश्यन्ते त्वयि वीर प्रशासति॥ १७॥
अमानुषाणि सत्त्वानि व्याहृतानि मुहुर्मुहुः।
अनामयश्च मर्त्यानां साग्रो मासो गतो ह्ययम्॥ १८॥
जीर्णानामपि सत्त्वानां मृत्युर्नायाति राघव।
अरोगप्रसवा नार्यो वपुष्मन्तो हि मानवाः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “May no obstruction hinder you as you wander in all directions at your sweet will.” “So be it”, replied Puṣpaka. Then Puṣpaka, which had been asked to go, after having been worshipped by Śrī Rāma, proceeded from there in the direction of its choice. On Puṣpaka, an embodiment of virtues, having thus gone out of sight, Bharata, with joined palms, addressed Śrī Rāma, the delight of the Raghus, in the following words: “Beings which do not claim their descent in Adam’s line, speak again and again like men, under your reign, O valiant One, having a divine soul! Only more than a month has elapsed since you took the sceptre in your hand, O Rāghava! and mortals have become strangers to disease, death does not overtake even men worn out with age, women undergo no labour-pains during parturition and human beings are well-built indeed. (15—19)

verses.text:
हर्षश्चाभ्यधिको राजञ्जनस्य पुरवासिनः।
काले वर्षति पर्जन्यः पातयन्नमृतं पयः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “An abundance of joy has fallen to the lot of every citizen dwelling in the town, O king! Pouring down nectarean water clouds rain at the proper time. (20)

verses.text:
वाताश्चापि प्रवान्त्येते स्पर्शयुक्ताः सुखाः शिवाः।
ईदृशो नश्चिरं राजा भवेदिति नरेश्वरः॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Even the very winds which blow here are capable of giving a delightful touch, and are pleasing and healthful. People living both in the cities and in the country, arriving in the capital, declare, ‘May such a sovereign be our ruler for long’, O king!” (21)

verses.text:
कथयन्ति पुरे राजन् पौरजानपदास्तथा।
एता वाचः सुमधुरा भरतेन समीरिताः।
श्रुत्वा रामो मुदा युक्तो बभूव नृपसत्तमः॥ २२॥
verses.m: Hearing these exquisitely honeyed words beautifully uttered by Bharata, Śrī Rāma, the best of kings, became thrilled with joy. (22)

verses.text:
स विसृज्य ततो रामः पुष्पकं हेमभूषितम्।
प्रविवेश महाबाहुरशोकवनिकां तदा॥ १॥
चन्दनागुरुचूतैश्च तुङ्गकालेयकैरपि।
देवदारुवनैश्चापि समन्तादुपशोभिताम्॥ २॥
चम्पकाशोकपुंनागमधूकपनसासनैः।
शोभितां पारिजातैश्च विधूमज्वलनप्रभैः॥ ३॥
verses.m: Then after dismissing Puṣpaka, decked with gold, the mighty-armed Śrī Rāma entered the Aśoka-grove, which was rendered beautiful all around by the sandal, eaglewood (Aguru) and mango trees, so also by cocoanut, red-sandal and deodar groves too. It was graced by Campaka (Campā Campāka), Aśoka, Punnāgas, Madhūka, jack and Asana* trees, also by Pārijāta trees which looked like a blaze of fire without smoke. (1—3)

verses.text:
लोध्रनीपार्जुनैर्नागैः सप्तपर्णातिमुक्तकैः।
मन्दारकदलीगुल्मलताजालसमावृताम् ॥ ४॥
verses.m: It was abounded in Lodhra, Nīpa, Arjuna, Nāga, Saptaparṇa, Atimuktaka, Mandāra, plantain trees, bushes and a network of creepers. (4)

verses.text:
प्रियङ्गुभिः कदम्बैश्च तथा च बकुलैरपि।
जम्बूभिर्दाडिमैश्चैव कोविदारैश्च शोभिताम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: It was rendered by splendid Priyaṅgu, Kadamba and also by Bakula and pomegranate, Jambū (the rose-apple)and Kovidāra trees. (5)

verses.text:
सर्वदा कुसुमै रम्यैः फलवद्भिर्मनोरमैः।
दिव्यगन्धरसोपेतैस्तरुणाङ्कुरपल्लवैः ॥ ६॥
तथैव तरुभिर्दिव्यैः शिल्पिभिः परिकल्पितैः।
चारुपल्लवपुष्पाढ्यैर्मत्तभ्रमरसंकुलैः ॥ ७॥
कोकिलैर्भृङ्गराजैश्च नानावर्णैश्च पक्षिभिः।
शोभितां शतशश्चित्रां चूतवृक्षावतंसकैः॥ ८॥
verses.m: It was embellished by such lovely trees ever laden with fascinating flowers and fruits and tender sprouts and whorl of leaves full of celestial fragrance and juice, as were reared with care by divine gardeners, enriched by beautiful leaves and flowers and thronged by intoxicated bees, and rendered variegated by multi-coloured birds like Kokilas and Bhṛṅgarājas which served as ornaments to the hundreds of the mango trees. (6—8)

verses.text:
शातकुम्भनिभाः केचित् केचिदग्निशिखोपमाः।
नीलाञ्जननिभाश्चान्ये भान्ति तत्र स्म पादपाः॥ ९॥
verses.m: There in the Aśoka-grove some trees had golden brilliance, some glistened like the flames of fire and yet others shone with the splendour of dark collyrium. (9)

verses.text:
सुरभीणि च पुष्पाणि माल्यानि विविधानि च।
दीर्घिका विविधाकाराः पूर्णाः परमवारिणा॥ १०॥
माणिक्यकृतसोपानाः स्फाटिकान्तरकुट्टिमाः।
फुल्लपद्मोत्पलवनाश्चक्रवाकोपशोभिताः ॥ ११॥
दात्यूहशुकसंघुष्टा हंससारसनादिताः।
तरुभिः पुष्पशबलैस्तीरजैरुपशोभिताः॥ १२॥
verses.m: There were fragrant flowers, blossoms of various kinds and also ponds of different shapes full of excellent water, which had flights of steps made of rubies ending in crystal platforms under water; which had masses of blooming lotuses and water-lilies; which were graced by Cakravāka birds; which resounded with the cries of water-hens and parrots; which were resonant with the cackling of swans and cranes and which were adorned with trees growing on their banks and wearing a motley appearance due to their being laden with flowers. (10—12)

verses.text:
प्राकारैर्विविधाकारैः शोभिताश्च शिलातलैः।
तत्रैव च वनोद्देशे वैदूर्यमणिसंनिभैः॥ १३॥
शाद्वलैः परमोपेतां पुष्पितद्रुमकाननाम्।
तत्र संघर्षजातानां वृक्षाणां पुष्पशालिनाम्॥ १४॥
प्रस्तराः पुष्पशबला नभस्तारागणैरिव।
नन्दनं हि यथेन्द्रस्य ब्राह्मं चैत्ररथं यथा॥ १५॥
verses.m: They were also bedecked with fences of various shapes and stone-slabs. Just there in that part of the woodland the grassy glades resembling the hue of Vaidurya (cat’s-eye) splendidly beautified the Aśokavanikā which had a multitude of trees ladden with flowers. There the stone-slabs, which were placed under the trees and served as couches, looked variegated due to flowers fallen from the trees as the sky with the stars. The lay-out of Śrī Rāma’s grove was like that of the Nandana garden of Indra and the Caitraratha garden of Kubera raised by Brahmā. (13—15)

verses.text:
तथाभूतं हि रामस्य काननं संनिवेशनम्।
बह्वासनगृहोपेतां लतागृहसमावृताम्॥ १६॥
अशोकवनिकां स्फीतां प्रविश्य रघुनन्दनः।
आसने च शुभाकारे पुष्पप्रकरभूषिते॥ १७॥
कुथास्तरणसंस्तीर्णे रामः संनिषसाद ह।
सीतामादाय हस्तेन मधु मैरेयकं शुचि॥ १८॥
पाययामास काकुत्स्थः शचीमिव पुरंदरः।
मांसानि च सुमृष्टानि फलानि विविधानि च॥ १९॥
रामस्याभ्यवहारार्थं किंकरास्तूर्णमाहरन्।
उपानृत्यंश्च राजानं नृत्यगीतविशारदाः॥ २०॥
verses.m: Having entered the large Aśokavanikā, which had dwellings provided with a number of seats and was surrounded by bowers, Śrī Rāma, the delight of Raghus, seated Himself on a fine-shaped couch decorated with clusters of flowers and over which a carpet was spread out. Taking in his hand the pure nectar of flowers as intoxicating as the ‘Maireyaka’ wine, Śrī Rāma (a descendant of Kakutstha) made Śrī Sītā drink it, just as Indra does Śacī. Attendants speedily brought well-cooked edibles (fit for the royalty) and a variety of fruits for Śrī Rāma’s repast. A troupe of celestial nymphs and Nāga damsels adept in singing and dancing and surrounded by Kinnarīs danced before the king. (16—20)

verses.text:
अप्सरोरगसंघाश्च किंनरीपरिवारिताः।
दक्षिणा रूपवत्यश्च स्त्रियः पानवशं गताः॥ २१॥
उपानृत्यन्त काकुत्स्थं नृत्यगीतविशारदाः।
मनोऽभिरामा रामास्ता रामो रमयतां वरः॥ २२॥
रमयामास धर्मात्मा नित्यं परमभूषिताः।
स तया सीतया सार्धमासीनो विरराज ह॥ २३॥
अरुन्धत्या इवासीनो वसिष्ठ इव तेजसा।
एवं रामो मुदा युक्तः सीतां सुरसुतोपमाम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: Under the influence of intoxicating drinks courteous and beautiful women, who were expert in dancing and singing danced before Śrī Rāma (a scion of Kakutstha). These mind-fascinating belles were always adorned with ornaments. Pious-souled Śrī Rāma, the foremost among those who delighted others, made them rejoice. Seated in the company of the celebrated Sītā, He shone with splendour like Vasiṣṭha seated alongwith Arundhatī. (21—24)

verses.text:
रमयामास वैदेहीमहन्यहनि देववत्।
तथा तयोर्विहरतोः सीताराघवयोश्चिरम्॥ २५॥
अत्यक्रामच्छुभः कालः शैशिरो भोगदः सदा।
प्राप्तयोर्विविधान् भोगानतीतः शिशिरागमः॥ २६॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma, steeped in joy like gods, afforded delight thus day after day to the daughter of Videha (Janaka) Śrī Sītā, who resembled a divine damsel. In this way, while both Śrī Sītā and Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghus) revelled for long, the auspicious winter season which always provides enjoyment came to an end. When the Couple had relished a variety of enjoyments, the advent of another* winter became an event of the past. (25-26)

verses.text:
पूर्वाह्णे धर्मकार्याणि कृत्वा धर्मेण धर्मवित्।
शेषं दिवसभागार्धमन्तःपुरगतोऽभवत्॥ २७॥
सीतापि देवकार्याणि कृत्वा पौर्वाह्णिकानि वै।
श्वश्रूणामकरोत् पूजां सर्वासामविशेषतः॥ २८॥
verses.m: Having performed the religious duties as enjoined by Virtue in the first half of the day, Śrī Rāma (the knower of Virtue) remained in the gynaeceum for the remaining half of the day. Śrī Sītā too, having performed all duties relating to gods, enjoined to be done in the forepart of the day, respectfully waited upon all the mothers-in-law without any distinction. (27-28)

verses.text:
अभ्यगच्छत् ततो रामं विचित्राभरणाम्बरा।
त्रिविष्टपे सहस्राक्षमुपविष्टं यथा शची॥ २९॥
