verses.text:
स तां पद्मपलाशाक्षीं पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम्।
वरुणो वरयामास मैथुनायाप्सरोवराम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Varuṇa invited her, the eminent Apsarā, whose eyes were large like the leaf of a lotus and whose face was beautiful like the full moon, for union. (15)

verses.text:
प्रत्युवाच ततः सा तु वरुणं प्राञ्जलिः स्थिता।
मित्रेणाहं वृता साक्षात् पूर्वमेव सुरेश्वर॥ १६॥
verses.m: “On this she replied to Varuṇa, with folded hands: ‘Sureśwara! I have already been chosen by god Mitra himself.’ (16)

verses.text:
वरुणस्त्वब्रवीद् वाक्यं कन्दर्पशरपीडितः।
इदं तेजः समुत्स्रक्ष्ये कुम्भेऽस्मिन् देवनिर्मिते॥ १७॥
एवमुत्सृज्य सुश्रोणि त्वय्यहं वरवर्णिनि।
कृतकामो भविष्यामि यदि नेच्छसि सङ्गमम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: Tormented by the arrows of cupid, Varuṇa said the following words: In your presence I cast my semen into this pitcher made by gods, O Pretty woman, having beautiful hips! Thus having dropped my semen, I shall get my desire fulfilled in case you do not desire our physical union. (17-18)

verses.text:
तस्य तल्लोकनाथस्य वरुणस्य सुभाषितम्।
उर्वशी परमप्रीता श्रुत्वा वाक्यमुवाच ह॥ १९॥
verses.m: “On hearing these sweet words of Varuṇa, the Lord of the western Region known as Varuṇa-Loka, Urvaśī became very happy and said the following words: (19)

verses.text:
काममेतद् भवत्वेवं हृदयं मे त्वयि स्थितम्।
भावश्चाप्यधिकं तुभ्यं देहो मित्रस्य तु प्रभो॥ २०॥
verses.m: “ ‘Be it so. My heart is set on you. I love you more, but, O Lord! my physical body belongs to Mitra.’ (20)

verses.text:
उर्वश्या एवमुक्तस्तु रेतस्तन्महदद्भुतम्।
ज्वलदग्निसमप्रख्यं तस्मिन् कुम्भे न्यवासृजत्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Thus told by Urvaśī, Varuṇa dropped his mighty wonderful semen, which was like a flame of burning fire, into the pitcher. (21)

verses.text:
उर्वशी त्वगमत् तत्र मित्रो वै यत्र देवता।
तां तु मित्रः सुसंक्रुद्ध उर्वशीमिदमब्रवीत्॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Urvaśī left for the place where god Mitra was waiting for her. Mitra was infuriated and said to Urvaśī: (22)

verses.text:
मयाभिमन्त्रिता पूर्वं कस्मात् त्वमवसर्जिता।
पतिमन्यं वृतवती किमर्थं दुष्टचारिणि॥ २३॥
verses.m: “ ‘You were first invited by me. O impious woman! Why did you forsake me and chose someone else? (23)

verses.text:
अनेन दुष्कृतेन त्वं मत्क्रोधकलुषीकृता।
मनुष्यलोकमास्थाय कंचित् कालं निवत्स्यसि॥ २४॥
verses.m: “ ‘Defiled by my anger on account of this sin of yours, you will live for sometime in the world of the mortals. (24)

verses.text:
बुधस्य पुत्रो राजर्षिः काशिराजः पुरूरवाः।
तमभ्यागच्छ दुर्बुद्धे स ते भर्ता भविष्यति॥ २५॥
verses.m: “ ‘O Evil-minded one! There is a Rājarṣi Purūravā, son of Budha and king of Kāśī. Go to him. He will be your husband.’ (25)

verses.text:
ततः सा शापदोषेण पुरूरवसमभ्यगात्।
प्रतिष्ठाने पुरूरवं बुधस्यात्मजमौरसम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Then as an evil consequence of the curse she went to Budha’s legitimate son, Purūravā, who ruled in the city of Pratiṣṭhāna. (26)

verses.text:
तस्य जज्ञे ततः श्रीमानायुः पुत्रो महाबलः।
नहुषो यस्य पुत्रस्तु बभूवेन्द्रसमद्युतिः॥ २७॥
verses.m: “From her a majestic son named Āyu endowed with great prowess, was born to him, whose son was Nahuṣa and whose majesty was like that of Indra. (27)

verses.text:
वज्रमुत्सृज्य वृत्राय श्रान्तेऽथ त्रिदिवेश्वरे।
शतं वर्षसहस्राणि येनेन्द्रत्वं प्रशासितम्॥ २८॥
verses.m: “When Indra vacated his post after hurling his thunderbolt on Vṛtra, Nahuṣa, ruled as Indra for a hundred thousand years. (28)

verses.text:
सा तेन शापेन जगाम भूमिं
तदोर्वशी चारुदती सुनेत्रा।
बहूनि वर्षाण्यवसच्च सुभ्रूः
शापक्षयादिन्द्रसदो ययौ च॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Thus, following the curse, Urvaśī, who had beautiful teeth and eyes went to the region of the earth and the beautiful woman lived there for several years and when the duration of the curse was over, she repaired to the abode of Indra.” (29)

verses.text:
तां श्रुत्वा दिव्यसंकाशां कथामद्भुतदर्शनाम्।
लक्ष्मणः परमप्रीतो राघवं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: On hearing that charming and wonderful story, Lakṣmaṇa became very happy and addressed the following words to Śrī Rāma, a descendant of Raghu: (1)

verses.text:
निक्षिप्तदेहौ काकुत्स्थ कथं तौ द्विजपार्थिवौ।
पुनर्देहेन संयोगं जग्मतुर्देवसम्मतौ॥ २॥
verses.m: “O Descendant of Kākutstha! How is it that the Brāhmaṇa Vasiṣṭha and the king Nimi, who were revered even by the gods, again became embodied after having left their body?” (2)

verses.text:
तस्य तद् भाषितं श्रुत्वा रामः सत्यपराक्रमः।
तां कथां कथयामास वसिष्ठस्य महात्मनः॥ ३॥
verses.m: On hearing the speech of Lakṣmaṇa, Śrī Rāma, who was endowed with true valour, narrated the story of the high-souled Vasiṣṭha. (3)

verses.text:
यः स कुम्भो रघुश्रेष्ठ तेजःपूर्णो महात्मनोः।
तस्मिंस्तेजोमयौ विप्रौ सम्भूतावृषिसत्तमौ॥ ४॥
verses.m: “O best among the Raghus! the two brilliant Brāhmaṇas were born from the pitcher which was filled with the lustre (semen) of those two high-souled ones (viz., Mitra and Varuṇa). They were the most eminent sages. (4)

verses.text:
पूर्वं समभवत् तत्र अगस्त्यो भगवानृषिः।
नाहं सुतस्तवेत्युक्त्वा मित्रं तस्मादपाक्रमत्॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Out of pitcher the first to be born was the illustrious sage Agastya, ‘I am not only your son,’ thus addressing Mitra he left. (5)

verses.text:
तद्धि तेजस्तु मित्रस्य उर्वश्याः पूर्वमाहितम्।
तस्मिन् समभवत् कुम्भे तत्तेजो यत्र वारुणम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “It was Mitra’s lustre which was deposited first in the presence of Urvaśī. There in that pitcher Varuṇa’s lustre was also added to it. (6)

verses.text:
कस्यचित् त्वथ कालस्य मित्रावरुणसम्भवः।
वसिष्ठस्तेजसा युक्तो जज्ञे इक्ष्वाकुदैवतम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “After sometime from the luster of Mitra and Varuṇa was born the majestic Vasiṣṭha, who became the family-priest of the Ikṣvākus. (7)

verses.text:
तमिक्ष्वाकुर्महातेजा जातमात्रमनिन्दितम्।
वव्रे पुरोधसं सौम्य वंशस्यास्य हिताय नः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “O gentle one! No sooner was the blameless Vasiṣṭha born than the most brilliant Ikṣvāku chose him as priest for the welfare of our (the line of Sun or Raghus) family. (8)

verses.text:
एवं त्वपूर्वदेहस्य वसिष्ठस्य महात्मनः।
कथितो निर्गमः सौम्य निमेः शृणु यथाभवत्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “O gentle one! Thus I have narrated the account of the birth of the high-souled Vasiṣṭha embodied anew. Now listen to what happened to Nimi. (9)

verses.text:
दृष्ट्वा विदेहं राजानमृषयः सर्व एव ते।
तं च ते याजयामासुर्यज्ञदीक्षां मनीषिणः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “On seeing that the king was dead, all the wise sages took the initiation for the sacrifice and concluded the sacrifice. (10)

verses.text:
तं च देहं नरेन्द्रस्य रक्षन्ति स्म द्विजोत्तमाः।
गन्धैर्माल्यैश्च वस्त्रैश्च पौरभृत्यसमन्विताः॥ ११॥
verses.m: “The eminent Brāhmaṇas or Brāhmarṣis alongwith the citizens and servants preserved the body of the king, together with perfumes, garlands and garments. (11)

verses.text:
ततो यज्ञे समाप्ते तु भृगुस्तत्रेदमब्रवीत्।
आनयिष्यामि ते चेतस्तुष्टोऽस्मि तव पार्थिव॥ १२॥
verses.m: “After the conclusion of the sacrifice, Bhṛgu addressed, ‘O King! I am pleased with you. I shall restore your soul (consciousness).’ (12)

verses.text:
सुप्रीताश्च सुराः सर्वे निमेश्चेतस्तदाब्रुवन्।
वरं वरय राजर्षे क्व ते चेतो निरूप्यताम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “All the gods were also very much pleased and thus addressed the King, ‘O sage-king! Ask for a boon. Where should your soul (consciousness) be made to reside?’ (13)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तः सुरैः सर्वैर्निमेश्चेतस्तदाब्रवीत्।
नेत्रेषु सर्वभूतानां वसेयं सुरसत्तमाः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “On being thus told by all the gods, the spirit of Nimi said, ‘O Best of gods! Let me dwell on the eye-lids of all living beings.’ (14)

verses.text:
बाढमित्येव विबुधा निमेश्चेतस्तदाब्रुवन्।
नेत्रेषु सर्वभूतानां वायुभूतश्चरिष्यसि॥ १५॥
verses.m: “The gods said to Nimi’s spirit: ‘Very well! You will dwell (move about) on the eye-lids of all the living beings in the form of air. (15)

verses.text:
त्वत्कृते च निमिष्यन्ति चक्षूंषि पृथिवीपते।
वायुभूतेन चरता विश्रामार्थं मुहुर्मुहुः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “O Lord of the earth! In order to provide rest to you, who would be ever moving about in the form of air, living beings shall blink their eyes frequently.’ (16)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा तु विबुधाः सर्वे जग्मुर्यथागतम्।
ऋषयोऽपि महात्मानो निमेर्देहं समाहरन्॥ १७॥
अरणिं तत्र निक्षिप्य मथनं चक्रुरोजसा।
मन्त्रहोमैर्महात्मानः पुत्रहेतोर्निमेस्तदा॥ १८॥
अरण्यां मथ्यमानायां प्रादुर्भूतो महातपाः।
मथनान्मिथिरित्याहुर्जननाज्जनकोऽभवत् ॥ १९॥
यस्माद् विदेहात् सम्भूतो वैदेहस्तु ततः स्मृतः।
एवं विदेहराजश्च जनकः पूर्वकोऽभवत्।
मिथिर्नाम महातेजास्तेनायं मैथिलोऽभवत्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Having said thus, all the gods left as they had come. The high-souled sages held Nimi’s body and started churning Araṇi vigorously. In order that a son should be born to Nimi, when the high-souled ones were subjecting the fire-producing wood to friction and performing ‘oblation’ and reciting hymns a son was born called Mithi, by the great ascetics. He was called Videha as he was born of ‘Videha’. He was called Mithi, having been born from friction. He was called Janaka, since he was born in a mysterious manner. Thus at first the illustrious Janaka was also called Mithi, and hence the dynasty of Janaka was called Maithila (Dynasty). (17—20)

verses.text:
इति सर्वमशेषतो मया
कथितं सम्भवकारणं तु सौम्य।
नृपपुङ्गवशापजं द्विजस्य
द्विजशापाच्च यदद्भुतं नृपस्य॥ २१॥
verses.m: “O Gentle-one! I have thus fully narrated the circumstances leading to the birth of Brāhmaṇa Vasiṣṭha as a result of the curse of Nimi, the foremost among kings and of king Nimi as a result of the curse of Brāhmaṇa Vasiṣṭha.” (21)

verses.text:
एवं ब्रुवति रामे तु लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा।
प्रत्युवाच महात्मानं ज्वलन्तमिव तेजसा॥ १॥
महदद्भुतमाश्चर्यं विदेहस्य पुरातनम्।
निर्वृत्तं राजशार्दूल वसिष्ठस्य मुनेश्च ह॥ २॥
verses.m: Thus spoken to by Śrī Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, the destroyer of the heroes among foes, spoke thus to the noble one, Śrī Rāma, lustrous with vigour: ‘O Lion among kings, that which took place to Vasiṣṭha, Videha, who had no mortal frame in ancient times, was indeed surprising and caused great wonder. (1-2)

verses.text:
निमिस्तु क्षत्रियः शूरो विशेषेण च दीक्षितः।
न क्षमं कृतवान् राजा वसिष्ठस्य महात्मनः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “The Kṣatriya king Nimi, the brave and well-initiated one, on his part did not behave properly, by not forgiving the noble Vasiṣṭha.” (3)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तु तेनायं रामः क्षत्रियपुङ्गवः।
उवाच लक्ष्मणं वाक्यं सर्वशास्त्रविशारदम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Thus addressed to by him (Lakṣmaṇa), the foremost among the Kṣatriyas, Śrī Rāma uttered the following words to Lakṣmaṇa, who was well-versed in all the Śāstras. (4)

verses.text:
रामो रमयतां श्रेष्ठो भ्रातरं दीप्ततेजसम्।
न सर्वत्र क्षमा वीर पुरुषेषु प्रदृश्यते॥ ५॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma the best among those who cause pleasure to others, spoke to his brother illuminated with vigour: “O brave one, forgiveness is not found among all kinds of men. (5)

verses.text:
सौमित्रे दुःसहो रोषो यथा क्षान्तो ययातिना।
सत्त्वानुगं पुरस्कृत्य तन्निबोध समाहितः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “O son of Sumitrā, listen with attention as to how the unbearable rage was mitigated by Yayāti, resorting to a device, where the Sattva Guṇa was predominant. (6)

verses.text:
नहुषस्य सुतो राजा ययातिः पौरवर्धनः।
तस्य भार्याद्वयं सौम्य रूपेणाप्रतिमं भुवि॥ ७॥
verses.m: “There was a king Yayāti, the son of Nahuṣa, the bringer of prosperity to the citizens. His two spouses were paragons of unequal beauty, indeed. (7)

verses.text:
एका तु तस्य राजर्षेर्नाहुषस्य पुरस्कृता।
शर्मिष्ठा नाम दैतेयी दुहिता वृषपर्वणः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “One of these, the daughter of Vṛṣaparvā, the grand-daughter of Diti, Śarmiṣṭhā by name was held in great esteem by the Ṛṣi among Kings, Nahuṣa. (8)

verses.text:
अन्या तूशनसः पत्नी ययातेः पुरुषर्षभ।
न तु सा दयिता राज्ञो देवयानी सुमध्यमा॥ ९॥
verses.m: “The other, the daughter of Uśanā, the wife of Yayāti, Devayānī by name. O bull among men, was not loved by the King, although she possessed a beautiful form. (9)

verses.text:
तयोः पुत्रौ तु सम्भूतौ रूपवन्तौ समाहितौ।
शर्मिष्ठाजनयत् पूरुं देवयानी यदुं तदा॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Two sons were born to them, who were handsome and devoted. Śarmiṣṭhā begot Pūru; while Devayānī gave birth to Yadu. (10)

verses.text:
पूरुस्तु दयितो राज्ञो गुणैर्मातृकृतेन च।
ततो दुःखसमाविष्टो यदुर्मातरमब्रवीत्॥ ११॥
भार्गवस्य कुले जाता देवस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः।
सहसे हृद्गतं दुःखमवमानं च दुःसहम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Pūru was the beloved of the King, by his own merits and also due to being the progeny of his mother. Consequently, Yadu being in grief addressed his mother thus: ‘Born in the family of the Bhārgava (son of Bhṛgu), the lord of unwearied action, you bear up with mental sorrow and unbearable insult. (11-12)

verses.text:
आवां च सहितौ देवि प्रविशाव हुताशनम्।
राजा तु रमतां सार्धं दैत्यपुत्र्या बहुक्षपाः॥ १३॥
verses.m: ‘O mother, we shall enter the fire together, may the King enjoy himself with the daughter of the son of Diti for many nights. (13)

verses.text:
यदि वा सहनीयं ते मामनुज्ञातुमर्हसि।
क्षम त्वं न क्षमिष्येऽहं मरिष्यामि न संशयः॥ १४॥
verses.m: ‘If, however, you consider it as endurable by you, allow me to depart. You may bear up with it, but I cannot bear. I shall die without hesitation.’ (14)

verses.text:
पुत्रस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा परमार्तस्य रोदतः।
देवयानी तु संक्रुद्धा सस्मार पितरं तदा॥ १५॥
verses.m: Hearing the words of her son, who was full in tears due to great agony, Devayānī in rage remembered her Father. (15)

verses.text:
इङ्गितं तदभिज्ञाय दुहितुर्भार्गवस्तदा।
आगतस्त्वरितं तत्र देवयानी स्म यत्र सा॥ १६॥
verses.m: Knowing the feelings of his daughter, the son of Bhṛgu (Ācārya Śukra) came in haste there where Devayānī was staying. (16)

verses.text:
दृष्ट्वा चाप्रकृतिस्थां तामप्रहृष्टामचेतनाम्।
पिता दुहितरं वाक्यं किमेतदिति चाब्रवीत्॥ १७॥
verses.m: Finding Devayānī not in her normal state and almost unconscious with pain and unhappy, the father (Bhārgava) Śukra enquired the daughter as to what had caused her such grief. (17)

verses.text:
पृच्छन्तमसकृत् तं वै भार्गवं दीप्ततेजसम्।
देवयानी तु संक्रुद्धा पितरं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ १८॥
अहमग्निं विषं तीक्ष्णमपो वा मुनिसत्तम।
भक्षयिष्ये प्रवेक्ष्ये वा न तु शक्ष्यामि जीवितुम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: Devayānī in anger said thus to her father, the son of Bhṛgu who was mentally roused and had asked her several times the cause of her anger. ‘O Best among the ascetics, I shall indeed enter fire or water or take strong poison. It is indeed not possible for me to live. (18-19)

verses.text:
न मां त्वमवजानीषे दुःखितामवमानिताम्।
वृक्षस्यावज्ञया ब्रह्मंश्छिद्यन्ते वृक्षजीविनः॥ २०॥
verses.m: ‘You do not know how I am pained and insulted, O Brāhmaṇa. Having no tender feelings for the tree, its leaves and flowers are cut and destroyed. (20)

verses.text:
अवज्ञया च राजर्षिः परिभूय च भार्गव।
मय्यवज्ञां प्रयुङ्क्ते हि न च मां बहु मन्यते॥ २१॥
verses.m: ‘The Ṛṣi among Kings, causing insult to me, ignores me and does not look upon me as one worthy of consideration.’ (21)

verses.text:
तस्यास्तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा कोपेनाभिपरीवृतः।
व्याहर्तुमुपचक्राम भार्गवो नहुषात्मजम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: Hearing these words of Devayānī, before himself, the son of Bhṛgu was highly enraged and he uttered curse to the son of Nahuṣa: (22)

verses.text:
यस्मान्मामवजानीषे नाहुष त्वं दुरात्मवान्।
वयसा जरया जीर्णः शैथिल्यमुपयास्यसि॥ २३॥
verses.m: ‘O son of Nahuṣa, O ignoble one, as you insult me, so you shall lose all your organ power, and become weakened by old age.’ (23)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा दुहितरं समाश्वास्य स भार्गवः।
पुनर्जगाम ब्रह्मर्षिर्भवनं स्वं महायशाः॥ २४॥
verses.m: Thus having uttered the curse and consoled his daughter, that son of Bhṛgu, the Brāhmaṇa Ṛṣi, the famous one, departed to his abode. (24)

verses.text:
स एवमुक्त्वा द्विजपुङ्गवाग्र्यः
सुतां समाश्वास्य च देवयानीम्।
पुनर्ययौ सूर्यसमानतेजा
दत्त्वा च शापं नहुषात्मजाय॥ २५॥
verses.m: The best among the twice-born, thus said and consoled Devayānī, he with sunlike lustre, repaired pronouncing curse on Yayāti, the son of Nahuṣa. (25)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा तूशनसं क्रुद्धं तदार्तो नहुषात्मजः।
जरां परमिकां प्राप्य यदुं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Hearing the words of Uśanā uttered in rage, the penitent son of Nahuṣa, Yayāti, then possessed of ripe old age said to Yadu: (1)

verses.text:
यदो त्वमसि धर्मज्ञो मदर्थं प्रतिगृह्यताम्।
जरा परमिका पुत्र भोगै रंस्ये महायशः॥ २॥
verses.m: ‘O Yadu, my son of a great fame, you are righteous, accept for my sake my old age, may I enjoy the objects of desire. (2)

verses.text:
न तावत् कृतकृत्योऽस्मि विषयेषु नरर्षभ।
अनुभूय तदा कामं ततः प्राप्स्याम्यहं जराम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: ‘I have not been satisfied with the pleasure of senses. O bull among men, having experienced the joy of senses, I shall again attain my old age’ (3)

verses.text:
यदुस्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रत्युवाच नरर्षभम्।
पुत्रस्ते दयितः पूरुः प्रतिगृह्णातु वै जराम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Hearing these words of Yayāti, Yadu replied to the bull among men (Yayāti), ‘Pūru is your dear son, may he accept the old age. (4)

verses.text:
बहिष्कृतोऽहमर्थेषु संनिकर्षाच्च पार्थिव।
प्रतिगृह्णातु वै राजन् यैः सहाश्नासि भोजनम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: ‘O King, I have been deprived of the objects of desire and wealth and also your company. He alone among men with whom you take your food, can accept it.’ (5)

verses.text:
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा राजा पूरुमथाब्रवीत्।
इयं जरा महाबाहो मदर्थं प्रतिगृह्यताम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: Hearing these words spoken by him, Yayāti, the king then said to Pūru: ‘O one of long-arms, please accept this old age.’ (6)

verses.text:
नाहुषेणैवमुक्तस्तु पूरुः प्राञ्जलिरब्रवीत्।
धन्योऽस्म्यनुगृहीतोऽस्मि शासनेऽस्मि तव स्थितः॥ ७॥
verses.m: Thus requested by Yayāti, the son of Nahuṣa, Pūru with folded hands said: ‘I am fortunate and feel obliged to you, I am at your command.’ (7)

verses.text:
पूरोर्वचनमाज्ञाय नाहुषः परया मुदा।
प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे जरां संक्रामयच्च ताम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: Having heard the word of Pūru, the son of Nahuṣa, Yayāti, was highly pleased, and transferred that old age to him. (8)

verses.text:
ततः स राजा तरुणः प्राप्य यज्ञान् सहस्रशः।
बहुवर्षसहस्राणि पालयामास मेदिनीम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: Then the youthful king, having performed a thousandfold sacrifices ruled over the earth for many thousand years. (9)

verses.text:
अथ दीर्घस्य कालस्य राजा पूरुमथाब्रवीत्।
आनयस्व जरां पुत्र न्यासं निर्यातयस्व मे॥ १०॥
verses.m: Then after a long time the king spoke thus to Pūru: ‘O dear son, bring forth my old age, return that which was deposited in you as trust. (10)

verses.text:
न्यासभूता मया पुत्र त्वयि संक्रामिता जरा।
तस्मात् प्रतिगृहीष्यामि तां जरां मा व्यथां कृथाः॥ ११॥
verses.m: ‘O son! the old age which was in the form of deposit, was transferred to you; therefore, now I shall take back my old age, do not feel pained. (11)

verses.text:
प्रीतश्चास्मि महाबाहो शासनस्य प्रतिग्रहात्।
त्वां चाहमभिषेक्ष्यामि प्रीतियुक्तो नराधिपम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: ‘O one of long-arms, I am pleased by your acceptance of my command, I shall also consecrate you with joy as a ruler of the subjects among men.’ (12)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा सुतं पूरुं ययातिर्नहुषात्मजः।
देवयानीसुतं क्रुद्धो राजा वाक्यमुवाच ह॥ १३॥
राक्षसस्त्वं मया जातः क्षत्ररूपो दुरासदः।
प्रतिहंसि ममाज्ञां त्वं प्रजार्थे विफलो भव॥ १४॥
verses.m: Thus having spoken to his son Pūru, Yayāti, the son of Nahuṣa, in anger uttered these words to the son of Devayānī: ‘By me, you are born a Rākṣasa (demon) in the form of Kṣatriya. As you defy my orders you lose chance to rule over the subjects. (13-14)

verses.text:
पितरं गुरुभूतं मां यस्मात् त्वमवमन्यसे।
राक्षसान् यातुधानांस्त्वं जनयिष्यसि दारुणान्॥ १५॥
verses.m: ‘As thou showest disrespect to me, your father and preceptor, you will create the cruel Rākṣasas and Yātudhānas (evil spirits). (15)

verses.text:
न तु सोमकुलोत्पन्ने वंशे स्थास्यति दुर्मतेः।
वंशोऽपि भवतस्तुल्यो दुर्विनीतो भविष्यति॥ १६॥
verses.m: ‘Your progeny will not belong to the family originating from the race of Soma, the moon. O evil-minded one, your family will also be wicked as you are.’ (16)

verses.text:
तमेवमुक्त्वा राजर्षिः पूरुं राज्यविवर्धनम्।
अभिषेकेण सम्पूज्य आश्रमं प्रविवेश ह॥ १७॥
verses.m: Thus admonishing Yadu then, honouring Pūru, the enhancer of the royal suzerainty with consecration, entered the other Āśrama (Vānaprastha). (17)

verses.text:
ततः कालेन महता दिष्टान्तमुपजग्मिवान्।
त्रिदिवं स गतो राजा ययातिर्नहुषात्मजः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Then after a long time approaching his destiny as desired, the king Yayāti (the son of Nahuṣa) departed to heaven. (18)

verses.text:
पूरुश्चकार तद् राज्यं धर्मेण महता वृतः।
प्रतिष्ठाने पुरवरे काशिराज्ये महायशाः॥ १९॥
verses.m: Pūru the mighty one ruled with great righteousness in the famous city of Pratiṣṭhāna in the kingdom of Kāśī. (19)

verses.text:
यदुस्तु जनयामास यातुधानान् सहस्रशः।
पुरे क्रौञ्चवने दुर्गे राजवंशबहिष्कृतः॥ २०॥
verses.m: Yadu produced Yātudhānas (evil beings) in thousands, in the forest of Krauñcavana, difficult to traverse, banished as he was from the royal family. (20)

verses.text:
एष तूशनसा मुक्तः शापोत्सर्गो ययातिना।
धारितः क्षत्रधर्मेण यं निमिश्चक्षमे न च॥ २१॥
verses.m: This is how the mighty curse that was uttered by Uśanā, which fell on Yayāti, was borne by him according to the code of conduct of the Kṣatriyas, and which Nimi could not forbear. (21)

verses.text:
एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं दर्शनं सर्वकारिणाम्।
अनुवर्तामहे सौम्य दोषो न स्याद् यथा नृगे॥ २२॥
verses.m: “All this has been narrated to you; we shall grant audience to all who come for action, so that we do not commit the fault that was committed by the king, Nṛga.” (22)

verses.text:
इति कथयति रामे चन्द्रतुल्याननेन
प्रविरलतरतारं व्योम जज्ञे तदानीम्।
अरुणकिरणरक्ता दिग् बभौ चैव पूर्वा
कुसुमरसविमुक्तं वस्त्रमागुण्ठितेव॥ २३॥
verses.m: As Rāma with moon-like face narrated this, the sky with fading stars appeared. The eastern quarter shone with red rays as if enveloped with a red garment. (23)

verses.text:
ततः प्रभाते विमले कृत्वा पौर्वाह्णिकीं क्रियाम्।
धर्मासनगतो राजा रामो राजीवलोचनः॥ १॥
राजधर्मानवेक्षन् वै ब्राह्मणैर्नैगमैः सह।
पुरोधसा वसिष्ठेन ऋषिणा कश्यपेन च॥ २॥
verses.m: Thereafter in the bright morning Śrī Rāma, of lotus-like eye having performed forenoon rites, took his seat in the Royal Council-chamber alongwith the Brāhmaṇas, who were masters of the Vedas, the priest Vasiṣṭha and the sage Kaśyapa, in order to look into the royal business. (1-2)

verses.text:
मन्त्रिभिर्व्यवहारज्ञैस्तथान्यैर्धर्मपाठकैः।
नीतिज्ञैरथ सभ्यैश्च राजभिः सा सभा वृता॥ ३॥
verses.m: The royal council (assembly) consisted of ministers, knowers of common practices, legal procedures and other teachers of laws who recite scriptures, diplomats (statesmen), kings and other members of the council. (3)

verses.text:
सभा यथा महेन्द्रस्य यमस्य वरुणस्य च।
शुशुभे राजसिंहस्य रामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः॥ ४॥
verses.m: The assembly of Śrī Rāma, the chief of kings and unwearied in actions looked graceful like the assembly of Indra, Yama and Varuṇa. (4)

verses.text:
अथ रामोऽब्रवीत् तत्र लक्ष्मणं शुभलक्षणम्।
निर्गच्छ त्वं महाबाहो सुमित्रानन्दवर्धन॥ ५॥
कार्यार्थिनश्च सौमित्रे व्याहर्तुं त्वमुपाक्रम।
रामस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणः शुभलक्षणः॥ ६॥
द्वारदेशमुपागम्य कार्यिणश्चाह्वयत् स्वयम्।
न कश्चिदब्रवीत् तत्र मम कार्यमिहाद्य वै॥ ७॥
verses.m: Then Śrī Rāma said to Lakṣmaṇa, who was seated there and who was characterised by auspicious marks, ‘O Long-armed Lakṣmaṇa! go out and call by turn those, who have come with some business’. Having listened to Śrī Rāma’s order, Lakṣmaṇa endowed with auspicious marks, going to the palace-gate himself called those who had come with some request. None there came forward saying that he had some request to make. (5—7)

verses.text:
नाधयो व्याधयश्चैव रामे राज्यं प्रशासति।
पक्वसस्या वसुमती सर्वौषधिसमन्विता॥ ८॥
न बालो म्रियते तत्र न युवा न च मध्यमः।
धर्मेण शासितं सर्वं न च बाधा विधीयते॥ ९॥
दृश्यते न च कार्यार्थी रामे राज्यं प्रशासति।
लक्ष्मणः प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा रामायैवं न्यवेदयत्॥ १०॥
verses.m: During the reign of Śrī Rāma no one was offended by either physical or mental ailment. The earth abounded in all kinds of plants and fully ripe agricultural produce. Thus in His kingdom neither any child nor any young man nor any middle-aged person died. Everything was administered according to ‘Dharma’ (moral law). No hindrance was ever put. While Srī Rāma ruled over the kingdom no one was seen coming with any request with folded hands, Lakṣmaṇa communicated all this to Him. (8—10)

verses.text:
अथ रामः प्रसन्नात्मा सौमित्रिमिदमब्रवीत्।
भूय एव तु गच्छ त्वं कार्यिणः प्रविचारय॥ ११॥
सम्यक्प्रणीतया नीत्या नाधर्मो विद्यते क्वचित्।
तस्माद् राजभयात् सर्वे रक्षन्तीह परस्परम्॥ १२॥
बाणा इव मया मुक्ता इह रक्षन्ति मे प्रजाः।
तथापि त्वं महाबाहो प्रजा रक्षस्व तत्परः॥ १३॥
verses.m: Then the gracious-minded Śrī Rāma addressed the following words to Lakṣmaṇa, “Go again and find out about those who have come with some request.” When the state policy is formulated properly and executed well, unrighteousness does not prevail anywhere. Therefore all persons protect one another due to the fear from the king (due to the apprehension of royal punishment). My officers protect the subjects like arrows shot by Me. Even then, O long-armed one! protect the subjects righteously. (11—13)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तु सौमित्रिर्निर्जगाम नृपालयात्।
अपश्यद् द्वारदेशे वै श्वानं तावदवस्थितम्॥ १४॥
तमेव वीक्षमाणं वै विक्रोशन्तं मुहुर्मुहुः।
दृष्ट्वाथ लक्ष्मणस्तं वै स पप्रच्छाथ वीर्यवान्॥ १५॥
किं ते कार्यं महाभाग ब्रूहि विस्रब्धमानसः।
लक्ष्मणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा सारमेयोऽभ्यभाषत॥ १६॥
verses.m: Thus told by Śrī Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa went out of the royal palace and saw a dog at the gate, which stood there looking at him and repeatedly barking. On seeing him, then the valiant Lakṣmaṇa asked—‘O Illustrious one! Tell me fearlessly your problem.’ On hearing Lakṣmaṇa’s words the dog replied thus: (14—16)

verses.text:
सर्वभूतशरण्याय रामायाक्लिष्टकर्मणे।
भयेष्वभयदात्रे च तस्मै वक्तुं समुत्सहे॥ १७॥
verses.m: ‘I can dare tell Śrī Rāma, who is a refuge to all living beings, who is ever unwearied in action and ensures protection whenever there is occasion for fear.’ (17)

verses.text:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा च वचनं सारमेयस्य लक्ष्मणः।
राघवाय तदाख्यातुं प्रविवेशालयं शुभम्॥ १८॥
निवेद्य रामस्य पुनर्निर्जगाम नृपालयात्।
वक्तव्यं यदि ते किंचित् तत्त्वं ब्रूहि नृपाय वै॥ १९॥
verses.m: On hearing the dog’s speech, Lakṣmaṇa entered the auspicious royal palace in order to communicate the same to Śrī Rāma and after informing Him, Lakṣmaṇa came out of the royal palace and said to the dog, “If you have to say something, then tell the king about it.” (18-19)

verses.text:
लक्ष्मणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा सारमेयोऽभ्यभाषत।
देवागारे नृपागारे द्विजवेश्मसु वै तथा॥ २०॥
वह्निः शतक्रतुश्चैव सूर्यो वायुश्च तिष्ठति।
नात्र योग्यास्तु सौमित्रे योनीनामधमा वयम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: Having heard Lakṣmaṇa’s speech the dog said, ‘Agni (the Fire-god), Indra, Sūrya (the sun-god) and Vāyu (the wind-god) are present in the temples, the royal abode and the houses of Brāhmaṇas. O Lakṣmaṇa! we, of the lowest origin, are unfit to go there. (20-21)

verses.text:
प्रवेष्टुं नात्र शक्ष्यामि धर्मो विग्रहवान् नृपः।
सत्यवादी रणपटुः सर्वसत्त्वहिते रतः॥ २२॥
verses.m: ‘I shall not be able to enter there (the royal palace). King Śrī Rāma is ‘Dharma.’ He speaks the truth, He is adept in battle-fighting and is devoted to doing good to all the people. (22)

verses.text:
षाड्गुण्यस्य पदं वेत्ति नीतिकर्ता स राघवः।
सर्वज्ञः सर्वदर्शी च रामो रमयतां वरः॥ २३॥
verses.m: ‘Śrī Rāma knows the appropriate time for the petitioners—practice of the six Guṇas. He dispenses justice. He is omniscient, He sees all things. Śrī Rāma is foremost among those who delight others. (23)

verses.text:
स सोमः स च मृत्युश्च स यमो धनदस्तथा।
वह्निः शतक्रतुश्चैव सूर्यो वै वरुणस्तथा॥ २४॥
verses.m: ‘He is Soma, He is Death. He is Yama (God of Death). He is Kubera, Agni and Indra, and He is Sūrya, the sun, and Varuṇa. (24)

verses.text:
तस्य त्वं ब्रूहि सौमित्रे प्रजापालः स राघवः।
अनाज्ञप्तस्तु सौमित्रे प्रवेष्टुं नेच्छयाम्यहम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: ‘Śrī Rāma is the protector of the subjects. O Lakṣmaṇa! tell Him, “Without permission, I do not want to enter the royal palace.’ (25)

verses.text:
आनृशंस्यान्महाभागः प्रविवेश महाद्युतिः।
नृपालयं प्रविश्याथ लक्ष्मणो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ २६॥
verses.m: On hearing this, the illustrious and glorious Lakṣmaṇa having entered the royal abode out of compassion said the following words: (26)

verses.text:
श्रूयतां मम विज्ञाप्यं कौसल्यानन्दवर्धन।
यन्मयोक्तं महाबाहो तव शासनजं विभो॥ २७॥
श्वा वै ते तिष्ठते द्वारि कार्यार्थी समुपागतः।
लक्ष्मणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा रामो वचनमब्रवीत्।
सम्प्रवेशय वै क्षिप्रं कार्यार्थी योऽत्र तिष्ठति॥ २८॥
verses.m: ‘O Śrī Rāma! listen to what I have to say. O delighter of Kausalyā! O long-armed one! O lord! According to what you had commanded, I called on those who have come with some business. A dog, which has come with a request is standing at your palace-gate.’ After hearing Lakṣmaṇa’s speech, Śrī Rāma said: “Let it enter quickly, the one standing there with some request.’ (27-28)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा रामस्य वचनं लक्ष्मणस्त्वरितस्तदा।
श्वानमाहूय मतिमान् राघवाय न्यवेदयत्॥ १॥
दृष्ट्वा समागतं श्वानं रामो वचनमब्रवीत्।
विवक्षितार्थं मे ब्रूहि सारमेय न ते भयम्॥ २॥
verses.m: On hearing Śrī Rāma’s speech, the wise Lakṣmaṇa, after hurriedly calling the dog, informed Śrī Rāma about its (the dog’s) arrival, and presented him before Śrī Rāma, Having seen the dog that had come, Śrī Rāma said to him, ‘O dog! Tell me what you have to say, you need not fear at all.’ (1-2)

verses.text:
अथापश्यत तत्रस्थं रामं श्वा भिन्नमस्तकः।
ततो दृष्ट्वा स राजानं सारमेयोऽब्रवीद् वचः॥ ३॥
verses.m: Thereafter the dog whose skull was shattered saw Śrī Rāma seated there. Having seen the king, the dog addressed the following speech: (3)

verses.text:
राजैव कर्ता भूतानां राजा चैव विनायकः।
राजा सुप्तेषु जागर्ति राजा पालयति प्रजाः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “The king is the creator of all living beings and the king is the leader of men. The king remains awake, when others are asleep. The king protects the subjects. (4)

verses.text:
नीत्या सुनीतया राजा धर्मं रक्षति रक्षिता।
यदा न पालयेद् राजा क्षिप्रं नश्यन्ति वै प्रजाः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “The king, who is the protector of all, protects Dharma by pursuing right policy. When the king does not protect, the subjects perish soon. (5)

verses.text:
राजा कर्ता च गोप्ता च सर्वस्य जगतः पिता।
राजा कालो युगं चैव राजा सर्वमिदं जगत्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “The king is the creator, protector and father of the entire world. The king is the time (sets the trend of the times) and the ‘Yuga’ (a particular age of the world). The king is the whole world. (6)

verses.text:
धारणाद् धर्ममित्याहुर्धर्मेण विधृताः प्रजाः।
यस्माद् धारयते सर्वं त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “They call it ‘Dharma’, for it sustains the world. The created beings are sustained by ‘Dharma’. Since it supports the three worlds together with all the movable and immovable things. (7)

verses.text:
धारणाद् विद्विषां चैव धर्मेणारञ्जयन् प्रजाः।
तस्माद् धारणमित्युक्तं स धर्म इति निश्चयः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “He sustains even his enemies, puts them on the right path and delights his subjects by ‘Dharma’. Therefore, he (his rule) is known as ‘Dharma’. (8)

verses.text:
एष राजन् परो धर्मः फलवान् प्रेत्य राघव।
नहि धर्माद् भवेत् किंचिद् दुष्प्रापमिति मे मतिः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “This act of ‘Dhāraṇa’ or sustaining is ‘Dharma’—this is the conclusion. O king Śrī Rāma, this is the highest ‘Dharma’ which yields reward after death. My view is that nothing is unattainable by ‘Dharma’. (9)

verses.text:
दानं दया सतां पूजा व्यवहारेषु चार्जवम्।
एष राम परो धर्मो रक्षणात् प्रेत्य चेह च॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Charity, compassion, honouring noble men, straight-forwardness in behaviour, O Rāma! this is the ‘Dharma’ in this life and the life hereafter that accrues from protecting the subjects. (10)

verses.text:
त्वं प्रमाणं प्रमाणानामसि राघव सुव्रत।
विदितश्चैव ते धर्मः सद्भिराचरितस्तु वै॥ ११॥
धर्माणां त्वं परं धाम गुणानां सागरोपमः।
अज्ञानाच्च मया राजन्नुक्तस्त्वं राजसत्तम॥ १२॥
प्रसादयामि शिरसा न त्वं क्रोद्धुमिहार्हसि।
शुनः स वचनं श्रुत्वा राघवो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “O Rāma, strict observer of vows! You are the authority par-excellence. You are conversant with the ‘Dharma’, which is practised by good people. You are the supreme abode of ‘Dharmas’ (Duties) and an ocean of virtues, as it were. I spoke out of my ignorance. Bowing my head, I pray, You should not get angry on this account.” (11—13)

verses.text:
किं ते कार्यं करोम्यद्य ब्रूहि विस्रब्ध मा चिरम्।
रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा सारमेयोऽब्रवीदिदम्॥ १४॥
धर्मेण राष्ट्रं विन्देत धर्मेणैवानुपालयेत्।
धर्माच्छरण्यतां याति राजा सर्वभयापहः॥ १५॥
verses.m: On this Śrī Rāma told the dog: “Tell me fearlessly what I should do for you. Do not delay,” On hearing Rāma’s speech, the dog addressed the follwoing words: ‘The king should acquire territory by ‘Dharma’ and should protect it by ‘Dharma.’ The king comes to be recognized as a refuge and dispels all fear. (14-15)

verses.text:
इदं विज्ञाय यत् कृत्यं श्रूयतां मम राघव।
भिक्षुः सर्वार्थसिद्धश्च ब्राह्मणावसथे वसन्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Having realized this, O Rāma! listen to what you have to do for me. There is a mendicant, named Sarvārthasiddha, who lives in the house of a Brāhmaṇa. Without any cause he struck at me! sinless though I was.” (16)

verses.text:
तेन दत्तः प्रहारो मे निष्कारणमनागसः।
एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु रामेण द्वाःस्थः सम्प्रेषितस्तदा॥ १७॥
आनीतश्च द्विजस्तेन सर्वसिद्धार्थकोविदः।
अथ द्विजवरस्तत्र रामं दृष्ट्वा महाद्युतिः॥ १८॥
किं ते कार्यं मया राम तद् ब्रूहि त्वं ममानघ।
एवमुक्तस्तु विप्रेण रामो वचनमब्रवीत्॥ १९॥
त्वया दत्तः प्रहारोऽयं सारमेयस्य वै द्विज।
किं तवापकृतं विप्र दण्डेनाभिहतो यतः॥ २०॥
क्रोधः प्राणहरः शत्रुः क्रोधो मित्रमुखो रिपुः।
क्रोधो ह्यसिर्महातीक्ष्णः सर्वं क्रोधोऽपकर्षति॥ २१॥
तपते यजते चैव यच्च दानं प्रयच्छति।
क्रोधेन सर्वं हरति तस्मात् क्रोधं विसर्जयेत्॥ २२॥
इन्द्रियाणां प्रदुष्टानां हयानामिव धावताम्।
कुर्वीत धृत्या सारथ्यं संहृत्येन्द्रियगोचरम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: On hearing this, Śrī Rāma sent the gatekeeper, who brought the learned Brāhmaṇa Sarvārthasiddha by name. Thus the eminent Brāhmaṇa, endowed with splendour seeing Śrī Rāma there asked him, ‘O sinless Śrī Rāma! Tell me what do you want me to do for you?’ Thus told by the Brāhmaṇa, Śrī Rāma addressed the following words, ‘O Brāhmaṇa! You hurt the dog. What ill did it do to you, for which you struck it with a stick? Anger is a deadly enemy, anger is a friend-faced enemy. Anger is a highly sharp sword. Anger takes away everything, destroys all virtues. Whichever sacrifices a person performs and whatever in charity he gives, all that he destroys by anger. Therefore, one should give up anger and control like a charioteer, one’s senses, running forth towards their objects like very wicked horses, after turning them away from their objects (17—23)

verses.text:
मनसा कर्मणा वाचा चक्षुषा च समाचरेत्।
श्रेयो लोकस्य चरतो न द्वेष्टि न च लिप्यते॥ २४॥
न तत् कुर्यादसिस्तीक्ष्णः सर्पो वा व्याहतः पदा।
अरिर्वा नित्यसंक्रुद्धो यथाऽऽत्मा दुरनुष्ठितः॥ २५॥
विनीतविनयस्यापि प्रकृतिर्न विधीयते।
प्रकृतिं गूहमानस्य निश्चयेन कृतिर्ध्रुवा॥ २६॥
verses.m: “A man should do good to the people around himself by thought, by action and by speech. He should not hurt anybody. No sin, therefore, will attach to him. The harm, which is wrought by evil thoughts, are not done by a sharp sword or a serpent trampled by foot or an ever wrothful enemy. One who has learnt discipline, even his temperament cannot be changed. Even if someone conceals his evil nature, it is surely betrayed by his action. (24—26)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तः स विप्रो वै रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा।
द्विजः सर्वार्थसिद्धस्तु अब्रवीद् रामसंनिधौ॥ २७॥
verses.m: Thus asked by Śrī Rāma, who was unwearied in actions, the Brāhmaṇa Sarvārthasiddha said this in Śrī Rāma’s presence: (27)

verses.text:
मया दत्तप्रहारोऽयं क्रोधेनाविष्टचेतसा।
भिक्षार्थमटमानेन काले विगतभैक्षके॥ २८॥
रथ्यास्थितस्त्वयं श्वा वै गच्छ गच्छेति भाषितः।
अथ स्वैरेण गच्छंस्तु रथ्यान्ते विषमं स्थितः॥ २९॥
verses.m: ‘While I was going about for begging food the appropriate time for begging had passed, I was overpowered by anger, so I beat it. The dog, which was standing on the road (blocking my way) was asked by me to move away. Not moving at all, it stood in the middle of the road in an odd manner. (28-29)

verses.text:
क्रोधेन क्षुधयाविष्टस्ततो दत्तोऽस्य राघव।
प्रहारो राजराजेन्द्र शाधि मामपराधिनम्॥ ३०॥
त्वया शस्तस्य राजेन्द्र नास्ति मे नरकाद्भयम्।
अथ रामेण सम्पृष्टाः सर्व एव सभासदः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: ‘Overtaken by hunger, O Rāma! I beat it angrily. O King of kings! Punish me, a guilty person, O chief of kings! Having been punished by you, I would not be afraid of hell.’ Thereafter Śrī Rāma asked all the members of the assembly, ‘What should be done to him, and what punishment should be meted out to him? For, if proper punishment is given to the guilty, the subjects are protected.’ (30-31)

verses.text:
किं कार्यमस्य वै ब्रूत दण्डो वै कोऽस्य पात्यताम्।
सम्यक्प्रणिहिते दण्डे प्रजा भवति रक्षिता॥ ३२॥
भृग्वाङ्गिरसकुत्साद्या वसिष्ठश्च सकाश्यपः।
धर्मपाठकमुख्याश्च सचिवा नैगमास्तथा॥ ३३॥
एते चान्ये च बहवः पण्डितास्तत्र संगताः।
अवध्यो ब्राह्मणो दण्डैरिति शास्त्रविदो विदुः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: Bhṛgu, Aṅgirā, Kutsa and others, Vasiṣṭha alongwith Kāśyapa, eminent teachers of laws, ministers and interpreters of the Vedas—these and many other scholars were present there. All of them—the masters of scriptures and those who were well-versed in state-affairs told Śrī Rāma that a Brāhmaṇa is not to be awarded capital punishment, it is declared by experts in scriptures. (32—34)

verses.text:
ब्रुवते राघवं सर्वे राजधर्मेषु निष्ठिताः।
अथ ते मुनयः सर्वे राममेवाब्रुवंस्तदा॥ ३५॥
राजा शास्ता हि सर्वस्य त्वं विशेषेण राघव।
त्रैलोक्यस्य भवान् शास्ता देवो विष्णुः सनातनः॥ ३६॥
verses.m: Then all the hermits addressed Śrī Rāma in following words, “A King holds sway over everyone. O Śrī Rāma! Specially You, who is the eternal god Viṣṇu, are the ruler of the three worlds.” (35-36)

verses.text:
एवमुक्ते तु तैः सर्वैः श्वा वै वचनमब्रवीत्।
यदि तुष्टोऽसि मे राम यदि देयो वरो मम॥ ३७॥
प्रतिज्ञातं त्वया वीर किं करोमीति विश्रुतम्।
प्रयच्छ ब्राह्मणस्यास्य कौलपत्यं नराधिप॥ ३८॥
कालञ्जरे महाराज कौलपत्यं प्रदीयताम्।
एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु रामेण कौलपत्येऽभिषेचितः॥ ३९॥
verses.m: When all of them had addressed thus, the dog said as follows: “If you are pleased with me, O Rāma, and if you are to bestow on me a boon, then listen to me, O Valiant One! You asked me what you should do for me, and promised (to do what I would request you to do). So make him O King! a ‘Kulapati’ as promised by you. Your Majesty! make him ‘Kulapati’ of Kālanjara.” On hearing this Śrī Rāma consecrated him as a Kulapati. (37—39)

verses.text:
प्रययौ ब्राह्मणो हृष्टो गजस्कन्धेन सोऽर्चितः।
अथ ते रामसचिवाः स्मयमाना वचोऽब्रुवन्॥ ४०॥
वरोऽयं दत्त एतस्य नायं शापो महाद्युते।
एवमुक्तस्तु सचिवै रामो वचनमब्रवीत्॥ ४१॥
न यूयं गतितत्त्वज्ञाः श्वा वै जानाति कारणम्।
अथ पृष्टस्तु रामेण सारमेयोऽब्रवीदिदम्॥ ४२॥
अहं कुलपतिस्तत्र आसं शिष्टान्नभोजनः।
देवद्विजातिपूजायां दासीदासेषु राघव॥ ४३॥
संविभागी शुभरतिर्देवद्रव्यस्य रक्षिता।
विनीतः शीलसम्पन्नः सर्वसत्त्वहिते रतः॥ ४४॥
सोऽहं प्राप्त इमां घोरामवस्थामधमां गतिम्।
एवं क्रोधान्वितो विप्रस्त्यक्तधर्माहिते रतः॥ ४५॥
क्रुद्धो नृशंसः परुष अविद्वांश्चाप्यधार्मिकः।
कुलानि पातयत्येव सप्त सप्त च राघव॥ ४६॥
verses.m: Thus honoured, the happy Brāhmaṇa went away riding on elephant-back. Then the ministers smilingly with astonishment, said to Śrī Rāma, “He has been given a boon. O resplendent one. This is not a curse.” Thus told by the ministers Śrī Rāma said: “You do not know the truth about the course of actions. The dog knows the reason (and will tell why the Brāhmaṇa has been made Kulapati).” On being asked thus by Śrī Rāma, the dog addressed the following speech: “I, In my previous birth, was the Kulapati of the same place, Kālañjara Maṭha. Partaking of the remains of sacrificial food, O Rāma ! I would be engaged in worshipping gods and Brāhmaṇas and gave to the male and maid-servants their due. I had a love for good things. I would protect the property dedicated to gods. I was modest and well-behaved and was engaged in doing good to all living beings. Even then I have been reduced to this wretched state and the lowest position. O Rāma! therefore such a Brāhmaṇa, who is irasible, who has given up his ‘Dharma’ and who is engaged in harming others, who is hot-tempered, ruthless, harsh, foolish (ignorant) and irreligious will lead to the downfall of fourteen generations. (40—46)

verses.text:
तस्मात् सर्वास्ववस्थासु कौलपत्यं न कारयेत्।
यमिच्छेन्नरकं नेतुं सपुत्रपशुबान्धवम्॥ ४७॥
देवेष्वधिष्ठितं कुर्याद् गोषु च ब्राह्मणेषु च।
ब्रह्मस्वं देवताद्रव्यं स्त्रीणां बालधनं च यत्॥ ४८॥
दत्तं हरति यो भूय इष्टैः सह विनश्यति।
ब्राह्मणद्रव्यमादत्ते देवानां चैव राघव॥ ४९॥
सद्यः पतति घोरे वै नरकेऽवीचिसंज्ञके।
मनसापि हि देवस्वं ब्रह्मस्वं च हरेत्तु यः॥ ५०॥
निरयान्निरयं चैव पतत्येव नराधमः।
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं रामो विस्मयोत्फुल्ललोचनः॥ ५१॥
श्वाप्यगच्छन्महातेजा यत एवागतस्ततः।
मनस्वी पूर्वजात्या स जातिमात्रोऽपदूषितः।
वाराणस्यां महाभागः प्रायं चोपविवेश ह॥ ५२॥
verses.m: “Therefore, one should not in any circumstances become a Kulapati. Only, he should be made to look after gods, cows and the Brāhmaṇas, whom one would wish to condemn to go to hell alongwith sons, cattle and relatives. One who takes away the property of the Brāhmaṇas, gods, women and children and takes back again what has been given away in charity, perishes alongwith one’s all dear ones. O Śrī Rāma! One who takes away the property belonging to the Brāhmaṇas and the gods, soon goes to the fearful hell known as ‘Avīci’ one who takes away even mentally the property belonging to the gods and the Brāhmaṇas, goes down from one hell to another.” On hearing the speech of the dog, the eyes of Śrī Rāma opened widely due to wonder, the dog, too possessed of lustre, went to place from where it had come. It was a high minded soul in its former birth but on being born as a dog it has been spoiled. The illustrious one sought death by abstaining from taking food in Vārāṇasī. (47—52)

verses.text:
तयोः संवदतोरेवं रामलक्ष्मणयोस्तदा।
वासन्तिकी निशा प्राप्ता न शीता न च घर्मदा॥ १॥
verses.m: Thus, as the day passed by with Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa conversing among themselves, the vernal night appeared, which was neither cold nor hot. (1)

verses.text:
ततः प्रभाते विमले कृतपूर्वाह्णिकक्रियः।
अभिचक्राम काकुत्स्थो दर्शनं पौरकार्यवित्॥ २॥
verses.m: After dawn in the morning, which was a clear one, having performed the morning duties, Śrī Rāma the scion of Kākutstha approached the place where he could see his subjects, desirous to know the activities of the citizens. (2)

verses.text:
ततः सुमन्त्रस्त्वागम्य राघवं वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
एते प्रतिहता राजन् द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति तापसाः॥ ३॥
verses.m: Then Sumantra, the charioteer, having come near Śrī Rāma, the scion of Raghus, spoke thus: ‘O King ! Some ascetics, not permited to enter, stand in need at the entrance door, (3)

verses.text:
भार्गवं च्यवनं चैव पुरस्कृत्य महर्षयः।
दर्शनं ते महाराज चोदयन्ति कृतत्वराः॥ ४॥
प्रीयमाणा नरव्याघ्र यमुनातीरवासिनः।
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा रामः प्रोवाच धर्मवित्॥ ५॥
प्रवेश्यन्तां महाभागा भार्गवप्रमुखा द्विजाः।
राज्ञस्त्वाज्ञां पुरस्कृत्य द्वाःस्थो मूर्ध्ना कृताञ्जलिः॥ ६॥
प्रवेशयामास तदा तापसान् सुदुरासदान्।
शतं समधिकं तत्र दीप्यमानं स्वतेजसा॥ ७॥
प्रविष्टं राजभवनं तापसानां महात्मनाम्।
ते द्विजाः पूर्णकलशैः सर्वतीर्थाम्बुसत्कृतैः॥ ८॥
गृहीत्वा फलमूलं च रामस्याभ्याहरन् बहु।
प्रतिगृह्य तु तत् सर्वं रामः प्रीतिपुरस्कृतः॥ ९॥
तीर्थोदकानि सर्वाणि फलानि विविधानि च।
उवाच च महाबाहुः सर्वानेव महामुनीन्॥ १०॥
verses.m: ‘O Tiger among men, Śrī Rāma, great Ṛṣis, who dwell at the banks of the Yamunā, and rejoice among themselves, placing Cyavana, the Bhārgava (son of Bhṛgu) at their head, implore us in haste for your audience’. Hearing him say so, Śrī Rāma the righteous one spoke: ‘Please let the Brāhmaṇas, headed by Bhārgava, enter.’ The charioteer then went near the door. Accepting the orders of the King, made the ascetics, who were unapproachable, enter: More than a hundred holy ascetics, glowing with their own lustre, entered the palace. Those Brāhmaṇas accompanied with pitchers full and sanctified with the waters of all the Tīrthas (pilgrimages), and with many fruits and roots offered them to Śrī Rāma. Accepting them, Śrī Rāma was pleased excessively getting the sacred waters of the Tīrthas and all kinds of fruits, He, Śrī Rāma, of long arms, then addressed all the great ascetics thus: (4—10)

verses.text:
इमान्यासनमुख्यानि यथार्हमुपविश्यताम्।
रामस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा सर्व एव महर्षयः॥ ११॥
बृसीषु रुचिराख्यासु निषेदुः काञ्चनीषु ते।
उपविष्टानृषींस्तत्र दृष्ट्वा परपुरंजयः।
प्रयतः प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा राघवो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “These are the special seats, please be seated as it sults you”. Hearing the words of Śrī Rāma all the great Ṛṣis seated themselves on the lovely golden cushions. Seeing them thus seated, the conqueror of the strongholds of enemies, the scion of the Raghus, serenly with joined hands uttered these words: (11-12)

verses.text:
किमागमनकार्यं वः किं करोमि समाहितः।
आज्ञाप्योऽहं महर्षीणां सर्वकामकरः सुखम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: ‘For what purpose do you come here, what should I perform for you. I am at your command. I shall happily perform all that is desired by you. (13)

verses.text:
इदं राज्यं च सकलं जीवितं च हृदि स्थितम्।
सर्वमेतद् द्विजार्थं मे सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि वः॥ १४॥
verses.m: ‘This kingdom, my entire life, and even what dwells in my heart, all that is for the Brāhmaṇas, I speak to you the truth’. (14)

verses.text:
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा साधुकारो महानभूत्।
ऋषीणामुग्रतपसां यमुनातीरवासिनाम्॥ १५॥
ऊचुश्चैव महात्मानो हर्षेण महता वृताः।
उपपन्नं नरश्रेष्ठ तवैव भुवि नान्यतः॥ १६॥
verses.m: Hearing these words of Śrī Rāma and His prolonged proclamation, the Ṛṣis, who were performing right penances and dwelling on the banks of the Yamunā, arose. In great joy the noble ones said: ‘O best among men, this befits you alone in this world, and none other. (15-16)

verses.text:
बहवः पार्थिवा राजन्नतिक्रान्ता महाबलाः।
कार्यस्य गौरवं मत्वा प्रतिज्ञां नाभ्यरोचयन्॥ १७॥
verses.m: ‘Many powerful kings have gone by, who looking at the greatness of our task, never desired to promise to fulfil them. (17)

verses.text:
त्वया पुनर्ब्राह्मणगौरवादियं
कृता प्रतिज्ञा ह्यनवेक्ष्य कारणम्।
ततश्च कर्ता ह्यसि नात्र संशयो
महाभयात् त्रातुमृषींस्त्वमर्हसि॥ १८॥
verses.m: ‘Respecting Brāhmaṇas you made promise, without having a second thought about the task. No doubt, therefore you will dispell all fears that haunt Ṛṣis.’ (18)

verses.text:
ब्रुवद्भिरेवमृषिभिः काकुत्स्थो वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
किं कार्यं ब्रूत मुनयो भयं तावदपैतु वः॥ १॥
verses.m: As the Ṛṣis spoke thus, Śrī Rāma the scion of Kakutstha said: ‘O ascetics, speak out the task that I should perform, so as your fear may be dispelled’. (1)

verses.text:
तथा ब्रुवति काकुत्स्थे भार्गवो वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
भयानां शृणु यन्मूलं देशस्य च नरेश्वर॥ २॥
verses.m: When the scion of Kakutstha spoke these words, Bhārgava replied: ‘O best among men! hark ! what causes fear to us and the country. (2)

verses.text:
पूर्वं कृतयुगे राजन् दैतेयः सुमहामतिः।
लोलापुत्रोऽभवज्ज्येष्ठो मधुर्नाम महासुरः॥ ३॥
verses.m: ‘Formerly, in the Kṛtayuga, O king ! In Kṛtayuga, Madhu from the Daitya clan, the wise and great Asura was the eldest son of Lolā. (3)

verses.text:
ब्रह्मण्यश्च शरण्यश्च बुद्ध्या च परिनिष्ठितः।
सुरैश्च परमोदारैः प्रीतिस्तस्यातुलाभवत्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “He was respectful to Brāhmaṇas and was also a source of refuge and well-composed of mind. His relations with the very gracious gods were incomparably cordial. (4)

verses.text:
स मधुर्वीर्यसम्पन्नो धर्मं च सुसमाहितः।
बहुमानाच्च रुद्रेण दत्तस्तस्याद्भुतो वरः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “That Madhu, although possessed of might, was well-established in the path of righteousness; and was given by Rudra, Mahādeva, a wonderful boon, because of his respect for the Devas. (5)

verses.text:
शूलं शूलाद् विनिष्कृष्य महावीर्यं महाप्रभम्।
ददौ महात्मा सुप्रीतो वाक्यं चैतदुवाच ह॥ ६॥
verses.m: “The great Mahādeva produced a most powerful and luminous trident from his own trident, being excessively pleased, gave it to him and said these words: (6)

verses.text:
त्वयायमतुलो धर्मो मत्प्रसादकरः कृतः।
प्रीत्या परमया युक्तो ददाम्यायुधमुत्तमम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “By your unparalleled right conduct, you have earned my pleasure: so highly pleased, I give you this excellent weapon. (7)

verses.text:
यावत् सुरैश्च विप्रैश्च न विरुध्येर्महासुर।
तावच्छूलं तवेदं स्यादन्यथा नाशमेष्यति॥ ८॥
verses.m: “As long as you do not oppose the Brāhmaṇas and the gods (Devas), this trident of yours will retain its power, otherwise it will perish. (8)

verses.text:
यश्च त्वामभियुञ्जीत युद्धाय विगतज्वरः।
तं शूलो भस्मसात्कृत्वा पुनरेष्यति ते करम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Whosoever fearlessly encounters you in battle, the trident will reduce him to ashes and return to your hand.” (9)

verses.text:
एवं रुद्राद् वरं लब्ध्वा भूय एव महासुरः।
प्रणिपत्य महादेवं वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Thus having obtained the boon from Lord Śiva, the great Asura on his part made obeisance to Mahādeva and also said: (10)

verses.text:
भगवन् मम वंशस्य शूलमेतदनुत्तमम्।
भवेत् तु सततं देव सुराणामीश्वरो ह्यसि॥ ११॥
verses.m: ‘O Lord, may this unparalleled trident, belong to my race forever. O God, You are the Lord of the all dieties.’ (11)

verses.text:
तं ब्रुवाणं मधुं देवः सर्वभूतपतिः शिवः।
प्रत्युवाच महादेवो नैतदेवं भविष्यति॥ १२॥
verses.m: The Mahādeva, Śiva, the Lord of all, replied to Madhu, ‘This cannot be so. (12)

verses.text:
मा भूत् ते विफला वाणी मत्प्रसादकृता शुभा।
भवतः पुत्रमेकं तु शूलमेतद् भविष्यति॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Though the sentence uttered by me out of pleasure, however, will not go in vain for you: this trident will belong to one of your sons. (13)

verses.text:
यावत् करस्थः शूलोऽयं भविष्यति सुतस्य ते।
अवध्यः सर्वभूतानां शूलहस्तो भविष्यति॥ १४॥
verses.m: “As long as this trident will remain in the hand of your son, he will be unassailable by all beings.” (14)

verses.text:
एवं मधुर्वरं लब्ध्वा देवात् सुमहदद्भुतम्।
भवनं सोऽसुरश्रेष्ठः कारयामास सुप्रभम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Thus having obtained the great and wonderful boon from Mahādeva, Madhu, the greatest among the Asuras, got a palace full of brilliance built. (15)

verses.text:
तस्य पत्नी महाभागा प्रिया कुम्भीनसीति या।
विश्वावसोरपत्यं साप्यनलायां महाप्रभा॥ १६॥
verses.m: ‘His dear wife, the famous beautiful Kumbhīnasī, the daughter of Viśvāvasu, was born from Analā. (16)

verses.text:
तस्याः पुत्रो महावीर्यो लवणो नाम दारुणः।
बाल्यात्प्रभृति दुष्टात्मा पापान्येव समाचरत्॥ १७॥
verses.m: ‘Her son, the powerful and cruel one, Lavaṇa by name, was wicked since childhood and performed only evil deeds. (17)

verses.text:
तं पुत्रं दुर्विनीतं तु दृष्ट्वा क्रोधसमन्वितः।
मधुः स शोकमापेदे न चैनं किंचिदब्रवीत्॥ १८॥
verses.m: ‘Seeing this son so wicked, Madhu was enraged and grieved, but did not say to him anything. (18)

verses.text:
स विहाय इमं लोकं प्रविष्टो वरुणालयम्।
शूलं निवेश्य लवणे वरं तस्मै न्यवेदयत्॥ १९॥
verses.m: ‘He entered the ocean, leaving this world, handing over the trident to Lavaṇa and conveying him the power of the boon. (19)

verses.text:
स प्रभावेण शूलस्य दौरात्म्येनात्मनस्तथा।
संतापयति लोकांस्त्रीन् विशेषेण च तापसान्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “He (Lavaṇa) by the power of the trident and with his wickedness, caused much trouble to the three worlds, especially the ascetics. (20)

verses.text:
एवंप्रभावो लवणः शूलं चैव तथाविधम्।
श्रुत्वा प्रमाणं काकुत्स्थ त्वं हि नः परमा गतिः॥ २१॥
verses.m: ‘So mighty is Lavaṇa and such is the trident. O scion of Kakutstha. Now you have heard; so it is up to you to do what is necessary, you are our ultimate resort. (21)

verses.text:
बहवः पार्थिवा राम भयार्तैर्ऋषिभिः पुरा।
अभयं याचिता वीर त्रातारं न च विद्महे॥ २२॥
verses.m: ‘Formerly many kings, O powerful one, were approached for protection by the Ṛṣis frightened, but we did not find any protector. (22)

verses.text:
ते वयं रावणं श्रुत्वा हतं सबलवाहनम्।
त्रातारं विद्महे तात नान्यं भुवि नराधिपम्।
तत् परित्रातुमिच्छामो लवणाद् भयपीडितान्॥ २३॥
verses.m: ‘So now, having heard of Rāvaṇa killed alongwith his army, O dear one, we do not consider any other king on this earth as protector, and thus we desire protection for those who are persecuted by Lavaṇa.(23)

verses.text:
इति राम निवेदितं तु ते
भयजं कारणमुत्थितं च यत्।
विनिवारयितुं भवान् क्षमः
कुरु तं काममहीनविक्रम॥ २४॥
verses.m: ‘Thus, we have conveyed to you, O Rāma of unfailing power, that fear and cause of that fear. We know, you can ward off that; do something.’ (24)

verses.text:
तथोक्ते तानृषीन् रामः प्रत्युवाच कृताञ्जलिः।
किमाहारः किमाचारो लवणः क्व च वर्तते॥ १॥
verses.m: When the Ṛṣis had thus spoken to Him, Śrī Rāma with folded hands replied: ‘What does he (Lavaṇa) take as his food, of what conduct is he and where does he stay?’ (1)

verses.text:
राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा ऋषयः सर्व एव ते।
ततो निवेदयामासुर्लवणो ववृधे यथा॥ २॥
verses.m: Hearing these words of Śrī Rāma, all those Ṛṣis then conveyed to Him how Lavaṇa fared. (2)

verses.text:
आहारः सर्वसत्त्वानि विशेषेण च तापसाः।
आचारो रौद्रता नित्यं वासो मधुवने तथा॥ ३॥
verses.m: His food comprises all beings, specially ascetics. His conduct is full of cruelty, every moment. His residence is in Madhuvana. (3)

verses.text:
हत्वा बहुसहस्राणि सिंहव्याघ्रमृगाण्डजान्।
मानुषांश्चैव कुरुते नित्यमाहारमाह्निकम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Having killed many thousands of lions, tigers, deers and birds and also human beings, he makes his daily meals of them. (4)

verses.text:
ततोऽन्तराणि सत्त्वानि खादते स महाबलः।
संहारे समनुप्राप्ते व्यादितास्य इवान्तकः॥ ५॥
verses.m: Then all other types of beings too, the mighty Lavaṇa devoures as if he was Death, with open mouth at the time. (5)

verses.text:
तच्छ्रुत्वा राघवो वाक्यमुवाच स महामुनीन्।
घातयिष्यामि तद् रक्षो व्यपगच्छतु वो भयम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: Hearing this, the scion of Raghu (Śrī Rāma) said to the great ascetics: ‘I shall kill that Rākṣasa, may your fears be dispelled.’ (6)

verses.text:
प्रतिज्ञाय तथा तेषां मुनीनामुग्रतेजसाम्।
स भ्रातॄन् सहितान् सर्वानुवाच रघुनन्दनः॥ ७॥
verses.m: Thus having promised to the ascetics, possessed of great vigour, that descendant of the Raghus, Śrī Rāma, spoke to his brothers altogether. (7)

verses.text:
को हन्ता लवणं वीरः कस्यांशः स विधीयताम्।
भरतस्य महाबाहोः शत्रुघ्नस्य च धीमतः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Who the brave shall kill Lavaṇa, to whom shall Lavaṇa be assigned, to long-armed Bharata or Śatrughna, the wise one?’ (8)

verses.text:
राघवेणैवमुक्तस्तु भरतो वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
अहमेनं वधिष्यामि ममांशः स विधीयताम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: When Śrī Rāma spoke thus, Bharata said: ‘I shall kill him. Kindly assign him to me’. (9)

verses.text:
भरतस्य वचः श्रुत्वा धैर्यशौर्यसमन्वितम्।
लक्ष्मणावरजस्तस्थौ हित्वा सौवर्णमासनम्॥ १०॥
शत्रुघ्नस्त्वब्रवीद् वाक्यं प्रणिपत्य नराधिपम्।
कृतकर्मा महाबाहुर्मध्यमो रघुनन्दन॥ ११॥
verses.m: Hearing the words of Bharata, (Śatrughna) younger brother of Lakṣmaṇa, stood up leaving his golden seat. Having bowed to the King, Śrī Rāma, Śatrughna said: The middle one, Bharata, among us, possessed of long arms, O descendant of Raghu, has already performed his share. (10-11)

verses.text:
आर्येण हि पुरा शून्या त्वयोध्या परिपालिता।
संतापं हृदये कृत्वा आर्यस्यागमनं प्रति॥ १२॥
verses.m: ‘He protected Ayodhyā in your absence undergoing so much mental agony, awaiting your arrival. (12)

verses.text:
दुःखानि च बहूनीह अनुभूतानि पार्थिव।
शयानो दुःखशय्यासु नन्दिग्रामे महायशाः॥ १३॥
फलमूलाशनो भूत्वा जटी चीरधरस्तथा।
अनुभूयेदृशं दुःखमेष राघवनन्दनः॥ १४॥
verses.m: ‘Here many sufferings were endured by him, O king: sleeping on uncomfortable bed in the Nandigrāma, this noble one consuming only fruits and roots, with matted hair, and dress of bark, has greatly experienced sorrow, O descendant of the Raghus. (13-14)

verses.text:
प्रेष्ये मयि स्थिते राजन् न भूयः क्लेशमाप्नुयात्।
तथा ब्रुवति शत्रुघ्ने राघवः पुनरब्रवीत्॥ १५॥
verses.m: ‘While I, the servant, am available, Bharata should not again be put to trouble. After Śatrughna said so, Śrī Rāma, the scion of the Raghus again spoke these words: (15)

verses.text:
एवं भवतु काकुत्स्थ क्रियतां मम शासनम्।
राज्ये त्वामभिषेक्ष्यामि मधोस्तु नगरे शुभे॥ १६॥
निवेशय महाबाहो भरतं यद्यवेक्षसे।
शूरस्त्वं कृतविद्यश्च समर्थश्च निवेशने॥ १७॥
नगरं यमुनाजुष्टं तथा जनपदान् शुभान्।
यो हि वंशं समुत्पाट्य पार्थिवस्य निवेशने॥ १८॥
न विधत्ते नृपं तत्र नरकं स हि गच्छति।
स त्वं हत्वा मधुसुतं लवणं पापनिश्चयम्॥ १९॥
राज्यं प्रशाधि धर्मेण वाक्यं मे यद्यवेक्षसे।
उत्तरं च न वक्तव्यं शूर वाक्यान्तरे मम॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Be it so, O Śatrughna (descendant of Kakutstha), carry out my orders, I shall consecrate you on the holy kingdom of Madhu. Establish the throne. Bharata be here. O one of long arms, if you consider it proper, You are brave and proficient, and also have the ability to establish a new city. Founding a city close to Yamunā, and many provinces of auspicious fame, one who having reduced a royal house in that very city, does not install a king there, indeed goes to hell. Therefore, you, having killed Lavaṇa, the son of Madhu, possessed of evil designs, rule over that kingdom. If you follow my words, then, O brave one, carry on the administration righteously, without making any argument or disobeying me.’ (16—20)

verses.text:
बालेन पूर्वजस्याज्ञा कर्तव्या नात्र संशयः।
अभिषेकं च काकुत्स्थ प्रतीच्छस्व ममोद्यतम्।
वसिष्ठप्रमुखैर्विप्रैर्विधिमन्त्रपुरस्कृतम् ॥ २१॥
verses.m: The elders must be obeyed by youngers there is no doubt about it. Please approve of the consecration, to be performed by me, accompained by the Mantras, sacred chants of the Brāhmaṇas headed by Śrī Vasiṣṭha, in prescribed manner. (21)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण परां व्रीडामुपागमत्।
शत्रुघ्नो वीर्यसम्पन्नो मन्दं मन्दमुवाच ह॥ १॥
verses.m: After Śrī Rāma said so, the mighty Śatrughna felt very much ashamed and spoke gently: (1)

verses.text:
अधर्मं विद्म काकुत्स्थ अस्मिन्नर्थे नरेश्वर।
कथं तिष्ठत्सु ज्येष्ठेषु कनीयानभिषिच्यते॥ २॥
verses.m: ‘O king, the descendent of Kakutstha, this transaction seems to me as against Dharma, how can a junior be consecrated on the throne, superseding the elders? (2)

verses.text:
अवश्यं करणीयं च शासनं पुरुषर्षभ।
तव चैव महाभाग शासनं दुरतिक्रमम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: ‘On the other hand, your orders must be carried out at any cost as it is impossible to supersede them. (3)

verses.text:
त्वत्तो मया श्रुतं वीर श्रुतिभ्यश्च मया श्रुतम्।
नोत्तरं हि मया वाच्यं मध्यमे प्रतिजानति॥ ४॥
verses.m: ‘I have heard from you, as well as from the Śrutis, O brave one! that I should not have said anything after the middle brother, Bharata, had already taken a vow. (4)

verses.text:
व्याहृतं दुर्वचो घोरं हन्तास्मि लवणं मृधे।
तस्यैवं मे दुरुक्तस्य दुर्गतिः पुरुषर्षभ॥ ५॥
verses.m: ‘It is most unfortunate that I have said something improper: ‘I will kill Lavaṇa in battle’. I think I have been put in this unenviable position as a result of my saying so. (5)

verses.text:
उत्तरं नहि वक्तव्यं ज्येष्ठेनाभिहिते पुनः।
अधर्मसहितं चैव परलोकविवर्जितम्॥ ६॥
सोऽहं द्वितीयं काकुत्स्थ न वक्ष्यामीति चोत्तरम्।
मा द्वितीयेन दण्डो वै निपतेन्मयि मानद॥ ७॥
verses.m: ‘When the elder one says something, the younger should not make a reply. Violation would be against the norms of Dharma and spoil the other world. Therefore, O Kakutstha, I will not speak anything again. O giver of respect, may I not be importuned for the punishment second time. (6-7)

verses.text:
कामकारो ह्यहं राजंस्तवास्मि पुरुषर्षभ।
अधर्मं जहि काकुत्स्थ मत्कृते रघुनन्दन॥ ८॥
verses.m: ‘O king, the best among persons and delighter of Raghus, I will follow your wishes but whatever wrongful happens in it from me, you please destroy it. I shall act according to your desire, O bull among men. Please leave out for my sake that which is unlawful, O scion of Kakutstha, descendant of the Raghus!’ (8)

verses.text:
एवमुक्ते तु शूरेण शत्रुघ्नेन महात्मना।
उवाच रामः संहृष्टो भरतं लक्ष्मणं तथा॥ ९॥
verses.m: After these words being uttered by the wise and the brave Śatrughna, Śrī Rāma was pleased and He spoke to Bharata and Lakṣmaṇa: (9)

verses.text:
सम्भारानभिषेकस्य आनयध्वं समाहिताः।
अद्यैव पुरुषव्याघ्रमभिषेक्ष्यामि राघवम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: ‘Bring forth all the requisites of consecration, this very day. I shall consecrate the scion of the Raghus, the tiger among men, Śatrughna. (10)

verses.text:
पुरोधसं च काकुत्स्थ नैगमानृत्विजस्तथा।
मन्त्रिणश्चैव तान् सर्वानानयध्वं ममाज्ञया॥ ११॥
verses.m: ‘By my orders, call all of them, the chief priest, Vasiṣṭha, the townsmen, and other priests and also the councillors.’(11)

verses.text:
राज्ञः शासनमाज्ञाय तथाकुर्वन्महारथाः।
अभिषेकसमारम्भं पुरस्कृत्य पुरोधसम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: Following the orders of the king, the great warriors, brought the necessary pūjā materials for the consecration, making the chief priest Vasiṣṭha play the prominent role. (12)

verses.text:
प्रविष्टा राजभवनं राजानो ब्राह्मणास्तथा।
ततोऽभिषेको ववृधे शत्रुघ्नस्य महात्मनः॥ १३॥
verses.m: The Kings and the Brāhmaṇas entered the royal palace; thus the consecration of the noble Śatrughna went on. (13)

verses.text:
सम्प्रहर्षकरः श्रीमान् राघवस्य पुरस्य च।
अभिषिक्तस्तु काकुत्स्थो बभौ चादित्यसंनिभः॥ १४॥
अभिषिक्तः पुरा स्कन्दः सेन्द्रैरिव दिवौकसैः।
अभिषिक्ते तु शत्रुघ्ने रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा॥ १५॥
पौराः प्रमुदिताश्चासन् ब्राह्मणाश्च बहुश्रुताः।
कौसल्या च सुमित्रा च मङ्गलं केकयी तथा॥ १६॥
चक्रुस्ता राजभवने याश्चान्या राजयोषितः।
ऋषयश्च महात्मानो यमुनातीरवासिनः॥ १७॥
हतं लवणमाशंसुः शत्रुघ्नस्याभिषेचनात्।
ततोऽभिषिक्तं शत्रुघ्नमङ्कमारोप्य राघवः।
उवाच मधुरां वाणीं तेजस्तस्याभिपूरयन्॥ १८॥
verses.m: The venerable scion of Kakutstha, when consecrated, shown as the sun and brought great joy to the descendant of Raghu (Rāma) and also to the citizens, as Skanda (Kārtikeya) when consecrated in the old days by the gods together with Indra. As Śatrughna was consecrated by Śrī Rāma, the citizens were happy and so also the learned Brāhmaṇas. Kausalyā, Sumitrā, Kaikeyī and all other king mothers performed auspicious acts in the royal palace. The noble Ṛṣis dwelling on the banks of the Yamunā were confident that Lavaṇa was as if dead due to the consecration of Śatrughna. Then the scion of the Raghus, Śrī Rāma, placing Śatrughna on His lap uttered these sweet words enhancing his power. (14—18)

verses.text:
अयं शरस्त्वमोघस्ते दिव्यः परपुरंजयः।
अनेन लवणं सौम्य हन्तासि रघुनन्दन॥ १९॥
verses.m: ‘I give you this divine arrow, which is unfailing and conquers the foes, O descendant of Raghu. O handsome one, you will kill Lavaṇa with this arrow. (19)

verses.text:
सृष्टः शरोऽयं काकुत्स्थ यदा शेते महार्णवे।
स्वयंभूरजितो दिव्यो यं नापश्यन् सुरासुराः॥ २०॥
verses.m: ‘This arrow was created O scion of Kakutstha, when the self-born unconquerable God, Viṣṇu, was reclining in the great ocean, whom the gods and the demons could not see. (20)

verses.text:
अदृश्यः सर्वभूतानां तेनायं हि शरोत्तमः।
सृष्टः क्रोधाभिभूतेन विनाशार्थं दुरात्मनोः॥ २१॥
मधुकैटभयोर्वीर विघाते सर्वरक्षसाम्।
स्रष्टुकामेन लोकांस्त्रींस्तौ चानेन हतौ युधि॥ २२॥
तौ हत्वा जनभोगार्थे कैटभं तु मधुं तथा।
अनेन शरमुख्येन ततो लोकांश्चकार सः॥ २३॥
verses.m: ‘Therefore, this one, the best among arrows, is invisible to all beings, this was created by angry Viṣṇu, desirous of the destruction of the two wicked ones, Madhu and Kaiṭabha, and creation of the three worlds after the two and the other Rākṣasas were killed with this arrow. (21—23)

verses.text:
नायं मया शरः पूर्वं रावणस्य वधार्थिना।
मुक्तः शत्रुघ्न भूतानां महान् ह्रासो भवेदिति॥ २४॥
verses.m: ‘This arrow was not shot by me formerly even to kill Rāvaṇa (the king of the Rākṣasas), O Śatrughna, for that would have caused the great destruction of other beings too. (24)

verses.text:
यच्च तस्य महच्छूलं त्र्यम्बकेण महात्मना।
दत्तं शत्रुविनाशाय मधोरायुधमुत्तमम्॥ २५॥
तत् संनिक्षिप्य भवने पूज्यमानं पुनः पुनः।
दिशः सर्वाः समासाद्य प्राप्नोत्याहारमुत्तमम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: ‘The great trident, the best among weapons, that was given to Madhu by the mighty three-eyed Lord Śiva for the purpose of destroying the foes; placing that honourable weapon at home, Lavaṇa proceeding to all quarters repeatedly acquires the best of his food. (25-26)

verses.text:
यदा तु युद्धमाकाङ्क्षन् कश्चिदेनं समाह्वयेत्।
तदा शूलं गृहीत्वा तु भस्म रक्षः करोति हि॥ २७॥
verses.m: ‘Whenever, desirous of struggle one per chance challanges him, then the Rākṣasa, Lavaṇa, taking hold of this trident reduces him indeed to ashes. (27)

verses.text:
स त्वं पुरुषशार्दूल तमायुधविनाकृतम्।
अप्रविष्टं पुरं पूर्वं द्वारि तिष्ठ धृतायुधः॥ २८॥
verses.m: ‘So you, O lion among men, accompanied with the weapon (arrow), stay at the eastern gate, and fight with him, dispossessed of the weapon (trident) and unable to enter the city. (28)

verses.text:
अप्रविष्टं च भवनं युद्धाय पुरुषर्षभ।
आह्वयेथा महाबाहो ततो हन्तासि राक्षसम्॥ २९॥
verses.m: ‘O one of long arms ! Challenge him to fight before he has entered his residence; then you shall kill the Rākṣasa. (29)

verses.text:
अन्यथा क्रियमाणे तु ह्यवध्यः स भविष्यति।
यदि त्वेवं कृतं वीर विनाशमुपयास्यति॥ ३०॥
verses.m: ‘If it is not so done, then, indeed, he will be unassailable, but if this is so done, then, O brave one, Lavaṇa will be destroyed. (30)

verses.text:
एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं शूलस्य च विपर्ययः।
श्रीमतः शितिकण्ठस्य कृत्यं हि दुरतिक्रमम्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: ‘Thus, all has been narrated to you, and also the warding off of the trident, the doings of the blue-throated Śiva are indeed difficult to overcome.’ (31)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा च काकुत्स्थं प्रशस्य च पुनः पुनः।
पुनरेवापरं वाक्यमुवाच रघुनन्दनः॥ १॥
verses.m: Having thus spoken to the scion of Kakutstha and eulogizing him again and again, the descendant of the Raghus, Śrī Rāma, spoke again to him: (1)

verses.text:
इमान्यश्वसहस्राणि चत्वारि पुरुषर्षभ।
रथानां द्वे सहस्रे च गजानां शतमुत्तमम्॥ २॥
अन्तरापणवीथ्यश्च नानापण्योपशोभिताः।
अनुगच्छन्तु काकुत्स्थं तथैव नटनर्तकाः॥ ३॥
verses.m: ‘These four thousand of horses, two thousand chariots and a hundred of the best elephants, the rows of stalls (inside the city), laden with goods for sale and purchase, may follow you O Śatrughna, the scion of Kakutstha and so also the actors and dancers. O Śatrughna, O bull among men, having taken a lac of pure gold-coins well-equipped with wealth and carriers (elephants and horses), you proceed to Madhurā. (2-3)

verses.text:
हिरण्यस्य सुवर्णस्य नियुतं पुरुषर्षभ।
आदाय गच्छ शत्रुघ्न पर्याप्तधनवाहनः॥ ४॥
बलं च सुभृतं वीर हृष्टतुष्टमनुद्धतम्।
सम्भाषासम्प्रदानेन रञ्जयस्व नरोत्तम॥ ५॥
verses.m: ‘O brave one, keep the army that is well-formed, in such good cheer that its constituents are happy and satisfied, and not arrogant, with your good words. (4-5)

verses.text:
नह्यर्थास्तत्र तिष्ठन्ति न दारा न च बान्धवाः।
सुप्रीतो भृत्यवर्गस्तु यत्र तिष्ठति राघव॥ ६॥
verses.m: ‘There (at the encounter) neither wealth nor spouse, nor even relatives are at your side, as the servants when kept happy. (6)

verses.text:
अतो हृष्टजनाकीर्णां प्रस्थाप्य महतीं चमूम्।
एक एव धनुष्पाणिर्गच्छ त्वं मधुनो वनम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: ‘Thus, having dispatched the mighty army full of happy men, you alone, with bow in your hand, can go to the forest of Madhu. (7)

verses.text:
यथा त्वां न प्रजानाति गच्छन्तं युद्धकाङ्क्षिणम्।
लवणस्तु मधोः पुत्रस्तथा गच्छेरशङ्कितम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: ‘You should go in a manner in which the son of Madhu, Lavaṇa does not know that you are going to him for an encounter. (8)

verses.text:
न तस्य मृत्युरन्योऽस्ति कश्चिद्धि पुरुषर्षभ।
दर्शनं योऽभिगच्छेत स वध्यो लवणेन हि॥ ९॥
verses.m: ‘O bull among men, there is indeed no other way in which Lavaṇa would die, whosoever goes to attack him, is killed by Lavaṇa, indeed. (9)

verses.text:
स ग्रीष्म अपयाते तु वर्षारात्र उपागते।
हन्यास्त्वं लवणं सौम्य स हि कालोऽस्य दुर्मतेः॥ १०॥
verses.m: ‘Thus when summer is passed, and the rainy season comes, you should kill Lavaṇa. O graceful one, that is the time of death for this wicked one. (10)

verses.text:
महर्षींस्तु पुरस्कृत्य प्रयान्तु तव सैनिकाः।
यथा ग्रीष्मावशेषेण तरेयुर्जाह्नवीजलम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: ‘Your warriors may proceed with the great Ṛṣis at their head, so that by the end of the summer season, they may cross the Gaṅgā, the daughter of Jāhnu. (11)

verses.text:
तत्र स्थाप्य बलं सर्वं नदीतीरे समाहितः।
अग्रतो धनुषा सार्धं गच्छ त्वं लघुविक्रम॥ १२॥
verses.m: ‘Then having stationed your army at the banks there, O one of speedy steps, you go ahead carefully alone with the bow.’ (12)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण शत्रुघ्नस्तान् महाबलान्।
सेनामुख्यान् समानीय ततो वाक्यमुवाच ह॥ १३॥
verses.m: Thus being spoken to by Śrī Rāma, Śatrughna, having gathered together the brave chiefs of the army spoke thus to them: (13)

verses.text:
एते वो गणिता वासा यत्र तत्र निवत्स्यथ।
स्थातव्यं चाविरोधेन यथा बाधा न कस्यचित्॥ १४॥
verses.m: ‘These are the decided places where you can dwell, according to your liking; wherever you are stay amicably.’ (14)

verses.text:
तथा तांस्तु समाज्ञाप्य प्रस्थाप्य च महद्बलम्।
कौसल्यां च सुमित्रां च कैकेयीं चाभ्यवादयत्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Thus ordering them and despatching the mighty army, he made obeisance to Kausalyā, Sumitrā and Kaikeyī. (15)

verses.text:
रामं प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य शिरसाभिप्रणम्य च।
लक्ष्मणं भरतं चैव प्रणिपत्य कृताञ्जलिः॥ १६॥
पुरोहितं वसिष्ठं च शत्रुघ्नः प्रयतात्मवान्।
रामेण चाभ्यनुज्ञातः शत्रुघ्नः शत्रुतापनः।
प्रदक्षिणमथो कृत्वा निर्जगाम महाबलः॥ १७॥
verses.m: Paying salutation to Śrī Rāma with his head and going round Him, and falling at the feet of Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata, and the chief priest Vasiṣṭha, Śatrughna of pious mind, the torturer of the foes, the mighty one going round Śrī Rāma again, departed. (16-17)

verses.text:
प्रस्थाप्य सेनामथ सोऽग्रतस्तदा
गजेन्द्रवाजिप्रवरौघसंकुलाम्।
उवास मासं तु नरेन्द्रपार्श्वत-
स्त्वथ प्रयातो रघुवंशवर्धनः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Sending ahead the army then, full of elephants and horses, he himself lived there with Śrī Rāma for a month and then he too started. (18)

verses.text:
प्रस्थाप्य च बलं सर्वं मासमात्रोषितः पथि।
एक एवाशु शत्रुघ्नो जगाम त्वरितं तदा॥ १॥
verses.m: Despatching the entire army, residing for a month only in Ayodhyā on his way, Śatrughna alone proceeded in haste. (1)

verses.text:
द्विरात्रमन्तरे शूर उष्य राघवनन्दनः।
वाल्मीकेराश्रमं पुण्यमगच्छद् वासमुत्तमम्॥ २॥
verses.m: After spending two nights on the way, Śatrughna, descendant of the Raghus, reached the holy hermitage of Vālmīki, the best of the places to dwell. (2)

verses.text:
सोऽभिवाद्य महात्मानं वाल्मीकिं मुनिसत्तमम्।
कृताञ्जलिरथो भूत्वा वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह॥ ३॥
verses.m: Śatrughna after saluting him with folded hands spoke these words to Vālmīki, the best among the ascetics: (3)

verses.text:
भगवन् वस्तुमिच्छामि गुरोः कृत्यादिहागतः।
श्वः प्रभाते गमिष्यामि प्रतीचीं वारुणीं दिशम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: ‘Sir, I desire to stay here; I have come for a mighty purpose. I shall go tomorrow morning to the west, the quarter of Varuṇa.’ (4)

verses.text:
शत्रुघ्नस्य वचः श्रुत्वा प्रहस्य मुनिपुङ्गवः।
प्रत्युवाच महात्मानं स्वागतं ते महायशः॥ ५॥
verses.m: Having heard those words of Śatrughna, the best among the ascetics, Vālmīki, said cheerfully to him (Śatrughna), the noble one: “Welcome to thee, O famous one. (5)

verses.text:
स्वमाश्रममिदं सौम्य राघवाणां कुलस्य वै।
आसनं पाद्यमर्घ्यं च निर्विशङ्कः प्रतीच्छ मे॥ ६॥
verses.m: “O gracious one, this hermitage is indeed your own, the family of the descendants of Raghu. Accept without hesitation the Pādya (ablutions of the foot), Arghya and the seat offered by me.” (6)

verses.text:
प्रतिगृह्य तदा पूजां फलमूलं च भोजनम्।
भक्षयामास काकुत्स्थस्तृप्तिं च परमां गतः॥ ७॥
verses.m: Accepting then the homage and the fruits and the roots, the scion of Kakutstha, took the food and was fully satisfied. (7)

verses.text:
स भुक्त्वा फलमूलं च महर्षिं तमुवाच ह।
पूर्वा यज्ञविभूतीयं कस्याश्रमसमीपतः॥ ८॥
verses.m: Having taken the fruits and the roots, he (Śatrughna) said to that great Ṛṣi: ‘To whom belong all these accoutrements of sacrifice that are seen on the eastern side, close to the hermitage’ (8)

verses.text:
तत् तस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा वाल्मीकिर्वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
शत्रुघ्न शृणु यस्येदं बभूवायतनं पुरा॥ ९॥
verses.m: Hearing these words of Śatrughna, Vālmīki spoke out: “O Śatrughna! listen as to whom this place of sacrifice belonged formerly. (9)

verses.text:
युष्माकं पूर्वको राजा सुदासस्तस्य भूपतेः।
पुत्रो वीरसहो नाम वीर्यवानतिधार्मिकः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Among your ancestors there was Saudāsa, and of that king, was a son named Vīrasaha, who was very brave and extremely pious. (10)

verses.text:
स बाल एव सौदासो मृगयामुपचक्रमे।
चञ्चूर्यमाणं ददृशे स शूरो राक्षसद्वयम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Although young, yet valiant Saudāsa went out for hunting in forest and saw two Rākṣasas roaming about. (11)

verses.text:
शार्दूलरूपिणौ घोरौ मृगान् बहुसहस्रशः।
भक्षमाणावसंतुष्टौ पर्याप्तिं नैव जग्मतुः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Those two Rākṣasas assuming the dreadful shape of the lion and devouring many thousands of animals, yet they were still unsatiated. (12)

verses.text:
स तु तौ राक्षसौ दृष्ट्वा निर्मृगं च वनं कृतम्।
क्रोधेन महताविष्टो जघानैकं महेषुणा॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Seeing those two Rākṣasas and the forest devoid of animals, he, Saudāsa, was enraged and killed one of them with a mighty shaft. (13)

verses.text:
विनिपात्य तमेकं तु सौदासः पुरुषर्षभः।
विज्वरो विगतामर्षो हतं रक्षो ह्युदैक्षत॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Having killed one of the Rākṣasas the bull among men, Saudāsa, without worry and anger looked at the slain Rākṣasa. (14)

verses.text:
निरीक्षमाणं तं दृष्ट्वा सहायं तस्य रक्षसः।
संतापमकरोद् घोरं सौदासं चेदमब्रवीत्॥ १५॥
यस्मादनपराधं तं सहायं मम जघ्निवान्।
तस्मात् तवापि पापिष्ठ प्रदास्यामि प्रतिक्रियाम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Having seen the dead Rākṣasa, his comrade was greatly pained and said to Saudāsa: ‘As you have killed that Rākṣasa, a friend of mine, who was not at all guilty, so O sinful one, I shall take my revenge on you.” (15-16)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा तु तद् रक्षस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत।
कालपर्याययोगेन राजा मित्रसहोऽभवत्॥ १७॥
verses.m: Having said so, that Rākṣasa disappeared. After the lapse of some time, Mitrasaha (Vīrasaha) became the king of Ayodhyā. (17)

verses.text:
राजापि यजते यज्ञमस्याश्रमसमीपतः।
अश्वमेधं महायज्ञं तं वसिष्ठोऽप्यपालयत्॥ १८॥
verses.m: The king also performed the great sacrifice, the Aśvamedha (horse-sacrifice) near the hermitage and Vasiṣṭha also participated in that sacrifice. (18)

verses.text:
तत्र यज्ञो महानासीद् बहुवर्षगणायुतः।
समृद्धः परया लक्ष्म्या देवयज्ञसमोऽभवत्॥ १९॥
verses.m: The great sacrifice lasted for many years and was comparable with the sacrifice of the gods being performed with great pomp. (19)

verses.text:
अथावसाने यज्ञस्य पूर्ववैरमनुस्मरन्।
वसिष्ठरूपी राजानमिति होवाच राक्षसः॥ २०॥
verses.m: Now at the end of this sacrifice, the Rākṣasa in the form of Vasiṣṭha remembering the former enmity spoke to the king. (20)

verses.text:
अद्य यज्ञावसानान्ते सामिषं भोजनं मम।
दीयतामतिशीघ्रं वै नात्र कार्या विचारणा॥ २१॥
verses.m: ‘At the conclusion of the last part of the sacrifice, give me immediately my food consisting of flesh, and do not ponder over this.’ (21)

verses.text:
तच्छ्रुत्वा व्याहृतं वाक्यं रक्षसा ब्रह्मरूपिणा।
सूदान् संस्कारकुशलानुवाच पृथिवीपतिः॥ २२॥
verses.m: Hearing those words, spoken by Rākṣasa in the form of Brāhmaṇa Vasiṣṭha, the king spoke to the expert cooks: (22)

verses.text:
हविष्यं सामिषं स्वादु यथा भवति भोजनम्।
तथा कुरुत शीघ्रं वै परितुष्येद् यथा गुरुः॥ २३॥
verses.m: ‘Prepare soon such food possessed of flesh, fatty and worthy of offering, so that our preceptor, Vasiṣṭha, is satisfied.’ (23)

verses.text:
शासनात् पार्थिवेन्द्रस्य सूदः सम्भ्रान्तमानसः।
तच्च रक्षः पुनस्तत्र सूदवेषमथाकरोत्॥ २४॥
verses.m: The chief of the cooks was perturbed in mind at the orders of the king; then that Rākṣasa soon took the form of the cook. (24)

verses.text:
स मानुषमथो मांसं पार्थिवाय न्यवेदयत्।
इदं स्वादु हविष्यं च सामिषं चान्नमाहृतम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: He brought human flesh to the king and said: “This tasteful food, possessed of flesh, has been brought by me.’ (25)

verses.text:
स भोजनं वसिष्ठाय पत्न्या सार्धमुपाहरत्।
मदयन्त्या नरश्रेष्ठ सामिषं रक्षसा हृतम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: That best among men (Vīrasaha) together with his wife Madayantī offered this food possessed of flesh brought by the Rākṣasa to Vasiṣṭha. (26)

verses.text:
ज्ञात्वा तदामिषं विप्रो मानुषं भाजनं गतम्।
क्रोधेन महताविष्टो व्याहर्तुमुपचक्रमे॥ २७॥
यस्मात् त्वं भोजनं राजन् ममैतद् दातुमिच्छसि।
तस्माद् भोजनमेतत् ते भविष्यति न संशयः॥ २८॥
verses.m: Knowing human flesh to have been brought as food, the Brāhmaṇa (Vasiṣṭha) possessed of great anger ventured to speak thus: ‘O king as you desire to give such food to me, so no doubt this shall be your food’. (27-28)

verses.text:
ततः क्रुद्धस्तु सौदासस्तोयं जग्राह पाणिना।
वसिष्ठं शप्तुमारेभे भार्या चैनमवारयत्॥ २९॥
verses.m: Then Saudāsa enraged by this, took up a hand-full of water and was on the point of cursing Vasiṣṭha; his wife, however, checked him. (29)

verses.text:
राजन् प्रभुर्यतोऽस्माकं वसिष्ठो भगवानृषिः।
प्रतिशप्तुं न शक्तस्त्वं देवतुल्यं पुरोधसम्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: ‘As the holy Ṛṣi Vasiṣṭha is our venerable preceptor and a chief priest comparable to the gods, O king! so you cannot curse him in return.’ (30)

verses.text:
ततः क्रोधमयं तोयं तेजोबलसमन्वितम्।
व्यसर्जयत धर्मात्मा ततः पादौ सिषेच च॥ ३१॥
verses.m: Then the pious Saudāsa employed the water held in his hand, which was infused with anger and his spiritual power and sprinkled his feet with it. (31)

verses.text:
तेनास्य राज्ञस्तौ पादौ तदा कल्माषतां गतौ।
तदाप्रभृति राजासौ सौदासः सुमहायशाः॥ ३२॥
कल्माषपादः संवृत्तः ख्यातश्चैव तथा नृपः।
स राजा सह पत्न्या वै प्रणिपत्य मुहुर्मुहुः।
पुनर्वसिष्ठं प्रोवाच यदुक्तं ब्रह्मरूपिणा॥ ३३॥
verses.m: By it (this sprinkling) the feet of the king became variegated in colour, and thence the king by name Saudāsa, became famous as Kalmāṣapāda (with feet of dark-variegated colour), and was so known. That King with his wife falling at the feet of Vasiṣṭha again and again repeated to Vasiṣṭha what was uttered by the Rākṣasa, in the form of a Brāhmaṇa. (32-33)

verses.text:
तच्छ्रुत्वा पार्थिवेन्द्रस्य रक्षसा विकृतं च तत्।
पुनः प्रोवाच राजानं वसिष्ठः पुरुषर्षभम्॥ ३४॥
verses.m: After having heard what the King said and knowing the food being contaminated by the Rākṣasa, Vasiṣṭḥa again spoke to Saudāsa, the bull among men: (34)

verses.text:
मया रोषपरीतेन यदिदं व्याहृतं वचः।
नैतच्छक्यं वृथा कर्तुं प्रदास्यामि च ते वरम्॥ ३५॥
verses.m: ‘These words that have been uttered by me in anger, cannot be rendered ineffective, I will, however, grant you a boon. (35)

verses.text:
कालो द्वादशवर्षाणि शापस्यान्तो भविष्यति।
मत् प्रसादाच्च राजेन्द्र अतीतं न स्मरिष्यसि॥ ३६॥
verses.m: The curse will come to an end after twelve years and by my grace, you will not remember the past.” (36)

verses.text:
एवं स राजा तं शापमुपभुज्यारिसूदनः।
प्रतिलेभे पुना राज्यं प्रजाश्चैवान्वपालयत्॥ ३७॥
verses.m: Thus that King, the extirpator of enemies, having borne that curse, regained his kingdom and protected his subjects. (37)

verses.text:
तस्य कल्माषपादस्य यज्ञस्यायतनं शुभम्।
आश्रमस्य समीपेऽस्य यन्मां पृच्छसि राघव॥ ३८॥
verses.m: ‘Of that Kalmāṣapāda is this holy place of sacrifice, near the hermitage about which you asked me’. (38)

verses.text:
तस्य तां पार्थिवेन्द्रस्य कथां श्रुत्वा सुदारुणाम्।
विवेश पर्णशालायां महर्षिमभिवाद्य च॥ ३९॥
verses.m: Having heard this dreadful story of that king Kalmāṣapāda, Śatrughna saluted the great Ṛṣi and entered the hutment. (39)

verses.text:
यामेव रात्रिं शत्रुघ्नः पर्णशालां समाविशत्।
तामेव रात्रिं सीतापि प्रसूता दारकद्वयम्॥ १॥
verses.m: During that night Śatrughna entered the arbour. The same very night Sītā gave birth to two sons. (1)

verses.text:
ततोऽर्धरात्रसमये बालका मुनिदारकाः।
वाल्मीकेः प्रियमाचख्युः सीतायाः प्रसवं शुभम्॥ २॥
verses.m: At midnight, the young ascetics spoke to sage Vālmīki about the auspicious motherhood of Sītā, which news very much pleased him: (2)

verses.text:
भगवन् रामपत्नी सा प्रसूता दारकद्वयम्।
ततो रक्षां महातेजः कुरु भूतविनाशिनीम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: ‘Sir, the wife of Rāma has given birth to two sons. So, O powerful one, make the protecting rites that destroy the ill spirits of the nether world.’ (3)

verses.text:
तेषां तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा महर्षिः समुपागमत्।
बालचन्द्रप्रतीकाशौ देवपुत्रौ महौजसौ॥ ४॥
verses.m: Hearing these words from them, the great sage went there and saw the two sons, who were like sons of the gods and were as effulgent as the moon. (4)

verses.text:
जगाम तत्र हृष्टात्मा ददर्श च कुमारकौ।
भूतघ्नीं चाकरोत् ताभ्यां रक्षां रक्षोविनाशिनीम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: The sage went there joyfully and looked at the two sons and made the sacrament for both of them that kills the inauspicous Bhūtas and destroys the Rākṣasa. (5)

verses.text:
कुशमुष्टिमुपादाय लवं चैव तु स द्विजः।
वाल्मीकिः प्रददौ ताभ्यां रक्षां भूतविनाशिनीम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: That Brāhmaṇa Vālmīki took the handful of Kuśa and Lava (the lower portion of the Kuśa grass) and preparing the totemic device, handed it over to them, the protective symbol that kills the Bhūtas. (6)

verses.text:
यस्तयोः पूर्वजो जातः स कुशैर्मन्त्रसत्कृतैः।
निर्मार्जनीयस्तु तदा कुश इत्यस्य नाम तत्॥ ७॥
