verses.m: ‘He who of the two was born first should be cleansed with the Kuśas purified by chants and then his name will be ‘Kuśa.’ (7)

verses.text:
यश्चावरो भवेत् ताभ्यां लवेन सुसमाहितः।
निर्मार्जनीयो वृद्धाभिर्लवेति च स नामतः॥ ८॥
verses.m: ‘Who happens to be born later, should be cleansed carefully with Lava by the old women and will be known by the name of Lava. (8)

verses.text:
एवं कुशलवौ नाम्ना तावुभौ यमजातकौ।
मत्कृताभ्यां च नामभ्यां ख्यातियुक्तौ भविष्यतः॥ ९॥
verses.m: ‘Thus these twins named Kuśa and Lava will become famous bearing the names given by me.’ (9)

verses.text:
तां रक्षां जगृहुस्तां च मुनिहस्तात् समाहिताः।
अकुर्वंश्च ततो रक्षां तयोर्विगतकल्मषाः॥ १०॥
verses.m: Then the old women of Āśrama pure in mind took with care the totemic device from the hands of the sage and performed the protective rites of the twins. (10)

verses.text:
तथा तां क्रियमाणां च वृद्धाभिर्गोत्रनाम च।
संकीर्तनं च रामस्य सीतायाः प्रसवौ शुभौ॥ ११॥
अर्धरात्रे तु शत्रुघ्नः शुश्राव सुमहत् प्रियम्।
पर्णशालां ततो गत्वा मातर्दिष्ट्येति चाब्रवीत्॥ १२॥
verses.m: While in this manner (the symbolic protection) was being performed by the old women, Śatrughna at midnight heard the joyful Gotra and name of Śrī Rāma and also the news of delivery of the two sons by Sītā and then having entered the arbour of Sītā said, ‘O mother, by the grace of God two sons are born to you.’ (11-12)

verses.text:
तदा तस्य प्रहृष्टस्य शत्रुघ्नस्य महात्मनः।
व्यतीता वार्षिकी रात्रिः श्रावणी लघुविक्रमा॥ १३॥
verses.m: Then the night of the rainy season of the month of Śrāvaṇa (full moon) passed swiftly with noble Śatrughna enjoying himself. (13)

verses.text:
प्रभाते सुमहावीर्यः कृत्वा पौर्वाह्णिकीं क्रियाम्।
मुनिं प्राञ्जलिरामन्त्र्य ययौ पश्चान्मुखः पुनः॥ १४॥
verses.m: At break of dawn, having performed the morning ablutions, he (Śatrughna) taking leave of the sage with folded hands, started forth to the western direction. (14)

verses.text:
स गत्वा यमुनातीरं सप्तरात्रोषितः पथि।
ऋषीणां पुण्यकीर्तीनामाश्रमे वासमभ्ययात्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Reaching the banks of the Yamunā, and having spent seven nights on the way he (Śatrughna) made for his stay in the hermitages of the sages of holy fame. (15)

verses.text:
स तत्र मुनिभिः सार्धं भार्गवप्रमुखैर्नृपः।
कथाभिरभिरूपाभिर्वासं चक्रे महायशाः॥ १६॥
verses.m: He, the famous one, dwelt there with the sages among whom Bhārgava was the foremost, taking part in talks proper to the occasion. (16)

verses.text:
स काञ्चनाद्यैर्मुनिभिः समेतै
रघुप्रवीरो रजनीं तदानीम्।
कथाप्रकारैर्बहुभिर्महात्मा
विरामयामास नरेन्द्रसूनुः॥ १७॥
verses.m: This way the mightiest among Raghus and great souled Śatrughna in the company of sages like Cyavana passed that night through hearing various religious tales. (17)

verses.text:
अथ रात्र्यां प्रवृत्तायां शत्रुघ्नो भृगुनन्दनम्।
पप्रच्छ च्यवनं विप्रं लवणस्य यथाबलम्॥ १॥
शूलस्य च बलं ब्रह्मन् के च पूर्वं विनाशिताः।
अनेन शूलमुख्येन द्वन्द्वयुद्धमुपागताः॥ २॥
verses.m: Then as the night appeared, Śatrughna asked the Brāhmaṇa, Cyavana, son of Bhṛgu the exact might of Lavaṇa, and the power of the trident also. He enquired, ‘O Brāhmaṇa, who were killed by this special trident having entered into a duel with Lavaṇa.’ (1-2)

verses.text:
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा शत्रुघ्नस्य महात्मनः।
प्रत्युवाच महातेजाश्च्यवनो रघुनन्दनम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Hearing these words of the noble Śatrughna, the mighty Cyavana said in reply to the scion of the Raghus: (3)

verses.text:
असंख्येयानि कर्माणि यान्यस्य रघुनन्दन।
इक्ष्वाकुवंशप्रभवे यद् वृत्तं तच्छृणुष्व मे॥ ४॥
verses.m: ‘Among the innumerable doings of this Lavaṇa listen to me that which took place in the context of the originator of the family of Ikṣvāku (Māndhātā). (4)

verses.text:
अयोध्यायां पुरा राजा युवनाश्वसुतो बली।
मान्धाता इति विख्यातस्त्रिषु लोकेषु वीर्यवान्॥ ५॥
verses.m: ‘In the old days, there was a powerful king, the son of Yuvanāśva, known as Māndhātā, noted for his might in the three worlds. (5)

verses.text:
स कृत्वा पृथिवीं कृत्स्नां शासने पृथिवीपतिः।
सुरलोकमितो जेतुमुद्योगमकरोन्नृपः॥ ६॥
verses.m: ‘Having ruled over the entire earth, that king, lord of the earth, embarked on a conquest of the world of the gods from here, the earth. (6)

verses.text:
इन्द्रस्य च भयं तीव्रं सुराणां च महात्मनाम्।
मान्धातरि कृतोद्योगे देवलोकजिगीषया॥ ७॥
verses.m: ‘Great fear overcame Indra and other mighty gods, when Māndhātā prepared to fight with a desire to conquer the world of gods. (7)

verses.text:
अर्धासनेन शक्रस्य राज्यार्धेन च पार्थिवः।
वन्द्यमानः सुरगणैः प्रतिज्ञामध्यरोहत॥ ८॥
verses.m: Propitiated by the host of gods, Māndhātā, the king, having vowed to take one half of Indra’s kingdom and the other half of earthly sovereignty, went up to raid heaven. (8)

verses.text:
तस्य पापमभिप्रायं विदित्वा पाकशासनः।
सान्त्वपूर्वमिदं वाक्यमुवाच युवनाश्वजम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: ‘Indra, the conqueror of Pāka Daitya, having known his evil intentions, uttered these conciliatory words to the progeny of Yuvanāśva. (9)

verses.text:
राजा त्वं मानुषे लोके न तावत् पुरुषर्षभ।
अकृत्वा पृथिवीं वश्यां देवराज्यमिहेच्छसि॥ १०॥
verses.m: ‘O bull among men, Māndhātā, you are still not established as a king in the mortal worlds, and you desire the kingdom of the gods here without subjugating the earth. (10)

verses.text:
यदि वीर समग्रा ते मेदिनी निखिला वशे।
देवराज्यं कुरुष्वेह सभृत्यबलवाहनः॥ ११॥
verses.m: ‘O brave one, if the entire earth is indeed under your sway then you may rule over the kingdom of the gods together with your attendants, army and carriers. (11)

verses.text:
इन्द्रमेवं ब्रुवाणं तं मान्धाता वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
क्व मे शक्र प्रतिहतं शासनं पृथिवीतले॥ १२॥
verses.m: Māndhātā said to Indra: ‘O Indra, where does my rule over the earth is obstructed’? (12)

verses.text:
तमुवाच सहस्राक्षो लवणो नाम राक्षसः।
मधुपुत्रो मधुवने न तेऽऽज्ञां कुरुतेऽनघ॥ १३॥
verses.m: The thousand-eyed Indra told him, ‘O sinless one, the son of Madhu, the Rākṣasa Lavaṇa by name, does not obey your orders.’ (13)

verses.text:
तच्छ्रुत्वा विप्रियं घोरं सहस्राक्षेण भाषितम्।
व्रीडितोऽवाङ्मुखो राजा व्याहर्तुं न शशाक ह॥ १४॥
verses.m: Having heard the dreadful unpleasant words, conveyed by Indra, the King put to shame with face downcast, could not speak. (14)

verses.text:
आमन्त्र्य तु सहस्राक्षं प्रायात् किंचिदवाङ्मुखः।
पुनरेवागमच्छ्रीमानिमं लोकं नरेश्वरः॥ १५॥
verses.m: Taking leave of the thousand-eyed god, with his face turned somewhat downwards, the lord of the mortals proceeded and came back again to this world. (15)

verses.text:
स कृत्वा हृदयेऽमर्षं सभृत्यबलवाहनः।
आजगाम मधोः पुत्रं वशे कर्तुमरिंदमः॥ १६॥
verses.m: That king, the destroyer of foes, with anger in his heart and together with his attendants and carriers came to bring the son of Madhu, Lavaṇa, under his sway. (16)

verses.text:
स काङ्क्षमाणो लवणं युद्धाय पुरुषर्षभः।
दूतं सम्प्रेषयामास सकाशं लवणस्य सः॥ १७॥
verses.m: Desirous to fight with Lavaṇa, the bull among men, Māndhātā, sent a messenger to Lavaṇa. (17)

verses.text:
स गत्वा विप्रियाण्याह बहूनि मधुनः सुतम्।
वदन्तमेवं तं दूतं भक्षयामास राक्षसः॥ १८॥
verses.m: He, the messenger, having approached the son of Madhu, said many unpleasant words; the Rākṣasa devoured that messenger while he was speaking thus. (18)

verses.text:
चिरायमाणे दूते तु राजा क्रोधसमन्वितः।
अर्दयामास तद् रक्षः शरवृष्ट्या समन्ततः॥ १९॥
verses.m: The messenger, on being late in returning, the King possessed of anger, inflicted injury on the Rākṣasa by shower of arrows on all sides. (19)

verses.text:
ततः प्रहस्य तद् रक्षः शूलं जग्राह पाणिना।
वधाय सानुबन्धस्य मुमोचायुधमुत्तमम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: Then that Rākṣasa laughed and took the trident in his hand and released the best among weapons, the trident, for the purpose of slaying Māndhātā with all his followers. (20)

verses.text:
तच्छूलं दीप्यमानं तु सभृत्यबलवाहनम्।
भस्मीकृत्वा नृपं भूयो लवणस्यागमत् करम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: That enflamed trident on its part, having rendered to ashes the king together with his attendant, army and carriers—came back to the hand of Lavaṇa. (21)

verses.text:
एवं स राजा सुमहान् हतः सबलवाहनः।
शूलस्य तु बलं सौम्य अप्रमेयमनुत्तमम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: Thus that great King was killed together with his army and carriers, O gracious one, the power of the trident is impossible to fathom. (22)

verses.text:
श्वः प्रभाते तु लवणं वधिष्यसि न संशयः।
अगृहीतायुधं क्षिप्रं ध्रुवो हि विजयस्तव॥ २३॥
verses.m: Tomorrow morning, you shall soon kill Lavaṇa while he is without the weapon, there is no doubt that your victory is certain. (23)

verses.text:
लोकानां स्वस्ति चैवं स्यात् कृते कर्मणि च त्वया।
एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं लवणस्य दुरात्मनः॥ २४॥
शूलस्य च बलं घोरमप्रमेयं नरर्षभ।
विनाशश्चैव मान्धातुर्यत्नेनाभूच्च पार्थिव॥ २५॥
verses.m: By you performing this deed the welfare of the worlds will be achieved. Thus all has been narrated to you, O bull among men, about the might of the wicked Lavaṇa and the unfathomable dreadful power of the trident, O king Māndhātā; Lavaṇa perished due to his own misdeeds. (24-25)

verses.text:
त्वं श्वः प्रभाते लवणं महात्मन्
वधिष्यसे नात्र तु संशयो मे।
शूलं विना निर्गतमामिषार्थे
ध्रुवो जयस्ते भविता नरेन्द्र॥ २६॥
verses.m: Tomorrow morning you will slay Lavaṇa I have no doubt, O noble one, when he will proceed for flesh, having not the trident with him, victory shall be yours, O king of men. (26)

verses.text:
कथां कथयतां तेषां जयं चाकाङ्क्षतां शुभम्।
व्यतीता रजनी शीघ्रं शत्रुघ्नस्य महात्मनः॥ १॥
verses.m: The night passed away quickly while staying at the hermitage of Cyavana, the noble Śatrughna conversing with Cyavana and other sages, who wished for his holy victory (against Lavaṇa). (1)

verses.text:
ततः प्रभाते विमले तस्मिन् काले स राक्षसः।
निर्गतस्तु पुराद् वीरो भक्ष्याहारप्रचोदितः॥ २॥
verses.m: Then in the morning when it was dawn, that Rākṣasa, Lavaṇa, the heroic one, went out of his city impelled by the desire to bring his food. (2)

verses.text:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे वीरः शत्रुघ्नो यमुनां नदीम्।
तीर्त्वा मधुपुरद्वारि धनुष्पाणिरतिष्ठत॥ ३॥
verses.m: In the meantime, Śatrughna, the brave one, having crossed the Yamunā, stood at the gates of the city of Madhu, with bow in his hand. (3)

verses.text:
ततोऽर्धदिवसे प्राप्ते क्रूरकर्मा स राक्षसः।
आगच्छद् बहुसाहस्रं प्राणिनां भारमुद्वहन्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Then at midday that Rākṣasa, Lavaṇa, the evil-doer returned bearing the load of many thousand creatures. (4)

verses.text:
ततो ददर्श शत्रुघ्नं स्थितं द्वारि धृतायुधम्।
तमुवाच ततो रक्षः किमनेन करिष्यसि॥ ५॥
verses.m: Then the Rākṣasa saw Śatrughna armed with the bow, standing at the gate and said to him: ‘What will you do with this weapon? (5)

verses.text:
ईदृशानां सहस्राणि सायुधानां नराधम।
भक्षितानि मया रोषात् कालेनानुगतो ह्यसि॥ ६॥
verses.m: ‘Many thousands of men like you accompanied with weapons, O wretched one, have been devoured by me in anger. Death seems to have come nearer to you. (6)

verses.text:
आहारश्चाप्यसम्पूर्णो ममायं पुरुषाधम।
स्वयं प्रविष्टोऽद्य मुखं कथमासाद्य दुर्मते॥ ७॥
verses.m: ‘O vile one, my food is yet incomplete, having come, you enter my mouth of your own accord?’ (7)

verses.text:
तस्यैवं भाषमाणस्य हसतश्च मुहुर्मुहुः।
शत्रुघ्नो वीर्यसम्पन्नो रोषादश्रूण्यवासृजत्॥ ८॥
verses.m: While the Rākṣasa spoke thus and laughing, the heroic Śatrughna broke in tears with anger. (8)

verses.text:
तस्य रोषाभिभूतस्य शत्रुघ्नस्य महात्मनः।
तेजोमया मरीच्यस्तु सर्वगात्रैर्विनिष्पतन्॥ ९॥
verses.m: Fiery rays issued forth from all the limbs of the noble and angry Śatrughna. (9)

verses.text:
उवाच च सुसंक्रुद्धः शत्रुघ्नः स निशाचरम्।
योद्धुमिच्छामि दुर्बुद्धे द्वन्द्वयुद्धं त्वया सह॥ १०॥
verses.m: Highly enraged, Śatrughna then addressed the demon, who roamed about thus at right, ‘O evil one, I wish to have a duel with you. (10)

verses.text:
पुत्रो दशरथस्याहं भ्राता रामस्य धीमतः।
शत्रुघ्नो नाम शत्रुघ्नो वधाकाङ्क्षी तवागतः॥ ११॥
verses.m: ‘I am the son of (King) Daśaratha, and the brother of the wise Śrī Rāma, the extirpator of foes, Śatrughna by name. I have come with a desire to kill you. (11)

verses.text:
तस्य मे युद्धकामस्य द्वन्द्वयुद्धं प्रदीयताम्।
शत्रुस्त्वं सर्वभूतानां न मे जीवन् गमिष्यसि॥ १२॥
verses.m: ‘So give the duel to me, who desires to fight with you! You are the enemy of all beings; with me alive here you shall not escape.’ (12)

verses.text:
तस्मिंस्तथा ब्रुवाणे तु राक्षसः प्रहसन्निव।
प्रत्युवाच नरश्रेष्ठं दिष्ट्या प्राप्तोऽसि दुर्मते॥ १३॥
verses.m: When Śatrughna had spoken thus, that Rākṣasa, Lavaṇa, replied to the best among men, as if laughing: ‘O wicked one, it is my good luck that you have come within my reach. (13)

verses.text:
मम मातृष्वसुर्भ्राता रावणो नाम राक्षसः।
हतो रामेण दुर्बुद्धे स्त्रीहेतोः पुरुषाधम॥ १४॥
verses.m: ‘O insensate one, the Rākṣasa Rāvaṇa the brother of my maternal aunt, was killed by Rāma for the sake of a woman. (14)

verses.text:
तच्च सर्वं मया क्षान्तं रावणस्य कुलक्षयम्।
अवज्ञां पुरतः कृत्वा मया यूयं विशेषतः॥ १५॥
verses.m: All I had forgiven, the destruction of the family of Rāvaṇa, and ignoring specially you. (15)

verses.text:
निहताश्च हि ते सर्वे परिभूतास्तृणं यथा।
भूताश्चैव भविष्याश्च यूयं च पुरुषाधमाः॥ १६॥
verses.m: ‘But now all of you, that have been born or will be born and even you vile ones, will be swept away by me like straws.(16)

verses.text:
तस्य ते युद्धकामस्य युद्धं दास्यामि दुर्मते।
तिष्ठ त्वं च मुहूर्तं तु यावदायुधमानये॥ १७॥
verses.m: ‘I shall indeed give you a fight, who wish it, O fool of vicious intellect. Just wait for a moment, while I bring my weapon (trident). (17)

verses.text:
ईप्सितं यादृशं तुभ्यं सज्जये यावदायुधम्।
तमुवाचाशु शत्रुघ्नः क्व मे जीवन् गमिष्यसि॥ १८॥
verses.m: ‘I am going to be equipped with the weapon with which I desire to kill you.’ At this Śatrughna at once spoke out: ‘Where will you go as long as I am alive? (18)

verses.text:
स्वयमेवागतः शत्रुर्न मोक्तव्यः कृतात्मना।
यो हि विक्लवया बुद्ध्या प्रसरं शत्रवे दिशेत्।
स हतो मन्दबुद्धिः स्याद् यथा कापुरुषस्तथा॥ १९॥
verses.m: ‘The enemy that has come of his own accord does not deserve to be set free by one disciplined in mind. Whoever with unsettled mind gives freedom to a foe to disappear, that weak-minded one indeed would be killed as a coward. (19)

verses.text:
तस्मात् सुदृष्टं कुरु जीवलोकं
शरैः शितैस्त्वां विविधैर्नयामि।
यमस्य गेहाभिमुखं हि पापं
रिपुं त्रिलोकस्य च राघवस्य॥ २०॥
verses.m: ‘You, therefore, have a good look at this world of mortals, O wicked one! I shall carry you to Yama’s abode with many sharp arrows, O foe of the three worlds and also of Raghu’s family.’ (20)

verses.text:
तच्छ्रुत्वा भाषितं तस्य शत्रुघ्नस्य महात्मनः।
क्रोधमाहारयत् तीव्रं तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Hearing these words of the noble Śatrughna, Lavaṇa became extremely angry and said: ‘Wait for a moment’. (1)

verses.text:
पाणौ पाणिं च निष्पिष्य दन्तान् कटकटाय्य च।
लवणो रघुशार्दूलमाह्वयामास चासकृत्॥ २॥
verses.m: Rubbing his one hand with the other, and making a rattling sound with his teeth, Lavaṇa challenged the lion among Raghus many times. (2)

verses.text:
तं ब्रुवाणं तथा वाक्यं लवणं घोरदर्शनम्।
शत्रुघ्नो देवशत्रुघ्न इदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ ३॥
verses.m: To that Lavaṇa of fearful appearance, speaking thus, Śatrughna, the killer of the enemies of the gods, said these words: (3)

verses.text:
शत्रुघ्नो न तदा जातो यदान्ये निर्जितास्त्वया।
तदद्य बाणाभिहतो व्रज त्वं यमसादनम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: ‘Śatrughna was not born, when others were conquered by you in battle, so go to the abode of Yama today, killed by my arrow. (4)

verses.text:
ऋषयोऽप्यद्य पापात्मन् मया त्वां निहतं रणे।
पश्यन्तु विप्रा विद्वांसस्त्रिदशा इव रावणम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: ‘O sinful one, may the sages too see you killed in encounter today, also the learned Brāhmaṇas, as the gods saw Rāvaṇa killed. (5)

verses.text:
त्वयि मद्बाणनिर्दग्धे पतितेऽद्य निशाचर।
पुरे जनपदे चापि क्षेममेव भविष्यति॥ ६॥
verses.m: ‘Today there will be peace indeed in the city and province, as you, the demon roaming about at night are slain by my arrow and lie prostrate on the ground and burnt. (6)

verses.text:
अद्य मद्बाहुनिष्क्रान्तः शरो वज्रनिभाननः।
प्रवेक्ष्यते ते हृदयं पद्ममंशुरिवार्कजः॥ ७॥
verses.m: ‘Today, the arrow, whose fore-point resembles the thunderbolt, released by my hand, shall enter your heart as the ray of the sun enters in the lotus.’ (7)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तो महावृक्षं लवणः क्रोधमूर्च्छितः।
शत्रुघ्नोरसि चिक्षेप स च तं शतधाच्छिनत्॥ ८॥
verses.m: Being thus spoken, Lavaṇa enraged with anger threw a mightly tree on the breast of Śatrughna; but Śatrughna cut it thousandfold with arrows. (8)

verses.text:
तद् दृष्ट्वा विफलं कर्म राक्षसः पुनरेव तु।
पादपान् सुबहून् गृह्य शत्रुघ्नायासृजद् बली॥ ९॥
verses.m: Thus seeing his action fruitless, the powerful Rākṣasa again taking hold of many trees hurled them at Śatrughna. (9)

verses.text:
शत्रुघ्नश्चापि तेजस्वी वृक्षानापततो बहून्।
त्रिभिश्चतुर्भिरेकैकं चिच्छेद नतपर्वभिः॥ १०॥
verses.m: The brave Śatrughna too, tore asunder each one coming upon him, by three or four arrows of flatterend ends. (10)

verses.text:
ततो बाणमयं वर्षं व्यसृजद् राक्षसोपरि।
शत्रुघ्नो वीर्यसम्पन्नो विव्यथे न स राक्षसः॥ ११॥
verses.m: Thus, Śatrughna then possessed of great might, let loose a shower of arrows on the Rākṣasa; however, the Rākṣasa was not troubled. (11)

verses.text:
ततः प्रहस्य लवणो वृक्षमुद्यम्य वीर्यवान्।
शिरस्यभ्यहनच्छूरं स्रस्ताङ्गः स मुमोह वै॥ १२॥
verses.m: Then the powerful Lavaṇa laughed, and lifting a tree attacked the brave one, Śatrughna, on the head; Śatrughna went into a swoon with the bodily joints loosened. (12)

verses.text:
तस्मिन् निपतिते वीरे हाहाकारो महानभूत्।
ऋषीणां देवसंघानां गन्धर्वाप्सरसां तथा॥ १३॥
verses.m: So, as the brave Śatrughna fell, long cries of ‘Hā’ emanated from the sages, the host of the gods, the Gandharvas and Apsarās (the celestial beings). (13)

verses.text:
तमवज्ञाय तु हतं शत्रुघ्नं भुवि पातितम्।
रक्षो लब्धान्तरमपि न विवेश स्वमालयम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: Ignoring Śatrughna, fallen on the ground whom he took killed, the Rākṣasa did not enter his residence, although given time to do so. (14)

verses.text:
नापि शूलं प्रजग्राह तं दृष्ट्वा भुवि पातितम्।
ततो हत इति ज्ञात्वा तान् भक्षान् समुदावहत्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Nor even did he, Lavaṇa, take up the trident seeing him (Śatrughna) lying on the ground, and then considering him, Śatrughna, dead, carried again his provisions. (15)

verses.text:
मुहूर्ताल्लब्धसंज्ञस्तु पुनस्तस्थौ धृतायुधः।
शत्रुघ्नो वै पुरद्वारि ऋषिभिः सम्प्रपूजितः॥ १६॥
verses.m: Gaining consciousness in a moment, Śatrughna, adored by the sages, stood up and waited at the door of the city of Madhu, weapon in his hand. (16)

verses.text:
ततो दिव्यममोघं तं जग्राह शरमुत्तमम्।
ज्वलन्तं तेजसा घोरं पूरयन्तं दिशो दश॥ १७॥
वज्राननं वज्रवेगं मेरुमन्दरसंनिभम्।
नतं पर्वसु सर्वेषु संयुगेष्वपराजितम्॥ १८॥
असृक्चन्दनदिग्धाङ्गं चारुपत्रं पतत्त्रिणम्।
दानवेन्द्राचलेन्द्राणामसुराणां च दारुणम्॥ १९॥
तं दीप्तमिव कालाग्निं युगान्ते समुपस्थिते।
दृष्ट्वा सर्वाणि भूतानि परित्रासमुपागमन्॥ २०॥
verses.m: Then Śatrughna took hold of the arrow: the divine and excelling others, flaming with brilliance and filling the ten quarters with its brilliance, shaped like the thunderbolt in front, resembling the thunderbolt in speed, equalling Meru and Mandara mountains, flat shaped, invincible in all encounters, smeared with red sandal-like blood, beautiful as the winged bird, dreadful for the lord of the Dānavas and also the mountains, resembling as if the fire of destruction kindled at the time of final dissolution. Seeing it, all beings were very much frightened. (17—20)

verses.text:
सदेवासुरगन्धर्वं मुनिभिः साप्सरोगणम्।
जगद्धि सर्वमस्वस्थं पितामहमुपस्थितम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: The whole world, together with the Devas, Asuras and Gandharvas and the sages, was in discomfort and all approached Pitāmaha (Brahmā). (21)

verses.text:
उवाच देवदेवेशं वरदं प्रपितामहम्।
देवानां भयसम्मोहो लोकानां संक्षयं प्रति॥ २२॥
verses.m: They narrated to the god of the gods, Prapitāmaha Brahmā, the bewilderment of the gods with fear regarding the security of the worlds. (22)

verses.text:
कच्चिल्लोकक्षयो देव सम्प्राप्तो वा युगक्षयः।
नेदृशं दृष्टपूर्वं च न श्रुतं प्रपितामह॥ २३॥
verses.m: ‘O lord ! is the destruction of the world at hand or has the end of the universe approached? O grand sire, never before has such a condition of the world been seen or heard.’ (23)

verses.text:
तेषां तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः।
भयकारणमाचष्ट देवानामभयंकरः॥ २४॥
verses.m: Hearing their words, Brahmā the grandfather of the worlds, protector of the gods, revealed the cause of the fear of the gods. (24)

verses.text:
उवाच मधुरां वाणीं शृणुध्वं सर्वदेवताः।
वधाय लवणस्याजौ शरः शत्रुघ्नधारितः॥ २५॥
verses.m: He said in a sweet voice: ‘All the gods listen to me; the arrow has been held by Śatrughna for the slaying of Lavaṇa in encounter. (25)

verses.text:
तेजसा तस्य सम्मूढाः सर्वे स्म सुरसत्तमाः।
एष पूर्वस्य देवस्य लोककर्तुः सनातनः॥ २६॥
शरस्तेजोमयो वत्सा येन वै भयमागतम्।
एष वै कैटभस्यार्थे मधुनश्च महाशरः॥ २७॥
सृष्टो महात्मना तेन वधार्थे दैत्ययोस्तयोः।
एक एव प्रजानाति विष्णुस्तेजोमयं शरम्॥ २८॥
verses.m: ‘All the great gods are bewildered at the power of that arrow ! O my children, this is the eternal powerful arrow of the former God, the creator of the world, Viṣṇu, due to which the gods are in fear; this mighty arrow was created for the destruction of those two sons of Diti, Madhu and Kaiṭabha; Viṣṇu alone knows well about this powerful arrow. (26—28)

verses.text:
एषा एव तनुः पूर्वा विष्णोस्तस्य महात्मनः।
इतो गच्छत पश्यध्वं वध्यमानं महात्मना॥ २९॥
रामानुजेन वीरेण लवणं राक्षसोत्तमम्।
तस्य ते देवदेवस्य निशम्य वचनं सुराः॥ ३०॥
आजग्मुर्यत्र युध्येते शत्रुघ्नलवणावुभौ।
तं शरं दिव्यसंकाशं शत्रुघ्नकरधारितम्॥ ३१॥
ददृशुः सर्वभूतानि युगान्ताग्निमिवोत्थितम्।
आकाशमावृतं दृष्ट्वा देवैर्हि रघुनन्दनः॥ ३२॥
सिंहनादं भृशं कृत्वा ददर्श लवणं पुनः।
आहूतश्च पुनस्तेन शत्रुघ्नेन महात्मना॥ ३३॥
verses.m: ‘This arrow is the ancient form of the noble Viṣṇu; go from here, O my children, and witness Lavaṇa being killed by the noble and heroic Śatrughna, the younger brother of Śrī Rāma.’ The gods hearing the words of the God of gods, came to the place where both Śatrughna and Lavaṇa were engaged in fighting; all beings witnessed that divine arrow borne by Śatrughna in his hand, as if it was the fire that broke out at the time of universal destruction. Seeing the sky filled with the gods, Śatrughna, again having roared like a loin, looked at Lavaṇa; he (Lavaṇa) was again challenged by the noble Śatrughna.(29—33)

verses.text:
लवणः क्रोधसंयुक्तो युद्धाय समुपस्थितः।
आकर्णात् स विकृष्याथ तद् धनुर्धन्विनां वरः॥ ३४॥
स मुमोच महाबाणं लवणस्य महोरसि।
उरस्तस्य विदार्याशु प्रविवेश रसातलम्॥ ३५॥
गत्वा रसातलं दिव्यः शरो विबुधपूजितः।
पुनरेवागमत् तूर्णमिक्ष्वाकुकुलनन्दनम्॥ ३६॥
verses.m: Lavaṇa filled with anger appeared to give him (Śatrughna) the fight. He, Śatrughna, the best among archers, then having stretched that bow up to his ear, shot the arrow at the mighty chest of Lavaṇa. That divine arrow descended to the nether-world breaking open Lavaṇa’s chest, and having gone there, being worshipped by the gods, came back quickly again to Śatrughna, the descendant of the family of Ikṣvāku. (34—36)

verses.text:
शत्रुघ्नशरनिर्भिन्नो लवणः स निशाचरः।
पपात सहसा भूमौ वज्राहत इवाचलः॥ ३७॥
verses.m: That demon Lavaṇa being struck by the arrow of Śatrughna, fell on the ground all at once like the mountain struck by the thunderbolt. (37)

verses.text:
तच्च शूलं महद् दिव्यं हते लवणराक्षसे।
पश्यतां सर्वदेवानां रुद्रस्य वशमन्वगात्॥ ३८॥
verses.m: On the Rākṣasa Lavaṇa being killed, that mighty divine arrow too, came back to the quiver of Rudra as all the gods looked on. (38)

verses.text:
एकेषुपातेन भयं निपात्य
लोकत्रयस्यास्य रघुप्रवीरः।
विनिर्बभावुत्तमचापबाण-
स्तमः प्रणुद्येव सहस्ररश्मिः॥ ३९॥
ततो हि देवा ऋषिपन्नगाश्च
प्रपूजिरे ह्यप्सरसश्च सर्वाः।
दिष्ट्या जयो दाशरथेरवाप्त-
स्त्यक्त्वा भयं सर्प इव प्रशान्तः॥ ४०॥
verses.m: Then the champion of Raghus, Śatrughna, felled with one arrow the terror of three worlds, shone forth as the sun dispelling the darkness. All gods, sages, serpents paid homage to him and Apsarās hailed the fearless victory of the son of Śrī Daśaratha, the serpent laid to rest. (39-40)

verses.text:
हते तु लवणे देवाः सेन्द्राः साग्निपुरोगमाः।
ऊचुः सुमधुरां वाणीं शत्रुघ्नं शत्रुतापनम्॥ १॥
verses.m: After Lavaṇa was killed, the gods, together with Indra and Agni as their head, spoke these sweet words to Śatrughna, the tormentor of the foes. (1)

verses.text:
दिष्ट्या ते विजयो वत्स दिष्ट्या लवणराक्षसः।
हतः पुरुषशार्दूल वरं वरय सुव्रत॥ २॥
verses.m: ‘O lion among men, by good fortune, victory is yours and the Rākṣasa is dead, O! of a noble vow! ask us for a boon. (2)

verses.text:
वरदास्तु महाबाहो सर्व एव समागताः।
विजयाकाङ्क्षिणस्तुभ्यममोघं दर्शनं हि नः॥ ३॥
verses.m: ‘All desirous of your victory are intending to grant boon to you. We have come; our presence here will not be fruitless.’ (3)

verses.text:
देवानां भाषितं श्रुत्वा शूरो मूर्ध्नि कृताञ्जलिः।
प्रत्युवाच महाबाहुः शत्रुघ्नः प्रयतात्मवान्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Hearing the words of the gods, Śatrughna, the long-armed one, disciplined in mind, keeping his folded hands on his head replied thus : (4)

verses.text:
इयं मधुपुरी रम्या मधुरा देवनिर्मिता।
निवेशं प्राप्नुयाच्छीघ्रमेष मेऽस्तु वरः परः॥ ५॥
verses.m: ‘This city of Madhu, Madhurā by name, built by the gods, may become the capital soon. This is the only boon that I desire: (5)

verses.text:
तं देवाः प्रीतमनसो बाढमित्येव राघवम्।
भविष्यति पुरी रम्या शूरसेना न संशयः॥ ६॥
verses.m: The gods said: ‘So be it’ O scion of the Raghus: This beautiful city will be Śūrasenā indeed, possessed of an army of brave men, there is no doubt about it.’ (6)

verses.text:
ते तथोक्त्वा महात्मानो दिवमारुरुहुस्तदा।
शत्रुघ्नोऽपि महातेजास्तां सेनां समुपानयत्॥ ७॥
verses.m: Thus saying the holy gods then ascended to heaven. Śatrughna too, the powerful one, brought back the army from the banks of the Gaṅgā. (7)

verses.text:
सा सेना शीघ्रमागच्छच्छ्रुत्वा शत्रुघ्नशासनम्।
निवेशनं च शत्रुघ्नः श्रावणेन समारभत्॥ ८॥
verses.m: That army came soon, hearing the news of the death of Lavaṇa at the hands of Śatrughna and commenced the establishment of the capital in the month of Śrāvaṇa (roughly corresponding to July-August). (8)

verses.text:
सा पुरा दिव्यसंकाशा वर्षे द्वादशमे शुभे।
निविष्टः शूरसेनानां विषयश्चाकुतोभयः॥ ९॥
verses.m: That holy country was established as the territory of the Śūrasenas, in the course of twelve years, as there was no cause for fear. (9)

verses.text:
क्षेत्राणि सस्ययुक्तानि काले वर्षति वासवः।
अरोगवीरपुरुषा शत्रुघ्नभुजपालिता॥ १०॥
verses.m: The fields were full with grains, Indra (the rain-god) brought forth rain in time, the warriors, protected by Śatrughna, were free of disease. (10)

verses.text:
अर्धचन्द्रप्रतीकाशा यमुनातीरशोभिता।
शोभिता गृहमुख्यैश्च चत्वरापणवीथिकैः।
चातुर्वर्ण्यसमायुक्ता नानावाणिज्यशोभिता॥ ११॥
verses.m: That city, shaped like the half-moon, beautified by the banks of the Yamunā, was also embellished with special mansions and quadrangular market-place. It was inhabited by the four Varṇas (castes) and abounded in all forms of merchandise and trade. (11)

verses.text:
यच्च तेन पुरा शुभ्रं लवणेन कृतं महत्।
तच्छोभयति शत्रुघ्नो नानावर्णोपशोभिताम्॥ १२॥
आरामैश्च विहारैश्च शोभमानां समन्ततः।
शोभितां शोभनीयैश्च तथान्यैर्देवमानुषैः॥ १३॥
verses.m: The white mansion that was formerly built by Lavaṇa, Śatrughna further beautified with pictures of various colours, looking beautiful on all sides with rest-houses and Vihāras, and that city was adorned with human and celestial embellishments. (12-13)

verses.text:
तां पुरीं दिव्यसंकाशां नानापण्योपशोभिताम्।
नानादेशगतैश्चापि वणिग्भिरुपशोभिताम्॥ १४॥
तां समृद्धां समृद्धार्थः शत्रुघ्नो भरतानुजः।
निरीक्ष्य परमप्रीतः परं हर्षमुपागमत्॥ १५॥
verses.m: The prosperous Śatrughna, the younger brother of Bharata, having seen the city, divine in appearance, filled with all forms of merchandise and inhabited by traders coming from various countries, was much pleased. (14-15)

verses.text:
तस्य बुद्धिः समुत्पन्ना निवेश्य मधुरां पुरीम्।
रामपादौ निरीक्षेऽहं वर्षे द्वादश आगते॥ १६॥
verses.m: Then at the commencement of the twelfth year, having established the city Madhurā, he thought ‘I shall see the feet of Śrī Rāma.’ (16)

verses.text:
ततः स ताममरपुरोपमां पुरीं
निवेश्य वै विविधजनाभिसंवृताम्।
नराधिपो रघुपतिपाददर्शने
दधे मतिं रघुकुलवंशवर्धनः॥ १७॥
verses.m: Then establishing that city, resembling a celestial one, Śatrughna filling it with men of various types, the enhancer of Raghu’s family, considered it appropriate to see Śrī Rāma’s feet. (17)

verses.text:
ततो द्वादशमे वर्षे शत्रुघ्नो रामपालिताम्।
अयोध्यां चकमे गन्तुमल्पभृत्यबलानुगः॥ १॥
verses.m: Then in the twelfth year Śatrughna, followed by a few attendants and the army, desired to proceed to Ayodhyā, ruled over by Śrī Rāma. (1)

verses.text:
ततो मन्त्रिपुरोगांश्च बलमुख्यान् निवर्त्य च।
जगाम हयमुख्येन रथानां च शतेन सः॥ २॥
verses.m: Then making the army-chiefs and the councillors to retreat, he (Śatrughna) proceeded riding on a special horse, accompanied by a hundred chariots. (2)

verses.text:
स गत्वा गणितान् वासान् सप्ताष्टौ रघुनन्दनः।
वाल्मीकाश्रममागत्य वासं चक्रे महायशाः॥ ३॥
verses.m: Śatrughna, the descendant of the Raghus, possessed of fame, halting at seven to eight places on the way, reached the hermitage of Vālmīki and dwelt there. (3)

verses.text:
सोऽभिवाद्य ततः पादौ वाल्मीकेः पुरुषर्षभः।
पाद्यमर्घ्यं तथातिथ्यं जग्राह मुनिहस्ततः॥ ४॥
verses.m: Having paid obeisance at the feet of sage Vālmīki, the famous Śatrughna accepted ablutions, offerings and hospitality from the sage. (4)

verses.text:
बहुरूपाः सुमधुराः कथास्तत्र सहस्रशः।
कथयामास स मुनिः शत्रुघ्नाय महात्मने॥ ५॥
verses.m: The sage, Vālmīki, narrated to the noble Śatrughna sweet tales of various themes. (5)

verses.text:
उवाच च मुनिर्वाक्यं लवणस्य वधाश्रितम्।
सुदुष्करं कृतं कर्म लवणं निघ्नता त्वया॥ ६॥
verses.m: Referring to the killing of Lavaṇa, the sage said: ‘By killing Lavaṇa, a difficult task has been accomplished by you. (6)

verses.text:
बहवः पार्थिवाः सौम्य हताः सबलवाहनाः।
लवणेन महाबाहो युध्यमाना महाबलाः॥ ७॥
verses.m: ‘O gracious one, of long-arms, many powerful kings, together with their army and carriers had been killed by Lavaṇa, when they came in encounter with him. (7)

verses.text:
स त्वया निहतः पापो लीलया पुरुषर्षभ।
जगतश्च भयं तत्र प्रशान्तं तव तेजसा॥ ८॥
verses.m: ‘O Bull among men, that evil one has been killed by you with ease, and by your prowess, the fright of worlds due to him has been dispelled. (8)

verses.text:
रावणस्य वधो घोरो यत्नेन महता कृताः।
इदं च सुमहत्कर्म त्वया कृतमयत्नतः॥ ९॥
verses.m: ‘The dreadful killing of Rāvaṇa by Śrī Rāma was achieved with great effort; this great task of killing Lavaṇa was performed by you without effort. (9)

verses.text:
प्रीतिश्चास्मिन् परा जाता देवानां लवणे हते।
भूतानां चैव सर्वेषां जगतश्च प्रियं कृतम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: ‘On Lavaṇa being killed, the gods are highly pleased. This admirable deed for all beings and the world has been performed by you. (10)

verses.text:
तच्च युद्धं मया दृष्टं यथावत् पुरुषर्षभ।
सभायां वासवस्याथ उपविष्टेन राघव॥ ११॥
verses.m: ‘That encounter with Lavaṇa was indeed seen by me, as it ensued, while I was sitting in the assembly of Vāsava (Indra), O bull among men. (11)

verses.text:
ममापि परमा प्रीतिर्हृदि शत्रुघ्न वर्तते।
उपाघ्रास्यामि ते मूर्ध्नि स्नेहस्यैषा परा गतिः॥ १२॥
verses.m: ‘My heart too, O Śatrughna, is filled with joy; I shall smell the crown of your head as this is the highest course of affection.’ (12)

verses.text:
इत्युक्त्वा मूर्ध्नि शत्रुघ्नमुपाघ्राय महामतिः।
आतिथ्यमकरोत् तस्य ये च तस्य पदानुगाः॥ १३॥
verses.m: Thus saying and smelling the crown of the head of Śatrughna, the wise one, Vālmīki, offered hospitality to him and all those who followed him. (13)

verses.text:
स भुक्तवान् नरश्रेष्ठो गीतमाधुर्यमुत्तमम्।
शुश्राव रामचरितं तस्मिन् काले यथाक्रमम्॥ १४॥
तन्त्रीलयसमायुक्तं त्रिस्थानकरणान्वितम्।
संस्कृतं लक्षणोपेतं समतालसमन्वितम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: That jewel among men, Śatrughna, took the food offered by Vālmīki; then heard the deeds of Śrī Rāma, as they were performed by Him at that time melodiously, accompanied with the sound of the lute with proper beats and the three musical tunes manifested at proper beats, and at proper places, in Sanskrit, and according to the rules of music and also with the beat of drums at proper intervals. (14-15)

verses.text:
शुश्राव रामचरितं तस्मिन् काले पुरा कृतम्।
तान्यक्षराणि सत्यानि यथावृत्तानि पूर्वशः॥ १६॥
verses.m: Śatrughna heard the deeds of Śrī Rāma as they were performed formerly, those words (comprising the song) were true and narrated as per the deeds performed in sequence. (16)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा पुरुषशार्दूलो विसंज्ञो बाष्पलोचनः।
स मुहूर्तमिवासंज्ञो विनिःश्वस्य मुहुर्मुहुः॥ १७॥
verses.m: Having heard the story duly sung, the lion among men, Śatrughna, with tears in his eyes, was rendered unconscious, and fell into a swoon immediately taking deep sighs repeatedly. (17)

verses.text:
तस्मिन् गीते यथावृत्तं वर्तमानमिवाशृणोत्।
पदानुगाश्च ये राज्ञस्तां श्रुत्वा गीतिसम्पदम्॥ १८॥
अवाङ्मुखाश्च दीनाश्च ह्याश्चर्यमिति चाब्रुवन्।
परस्परं च ये तत्र सैनिकाः सम्बभाषिरे॥ १९॥
verses.m: Śatrughna heard the deeds sung as if they were performed in the present. The warriors, who followed him, on hearing the rich song, were overwhelmed and speechless, indeed, and exclaimed to each other—‘How wonderful it is’. (18-19)

verses.text:
किमिदं क्व च वर्तामः किमेतत् स्वप्नदर्शनम्।
अर्थो यो नः पुरा दृष्टस्तमाश्रमपदे पुनः॥ २०॥
verses.m: ‘What is this, where are we, have we been in a dream, that thing, which we had seen formerly, we see again in the hermitage. (20)

verses.text:
शृणुमः किमिदं स्वप्ने गीतबन्धनमुत्तमम्।
विस्मयं ते परं गत्वा शत्रुघ्नमिदमब्रुवन्॥ २१॥
verses.m: ‘Do we hear in dream this beautifully composed song’ filled with great surprise, they said to Śatrughna: (21)

verses.text:
साधु पृच्छ नरश्रेष्ठ वाल्मीकिं मुनिपुङ्गवम्।
शत्रुघ्नस्त्वब्रवीत् सर्वान् कौतूहलसमन्वितान्॥ २२॥
सैनिका न क्षमोऽस्माकं परिप्रष्टुमिहेदृशः।
आश्चर्याणि बहूनीह भवन्त्यस्याश्रमे मुनेः॥ २३॥
न तु कौतूहलाद् युक्तमन्वेष्टुं तं महामुनिम्।
एवं तद् वाक्यमुक्त्वा तु सैनिकान् रघुनन्दनः।
अभिवाद्य महर्षिं तं स्वं निवेशं ययौ तदा॥ २४॥
verses.m: ‘Please ask Vālmīki, O best among men, who composed this song? Śatrughna on his part, told all the warriors filled with surprise: ‘Here I am not able to ask Vālmīki in this manner, many wonders exist here in this hermitage of the sage, it is not proper to go and question the great sage out of curiosity.’ Thus having spoken to the warriors, the scion of the Raghus then having saluted the great sage, started for his apartment. (22—24)

verses.text:
तं शयानं नरव्याघ्रं निद्रा नाभ्यागमत् तदा।
चिन्तयानमनेकार्थं रामगीतमनुत्तमम्॥ १॥
verses.m: Śatrughna, a tiger among men, could not sleep in the night ruminating over the song of Rāma’s deeds, full of meaning. (1)

verses.text:
तस्य शब्दं सुमधुरं तन्त्रीलयसमन्वितम्।
श्रुत्वा रात्रिर्जगामाशु शत्रुघ्नस्य महात्मनः॥ २॥
verses.m: Night passed away for the noble Śatrughna quickly, hearing the melodious sound of the song accompanied with that of the Vīṇā (lute) with proper beats. (2)

verses.text:
तस्यां रजन्यां व्युष्टायां कृत्वा पौर्वाह्णिकक्रमम्।
उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं शत्रुघ्नो मुनिपुङ्गवम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: After the night had ended, Śatrughna with folded hands said to Vālmīki, the best among sages, having performed the morning duties: (3)

verses.text:
भगवन् द्रष्टुमिच्छामि राघवं रघुनन्दनम्।
त्वयानुज्ञातुमिच्छामि सहैभिः संशितव्रतैः॥ ४॥
verses.m: ‘Sir, I wish to see Śrī Rāma, the scion of the Raghus, with your permission and also that of these sages, firmly adhering to their vowes.’ (4)

verses.text:
इत्येवं वादिनं तं तु शत्रुघ्नं शत्रुसूदनम्।
वाल्मीकिः सम्परिष्वज्य विससर्ज स राघवम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: Thus talking, Vālmīki embraced Śatrughna, the extirpator of foes, the scion of the Raghus, and let him go. (5)

verses.text:
सोऽभिवाद्य मुनिश्रेष्ठं रथमारुह्य सुप्रभम्।
अयोध्यामगमत् तूर्णं राघवोत्सुकदर्शनः॥ ६॥
verses.m: Saluting Vālmīki, the best among sages, he, Śatrughna, ascending the shining chariot, went on speedily to Ayodhyā, eager to see the scion of the Raghus, Śrī Rāma. (6)

verses.text:
स प्रविष्टः पुरीं रम्यां श्रीमानिक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः।
प्रविवेश महाबाहुर्यत्र रामो महाद्युतिः॥ ७॥
verses.m: The descendant of Ikṣvāku, the prosperous one, Śatrughna, reached the city, Ayodhyā, and entered the king’s palace where Śrī Rāma, the illustrious one, was. (7)

verses.text:
स रामं मन्त्रिमध्यस्थं पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननम्।
पश्यन्नमरमध्यस्थं सहस्रनयनं यथा॥ ८॥
सोऽभिवाद्य महात्मानं ज्वलन्तमिव तेजसा।
उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा रामं सत्यपराक्रमम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: Seeing Śrī Rāma with a face like full moon, seated among the councillors like Indra among the gods, and as if enflamed with vigour, Śatrughna with folded hands spoke to resplendant one after saluting Him: (8-9)

verses.text:
यदाज्ञप्तं महाराज सर्वं तत् कृतवानहम्।
हतः स लवणः पापः पुरी चास्य निवेशिता॥ १०॥
verses.m: ‘All that you ordered me to do, I have done; the evil Lavaṇa has been killed and the city, Madhupurī, has been reinstituted. (10)

verses.text:
द्वादशैतानि वर्षाणि त्वां विना रघुनन्दन।
नोत्सहेयमहं वस्तुं त्वया विरहितो नृप॥ ११॥
verses.m: ‘These twelve years I have spent without you. O king, I cannot now live afar, separated from you. (11)

verses.text:
स मे प्रसादं काकुत्स्थ कुरुष्वामितविक्रम।
मातृहीनो यथा वत्सो न चिरं प्रवसाम्यहम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: ‘O scion of the Kakutsthas, possessed of unmitigated power, give me thy favour, I cannot live without you for long, like a child separated from its mother.’ (12)

verses.text:
एवं ब्रुवाणं शत्रुघ्नं परिष्वज्येदमब्रवीत्।
मा विषादं कृथाः शूर नैतत् क्षत्रियचेष्टितम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: Then the scion of the Kakutsthas, Śrī Rāma, embraced him, Śatrughna, who spoke thus and said: ‘O brave one, do not lose heart, this does not become a Kṣatriya. (13)

verses.text:
नावसीदन्ति राजानो विप्रवासेषु राघव।
प्रजा च परिपाल्या हि क्षात्रधर्मेण राघव॥ १४॥
verses.m: ‘O descendant of Raghu, Śatrughna, the Kings staying away from their kingdom are not disheartened; the subjects are indeed to be protected as laid down among duties for the Kṣatriya. (14)

verses.text:
काले काले तु मां वीर अयोध्यामवलोकितुम्।
आगच्छ त्वं नरश्रेष्ठ गन्तासि च पुरं तव॥ १५॥
verses.m: ‘O brave one, come from time to time again to Ayodhyā to see me. O best among men, you should go to your city, the city of Madhurā. (15)

verses.text:
ममापि त्वं सुदयितः प्राणैरपि न संशयः।
अवश्यं करणीयं च राज्यस्य परिपालनम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: ‘You indeed are dearer to me than my life, there is no doubt. But for you looking after your territory is indeed obligatory. (16)

verses.text:
तस्मात् त्वं वस काकुत्स्थ सप्तरात्रं मया सह।
ऊर्ध्वं गन्तासि मधुरां सभृत्यबलवाहनः॥ १७॥
verses.m: ‘Therefore, O scion of the Kakutsthas, stay with me for seven nights and then you should proceed to Madhurā with attendants, army and carriers.’ (17)

verses.text:
रामस्यैतद् वचः श्रुत्वा धर्मयुक्तं मनोऽनुगम्।
शत्रुघ्नो दीनया वाचा बाढमित्येव चाब्रवीत्॥ १८॥
verses.m: Hearing these words of Śrī Rāma, spoken rightfully and in accordance with his Dharma, Śatrughna in a depressed tone spoke ‘So be it.’ (18)

verses.text:
सप्तरात्रं च काकुत्स्थो राघवस्य यथाज्ञया।
उष्य तत्र महेष्वासो गमनायोपचक्रमे॥ १९॥
verses.m: As desired by the descendant of Raghu, Śrī Rāma, Śatrughna, the mighty one, made himself ready to depart, having spent seven nights there. (19)

verses.text:
आमन्त्र्य तु महात्मानं रामं सत्यपराक्रमम्।
भरतं लक्ष्मणं चैव महारथमुपारुहत्॥ २०॥
verses.m: Taking leave of the noble Śrī Rāma of true valour, and also Bharata and Lakṣmaṇa, he ascended the marvellous chariot. (20)

verses.text:
दूरं पद्भ्यामनुगतो लक्ष्मणेन महात्मना।
भरतेन च शत्रुघ्नो जगामाशु पुरीं तदा॥ २१॥
verses.m: Followed by the noble Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata on foot, for a long distance, Śatrughna sped in haste to the city, Madhupurī. (21)

verses.text:
प्रस्थाप्य तु स शत्रुघ्नं भ्रातृभ्यां सह राघवः।
प्रमुमोद सुखी राज्यं धर्मेण परिपालयन्॥ १॥
verses.m: Having despatched Śatrughna, the descendant of Raghu, Śrī Rāma, together with the two brothers lived happily and contented, ruling rightfully over his kingdom. (1)

verses.text:
ततः कतिपयाहःसु वृद्धो जानपदो द्विजः।
मृतं बालमुपादाय राजद्वारमुपागमत्॥ २॥
verses.m: Then after a few days an old Brāhmaṇa citizen of Ayodhyā, carrying his dead son’s body, appeared at the royal gate. (2)

verses.text:
रुदन् बहुविधा वाचः स्नेहदुःखसमन्वितः।
असकृत् पुत्रपुत्रेति वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह॥ ३॥
किं नु मे दुष्कृतं कर्म पुरा देहान्तरे कृतम्।
यदहं पुत्रमेकं तु पश्यामि निधनं गतम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Filled with affection and sorrow, and crying, pronounced these words (exclamations) repeatedly ‘O son ! O son ! What evil deed have I committed in my former birth that I should see my only son dead. (3-4)

verses.text:
अप्राप्तयौवनं बालं पञ्चवर्षसहस्रकम्।
अकाले कालमापन्नं मम दुःखाय पुत्रक॥ ५॥
verses.m: ‘O son, you have met with death untimely, having not reached adolescence and being a child of merely five thousand days (less than fourteen years) which leads to my sorrow.(5)

verses.text:
अल्पैरहोभिर्निधनं गमिष्यामि न संशयः।
अहं च जननी चैव तव शोकेन पुत्रक॥ ६॥
verses.m: ‘O son, I, alongwith your mother, shall meet with death in a few days, there is no doubt about it. (6)

verses.text:
न स्मराम्यनृतं ह्युक्तं न च हिंसां स्मराम्यहम्।
सर्वेषां प्राणिनां पापं न स्मरामि कदाचन॥ ७॥
verses.m: ‘I do not remember having spoken untruth, nor, even ever having committed sinful acts with regard to all beings. (7)

verses.text:
केनाद्य दुष्कृतेनायं बाल एव ममात्मजः।
अकृत्वा पितृकार्याणि गतो वैवस्वतक्षयम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: ‘Due to what evil deed, my own son, although a child, has gone away to the abode of Yama, the son of Vivasvān, without having performed the paternal rites (our last rites). (8)

verses.text:
नेदृशं दृष्टपूर्वं मे श्रुतं वा घोरदर्शनम्।
मृत्युरप्राप्तकालानां रामस्य विषये ह्ययम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: ‘I have neither seen nor heard of such untimely death, of immature type, in the territory of Śrī Rāma. (9)

verses.text:
रामस्य दुष्कृतं किञ्चिन्महदस्ति न संशयः।
यथा हि विषयस्थानां बालानां मृत्युरागतः॥ १०॥
verses.m: ‘There is no doubt that there must have been some evil deed performed by Śrī Rāma due to which indeed death meets the children in his territory. (10)

verses.text:
नह्यन्यविषयस्थानां बालानां मृत्युतो भयम्।
स राजञ्जीवयस्वैनं बालं मृत्युवशं गतम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: ‘There is no fear of death for the children in other territories. So, O king, bring back to life this child, possessed by death. (11)

verses.text:
राजद्वारि मरिष्यामि पत्न्या सार्धमनाथवत्।
ब्रह्महत्यां ततो राम समुपेत्य सुखी भव॥ १२॥
verses.m: ‘At the very royal gate, I shall lay down my life with my wife, like an orphan, O Śrī Rāma; you be happy having committed the sin of killing a Brāhmaṇa. (12)

verses.text:
भ्रातृभिः सहितो राजन् दीर्घमायुरवाप्स्यसि।
उषिताः स्म सुखं राज्ये तवास्मिन् सुमहाबल॥ १३॥
verses.m: ‘You will attain longlife with your brothers: till now we have lived happily in your kingdom, O mighty one. (13)

verses.text:
इदं तु पतितं तस्मात् तव राम वशे स्थितान्।
कालस्य वशमापन्नाः स्वल्पं हि नहि नः सुखम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: ‘This death of my son has befallen on me. Therefore, O Śrī Rāma, staying under you we are under the sway of death, and there is little chance of happiness now. (14)

verses.text:
सम्प्रत्यनाथो विषय इक्ष्वाकूणां महात्मनाम्।
रामं नाथमिहासाद्य बालान्तकरणं ध्रुवम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: ‘Presently the reign of the noble Ikṣvākus is rendered orphan; now having accepted Śrī Rāma as the master, in whose reign certainly children’s death will occur. (15)

verses.text:
राजदोषैर्विपद्यन्ते प्रजा ह्यविधिपालिताः।
असद्वृत्ते हि नृपतावकाले म्रियते जनः॥ १६॥
verses.m: ‘The subjects, who are not protected rightfully, perish on account of the faults of the kings; when the king is not rightful, the people die untimely. (16)

verses.text:
यद् वा पुरेष्वयुक्तानि जना जनपदेषु च।
कुर्वते न च रक्षास्ति तदा कालकृतं भयम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: ‘Whatever impropriety is committed by men in towns and provinces, and if there is no protection from them, then there is indeed such untimely destruction by death. (17)

verses.text:
सुव्यक्तं राजदोषो हि भविष्यति न संशयः।
पुरे जनपदे चापि तथा बालवधो ह्ययम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: ‘Both in the towns and provinces it is clear that there must have been some fault in the king, there is no doubt, due to which this death of my son has occurred.’ (18)

verses.text:
एवं बहुविधैर्वाक्यैरुपरुध्य मुहुर्मुहुः।
राजानं दुःखसंतप्तः सुतं तमुपगूहति॥ १९॥
verses.m: Thus making such pitiful utterances again and again and keeping in check the King, inflicted by sorrow, he embraced the dead child repeatedly. (19)

verses.text:
तथा तु करुणं तस्य द्विजस्य परिदेवनम्।
शुश्राव राघवः सर्वं दुःखशोकसमन्वितम्॥ १॥
verses.m: The scion of the Raghus, Śrī Rāma, heard all the pitiful lamentations of that Brāhmaṇa, full of pain and sorrow. (1)

verses.text:
स दुःखेन च संतप्तो मन्त्रिणस्तानुपाह्वयत्।
वसिष्ठं वामदेवं च भ्रातॄंश्च सह नैगमान्॥ २॥
verses.m: Inflicted by pain He, Śrī Rāma, called His councillors, Vasiṣṭha and Vāmadeva and also his brothers, together with the citizens. (2)

verses.text:
ततो द्विजा वसिष्ठेन सार्धमष्टौ प्रवेशिताः।
राजानं देवसंकाशं वर्धस्वेति ततोऽब्रुवन्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Then eight Brāhmaṇas together with Vasiṣṭha were made to appear before the King comparable with the gods, and they said ‘victory to you.’ (3)

verses.text:
मार्कण्डेयोऽथ मौद्गल्यो वामदेवश्च काश्यपः।
कात्यायनोऽथ जाबालिर्गौतमो नारदस्तथा॥ ४॥
verses.m: Mārkaṇḍeya, Maudgalya, Vāmadeva, Kaśyapa, Kātyāyana, Jābāli, Gautama and Nārada were made to enter. (4)

verses.text:
एते द्विजर्षभाः सर्वे आसनेषूपवेशिताः।
महर्षीन् समनुप्राप्तानभिवाद्य कृताञ्जलिः॥ ५॥
मन्त्रिणो नैगमाश्चैव यथार्हमनुकूलतः।
तेषां समुपविष्टानां सर्वेषां दीप्ततेजसाम्॥ ६॥
राघवः सर्वमाचष्टे द्विजोऽयमुपरोधते।
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा राज्ञो दीनस्य नारदः॥ ७॥
प्रत्युवाच शुभं वाक्यमृषीणां संनिधौ स्वयम्।
शृणु राजन् यथाकाले प्राप्तो बालस्य संक्षयः॥ ८॥
श्रुत्वा कर्तव्यतां राजन् कुरुष्व रघुनन्दन।
पुरा कृतयुगे राजन् ब्राह्मणा वै तपस्विनः॥ ९॥
अब्राह्मणस्तदा राजन् न तपस्वी कथंचन।
तस्मिन् युगे प्रज्वलिते ब्रह्मभूते त्वनावृते॥ १०॥
verses.m: These excellent Brāhmaṇas were all provided with seats. The councillors and citizens all were suitably seated after all those effulgent ones had taken their seats. The descendant of Raghu, Śrī Rāma, having saluted the great sages with folded hands, conveyed to them: ‘This Brāhmaṇa obstructs the royal gate. Nārada hearing those words of the King in grief, replied with these opportune words in the presence of the sages; ‘Listen, O King, how the death of child has taken place untimely. Hearing what I say, O king, descendant of Raghu, do what requires to be done. In the Kṛtayuga formerly the Brāhmaṇas alone were performers of austerities; no non-Brāhmaṇas ever practised austerities in that Yuga, inflamed by penances, and dominated by Brāhmaṇa, and also there was no prevalence of ignorance. All were born immortal ones and also possessed of distant vision; then came the Tretāyuga for men possessed of mortal frame. (5—10).

verses.text:
अमृत्यवस्तदा सर्वे जज्ञिरे दीर्घदर्शिनः।
ततस्त्रेतायुगं नाम मानवानां वपुष्मताम्॥ ११॥
क्षत्रिया यत्र जायन्ते पूर्वेण तपसान्विताः।
वीर्येण तपसा चैव तेऽधिकाः पूर्वजन्मनि॥ १२॥
verses.m: ‘In Tretā, strongly built Kṣatriyas were dominant and practised austere penance. But those of Kṛtayuga were certainly superior in merit to those who belonged to Tretā (11-12)

verses.text:
मानवा ये महात्मानस्तत्र त्रेतायुगे युगे।
ब्रह्म क्षत्रं च तत् सर्वं यत् पूर्वमवरं च यत्॥ १३॥
युगयोरुभयोरासीत् समवीर्यसमन्वितम्।
अपश्यन्तस्तु ते सर्वे विशेषमधिकं ततः॥ १४॥
verses.m: ‘In Kṛtayuga Brāhmaṇas were superior and Kṣatriyas were inferior in the merits of austerity and effulgence but in Tretā both became equal and at par. (13-14)

verses.text:
स्थापनं चक्रिरे तत्र चातुर्वर्ण्यस्य सम्मतम्।
तस्मिन् युगे प्रज्वलिते धर्मभूते ह्यनावृते॥ १५॥
अधर्मः पादमेकं तु पातयत् पृथिवीतले।
अधर्मेण हि संयुक्तस्तेजो मन्दं भविष्यति॥ १६॥
verses.m: ‘Tretā is dominated by Varṇāśrama Dharma. But here itself irreligion had stepped in even though on one foot, yet hereafter gradually there will be decline in Dharma. (15-16)

verses.text:
आमिषं यच्च पूर्वेषां राजसं च मलं भृशम्।
अनृतं नाम तद् भूतं पादेन पृथिवीतले॥ १७॥
verses.m: ‘The Rājasika acts like agriculture was known to be low (अनृत) and was supposed to be not recommendable. The same act in the form of a foot of irreligion was firmly rooted on the earth in Tretā. (17)

verses.text:
अनृतं पातयित्वा तु पादमेकमधर्मतः।
ततः प्रादुष्कृतं पूर्वमायुषः परिनिष्ठितम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “This way by establishing one of his fruit in the shape of falsehood, the irreligion limited the life span of beings in Tretā in comparison to Satyayuga. (18)

verses.text:
पातिते त्वनृते तस्मिन्नधर्मेण महीतले।
शुभान्येवाचरँल्लोकः सत्यधर्मपरायणः॥ १९॥
verses.m: ‘Therefore in order to save themselves from the evil effect of falsehood, one foot of irreligion, people who were dedicated to truthful conduct scrupulously practised fully auspicious deeds. (19)

verses.text:
त्रेतायुगे च वर्तन्ते ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रियाश्च ये।
तपोऽतप्यन्त ते सर्वे शुश्रूषामपरे जनाः॥ २०॥
स्वधर्मः परमस्तेषां वैश्यशूद्रं तदागमत्।
पूजां च सर्ववर्णानां शूद्राश्चक्रुर्विशेषतः॥ २१॥
verses.m: ‘Yet in Tretā only Brāhmaṇas and Kṣatriyas engaged themselves in observing penance. The rest of the people did servicing (like production and manual labour) out of these four categories the Vaiśyas and Śūdras got as their share—the service as their own Dharma. Śūdras particularly served and adored the other three castes. (20-21)

verses.text:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तेषामधर्मे चानृते च ह।
ततः पूर्वे पुनर्ह्रासमगमन्नृपसत्तम॥ २२॥
verses.m: ‘O best among the kings, in the meanwhile the Tretā approaches its end, the Vaiśyas and Śūdras indulge in irreligion through falsehood as one of its feet. Then Brāhmaṇas and Kṣatriyas suffer more and more deterioration. (22)

verses.text:
ततः पादमधर्मस्य द्वितीयमवतारयत्।
ततो द्वापरसंख्या सा युगस्य समजायत॥ २३॥
verses.m: ‘Then unrighteousness placed on the earth its second foot, and by that the third Yuga was counted as Dvāpara (given to two feet). (23)

verses.text:
तस्मिन् द्वापरसंख्ये तु वर्तमाने युगक्षये।
अधर्मश्चानृतं चैव ववृधे पुरुषर्षभ॥ २४॥
verses.m: “With the coming into existence of the Dvāparayuga, unrighteousness and Anṛta (अनृत) flourished, O bull among men. (24)

verses.text:
अस्मिन् द्वापरसंख्याने तपो वैश्यान् समाविशत्।
त्रिभ्यो युगेभ्यस्त्रीन् वर्णान् क्रमाद् वै तप आविशत्॥ २५॥
verses.m: ‘In this Yuga, known as Dvāpara, penance entered the Vaiśya, thus through the three Yugas penance entered the three Varṇas (classes) successively. (25)

verses.text:
त्रिभ्यो युगेभ्यस्त्रीन् वर्णान् धर्मश्च परिनिष्ठितः।
न शूद्रो लभते धर्मं युगतस्तु नरर्षभ॥ २६॥
verses.m: ‘Righteousness was established in these three Yugas resorting to the three Varṇas (classes), the Śūdra could not attain the right of penance in these Yugas, O bull among men. (26)

verses.text:
हीनवर्णो नृपश्रेष्ठ तप्यते सुमहत्तपः।
भविष्यच्छूद्रयोन्यां हि तपश्चर्या कलौ युगे॥ २७॥
verses.m: ‘O best among kings, one belonging to lower caste performs severe penances. In the future Kali age the performance of penance will go to Śūdra. (27)

verses.text:
अधर्मः परमो राजन् द्वापरे शूद्रजन्मनः।
स वै विषयपर्यन्ते तव राजन् महातपाः॥ २८॥
verses.m: ‘Even in Dvāpara, penance by a Śūdra is taken to be great irreligion. (Now in Tretā surely) some Śūdra is engaged in severe penance in some frontier province—the wreched one. (28)

verses.text:
अद्य तप्यति दुर्बुद्धिस्तेन बालवधो ह्ययम्।
यो ह्यधर्ममकार्यं वा विषये पार्थिवस्य तु॥ २९॥
करोति चाश्रीमूलं तत्पुरे वा दुर्मतिर्नरः।
क्षिप्रं च नरकं याति स च राजा न संशयः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: ‘This infantile death is the result of the same. If some one practises Adharma in the territory of a King, it causes a great loss to the state prosperity and the king goes to hell; there is no doubt about it. (29-30)

verses.text:
अधीतस्य च तप्तस्य कर्मणः सुकृतस्य च।
षष्ठं भजति भागं तु प्रजा धर्मेण पालयन्॥ ३१॥
षड्भागस्य च भोक्तासौ रक्षते न प्रजाः कथम्।
स त्वं पुरुषशार्दूल मार्गस्व विषयं स्वकम्॥ ३२॥
दुष्कृतं यत्र पश्येथास्तत्र यत्नं समाचर।
एवं चेद् धर्मवृद्धिश्च नृणां चायुर्विवर्धनम्।
भविष्यति नरश्रेष्ठ बालस्यास्य च जीवितम्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: ‘Righteously ruling over the subjects, the king shares one sixth portion of the merit that accrues due to pious deeds performed by study and penance, why should partaker of one sixth not protect the subjects? So you, O lion among kings, investigate your territory. Wherever you see unrighteous actions done, then make efforts to put them right; thus righteousness and long life will prevail among men, O best among men, and also the child will come back to life.’ (31—33)

verses.text:
नारदस्य तु तद् वाक्यं श्रुत्वामृतमयं यथा।
प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे लक्ष्मणं चेदमब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Hearing those nectar-like words of Nārada, Śrī Rāma was highly pleased and spoke thus to Lakṣmaṇa: (1)

verses.text:
गच्छ सौम्य द्विजश्रेष्ठं समाश्वासय सुव्रत।
बालस्य च शरीरं तत् तैलद्रोण्यां निधापय॥ २॥
verses.m: ‘O gracious one, go and console the best among Brāhmaṇas, and place the body of the dead child in an oil tub. (2)

verses.text:
गन्धैश्च परमोदारैस्तैलैश्च सुसुगन्धिभिः।
यथा न क्षीयते बालस्तथा सौम्य विधीयताम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: ‘O gracious one, provide it (the tub) with lasting and fragrant oils, so that the body of the child may not decompose. (3)

verses.text:
यथा शरीरो बालस्य गुप्तः सन् क्लिष्टकर्मणः।
विपत्तिः परिभेदो वा न भवेच्च तथा कुरु॥ ४॥
verses.m: ‘Make arrangements to preserve the body of the child, the innocent one, so that it may not get decomposed and the limbs are not disjointed.’ (4)

verses.text:
एवं संदिश्य काकुत्स्थो लक्ष्मणं शुभलक्षणम्।
मनसा पुष्पकं दध्यावागच्छेति महायशाः॥ ५॥
verses.m: Having thus told the auspicious Lakṣmaṇa, the scion of the Kakutsthas, Śrī Rāma summoned mentally Puṣpaka: ‘Come O famous one.’ (5)

verses.text:
इङ्गितं स तु विज्ञाय पुष्पको हेमभूषितः।
आजगाम मुहूर्तेन समीपे राघवस्य वै॥ ६॥
verses.m: Puṣpaka, adorned with gold, taking the hint came at once near the descendant of Raghu, Śrī Rāma. (6)

verses.text:
सोऽब्रवीत् प्रणतो भूत्वा अयमस्मि नराधिप।
वश्यस्तव महाबाहो किंकरः समुपस्थितः॥ ७॥
verses.m: The Puṣpaka spoke bending down, to Śrī Rāma: ‘O King of long arms, here I am, your servant, at your command.’ (7)

verses.text:
भाषितं रुचिरं श्रुत्वा पुष्पकस्य नराधिपः।
अभिवाद्य महर्षीन् स विमानं सोऽध्यरोहत॥ ८॥
verses.m: Hearing these appealing words of the Puṣpaka, the king, Śrī Rāma, having saluted the great sages, ascended the plane. (8)

verses.text:
धनुर्गृहीत्वा तूणी च खड्गं च रुचिरप्रभम्।
निक्षिप्य नगरे चैतौ सौमित्रिभरतावुभौ॥ ९॥
प्रायात् प्रतीचीं हरितं विचिन्वंश्च ततस्ततः।
उत्तरामगमच्छ्रीमान् दिशं हिमवतावृताम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: Taking His bow and quiver and a dazzling sword, and leaving both Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata in the city, He went looking here and there to the western direction full of greenery and then proceeded to the northern direction covered by the snow-clad mountain, Himālaya. (9-10)

verses.text:
अपश्यमानस्तत्रापि स्वल्पमप्यथ दुष्कृतम्।
पूर्वामपि दिशं सर्वामथापश्यन्नराधिपः॥ ११॥
verses.m: Seeing not the slightest unrighteous thing done there, then He, Śrī Rāma, scanned also the whole eastern region. (11)

verses.text:
प्रविशुद्धसमाचारामादर्शतलनिर्मलाम्।
पुष्पकस्थो महाबाहुस्तदापश्यन्नराधिपः॥ १२॥
दक्षिणां दिशमाक्रामत् ततो राजर्षिनन्दनः।
शैवलस्योत्तरे पार्श्वे ददर्श सुमहत्सरः॥ १३॥
verses.m: The King, Śrī Rāma, then seated on the Puṣpaka, saw the southern quarter, where conduct was the purest, and which was as clear as the base of mirror, He saw on the northern side of the Śaivala mountain a great lake. (12-13)

verses.text:
तस्मिन् सरसि तप्यन्तं तापसं सुमहत्तपः।
ददर्श राघवः श्रीमाँल्लम्बमानमधोमुखम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: In that lake the descendant of Raghu, the noble one, saw an ascetic performing great penances, while suspended with head turned downward. (14)

verses.text:
राघवस्तमुपागम्य तप्यन्तं तप उत्तमम्।
उवाच च नृपो वाक्यं धन्यस्त्वमसि सुव्रत॥ १५॥
verses.m: The son of Raghu, the kind one, Śrī Rāma, having approached that ascetic, performing great penances, said to him: ‘O performer of vows, you are great. (15)

verses.text:
कस्यां योन्यां तपोवृद्ध वर्तसे दृढविक्रम।
कौतूहलात् त्वां पृच्छामि रामो दाशरथिर्ह्यहम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: ‘O powerful one, aged through penances, to which caste do you belong, I ask you out of curiosity. I am Rāma, son of King Daśaratha. (16)

verses.text:
कोऽर्थो मनीषितस्तुभ्यं स्वर्गलाभोऽपरोऽथवा।
वराश्रयो यदर्थं त्वं तपस्यन्यैः सुदुश्चरम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: ‘What object is desired by you to be obtained as boon, is it the attainment of the heaven or some other object, for which you perform penances, difficult to be performed by others? (17)

verses.text:
यमाश्रित्य तपस्तप्तं श्रोतुमिच्छामि तापस।
ब्राह्मणो वासि भद्रं ते क्षत्रियो वासि दुर्जयः।
वैश्यस्तृतीयो वर्णो वा शूद्रो वा सत्यवाग् भव॥ १८॥
verses.m: ‘For which object have you practised penances, that I want to hear, O ascetic? Are you a Brāhmaṇa? O good man, may welfare be with you, are you a Kṣatriya difficult to overcome, or belonging to the third caste, a Vaiśya, or a Śūdra? Please speak out the truth.’ (18)

verses.text:
इत्येवमुक्तः स नराधिपेन
अवाक्शिरा दाशरथाय तस्मै।
उवाच जातिं नृपपुङ्गवाय
यत्कारणं चैव तपःप्रयत्नः॥ १९॥
verses.m: Thus enquired by the King, the son of Daśaratha, King of Kings, that ascetic spoke of his own caste and reason for practising the penances.’ (19)

verses.text:
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा रामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः।
अवाक्शिरास्तथाभूतो वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह॥ १॥
verses.m: Hearing those words of Śrī Rāma capable of doing anything with ease, remaining with the head downwards, he (the ascetic) replied: (1)

verses.text:
शूद्रयोन्यां प्रजातोऽस्मि तप उग्रं समास्थितः।
देवत्वं प्रार्थये राम सशरीरो महायशः॥ २॥
verses.m: ‘O famous one, I am born in the line of the Śūdra caste, and have resorted to great penance. I desire godhood, O Śrī Rāma, with this body. (2)

verses.text:
न मिथ्याहं वदे राम देवलोकजिगीषया।
शूद्रं मां विद्धि काकुत्स्थ शम्बूकं नाम नामतः॥ ३॥
verses.m: ‘I do not speak untruth as I wish to conquer the world of the gods, know me as Śūdra, Śambūka by name, O scion of the Kakutsthas, Śrī Rāma.’ (3)

verses.text:
भाषतस्तस्य शूद्रस्य खड्गं सुरुचिरप्रभम्।
निष्कृष्य कोशाद् विमलं शिरश्चिच्छेद राघवः॥ ४॥
verses.m: On this the descendant of Raghu, taking out dazling sword from its sheath, chopped off the head of the Śūdra, while he was speaking thus. (4)

verses.text:
तस्मिञ्शूद्रे हते देवाः सेन्द्राः साग्निपुरोगमाः।
साधुसाध्विति काकुत्स्थं ते शशंसुर्मुहुर्मुहुः॥ ५॥
verses.m: On the Śūdra being killed, the gods headed by Agni together with Indra repeatedly praised the scion of the Kakutsthas saying: ‘Well done.’ (5)

verses.text:
पुष्पवृष्टिर्महत्यासीद् दिव्यानां सुसुगन्धिनाम्।
पुष्पाणां वायुमुक्तानां सर्वतः प्रपपात ह॥ ६॥
verses.m: A shower of very fragrant divine flowers, carried by the wind, fell from all sides. (6)

verses.text:
सुप्रीताश्चाब्रुवन् रामं देवाः सत्यपराक्रमम्।
सुरकार्यमिदं देव सुकृतं ते महामते॥ ७॥
verses.m: The gods highly pleased said to Śrī Rāma of true valour: ‘O king, O wise one, you have done this wonderful job for gods. (7)

verses.text:
गृहाण च वरं सौम्य यं त्वमिच्छस्यरिंदम।
स्वर्गभाङ् नहि शूद्रोऽयं त्वत्कृते रघुनन्दन॥ ८॥
verses.m: ‘Take whatever boon you desire, O Subjugator of foes, due to your good deed this Śūdra will not attain heaven, O descendant of Raghu’. (8)

verses.text:
देवानां भाषितं श्रुत्वा रामः सत्यपराक्रमः।
उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं सहस्राक्षं पुरंदरम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: Hearing the words of the gods, Śrī Rāma of true valour spoke to Indra the destroyer of enemy fortresses thus: (9)

verses.text:
यदि देवाः प्रसन्ना मे द्विजपुत्रः स जीवतु।
दिशन्तु वरमेतं मे ईप्सितं परमं मम॥ १०॥
verses.m: “If the gods are pleased, may that son of the Brāhmaṇa come back to life, grant me this boon, this is the best and most coveted boon for me. (10)

verses.text:
ममापचाराद् बालोऽसौ ब्राह्मणस्यैकपुत्रकः।
अप्राप्तकालः कालेन नीतो वैवस्वतक्षयम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “The only child of the Brāhmaṇa was taken to the abode of Yama, the son of Vivasvān, untimely due to my some wrongful doing. (11)

verses.text:
तं जीवयत भद्रं वो नानृतं कर्तुमर्हथ।
द्विजस्य संश्रुतोऽर्थो मे जीवयिष्यामि ते सुतम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “So please bring the child to life again, may welfare be with you. ‘I shall bring your child back to life,’ thus I have promised to the Brāhmaṇa. May my words not be untrue.” (12)

verses.text:
राघवस्य तु तद् वाक्यं श्रुत्वा विबुधसत्तमाः।
प्रत्यूचू राघवं प्रीता देवाः प्रीतिसमन्वितम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: Hearing these words of Śrī Rāma, the best among the gods, highly pleased, replied to the descendant of Raghu: (13)

verses.text:
निर्वृतो भव काकुत्स्थ सोऽस्मिन्नहनि बालकः।
जीवितं प्राप्तवान् भूयः समेतश्चापि बन्धुभिः॥ १४॥
verses.m: ‘Be contended, O Scion of Kakutstha, that child has come back to life and joined his kinsmen. (14)

verses.text:
यस्मिन् मुहूर्ते काकुत्स्थ शूद्रोऽयं विनिपातितः।
तस्मिन् मुहूर्ते बालोऽसौ जीवेन समयुज्यत॥ १५॥
verses.m: ‘The moment the Śūdra was killed, that very moment this child came to life. (15)

verses.text:
स्वस्ति प्राप्नुहि भद्रं ते साधु याम नरर्षभ।
अगस्त्यस्याश्रमपदं द्रष्टुमिच्छाम राघव॥ १६॥
verses.m: ‘Hail to Thee, we wish your welfare; now we may proceed, O bull among men, O descendant of Raghu, we wish to see the hermitage of Agastya. (16)

verses.text:
तस्य दीक्षा समाप्ता हि ब्रह्मर्षेः सुमहाद्युतेः।
द्वादशं हि गतं वर्षं जलशय्यां समासतः॥ १७॥
verses.m: ‘The brilliant one, the initiation (vow) of that Ṛṣi (sage) among Brāhmaṇas, Agastya, has come to an end, twelfth year he has passed observing the vow of sleeping on the water. (17)

verses.text:
काकुत्स्थ तद् गमिष्यामो मुनिं समभिनन्दितुम्।
त्वं चापि गच्छ भद्रं ते द्रष्टुं तमृषिसत्तमम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: ‘Therefore, O scion of Kakutstha, we shall go to applaud the sage, you too should go to see that great sage; we wish your welfare!’(18)

verses.text:
स तथेति प्रतिज्ञाय देवानां रघुनन्दनः।
आरुरोह विमानं तं पुष्पकं हेमभूषितम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: ‘The descendant of the Raghus, Śrī Rāma, having promised to do so, ascended the chariot, Puṣpaka, ornamented with gold. (19)

verses.text:
ततो देवाः प्रयातास्ते विमानैर्बहुविस्तरैः।
रामोऽप्यनुजगामाशु कुम्भयोनेस्तपोवनम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: Then the gods proceeded on spacious Vimānas, planes : Śrī Rāma too followed them soon to the hermitage of the pitcher-born, Agastya. (20)

verses.text:
दृष्ट्वा तु देवान् सम्प्राप्तानगस्त्यस्तपसां निधिः।
अर्चयामास धर्मात्मा सर्वांस्तानविशेषतः॥ २१॥
verses.m: Seeing the gods arrived, Agastya, the repository of penances, the holy one, worshipped all of them without discrimination. (21)

verses.text:
प्रतिगृह्य ततः पूजां सम्पूज्य च महामुनिम्।
जग्मुस्ते त्रिदशा हृष्टा नाकपृष्ठं सहानुगाः॥ २२॥
verses.m: Accepting the worship and adoring the great sage, Agastya, the gods highly pleased went away to the upper-most heaven together with their followers. (22)

verses.text:
गतेषु तेषु काकुत्स्थः पुष्पकादवरुह्य च।
ततोऽभिवादयामास अगस्त्यमृषिसत्तमम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: After the gods had departed, the scion of Kakutstha descending from Puṣpaka, made obeisance to the great sage, Agastya. (23)

verses.text:
सोऽभिवाद्य महात्मानं ज्वलन्तमिव तेजसा।
आतिथ्यं परमं प्राप्य निषसाद नराधिपः॥ २४॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma paid obeisance to the noble sage, effulgent with the Tapa of austerity and having received the best hospitality, took his seat. (24)

verses.text:
तमुवाच महातेजाः कुम्भयोनिर्महातपाः।
स्वागतं ते नरश्रेष्ठ दिष्ट्या प्राप्तोऽसि राघव॥ २५॥
verses.m: Agastya, the sage of great penances, said to Śrī Rāma : ‘Welcome to you, best among men, O descendant of Raghu, it is my fortune that you have come. (25)

verses.text:
त्वं मे बहुमतो राम गुणैर्बहुभिरुत्तमैः।
अतिथिः पूजनीयश्च मम राजन् हृदि स्थितः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “By your excellent virtues you are worthy of adoration as my honoured guest, O king, you always dwell in my heart. (26)

verses.text:
सुरा हि कथयन्ति त्वामागतं शूद्रघातिनम्।
ब्राह्मणस्य तु धर्मेण त्वया जीवापितः सुतः॥ २७॥
verses.m: “The gods say that You have come here after killing the Śūdra and by your righteous act, (of killing the Śūdra) You have thus restored to life the son of the Brāhmaṇa. (27)

verses.text:
उष्यतां चेह रजनीं सकाशे मम राघव।
प्रभाते पुष्पकेण त्वं गन्तासि पुरमेव हि॥ २८॥
त्वं हि नारायणः श्रीमांस्त्वयि सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम्।
त्वं प्रभुः सर्वदेवानां पुरुषस्त्वं सनातनः॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Stay one night with me, O descendant of Raghu, You are Nārāyaṇa (the abode of all souls), and all is established in You. You are lord of all the gods, the eternal Puruṣa, You may, indeed, go back to your city at dawn. (28-29)

verses.text:
इदं चाभरणं सौम्य निर्मितं विश्वकर्मणा।
दिव्यं दिव्येन वपुषा दीप्यमानं स्वतेजसा॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “This divine ornament glowing with its own divine lusture, O gracious one, has been made by Viśvakarmā (the divine artisan). (30)

verses.text:
प्रतिगृह्णीष्व काकुत्स्थ मत्प्रियं कुरु राघव।
दत्तस्य हि पुनर्दाने सुमहत् फलमुच्यते॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Please accept this, O scion of Kakutstha, for my pleasure, a gift when offered again constitutes great merit. (31)

verses.text:
भरणे हि भवाञ्शक्तः फलानां महतामपि।
त्वं हि शक्तस्तारयितुं सेन्द्रानपि दिवौकसः॥ ३२॥
तस्मात् प्रदास्ये विधिवत् तत् प्रतीच्छ नराधिप।
अथोवाच महात्मानमिक्ष्वाकूणां महारथः॥ ३३॥
रामो मतिमतां श्रेष्ठः क्षत्रधर्ममनुस्मरन्।
प्रतिग्रहोऽयं भगवन् ब्राह्मणस्याविगर्हितः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “You are worthy of wearing this ornament. You indeed are capable of giving precious gifts, and also protecting the gods together with Indra. Therefore, duly I give this to you, please accept it.” The wisest among the wise, the great charioteer of Ikṣvāku dynasty, Śrī Rāma while aware of his Kṣatriya duties, asked the Mahātmā: “Sir, accepting donation is not prohibited only for Brāhmaṇas. (32—34)

verses.text:
क्षत्रियेण कथं विप्र प्रतिग्राह्यं भवेत् ततः।
प्रतिग्रहो हि विप्रेन्द्र क्षत्रियाणां सुगर्हितः॥ ३५॥
ब्राह्मणेन विशेषेण दत्तं तद् वक्तुमर्हसि।
एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण प्रत्युवाच महानृषिः॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “O best among the Brāhmaṇas, it is strictly prohibited for the Kṣatriya to accept any charitable gift. It is more so in case a Brāhmaṇa is the donor. Kindly explain.” Having been thus enquired by Śrī Rāma, the great sage Agastya said in reply: (35-36)

verses.text:
आसन् कृतयुगे राम ब्रह्मभूते पुरायुगे।
अपार्थिवाः प्रजाः सर्वाः सुराणां तु शतक्रतुः॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “O Śrī Rāma! In the times during the Satyayuga, an age of Brahma, all the subjects were without a king. Later on Indra was declared as king of gods. (37)

verses.text:
ताः प्रजा देवदेवेशं राजार्थं समुपाद्रवन्।
सुराणां स्थापितो राजा त्वया देव शतक्रतुः॥ ३८॥
प्रयच्छास्मासु लोकेश पार्थिवं नरपुङ्गवम्।
यस्मै पूजां प्रयुञ्जाना धूतपापाश्चरेमहि॥ ३९॥
verses.m: Then people went to god Brahmā in order to have a king and prayed to him, ‘O Lord, you have appointed Indra as king of gods. Similarly, for us also provide a worthy man as our king, so that worshipping him we could move about in the world, becoming free of sins. (38-39)

verses.text:
न वसामो विना राज्ञा एष नो निश्चयः परः।
ततो ब्रह्मा सुरश्रेष्ठो लोकपालान् सवासवान्॥ ४०॥
समाहूयाब्रवीत् सर्वांस्तेजोभागान् प्रयच्छत।
ततो ददुर्लोकपालाः सर्वे भागान् स्वतेजसः॥ ४१॥
verses.m: ‘We shall not live without a king, This is our supreme decision.’ Then Brahmā, the highest god, after calling the guardians of regions alongwith Indra, said: ‘All of you give me a portion of your authority.’ Then all the guardians gave away a portion of their power. (40-41)

verses.text:
अक्षुपच्च ततो ब्रह्मा यतो जातः क्षुपो नृपः।
तं ब्रह्मा लोकपालानां समांशैः समयोजयत्॥ ४२॥
verses.m: ‘Then Brahmā sneezed, whence was born king Kṣupa. Brahmā invested him with the entire might of the guardians (of regions given away by them). (42)

verses.text:
ततो ददौ नृपं तासां प्रजानामीश्वरं क्षुपम्।
तत्रैन्द्रेण च भागेन महीमाज्ञापयन्नृपः॥ ४३॥
verses.m: Then he made Kṣupa the ruling king of the people. Kṣupa after becoming king ruled the earth by virtue of the portion of the might given by Indra. (43)

verses.text:
वारुणेन तु भागेन वपुः पुष्यति पार्थिवः।
कौबेरेण तु भागेन वित्तपाभां ददौ तदा॥ ४४॥
यस्तु याम्योऽभवद् भागस्तेन शास्ति स्म स प्रजाः।
तत्रैन्द्रेण नरश्रेष्ठ भागेन रघुनन्दन॥ ४५॥
प्रतिगृह्णीष्व भद्रं ते तारणार्थं मम प्रभो।
तद् रामः प्रतिजग्राह मुनेस्तस्य महात्मनः॥ ४६॥
दिव्यमाभरणं चित्रं प्रदीप्तमिव भास्करम्।
प्रतिगृह्य ततो रामस्तदाभरणमुत्तमम्॥ ४७॥
आगमं तस्य दीप्तस्य प्रष्टुमेवोपचक्रमे।
अत्यद्भुतमिदं दिव्यं वपुषा युक्तमद्भुतम्॥ ४८॥
कथं वा भवता प्राप्तं कुतो वा केन वाऽऽहृतम्।
कौतूहलतया ब्रह्मन् पृच्छामि त्वां महायशः॥ ४९॥
आश्चर्याणां बहूनां हि निधिः परमको भवान्।
एवं ब्रुवति काकुत्स्थे मुनिर्वाक्यमथाब्रवीत्॥ ५०॥
शृणु राम यथावृत्तं पुरा त्रेतायुगे युगे॥ ५१॥
verses.m: The king nourished the people by the portion of power given to him by Varuṇa. By the portion of the mighty Kubera, he then, lent to the people the glory of Kubera, the Lord of riches. By the portion of Yama he devised punishment to the people as and when they committed sin(s). ‘O Śrī Rāma, the foremost among men! (as king, you are also invested with the might of the guardians of regions). For my deliverance accept this ornament through the portion (of the might) of Indra, O Lord ! Prosperity be unto you !’ Then Śrī Rāma accepted the divine ornament, bright like the sun, given by the high-souled hermit, and asked about his acquisition of the ornament. ‘O Eminent Brāhmaṇa ! How and from where did you acquire this divine and wonderful ornament? I am asking this out of curiosity, as you are a great repository of wonders.’ After Śrī Rāma enquired of, the sage said to Śrī Rāma, ‘Listen, O Śrī Rāma, what happened in the old Tretā age.’ (44—51)

verses.text:
पुरा त्रेतायुगे राम बभूव बहुविस्तरम्।
समन्ताद् योजनशतं विमृगं पक्षिवर्जितम्॥ १॥
verses.m: “O Śrī Rāma! In the former Tretāyuga there was a forest, extending to hundred Yojanas, where there were neither animals nor birds. (1)

verses.text:
तस्मिन् निर्मानुषेऽरण्ये कुर्वाणस्तप उत्तमम्।
अहमाक्रमितुं सौम्य तदरण्यमुपागमम्॥ २॥
verses.m: “In that forest, uninhabited by men, I practised askesis, which was the best of penances, O gracious one ! I set my foot to know all about the forest. (2)

verses.text:
तस्य रूपमरण्यस्य निर्देष्टुं न शशाक ह।
फलमूलैः सुखास्वादैर्बहुरूपैश्च पादपैः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “I could not indeed specify the beauty of that forest with its tasty fruits and roots and groves of various types. (3)

verses.text:
तस्यारण्यस्य मध्ये तु सरो योजनमायतम्।
हंसकारण्डवाकीर्णं चक्रवाकोपशोभितम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “In the midst of the forest was a lake, one Yojana wide; filled with swans and ducks and beautified with Cakrawāka birds. (4)

verses.text:
पद्मोत्पलसमाकीर्णं समतिक्रान्तशैवलम्।
तदाश्चर्यमिवात्यर्थं सुखास्वादमनुत्तमम्॥ ५॥
अरजस्कं तदक्षोभ्यं श्रीमत्पक्षिगणायुतम्।
तस्मिन् सरःसमीपे तु महदद्भुतमाश्रमम्॥ ६॥
पुराणं पुण्यमत्यर्थं तपस्विजनवर्जितम्।
तत्राहमवसं रात्रिं नैदाघीं पुरुषर्षभ॥ ७॥
verses.m: “The lake was full of lotuses and water-lilies with no trace of moss, it was a great wonder, enjoyable and excelled by none, it was clear like crystal and calm and inhabited by innumerable lovely birds. Near that lake there was a strong, brilliant, wonderful hermitage, old and extremely holy; but not inhabited by the ascetics: There O bull among men ! I dwelt one summer night. (5—7)

verses.text:
प्रभाते कल्यमुत्थाय सरस्तदुपचक्रमे।
अथापश्यं शवं तत्र सुपुष्टमरजः क्वचित्॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Rising in the early morning for day-break-duties I reached the lake and then saw there a corpse (dead body) plump and spotless shining in the water. (8)

verses.text:
तिष्ठन्तं परया लक्ष्म्या तस्मिंस्तोयाशये नृप।
तमर्थं चिन्तयानोऽहं मुहूर्तं तत्र राघव॥ ९॥
विष्ठितोऽस्मि सरस्तीरे किं न्विदं स्यादिति प्रभो।
अथापश्यं मुहूर्तात् तु दिव्यमद्भुतदर्शनम्॥ १०॥
विमानं परमोदारं हंसयुक्तं मनोजवम्।
अत्यर्थं स्वर्गिणं तत्र विमाने रघुनन्दन॥ ११॥
उपास्तेऽप्सरसां वीर सहस्रं दिव्यभूषणम्।
गायन्ति काश्चिद् रम्याणि वादयन्ति तथापराः॥ १२॥
मृदङ्गवीणापणवान् नृत्यन्ति च तथापराः।
अपराश्चन्द्ररश्म्याभैर्हेमदण्डैर्महाधनैः ॥ १३॥
दोधूयुर्वदनं तस्य पुण्डरीकनिभेक्षणाः।
ततः सिंहासनं हित्वा मेरुकूटमिवांशुमान्॥ १४॥
पश्यतो मे तदा राम विमानादवरुह्य च।
तं शवं भक्षयामास स स्वर्गी रघुनन्दन॥ १५॥
verses.m: Pondering over it lying with all its beauty inside the lake, I, for a moment, O descendant of Raghu, stood apart and thought: O lord, what could this be. Then all at once I saw a divine and wonderful spacious chariot yoked by swans and having the speed of mind; O scion of Raghus! I saw a denizen of the heaven on that chariot, thousands of divinely ornamented nymphs served him, some were singing, others were melodiously playing on the Mṛdaṅga (drum), lute and Paṇava (symbol), and others were dancing; Some other with lotus-like eyes fanned his face with expensive chowries with gold-handles and the lustre comparable with the rays of the moon; Then raising himself up from the throne, as the sun rises on the summits of Meru mountain, he, the denizen of heaven getting down from the chariot ate up the corpse, while I looked on, O descendant of Raghu. (9—15)

verses.text:
ततो भुक्त्वा यथाकामं मांसं बहु सुपीवरम्।
अवतीर्य सरः स्वर्गी संस्प्रष्टुमुपचक्रमे॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Then having consumed to his satisfaction, the flesh rich in fat, the celestial being, going down the lake performed ablutions. (16)

verses.text:
उपस्पृश्य यथान्यायं स स्वर्गी रघुनन्दन।
आरोढुमुपचक्राम विमानवरमुत्तमम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Having sipped water (in ablution) in the prescribed way that celestial being, O descendant of Raghu, got ready to ascend the excellent chariot. (17)

verses.text:
तमहं देवसंकाशमारोहन्तमुदीक्ष्य वै।
अथाहमब्रुवं वाक्यं तमेव पुरुषर्षभ॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Seeing him, who was like a god, ascending the chariot, I, on my part, spoke to him these words: ‘O bull among men ! Who are you? O god-like one, O gracious one, You should tell me why you ate this loathsome food, looked down upon by others. (18)

verses.text:
को भवान् देवसंकाश आहारश्च विगर्हितः।
त्वयेदं भुज्यते सौम्य किमर्थं वक्तुमर्हसि॥ १९॥
कस्य स्यादीदृशो भाव आहारो देवसम्मतः।
आश्चर्यं वर्तते सौम्य श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः।
नाहमौपयिकं मन्ये तव भक्ष्यमिमं शवम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “ ‘You possess ethereal beauty. Sir, whose food could be this; therefore, O gracious one, I am wonder-struck. I wish to know the facts. I do not consider this corpse as your food in expediency.’ (19-20)

verses.text:
इत्येवमुक्तः स नरेन्द्र नाकी
कौतूहलात् सूनृतया गिरा च।
श्रुत्वा च वाक्यं मम सर्वमेतत्
सर्वं तथा चाकथयन्ममेति॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Thus spoken to out of curiosity and also in well-chosen words, the celestial one, O King, having heard me, narrated all that I had enquired.” (21)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा तु भाषितं वाक्यं मम राम शुभाक्षरम्।
प्राञ्जलिः प्रत्युवाचेदं स स्वर्गी रघुनन्दन॥ १॥
verses.m: Hearing the words comprised of holy syllables spoken by me, O descendant of Raghu, Śrī Rāma, the celestial being, with folded hands replied thus: (1)

verses.text:
शृणु ब्रह्मन् पुरा वृत्तं ममैतत् सुखदुःखयोः।
अनतिक्रमणीयं च यथा पृच्छसि मां द्विज॥ २॥
verses.m: “O Brāhmaṇa ! listen to what happened formerly, that could not be resisted and which is the cause of my pleasure and sorrow, as you desire to know it. (2)

verses.text:
पुरा वैदर्भको राजा पिता मम महायशाः।
सुदेव इति विख्यातस्त्रिषु लोकेषु वीर्यवान्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “In the old days, my father Vaidarbha of great fame was possessed of great power and was known in the three worlds by the name of Sudeva. (3)

verses.text:
तस्य पुत्रद्वयं ब्रह्मन् द्वाभ्यां स्त्रीभ्यामजायत।
अहं श्वेत इति ख्यातो यवीयान् सुरथोऽभवत्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Two sons were born to him from his two wives. I, the elder one, was known as Śweta, while my younger brother was known as Suratha. (4)

verses.text:
ततः पितरि स्वर्याते पौरा मामभ्यषेचयन्।
तत्राहं कृतवान् राज्यं धर्म्यं च सुसमाहितः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “On my father having attained heaven, the citizens consecrated me. And I ruled righteously, with care. (5)

verses.text:
एवं वर्षसहस्राणि समतीतानि सुव्रत।
राज्यं कारयतो ब्रह्मन् प्रजा धर्मेण रक्षतः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “O Brāhmaṇa, observer of vows, thus a thousand years passed by, with my ruling over the kingdom and protecting my subjects. (6)

verses.text:
सोऽहं निमित्ते कस्मिंश्चिद् विज्ञातायुर्द्विजोत्तम।
कालधर्मं हृदि न्यस्य ततो वनमुपागमम्॥ ७॥
सोऽहं वनमिदं दुर्गं मृगपक्षिविवर्जितम्।
तपश्चर्तुं प्रविष्टोऽस्मि समीपे सरसः शुभे॥ ८॥
verses.m: “ So, O best among Brāhmaṇas, knowing from some men about the span of my life, keeping in mind the approach of death, I came and entered this forest near the beautiful lake, difficult to enter and with no animals or birds residing therein to perform penances. (7-8)

verses.text:
भ्रातरं सुरथं राज्ये अभिषिच्य महीपतिम्।
इदं सरः समासाद्य तपस्तप्तं मया चिरम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Having consecrated Suratha as the king, and reaching this lake, I performed penances for long. (9)

verses.text:
सोऽहं वर्षसहस्राणि तपस्त्रीणि महावने।
तप्त्वा सुदुष्करं प्राप्तो ब्रह्मलोकमनुत्तमम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Practising severe austerities for three thousand years in this great forest, I obtained the world of Brahmā (heaven) excelling all other worlds. (10)

verses.text:
तस्येमे स्वर्गभूतस्य क्षुत्पिपासे द्विजोत्तम।
बाधेते परमोदार ततोऽहं व्यथितेन्द्रियः॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Having reached the heaven, O best among Brāhmaṇas, great hunger and thirst pained me and my senses were badly afflicted. (11)

verses.text:
गत्वा त्रिभुवनश्रेष्ठं पितामहमुवाच ह।
भगवन् ब्रह्मलोकोऽयं क्षुत्पिपासाविवर्जितः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Then approaching Brahmā the best in the three worlds, I said, ‘Sir, this world of Brahmā is free from hunger and thirst. (12)

verses.text:
कस्यायं कर्मणः पाकः क्षुत्पिपासानुगो ह्यहम्।
आहारः कश्च मे देव तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥ १३॥
verses.m: “ ‘As a consequence of which actions I am afflicted by hunger and thirst? What my food is, O God? O Brahmā! please tell me that’. (13)

verses.text:
पितामहस्तु मामाह तवाहारः सुदेवज।
स्वादूनि स्वानि मांसानि तानि भक्षय नित्यशः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “On this Brahmā told me, ‘O son of Sudeva, your food is your own tasty flesh, eat that for ever. (14)

verses.text:
स्वशरीरं त्वया पुष्टं कुर्वता तप उत्तमम्।
अनुप्तं रोहते श्वेत न कदाचिन्महामते॥ १५॥
verses.m: “You have well-nourished your own body performing the best of penances. That which is not sown, shall never sprout O wise one. (15)

verses.text:
दत्तं न तेऽस्ति सूक्ष्मोऽपि तप एव निषेवसे।
तेन स्वर्गगतो वत्स बाध्यसे क्षुत्पिपासया॥ १६॥
verses.m: “You have not given even the smallest thing in charity, and have only practised great penances. Therefore, having reached heaven hunger and thirst afflict you. (16)

verses.text:
स त्वं सुपुष्टमाहारैः स्वशरीरमनुत्तमम्।
भक्षयित्वामृतरसं तेन वृत्तिर्भविष्यति॥ १७॥
verses.m: “As you eat your own body, well-nourished by edibles, full of the flavour of nectar; therefore, by that (eating flesh) you will live. (17)

verses.text:
यदा तु तद्वनं श्वेत अगस्त्यः स महानृषिः।
आगमिष्यति दुर्धर्षस्तदा कृच्छ्राद् विमोक्ष्यसे॥ १८॥
verses.m: “When the great and unconquerable sage Agastya will come to that forest, O Śweta, you will be delivered of this trouble. (18)

verses.text:
स हि तारयितुं सौम्य शक्तः सुरगणानपि।
किं पुनस्त्वां महाबाहो क्षुत्पिपासावशं गतम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: “O gracious one, Agastya is capable of delivering even the host of gods, what to say of you, afflicted with hunger and thirst, O long-armed one! (19)

verses.text:
सोऽहं भगवतः श्रुत्वा देवदेवस्य निश्चयम्।
आहारं गर्हितं कुर्मि स्वशरीरं द्विजोत्तम॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Thus having learnt of the decision of the god of the gods, Brahmā, O best among men, I make food of my own body. (20)

verses.text:
बहून् वर्षगणान् ब्रह्मन् भुज्यमानमिदं मया।
क्षयं नाभ्येति ब्रह्मर्षे तृप्तिश्चापि ममोत्तमा॥ २१॥
verses.m: “O Brāhmaṇa, this body does not exhaust, although enjoyed by me for many years, and O Ṛṣi! I am fully quenched too.(21)

verses.text:
तस्य मे कृच्छ्रभूतस्य कृच्छ्रादस्माद् विमोक्षय।
अन्येषां न गतिर्ह्यत्र कुम्भयोनिमृते द्विजम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: “So deliver me—troubled one, from the difficulty. None other than Agastya, the pitcher-born ascetic, has power to do so. (22)

verses.text:
इदमाभरणं सौम्य तारणार्थं द्विजोत्तम।
प्रतिगृह्णीष्व भद्रं ते प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि॥ २३॥
verses.m: “O gracious one, best among Brāhmaṇas, accept this ornament for wearing, may welfare be with you. Please favour me by accepting this. (23)

verses.text:
इदं तावत् सुवर्णं च धनं वस्त्राणि च द्विज।
भक्ष्यं भोज्यं च ब्रह्मर्षे ददात्याभरणानि च॥ २४॥
verses.m: “All this gold, wealth, apparel, edibles and enjoyables, O Ṛṣi among Brāhmaṇas, I offer you as also the ornaments. (24)

verses.text:
सर्वान् कामान् प्रयच्छामि भोगांश्च मुनिपुङ्गव।
तारणे भगवन् मह्यं प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि॥ २५॥
verses.m: “All desirables and enjoyables also I surrender to you. I deserve to be favoured by you by releasing me of troubles.” (25)

verses.text:
तस्याहं स्वर्गिणो वाक्यं श्रुत्वा दुःखसमन्वितम्।
तारणायोपजग्राह तदाभरणमुत्तमम्॥ २६॥
