verses.m: ‘Having heard these words full of sorrow from the celestial one, I accepted this wonderful ornament for releaving him. (26)

verses.text:
मया प्रतिगृहीते तु तस्मिन्नाभरणे शुभे।
मानुषः पूर्वको देहो राजर्षेर्विननाश ह॥ २७॥
प्रणष्टे तु शरीरेऽसौ राजर्षिः परया मुदा।
तृप्तः प्रमुदितो राजा जगाम त्रिदिवं सुखम्॥ २८॥
verses.m: ‘As soon as I accepted that auspicious ornament, the former body of the Ṛṣi among kings (Śweta) vanished and the Ṛṣi among kings, extremely happy and satisfied, went to the heaven. (27-28)

verses.text:
तेनेदं शक्रतुल्येन दिव्यमाभरणं मम।
तस्मिन्निमित्ते काकुत्स्थ दत्तमद्भुतदर्शनम्॥ २९॥
verses.m: ‘By him (Śweta) equal to Indra, this divine ornament, of wonderful form, was given to me, O scion of Kakutstha, for that purpose.’ (29)

verses.text:
तदद्भुततमं वाक्यं श्रुत्वागस्त्यस्य राघवः।
गौरवाद् विस्मयाच्चैव भूयः प्रष्टुं प्रचक्रमे॥ १॥
verses.m: Hearing that most wonderful and marvellous story, narrated by Agastya, Śrī Rāma asked him again, full of dismay and reverence. (1)

verses.text:
भगवंस्तद् वनं घोरं तपस्तप्यति यत्र सः।
श्वेतो वैदर्भको राजा कथं तदमृगद्विजम्॥ २॥
verses.m: “Sir, how was that fearful forest, where the Vaidarbhaka king Śweta was performing penances, devoid of animals and birds. (2)

verses.text:
तद् वनं स कथं राजा शून्यं मनुजवर्जितम्।
तपश्चर्तुं प्रविष्टः स श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “I wish to know in detail how that king entered that forest, which was barren and uninhabited by men, to perform penances.” (3)

verses.text:
रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा कौतूहलसमन्वितम्।
वाक्यं परमतेजस्वी वक्तुमेवोपचक्रमे॥ ४॥
verses.m: Hearing the words of Śrī Rāma uttered out of curiosity, the highly powerful one, Agastya, spoke thus: (4)

verses.text:
पुरा कृतयुगे राम मनुर्दण्डधरः प्रभुः।
तस्य पुत्रो महानासीदिक्ष्वाकुः कुलनन्दनः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “In the former Kṛtayuga, Manu (Vaivasvata) was the king. His son, a joy to his family, was the famous Ikṣvāku. (5)

verses.text:
तं पुत्रं पूर्वकं राज्ये निक्षिप्य भुवि दुर्जयम्।
पृथिव्यां राजवंशानां भव कर्तेत्युवाच तम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Placing the first son, Ikṣvāku, unconquerable on the earth, incharge of the kingdom, Manu said to him: ‘Be the progenitor of all royal families.’ (6)

verses.text:
तथैव च प्रतिज्ञातं पितुः पुत्रेण राघव।
ततः परमसंतुष्टो मनुः पुत्रमुवाच ह॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Then, O descendant of Raghu, the son promised to do so and being fully satisfied Manu addressed him thus. (7)

verses.text:
प्रीतोऽस्मि परमोदार कर्ता चासि न संशयः।
दण्डेन च प्रजा रक्ष मा च दण्डमकारणे॥ ८॥
verses.m: “O noble one, I am pleased, you will be the forerunner of all royal families, there is no doubt. By punishment as a sign of authority protect the subjects; do not mete out unnecessary punishments. (8)

verses.text:
अपराधिषु यो दण्डः पात्यते मानवेषु वै।
स दण्डो विधिवन्मुक्तः स्वर्गं नयति पार्थिवम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “That form of punishment, which is meted out to the guilty men, being given in proper manner, leads the king to heaven. (9)

verses.text:
तस्माद् दण्डे महाबाहो यत्नवान् भव पुत्रक।
धर्मो हि परमो लोके कुर्वतस्ते भविष्यति॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Therefore, O dear son of long arms, make efforts to mete out punishment according to prescriptions in the Śāstras. Resorting to just punishment properly, you will attain great righteousness.” (10)

verses.text:
इति तं बहु संदिश्य मनुः पुत्रं समाधिना।
जगाम त्रिदिवं हृष्टो ब्रह्मलोकं सनातनम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: Thus, having instructed him, Manu, pleased with himself, went to the eternal abode of Brahmā through Samādhi (trance). (11)

verses.text:
प्रयाते त्रिदिवं तस्मिन्निक्ष्वाकुरमितप्रभः।
जनयिष्ये कथं पुत्रानिति चिन्तापरोऽभवत्॥ १२॥
verses.m: When Manu had left for heaven, Ikṣvāku of unlimited brilliance, fell to thinking, ‘How shall I produce sons?’ (12)

verses.text:
कर्मभिर्बहुरूपैश्च तैस्तैर्मनुसुतस्तदा।
जनयामास धर्मात्मा शतं देवसुतोपमान्॥ १३॥
verses.m: Through true actions of many types, then the son of Manu, the pious one, procreated the hundred sons, comparable with the sons of the gods. (13)

verses.text:
तेषामवरजस्तात सर्वेषां रघुनन्दन।
मूढश्चाकृतविद्यश्च न शुश्रूषति पूर्वजान्॥ १४॥
नाम तस्य च दण्डेति पिता चक्रेऽल्पमेधसः।
अवश्यं दण्डपतनं शरीरेऽस्य भविष्यति॥ १५॥
verses.m: The youngest one of them, was ignorant, and illiterate and did not serve his elders. His father gave him, dull-witted son, the name ‘Daṇḍa’, thinking that physical punishment shall certainly be the fate of this one (son). (14-15)

verses.text:
अपश्यमानस्तं देशं घोरं पुत्रस्य राघव।
विन्ध्यशैवलयोर्मध्ये राज्यं प्रादादरिंदम॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Not seeing any territory fully fearful, the father gave him the kingdom situated between the Vindhya and Śaivala mountains. (16)

verses.text:
स दण्डस्तत्र राजाभूद् रम्ये पर्वतरोधसि।
पुरं चाप्रतिमं राम न्यवेशयदनुत्तमम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “That Daṇḍa became the king of that territory situated at the foot of the mountains and established a city unmatched and the best (among the cities). (17)

verses.text:
पुरस्य चाकरोन्नाम मधुमन्तमिति प्रभो।
पुरोहितं तूशनसं वरयामास सुव्रतम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Daṇḍa named the city Madhumanta, O lord, and chose as his chief priest Uśanā, rich in vows. (18)

verses.text:
एवं स राजा तद् राज्यमकरोत् सपुरोहितः।
प्रहृष्टमनुजाकीर्णं देवराजो यथा दिवि॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Thus that king, Daṇḍa, ruled over that kingdom together with the chief priest, the Kingdom being filled with joyful men as the king of gods rules in the heaven. (19)

verses.text:
ततः स राजा मनुजेन्द्रपुत्रः
सार्धं च तेनोशनसा तदानीम्।
चकार राज्यं सुमहान्महात्मा
शक्रो दिवीवोशनसा समेतः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Then that King, Daṇḍa, the grandson of Manu, together with Uśana of great fame, ruled as a highly pious king, like Indra ruling over the gods.” (20)

verses.text:
एतदाख्याय रामाय महर्षिः कुम्भसम्भवः।
अस्यामेवापरं वाक्यं कथायामुपचक्रमे॥ १॥
verses.m: Having thus narrated the story of Ikṣvāku to Śrī Rāma, the great sage, Agastya, the pitcher-born one, began to narrate another story connected with the same. (1)

verses.text:
ततः स दण्डः काकुत्स्थ बहुवर्षगणायुतम्।
अकरोत् तत्र दान्तात्मा राज्यं निहतकण्टकम्॥ २॥
verses.m: ‘Then, O scion of Kakutstha, that Daṇḍa, the self-controlled one, ruled over that kingdom there, uprooting all foes, for successively ten thousand years. (2)

verses.text:
अथ काले तु कस्मिंश्चिद् राजा भार्गवमाश्रमम्।
रमणीयमुपाक्रामच्चैत्रे मासि मनोरमे॥ ३॥
verses.m: Then at one time the king, Daṇḍa, went to the beautiful hermitage of sage Bhārgava (Śukra), in the enjoyable month of Caitra. (3)

verses.text:
तत्र भार्गवकन्यां स रूपेणाप्रतिमां भुवि।
विचरन्तीं वनोद्देशे दण्डोऽपश्यदनुत्तमाम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: There Daṇḍa saw the daughter of Bhārgava, a paragon of beauty, roaming about in the forest. (4)

verses.text:
स दृष्ट्वा तां सुदुर्मेधा अनङ्गशरपीडितः।
अभिगम्य सुसंविग्नां कन्यां वचनमब्रवीत्॥ ५॥
verses.m: Having seen her, that wicked minded Daṇḍa, dull-witted, one afflicted by the arrows of cupid, greatly agitated approached the daughter of Bhārgava and said: (5)

verses.text:
कुतस्त्वमसि सुश्रोणि कस्य वासि सुता शुभे।
पीडितोऽहमनङ्गेन पृच्छामि त्वां शुभानने॥ ६॥
verses.m: ‘O one of beautiful hips and loins, wherefrom do you hail, O beautiful one ! whose daughter you are? O of auspicious face, afflicted as I am by cupid, I ask you.’ (6)

verses.text:
तस्य त्वेवं ब्रुवाणस्य मोहोन्मत्तस्य कामिनः।
भार्गवी प्रत्युवाचेदं वचः सानुनयं त्विदम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: When he said so, blinded by the sexual urge and madly infatuated as he was, the daughter of Bhārgava replied thus courteously: (7)

verses.text:
भार्गवस्य सुतां विद्धि देवस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः।
अरजां नाम राजेन्द्र ज्येष्ठामाश्रमवासिनीम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: ‘Know me as the daughter of the lord Bhārgava, unwearied in action, named Arajā, the eldest one residing in the hermitage. (8)

verses.text:
मा मां स्पृश बलाद् राजन् कन्या पितृवशा ह्यहम्।
गुरुः पिता मे राजेन्द्र त्वं च शिष्यो महात्मनः॥ ९॥
verses.m: ‘Do not touch me by force, I am under the control of my father, O best among kings. My father is your preceptor and you are the pupil of that noble one. (9)

verses.text:
व्यसनं सुमहत् क्रुद्धः स ते दद्यान्महातपाः।
यदि वान्यन्मया कार्यं धर्मदृष्टेन सत्पथा॥ १०॥
वरयस्व नरश्रेष्ठ पितरं मे महाद्युतिम्।
अन्यथा तु फलं तुभ्यं भवेद् घोराभिसंहितम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: ‘Enraged, he (Bhārgava), the performer of great penances, shall cause you much grief. If, however, for something other than mere passion, you desire me, then ask my hand following the righteous path from my father, O best among men; otherwise you will meet with frightful consequences. (10-11)

verses.text:
क्रोधेन हि पिता मेऽसौ त्रैलोक्यमपि निर्दहेत्।
दास्यते चानवद्याङ्ग तव मा याचितः पिता॥ १२॥
verses.m: ‘In anger my father would burn up the three worlds O one of perfect limbs. He will give me to you if asked for.’ (12)

verses.text:
एवं ब्रुवाणामरजां दण्डः कामवशं गतः।
प्रत्युवाच मदोन्मत्तः शिरस्याधाय चाञ्जलिम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: To Arajā speaking thus, Daṇḍa under the power of cupid, intoxicated with passion, replied folding his hands over his head: (13)

verses.text:
प्रसादं कुरु सुश्रोणि न कालं क्षेप्तुमर्हसि।
त्वत्कृते हि मम प्राणा विदीर्यन्ते वरानने॥ १४॥
verses.m: ‘Please favour me, O one of beautiful hips and loins, do not delay, O beautiful one, my vital breaths are shattering on your account. (14)

verses.text:
त्वां प्राप्य तु वधो वापि पापं वापि सुदारुणम्।
भक्तं भजस्व मां भीरु भजमानं सुविह्वलम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: ‘By possessing you, let there be my death, or a great sin committed, accept me, devoted to you and asking for you, highly agitated.’ (15)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा तु तां कन्यां दोर्भ्यां प्राप्य बलाद् बली।
विस्फुरन्तीं यथाकामं मैथुनायोपचक्रमे॥ १६॥
verses.m: Thus saying, he, Daṇḍa, the strong one, seizing the trembling daughter of Bhārgava between his arms by force, he raped her. (16)

verses.text:
तमनर्थं महाघोरं दण्डः कृत्वा सुदारुणम्।
नगरं प्रययावाशु मधुमन्तमनुत्तमम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: Having committed that terrible heinous crime, he went back soon to the unparalleled Madhumanta. (17)

verses.text:
अरजापि रुदन्ती सा आश्रमस्याविदूरतः।
प्रतीक्षते सुसंत्रस्ता पितरं देवसंनिभम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: That Arajā too, remained weeping near the hermitage, and in great fright waited for her father, who was just like a god. (18)

verses.text:
स मुहूर्तादुपश्रुत्य देवर्षिरमितप्रभः।
स्वमाश्रमं शिष्यवृतः क्षुधार्तः संन्यवर्तत॥ १॥
verses.m: Having heard the account of Arajā that gracious divine Ṛṣi Bhārgava came back at once to his hermitage surrounded by his pupils, although bitten by hunger. (1)

verses.text:
सोऽपश्यदरजां दीनां रजसा समभिप्लुताम्।
ज्योत्स्नामिव ग्रहग्रस्तां प्रत्यूषे न विराजतीम्॥ २॥
verses.m: He saw the pitiable Arajā covered with semen, as the full-moon at dawn faded out due to being eclipsed. (2)

verses.text:
तस्य रोषः समभवत् क्षुधार्तस्य विशेषतः।
निर्दहन्निव लोकांस्त्रीन् शिष्यांश्चैतदुवाच ह॥ ३॥
verses.m: Anger flared up in him, specially as he was bitten by hunger, as if to burn the three worlds, and he said to his pupils: (3)

verses.text:
पश्यध्वं विपरीतस्य दण्डस्याविदितात्मनः।
विपत्तिं घोरसंकाशां क्रुद्धादग्निशिखामिव॥ ४॥
verses.m: “See how this performer of action contrary to good conduct, and ignorant one meets with severe calamities produced by me in anger, and comparable with the flames of fire. (4)

verses.text:
क्षयोऽस्य दुर्मतेः प्राप्तः सानुगस्य दुरात्मनः।
यः प्रदीप्तां हुताशस्य शिखां वै स्प्रष्टुमर्हति॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Destruction is the fate of that dull-witted one who wishes to touch the flames of the kindled fire. (5)

verses.text:
यस्मात् स कृतवान् पापमीदृशं घोरसंहितम्।
तस्मात् प्राप्स्यति दुर्मेधाः फलं पापस्य कर्मणः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “As he has committed this heinous crime, so this dull-witted one will get the fruit of his sin. (6)

verses.text:
सप्तरात्रेण राजासौ सपुत्रबलवाहनः।
पापकर्मसमाचारो वधं प्राप्स्यति दुर्मतिः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “In seven nights, this king, the dull-witted one, with his sons, army and carriers, and of sinful conduct, shall meet with death. (7)

verses.text:
समन्ताद् योजनशतं विषयं चास्य दुर्मतेः।
धक्ष्यते पांसुवर्षेण महता पाकशासनः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “For a hundred Yojanas all round, the territory of this dull-witted one, the extirpator of Pāka, Indra shall burn up with a shower of dust. (8)

verses.text:
सर्वसत्त्वानि यानीह स्थावराणि चराणि च।
महता पांसुवर्षेण विलयं सर्वतोऽगमन्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “All beings, stationary and moving, that are here, will perish due to this heavy shower of dust. (9)

verses.text:
दण्डस्य विषयो यावत् तावत् सर्वं समुच्छ्रयम्।
पांसुवर्षमिवालक्ष्यं सप्तरात्रं भविष्यति॥ १०॥
verses.m: “After seven nights, the prosperous territory of Daṇḍa will entirely disappear alongwith the shower of dust.” (10)

verses.text:
इत्युक्त्वा क्रोधताम्राक्षस्तमाश्रमनिवासिनम्।
जनं जनपदान्तेषु स्थीयतामिति चाब्रवीत्॥ ११॥
verses.m: Thus speaking to the inhabitors of the hermitage, he, Bhārgava, possessed of red eyes with rage said to them again, ‘stay at the outskirts of this territory.’ (11)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा तूशनसो वाक्यं सोऽऽश्रमावसथो जनः।
निष्क्रान्तो विषयात् तस्मात् स्थानं चक्रेऽथ बाह्यतः॥ १२॥
verses.m: Hearing these words of Uśanā, the Āśrama-dwellers, went out of his territory and made place for themselves elsewhere. (12)

verses.text:
स तथोक्त्वा मुनिजनमरजामिदमब्रवीत्।
इहैव वस दुर्मेधे आश्रमे सुसमाहिता॥ १३॥
verses.m: Having thus spoken to the ascetics, Bhārgava then addressed Arajā, “O dull-witted, you will stay in this Āśrama, conscious of your duties. (13)

verses.text:
इदं योजनपर्यन्तं सरः सुरुचिरप्रभम्।
अरजे विज्वरा भुङ्क्ष्व कालश्चात्र प्रतीक्ष्यताम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: “O Arajā, free from worry, enjoy this lake of beautiful form and extending to a Yojana, and also wait for some time. (14)

verses.text:
त्वत्समीपे च ये सत्त्वा वासमेष्यन्ति तां निशाम्।
अवध्याः पांसुवर्षेण ते भविष्यन्ति नित्यदा॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Those beings, who will come to stay near you for a night, will be unassailable forever by the shower of dust.” (15)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा नियोगं ब्रह्मर्षेः सारजा भार्गवी तदा।
तथेति पितरं प्राह भार्गवं भृशदुःखिता॥ १६॥
verses.m: “On hearing the command of the Brahmarṣi, Arajā, the daughter of Bhṛgu, despite being very much pained said to her father “Very well.” (16)

verses.text:
इत्युक्त्वा भार्गवो वासमन्यत्र समकारयत्।
तच्च राज्यं नरेन्द्रस्य सभृत्यबलवाहनम्॥ १७॥
सप्ताहाद् भस्मसाद् भूतं यथोक्तं ब्रह्मवादिना।
तस्यासौ दण्डविषयो विन्ध्यशैवलयोर्नृप॥ १८॥
शप्तो ब्रह्मर्षिणा तेन वैधर्म्ये सहिते कृते।
ततः प्रभृति काकुत्स्थ दण्डकारण्यमुच्यते॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Having said this, Bhṛgu took up his abode elsewhere. That kingdom of the chief of the kings alongwith his servants, the army and the vehicles, was reduced to ashes within seven days, as was declared by the Brahmavādī Bhṛgu. This kingdom of Daṇḍa lying between the Vindhya and the Śaivala mountains, was cursed by the Brahmarṣi, since Daṇḍa had acted unrighteously. Since then, O descendant of Kakutstha, it has been called Daṇḍakāraṇya. (17—19)

verses.text:
तपस्विनः स्थिता ह्यत्र जनस्थानमतोऽभवत्।
एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं यन्मां पृच्छसि राघव॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Since ascetics came and inhabited here it has been known as ‘Janasthāna’, O Rāma ! I have told you everything about what you enquired of me. (20)

verses.text:
संध्यामुपासितुं वीर समयो ह्यतिवर्तते।
एते महर्षयः सर्वे पूर्णकुम्भाः समन्ततः॥ २१॥
कृतोदका नरव्याघ्र आदित्यं पर्युपासते।
स तैर्ब्राह्मणमभ्यस्तं सहितैर्ब्रह्मवित्तमैः।
रविरस्तंगतो राम गच्छोदकमुपस्पृश॥ २२॥
verses.m: “O Valiant one ! The time for the performance of Sandhyā is passing. All these great sages, O foremost among men ! after having finished their bath, are worshipping the sun, with their respective pitcher filled with water. The sun, having accepted the worship in the form of recitation of Vedic hymns by the knowers of Brahma, has set in. You also go and take bath and sip water and perform Sandhyā.” (21-22)

verses.text:
ऋषेर्वचनमाज्ञाय रामः संध्यामुपासितुम्।
उपाक्रमत् सरः पुण्यमप्सरोगणसेवितम्॥ १॥
verses.m: Having heard with reverence the words of the sage, Agastya, Śrī Rāma approached the holy lake inhabited by the host of Apsarās, for performing his evening adoration. (1)

verses.text:
तत्रोदकमुपस्पृश्य संध्यामन्वास्य पश्चिमाम्।
आश्रमं प्राविशद् रामः कुम्भयोनेर्महात्मनः॥ २॥
verses.m: Having sipped the water there and performed the evening Pūjā, Śrī Rāma entered the hermitage of Agastya, the holy pitcher-born one. (2)

verses.text:
तस्यागस्त्यो बहुगुणं कन्दमूलं तथौषधम्।
शाल्यादीनि पवित्राणि भोजनार्थमकल्पयत्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Agastya offered to him for food radish of good quality and also purified rice and other edibles. (3)

verses.text:
स भुक्तवान् नरश्रेष्ठस्तदन्नममृतोपमम्।
प्रीतश्च परितुष्टश्च तां रात्रिं समुपाविशत्॥ ४॥
verses.m: That best among men, Śrī Rāma, enjoyed that food comparable with nectar, was highly pleased and satisfied. He spent that night together with the sage. (4)

verses.text:
प्रभाते काल्यमुत्थाय कृत्वाऽऽह्निकमरिंदमः।
ऋषिं समुपचक्राम गमनाय रघूत्तमः॥ ५॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma, the best among the Raghus, the tamer of foes, getting up at dawn and having performed the morning daily rites, approached the sage to beg leave of him and to depart. (5)

verses.text:
अभिवाद्याब्रवीद् रामो महर्षिं कुम्भसम्भवम्।
आपृच्छे स्वां पुरीं गन्तुं मामनुज्ञातुमर्हसि॥ ६॥
verses.m: Having saluted the great sage, born of the pitcher, Agastya, Śrī Rāma said to him: ‘I beg leave of you to depart to my own capital; may you permit me to do so. (6)

verses.text:
धन्योऽस्म्यनुगृहीतोऽस्मि दर्शनेन महात्मनः।
द्रष्टुं चैवागमिष्यामि पावनार्थमिहात्मनः॥ ७॥
verses.m: ‘I am fortunate having been favoured by seeing you. I shall come again to see you, O holy one, for purification of myself.’ (7)

verses.text:
तथा वदति काकुत्स्थे वाक्यमद्भुतदर्शनम्।
उवाच परमप्रीतो धर्मनेत्रस्तपोधनः॥ ८॥
verses.m: While Rāma spoke in this marvellous manner, the great ascetic possessed of virtuous vision was highly pleased and said : (8)

verses.text:
अत्यद्भुतमिदं वाक्यं तव राम शुभाक्षरम्।
पावनः सर्वभूतानां त्वमेव रघुनन्दन॥ ९॥
verses.m: ‘O Rāma, your speech of auspicious syllables is indeed wonderful, O descendant of Raghu, you are the purifier of all beings. (9)

verses.text:
मुहूर्तमपि राम त्वां येऽनुपश्यन्ति केचन।
पाविताः स्वर्गभूताश्च पूज्यास्ते त्रिदिवेश्वरैः॥ १०॥
verses.m: ‘The few who see you even for a moment, are purified, and attain heaven, and are worshipped by the lord of heaven (gods). (10)

verses.text:
ये च त्वां घोरचक्षुर्भिः पश्यन्ति प्राणिनो भुवि।
हतास्ते यमदण्डेन सद्यो निरयगामिनः॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Those beings on earth, who see you with inimical eyes, they are instantly struck by the rod of Yama and descend to hell.(11)

verses.text:
ईदृशस्त्वं रघुश्रेष्ठ पावनः सर्वदेहिनाम्।
भुवि त्वां कथयन्तो हि सिद्धिमेष्यन्ति राघव॥ १२॥
verses.m: ‘O best among the Raghus, in this manner you are the purifier of all mortals, O scion of Raghu. The one describing Your sports (Līlās) on earth shall attain perfection. (12)

verses.text:
त्वं गच्छारिष्टमव्यग्रः पन्थानमकुतोभयम्।
प्रशाधि राज्यं धर्मेण गतिर्हि जगतो भवान्॥ १३॥
verses.m: ‘You go with pleasure on your path unagitated and without fear and rule over your Kingdom righteously; you are the resort of this world.’ (13)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तु मुनिना प्राञ्जलिः प्रग्रहो नृपः।
अभ्यवादयत प्राज्ञस्तमृषिं सत्यशीलिनम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: Thus spoken to by the sage, the king with folded and outstretched hands, the wise one, saluted that sage of truthful conduct. (14)

verses.text:
अभिवाद्य ऋषिश्रेष्ठं तांश्च सर्वांस्तपोधनान्।
अध्यारोहत् तदव्यग्रः पुष्पकं हेमभूषितम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Saluting the best among sages, Agastya, and all other great ascetics, he ascended unagitated that Puṣpaka, ornamented with gold. (15)

verses.text:
तं प्रयान्तं मुनिगणा आशीर्वादैः समन्ततः।
अपूजयन् महेन्द्राभं सहस्राक्षमिवामराः॥ १६॥
verses.m: The host of sages on all sides honoured him with blessings as the gods honour Indra, the thousand-eyed one. (16)

verses.text:
खस्थः स ददृशे रामः पुष्पके हेमभूषिते।
शशी मेघसमीपस्थो यथा जलधरागमे॥ १७॥
verses.m: The well-composed Śrī Rāma on the Puṣpaka, ornamented with gold, looked like the moon near the cloud at the approach of the rainy season. (17)

verses.text:
ततोऽर्धदिवसे प्राप्ते पूज्यमानस्ततस्ततः।
अयोध्यां प्राप्य काकुत्स्थो मध्यकक्षामवातरत्॥ १८॥
verses.m: Then, by the advent of midday, being honoured here and there, and having reached Ayodhyā, the scion of Kakutstha descended in the middle of the city. (18)

verses.text:
ततो विसृज्य रुचिरं पुष्पकं कामगामिनम्।
विसर्जयित्वा गच्छेति स्वस्ति तेऽस्त्विति च प्रभुः॥ १९॥
verses.m: Then leaving the beautiful Puṣpaka, moving at will, He said: ‘Leaving me, go to Kubera, O powerful one; may welfare be with thee.’ (19)

verses.text:
कक्षान्तरस्थितं क्षिप्रं द्वाःस्थं रामोऽब्रवीद् वचः।
लक्ष्मणं भरतं चैव गत्वा तौ लघुविक्रमौ।
ममागमनमाख्याय शब्दापयत मा चिरम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: Then Śrī Rāma hurriedly ordered the door-keeper in the other apartment : ‘Go to Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata, those two of swift valour, and having conveyed to them my arrival, call them here, do not delay.’ (20)

verses.text:
तच्छ्रुत्वा भाषितं तस्य रामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः।
द्वाःस्थः कुमारावाहूय राघवाय न्यवेदयत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Having heard the words of Śrī Rāma, who was unwearied in performance, the door-keeper called the two princes and they reported to the scion of Raghu. (1)

verses.text:
दृष्ट्वा तु राघवः प्राप्तावुभौ भरतलक्ष्मणौ।
परिष्वज्य ततो रामो वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह॥ २॥
verses.m: The scion of the Raghus seeing both the princes arrived, embraced them and then spoke to them these words : (2)

verses.text:
कृतं मया यथा तथ्यं द्विजकार्यमनुत्तमम्।
धर्मसेतुमथो भूयः कर्तुमिच्छामि राघवौ॥ ३॥
verses.m: “I have done the service to the Brāhmaṇa as expected. Now I want to perform Rājasūya—the outer limit of piety, O brothers. (3)

verses.text:
अक्षयश्चाव्ययश्चैव धर्मसेतुर्मतो मम।
धर्मप्रवचनं चैव सर्वपापप्रणाशनम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “In my opinion the bridge of righteousness is imperishable and unchangeable; the discourse on righteousness destroys all sins. (4)

verses.text:
युवाभ्यामात्मभूताभ्यां राजसूयमनुत्तमम्।
सहितो यष्टुमिच्छामि तत्र धर्मस्तु शाश्वतः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Together with both of you, who are dear to me as myself, I wish to perform the excellent Rājasūya. Therein resides eternal righteousness. (5)

verses.text:
इष्ट्वा तु राजसूयेन मित्रः शत्रुनिबर्हणः।
सुहुतेन सुयज्ञेन वरुणत्वमुपागमत्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “The killer of foes, Mitra, attained the position of Varuṇa, having performed the Rājasūya with proper offerings and sacrifice. (6)

verses.text:
सोमश्च राजसूयेन इष्ट्वा धर्मेण धर्मवित्।
प्राप्तश्च सर्वलोकेषु कीर्तिं स्थानं च शाश्वतम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “The knower of Dharma (Law), Soma, having performed the Rājasūya, righteously, attained fame and eternal place in all the worlds. (7)

verses.text:
अस्मिन्नहनि यच्छ्रेयश्चिन्त्यतां तन्मया सह।
हितं चायतियुक्तं च प्रयतौ वक्तुमर्हथः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Reflect on what is the best this day together with me, you two active ones should tell me what is good for the world and also what is proper for the future.” (8)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा तु राघवस्यैतद् वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः।
भरतः प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह॥ ९॥
verses.m: Hearing these words of the scion of Raghus, Śrī Rāma, Bharata, proficient in speaking, spoke thus, folding his hands: (9)

verses.text:
त्वयि धर्मः परः साधो त्वयि सर्वा वसुंधरा।
प्रतिष्ठिता महाबाहो यशश्चामितविक्रम॥ १०॥
verses.m: “O righteous one, in you is established the highest form of righteousness, this entire earth and all fame, O one of long arms and possessing uncomparable valour. (10)

verses.text:
महीपालाश्च सर्वे त्वां प्रजापतिमिवामराः।
निरीक्षन्ते महात्मानं लोकनाथं यथा वयम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “All kings like us, look upon Thee, O holy one, the lord of worlds as the gods look upon Prajāpati. (11)

verses.text:
पुत्राश्च पितृवद् राजन् पश्यन्ति त्वां महाबल।
पृथिव्यां गतिभूतोऽसि प्राणिनामपि राघव॥ १२॥
verses.m: “O King, O Raghunandana of mighty strength, all kings regard you as sons look to their fathers. You are the resort of this world and also of all beings, O scion of Raghu. (12)

verses.text:
स त्वमेवंविधं यज्ञमाहर्तासि कथं नृप।
पृथिव्यां राजवंशानां विनाशो यत्र दृश्यते॥ १३॥
verses.m: “How, O king, you being so, wish to perform the Rājasūya sacrifice, in which there shall be the destruction of royal families on earth. (13)

verses.text:
पृथिव्यां ये च पुरुषा राजन् पौरुषमागताः।
सर्वेषां भविता तत्र संक्षयः सर्वकोपजः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “O King, those men, who on this earth are possessed of valour, all of them will be destroyed in that Yajña due to the anger of all. (14)

verses.text:
सर्वं पुरुषशार्दूल गुणैरतुलविक्रम।
पृथिवीं नार्हसे हन्तुं वशे हि तव वर्तते॥ १५॥
verses.m: “O lion among men, possessed of unparalleled valour, accompanied with merits, it befits you not to destroy this earth, all indeed are under your sway.” (15)

verses.text:
भरतस्य तु तद् वाक्यं श्रुत्वामृतमयं यथा।
प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे रामः सत्यपराक्रमः॥ १६॥
उवाच च शुभं वाक्यं कैकेय्यानन्दवर्धनम्।
प्रीतोऽस्मि परितुष्टोऽस्मि तवाद्य वचनेऽनघ॥ १७॥
verses.m: Hearing these nectar-like words of Bharata, Śrī Rāma of true valour was extremely pleased and said these auspicious words to the enhancer of the joy of Kaikeyī, Bharata: ‘I am pleased and satisfied today at what you say, O sinless one. (16-17)

verses.text:
इदं वचनमक्लीबं त्वया धर्मसमागतम्।
व्याहृतं पुरुषव्याघ्र पृथिव्याः परिपालनम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: ‘These words spoken by you are potent and accompanied by righteousness. O tiger among men, as they relate to the protection of the earth. (18)

verses.text:
एष्यदस्मदभिप्रायाद् राजसूयात् क्रतूत्तमात्।
निवर्तयामि धर्मज्ञ तव सुव्याहृतेन च॥ १९॥
verses.m: ‘I refrain, after what you have said, from the performance of the excellent sacrifice, Rājasūya, that was our intention, O Knower of Dharma (Law). (19)

verses.text:
लोकपीडाकरं कर्म न कर्तव्यं विचक्षणैः।
बालानां तु शुभं वाक्यं ग्राह्यं लक्ष्मणपूर्वज।
तस्माच्छृणोमि ते वाक्यं साधु युक्तं महाबल॥ २०॥
verses.m: ‘That action is not to be undertaken by the wise which causes pain to the worlds, O elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa. The words even of the young ones are worthy of acceptance if they are carrier of good. Therefore, I have listened to your sagacious talk, O mighty one; you have spoken so well.’ (20)

verses.text:
तथोक्तवति रामे तु भरते च महात्मनि।
लक्ष्मणोऽथ शुभं वाक्यमुवाच रघुनन्दनम्॥ १॥
verses.m: When Śrī Rāma and the noble Bharata had spoken thus, Lakṣmaṇa addressed these auspicious words to Śrī Rāma: (1)

verses.text:
अश्वमेधो महायज्ञः पावनः सर्वपाप्मनाम्।
पावनस्तव दुर्धर्षो रोचतां रघुनन्दन॥ २॥
verses.m: “O descendant of Raghu, the great sacrifice, Aśvamedha, is the purifier of all sins and shall be your purifier, although difficult to perform, if you so please. (2)

verses.text:
श्रूयते हि पुरावृत्तं वासवे सुमहात्मनि।
ब्रह्महत्यावृतः शक्रो हयमेधेन पावितः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “The legend about the very noble Vāsava (Indra) is heard, that Indra tainted by the sin of the killing of Brāhmaṇa was purified by the Horse-sacrifice. (3)

verses.text:
पुरा किल महाबाहो देवासुरसमागमे।
वृत्रो नाम महानासीद् दैतेयो लोकसम्मतः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “In the ancient times, O one of long arms, in the struggle that ensued between the gods and demons, there happened to be the mighty Vṛtra, son of Diti, honoured by the worlds. (4)

verses.text:
विस्तीर्णो योजनशतमुच्छ्रितस्त्रिगुणं ततः।
अनुरागेण लोकांस्त्रीन् स्नेहात् पश्यति सर्वतः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “A hundred Yojanas horizontally and thrice in height, he out of affection for three worlds, looked on all beings with compassion. (5)

verses.text:
धर्मज्ञश्च कृतज्ञश्च बुद्ध्या च परिनिष्ठितः।
शशास पृथिवीं स्फीतां धर्मेण सुसमाहितः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Righteous and dutiful and well-composed in mind, he ruled over this wide earth righteously with great care. (6)

verses.text:
तस्मिन् प्रशासति तदा सर्वकामदुघा मही।
रसवन्ति प्रसूनानि मूलानि च फलानि च॥ ७॥
verses.m: “In his reign the earth yielded all such desirable and flavoured things, as flowers, roots and fruits. (7)

verses.text:
अकृष्टपच्या पृथिवी सुसम्पन्ना महात्मनः।
स राज्यं तादृशं भुङ्क्ते स्फीतमद्भुतदर्शनम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: “The earth belonging to him yielded forth fruits without being ploughed. He ruled over that sort of kingdom, prosperous with wonderful appearance. (8)

verses.text:
तस्य बुद्धिः समुत्पन्ना तपः कुर्यामनुत्तमम्।
तपो हि परमं श्रेयः सम्मोहमितरत् सुखम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “It arose in his mind: ‘I shall perform the penance unequalled, penance is indeed the highest form of welfare; all other forms of happiness are out of illusions.’ (9)

verses.text:
स निक्षिप्य सुतं ज्येष्ठं पौरेषु मधुरेश्वरम्।
तप उग्रं समातिष्ठत् तापयन् सर्वदेवताः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Leaving his eldest son, Madhureśwara, as in-charge of the citizens, he performed frightful penances, tormenting all gods. (10)

verses.text:
तपस्तप्यति वृत्रे तु वासवः परमार्तवत्।
विष्णुं समुपसंक्रम्य वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह॥ ११॥
verses.m: “On Vṛtra performing penances, Vāsava (Indra) being highly afraid, approaching Viṣṇu spoke thus, indeed. (11)

verses.text:
तपस्यता महाबाहो लोकाः सर्वे विनिर्जिताः।
बलवान् स हि धर्मात्मा नैनं शक्ष्यामि शासितुम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “ ‘O one of long arms, all the worlds have been conquered by him performing penances, he is righteous and powerful, I cannot subdue him. (12)

verses.text:
यद्यसौ तप आतिष्ठेद् भूय एव सुरेश्वर।
यावल्लोका धरिष्यन्ति तावदस्य वशानुगाः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “ ‘If again he performs penances, all beings of the worlds will be under him.(13)

verses.text:
तं चैनं परमोदारमुपेक्षसि महाबल।
क्षणं हि न भवेद् वृत्रः क्रुद्धे त्वयि सुरेश्वर॥ १४॥
verses.m: “ ‘O powerful one, you are overlooking this demon, O lord of the gods, if you are in anger, Vṛtra will not stand even for a moment. (14)

verses.text:
यदा हि प्रीतिसंयोगं त्वया विष्णो समागतः।
तदाप्रभृति लोकानां नाथत्वमुपलब्धवान्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “ ‘Ever since you patronised him, he has attained supremacy over the worlds.(15)

verses.text:
स त्वं प्रसादं लोकानां कुरुष्व सुसमाहितः।
त्वत्कृतेन हि सर्वं स्यात् प्रशान्तमरुजं जगत्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “So, have mercy on the worlds now; by your favour, indeed, this world will be free from pain. (16)

verses.text:
इमे हि सर्वे विष्णो त्वां निरीक्षन्ते दिवौकसः।
वृत्रघातेन महता तेषां साह्यं कुरुष्व ह॥ १७॥
verses.m: “These denizens of heaven (gods) look upon Thee, O Viṣṇu, please help them by killing the mighty Vṛtra. (17)

verses.text:
त्वया हि नित्यशः साह्यं कृतमेषां महात्मनाम्।
असह्यमिदमन्येषामगतीनां गतिर्भवान्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “By you forever succour was given to the noble ones i.e., gods. For others these ignoble Asuras are unbearable. You, Sir, are the resort of those who have no shelter.” (18)

verses.text:
लक्ष्मणस्य तु तद् वाक्यं श्रुत्वा शत्रुनिबर्हणः।
वृत्रघातमशेषेण कथयेत्याह सुव्रत॥ १॥
verses.m: Hearing those words of Lakṣmaṇa, the extirpator of foes, Śrī Rāma, said: ‘O observer of vows, narrate in totality the killing of Vṛtra.’ (1)

verses.text:
राघवेणैवमुक्तस्तु सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनः।
भूय एव कथां दिव्यां कथयामास सुव्रतः॥ २॥
verses.m: Being thus spoken to by the scion of Raghu, Śrī Rāma, the enhancer of the joy of Sumitrā, Lakṣmaṇa, the observer of vows, narrated the divine story of the killing of Vṛtra again. (2)

verses.text:
सहस्राक्षवचः श्रुत्वा सर्वेषां च दिवौकसाम्।
विष्णुर्देवानुवाचेदं सर्वानिन्द्रपुरोगमान्॥ ३॥
verses.m: ‘Having heard the words of the thousand-eyed one, Indra, and also of all the gods, Viṣṇu spoke thus to all the gods headed by Indra. (3)

verses.text:
पूर्वं सौहृदबद्धोऽस्मि वृत्रस्येह महात्मनः।
तेन युष्मत्प्रियार्थं हि नाहं हन्मि महासुरम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: ‘Formerly I was attached affectionately to Vṛtra here and thus for your good indeed I am not killing the great Asura. (4)

verses.text:
अवश्यं करणीयं च भवतां सुखमुत्तमम्।
तस्मादुपायमाख्यास्ये सहस्राक्षो वधिष्यति॥ ५॥
verses.m: ‘That which leads to your great happiness, has indeed to be performed: Therefore, I shall tell you the means by which Vṛtra will be killed; the thousand-eyed one, Indra, will kill Vṛtra. (5)

verses.text:
त्रेधाभूतं करिष्यामि आत्मानं सुरसत्तमाः।
तेन वृत्रं सहस्राक्षो वधिष्यति न संशयः॥ ६॥
verses.m: ‘O best among gods, I shall divide myself threefold, by that the thousand-eyed one, Indra, will indeed kill Vṛtra. There is no doubt about it. (6)

verses.text:
एकांशो वासवं यातु द्वितीयो वज्रमेव तु।
तृतीयो भूतलं यातु तदा वृत्रं हनिष्यति॥ ७॥
verses.m: ‘One part of mine may go to Vāsava (Indra), the second part may enter the thunderbolt and third, the earth; then Indra shall kill Vṛtra.’ (7)

verses.text:
तथा ब्रुवति देवेशे देवा वाक्यमथाब्रुवन्।
एवमेतन्न संदेहो यथा वदसि दैत्यहन्॥ ८॥
verses.m: On the lord of gods, Viṣṇu, speaking thus, the gods then said: ‘This is as You say, there is no doubt, O killer of the Daityas, sons of Diti. (8)

verses.text:
भद्रं तेऽस्तु गमिष्यामो वृत्रासुरवधैषिणः।
भजस्व परमोदार वासवं स्वेन तेजसा॥ ९॥
verses.m: ‘Let welfare be with You, we shall now depart desiring the killing of the Asura, Vṛtra. O extremely liberal one, Viṣṇu, may you bestow Vāsava with your power.’ (9)

verses.text:
ततः सर्वे महात्मानः सहस्राक्षपुरोगमाः।
तदरण्यमुपाक्रामन् यत्र वृत्रो महासुरः॥ १०॥
verses.m: Then all the noble ones headed by the thousand-eyed god, Indra, went to that forest where the great Asura, Vṛtra, was. (10)

verses.text:
तेऽपश्यंस्तेजसा भूतं तप्यन्तमसुरोत्तमम्।
पिबन्तमिव लोकांस्त्रीन् निर्दहन्तमिवाम्बरम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: They saw the mighty Asura possessed of his own power performing penance, as if drinking the three worlds and burning up the sky. (11)

verses.text:
दृष्ट्वैव चासुरश्रेष्ठं देवास्त्रासमुपागमन्।
कथमेनं वधिष्यामः कथं न स्यात् पराजयः॥ १२॥
verses.m: On seeing the best of Asuras, gods were frightened, and thought ‘how shall we kill him, and how indeed we shall not be conquered by him?’ (12)

verses.text:
तेषां चिन्तयतां तत्र सहस्राक्षः पुरंदरः।
वज्रं प्रगृह्य पाणिभ्यां प्राहिणोद् वृत्रमूर्धनि॥ १३॥
verses.m: While the gods were thus contemplating, the thousand-eyed one, the destroyer of fortress, Indra, taking hold of the thunderbolt with both of his hands, hurled it at the head of Vṛtra. (13)

verses.text:
कालाग्निनेव घोरेण दीप्तेनेव महार्चिषा।
पतता वृत्रशिरसा जगत् त्रासमुपागमत्॥ १४॥
verses.m: When the head of Vṛtra struck by the thunderbolt, blazing like fire of destruction and inflamed by its own lustre, fell down, it simultaneously terrified the whole universe. (14)

verses.text:
असम्भाव्यं वधं तस्य वृत्रस्य विबुधाधिपः।
चिन्तयानो जगामाशु लोकस्यान्तं महायशाः॥ १५॥
verses.m: The lord of the gods, possessed of fame, Indra, thinking that the killing of Vṛtra was not proper, fled soon to the ends of the earth out of fear. (15)

verses.text:
तमिन्द्रं ब्रह्महत्याऽऽशु गच्छन्तमनुगच्छति।
अपतच्चास्य गात्रेषु तमिन्द्रं दुःखमाविशत्॥ १६॥
verses.m: The slaughter of a Brāhmaṇa pursued Indra, fleeing fast and pervaded his limbs; sorrow came upon Indra. (16)

verses.text:
हतारयः प्रणष्टेन्द्रा देवाः साग्निपुरोगमाः।
विष्णुं त्रिभुवनेशानं मुहुर्मुहुरपूजयन्॥ १७॥
verses.m: With their foe killed, and bereft of Indra, the gods, with Agni at their head, worshipped Viṣṇu, the lord of the three worlds again and again. (17)

verses.text:
त्वं गतिः परमेशान पूर्वजो जगतः पिता।
रक्षार्थं सर्वभूतानां विष्णुत्वमुपजग्मिवान्॥ १८॥
verses.m: ‘O mightiest of all, you are the resort, and being born first, the father of this earth, you assumed the form of Viṣṇu for the protection of all beings. (18)

verses.text:
हतश्चायं त्वया वृत्रो ब्रह्महत्या च वासवम्।
बाधते सुरशार्दूल मोक्षं तस्य विनिर्दिश॥ १९॥
verses.m: ‘By you Vṛtra is killed; the slaughter of a Brāhmaṇa afflicts Vāsava (Indra), O lion among gods. Kindly arrange for his deliverance.’ (19)

verses.text:
तेषां तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा देवानां विष्णुरब्रवीत्।
मामेव यजतां शक्रः पावयिष्यामि वज्रिणम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: Hearing those words of the gods, Viṣṇu said “Let Indra worship me, I shall purify the carrier of the thunderbolt. (20)

verses.text:
पुण्येन हयमेधेन मामिष्ट्वा पाकशासनः।
पुनरेष्यति देवानामिन्द्रत्वमकुतोभयः॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Having propitiated me through the holy Aśvamedha, the humbler of Pāka, Indra, shall again attain the position of Indra among the gods, without fear from anywhere.” (21)

verses.text:
एवं संदिश्य तां वाणीं देवानां चामृतोपमाम्।
जगाम विष्णुर्देवेशः स्तूयमानस्त्रिविष्टपम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: Thus pronouncing those nectar-like words before the gods, the lord of the gods, Viṣṇu, being eulogized by the gods, proceeded to heaven. (22)

verses.text:
तदा वृत्रवधं सर्वमखिलेन स लक्ष्मणः।
कथयित्वा नरश्रेष्ठः कथाशेषं प्रचक्रमे॥ १॥
ततो हते महावीर्ये वृत्रे देवभयंकरे।
ब्रह्महत्यावृतः शक्रः संज्ञां लेभे न वृत्रहा॥ २॥
verses.m: That Lakṣmaṇa, having narrated the whole episode of the slaying of Vṛtra, proceeded to describe the remaining part of the story. On, Vṛtra of mighty power, a terror to the gods, being killed, Indra, the killer of Vṛtra, afflicted by the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter, became unconscious. (1-2)

verses.text:
सोऽन्तमाश्रित्य लोकानां नष्टसंज्ञो विचेतनः।
कालं तत्रावसत् कंचिद् वेष्टमान इवोरगः॥ ३॥
verses.m: Deprived of consciousness, he (Indra) went beyond the border of the world, where he remained for sometime as if writhing like a snake. (3)

verses.text:
अथ नष्टे सहस्राक्षे उद्विग्नमभवज्जगत्।
भूमिश्च ध्वस्तसंकाशा निःस्नेहा शुष्ककानना॥ ४॥
निःस्रोतसस्ते सर्वे तु ह्रदाश्च सरितस्तथा।
संक्षोभश्चैव सत्त्वानामनावृष्टिकृतोऽभवत्॥ ५॥
verses.m: The thousand-eyed one, Indra, having disappeared, the world was agitated, and the earth lost its form, moisture and the forestations, all lakes and rivulets dried up, commotion prevailed among beings due to draught. (4-5)

verses.text:
क्षीयमाणे तु लोकेऽस्मिन् सम्भ्रान्तमनसः सुराः।
यदुक्तं विष्णुना पूर्वं तं यज्ञं समुपानयन्॥ ६॥
verses.m: When the world was tottering, the gods agitated in mind, started the sacrifice that had been mentioned by Viṣṇu formerly. (6)

verses.text:
ततः सर्वे सुरगणाः सोपाध्यायाः सहर्षिभिः।
तं देशं समुपाजग्मुर्यत्रेन्द्रो भयमोहितः॥ ७॥
verses.m: Then all hosts of gods, together with the preceptors and the sages, approached the place where Indra was hiding, quite unconscious due to fear. (7)

verses.text:
ते तु दृष्ट्वा सहस्राक्षमावृतं ब्रह्महत्यया।
तं पुरस्कृत्य देवेशमश्वमेधं प्रचक्रिरे॥ ८॥
verses.m: Having seen the thousand-eyed one possessed by the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter, the gods performed the Aśvamedha with their Lord, Indra, at their head. (8)

verses.text:
ततोऽश्वमेधः सुमहान् महेन्द्रस्य महात्मनः।
ववृते ब्रह्महत्यायाः पावनार्थं नरेश्वर॥ ९॥
verses.m: Then, O lord of men, Śrī Rāma, the mighty Aśvamedha yajña came to be performed for the purification of the noble Mahendra (Indra) from the Brahma-hatyā.(9)

verses.text:
ततो यज्ञे समाप्ते तु ब्रह्महत्या महात्मनः।
अभिगम्याब्रवीद् वाक्यं क्व मे स्थानं विधास्यथ॥ १०॥
verses.m: Then as the sacrifice, Aśvamedha, came to an end, Brahma hatyā (in person) of the noble Indra approached the gods and said : ‘Where would you give me place?’ (10)

verses.text:
ते तामूचुस्ततो देवास्तुष्टाः प्रीतिसमन्विताः।
चतुर्धा विभजात्मानमात्मनैव दुरासदे॥ ११॥
verses.m: Then the gods satisfied, happily said to her (the Brahma-hatyā), ‘O one difficult to reach, divide yourself four-fold.’ (11)

verses.text:
देवानां भाषितं श्रुत्वा ब्रह्महत्या महात्मनाम्।
संदधौ स्थानमन्यत्र वरयामास दुर्वसा॥ १२॥
verses.m: Having heard the words of the noble gods, Brahma-hatyā (in person) split itself, and staying with difficulty in Indra’s person, chose shelter elsewhere. (12)

verses.text:
एकेनांशेन वत्स्यामि पूर्णोदासु नदीषु वै।
चतुरो वार्षिकान् मासान् दर्पघ्नी कामचारिणी॥ १३॥
verses.m: ‘By one part, I shall stay for four months of the rainy season, shattering the pride of sinful ones and moving at will in the rivers swollen with water. (13)

verses.text:
भूम्यामहं सर्वकालमेकेनांशेन सर्वदा।
वसिष्यामि न संदेहः सत्येनैतद् ब्रवीमि वः॥ १४॥
verses.m: By another part, I shall stay for all times on earth, there is no doubt, I speak out the truth to you all. (14)

verses.text:
योऽयमंशस्तृतीयो मे स्त्रीषु यौवनशालिषु।
त्रिरात्रं दर्पपूर्णासु वसिष्ये दर्पघातिनी॥ १५॥
verses.m: By the part which is my third one, I shall stay for three nights every month in the proud and youthful women, destroying their pride.(15)

verses.text:
हन्तारो ब्राह्मणान् ये तु मृषापूर्वमदूषकान्।
तांश्चतुर्थेन भागेन संश्रयिष्ये सुरर्षभाः॥ १६॥
verses.m: Those who kill innocent Brāhmaṇas on false pleas, them I shall attack by the fourth part, O bulls among gods.’ (16)

verses.text:
प्रत्यूचुस्तां ततो देवा यथा वदसि दुर्वसे।
तथा भवतु तत् सर्वं साधयस्व यदीप्सितम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: Then the gods replied : ‘O one of painful stay, may all that be as you say, do as you like.’ (17)

verses.text:
ततः प्रीत्यान्विता देवाः सहस्राक्षं ववन्दिरे।
विज्वरः पूतपाप्मा च वासवः समपद्यत॥ १८॥
verses.m: Then the gods fully pleased saluted the thousand-eyed one, Vāsava (Indra), since he was now carefree and purified from sin. (18)

verses.text:
प्रशान्तं च जगत् सर्वं सहस्राक्षे प्रतिष्ठिते।
यज्ञं चाद्भुतसंकाशं तदा शक्रोऽभ्यपूजयत्॥ १९॥
verses.m: On Indra being established again, the whole world was rendered calm, then Indra worshipped through the wonderful sacrifice, Aśvamedha. (19)

verses.text:
ईदृशो ह्यश्वमेधस्य प्रभावो रघुनन्दन।
यजस्व सुमहाभाग हयमेधेन पार्थिव॥ २०॥
verses.m: O descendant of Raghu, this is the results from Aśvamedha. So, O fortunate one, O King, perform the Aśvamedha sacrifice. (20)

verses.text:
इति लक्ष्मणवाक्यमुत्तमं
नृपतिरतीव मनोहरं महात्मा।
परितोषमवाप हृष्टचेताः
स निशम्येन्द्रसमानविक्रमौजाः॥ २१॥
verses.m: Having heard the beautiful and charming words of Lakṣmaṇa, the king Śrī Rāmacandra, a great soul and equal to Indra in might and valour, was very much pleased and fully satisfied. (21)

verses.text:
तच्छ्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणेनोक्तं वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः।
प्रत्युवाच महातेजाः प्रहसन् राघवो वचः॥ १॥
verses.m: Having heard the words spoken by Lakṣmaṇa, the mighty scion of Raghu, knower of the import of words, replied smilingly to him: (1)

verses.text:
एवमेव नरश्रेष्ठ यथा वदसि लक्ष्मण।
वृत्रघातमशेषेण वाजिमेधफलं च यत्॥ २॥
verses.m: “O best among men, Lakṣmaṇa, it is as you say, all that you say about the killing of Vṛtra and also the fruit of the horse-sacrifice. (2)

verses.text:
श्रूयते हि पुरा सौम्य कर्दमस्य प्रजापतेः।
पुत्रो बाह्लीश्वरः श्रीमानिलो नाम सुधार्मिकः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “O gracious one, it is heard that in the former days there was prosperous and pious Ila, ruler of Bāhlīka and the son of the Prajāpati Kardama. (3)

verses.text:
स राजा पृथिवीं सर्वां वशे कृत्वा महायशाः।
राज्यं चैव नरव्याघ्र पुत्रवत् पर्यपालयत्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “That King of high fame, having brought under his sway the whole earth, protected the kingdom like his son O tiger among men, Lakṣmaṇa. (4)

verses.text:
सुरैश्च परमोदारैर्दैतेयैश्च महाधनैः।
नागराक्षसगन्धर्वैर्यक्षैश्च सुमहात्मभिः॥ ५॥
पूज्यते नित्यशः सौम्य भयार्तै रघुनन्दन।
अबिभ्यंश्च त्रयो लोकाः सरोषस्य महात्मनः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “He was honoured always, O gracious one, by the liberal gods and the wealthy sons of Diti, and also by the Nāgas, Rākṣasas, Gandharvas and even the noble Yakṣas, possessed of fear. The three worlds were frightened when the powerful one was in rage. (5-6)

verses.text:
स राजा तादृशोऽप्यासीद् धर्मे वीर्ये च निष्ठितः।
बुद्ध्या च परमोदारो बाह्लीकेशो महायशाः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “That king, lord of Bāhlīka, of high fame, although so proficient in righteousness and valour, was very liberal at heart. (7)

verses.text:
स प्रचक्रे महाबाहुर्मृगयां रुचिरे वने।
चैत्रे मनोरमे मासे सभृत्यबलवाहनः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “That one of long arms went out to hunt in a beautiful forest together with his attendants, army and carriers in the charming month of Caitra. (8)

verses.text:
प्रजघ्ने स नृपोऽरण्ये मृगान् शतसहस्रशः।
हत्वैव तृप्तिर्नाभूच्च राज्ञस्तस्य महात्मनः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “The King killed hundreds and thousands of animals in the forest. Having killed them, however, the noble king was not satisfied. (9)

verses.text:
नानामृगाणामयुतं वध्यमानं महात्मना।
यत्र जातो महासेनस्तं देशमुपचक्रमे॥ १०॥
verses.m: “By that noble one were killed ten thousand animals of many species, he reached the place, where Mahāsena (Kārtikeya) was born. (10)

verses.text:
तस्मिन् प्रदेशे देवेशः शैलराजसुतां हरः।
रमयामास दुर्धर्षः सर्वैरनुचरैः सह॥ ११॥
verses.m: In that place the Lord of gods, the unconquerable Hara (Śiva), living with His attendants dallied with the daughter of the lord of mountains, Pārvatī. (11)

verses.text:
कृत्वा स्त्रीरूपमात्मानमुमेशो गोपतिध्वजः।
देव्याः प्रियचिकीर्षुः संस्तस्मिन् पर्वतनिर्झरे॥ १२॥
verses.m: Assuming himself the form of a woman, desiring to please the Devī Pārvatī, the lord, having the bull as emblem, stayed near that hilly stream: (12)

verses.text:
यत्र यत्र वनोद्देशे सत्त्वाः पुरुषवादिनः।
वृक्षाः पुरुषनामानस्ते सर्वे स्त्रीजना भवन्॥ १३॥
verses.m: Whatever masculine beings were there in the forest, all of them and even the trees’ masculine names were changed in the form of female beings. (13)

verses.text:
यच्च किंचन तत् सर्वं नारीसंज्ञं बभूव ह।
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे राजा स इलः कर्दमात्मजः॥ १४॥
निघ्नन् मृगसहस्राणि तं देशमुपचक्रमे।
स दृष्ट्वा स्त्रीकृतं सर्वं सव्यालमृगपक्षिणम्॥ १५॥
आत्मानं स्त्रीकृतं चैव सानुगं रघुनन्दन।
तस्य दुःखं महच्चासीद् दृष्ट्वाऽऽत्मानं तथागतम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: Whatever there was, was rendered feminine. In the meantime that King Ila, the son of Kardama, killing thousands of animals reached that place, and seeing all reptiles, animals and birds rendered feminine, and also himself together with his followers turned into feminine, he felt great sorrow, specially seeing himself in that form. (14—16)

verses.text:
उमापतेश्च तत् कर्म ज्ञात्वा त्रासमुपागमत्।
ततो देवं महात्मानं शितिकण्ठं कपर्दिनम्॥ १७॥
जगाम शरणं राजा सभृत्यबलवाहनः।
ततः प्रहस्य वरदः सह देव्या महेश्वरः॥ १८॥
प्रजापतिसुतं वाक्यमुवाच वरदः स्वयम्।
उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ राजर्षे कार्दमेय महाबल॥ १९॥
पुरुषत्वमृते सौम्य वरं वरय सुव्रत।
ततः स राजा शोकार्तः प्रत्याख्यातो महात्मना॥ २०॥
verses.m: Knowing that it was wrought by the lord of Umā, Śiva, he was afraid. Then the King together with the army and carriers sought refuge in the mighty lord, the blue-throated and skull-adorned one; the great lord Śiva, giver of boons, together with goddess Pārvatī, himself spoke to the son of Prajāpati: ‘Arise, O Ṛṣi among Kings, O mighty one, son of Kardama, performer of vows, gracious one, barring manhood ask for any boon’. Then that King being thus rebuffed, was afflicted by sorrow. (17—20)

verses.text:
स्त्रीभूतोऽसौ न जग्राह वरमन्यं सुरोत्तमात्।
ततः शोकेन महता शैलराजसुतां नृपः॥ २१॥
प्रणिपत्य उमां देवीं सर्वेणैवान्तरात्मना।
ईशे वराणां वरदे लोकानामसि भामिनी॥ २२॥
अमोघदर्शने देवि भज सौम्येन चक्षुषा।
हृद्गतं तस्य राजर्षेर्विज्ञाय हरसंनिधौ॥ २३॥
प्रत्युवाच शुभं वाक्यं देवी रुद्रस्य सम्मता।
अर्धस्य देवो वरदो वरार्धस्य तव ह्यहम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: Having become a woman, he did not ask for any other boon from the Lord of the gods, Śiva. Then in great sorrow, the King paying obeisance to the daughter of the lord of mountains, Pārvatī, with all his heart, said: ‘O goddess of boons, giver of boons, you are the loveliest woman of the worlds. O goddess whose vision is fruitful, with your benevolent eye favour me. Knowing what was in the mind of the Ṛṣi among kings, Ila, She spoke these auspicious words approved by Lord Śiva in his presence: ‘The giver of one half of the boon is the Lord and that of the other half I am the giver. (21—24)

verses.text:
तस्मादर्धं गृहाण त्वं स्त्रीपुंसोर्यावदिच्छसि।
तदद्भुततरं श्रुत्वा देव्या वरमनुत्तमम्॥ २५॥
सम्प्रहृष्टमना भूत्वा राजा वाक्यमथाब्रवीत्।
यदि देवि प्रसन्ना मे रूपेणाप्रतिमा भुवि॥ २६॥
मासं स्त्रीत्वमुपासित्वा मासं स्यां पुरुषः पुनः।
ईप्सितं तस्य विज्ञाय देवी सुरुचिरानना॥ २७॥
प्रत्युवाच शुभं वाक्यमेवमेव भविष्यति।
राजन् पुरुषभूतस्त्वं स्त्रीभावं न स्मरिष्यसि॥ २८॥
स्त्रीभूतश्च परं मासं न स्मरिष्यसि पौरुषम्।
एवं स राजा पुरुषो मासं भूत्वाथ कार्दमिः।
त्रैलोक्यसुन्दरी नारी मासमेकमिलाभवत्॥ २९॥
verses.m: ‘Therefore, accept half of the period as a woman and the other half as man for as long as you desire.’ Hearing this most wonderful and excellent boon being granted by the goddess, highly pleased the king then said: ‘O goddess, possessed of loveliness, uncomparable on this earth, if thou art pleased with me, I may remain as man for a month, and a woman for the other,’ The goddess of lovely face, having known the desire of the king, replied in these auspicious words : ‘Thus will it be; O king, becoming a man you shall not remember your woman-hood. Becoming a woman too you shall not remember your manhood’. Thus that King, son of Kardama, became a man for one month and a most beautiful lady in the next, i.e., one month Ila and one month Ilā). (25—29)

verses.text:
तां कथामैलसम्बद्धां रामेण समुदीरिताम्।
लक्ष्मणो भरतश्चैव श्रुत्वा परमविस्मितौ॥ १॥
verses.m: Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata were extremely wonderstruck, after hearing the story of Ila, narrated by Śrī Rāma. (1)

verses.text:
तौ रामं प्राञ्जली भूत्वा तस्य राज्ञो महात्मनः।
विस्तरं तस्य भावस्य तदा पप्रच्छतुः पुनः॥ २॥
verses.m: Both of them again asked Śrī Rāma with folded hands to delineate in detail the story of Ila and also his double form: (2)

verses.text:
कथं स राजा स्त्रीभूतो वर्तयामास दुर्गतिः।
पुरुषः स यदा भूतः कां वृत्तिं वर्तयत्यसौ॥ ३॥
verses.m: ‘Being formed into a woman, how did the king fare in misery, and when he was changed into a male, what was his way of life.’ (3)

verses.text:
तयोस्तद् भाषितं श्रुत्वा कौतूहलसमन्वितम्।
कथयामास काकुत्स्थस्तस्य राज्ञो यथागतम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Hearing the words of the two, spoken out of curiosity, Śrī Rāma, the scion of Kakutstha narrated the story of that king as was traditionally handed down: (4)

verses.text:
तमेव प्रथमं मासं स्त्री भूत्वा लोकसुन्दरी।
ताभिः परिवृता स्त्रीभिर्येऽस्य पूर्वं पदानुगाः॥ ५॥
verses.m: ‘Becoming a lady matchlessly beautiful for the first month, (he) was surrounded by those (women), who formerly followed him in their masculine form. (5)

verses.text:
तत्काननं विगाह्याशु विजह्रे लोकसुन्दरी।
द्रुमगुल्मलताकीर्णं पद्भ्यां पद्मदलेक्षणा॥ ६॥
verses.m: ‘The feminine bea She the unparalleled beauty of the worlds having penetrated that forest full of trees, chesters and creepers, roamed on foot, possessed of eyes like lotus-petals. (6)

verses.text:
वाहनानि च सर्वाणि संत्यक्त्वा वै समन्ततः।
पर्वताभोगविवरे तस्मिन् रेमे इला तदा॥ ७॥
verses.m: ‘Leaving aside all carriers, Ilā then sported on in that cavity of the great mountain. (7)

verses.text:
अथ तस्मिन् वनोद्देशे पर्वतस्याविदूरतः।
सरः सुरुचिरप्रख्यं नानापक्षिगणायुतम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: ‘Then in that forest, not far from the mountain, was a pond beautiful in appearance, abided by many groups of birds. (8)

verses.text:
ददर्श सा इला तस्मिन् बुधं सोमसुतं तदा।
ज्वलन्तं स्वेन वपुषा पूर्णं सोममिवोदितम्॥ ९॥
तपन्तं च तपस्तीव्रमम्भोमध्ये दुरासदम्।
यशस्करं कामकरं तारुण्ये पर्यवस्थितम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: ‘Ilā then saw in that lake Budha, the son of Soma (moon), quite youthful, effulgent with his own brilliant form as if (he was) the moon arisen. He was performing severe penance inside the waters of the lake, producing fame and fulfilling desires. (9-10)

verses.text:
सा तं जलाशयं सर्वं क्षोभयामास विस्मिता।
सह तैः पूर्वपुरुषैः स्त्रीभूतै रघुनन्दन॥ ११॥
verses.m: ‘O descendant of Raghu, fully amazed, she stirred up the entire lake together with those former men changed into women. (11)

verses.text:
बुधस्तु तां समीक्ष्यैव कामबाणवशं गतः।
नोपलेभे तदात्मानं स चचाल तदाम्भसि॥ १२॥
verses.m: ‘Budha on seeing her, came under the influence of the arrow of cupid, he could not control himself and moved in the waters. (12)

verses.text:
इलां निरीक्षमाणस्तु त्रैलोक्यादधिकां शुभाम्।
चित्तं समभ्यतिक्रामत् का न्वियं देवताधिका॥ १३॥
verses.m: ‘Perceiving Ilā, who was more auspicious than any other in the three worlds, it came to his mind: ‘Who indeed is She, lovlier than a goddess. (13)

verses.text:
न देवीषु न नागीषु नासुरीष्वप्सरःसु च।
दृष्टपूर्वा मया काचिद् रूपेणानेन शोभिता॥ १४॥
verses.m: ‘I have not seen formerly any woman possessed of such beauty among the goddesses, the female Nāgas, the wives of Asuras or even the Apsarās. (14)

verses.text:
सदृशीयं मम भवेद् यदि नान्यपरिग्रहः।
इति बुद्धिं समास्थाय जलात् कूलमुपागमत्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “If not wedded to another, she may be favourable to me. Thus thinking, Budha came out of the waters on the bank of the lake. (15)

verses.text:
आश्रमं समुपागम्य ततस्ताः प्रमदोत्तमाः।
शब्दापयत धर्मात्मा ताश्चैनं च ववन्दिरे॥ १६॥
verses.m: ‘Reaching the hermitage, he, the noble one, called those beautiful women, and they all also saluted him. (16)

verses.text:
स ताः पप्रच्छ धर्मात्मा कस्यैषा लोकसुन्दरी।
किमर्थमागता चैव सर्वमाख्यात मा चिरम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: ‘He, the noble one, then enquired of those women, thus : ‘To whom belongs this faminine beauty of the worlds? Why has she come, please let me know fully without delay?’ (17)

verses.text:
शुभं तु तस्य तद् वाक्यं मधुरं मधुराक्षरम्।
श्रुत्वा स्त्रियश्च ताः सर्वा ऊचुर्मधुरया गिरा॥ १८॥
verses.m: Hearing those words of his, spoken with sweet syllables, all those women replied in sweet tones: (18)

verses.text:
अस्माकमेषा सुश्रोणी प्रभुत्वे वर्तते सदा।
अपतिः काननान्तेषु सहास्माभिश्चरत्यसौ॥ १९॥
verses.m: ‘This woman of beautiful limbs always commands us, is unmarried and roams about in the forest alongwith us.’ (19)

verses.text:
तद् वाक्यमाव्यक्तपदं तासां स्त्रीणां निशम्य च।
विद्यामावर्तनीं पुण्यामावर्तयत स द्विजः॥ २०॥
verses.m: ‘Having heard the words of unmanifest syllables of those women, that Brāhmaṇa (Budha) recited the holy Āvartanī Vidyā Stotra or chantings. (20)

verses.text:
सोऽर्थं विदित्वा सकलं तस्य राज्ञो यथा तथा।
सर्वा एव स्त्रियस्ताश्च बभाषे मुनिपुङ्गवः॥ २१॥
verses.m: Having thus known the whole account of that king, as it had happened, the great ascetic then spoke to all those women: (21)

verses.text:
अत्र किंपुरुषीर्भूत्वा शैलरोधसि वत्स्यथ।
आवासस्तु गिरावस्मिन् शीघ्रमेव विधीयताम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: ‘Beside at the foot of this mountain as Kiṁpuruṣīs, find out your residence soon of this mountain. (22)

verses.text:
मूलपत्रफलैः सर्वा वर्तयिष्यथ नित्यदा।
स्त्रियः किंपुरुषान्नाम भर्तृन् समुपलप्स्यथ॥ २३॥
verses.m: ‘Subsist always on roots, leaves and fruits all of you women, and obtain Kiṁpuruṣas as husbands.’ (23)

verses.text:
ताः श्रुत्वा सोमपुत्रस्य स्त्रियः किंपुरुषीकृताः।
उपासांचक्रिरे शैलं वध्वस्ता बहुलास्तदा॥ २४॥
verses.m: Then those women hearing the words of the son of Soma, changed into Kiṁpuruṣīs, resided near the mountain in a large number. (24)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा किंपुरुषोत्पत्तिं लक्ष्मणो भरतस्तथा।
आश्चर्यमिति च ब्रूतामुभौ रामं जनेश्वरम्॥ १॥
verses.m: Having heard the account of the origin of Kiṁpuruṣas, Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata said to Śrī Rāma the king: ‘O Lord, how wonderful it is!’ (1)

verses.text:
अथ रामः कथामेतां भूय एव महायशाः।
कथयामास धर्मात्मा प्रजापतिसुतस्य वै॥ २॥
verses.m: Then Śrī Rāma, the noble one, continued to narrate the story of Ila, the son of Prajāpati: (2)

verses.text:
सर्वास्ता विद्रुता दृष्ट्वा किन्नरीर्ऋषिसत्तमः।
उवाच रूपसम्पन्नां तां स्त्रियं प्रहसन्निव॥ ३॥
verses.m: ‘Seeing that all the female Kinnaras (Kiṁpuruṣas) had departed, the great sage, Budha, said to that beautiful woman, Ilā, as if laughing: (3)

verses.text:
सोमस्याहं सुदयितः सुतः सुरुचिरानने।
भजस्व मां वरारोहे भक्त्या स्निग्धेन चक्षुषा॥ ४॥
verses.m: ‘O one of beautiful face, I am the beloved son of Soma, the moon-god; kindly look at me with love and own me.’ (4)

verses.text:
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा शून्ये स्वजनवर्जिते।
इला सुरुचिरप्रख्यं प्रत्युवाच महाप्रभम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: ‘Having heard those words of Budha, Ilā, left by her friends, alone, spoke to the beautiful and lustrous one, Budha: (5)

verses.text:
अहं कामचरी सौम्य तवास्मि वशवर्तिनी।
प्रशाधि मां सोमसुत यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु॥ ६॥
verses.m: ‘O son of Soma, although free to move at will, I am now at your command, order me and do as you like.’ (6)

verses.text:
तस्यास्तदद्भुतप्रख्यं श्रुत्वा हर्षमुपागतः।
स वै कामी सह तया रेमे चन्द्रमसः सुतः॥ ७॥
verses.m: Hearing these wonderful words of her, Ilā, that lover, Budha, the son of the moon, was highly pleased and dallied with her. (7)

verses.text:
बुधस्य माधवो मासस्तामिलां रुचिराननाम्।
गतो रमयतोऽत्यर्थं क्षणवत् तस्य कामिनः॥ ८॥
verses.m: While Budha was dallying with Ilā of beautiful face, the spring season passed away just like a moment. (8)

verses.text:
अथ मासे तु सम्पूर्णे पूर्णेन्दुसदृशाननः।
प्रजापतिसुतः श्रीमान् शयने प्रत्यबुध्यत॥ ९॥
verses.m: After the lapse of a month, Ila the prosperous son of Prajāpati, having a face comparable to the full moon, woke up in bed. (9)

verses.text:
सोऽपश्यत् सोमजं तत्र तपन्तं सलिलाशये।
ऊर्ध्वबाहुं निरालम्बं तं राजा प्रत्यभाषत॥ १०॥
verses.m: He saw that son of Soma was performing penance in that lake, with his hand raised upwards and without any support and addressed him thus: (10)

verses.text:
भगवन् पर्वतं दुर्गं प्रविष्टोऽस्मि सहानुगः।
न च पश्यामि तत् सैन्यं क्व नु ते मामका गताः॥ ११॥
verses.m: ‘Sir, I entered the impenetrable forest with my attendants for hunting; I do not, however, see my army, where they have gone, they who belonged to me.’ (11)

verses.text:
तच्छ्रुत्वा तस्य राजर्षेर्नष्टसंज्ञस्य भाषितम्।
प्रत्युवाच शुभं वाक्यं सान्त्वयन् परया गिरा॥ १२॥
verses.m: Having heard those words of the bull among Kings, who had lost his consciousness formerly, he, Budha, replied to him in very auspicious words, consoling him: (12)

verses.text:
अश्मवर्षेण महता भृत्यास्ते विनिपातिताः।
त्वं चाश्रमपदे सुप्तो वातवर्षभयार्दितः॥ १३॥
verses.m: ‘Your servants were killed by a hail storm; you, however, filled with fear of wind and rain fell asleep in the hermitage. (13)

verses.text:
समाश्वसिहि भद्रं ते निर्भयो विगतज्वरः।
फलमूलाशनो वीर निवसेह यथासुखम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: ‘Do not feel fear or worry. Be consoled and well. O brave one, live here happily, consuming fruits and roots.’ (14)

verses.text:
स राजा तेन वाक्येन प्रत्याश्वस्तो महामतिः।
प्रत्युवाच ततो वाक्यं दीनो भृत्यजनक्षयात्॥ १५॥
verses.m: The King possessed of wisdom having regained confidence by those words, replied auspiciously, feeling grieved on the perishing of his attendants. (15)

verses.text:
त्यक्ष्याम्यहं स्वकं राज्यं नाहं भृत्यैर्विनाकृतः।
वर्तयेयं क्षणं ब्रह्मन् समनुज्ञातुमर्हसि॥ १६॥
verses.m: ‘I shall forsake my kingdom, having lost my attendants; I shall not subsist even for a moment, O Brāhmaṇa, you should advise me : what to do. (16)

verses.text:
सुतो धर्मपरो ब्रह्मन् ज्येष्ठो मम महायशाः।
शशबिन्दुरिति ख्यातः स मे राज्यं प्रपत्स्यते॥ १७॥
verses.m: ‘My righteous and famous son, O best among Brāhmaṇas, is well-known by the name of Śaśabindu. He shall possess my kingdom. (17)

verses.text:
नहि शक्ष्याम्यहं हित्वा भृत्यदारान् सुखान्वितान्।
प्रतिवक्तुं महातेजः किंचिदप्यशुभं वचः॥ १८॥
verses.m: ‘Having lost my attendants and spouses, who were happy, O powerful one, I shall not be able to say anything inauspicious.’ (18)

verses.text:
तथा ब्रुवति राजेन्द्रे बुधः परममद्भुतम्।
सान्त्वपूर्वमथोवाच वासस्त इह रोचताम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: When the king said so, Budha said in a very pleasing manner consoling him, ‘O king, you may stay here in the Āśrama happily.’ (19)

verses.text:
न संतापस्त्वया कार्यः कार्दमेय महाबल।
संवत्सरोषितस्येह कारयिष्यामि ते हितम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: ‘O mighty one, son of Kardama, you should not be grieved. I shall do well to you, after you have passed a year here.’ (20)

verses.text:
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा बुधस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः।
वासाय विदधे बुद्धिं यदुक्तं ब्रह्मवादिना॥ २१॥
verses.m: Hearing those amiable words of that Budha, unwearied in performance, the king contemplated, residing there as advised by the discourses on Brahma by Budha. (21)

verses.text:
मासं स स्त्री तदा भूत्वा रमयत्यनिशं सदा।
मासं पुरुषभावेन धर्मबुद्धिं चकार सः॥ २२॥
verses.m: Then he, there becoming a woman, dallied constantly for ever for a month; and as a man he contemplated righteous performance for a month. (22)

verses.text:
ततः सा नवमे मासि इला सोमसुतात् सुतम्।
जनयामास सुश्रोणी पुरूरवसमूर्जितम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: Then that Ilā begot a powerful son, Purūravā in the ninth month, by Budha, the son of Soma. (23)

verses.text:
जातमात्रे तु सुश्रोणी पितुर्हस्ते न्यवेशयत्।
बुधस्य समवर्णं च इला पुत्रं महाबलम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: That one of beautiful loins, Ilā, handed over her son possessed of great power, and similar to his father, Budha, in appearance, to his father as he was born. (24)

verses.text:
बुधस्तु पुरुषीभूतं स वै संवत्सरान्तरम्।
कथाभी रमयामास धर्मयुक्ताभिरात्मवान्॥ २५॥
verses.m: For the remaining months in the completion of a year, Budha, self-possessed, however, pleased him during the months when he turned into a male, with stories full of righteous actions. (25)

verses.text:
तथोक्तवति रामे तु तस्य जन्म तदद्भुतम्।
उवाच लक्ष्मणो भूयो भरतश्च महायशाः॥ १॥
इला सा सोमपुत्रस्य संवत्सरमथोषिता।
अकरोत् किं नरश्रेष्ठ तत्त्वं शंसितुमर्हसि॥ २॥
verses.m: On Śrī Rāma describing Purūravā’s wonderful birth, Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata, the famous one, said again : ‘O best among men, please tell us what Ilā did after staying a year with the son of Soma (Budha).’ (1-2)

verses.text:
तयोस्तद् वाक्यमाधुर्यं निशम्य परिपृच्छतोः।
रामः पुनरुवाचेमां प्रजापतिसुते कथाम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Hearing those sweet words of those two, Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata, who eagerly asked him, Śrī Rāma again described the story of the son of Prajāpati, Ila. (3)

verses.text:
पुरुषत्वं गते शूरे बुधः परमबुद्धिमान्।
संवर्तं परमोदारमाजुहाव महायशाः॥ ४॥
verses.m: When Ila, had regained manhood for a month, the very wise one and possessed of fame, Budha, invited the very noble Saṁvarta Ṛṣi. (4)

verses.text:
च्यवनं भृगुपुत्रं च मुनिं चारिष्टनेमिनम्।
प्रमोदनं मोदकरं ततो दुर्वाससं मुनिम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: He also invited Cyavana, the son of Bhṛgu, and the sage Ariṣṭanemi, the humorous Pramodana, Modakara and also the sage Durvāsā. (5)

verses.text:
एतान् सर्वान् समानीय वाक्यज्ञस्तत्त्वदर्शनः।
उवाच सर्वान् सुहृदो धैर्येण सुसमाहितान्॥ ६॥
verses.m: Budha, skilled in conversation and truthful, addressed them all, who were friendly to him and were full of patience. (6)

verses.text:
अयं राजा महाबाहुः कर्दमस्य इलः सुतः।
जानीतैनं यथाभूतं श्रेयो ह्यत्र विधीयताम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: That king of long arms is Ila, the son of Kardama : know what happened to him, do whatever is good for him here.’ (7)

verses.text:
तेषां संवदतामेव द्विजैः सह महात्मभिः।
कर्दमस्तु महातेजास्तदाश्रममुपागमत्॥ ८॥
verses.m: While the Brāhmaṇas conversed with the sages, Kardama, the mighty one, came to that hermitage. (8)

verses.text:
पुलस्त्यश्च क्रतुश्चैव वषट्कारस्तथैव च।
ओङ्कारश्च महातेजास्तमाश्रममुपागमन्॥ ९॥
verses.m: Pulastya, Kratu and also Vaṣaṭkāra, Oṁkāra, the mighty one, too entered the hermitage. (9)

verses.text:
ते सर्वे हृष्टमनसः परस्परसमागमे।
हितैषिणो बाह्लिपतेः पृथग्वाक्यान्यथाब्रुवन्॥ १०॥
verses.m: All those, happy at meeting each other, desirous of doing good to the lord of Bāhlīka, then spoke separately. (10)

verses.text:
कर्दमस्त्वब्रवीद् वाक्यं सुतार्थं परमं हितम्।
द्विजाः शृणुत मद्वाक्यं यच्छ्रेयः पार्थिवस्य हि॥ ११॥
verses.m: Kardama, on his part, said that was best for his son, ‘O Brāhmaṇas, listen to me, which shall be for the welfare of the King. (11)

verses.text:
नान्यं पश्यामि भैषज्यमन्तरा वृषभध्वजम्।
नाश्वमेधात् परो यज्ञः प्रियश्चैव महात्मनः॥ १२॥
verses.m: ‘I do not see any other cure except the pleasure of Rudra with the bull as emblem and no sacrifice other than the Aśvamedha is dearer to Śiva, the noble one. (12)

verses.text:
तस्माद् यजामहे सर्वे पार्थिवार्थे दुरासदम्।
कर्दमेनैवमुक्तास्तु सर्व एव द्विजर्षभाः॥ १३॥
verses.m: ‘Therefore, all of us, bulls among Brāhmaṇas, will perform a Yajña for the sake of the king’. (13)

verses.text:
रोचयन्ति स्म तं यज्ञं रुद्रस्याराधनं प्रति।
संवर्तस्य तु राजर्षिः शिष्यः परपुरंजयः॥ १४॥
मरुत्त इति विख्यातस्तं यज्ञं समुपाहरत्।
ततो यज्ञो महानासीद् बुधाश्रमसमीपतः॥ १५॥
verses.m: They (Brāhmaṇas) approved of that sacrifice indeed for the appeasement of God Rudra (Śiva). A Ṛṣi among kings, well-known as Marutta, destroyer of enemies, who was the pupil of Saṁvarta, made necessary arrangements for that sacrifice. A great sacrifice was performed close to the hermitage of Budha. (14-15)

verses.text:
रुद्रश्च परमं तोषमाजगाम महायशाः।
अथ यज्ञे समाप्ते तु प्रीतः परमया मुदा॥ १६॥
उमापतिर्द्विजान् सर्वानुवाच इलसंनिधौ।
प्रीतोऽस्मि हयमेधेन भक्त्या च द्विजसत्तमाः॥ १७॥
verses.m: The mighty Rudra was extremely pleased at the completion of the sacrifice. Śiva, the lord of Umā, pleased and happy, spoke to all of them in the presence of Ila: ‘O best among Brāhmaṇas, I am pleased by the horse-sacrifice performed with devotion. (16-17)

verses.text:
अस्य बाह्लिपतेश्चैव किं करोमि प्रियं शुभम्।
तथा वदति देवेशे द्विजास्ते सुसमाहिताः॥ १८॥
प्रसादयन्ति देवेशं यथा स्यात् पुरुषस्त्विला।
ततः प्रीतो महादेवः पुरुषत्वं ददौ पुनः॥ १९॥
verses.m: ‘What good and auspicious act may I do for the lord of Bāhlīka.’ On the lord of gods speaking thus, those Brāhmaṇas, well-composed, propitiated the lord of gods, Śiva, in a manner that Ilā may turn into a man’. Then pleased, the great lord Śiva granted to Ilā perpetual manhood again. (18-19)

verses.text:
इलायै सुमहातेजा दत्त्वा चान्तरधीयत।
निवृत्ते हयमेधे च गते चादर्शनं हरे॥ २०॥
यथागतं द्विजाः सर्वे तेऽगच्छन् दीर्घदर्शिनः।
राजा तु बाह्लिमुत्सृज्य मध्यदेशे ह्यनुत्तमम्॥ २१॥
निवेशयामास पुरं प्रतिष्ठानं यशस्करम्।
शशबिन्दुश्च राजर्षिर्बाह्लिं परपुरंजयः॥ २२॥
verses.m: ‘The powerful Śiva, having granted manhood to Ilā, disappeared; and the horse-sacrifice being completed and Hara having disappeared, all the farsighted Brāhmaṇas went away as they came. The king, Ila, leaving Bāhlīka established the famous and unequalled Pratiṣṭhāna in the central region; Śaśabindu too the conqueror of fortresses of enemies re-established Bāhlīka. (20—22)

verses.text:
प्रतिष्ठाने इलो राजा प्रजापतिसुतो बली।
स काले प्राप्तवाँल्लोकमिलो ब्राह्ममनुत्तमम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: ‘At Pratiṣṭhāna, the king, son of Prajāpati, the powerful one, Ila in time attained the world of Brahmā. (23)

verses.text:
ऐलः पुरूरवा राजा प्रतिष्ठानमवाप्तवान्।
ईदृशो ह्यश्वमेधस्य प्रभावः पुरुषर्षभौ।
स्त्रीभूतः पौरुषं लेभे यच्चान्यदपि दुर्लभम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: The king, Purūravā, son of Ila, obtained Pratiṣṭhāna, such is the power of Aśvamedha, O bull among men, one who was formerly a woman, achieved manhood—all that was difficult to obtain.’ (24)

verses.text:
एतदाख्याय काकुत्स्थो भ्रातृभ्याममितप्रभः।
लक्ष्मणं पुनरेवाह धर्मयुक्तमिदं वचः॥ १॥
verses.m: Having narrated to his brothers, Śrī Rāma, with unlimited splendour, again spoke these righteous words to Lakṣmaṇa: (1)

verses.text:
वसिष्ठं वामदेवं च जाबालिमथ काश्यपम्।
द्विजांश्च सर्वप्रवरानश्वमेधपुरस्कृतान्॥ २॥
एतान् सर्वान् समानीय मन्त्रयित्वा च लक्ष्मण।
हयं लक्षणसम्पन्नं विमोक्ष्यामि समाधिना॥ ३॥
verses.m: ‘O Lakṣmaṇa, after having brought together all the sages e.g., Vasiṣṭha, Vāmadeva, Jābāli, Kāśyapa, and all Brāhmaṇas belonging to all Pravaras (Ṛṣi ancestors) and proficient in the performance of the Aśvamedha and also consulting them, I shall let loose a horse, with auspicious marks, carefully.’ (2-3)

verses.text:
तद् वाक्यं राघवेणोक्तं श्रुत्वा त्वरितविक्रमः।
द्विजान् सर्वान् समाहूय दर्शयामास राघवम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Hearing those words of the descendant of Raghu, Śrī Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa of speedy gait, calling all Brāhmaṇas presented them to the scion of Raghu. (4)

verses.text:
ते दृष्ट्वा देवसंकाशं कृतपादाभिवन्दनम्।
राघवं सुदुराधर्षमाशीर्भिः समपूजयन्॥ ५॥
verses.m: Having seen him, who was like a god, and had adored their feet, they honoured Śrī Rāma, the invincible, with blessings. (5)

verses.text:
प्राञ्जलिः स तदा भूत्वा राघवो द्विजसत्तमान्।
उवाच धर्मसंयुक्तमश्वमेधाश्रितं वचः॥ ६॥
verses.m: Then folding his hands in salutation, the scion of Raghu, spoke to the best Brāhmaṇas about Aśvamedha, full of righteousness. (6)

verses.text:
तेऽपि रामस्य तच्छ्रुत्वा नमस्कृत्वा वृषध्वजम्।
अश्वमेधं द्विजाः सर्वे पूजयन्ति स्म सर्वशः॥ ७॥
verses.m: All those Brāhmaṇas too having heard (the intention) of Śrī Rāma paying obeisance to Mahādeva, the god with the bull as His emblem, spoke very high of Aśvamedha. (7)

verses.text:
स तेषां द्विजमुख्यानां वाक्यमद्भुतदर्शनम्।
अश्वमेधाश्रितं श्रुत्वा भृशं प्रीतोऽभवत् तदा॥ ८॥
verses.m: Having heard the wonderful words of the leading Brāhmaṇas, related to the Aśvamedha, he was extremely pleased. (8)

verses.text:
विज्ञाय कर्म तत् तेषां रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्।
प्रेषयस्व महाबाहो सुग्रीवाय महात्मने॥ ९॥
यथा महद्भिर्हरिभिर्बहुभिश्च वनौकसाम्।
सार्धमागच्छ भद्रं ते अनुभोक्तुं महोत्सवम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: Knowing their intention to perform that sacrifice, Śrī Rāma spoke to Lakṣmaṇa : ‘O one of long arms, send for the noble Sugrīva, alongwith several great monkeys and other denizens of the forest, to enjoy this great ceremony; may welfare be with them. (9-10)

verses.text:
विभीषणश्च रक्षोभिः कामगैर्बहुभिर्वृतः।
अश्वमेधं महायज्ञमायात्वतुलविक्रमः॥ ११॥
verses.m: ‘May Vibhīṣaṇa, too, possessed of great power, come to the great sacrifice, Aśvamedha, accompanied by the Rākṣasas (demons) moving at will. (11)

verses.text:
राजानश्च महाभागा ये मे प्रियचिकीर्षवः।
सानुगाः क्षिप्रमायान्तु यज्ञं भूमिनिरीक्षकाः॥ १२॥
verses.m: ‘All those kings of great fortune, who are desirous of my welfare, will come soon with attendants to see the ground of Aśvamedha. (12)

verses.text:
देशान्तरगता ये च द्विजा धर्मसमाहिताः।
आमन्त्रयस्व तान् सर्वानश्वमेधाय लक्ष्मण॥ १३॥
ऋषयश्च महाबाहो आहूयन्तां तपोधनाः।
देशान्तरगताः सर्वे सदाराश्च द्विजातयः॥ १४॥
verses.m: ‘O Lakṣmaṇa, invite all those Brāhmaṇas, who have migrated to other countries, are devoted to righteousness, on the occasion of Aśvamedha. O one of long arms, invite the sages rich in penance, and all the Brāhmaṇas staying abroad together with their spouses. (13-14)

verses.text:
तथैव तालावचरास्तथैव नटनर्तकाः।
यज्ञवाटश्च सुमहान् गोमत्या नैमिषे वने॥ १५॥
आज्ञाप्यतां महाबाहो तद्धि पुण्यमनुत्तमम्।
शान्तयश्च महाबाहो प्रवर्तन्तां समन्ततः॥ १६॥
verses.m: ‘So also call the dancers with symbols, the actors and other dancers, make the great sacrificial place to be ready. O one of long arms, in the Naimiṣa forest on the banks of the Gomatī, that Naimiṣa forest is extremely holy; may propitiatory rites for averting evil be performed on all sides. (15-16)

verses.text:
शतशश्चापि धर्मज्ञाः क्रतुमुख्यमनुत्तमम्।
अनुभूय महायज्ञं नैमिषे रघुनन्दन॥ १७॥
तुष्टः पुष्टश्च सर्वोऽसौ मानितश्च यथाविधि।
प्रतियास्यति धर्मज्ञ शीघ्रमामन्त्र्यतां जनः॥ १८॥
verses.m: ‘O one of long arms, descendant of Raghu, may righteous persons in thousands be satisfied, seeing the great sacrifice, the best among rites, Aśvamedha. O knower of righteousness, do invite all people soon, they will return satisfied, well-fed and honoured in the proper manner. (17-18)

verses.text:
शतं वाहसहस्राणां तण्डुलानां वपुष्मताम्।
अयुतं तिलमुद्गस्य प्रयात्वग्रे महाबल॥ १९॥
चणकानां कुलित्थानां माषाणां लवणस्य च।
अतोऽनुरूपं स्नेहं च गन्धं संक्षिप्तमेव च॥ २०॥
verses.m: ‘O mighty one, Lakṣmaṇa, may hundred thousand carriers carry unbroken rice, and ten thousand of them carry sesame and beans, grains, pulses, black gram a little and salt; and in proportionate quantity, lubricants and fragrant materials. (19—20)

verses.text:
सुवर्णकोट्यो बहुला हिरण्यस्य शतोत्तराः।
अग्रतो भरतः कृत्वा गच्छत्वग्रे समाधिना॥ २१॥
अन्तरापणवीथ्यश्च सर्वे च नटनर्तकाः।
सूदा नार्यश्च बहवो नित्यं यौवनशालिनः॥ २२॥
भरतेन तु सार्धं ते यान्तु सैन्यानि चाग्रतः।
नैगमान् बालवृद्धांश्च द्विजांश्च सुसमाहितान्॥ २३॥
कर्मान्तिकान् वर्धकिनः कोशाध्यक्षांश्च नैगमान्।
मम मातृस्तथा सर्वाः कुमारान्तःपुराणि च॥ २४॥
काञ्चनीं मम पत्नीं च दीक्षायां ज्ञांश्च कर्मणि।
अग्रतो भरतः कृत्वा गच्छत्वग्रे महायशाः॥ २५॥
verses.m: ‘May Bharata proceed carrying coins in many hundred millions of gold and silver, carefully. Many rows of mobile markets, all actors and dancers, cooks, many damsels possessed of eternal charm, may they accompany Bharata; the citizens, both young and aged ones, Brāhmaṇas in front leading the march, the labourers, carpenters, treasurers and knowers of Veda, all my mothers (Kaikeyī with Sumitrā and Kausalyā), the spouses of the princes (Bharata etc.) ‘the gold statue of my wife, Sītā, and the knowers of the consecration ceremony, may Bharata possessed of great fame proceed.’ (21—25)

verses.text:
उपकार्या महार्हाश्च पार्थिवानां महौजसाम्।
सानुगानां नरश्रेष्ठो व्यादिदेश महाबलः॥ २६॥
verses.m: The powerful, Śrī Rāma, possessed of great power ordered to be built many costly dwellings for the powerful kings, together with their attendants. (26)

verses.text:
अन्नपानानि वस्त्राणि अनुगानां महात्मनाम्।
भरतः स तदा यातः शत्रुघ्नसहितस्तदा॥ २७॥
verses.m: He also ordered for the provision of food and drinks for the noble ones, who followed them (kings). Bharata then proceeded together with Śatrughna. (27)

verses.text:
वानराश्च महात्मानः सुग्रीवसहितास्तदा।
विप्राणां प्रवराः सर्वे चक्रुश्च परिवेषणम्॥ २८॥
verses.m: The noble monkeys, together with Sugrīva and the select Brāhmaṇas, then served the food. (28)

verses.text:
विभीषणश्च रक्षोभिः स्त्रीभिश्च बहुभिर्वृतः।
ऋषीणामुग्रतपसां पूजां चक्रे महात्मनाम्॥ २९॥
verses.m: Vibhīṣaṇa together with the Rākṣasas and many women, received with honour the noble Ṛṣis of great penances. (29)

verses.text:
तत् सर्वमखिलेनाशु प्रस्थाप्य भरताग्रजः।
हयं लक्षणसम्पन्नं कृष्णसारं मुमोच ह॥ १॥
verses.m: Dispatching all objects for performance of Yajña, the elder brother of Bharata, Śrī Rāma, let loose a horse, mostly black (like the spotted deer), possessed of auspicious marks. (1)

verses.text:
ऋत्विग्भिर्लक्ष्मणं सार्धमश्वे च विनियुज्य च।
ततोऽभ्यगच्छत् काकुत्स्थः सह सैन्येन नैमिषम्॥ २॥
verses.m: Entrusting Lakṣmaṇa together with the priests to look after the horse, the scion of Kakutstha proceeded to Naimiṣa with his army. (2)

verses.text:
यज्ञवाटं महाबाहुर्दृष्ट्वा परममद्भुतम्।
प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे श्रीमानिति च सोऽब्रवीत्॥ ३॥
verses.m: That one of long arms, Śrī Rāma, seeing the most wonderful place of performance of the sacrifice, Aśvamedha, was highly pleased and exclaimed: This indeed is auspicious.’ (3)

verses.text:
नैमिषे वसतस्तस्य सर्व एव नराधिपाः।
आनिन्युरुपहारांश्च तान् रामः प्रत्यपूजयत्॥ ४॥
verses.m: While Śrī Rāma was residing in Naimiṣa, all other kings brought presents for him, and He reciprocated their benevolence by honouring them. (4)

verses.text:
अन्नपानादिवस्त्राणि सर्वोपकरणानि च।
भरतः सहशत्रुघ्नो नियुक्तो राजपूजने॥ ५॥
verses.m: Food and drinks, clothes and all other requirements were provided for them. Bharata and Śatrughna were charged with the duty of honouring the kings. (5)

verses.text:
वानराश्च महात्मानः सुग्रीवसहितास्तदा।
परिवेषणं च विप्राणां प्रयताः सम्प्रचक्रिरे॥ ६॥
verses.m: The noble monkeys alongwith Sugrīva then served scrupulously clean and purified food to Brāhmaṇas attentively. (6)

verses.text:
विभीषणश्च रक्षोभिर्बहुभिः सुसमाहितः।
ऋषीणामुग्रतपसां किंकरः समपद्यत॥ ७॥
verses.m: Vibhīṣaṇa with many ogres offered their services to the Ṛṣis rich in austerities. (7)

verses.text:
उपकार्या महार्हाश्च पार्थिवानां महात्मनाम्।
सानुगानां नरश्रेष्ठो व्यादिदेश महाबलः॥ ८॥
verses.m: The mighty one, best of kings Śrī Rāma ordered to be built costly dwellings for the noble kings as also for their followers. (8)

verses.text:
एवं सुविहितो यज्ञो ह्यश्वमेधो ह्यवर्तत।
लक्ष्मणेन सुगुप्ता सा हयचर्या प्रवर्तत॥ ९॥
verses.m: Thus the Aśvamedha Yajña was well-begun; the ambulation of the horse, protected by Lakṣmaṇa, was commended well. (9)

verses.text:
ईदृशं राजसिंहस्य यज्ञप्रवरमुत्तमम्।
नान्यः शब्दोऽभवत् तत्र हयमेधे महात्मनः॥ १०॥
छन्दतो देहि देहीति यावत् तुष्यन्ति याचकाः।
तावत् सर्वाणि दत्तानि क्रतुमुख्ये महात्मनः॥ ११॥
विविधानि च गौडानि खाण्डवानि तथैव च।
न निःसृतं भवत्योष्ठाद् वचनं यावदर्थिनाम्॥ १२॥
तावद् वानररक्षोभिर्दत्तमेवाभ्यदृश्यत।
न कश्चिन्मलिनो वापि दीनो वाप्यथवा कृशः॥ १३॥
तस्मिन् यज्ञवरे राज्ञो हृष्टपुष्टजनावृते।
ये च तत्र महात्मानो मुनयश्चिरजीविनः॥ १४॥
नास्मरंस्तादृशं यज्ञं दानौघसमलंकृतम्।
यः कृत्यवान् सुवर्णेन सुवर्णं लभते स्म सः॥ १५॥
वित्तार्थी लभते वित्तं रत्नार्थी रत्नमेव च।
हिरण्यानां सुवर्णानां रत्नानामथ वाससाम्॥ १६॥
अनिशं दीयमानानां राशिः समुपदृश्यते।
न शक्रस्य न सोमस्य यमस्य वरुणस्य च॥ १७॥
ईदृशो दृष्टपूर्वो न एवमूचुस्तपोधनाः।
सर्वत्र वानरास्तस्थुः सर्वत्रैव च राक्षसाः॥ १८॥
verses.m: In this manner the great sacrifice of the lion among kings, Śrī Rāma, was performed; in that horse-sacrifice undertaken by Śrī Rāma, the noble one, no other sound was heard excepting cries of “Go on distributing till the needy ones are satisfied.” In that grand sacrifice of the noble one, were given various articles of jellys and also sugar. The monkeys and Rākṣasas were seen distributing food among those who begged for food till words of satisfaction did not come out of their lips. There was no one unclean, poor or emaciated in that great horse-sacrifice of the king, surrounded by happy and well-nourished beings. Those noble ascetics, long-lived ones, who came there, could not recall a sacrifice of that type so enriched with fabulous gifts and donations, who felt satisfied with gifts of gold, indeed; he who desired wealth, received it and one wishing gems also received them; Heaps of silver, gold, gems and garments being distributed constantly was seen in that sacrifice; ‘we have not seen such a sacrifice performed formerly by Indra, Soma, Yama or Varuṇa, thus said the sages rich in austerities. At all corners, there stood monkeys and demons; they distributed liberally among the suppliants, who desired clothes, wealth and food. (10—18)

verses.text:
वासोधनान्नकामेभ्यः पूर्णहस्ता ददुर्भृशम्।
ईदृशो राजसिंहस्य यज्ञः सर्वगुणान्वितः।
संवत्सरमथो साग्रं वर्तते न च हीयते॥ १९॥
verses.m: Such a sacrifice of the lion among kings, possessed of all merits, went on for more than a year unobstructed. (19)

verses.text:
वर्तमाने तथाभूते यज्ञे च परमाद्भुते।
सशिष्य आजगामाशु वाल्मीकिर्भगवानृषिः॥ १॥
verses.m: While that most wonderful sacrifice was going on, the venerable sage Vālmīki with his pupils came there soon. (1)

verses.text:
स दृष्ट्वा दिव्यसंकाशं यज्ञमद्भुतदर्शनम्।
एकान्त ऋषिवाहानां चकार उटजान् शुभान्॥ २॥
शकटांश्च बहून् पूर्णान् फलमूलांश्च शोभनान्।
वाल्मीकिवाटे रुचिरे स्थापयन्नविदूरतः॥ ३॥
verses.m: Ṛṣi Vālmīki saw the divine and astounding sacrifice. Vālmīki got his hut raised in the vicinity of other cottages of seers. They were all wonderful to look at. A number of carts, full of food-grains, lovely roots and fruits, were provided near his hut, not far from the sacrificial ground. (2-3)

verses.text:
आसीत् सुपूजितो राज्ञा मुनिभिश्च महात्मभिः।
वाल्मीकिः सुमहातेजा न्यवसत् परमात्मवान्॥ ४॥
verses.m: The self-controlled Vālmīki of great lustre was respected by the king, Śrī Rāma and other hermits and great souls staying there.(4)

verses.text:
स शिष्यावब्रवीद् हृष्टौ युवां गत्वा समाहितौ।
कृत्स्नं रामायणं काव्यं गायतां परया मुदा॥ ५॥
verses.m: Vālmīki addressed the two cheerful pupils thus; ‘Go and carefully sing the entire poem, Rāmāyaṇa, most joyfully. (5)

verses.text:
ऋषिवाटेषु पुण्येषु ब्राह्मणावसथेषु च।
रथ्यासु राजमार्गेषु पार्थिवानां गृहेषु च॥ ६॥
verses.m: ‘Sing in the holy huts of sages, in the dwellings of Brāhmaṇas, on the by-ways and highways and also in the residences of the kings,” (6)

verses.text:
रामस्य भवनद्वारि यत्र कर्म च कुर्वते।
ऋत्विजामग्रतश्चैव तत्र गेयं विशेषतः॥ ७॥
verses.m: ‘At the entrance of the apartment of Śrī Rāma and also where the ritual is being performed, and specially before the priests, this poem is to be sung. (7)

verses.text:
इमानि च फलान्यत्र स्वादूनि विविधानि च।
जातानि पर्वताग्रेषु आस्वाद्यास्वाद्य गायताम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: ‘These tasty fruits of many varieties have grown on the tops of the mountains. Enjoying them again and again, sing the poem. (8)

verses.text:
न यास्यथः श्रमं वत्सौ भक्षयित्वा फलान्यथ।
मूलानि च सुमृष्टानि न रागात् परिहास्यथः॥ ९॥
verses.m: ‘O you two, dear ones, having eaten the fruits and also the roots well-ruled, you shall not tire and not deviate from the Rāga (musical notes). (9)

verses.text:
यदि शब्दापयेद् रामः श्रवणाय महीपतिः।
ऋषीणामुपविष्टानां यथायोग्यं प्रवर्तताम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: ‘If Śrī Rāma calls you to hear your song, then perform the singing of the poem in front of the sages seated, to the best of your ability. (10)

verses.text:
दिवसे विंशतिः सर्गा गेया मधुरया गिरा।
प्रमाणैर्बहुभिस्तत्र यथोद्दिष्टं मया पुरा॥ ११॥
verses.m: ‘Twenty cantoes are to be sung in a day in a melodious voice, as instructed by me with different number of verses as instructed by me earlier. (11)

verses.text:
लोभश्चापि न कर्तव्यः स्वल्पोऽपि धनवाञ्छया।
किं धनेनाश्रमस्थानां फलमूलाशिनां सदा॥ १२॥
verses.m: ‘Do not be greedy even in the least with desire for wealth; of what use is wealth to dwellers of hermitages and subsisting always on fruits and roots? (12)

verses.text:
यदि पृच्छेत् स काकुत्स्थो युवां कस्येति दारकौ।
वाल्मीकेरथ शिष्यौ द्वौ ब्रूतमेवं नराधिपम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: ‘If that scion of Kakutstha asks you: “whose sons are you two, then say to the king thus “We are the two disciples of Vālmīki”. (13)

verses.text:
इमास्तन्त्रीः सुमधुराः स्थानं वापूर्वदर्शनम्।
मूर्च्छयित्वा सुमधुरं गायतां विगतज्वरौ॥ १४॥
verses.m: ‘Playing on these lutes, emitting sweet sounds, and wonderfully divided according to musical notes, sing sweetly, having no worry. (14)

verses.text:
आदिप्रभृति गेयं स्यान्न चावज्ञाय पार्थिवम्।
