पिता हि सर्वभूतानां राजा भवति धर्मतः॥ १५॥
verses.m: ‘This Rāmāyaṇa has to be sung from the beginning; do nothing disrespectful to the king; the king is the father of all beings, according to the law. (15)

verses.text:
तद् युवां हृष्टमनसौ श्वः प्रभाते समाहितौ।
गायतं मधुरं गेयं तन्त्रीलयसमन्वितम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: ‘Therefore, you two, with a cheerful mind and attentively sing tomorrow morning the sweet song, accompanied with the lute and keeping proper tune and rhythm. (16)

verses.text:
इति संदिश्य बहुशो मुनिः प्राचेतसस्तदा।
वाल्मीकिः परमोदारस्तूष्णीमासीन्महामुनिः॥ १७॥
verses.m: Having thus instructed many times, the son of Pracetā, the great sage Vālmīki, the most large-hearted one, then became silent. (17)

verses.text:
संदिष्टौ मुनिना तेन तावुभौ मैथिलीसुतौ।
तथैव करवावेति निर्जग्मतुररिंदमौ॥ १८॥
verses.m: Thus instructed by that sage, both those two sons of Maithilī (Sītā), the subduer of foes, saying ‘we shall do as you say’ went out. (18)

verses.text:
तामद्भुतां तौ हृदये कुमारौ
निवेश्य वाणीमृषिभाषितां तदा।
समुत्सुकौ तौ सुखमूषतुर्निशां
यथाश्विनौ भार्गवनीतिसंहिताम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: Then keeping the wonderful words of the sage Vālmīki, the two young children, Lava and Kuśa, eager to sing slept with ease like the two Aśwanīkumāras having learnt the teachings of Śukra. (19)

verses.text:
तौ रजन्यां प्रभातायां स्नातौ हुतहुताशनौ।
यथोक्तमृषिणा पूर्वं सर्वं तत्रोपगायताम्॥ १॥
तां स शुश्राव काकुत्स्थः पूर्वाचार्यविनिर्मिताम्।
अपूर्वां पाठ्यजातिं च गेयेन समलंकृताम्॥ २॥
verses.m: As the night passed and the day approached, both Kuśa and Lava having taken their bath and made offerings to the fire, sang the poem there, as instructed by the sage Vālmīki. That scion of Kakutstha heard that musical recitation accompanied with musical notes, unheard of before, composed as per the cadences set by former great masters of music. (1-2)

verses.text:
प्रमाणैर्बहुभिर्बद्धां तन्त्रीलयसमन्विताम्।
बालाभ्यां राघवः श्रुत्वा कौतूहलपरोऽभवत्॥ ३॥
verses.m: The descendant of Raghu, Śrī Rāma, hearing that song, set to the proper time and tune and accompanied by the playing of the lute by the two boys, was amazed. (3)

verses.text:
अथ कर्मान्तरे राजा समाहूय महामुनीन्।
पार्थिवांश्च नरव्याघ्रः पण्डितान् नैगमांस्तथा॥ ४॥
पौराणिकान् शब्दविदो ये वृद्धाश्च द्विजातयः।
स्वराणां लक्षणज्ञांश्च उत्सुकान् द्विजसत्तमान्॥ ५॥
लक्षणज्ञांश्च गान्धर्वान् नैगमांश्च विशेषतः।
पादाक्षरसमासज्ञांश्छन्दःसु परिनिष्ठितान्॥ ६॥
कलामात्राविशेषज्ञाञ्ज्यौतिषे च परं गतान्।
क्रियाकल्पविदश्चैव तथा कार्यविशारदान्॥ ७॥
भाषाज्ञानिङ्गितज्ञांश्च नैगमांश्चाप्यशेषतः।
हेतूपचारकुशलान् हैतुकांश्च बहुश्रुतान्॥ ८॥
छन्दोविदः पुराणज्ञान् वैदिकान् द्विजसत्तमान्।
चित्रज्ञान् वृत्तसूत्रज्ञान् गीतनृत्यविशारदान्॥ ९॥
शास्त्रज्ञान् नीतिनिपुणान् वेदान्तार्थप्रबोधकान्।
एतान् सर्वान् समानीय गातारौ समवेशयत्॥ १०॥
verses.m: Then in the midst of the performance of the Aśvamedha Yajña, the king, Śrī Rāma, the tiger among men, having called, the great ascetics, the other kings and the learned citizens, the specialists in the Purāṇas, and also those aged Brāhmaṇas who were proficient in the knowledge of words, and also those best among Brāhmaṇas, who were curious to hear the Rāmāyaṇa and knew the specialities of musical notes, the knowers of auspicious marks, the musicians, all citizens, the knowers of the relation between the syllables of stanza and were proficient in metres; those who excelled in art only, and those well-versed in astrology, knowers of ritual performances, and also those specializing in the details of the ritual and those skilled in suggesting remedial forms of ritual, the logicians and also the erudite ones, the verifiers and knowers of the Purāṇas, the Vedas, the best among Brāhmaṇas, knowers of the Citra (forms of the Kāvya), knowers of the Sūtras on righteous conduct (Dharmasūtras) and also experts in vocal music and dance, and bringing all of them together, made the two singers sit in the assembly of all these. (4—10)

verses.text:
तेषां संवदतां तत्र श्रोतॄणां हर्षवर्धनम्।
गेयं प्रचक्रतुस्तत्र तावुभौ मुनिदारकौ॥ ११॥
verses.m: Those two sons of the sage (Lava and Kuśa) then started singing, causing more joy to audience who were talking among themselves. (11)

verses.text:
ततः प्रवृत्तं मधुरं गान्धर्वमतिमानुषम्।
न च तृप्तिं ययुः सर्वे श्रोतारो गेयसम्पदा॥ १२॥
verses.m: Then continued the super-human music; all hearing it were not satiated by its musical culture and desired to hear more of it. (12)

verses.text:
हृष्टा मुनिगणाः सर्वे पार्थिवाश्च महौजसः।
पिबन्त इव चक्षुर्भिः पश्यन्ति स्म मुहुर्मुहुः॥ १३॥
verses.m: The hosts of sages were in joy and also the mighty kings, seeing again and again the two boys as if they would drink them up through their eyes. (13)

verses.text:
ऊचुः परस्परं चेदं सर्व एव समाहिताः।
उभौ रामस्य सदृशौ बिम्बाद् बिम्बमिवोत्थितौ॥ १४॥
verses.m: They looked attentively and said to each other: ‘Both are similar to Śrī Rāma as a reflection of the original object. (14)

verses.text:
जटिलौ यदि न स्यातां न वल्कलधरौ यदि।
विशेषं नाधिगच्छामो गायतो राघवस्य च॥ १५॥
verses.m: ‘If they were not bearing matted hair or not dressed in bark-garments, we could not differentiate between those two singers and the descendant of Raghu, the king, Śrī Rāma. (15)

verses.text:
एवं प्रभाषमाणेषु पौरजानपदेषु च।
प्रवृत्तमादितः पूर्वसर्गं नारददर्शितम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: While the citizens and townsmen talked in this way, the first canto attributed to Nārada was sung from the beginning. (16)

verses.text:
ततः प्रभृति सर्गांश्च यावद् विंशत्यगायताम्।
ततोऽपराह्णसमये राघवः समभाषत॥ १७॥
श्रुत्वा विंशतिसर्गांस्तान् भ्रातरं भ्रातृवत्सलः।
अष्टादश सहस्राणि सुवर्णस्य महात्मनोः॥ १८॥
प्रयच्छ शीघ्रं काकुत्स्थ यदन्यदभिकांक्षितम्।
ददौ स शीघ्रं काकुत्स्थो बालयोर्वै पृथक् पृथक्॥ १९॥
verses.m: From then on, they sang till the twenty cantos were completed. Then in the evening Śrī Rāma, the descendant of Raghu, affectionate to his brothers after hearing the twenty cantos, spoke to his brother: “Give to these two noble ones soon, eighteen thousand gold coins, and whatever else they ask for.” The scion of Kakutstha, Bharata, at once began to give it to those two boys separately. (17—19)

verses.text:
दीयमानं सुवर्णं तु नागृह्णीतां कुशीलवौ।
ऊचतुश्च महात्मानौ किमनेनेति विस्मितौ॥ २०॥
verses.m: The two—Kuśa and Lava, the noble ones, did not accept the gold coins being given to them and they said in surprise: ‘Of what use are these to us.’ (20)

verses.text:
वन्येन फलमूलेन निरतौ वनवासिनौ।
सुवर्णेन हिरण्येन किं करिष्यावहे वने॥ २१॥
verses.m: ‘We reside in the forest and subsist daily on fruits and roots. What shall we do with gold and silver coins in the forest.’ (21)

verses.text:
तथा तयोः प्रब्रुवतोः कौतूहलसमन्विताः।
श्रोतारश्चैव रामश्च सर्व एव सुविस्मिताः॥ २२॥
verses.m: Thus as both of them spoke, those who heard them together with Śrī Rāma, too, were surprised and filled with curiosity. (22)

verses.text:
तस्य चैवागमं रामः काव्यस्य श्रोतुमुत्सुकः।
पप्रच्छ तौ महातेजास्तावुभौ मुनिदारकौ॥ २३॥
verses.m: Desirous to know the composer of that poem, Śrī Rāma, the mighty one, asked both of those two ascetics: (23)

verses.text:
किं प्रमाणमिदं काव्यं का प्रतिष्ठा महात्मनः।
कर्ता काव्यस्य महतः क्व चासौ मुनिपुङ्गवः॥ २४॥
verses.m: “How long is this poem? What is the object of the noble one, Vālmīki? Where is the composer of this poem, the best among ascetics.” (24)

verses.text:
पृच्छन्तं राघवं वाक्यमूचतुर्मुनिदारकौ।
वाल्मीकिर्भगवान् कर्ता सम्प्राप्तो यज्ञसंविधम्।
येनेदं चरितं तुभ्यमशेषं सम्प्रदर्शितम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: The two sons of ascetic said to the scion of Raghu, ‘The venerable sage Vālmīki is the composer who has come to this place of performance. By this poem he has revealed the whole life’s account to you. (25)

verses.text:
संनिबद्धं हि श्लोकानां चतुर्विंशत्सहस्रकम्।
उपाख्यानशतं चैव भार्गवेण तपस्विना॥ २६॥
verses.m: ‘Twenty-four thousand Ślokas (verses) with a hundred legends have been composed by the ascetic, Bhārgava Vālmīki, the brother of Bhṛgu. (26)

verses.text:
आदिप्रभृति वै राजन् पञ्चसर्गशतानि च।
काण्डानि षट्कृतानीह सोत्तराणि महात्मना॥ २७॥
कृतानि गुरुणास्माकमृषिणा चरितं तव।
प्रतिष्ठा जीवितं यावत् तावत् सर्वस्य वर्तते॥ २८॥
verses.m: ‘From the beginning, O King, five hundred cantos with six Kāṇḍas (parts) together with the Uttara (best Kāṇḍa) have been composed by the noble one, our preceptor, sage Vālmīki, keeping in mind your life’s deeds which will continue till all beings live. (27-28)

verses.text:
यदि बुद्धिः कृता राजन् श्रवणाय महारथ।
कर्मान्तरे क्षणीभूतस्तच्छृणुष्व सहानुजः॥ २९॥
verses.m: ‘O king, the great chariot-warrior, if you have a mind to hear it, then in between this performance of Yajña, listen joyfully together with your brothers.’ (29)

verses.text:
बाढमित्यब्रवीद् रामस्तौ चानुज्ञाप्य राघवम्।
प्रहृष्टौ जग्मतुः स्थानं यत्रास्ते मुनिपुङ्गवः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Be it so” said Śrī Rāma, and the two taking leave (of Śrī Rāma), went cheerfully to the place where the great sage was staying. (30)

verses.text:
रामोऽपि मुनिभिः सार्धं पार्थिवैश्च महात्मभिः।
श्रुत्वा तद् गीतिमाधुर्यं कर्मशालामुपागमत्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma too with the ascetics and the noble kings, having heard the sweet song, approached the place of performance. (31)

verses.text:
शुश्राव तत्ताललयोपपन्नं
सर्गान्वितं सुस्वरशब्दयुक्तम्।
तन्त्रीलयव्यञ्जनयोगयुक्तं
कुशीलवाभ्यां परिगीयमानम्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: The song set into Chandas with proper words, embettered by proper beats and time, sung by Kuśa and Lava with lute in harmony, was heard by the scion of the Kakutsthas, Śrī Rāma. (32)

verses.text:
रामो बहून्यहान्येव तद् गीतं परमं शुभम्।
शुश्राव मुनिभिः सार्धं पार्थिवैः सह वानरैः॥ १॥
verses.m: For many days Śrī Rāma, together with the ascetics, kings and monkeys, heard that wonderful song of holy content. (1)

verses.text:
तस्मिन् गीते तु विज्ञाय सीतापुत्रौ कुशीलवौ।
तस्याः परिषदो मध्ये रामो वचनमब्रवीत्॥ २॥
verses.m: Having known through that song, Lava and Kuśa as the sons of Sītā, Śrī Rāma spoke in that assembly of sages, kings and monkeys. (2)

verses.text:
दूतान् शुद्धसमाचारानाहूयात्ममनीषया।
मद् वचो ब्रूत गच्छध्वमितो भगवतोऽन्तिके॥ ३॥
verses.m: Having called envoys of pure conduct, and contemplating inwardly, said to them: “Go to the venerable Ṛṣi Vālmīki and convey to him my words ! (3)

verses.text:
यदि शुद्धसमाचारा यदि वा वीतकल्मषा।
करोत्विहात्मनः शुद्धिमनुमान्य महामुनिम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “If she (Sītā) is pure of conduct, if any of the sins do not dwell in her, then may she prove her purity here at the bidding of the great sage Vālmīki. (4)

verses.text:
छन्दं मुनेश्च विज्ञाय सीतायाश्च मनोगतम्।
प्रत्ययं दातुकामायास्ततः शंसत मे लघु॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Having known the wish of the sage and Sītā’s willingness to give proof of her purity, let me know at once. (5)

verses.text:
श्वः प्रभाते तु शपथं मैथिली जनकात्मजा।
करोतु परिषन्मध्ये शोधनार्थं ममैव च॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Let Maithilī (Sītā), the daughter of Janaka, take oath in front of this assembly to remove blemishes from me also tomorrow morning.” (6)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा तु राघवस्यैतद् वचः परममद्भुतम्।
दूताः सम्प्रययुर्बाढं यत्र वै मुनिपुङ्गवः॥ ७॥
verses.m: Hearing these wonderful words of Śrī Rāma, the descendant of Raghu, envoys nodding ascent, went to the place where the great sage Vālmīki stayed. (7)

verses.text:
ते प्रणम्य महात्मानं ज्वलन्तममितप्रभम्।
ऊचुस्ते रामवाक्यानि मृदूनि मधुराणि च॥ ८॥
verses.m: Having saluted the noble one of inimitable lustre and resplendent, they spoke the words of Śrī Rāma, soft and sweet. (8)

verses.text:
तेषां तद् भाषितं श्रुत्वा रामस्य च मनोगतम्।
विज्ञाय सुमहातेजा मुनिर्वाक्यमथाब्रवीत्॥ ९॥
verses.m: Having heard their words, and knowing the intention of Śrī Rāma, the very powerful sage spoke thus: (9)

verses.text:
एवं भवतु भद्रं वो यथा वदति राघवः।
तथा करिष्यते सीता दैवतं हि पतिः स्त्रियाः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “So be it, welfare be with you, Sītā will do as desired by Śrī Rāma, as husband is indeed a god for the wife.” (10)

verses.text:
तथोक्ता मुनिना सर्वे राजदूता महौजसम्।
प्रत्येत्य राघवं सर्वं मुनिवाक्यं बभाषिरे॥ ११॥
verses.m: Thus spoken to by the sage, all the royal envoys, coming back, repeated all that the sage had said, to mighty Rāma. (11)

verses.text:
ततः प्रहृष्टः काकुत्स्थः श्रुत्वा वाक्यं महात्मनः।
ऋषींस्तत्र समेतांश्च राज्ञश्चैवाभ्यभाषत॥ १२॥
verses.m: Then Śrī Rāma, the scion of Kakutstha, highly pleased on hearing the words of Vālmīki, the noble one, addressed the sages and also the kings assembled there: (12)

verses.text:
भगवन्तः सशिष्या वै सानुगाश्च नराधिपाः।
पश्यन्तु सीताशपथं यश्चैवान्योऽपि कांक्षते॥ १३॥
verses.m: ‘Venerable sages, with pupils and kings with attendants or anyone else, so desiring, may witness the oath-taking of Sītā. (13)

verses.text:
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा राघवस्य महात्मनः।
सर्वेषामृषिमुख्यानां साधुवादो महानभूत्॥ १४॥
verses.m: Hearing those words of the noble descendant of Raghu, all the chief sages exclaimed ‘well done.’ (14)

verses.text:
राजानश्च महात्मानं प्रशंसन्ति स्म राघवम्।
उपपन्नं नरश्रेष्ठ त्वय्येव भुवि नान्यतः॥ १५॥
verses.m: The noble kings praised indeed the descendant of Raghu thus: ‘O best among men, this behoves you only, and no one else.’ (15)

verses.text:
एवं विनिश्चयं कृत्वा श्वोभूत इति राघवः।
विसर्जयामास तदा सर्वांस्ताञ्छत्रुसूदनः॥ १६॥
verses.m: Thus deciding that the oath-taking shall take place tomorrow, then the descendant of Raghu, the extirpator of foes, discharged the assembly. (16)

verses.text:
इति सम्प्रविचार्य राजसिंहः
श्वोभूते शपथस्य निश्चयम्।
विससर्ज मुनीन् नृपांश्च सर्वान्
स महात्मा महतो महानुभावः॥ १७॥
verses.m: That lion among kings, the great and next day, allowed all noble ones to leave. (17)

verses.text:
तस्यां रजन्यां व्युष्टायां यज्ञवाटं गतो नृपः।
ऋषीन् सर्वान् महातेजाः शब्दापयति राघवः॥ १॥
वसिष्ठो वामदेवश्च जाबालिरथ काश्यपः।
विश्वामित्रो दीर्घतमा दुर्वासाश्च महातपाः॥ २॥
पुलस्त्योऽपि तथा शक्तिर्भार्गवश्चैव वामनः।
मार्कण्डेयश्च दीर्घायुर्मौद्गल्यश्च महायशाः॥ ३॥
गर्गश्च च्यवनश्चैव शतानन्दश्च धर्मवित्।
भरद्वाजश्च तेजस्वी अग्निपुत्रश्च सुप्रभः॥ ४॥
नारदः पर्वतश्चैव गौतमश्च महायशाः।
कात्यायनः सुयज्ञश्च ह्यगस्त्यस्तपसां निधिः॥ ५॥
एते चान्ये च बहवो मुनयः संशितव्रताः।
कौतूहलसमाविष्टाः सर्व एव समागताः॥ ६॥
राक्षसाश्च महावीर्या वानराश्च महाबलाः।
सर्व एव समाजग्मुर्महात्मानः कुतूहलात्॥ ७॥
verses.m: As the night passed, the King, Śrī Rāma, the powerful one, going to the place of sacrifice, reckoned all the sages—Vasiṣṭha, Vāmadeva, Jābāli and Kāśyapa, Viśvāmitra, Dīrghatamā, the great ascetic Durvāsā, also Pulastya and Śakti, Bhārgava, Vāmana, Markaṇḍeya the long-lived one, the famous Maudgalya, Garga, Cyavana, the religious Śatānanda, the splendrous Bharadvāja, the son of Agni, the lustrous one, Nārada, Parvata, the most famous Gautama all these sages and other ascetics of austere vows, filled with curiosity, came, and also the most powerful Rākṣasas and monkeys. (1—7)

verses.text:
क्षत्रिया ये च शूद्राश्च वैश्याश्चैव सहस्रशः।
नानादेशगताश्चैव ब्राह्मणाः संशितव्रताः॥ ८॥
verses.m: All Kṣatriyas and Śūdras, and thousands of Vaiśyas, noble ones, came out of curiosity. (8)

verses.text:
ज्ञाननिष्ठाः कर्मनिष्ठा योगनिष्ठास्तथापरे।
सीताशपथवीक्षार्थं सर्व एव समागताः॥ ९॥
verses.m: Brāhmaṇas coming from all places, well-versed in vows came to witness the oath-taking of Sītā. (9)

verses.text:
तदा समागतं सर्वमश्मभूतमिवाचलम्।
श्रुत्वा मुनिवरस्तूर्णं ससीतः समुपागमत्॥ १०॥
verses.m: Then coming to know that all those who came were rendered motionless as stone, the great sage Vālmīki came soon after, accompanied by Sītā. (10)

verses.text:
तमृषिं पृष्ठतः सीता अन्वगच्छदवाङ्मुखी।
कृताञ्जलिर्बाष्पकला कृत्वा रामं मनोगतम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: Sītā followed the sage, with face downcast and hands folded, inarticulate due to tears, keeping Śrī Rāma in the heart. (11)

verses.text:
तां दृष्ट्वा श्रुतिमायान्तीं ब्रह्माणमनुगामिनीम्।
वाल्मीकेः पृष्ठतः सीतां साधुवादो महानभूत्॥ १२॥
verses.m: Seeing Sītā approaching after Vālmīki as the Śruti (Vedas) follows Brahmā (creator). There was great uproar of appreciation. (12)

verses.text:
ततो हलहलाशब्दः सर्वेषामेवमाबभौ।
दुःखजन्मविशालेन शोकेनाकुलितात्मनाम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: Then the sound of Halahalā (sighs of sorrow) arose among all those who were agitated by great sorrow arising out of suffering. (13)

verses.text:
साधु रामेति केचित् तु साधु सीतेति चापरे।
उभावेव च तत्रान्ये प्रेक्षकाः सम्प्रचुक्रुशुः॥ १४॥
verses.m: Some said: ‘Well done’ Śrī Rāma, while others said: ‘Well done’ Śrī Sītā. There all observers praised both of them, Śrī Rāma and Śrī Sītā. (14)

verses.text:
ततो मध्ये जनौघस्य प्रविश्य मुनिपुङ्गवः।
सीतासहायो वाल्मीकिरिति होवाच राघवम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Then in the midst of that assembly of men the great sage entering, accompanied by Sītā, spoke thus to the descendant of Raghu: (15)

verses.text:
इयं दाशरथे सीता सुव्रता धर्मचारिणी।
अपवादात् परित्यक्ता ममाश्रमसमीपतः॥ १६॥
verses.m: ‘O son of Daśaratha, this pious Sītā of righteous conduct was left by you near my hermitage out of fear of censure by folks. (16)

verses.text:
लोकापवादभीतस्य तव राम महाव्रत।
प्रत्ययं दास्यते सीता तामनुज्ञातुमर्हसि॥ १७॥
verses.m: ‘O Rāma, possessed of great vows, Sītā will give assurance of her good conduct before you as you are afraid of public censure, please permit her to do so. (17)

verses.text:
इमौ तु जानकीपुत्रावुभौ च यमजातकौ।
सुतौ तवैव दुर्धर्षौ सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥ १८॥
verses.m: ‘These twin sons of Sītā are indeed your sons, difficult to conquer by foes, this is the truth, I tell you. (18)

verses.text:
प्रचेतसोऽहं दशमः पुत्रो राघवनन्दन।
न स्मराम्यनृतं वाक्यमिमौ तु तव पुत्रकौ॥ १९॥
verses.m: ‘O descendant of Raghu, I am the tenth son of Pracetā (Varuṇa). I do not remember having spoken untruth. These twins are verily your sons. (19)

verses.text:
बहुवर्षसहस्राणि तपश्चर्या मया कृता।
नोपाश्नीयां फलं तस्या दुष्टेयं यदि मैथिली॥ २०॥
verses.m: ‘I have practised penances for many thousand years—may I not obtain the fruits thereof, if Maithilī (Sītā) is wicked of conduct. (20)

verses.text:
मनसा कर्मणा वाचा भूतपूर्वं न किल्बिषम्।
तस्याहं फलमश्नामि अपापा मैथिली यदि॥ २१॥
verses.m: ‘No sin has been committed by me in my earlier life through mind, speech or action; may I gain the fruit of this sinless conduct if Sītā is sinless. (21)

verses.text:
अहं पञ्चसु भूतेषु मनःषष्ठेषु राघव।
विचिन्त्य सीता शुद्धेति जग्राह वननिर्झरे॥ २२॥
verses.m: ‘Rāghava, through deep meditation I came to the conclusion that all ingredients like five gross elements and mind etc., subtle elements in Sītā are in their purest form. And it is only then that I took her from the bank of the river in the forest to my hermitage. (22)

verses.text:
इयं शुद्धसमाचारा अपापा पतिदेवता।
लोकापवादभीतस्य प्रत्ययं तव दास्यति॥ २३॥
verses.m: ‘This sinless, pure of conduct, Sītā, looking upon her husband as the only god, shall give assurance to you, afraid as you are of censure by public. (23)

verses.text:
तस्मादियं नरवरात्मज शुद्धभावा
दिव्येन दृष्टिविषयेण मया प्रविष्टा।
लोकापवादकलुषीकृतचेतसा या
त्यक्ता त्वया प्रियतमा विदितापि शुद्धा॥ २४॥
verses.m: ‘Therefore, this one O! son of king Daśaratha, forsakan by you for fear of public censure, I have known her through divine vision to be of pure conduct and devoted to you even though you already knew that she was chaste.’ (24)

verses.text:
वाल्मीकिनैवमुक्तस्तु राघवः प्रत्यभाषत।
प्राञ्जलिर्जगतो मध्ये दृष्ट्वा तां वरवर्णिनीम्॥ १॥
verses.m: Thus spoken to by Vālmīki, the scion of Raghu, replied with folded hands, seeing the beautiful complexioned one, Sītā, within the sight of everybody: (1)

verses.text:
एवमेतन्महाभाग यथा वदसि धर्मवित्।
प्रत्ययस्तु मम ब्रह्मंस्तव वाक्यैरकल्मषैः॥ २॥
verses.m: ‘O holy one, this is as you say, O knower of law, O Brāhmaṇa, by your guiltless words, I am assured. (2)

verses.text:
प्रत्ययश्च पुरा वृत्तो वैदेह्याः सुरसंनिधौ।
शपथश्च कृतस्तत्र तेन वेश्म प्रवेशिता॥ ३॥
verses.m: ‘Sītā, the daughter of Videha, has already assured us of her pure conduct in front of the gods, and taken oath and then she was allowed to enter the apartment. (3)

verses.text:
लोकापवादो बलवान् येन त्यक्ता हि मैथिली।
सेयं लोकभयाद् ब्रह्मन्नपापेत्यभिजानता।
परित्यक्ता मया सीता तद् भवान् क्षन्तुमर्हति॥ ४॥
verses.m: ‘The censure by people is great, due to which Maithilī (Sītā) was forsaken. This Sītā, O Brāhmaṇa, was forsaken by me due to fear of censure, although knowing that she was sinless, so please forgive me. (4)

verses.text:
जानामि चेमौ पुत्रौ मे यमजातौ कुशीलवौ।
शुद्धायां जगतो मध्ये मैथिल्यां प्रीतिरस्तु मे॥ ५॥
verses.m: ‘I know these two are my sons, the twins, Kuśa and Lava, and yet let her chastity be acknowledged by the world and my love in her reinstated.’ (5)

verses.text:
अभिप्रायं तु विज्ञाय रामस्य सुरसत्तमाः।
सीतायाः शपथे तस्मिन् महेन्द्राद्या महौजसः॥ ६॥
verses.m: Knowing the intention of Śrī Rāma, the great gods, all of them came in connection with the oath-taking of Sītā. (6)

verses.text:
पितामहं पुरस्कृत्य सर्व एव समागताः।
आदित्या वसवो रुद्रा विश्वेदेवा मरुद्गणाः॥ ७॥
साध्याश्च देवाः सर्वे ते सर्वे च परमर्षयः।
नागाः सुपर्णाः सिद्धाश्च ते सर्वे हृष्टमानसाः॥ ८॥
verses.m: Having Brahmā at their head, the Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, Viśvadevas, the hosts of Maruts, all the Sādhya gods, all great sages, the Nāgas, Suparṇas and the Siddhas, all came joyfully. (7-8)

verses.text:
सीताशपथसम्भ्रान्ताः सर्व एव समागताः।
दृष्ट्वा देवानृषींश्चैव राघवः पुनरब्रवीत्॥ ९॥
verses.m: Seeing all the gods and sages, who came out of respect for the scion of Raghu, again said: ‘O best among men, my faith is gained by the guiltless words of the sage, Vālmīki’. (9)

verses.text:
प्रत्ययो मे सुरश्रेष्ठ ऋषिवाक्यैरकल्मषैः।
शुद्धायां जगतो मध्ये वैदेह्यां प्रीतिरस्तु मे॥ १०॥
verses.m: ‘May my love for Sītā, sinless in the eyes of all, be all out.’ (10)

verses.text:
ततो वायुः शुभः पुण्यो दिव्यगन्धो मनोरमः।
तं जनौघं सुरश्रेष्ठो ह्लादयामास सर्वतः॥ ११॥
verses.m: Then the holy and pure wind-god blew emitting divine fragrance, caused joy to all on all sides. (11)

verses.text:
तदद्भुतमिवाचिन्त्यं निरैक्षन्त समाहिताः।
मानवाः सर्वराष्ट्रेभ्यः पूर्वं कृतयुगे यथा॥ १२॥
verses.m: That wonderful and unconceivable happening as used to be in Kṛtayuga was seen by all men coming from various countries. (12)

verses.text:
सर्वान् समागतान् दृष्ट्वा सीता काषायवासिनी।
अब्रवीत् प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यमधोदृष्टिरवाङ् मुखी॥ १३॥
verses.m: Sītā wearing a brown garment, having seen all of them arrived, with folded hands, keeping her gaze downwards and face cast down, said: (13)

verses.text:
यथाहं राघवादन्यं मनसापि न चिन्तये।
तथा मे माधवी देवी विवरं दातुमर्हति॥ १४॥
verses.m: ‘As I have not contemplated about anyone other than the scion of Raghu even in mind, so the goddess Mādhavī, the earth-goddess, may provide space to me to enter. (14)

verses.text:
मनसा कर्मणा वाचा यथा रामं समर्चये।
तथा मे माधवी देवी विवरं दातुमर्हति॥ १५॥
verses.m: ‘As I worship Śrī Rāma, in mind, speech and action, so the spouse of Mādhava (the earth-goddess Mādhavī) may grant space to me to enter. (15)

verses.text:
यथैतत् सत्यमुक्तं मे वेद्मि रामात् परं न च।
तथा मे माधवी देवी विवरं दातुमर्हति॥ १६॥
verses.m: ‘As I have spoken the truth that I do not know anyone except Śrī Rāma, so the earth-goddess may grant space to me.’ (16)

verses.text:
तथा शपन्त्यां वैदेह्यां प्रादुरासीत् तदद्भुतम्।
भूतलादुत्थितं दिव्यं सिंहासनमनुत्तमम्॥ १७॥
ध्रियमाणं शिरोभिस्तु नागैरमितविक्रमैः।
दिव्यं दिव्येन वपुषा दिव्यरत्नविभूषितैः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Then, while Sītā, the daughter of Videha, was taking oath, a divine throne, of wonderful beauty arose from the earth, borne on the head by very powerful Nāgas (serpents) adorned with divine ornaments, and looking divine in form sprang up. (17-18)

verses.text:
तस्मिंस्तु धरणी देवी बाहुभ्यां गृह्य मैथिलीम्।
स्वागतेनाभिनन्द्यैनामासने चोपवेशयत्॥ १९॥
verses.m: On that throne, the earth-goddess, welcoming her with words of welcome, and taking her by her hands made Sītā be seated on the seat. (19)

verses.text:
तामासनगतां दृष्ट्वा प्रविशन्तीं रसातलम्।
पुष्पवृष्टिरविच्छिन्ना दिव्या सीतामवाकिरत्॥ २०॥
verses.m: Seeing Sītā thus seated, entering the netherworld, a divine shower of flowers in succession covered Sītā. (20)

verses.text:
साधुकारश्च सुमहान् देवानां सहसोत्थितः।
साधुसाध्विति वै सीते यस्यास्ते शीलमीदृशम्॥ २१॥
एवं बहुविधा वाचो ह्यन्तरिक्षगताः सुराः।
व्याजह्रुर्हृष्टमनसो दृष्ट्वा सीताप्रवेशनम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: All of a sudden loud shouts of ‘well-done’ arose from the gods “Well done,” Well done, O Sītā, who are of such conduct’—thus and other words of approbation were uttered by the gods, happy in mind seeing Sītā’s entry into the netherworld. (21-22)

verses.text:
यज्ञवाटगताश्चापि मुनयः सर्व एव ते।
राजानश्च नरव्याघ्रा विस्मयान्नोपरेमिरे॥ २३॥
verses.m: All ascetics and kings, tigers among men, that had come to the place of great event, continued to acclaim Sītā out of amazement. (23)

verses.text:
अन्तरिक्षे च भूमौ च सर्वे स्थावरजङ्गमाः।
दानवाश्च महाकायाः पाताले पन्नगाधिपाः॥ २४॥
verses.m: In the firmament, on earth all movable and stationary beings, the mighty sons of Danu (devils) and overlords of serpents acclaimed. (24)

verses.text:
केचिद् विनेदुः संहृष्टाः केचिद् ध्यानपरायणाः।
केचिद् रामं निरीक्षन्ते केचित् सीतामचेतसः॥ २५॥
verses.m: Some uttered hurrahs of joy, other fixed their gaze on Sītā, while others looked at Śrī Rāma, although in meditation. (25)

verses.text:
सीताप्रवेशनं दृष्ट्वा तेषामासीत् समागमः।
तन्मुहूर्तमिवात्यर्थं समं सम्मोहितं जगत्॥ २६॥
verses.m: All had assembled to witness the submersion of Sītā into the netherworld; that moment all the world was as if stupefied. (26)

verses.text:
रसातलं प्रविष्टायां वैदेह्यां सर्ववानराः।
चुक्रुशुः साधुसाध्वीति मुनयो रामसंनिधौ॥ १॥
verses.m: When Sītā had entered the netherworld, all the monkeys and the ascetics exclaimed ‘well-done’ in the presence of Śrī Rāma. (1)

verses.text:
दण्डकाष्ठमवष्टभ्य बाष्पव्याकुलितेक्षणः।
अवाक्शिरा दीनमना रामो ह्यासीत् सुदुःखितः॥ २॥
verses.m: Propping himself on the wooden stick, with his eyes afflicted by tears, head downcast in mental agony, Śrī Rāma was indeed very much grieved. (2)

verses.text:
स रुदित्वा चिरं कालं बहुशो बाष्पमुत्सृजन्।
क्रोधशोकसमाविष्टो रामो वचनमब्रवीत्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Weeping long and shedding tears in profusion, possessed of both anger and sorrow, he said: (3)

verses.text:
अभूतपूर्वं शोकं मे मनः स्प्रष्टुमिवेच्छति।
पश्यतो मे यथा नष्टा सीता श्रीरिव रूपिणी॥ ४॥
verses.m: ‘A sorrow unexperienced before, is about to overpower mind as Sītā the goddess of wealth—incarnate disappeared just before my eyes. (4)

verses.text:
सादर्शनं पुरा सीता लङ्कां पारे महोदधेः।
ततश्चापि मयाऽऽनीता किं पुनर्वसुधातलात्॥ ५॥
verses.m: Sītā disappeared formerly, being carried to Laṅkā across the ocean; I brought her back from there; what to say of bringing her back from the Earth. He spoke: (5)

verses.text:
वसुधे देवि भवति सीता निर्यात्यतां मम।
दर्शयिष्यामि वा रोषं यथा मामवगच्छसि॥ ६॥
verses.m: ‘O goddess of Earth, venerable one, please return to me Sītā or else I shall show my anger as you know me (my might). (6)

verses.text:
कामं श्वश्रूर्ममैव त्वं त्वत्सकाशात् तु मैथिली।
कर्षता फालहस्तेन जनकेनोद्धृता पुरा॥ ७॥
verses.m: ‘You indeed are my mother-in-law; Maithilī (Sītā) was taken out of you formerly by Janaka while ploughing field with a golden plough. (7)

verses.text:
तस्मान्निर्यात्यतां सीता विवरं वा प्रयच्छ मे।
पाताले नाकपृष्ठे वा वसेयं सहितस्तया॥ ८॥
verses.m: ‘Therefore, either return Sītā or else grant space to me. I will stay with her in the netherworld or in heaven. (8)

verses.text:
आनय त्वं हि तां सीतां मत्तोऽहं मैथिलीकृते।
न मे दास्यसि चेत् सीतां यथारूपां महीतले॥ ९ ॥
सपर्वतवनां कृत्स्नां विधमिष्यामि ते स्थितिम्।
नाशयिष्याम्यहं भूमिं सर्वमापो भवन्त्विह॥ १०॥
verses.m: ‘Please bring that Sītā; I have gone mad for her; if you will not give back to me Sītā as she was on this earth, I shall put you to ruin, with the mountains and forests ruined entirely; I shall destroy the whole earth—may the waters flood over the entire earth.’ (9-10)

verses.text:
एवं ब्रुवाणे काकुत्स्थे क्रोधशोकसमन्विते।
ब्रह्मा सुरगणैः सार्धमुवाच रघुनन्दनम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: On being thus spoken by the scion of Kākutstha, overtaken by anger and sorrow, Brahmā together with the gods spoke to the descendant of Raghu: (11)

verses.text:
राम राम न संतापं कर्तुमर्हसि सुव्रत।
स्मर त्वं पूर्वकं भावं मन्त्रं चामित्रकर्शन॥ १२॥
verses.m: ‘O Rāma, O Śrī Rāma, possessor of good vows, please do not be grieved, recall your previous form and advice to the gods, O destroyer of foes. (12)

verses.text:
न खलु त्वां महाबाहो स्मारयेयमनुत्तमम्।
इमं मुहूर्तं दुर्धर्ष स्मर त्वं जन्म वैष्णवम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: ‘I do not dare remind you of your former form, O one of long arms, but pray to you to remember at this moment, O one, difficult to conquer, your incarnation pertaining to Viṣṇu. (13)

verses.text:
सीता हि विमला साध्वी तव पूर्वपरायणा।
नागलोकं सुखं प्रायात् त्वदाश्रयतपोबलात्॥ १४॥
verses.m: ‘The pure and noble Sītā, devoted to yourself as before, has gone to the netherworld (Nāgaloka both netherworld and also the world of Viṣṇu) by the power of penances in the form of complete surrender to you. (14)

verses.text:
स्वर्गे ते संगमो भूयो भविष्यति न संशयः।
अस्यास्तु परिषन्मध्ये यद् ब्रवीमि निबोध तत्॥ १५॥
verses.m: ‘Your union with her will again take place in heaven, listen to what I say in the midst of this assembly. (15)

verses.text:
एतदेव हि काव्यं ते काव्यानामुत्तमं श्रुतम्।
सर्वं विस्तरतो राम व्याख्यास्यति न संशयः॥ १६॥
verses.m: ‘This poem, Rāmāyaṇa, dedicated to you, that you have heard is the best among all poems, O Rāma; it shall describe everything in detail, there is no doubt. (16)

verses.text:
जन्मप्रभृति ते वीर सुखदुःखोपसेवनम्।
भविष्यदुत्तरं चेह सर्वं वाल्मीकिना कृतम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: ‘In this poem all has been described by Vālmīki, all happiness and sorrow that you have experienced from your birth, and also what you will experience in future. (17)

verses.text:
आदिकाव्यमिदं राम त्वयि सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम्।
नह्यन्योऽर्हति काव्यानां यशोभाग् राघवादृते॥ १८॥
verses.m: ‘This first and foremost poem, O Rāma, is entirely based on you. No one other than you will be possessed of fame to be described as hero by the poem. (18)

verses.text:
श्रुतं ते पूर्वमेतद्धि मया सर्वं सुरैः सह।
दिव्यमद्भुतरूपं च सत्यवाक्यमनावृतम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: ‘I have heard all this formerly, together with the gods, all wonderful and possessed of true statements with nothing concealed. (19)

verses.text:
स त्वं पुरुषशार्दूल धर्मेण सुसमाहितः।
शेषं भविष्यं काकुत्स्थ काव्यं रामायणं शृणु॥ २०॥
verses.m: ‘So you, O lion among men, scion of Kākutsthas should carefully listen to the remaining portion of the poem, Rāmāyaṇa dealing with happenings of the future. (20)

verses.text:
उत्तरं नाम काव्यस्य शेषमत्र महायशः।
तच्छृणुष्व महातेज ऋषिभिः सार्धमुत्तमम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: ‘The remaining part of this poem, O famous one, is known as Uttarakāṇḍa; O powerful one, listen to it, possessed of excellence, with the sages. (21)

verses.text:
न खल्वन्येन काकुत्स्थ श्रोतव्यमिदमुत्तमम्।
परम ऋषिणा वीर त्वयैव रघुनन्दन॥ २२॥
verses.m: O Scion of Kākutstha, this best portion is indeed not to be heard by anyone else, composed by the great great sage, O brave, it is to be heard only by you.’ (22)

verses.text:
एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं ब्रह्मा त्रिभुवनेश्वरः।
जगाम त्रिदिवं देवो देवैः सह सबान्धवैः॥ २३॥
verses.m: Having spoken this much, Brahmā, the lord of the three worlds, went to heaven together with other gods. (23)

verses.text:
ये च तत्र महात्मान ऋषयो ब्राह्मलौकिकाः।
ब्रह्मणा समनुज्ञाता न्यवर्तन्त महौजसः॥ २४॥
उत्तरं श्रोतुमनसो भविष्यं यच्च राघवे।
ततो रामः शुभां वाणीं देवदेवस्य भाषिताम्॥ २५॥
श्रुत्वा परमतेजस्वी वाल्मीकिमिदमब्रवीत्।
भगवन् श्रोतुमनस ऋषयो ब्राह्मलौकिकाः॥ २६॥
भविष्यदुत्तरं यन्मे श्वोभूते सम्प्रवर्तताम्।
एवं विनिश्चयं कृत्वा सम्प्रगृह्य कुशीलवौ॥ २७॥
तं जनौघं विसृज्याथ पर्णशालामुपागमत्।
तामेव शोचतः सीता सा व्यतीता च शर्वरी॥ २८॥
verses.m: The noble and splendrous sages belonging to the world of Brahmā, being ordered by Brahmā, returned, having a mind to hear what will happen to the scion of Raghu thereafter in the future. Then the most powerful Śrī Rāma after hearing the holy words spoken by the God of gods, Brahmā, said to Vālmīki: ‘Sir the Uttarakāṇḍa pertaining to what will happen to me in future, that the sages of the world of Brahmā desire to hear, may be described tomorrow.’ Thus having decided, taking hold to Kuśa and Lava, He (Śrī Rāma) leaving that assembly of men, went to his arbour—and as he kept thinking of Sītā, that night passed. (24—28)

verses.text:
रजन्यां तु प्रभातायां समानीय महामुनीन्।
गीयतामविशङ्काभ्यां रामः पुत्रावुवाच ह॥ १॥
verses.m: After the night had passed, dawn came, Rāma said to the two sons, calling all the great sages, “Sing unhesitatingly”. (1)

verses.text:
ततः समुपविष्टेषु महर्षिषु महात्मसु।
भविष्यदुत्तरं काव्यं जगतुस्तौ कुशीलवौ॥ २॥
verses.m: Then after the great and noble sages had taken their seats, the twin Kuśa and Lava sang the poem relating to the Uttarakāṇḍa, dealing with events of the future: (2)

verses.text:
प्रविष्टायां तु सीतायां भूतलं सत्यसम्पदा।
तस्यावसाने यज्ञस्य रामः परमदुर्मनाः॥ ३॥
अपश्यमानो वैदेहीं मेने शून्यमिदं जगत्।
शोकेन परमायस्तो न शान्तिं मनसागमत्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “On Sītā entering the netherworld through the efficacy of truth, Śrī Rāma was much agitated at the conclusion of the sacrifice and considered this earth as a void. Not being able to see Sītā and being terribly afflicted by sorrow, he had no peace of mind. (3-4)

verses.text:
विसृज्य पार्थिवान् सर्वानृक्षवानरराक्षसान्।
जनौघं विप्रमुख्यानां वित्तपूर्वं विसृज्य च॥ ५॥
एवं समाप्य यज्ञं तु विधिवत् स तु राघवः।
ततो विसृज्य तान् सर्वान् रामो राजीवलोचनः॥ ६॥
हृदि कृत्वा तदा सीतामयोध्यां प्रविवेश ह।
इष्टयज्ञो नरपतिः पुत्रद्वयसमन्वितः॥ ७॥
verses.m: Leaving all kings, the bears and monkeys, and also the great assembly of the chief Brāhmaṇas, giving them precious gifts, Lotus-eyed Rāma, after finishing the sacrifice, alongwith his two sons, Sītā in his heart, entered Ayodhyā. (5—7)

verses.text:
न सीतायाः परां भार्यां वव्रे स रघुनन्दनः।
यज्ञे यज्ञे च पत्न्यर्थं जानकी काञ्चनीभवत्॥ ८॥
verses.m: That descendant of Raghu did not take as wife any one other than Sītā and at every sacrifice (Aśvamedha) the gold image of the daughter of Janaka served as the queen. (8)

verses.text:
दशवर्षसहस्राणि वाजिमेधानथाकरोत्।
वाजपेयान् दशगुणांस्तथा बहुसुवर्णकान्॥ ९॥
verses.m: Then He, Śrī Rāma, performed horse-sacrifices and Vājapeya sacrifices ten times that number, full with the distribution of gold coins, for ten thousand years. (9)

verses.text:
अग्निष्टोमातिरात्राभ्यां गोसवैश्च महाधनैः।
ईजे क्रतुभिरन्यैश्च स श्रीमानाप्तदक्षिणैः॥ १०॥
verses.m: That prosperous one, Śrī Rāma, performed many Gosavas with the Agniṣṭoma and the Atirātra and also other sacrifices, giving donations in plenty. (10)

verses.text:
एवं स कालः सुमहान् राज्यस्थस्य महात्मनः।
धर्मे प्रयतमानस्य व्यतीयाद् राघवस्य च॥ ११॥
verses.m: Thus that period of Śrī Rāma elapsed, the descendant of Raghu, acting righteously, ruling over His Kingdom. (11)

verses.text:
ऋक्षवानररक्षांसि स्थिता रामस्य शासने।
अनुरञ्जन्ति राजानो ह्यहन्यहनि राघवम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: The bears, monkeys and demons obeyed the command of the descendant of Raghu, the Kings paid tributes to Him day by day. (12)

verses.text:
काले वर्षति पर्जन्यः सुभिक्षं विमला दिशः।
हृष्टपुष्टजनाकीर्णं पुरं जनपदास्तथा॥ १३॥
verses.m: The clouds rained timely, the harvest was good and the quarters shone clearly, and the towns and cities were full of happy, well-fed and healthy persons in His reign. (13)

verses.text:
नाकाले म्रियते कश्चिन्न व्याधिः प्राणिनां तथा।
नानर्थो विद्यते कश्चिद् रामे राज्यं प्रशासति॥ १४॥
verses.m: No one died prematurely, no physical ailment was suffered by living beings, no calamity took place as Śrī Rāma ruled over his Kingdom. (14)

verses.text:
अथ दीर्घस्य कालस्य राममाता यशस्विनी।
पुत्रपौत्रैः परिवृता कालधर्ममुपागमत्॥ १५॥
verses.m: After a long lapse of time the mother of Rāma, Kausalyā of great fame, surrounded by her son and grandsons, succumbed to the law of time. (15)

verses.text:
अन्वियाय सुमित्रा च कैकेयी च यशस्विनी।
धर्मं कृत्वा बहुविधं त्रिदेवे पर्यवस्थिता॥ १६॥
verses.m: Sumitrā and the Kaikeyī also followed her, performing various charitable deeds, and praiseworthy, were established in heaven. (16)

verses.text:
सर्वाः प्रमुदिताः स्वर्गे राज्ञा दशरथेन च।
समागता महाभागाः सर्वधर्मं च लेभिरे॥ १७॥
verses.m: All happy and righteous ones, united with Daśaratha in heaven, attained the fruit of all religious performances. (17)

verses.text:
तासां रामो महादानं काले काले प्रयच्छति।
मातॄणामविशेषेण ब्राह्मणेषु तपस्विषु॥ १८॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma made great donations for his mothers, Kausalyā, Kaikeyī, Sumitrā, without any difference, to the Brāhmaṇa ascetics. (18)

verses.text:
पित्र्याणि ब्रह्मरत्नानि यज्ञान् परमदुस्तरान्।
चकार रामो धर्मात्मा पितॄन् देवान् विवर्धयन्॥ १९॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma, the noble one, donated the most cherished things to Brāhmaṇas and performed the sacrifices most difficult to accomplish, to add to the glory of his ancestors and the gods. (19)

verses.text:
एवं वर्षसहस्राणि बहून्यथ ययुः सुखम्।
यज्ञैर्बहुविधं धर्मं वर्धयानस्य सर्वदा॥ २०॥
verses.m: Many a thousand years passed while Śrī Rāma upraised the course of Dharma (religion) by performing various sacrifices. (20)

verses.text:
कस्यचित् त्वथ कालस्य युधाजित् केकयो नृपः।
स्वगुरुं प्रेषयामास राघवाय महात्मने॥ १॥
गार्ग्यमङ्गिरसः पुत्रं ब्रह्मर्षिममितप्रभम्।
दश चाश्वसहस्राणि प्रीतिदानमनुत्तमम्॥ २॥
कम्बलानि च रत्नानि चित्रवस्त्रमथोत्तमम्।
रामाय प्रददौ राजा शुभान्याभरणानि च॥ ३॥
verses.m: After some time, the King of Kekaya, Yudhājit, sent his preceptor, Brāhmaṇa Gārgya, the son of Aṅgirā, possessed of inimitable lustre to Śrī Rāma, the noble descendant of Raghu. The King presented a §gift of ten thousand horses as a token of affection and also blankets and precious gems, and garments of various kinds and brilliant ornaments. (1—3)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा तु राघवो धीमान् महर्षिं गार्ग्यमागतम्।
मातुलस्याश्वपतिनः प्रहितं तन्महाधनम्॥ ४॥
प्रत्युद्गम्य च काकुत्स्थः क्रोशमात्रं सहानुजः।
गार्ग्यं सम्पूजयामास यथा शक्रो बृहस्पतिम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: Having heard that the great sage Gārgya had come, bringing with him the rich gifts sent by the maternal uncle, Aśvapati, Śrī Rama, alongwith his brothers, welcomed Gārgya at a distance of two miles in advance, and honoured Gārgya as Indra honours Bṛhaspati. (4-5)

verses.text:
तथा सम्पूज्य तमृषिं तद् धनं प्रतिगृह्य च।
पृष्ट्वा प्रतिपदं सर्वं कुशलं मातुलस्य च॥ ६॥
उपविष्टं महाभागं रामः प्रष्टुं प्रचक्रमे।
किमाह मातुलो वाक्यं यदर्थं भगवानिह॥ ७॥
प्राप्तो वाक्यविदां श्रेष्ठः साक्षादिव बृहस्पतिः।
रामस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा महर्षिः कार्यविस्तरम्॥ ८॥
वक्तुमद्भुतसंकाशं राघवायोपचक्रमे।
मातुलस्ते महाबाहो वाक्यमाह नरर्षभः॥ ९॥
युधाजित् प्रीतिसंयुक्तं श्रूयतां यदि रोचते।
अयं गन्धर्वविषयः फलमूलोपशोभितः॥ १०॥
सिन्धोरुभयतः पार्श्वे देशः परमशोभनः।
तं च रक्षन्ति गन्धर्वाः सायुधा युद्धकोविदाः॥ ११॥
शैलूषस्य सुता वीर तिस्रः कोट्यो महाबलाः।
तान् विनिर्जित्य काकुत्स्थ गन्धर्वनगरं शुभम्॥ १२॥
निवेशय महाबाहो स्वे पुरे सुसमाहिते।
अन्यस्य न गतिस्तत्र देशः परमशोभनः।
रोचतां ते महाबाहो नाहं त्वामहितं वदे॥ १३॥
verses.m: Thus having honoured that sage and accepting the gifts, he enquired of the welfare of his maternal uncle. Śrī Rāma asked the holy one when he had seated himself thus: ‘What has my maternal uncle said for which O Venerable Sir, best among the knowers of Śāstras, like Bṛhaspti himself, you have come.’ Having heard the words of Śrī Rāma, the great sage began to speak in detail the wondrous purpose to the descendant of Raghu: ‘O one of long arms, bull among men, your maternal uncle Yudhājit has said pleasingly, listen if it appeals to you. The territory of the Gandharvas, rich with fruits and roots, is a region most beautiful on both sides of the Sindhu river, that is protected by the Gandharvas, the experts in war, possessed of arms, the powerful three million sons of Śailūṣa, O brave one. Having conquered them, O scion of Kakutstha, merge the holy city of the Gandharvas in your own kingdom, which no one else can do. May it please you to occupy it, O one of long arms; I do not say this against your interests.’ (6—13)

verses.text:
तच्छ्रुत्वा राघवः प्रीतो महर्षेर्मातुलस्य च।
उवाच बाढमित्येव भरतं चान्ववैक्षत॥ १४॥
verses.m: Having heard this, Śrī Rāma the descendant of Raghu, being pleased with what the sage and his maternal uncle said: ‘So shall it be’ and looked at Bharata. (14)

verses.text:
सोऽब्रवीद् राघवः प्रीतः साञ्जलिप्रग्रहो द्विजम्।
इमौ कुमारौ तं देशं ब्रह्मर्षे विचरिष्यतः॥ १५॥
भरतस्यात्मजौ वीरौ तक्षः पुष्कल एव च।
मातुलेन सुगुप्तौ तु धर्मेण सुसमाहितौ॥ १६॥
verses.m: That descendant of Raghu was pleased and with folded hands courteously said: ‘O Ṛṣi among Brāhmaṇas, these two brave sons (of Bharata) Takṣa and Puṣkala will go to that region, well-protected by my maternal uncle and observing religious norms. (15-16)

verses.text:
भरतं चाग्रतः कृत्वा कुमारौ सबलानुगौ।
निहत्य गन्धर्वसुतान् द्वे पुरे विभजिष्यतः॥ १७॥
verses.m: ‘Keeping Bharata ahead, the two sons together with their army and attendants, will divide the two regions having killed the sons of the Gandharva, Śailūṣa. (17)

verses.text:
निवेश्य ते पुरवरे आत्मजौ संनिवेश्य च।
आगमिष्यति मे भूयः सकाशमतिधार्मिकः॥ १८॥
verses.m: ‘Establishing those two cities and foresetting his two sons there, this most pious one, Bharata, will again return to me.’ (18)

verses.text:
ब्रह्मर्षिमेवमुक्त्वा तु भरतं सबलानुगम्।
आज्ञापयामास तदा कुमारौ चाभ्यषेचयत्॥ १९॥
नक्षत्रेण च सौम्येन पुरस्कृत्याङ्गिरःसुतम्।
भरतः सह सैन्येन कुमाराभ्यां विनिर्ययौ॥ २०॥
verses.m: Thus having spoken to the Brāhmaṇas, he (Rāma) ordered Bharata to proceed with his army and attendants, and also consecrated the two sons on an auspicious day with the holy star, putting the son of Aṅgirā at their head, Bharata with his army and his sons proceeded. (19-20)

verses.text:
सा सेना शक्रयुक्तेव नगरान्निर्ययावथ।
राघवानुगता दूरं दुराधर्षा सुरैरपि॥ २१॥
verses.m: Then that army went out of the royal city Ayodhyā like the army of Indra, followed by the descendant of Raghu for a long distance—the army that was difficult to conquer even by the gods. (21)

verses.text:
मांसाशिनश्च ये सत्त्वा रक्षांसि सुमहान्ति च।
अनुजग्मुर्हि भरतं रुधिरस्य पिपासया॥ २२॥
verses.m: The flesh-eaters and the mighty Rākṣasas followed Bharata out of thirst for blood. (22)

verses.text:
भूतग्रामाश्च बहवो मांसभक्षाः सुदारुणाः।
गन्धर्वपुत्रमांसानि भोक्तुकामाः सहस्रशः॥ २३॥
verses.m: Hosts of Bhūtas (demons), eaters of flesh, the terrible ones, desirous of devouring the flesh of the sons of the Gandharva, followed in thousands. (23)

verses.text:
सिंहव्याघ्रवराहाणां खेचराणां च पक्षिणाम्।
बहूनि वै सहस्राणि सेनाया ययुरग्रतः॥ २४॥
verses.m: Lions, tigers, bears and the sky-roving birds, thousands in number went to herald the army. (24)

verses.text:
अध्यर्धमासमुषिता पथि सेना निरामया।
हृष्टपुष्टजनाकीर्णा केकयं समुपागमत्॥ २५॥
verses.m: Having spent one and half months on the way, the army, hale and hearty, bearing happy and well-fed men, reached Kekaya territory. (25)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा सेनापतिं प्राप्तं भरतं केकयाधिपः।
युधाजिद् गार्ग्यसहितं परां प्रीतिमुपागमत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Yudhājit, the king of Kekaya, having heard of the arrival of Bharata as the Commander-in-chief of his army, was highly pleased together with Gārgya. (1)

verses.text:
स निर्ययौ जनौघेन महता केकयाधिपः।
त्वरमाणोऽभिचक्राम गन्धर्वान् कामरूपिणः॥ २॥
verses.m: He, the lord of Kekaya, and Bharata set out accompanied by a large army and quickly reached the capital of the Gandharvas. (2)

verses.text:
भरतश्च युधाजिच्च समेतौ लघुविक्रमैः।
गन्धर्वनगरं प्राप्तौ सबलौ सपदानुगौ॥ ३॥
verses.m: Bharata and Yudhājit accompanied by the rapid action warriors reached the city of Gandharvas with the army and attendants. (3)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा तु भरतं प्राप्तं गन्धर्वास्ते समागताः।
योद्धुकामा महावीर्या व्यनदंस्ते समन्ततः॥ ४॥
verses.m: Those Gandharvas, possessed of great power, and desirous of war came out, shouting war cries every where. (4)

verses.text:
ततः समभवद्युद्धं तुमुलं लोमहर्षणम्।
सप्तरात्रं महाभीमं न चान्यतरयोर्जयः॥ ५॥
verses.m: Then there ensued a great battle enough to cause horripilation for seven nights in a terrible form, and yet none came out victorious. (5)

verses.text:
खड्गशक्तिधनुर्ग्राहा नद्यः शोणितसंस्रवाः।
नृकलेवरवाहिन्यः प्रवृत्ताः सर्वतोदिशम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: Rivers with streams of blood, having crocodiles in the form of swords, arrows and bows, and carrying the corpses of men, gushed forth on all sides. (6)

verses.text:
ततो रामानुजः क्रुद्धः कालस्यास्त्रं सुदारुणम्।
संवर्तं नाम भरतो गन्धर्वेष्वभ्यचोदयत्॥ ७॥
verses.m: Then Bharata, the brother of Śrī Rāma, highly enraged directed the most terrible weapon of death, Saṁvarta by name, towards the Gandharvas. (7)

verses.text:
ते बद्धाः कालपाशेन संवर्तेन विदारिताः।
क्षणेनाभिहतास्तेन तिस्रः कोट्यो महात्मना॥ ८॥
verses.m: Struck by the mighty Saṁvarta, as if bound by the noose of death, they the Gandharvas, three million in number, perished in a moment. (8)

verses.text:
तद् युद्धं तादृशं घोरं न स्मरन्ति दिवौकसः।
निमेषान्तरमात्रेण तादृशानां महात्मनाम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: Even the gods did not remember a battle so fierce in which those mighty Gandharvas were killed in a moment. (9)

verses.text:
हतेषु तेषु सर्वेषु भरतः केकयीसुतः।
निवेशयामास तदा समृद्धे द्वे पुरोत्तमे॥ १०॥
तक्षं तक्षशिलायां तु पुष्कलं पुष्कलावते।
गन्धर्वदेशे रुचिरे गान्धारविषये च सः॥ ११॥
verses.m: On all of the Gandharvas being killed, Bharata, the son of Kaikeyī, founded there two great and prosperous cities and he installed Takṣa on Takṣaśilā in the Gandharva-Deśa and Puṣkala on Puṣkalāvata in the territory of Gāndhāras. (10-11)

verses.text:
धनरत्नौघसंकीर्णे काननैरुपशोभिते।
अन्योन्यसंघर्षकृते स्पर्धया गुणविस्तरैः॥ १२॥
उभे सुरुचिरप्रख्ये व्यवहारैरकिल्बिषैः।
उद्यानयानसम्पूर्णे सुविभक्तान्तरापणे॥ १३॥
उभे पुरवरे रम्ये विस्तरैरुपशोभिते।
गृहमुख्यैः सुरुचिरैर्विमानैर्बहुभिर्वृते॥ १४॥
शोभिते शोभनीयैश्च देवायतनविस्तरैः।
तालैस्तमालैस्तिलकैर्बकुलैरुपशोभिते ॥ १५॥
निवेश्य पञ्चभिर्वर्षैर्भरतो राघवानुजः।
पुनरायान्महाबाहुरयोध्यां केकयीसुतः॥ १६॥
verses.m: Having fully established the two above—named cities, filled with wealth and gems, beautified by gardens, trying each other to excel through competitive spirit, both extremely lovely and rich with fresh business, abounding in pleasant groves and carrier vehicles and well-planned with markets, both great cities, beautifully decorated with mansions and many lovely Vimānas (palaces), adorned with attractive temples of worship, made lovely with the Tālas, Tamālas, Tilaka and Vakula trees. In five years, Bharata the younger brother of Śrī Rāma, the descendant of Raghus, possessed of long arms, the son of Kaikeyī, returned to Ayodhyā. (12—16)

verses.text:
सोऽभिवाद्य महात्मानं साक्षाद्धर्ममिवापरम्।
राघवं भरतः श्रीमान् ब्रह्माणमिव वासवः॥ १७॥
शशंस च यथावृत्तं गन्धर्ववधमुत्तमम्।
निवेशनं च देशस्य श्रुत्वा प्रीतोऽस्य राघवः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Having bowed to Śrī Rāma, the noble descendant of Raghu, who was as if he were another Dharma (Law)—incarnate, as Indra bows to Brahmā, the graceful Bharata narrated to him how the great battle with the Gandharvas was fought and how were founded the two cities, too. Hearing him, Śrī Rāma, the descendant of Raghu, was highly pleased. (17-18)

verses.text:
तच्छ्रुत्वा हर्षमापेदे राघवो भ्रातृभिः सह।
वाक्यं चाद्भुतसंकाशं भ्रातॄन् प्रोवाच राघवः॥ १॥
verses.m: Hearing this account of Bharata, Śrī Rāma, together with his brothers, was pleased and said to Lakṣmaṇa these words of wonderful content: (1)

verses.text:
इमौ कुमारौ सौमित्रे तव धर्मविशारदौ।
अङ्गदश्चन्द्रकेतुश्च राज्यार्थे दृढविक्रमौ॥ २॥
verses.m: ‘O son of Sumitrā, Lakṣmaṇa, your these two sons are knower of Dharma (Law and righteousness)—named Aṅgada and Candraketu, possessed of firm fortitude, for the protection of their kingdoms. (2)

verses.text:
इमौ राज्येऽभिषेक्ष्यामि देशः साधु विधीयताम्।
रमणीयो ह्यसम्बाधो रमेतां यत्र धन्विनौ॥ ३॥
verses.m: ‘I shall consecrate these two, find out a suitable region, that is enjoyable and where the two archers may remain happily without being obstructed. (3)

verses.text:
न राज्ञां यत्र पीडा स्यान्नाश्रमाणां विनाशनम्।
स देशो दृश्यतां सौम्य नापराध्यामहे यथा॥ ४॥
verses.m: ‘O gracious one, find out that place, where the kings are not tormented and the hermitages are well-protected and we may not be at fault later on.’ (4)

verses.text:
तथोक्तवति रामे तु भरतः प्रत्युवाच ह।
अयं कारुपथो देशो रमणीयो निरामयः॥ ५॥
निवेश्यतां तत्र पुरमङ्गदस्य महात्मनः।
चन्द्रकेतोः सुरुचिरं चन्द्रकान्तं निरामयम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: On Śrī Rāma saying thus, Bharata replied: ‘This region known as Kārupatha is indeed beautiful and free from all ills. Establish there the city under the noble Aṅgada and also a region known as Candrakānta free from sorrow, for Candraketu, the noble one.’ (5-6)

verses.text:
तद् वाक्यं भरतेनोक्तं प्रतिजग्राह राघवः।
तं च कृत्वा वशे देशमङ्गदस्य न्यवेशयत्॥ ७॥
verses.m: This statement of Bharata was accepted by Śrī Rāma, descendant of Raghu and having brought that territory Kārupatha under him, he established the city there for Aṅgada. (7)

verses.text:
अङ्गदीया पुरी रम्याप्यङ्गदस्य निवेशिता।
रमणीया सुगुप्ता च रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा॥ ८॥
verses.m: The city that was bestowed by Śrī Rāma on Aṅgada was beautiful indeed and well-protected on all sides. (8)

verses.text:
चन्द्रकेतोश्च मल्लस्य मल्लभूम्यां निवेशिता।
चन्द्रकान्तेति विख्याता दिव्या स्वर्गपुरी यथा॥ ९॥
verses.m: For the wrestler Candraketu, the city well-known as Candrakāntā in Malla country was established as the divine city in heaven. (9)

verses.text:
ततो रामः परां प्रीतिं लक्ष्मणो भरतस्तथा।
ययुर्युद्धे दुराधर्षा अभिषेकं च चक्रिरे॥ १०॥
verses.m: Then Śrī Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata, all difficult to conquer in war, were highly pleased and performed the coronation of Aṅgada and Candraketu. (10)

verses.text:
अभिषिच्य कुमारौ द्वौ प्रस्थाप्य सुसमाहितौ।
अङ्गदं पश्चिमां भूमिं चन्द्रकेतुमुदङ्मुखम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: Having consecrated and sent Aṅgada to the western region and Candraketu northwards, both firm in mind, they were well pleased. (11)

verses.text:
अङ्गदं चापि सौमित्रिर्लक्ष्मणोऽनुजगाम ह।
चन्द्रकेतोस्तु भरतः पार्ष्णिग्राहो बभूव ह॥ १२॥
verses.m: Lakṣmaṇa, the son of Sumitrā, too, followed Aṅgada and Bharata on his part followed Candraketu as the rear guard. (12)

verses.text:
लक्ष्मणस्त्वङ्गदीयायां संवत्सरमथोषितः।
पुत्रे स्थिते दुराधर्षे अयोध्यां पुनरागमत्॥ १३॥
verses.m: Having stayed for one full year in the city of Aṅgada, when his son, difficult to conquer was well-established, Lakṣmaṇa came back again to Ayodhyā. (13)

verses.text:
भरतोऽपि तथैवोष्य संवत्सरमतोऽधिकम्।
अयोध्यां पुनरागम्य रामपादावुपास्त सः॥ १४॥
verses.m: Bharata too, having spent a year and more, in the same manner returned to Ayodhyā and worshipped the feet of Śrī Rāma. (14)

verses.text:
उभौ सौमित्रिभरतौ रामपादावनुव्रतौ।
कालं गतमपि स्नेहान्न जज्ञातेऽतिधार्मिकौ॥ १५॥
verses.m: Both—the son of Sumitrā (Lakṣmaṇa) and Bharata, the most noble ones, ardently attached to the feet of Śrī Rāma, were oblivious of the lapse of time due to the deep affection of Śrī Rāma. (15)

verses.text:
एवं वर्षसहस्राणि दश तेषां ययुस्तदा।
धर्मे प्रयतमानानां पौरकार्येषु नित्यदा॥ १६॥
verses.m: Thus, ten thousand years passed with Śrī Rāma, Bharata and Lakṣmaṇa striving always to perform tasks for the citizens and always ready to follow Dharma. (16)

verses.text:
विहृत्य कालं परिपूर्णमानसाः
श्रिया वृता धर्मपुरे च संस्थिताः।
त्रयः समिद्धाहुतिदीप्ततेजसो
हुताग्नयः साधुमहाध्वरे त्रयः॥ १७॥
verses.m: With desires all fulfilled, established in the city of virtue, full of prosperity, the three brothers radiated effulgence like the three great sacrificial fires, inflamed by oblations well poured. (17)

verses.text:
कस्यचित् त्वथ कालस्य रामे धर्मपरे स्थिते।
कालस्तापसरूपेण राजद्वारमुपागमत्॥ १॥
verses.m: After sometime, while Śrī Rāma was engaged in virtuous deeds, Death in the form of an ascetic appeared at the royal gate. (1)

verses.text:
सोऽब्रवील्लक्ष्मणं वाक्यं धृतिमन्तं यशस्विनम्।
मां निवेदय रामाय सम्प्राप्तं कार्यगौरवात्॥ २॥
verses.m: He spoke to courageous and glorious Lakṣmaṇa, who was standing at the door thus: ‘I have come here for a great purpose, you report my arrival to Śrī Rāma. (2)

verses.text:
दूतो ह्यतिबलस्याहं महर्षेरमितौजसः।
रामं दिदृक्षुरायातः कार्येण हि महाबल॥ ३॥
verses.m: ‘I am the messenger of the sage Atibala, possessed of great power and have come desiring to see Śrī Rāma with a purpose, O mighty one.’ (3)

verses.text:
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा सौमित्रिस्त्वरयान्वितः।
न्यवेदयत रामाय तापसं तं समागतम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Having heard the words of the ascetic, the son of Sumitrā, Lakṣmaṇa, at once reported the arrival of that ascetic to Śrī Rāma ! (4)

verses.text:
जयस्व राजधर्मेण उभौ लोकौ महाद्युते।
दूतस्त्वां द्रष्टुमायातस्तपसा भास्करप्रभः॥ ५॥
verses.m: ‘O one possessed of great power, be victorious over both the worlds: a messenger, who is as lustrous as the sun, due to austerities, has come to see you.’ (5)

verses.text:
तद् वाक्यं लक्ष्मणोक्तं वै श्रुत्वा राम उवाच ह।
प्रवेश्यतां मुनिस्तात महौजास्तस्य वाक्यधृक्॥ ६॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma on his part hearing the words of Lakṣmaṇa said: ‘O dear, let the messenger possessed of great vigour, who carries the message of his patron, enter.’ (6)

verses.text:
सौमित्रिस्तु तथेत्युक्त्वा प्रावेशयत तं मुनिम्।
ज्वलन्तमेव तेजोभिः प्रदहन्तमिवांशुभिः॥ ७॥
verses.m: Then the son of Sumitrā, Lakṣmaṇa, also having said, ‘It shall be as you say’, He presented before Rāma, the great ascetic as if enveloped with effulgence and burning others with his beams. (7)

verses.text:
सोऽभिगम्य रघुश्रेष्ठं दीप्यमानं स्वतेजसा।
ऋषिर्मधुरया वाचा वर्धस्वेत्याह राघवम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: That sage having approached the best among the descendants of Raghus, glowing with his splendour said in a sweet voice, ‘Hail to Thee.’ (8)

verses.text:
तस्मै रामो महातेजाः पूजामर्घ्यपुरोगमाम्।
ददौ कुशलमव्यग्रं प्रष्टुं चैवोपचक्रमे॥ ९॥
verses.m: The powerful Śrī Rāma worshipped him with offerings of Arghya and then began to ask him about his welfare. (9)

verses.text:
पृष्टश्च कुशलं तेन रामेण वदतां वरः।
आसने काञ्चने दिव्ये निषसाद महायशाः॥ १०॥
verses.m: The famous ascetic, the best among speakers, being thus enquired about his welfare by Śrī Rāma, seated himself on the beautiful golden seat. (10)

verses.text:
तमुवाच ततो रामः स्वागतं ते महामते।
प्रापयस्व च वाक्यानि यतो दूतस्त्वमागतः॥ ११॥
verses.m: Then Śrī Rāma said to him, ‘Welcome to you, O one of great wisdom. Please do convey the message of him from whom you have come as messenger.’ (11)

verses.text:
चोदितो राजसिंहेन मुनिर्वाक्यमभाषत।
द्वन्द्वे ह्येतत् प्रवक्तव्यं हितं वै यद्यवेक्षसे॥ १२॥
verses.m: Impelled by Śrī Rāma, the lion among kings, the ascetic said: ‘My message is to be conveyed only between two of us secretly, if you keep the common interest in mind. (12)

verses.text:
यः शृणोति निरीक्षेद् वा स वध्यो भविता तव।
भवेद् वै मुनिमुख्यस्य वचनं यद्यवेक्षसे॥ १३॥
verses.m: ‘If you pay heed to the words of the chief of the ascetics, the intruder who sees us or hears our talk must be sentenced to death. (13)

verses.text:
तथेति च प्रतिज्ञाय रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्।
द्वारि तिष्ठ महाबाहो प्रतिहारं विसर्जय॥ १४॥
verses.m: Saying “So shall it be”, Śrī Rāma said to Lakṣmaṇa, “Go, and stand at the door; O one of long arms and dismiss the door-attendant. (14)

verses.text:
स मे वध्यः खलु भवेद् वाचं द्वन्द्वसमीरितम्।
ऋषेर्मम च सौमित्रे पश्येद् वा शृणुयाच्च यः॥ १५॥
verses.m: He shall indeed be killed who sees or hears the words spoken between two of us.’ (15)

verses.text:
ततो निक्षिप्य काकुत्स्थो लक्ष्मणं द्वारि संग्रहम्।
तमुवाच मुने वाक्यं कथयस्वेति राघवः॥ १६॥
verses.m: Then placing Lakṣmaṇa, who could catch of the meaning of Śrī Rāma’s word at the door, the descendant of Raghu said to that ascetic, ‘O ascetic, speak what you have to say. (16)

verses.text:
तत् ते मनीषितं वाक्यं येन वासि समाहितः।
कथयस्वाविशङ्कस्त्वं ममापि हृदि वर्तते॥ १७॥
verses.m: Do speak out the intention of that one by whom you have been sent without any hesitation. I am eager to know what you have got to say. (17)

verses.text:
शृणु राजन् महासत्त्व यदर्थमहमागतः।
पितामहेन देवेन प्रेषितोऽस्मि महाबल॥ १॥
verses.m: ‘Hear, O King of great prowess, the purpose for which I have come, O powerful one, I have been sent by the god Brahmā. (1)

verses.text:
तवाहं पूर्वके भावे पुत्रः परपुरंजय।
मायासम्भावितो वीर कालः सर्वसमाहरः॥ २॥
verses.m: ‘In the primeval form, O brave one, destroyer of the forts of enemies, at the time of creation I was your son, in the form of Time brought forth by your Māyā (the illusory power), and the destroyer of all. (2)

verses.text:
पितामहश्च भगवानाह लोकपतिः प्रभुः।
समयस्ते कृतः सौम्य लोकान् सम्परिरक्षितुम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: ‘Our lord, the master of all worlds, the venerable Brahmā has said: ‘O gracious one, you have promised formerly for the protection of the worlds and that has been fulfilled. (3)

verses.text:
संक्षिप्य हि पुरा लोकान् मायया स्वयमेव हि।
महार्णवे शयानोऽप्सु मां त्वं पूर्वमजीजनः॥ ४॥
verses.m: ‘Prior to creation, you yourself by your Māyā having merged all the worlds in you reposing on the great ocean, had created me (Brahmā) first. (4)

verses.text:
भोगवन्तं ततो नागमनन्तमुदकेशयम्।
मायया जनयित्वा त्वं द्वौ च सत्त्वौ महाबलौ॥ ५॥
मधुं च कैटभं चैव ययोरस्थिचयैर्वृता।
इयं पर्वतसम्बाधा मेदिनी चाभवत् तदा॥ ६॥
verses.m: ‘Then having created by your Māyā the thousand-hooded Ananta (serpent) lying on the waters, you created the two powerful beings, Madhu and Kaiṭabha by the heaps of bones of whom this earth was crowded and covered with mountains, and then became the earth, Medinī, (having fatness-fertility). (5-6)

verses.text:
पद्मे दिव्येऽर्कसंकाशे नाभ्यामुत्पाद्य मामपि।
प्राजापत्यं त्वया कर्म मयि सर्वं निवेशितम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: ‘Creating from Your navel, two divine lotus, having the lustre of the sun, and from it myself, the work ordained for Prajāpati (creator) was entrusted to me. (7)

verses.text:
सोऽहं संन्यस्तभारो हि त्वामुपास्य जगत्पतिम्।
रक्षां विधत्स्व भूतेषु मम तेजस्करो भवान्॥ ८॥
verses.m: ‘So I, having been entrusted with the task of creation, by worshipping you, I request you: Lord! protect all creatures as you only bestow power upon me. (8)

verses.text:
ततस्त्वमसि दुर्धर्षात् तस्माद् भावात् सनातनात्।
रक्षां विधास्यन् भूतानां विष्णुत्वमुपजग्मिवान्॥ ९॥
verses.m: ‘Due to that prayer for the protection of the beings on earth, you took the form of Viṣṇu, from that ethereal eternal form. (9)

verses.text:
अदित्यां वीर्यवान् पुत्रो भ्रातॄणां वीर्यवर्धनः।
समुत्पन्नेषु कृत्येषु तेषां साह्याय कल्पसे॥ १०॥
verses.m: ‘From Aditi (the mother of the gods), you were born as the brave son, Vāmana, the Divine Dwarf adding to the valour of your brothers (the gods) and extended help to them whenever the occasion demanded. (10)

verses.text:
स त्वं वित्रास्यमानासु प्रजासु जगतां वर।
रावणस्य वधाकाङ्क्षी मानुषेषु मनोऽदधाः॥ ११॥
दशवर्षसहस्राणि दशवर्षशतानि च।
कृत्वा वासस्य नियमं स्वयमेवात्मना पुरा॥ १२॥
verses.m: ‘O best in the world, You had set your mind on having a human form, desirous to kill Rāvaṇa, when the human beings were being extirpated, you yourself fixed the span of your stay among the mortals for ten thousand and ten hundred years formerly. (11-12)

verses.text:
स त्वं मनोमयः पुत्रः पूर्णायुर्मानुषेष्विह।
कालोऽयं ते नरश्रेष्ठ समीपमुपवर्तितुम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: ‘You were thus a mind-born son of Daśaratha. The span of your stay on earth as human being is complete and now it is time for you to come back to us. (13)

verses.text:
यदि भूयो महाराज प्रजा इच्छस्युपासितुम्।
वस वा वीर भद्रं ते एवमाह पितामहः॥ १४॥
verses.m: ‘If, O brave one, you desire again to serve men, then dwell as you wish, may welfare be with Thee, thus Brahmā said.’ (14)

verses.text:
अथ वा विजिगीषा ते सुरलोकाय राघव।
सनाथा विष्णुना देवा भवन्तु विगतज्वराः॥ १५॥
verses.m: ‘If, however, O descendant of Raghu, there is the desire in you to protect the gods, then let the gods have Viṣṇu as their Lord.’ (15)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा पितामहेनोक्तं वाक्यं कालसमीरितम्।
राघवः प्रहसन् वाक्यं सर्वसंहारमब्रवीत्॥ १६॥
verses.m: Having heard, the words of Brahmā spoken by Death, Śrī Rāma said laughingly to the destroyer of all, the Death: (16)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा मे देवदेवस्य वाक्यं परममद्भुतम्।
प्रीतिर्हि महती जाता तवागमनसम्भवा॥ १७॥
verses.m: ‘Hearing the words so full of wonder, of the god of gods (Brahmā), fills me with great pleasure born out of your visit. (17)

verses.text:
त्रयाणामपि लोकानां कार्यार्थं मम सम्भवः।
भद्रं तेऽस्तु गमिष्यामि यत एवाहमागतः॥ १८॥
verses.m: ‘To carry out the work of the three worlds is the purpose of my birth as human being, may welfare be with you; I will go now to heaven, wherefrom I came. (18)

verses.text:
हृद्गतो ह्यसि सम्प्राप्तो न मे तत्र विचारणा।
मया हि सर्वकृत्येषु देवानां वशवर्तिना।
स्थातव्यं सर्वसंहार यथा ह्याह पितामहः॥ १९॥
verses.m: ‘You have come as my heart desired, so there is nothing for me to ponder over. O destroyer of all, I have to stay at will of gods for performing all their deeds as Brahmā has said.’ (19)

verses.text:
तथा तयोः संवदतोर्दुर्वासा भगवानृषिः।
रामस्य दर्शनाकाङ्क्षी राजद्वारमुपागमत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Thus while the two (Śrī Rāma and Death) were conversing, the venerable sage, Durvāsā, desirous of seeing Śrī Rāma appeared at the royal gate. (1)

verses.text:
सोऽभिगम्य तु सौमित्रिमुवाच ऋषिसत्तमः।
रामं दर्शय मे शीघ्रं पुरा मेऽर्थोऽतिवर्तते॥ २॥
verses.m: The great sage approaching Lakṣmaṇa (the son of Sumitrā) said: ‘Let me see Śrī Rāma at once, for, the purpose for which I have come is being lost.’ (2)

verses.text:
मुनेस्तु भाषितं श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा।
अभिवाद्य महात्मानं वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह॥ ३॥
verses.m: Lakṣmaṇa the killer of the enemy heroes, on hearing words of the ascetic, spoke after having saluted the noble one, Durvāsā: (3)

verses.text:
किं कार्यं ब्रूहि भगवन् को ह्यर्थः किं करोम्यहम्।
व्यग्रो हि राघवो ब्रह्मन् मुहूर्तं परिपाल्यताम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: ‘Sir, what has to be done for you for what purpose you have come? What should I do? The descendant of Raghu is now indeed busy, O Brāhmaṇa, wait for a moment.’ (4)

verses.text:
तच्छ्रुत्वा ऋषिशार्दूलः क्रोधेन कलुषीकृतः।
उवाच लक्ष्मणं वाक्यं निर्दहन्निव चक्षुषा॥ ५॥
verses.m: Having heard this, Durvāsā, the lion among sages, darkened by rage said to Lakṣmaṇa, as if burning all by his eyes: (5)

verses.text:
अस्मिन् क्षणे मां सौमित्रे रामाय प्रतिवेदय।
अस्मिन् क्षणे गां सौमित्रे न निवेदयसे यदि।
विषयं त्वां पुरं चैव शपिष्ये राघवं तथा॥ ६॥
भरतं चैव सौमित्रे युष्माकं या च संततिः।
न हि शक्ष्याम्यहं भूयो मन्युं धारयितुं हृदि॥ ७॥
verses.m: ‘Inform about me at this very moment Śrī Rāma, O son of Sumitrā, If you do not do so, I shall curse this city, you, this territory, Bharata and also Rāma and even this city’s progeny, I am indeed unable to contain my anger inside me anymore. (6-7)

verses.text:
तच्छ्रुत्वा घोरसंकाशं वाक्यं तस्य महात्मनः।
चिन्तयामास मनसा तस्य वाक्यस्य निश्चयम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: Hearing those dreadful words of the Mahātmā (Durvāsā), Lakṣmaṇa thought in his mind the real purport of his (Durvāsā) words. (8)

verses.text:
एकस्य मरणं मेऽस्तु मा भूत् सर्वविनाशनम्।
इति बुद्ध्या विनिश्चित्य राघवाय न्यवेदयत्॥ ९॥
verses.m: ‘Let me die alone, let not all others perish’ deciding thus he reported the arrival of Durvāsā to Śrī Rāma. (9)

verses.text:
लक्ष्मणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा रामः कालं विसृज्य च।
निःसृत्य त्वरितो राजा अत्रेः पुत्रं ददर्श ह॥ १०॥
verses.m: Hearing the words of Lakṣmaṇa, the king Śrī Rāma disposing Death, came out in haste and saw the son of Atri (Durvāsā). (10)

verses.text:
सोऽभिवाद्य महात्मानं ज्वलन्तमिव तेजसा।
किं कार्यमिति काकुत्स्थः कृताञ्जलिरभाषत॥ ११॥
verses.m: Having saluted him the noble one, enflamed with effulgence, Śrī Rāma, the descendant of Kakutstha, with folded hands said: ‘What has to be done by me.’ (11)

verses.text:
तद् वाक्यं राघवेणोक्तं श्रुत्वा मुनिवरः प्रभुः।
प्रत्याह रामं दुर्वासाः श्रूयतां धर्मवत्सल॥ १२॥
अद्य वर्षसहस्रस्य समाप्तिर्मम राघव।
सोऽहं भोजनमिच्छामि यथासिद्धं तवानघ॥ १३॥
verses.m: Hearing these words spoken by Śrī Rāma, Durvāsā replied: ‘O one of loving piety, listen, the thousand years of my vow of keeping fast has ended today, so I want cooked food, whatsoever may be ready.’ (12-13)

verses.text:
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं राजा राघवः प्रीतमानसः।
भोजनं मुनिमुख्याय यथासिद्धमुपाहरत्॥ १४॥
verses.m: Hearing these words Śrī Rāma the king, with gratified mind, offered food readily available. (14)

verses.text:
स तु भुक्त्वा मुनिश्रेष्ठस्तदन्नममृतोपमम्।
साधु रामेति सम्भाष्य स्वमाश्रममुपागमत्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Durvāsā the best among ascetics, having consumed that food like nectar, ‘saying appreciatory words to Śrī Rāma’, went away to his hermitage. (15)

verses.text:
तस्मिन् गते मुनिवरे स्वाश्रमं लक्ष्मणाग्रजः।
संस्मृत्य कालवाक्यानि ततो दुःखमुपागमत्॥ १६॥
verses.m: After Durvāsā was gone to his hermitage, Rāma remembering the utterances of Kāla became sad. (16)

verses.text:
दुःखेन च सुसंतप्तः स्मृत्वा तद्घोरदर्शनम्।
अवाङ् मुखो दीनमना व्याहर्तुं न शशाक ह॥ १७॥
verses.m: Thinking of terrible sorrow that would be ensued from the separation of a brother like Lakṣmaṇa, Rāma was tormented to the extreme. With his down cast face and a miserable heart he could not speak a word. (17)

verses.text:
ततो बुद्ध्या विनिश्चित्य कालवाक्यानि राघवः।
नैतदस्तीति निश्चित्य तूष्णीमासीन्महायशाः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Considering pros and cons of the utterances of Kāla, Rāma came to the conclusion that now nothing will remain, he kept silent. (18)

verses.text:
अवाङ्मुखमथो दीनं दृष्ट्वा सोममिवाप्लुतम्।
राघवं लक्ष्मणो वाक्यं हृष्टो मधुरमब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Seeing the descendant of Raghu, Śrī Rāma, speechless and in sorrow like the moon eclipsed by Rāhu, Lakṣmaṇa cheerfully spoke to him in sweet accents: (1)

verses.text:
न संतापं महाबाहो मदर्थं कर्तुमर्हसि।
पूर्वनिर्माणबद्धा हि कालस्य गतिरीदृशी॥ २॥
verses.m: ‘O one of long arms, you should not feel grieved for me, because bound by former actions, this is the law of time (Death). (2)

verses.text:
जहि मां सौम्य विस्रब्धं प्रतिज्ञां परिपालय।
हीनप्रतिज्ञाः काकुत्स्थ प्रयान्ति नरकं नराः॥ ३॥
verses.m: ‘Give me death award, O gracious one, and confidently keep your word, O scion of Kakutstha; those men who do not keep their promises do go to Hell. (3)

verses.text:
यदि प्रीतिर्महाराज यद्यनुग्राह्यता मयि।
जहि मां निर्विशङ्कस्त्वं धर्मं वर्धय राघव॥ ४॥
verses.m: ‘O King, descendant of Raghu, kill me without hesitation if you have love for and are favourable to me, and promote righteousness.’ (4)

verses.text:
लक्ष्मणेन तथोक्तस्तु रामः प्रचलितेन्द्रियः।
मन्त्रिणः समुपानीय तथैव च पुरोधसम्॥ ५॥
अब्रवीच्च तदा वृत्तं तेषां मध्ये स राघवः।
दुर्वासोऽभिगमं चैव प्रतिज्ञां तापसस्य च॥ ६॥
verses.m: Thus spoken to by Lakṣmaṇa, Śrī Rāma with his senses disturbed, summoned his councillors and also priests, and said in their midst, what had happened, i.e., the arrival of Durvāsā and also the promise made in accordance with the condition laid down by the ascetic. (5-6)

verses.text:
तच्छ्रुत्वा मन्त्रिणः सर्वे सोपाध्यायाः समासत।
वसिष्ठस्तु महातेजा वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह॥ ७॥
verses.m: Hearing these words all the councillors together with the preceptors kept mum. Then Vasiṣṭha, the powerful one, however, said thus: (7)

verses.text:
दृष्टमेतन्महाबाहो क्षयं ते रोमहर्षणम्।
लक्ष्मणेन वियोगश्च तव राम महायशः॥ ८॥
verses.m: ‘O one of long arms, this end of yours was foreseen by me, which causes horripilation and also separation from Lakṣmaṇa, O Śrī Rāma, possessed of glory. (8)

verses.text:
त्यजैनं बलवान् कालो मा प्रतिज्ञां वृथा कृथाः।
प्रतिज्ञायां हि नष्टायां धर्मो हि विलयं व्रजेत्॥ ९॥
verses.m: ‘Leave him, Lakṣmaṇa. Time (Death) is indeed too powerful, do not give up your promise, for, it being given up, righteousness will perish. (9)

verses.text:
ततो धर्मे विनष्टे तु त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम्।
सदेवर्षिगणं सर्वं विनश्येत् तु न संशयः॥ १०॥
verses.m: ‘With righteousness gone, the three worlds, both moving and stationary, indeed the hosts of divine sages, shall perish, there is no doubt. (10)

verses.text:
स त्वं पुरुषशार्दूल त्रैलोक्यस्याभिपालनात्।
लक्ष्मणेन विना चाद्य जगत् स्वस्थं कुरुष्व ह॥ ११॥
verses.m: ‘Therefore, O lion among men, separated from Lakṣmaṇa today, you, on your part, restore normalcy to this earth with the protection of the three worlds.’ (11)

verses.text:
तेषां तत् समवेतानां वाक्यं धर्मार्थसंहितम्।
श्रुत्वा परिषदो मध्ये रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्॥ १२॥
verses.m: Hearing these words full of righteous import, spoken by those assembled, Śrī Rāma said to Lakṣmaṇa in the midst of that assembly: (12)

verses.text:
विसर्जये त्वां सौमित्रे मा भूद् धर्मविपर्ययः।
त्यागो वधो वा विहितः साधूनां ह्युभयं समम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: ‘I leave you, O son of Sumitrā (Lakṣmaṇa), may not the cause of righteousness suffer; desertion or slaying—both are the same to the pious ones.’ (13)

verses.text:
रामेण भाषिते वाक्ये बाष्पव्याकुलितेन्द्रियः।
लक्ष्मणस्त्वरितं प्रायात् स्वगृहं न विवेश ह॥ १४॥
verses.m: On Śrī Rāma speaking thus, Lakṣmaṇa, with his eyes filled with tears, went out in haste and did not enter his apartment. (14)

verses.text:
स गत्वा सरयूतीरमुपस्पृश्य कृताञ्जलिः।
निगृह्य सर्वस्रोतांसि निःश्वासं न मुमोच ह॥ १५॥
verses.m: Having reached the banks of the Sarayū, he performed ablutions, restraining all senses and holding his breath. (15)

verses.text:
अनिःश्वसन्तं युक्तं तं सशक्राः साप्सरोगणाः।
देवाः सर्षिगणाः सर्वे पुष्पैरभ्यकिरंस्तदा॥ १६॥
verses.m: The gods, together with Indra, the Apsarās and all sages sprinkled flowers on him, who was performing the Yoga of restraining senses. (16)

verses.text:
अदृश्यं सर्वमनुजैः सशरीरं महाबलम्।
प्रगृह्य लक्ष्मणं शक्रस्त्रिदिवं संविवेश ह॥ १७॥
verses.m: Taking hold of Lakṣmaṇa alive and invisible to men, Indra entered the heaven alongwith him. (17)

verses.text:
ततो विष्णोश्चतुर्भागमागतं सुरसत्तमाः।
हृष्टाः प्रमुदिताः सर्वे पूजयन्ति स्म राघवम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: Then all the great gods, pleased at seeing the fourth part of Viṣṇu coming back to heaven, honoured indeed the descendant of Raghu, Lakṣmaṇa. (18)

verses.text:
विसृज्य लक्ष्मणं रामो दुःखशोकसमन्वितः।
पुरोधसं मन्त्रिणश्च नैगमांश्चेदमब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Having discharged Lakṣmaṇa, Śrī Rāma full of agony and sorrow, spoke thus to the priests, councillors and citizens: (1)

verses.text:
अद्य राज्येऽभिषेक्ष्यामि भरतं धर्मवत्सलम्।
अयोध्यायाः पतिं वीरं ततो यास्याम्यहं वनम्॥ २॥
verses.m: ‘I shall consecrate the brave one, Bharata, given to piety in this kingdom as the lord of Ayodhyā this very day and then depart to the forest. (2)

verses.text:
प्रवेशयत सम्भारान् मा भूत् कालात्ययो यथा।
अद्यैवाहं गमिष्यामि लक्ष्मणेन गतां गतिम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: ‘All the necessaries for consecration may be brought without delay. I shall tread on the path that Lakṣmaṇa has gone this very day.’ (3)

verses.text:
तच्छ्रुत्वा राघवेणोक्तं सर्वाः प्रकृतयो भृशम्।
मूर्धभिः प्रणता भूमौ गतसत्त्वा इवाभवन्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Hearing these words of the descendant of Raghu, all subjects prostrated on the ground and were almost rendered as if lifeless. (4)

verses.text:
भरतश्च विसंज्ञोऽभूच्छ्रुत्वा राघवभाषितम्।
राज्यं विगर्हयामास वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्॥ ५॥
verses.m: Bharata too became almost unconscious on hearing the words of the descendant of Raghu, Śrī Rāma, and spoke ill of kingship and then said: (5)

verses.text:
सत्येनाहं शपे राजन् स्वर्गभोगेन चैव हि।
न कामये यथा राज्यं त्वां विना रघुनन्दन॥ ६॥
verses.m: ‘I swear, by the truth and heavenly enjoyments, O descendant of Raghu, I do not desire kingship without you. (6)

verses.text:
इमौ कुशीलवौ राजन्नभिषिच्य नराधिप।
कोशलेषु कुशं वीरमुत्तरेषु तथा लवम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: ‘O King, consecrate Kuśa in the territory of south Kosala and Lava in the Uttara Kosala territory. (7)

verses.text:
शत्रुघ्नस्य च गच्छन्तु दूतास्त्वरितविक्रमाः।
इदं गमनमस्माकं शीघ्रमाख्यातु मा चिरम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: ‘May messengers of speedy gait go to Śatrughna, and convey soon the news of our departure, may there be no delay’. (8)

verses.text:
तच्छ्रुत्वा भरतेनोक्तं दृष्ट्वा चापि ह्यधोमुखान्।
पौरान् दुःखेन संतप्तान् वसिष्ठो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ ९॥
verses.m: Having heard the words spoken by Bharata and also seen the citizens with faces downcast and afflicted by pain, Vasiṣṭha said: (9)

verses.text:
वत्स राम इमाः पश्य धरणिं प्रकृतीर्गताः।
ज्ञात्वैषामीप्सितं कार्यं मा चैषां विप्रियं कृथाः॥ १०॥
verses.m: ‘O Child Śrī Rāma, see the subjects lying prostrate on the ground, you should act after knowing their desire; do not do something disliked by them.’ (10)

verses.text:
वसिष्ठस्य तु वाक्येन उत्थाप्य प्रकृतीजनम्।
किं करोमीति काकुत्स्थः सर्वान् वचनमब्रवीत्॥ ११॥
verses.m: Impelled by the words of Vasiṣṭha, the descendant of Kakutstha made the subjects rise, and said to all of them ‘What may I do.(11)

verses.text:
ततः सर्वाः प्रकृतयो रामं वचनमब्रुवन्।
गच्छन्तमनुगच्छामो यत्र राम गमिष्यसि॥ १२॥
verses.m: Then all the subjects said to Śrī Rāma: ‘O Śrī Rāma, we shall follow you wherever you go. (12)

verses.text:
पौरेषु यदि ते प्रीतिर्यदि स्नेहो ह्यनुत्तमः।
सपुत्रदाराः काकुत्स्थ समं गच्छाम सत्पथम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: ‘If you are pleased with the citizens and do bear great affection for them, then, O descendant of Kakutstha, we shall proceed on the right path simultaneously (the way to heaven), together with our progeny and spouses. (13)

verses.text:
तपोवनं वा दुर्गं वा नदीमम्भोनिधिं तथा।
वयं ते यदि न त्याज्याः सर्वान्नो नय ईश्वर॥ १४॥
verses.m: ‘Take all of us to the forest, unnavigable land or river or the ocean, O lord, if we are not to be deserted by you. (14)

verses.text:
एषा नः परमा प्रीतिरेष नः परमो वरः।
हृद्गता नः सदा प्रीतिस्तवानुगमने नृप॥ १५॥
verses.m: ‘This is what we most desire, O King, in following you lies the pleasure of our life.’ (15)

verses.text:
पौराणां दृढभक्तिं च बाढमित्येव सोऽब्रवीत्।
स्वकृतान्तं चान्ववेक्ष्य तस्मिन्नहनि राघवः॥ १६॥
कोशलेषु कुशं वीरमुत्तरेषु तथा लवम्।
अभिषिच्य महात्मानावुभौ रामः कुशीलवौ॥ १७॥
अभिषिक्तौ सुतावङ्के प्रतिष्ठाप्य पुरे ततः।
परिष्वज्य महाबाहुर्मूर्ध्न्युपाघ्राय चासकृत्॥ १८॥
रथानां तु सहस्राणि नागानामयुतानि च।
दशायुतानि चाश्वानामेकैकस्य धनं ददौ॥ १९॥
verses.m: Seeing the firm devotion of the citizens, He, Śrī Rāma, said, ‘so be it. Visualizing the end of his earthly sojourn that very day, the descendant of Raghu, Śrī Rāma, having coronated both the noble ones Kuśa in the south Kośala territory and Lava in the Uttara Kośala territory, then seating them in his lap, embracing them, smelling their heads more than once and establishing them as kings, gave to each a thousand chariots, ten thousand elephants and hundred thousand horses. (16—19)

verses.text:
बहुरत्नौ बहुधनौ हृष्टपुष्टजनावृतौ।
स्वे पुरे प्रेषयामास भ्रातरौ तौ कुशीलवौ॥ २०॥
verses.m: He (Śrī Rāma) sent the two brothers, Kuśa and Lava to their respective kingdoms, with many gems and a lot of wealth and full of happy and prosperous men. (20)

verses.text:
अभिषिच्य ततो वीरौ प्रस्थाप्य स्वपुरे तदा।
दूतान् सम्प्रेषयामास शत्रुघ्नाय महात्मने॥ २१॥
verses.m: Then, having coronated both of them and establishing them in their own kingdom, caused messengers to be sent to the noble Śatrughna. (21)

verses.text:
ते दूता रामवाक्येन चोदिता लघुविक्रमाः।
प्रजग्मुर्मधुरां शीघ्रं चक्रुर्वासं न चाध्वनि॥ १॥
verses.m: Then the messengers of speedy gait, receiving the orders of Śrī Rāma, went to Madhurā with all haste and did not halt on the way. (1)

verses.text:
ततस्त्रिभिरहोरात्रैः सम्प्राप्य मधुरामथ।
शत्रुघ्नाय यथातत्त्वमाचख्युः सर्वमेव तत्॥ २॥
लक्ष्मणस्य परित्यागं प्रतिज्ञां राघवस्य च।
पुत्रयोरभिषेकं च पौरानुगमनं तथा॥ ३॥
verses.m: Then after three days and nights, having reached Madhurā, they (the messengers) narrated all that had happened exactly; the desertion of Lakṣmaṇa, and the determination of Śrī Rāma, the descendant of Raghu, on the consecration of the two sons (of Śrī Rāma) and the citizens following Him.(2-3)

verses.text:
कुशस्य नगरी रम्या विन्ध्यपर्वतरोधसि।
कुशावतीति नाम्ना सा कृता रामेण धीमता॥ ४॥
श्रावस्तीति पुरी रम्या श्राविता च लवस्य ह।
अयोध्यां विजनां कृत्वा राघवो भरतस्तथा॥ ५॥
स्वर्गस्य गमनोद्योगं कृतवन्तौ महारथौ।
एवं सर्वं निवेद्याशु शत्रुघ्नाय महात्मने॥ ६॥
विरेमुस्ते ततो दूतास्त्वर राजेति चाब्रुवन्।
तच्छ्रुत्वा घोरसंकाशं कुलक्षयमुपस्थितम्॥ ७॥
प्रकृतीस्तु समानीय काञ्चनं च पुरोधसम्।
तेषां सर्वं यथावृत्तमब्रवीद् रघुनन्दनः॥ ८॥
verses.m: That beautiful city of Kuśa at the foot of the Vindhya mountain, was named Kuśāvatī by the wise Śrī Rāma and that beautiful city of Lava, Śrāvastī, was also made famous. Thus after having rendered Ayodhyā desolate, the descendant of Raghu, Śrī Rāma and Bharata, the two great warriors, have made themselves ready to go to heaven. Having thus narrated all events to the noble Śatrughna, those messengers then stopped narrating and said: ‘O king, make haste’, having heard the terrible news of his family coming to an end, the descendant of Raghu, calling all his subjects and the priest Kāñcana, spoke to them all that had happened. (4—8)

verses.text:
आत्मनश्च विपर्यासं भविष्यं भ्रातृभिः सह।
ततः पुत्रद्वयं वीरः सोऽभ्यषिञ्चन्नराधिपः॥ ९॥
सुबाहुर्मधुरां लेभे शत्रुघाती च वैदिशम्।
द्विधा कृत्वा तु तां सेनां माधुरीं पुत्रयोर्द्वयोः।
धनं च युक्तं कृत्वा वै स्थापयामास पार्थिवः॥ १०॥
verses.m: He also communicated his approaching death with his brothers. Śatrughna then consecrated his two sons. Subāhu obtained Madhurā, while Śatrughātī, Vidiśa (Bhelsa). Having divided the army of Madhurā into two and making them possessed of wealth, the king, Śatrughna, established his two sons there. (9-10)

verses.text:
सुबाहुं मधुरायां च वैदिशे शत्रुघातिनम्।
ययौ स्थाप्य तदायोध्यां रथेनैकेन राघवः॥ ११॥
verses.m: Having established Subāhu in Madhurā (Mathurā) and Śatrughātī in Vidiśa, the descendant of Raghu, Śatrughna, went to Ayodhyā by a chariot, alone. (11)

verses.text:
स ददर्श महात्मानं ज्वलन्तमिव पावकम्।
सूक्ष्मक्षौमाम्बरधरं मुनिभिः सार्धमक्षयैः॥ १२॥
verses.m: He saw Śrī Rāma, the noble one, as though the fire in flames, dressed in fine silken garments sitting together with the immortal sages. (12)

verses.text:
सोऽभिवाद्य ततो रामं प्राञ्जलिः प्रयतेन्द्रियः।
उवाच वाक्यं धर्मज्ञं धर्ममेवानुचिन्तयन्॥ १३॥
verses.m: Having saluted Śrī Rāma, with folded hands and his senses in control, contemplating on the law of righteousness, he, Śatrughna, spoke to him, the knower of Dharma: (13)

verses.text:
कृत्वाभिषेकं सुतयोर्द्वयो राघवनन्दन।
तवानुगमने राजन् विद्धि मां कृतनिश्चयम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: ‘O descendant of Raghu, know me as one having decided to follow you after having coronated my two sons. (14)

verses.text:
न चान्यदद्य वक्तव्यमतो वीर न शासनम्।
विहन्यमानमिच्छामि मद्विधेन विशेषतः॥ १५॥
verses.m: ‘No word other than that of consent is to be spoken by you, O brave one ! I do not wish that your orders be transgressed by one like me, in particular.’ (15)

verses.text:
तस्य तां बुद्धिमक्लीबां विज्ञाय रघुनन्दनः।
बाढमित्येव शत्रुघ्नं रामो वाक्यमुवाच ह॥ १६॥
verses.m: Knowing that potent desire (of Śatrughna), the descendant of Raghu, said ‘Indeed, may it be so, O Śatrughna’. (16)

verses.text:
तस्य वाक्यस्य वाक्यान्ते वानराः कामरूपिणः।
ऋक्षराक्षससङ्घाश्च समापेतुरनेकशः॥ १७॥
verses.m: As he finished his sentence, the monkeys, who could change their form according to their will, and also the bears and Rākṣasas in great number arrived there. (17)

verses.text:
सुग्रीवं ते पुरस्कृत्य सर्व एव समागताः।
तं रामं द्रष्टुमनसः स्वर्गायाभिमुखं स्थितम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: Having put Sugrīva at their head, came all of them wishing to see Śrī Rāma on his way to heaven. (18)

verses.text:
देवपुत्रा ऋषिसुता गन्धर्वाणां सुतास्तथा।
रामक्षयं विदित्वा ते सर्व एव समागताः॥ १९॥
verses.m: Knowing that the end of the earthly sojourn of Śrī Rāma has arrived, the sons of gods, the sons of sages and also the sons of the Gandharvas came. (19)

verses.text:
ते राममभिवाद्योचुः सर्वे वानरराक्षसाः।
तवानुगमने राजन् सम्प्राप्ताः स्म समागताः॥ २०॥
यदि राम विनास्माभिर्गच्छेस्त्वं पुरुषोत्तम।
यमदण्डमिवोद्यम्य त्वया स्म विनिपातिताः॥ २१॥
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे रामं सुग्रीवोऽपि महाबलः।
प्रणम्य विधिवद् वीरं विज्ञापयितुमुद्यतः॥ २२॥
verses.m: They said: ‘O King, we have come to follow you, O Śrī Rāma, the best among men, if you will go without us, then indeed we will take it as having been killed as if by you by the rod of Yama. In this midst, the powerful Sugrīva also having saluted the brave one, Śrī Rāma, properly, became eager to convey his wish and said: (20—22)

verses.text:
अभिषिच्याङ्गदं वीरमागतोऽस्मि नरेश्वर।
तवानुगमने राजन् विद्धि मां कृतनिश्चयम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: ‘O king of men, having coronated the brave Aṅgada (son of Vālī) on the throne, I have come. Know me, O king, as one having decided to follow you.’ (23)

verses.text:
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा रामो रमयतां वरः।
वानरेन्द्रमथोवाच मैत्रं तस्यानुचिन्तयन्॥ २४॥
verses.m: Hearing him so saying, Rāma, the best among rejoicers, having in consideration his friendship spoke to Sugrīva: (24)

verses.text:
सखे शृणुष्व सुग्रीव न त्वयाहं विनाकृतः।
गच्छेयं देवलोकं वा परमं वा पदं महत्॥ २५॥
